Inside the transaction one project is left; after the rollback, both are back.

properties.heading: Check destructive statements before they run
properties.text:
The CLI prints no summary of what a write changed, so a read afterwards is the check. Two cases need care:

- `DROP INDEX` and `DROP CONSTRAINT` print nothing when they succeed. `SHOW INDEXES` and `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` list what exists before anything is dropped.
- A write that changed nothing exits 0 and prints a note on stderr. A `MATCH` that finds no rows skips the rest of its statement, so the `SET` never runs.

This statement opens `team.rl` for writing but matches nobody:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Zed'}) SET p.role = 'maintainer'"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.397583,"execute_ms":0.208541,"lex_parse_ms":0.005915999999999999,"lower_ms":0.005417,"parse_ms":0.17962499999999998,"plan_ms":0.004667,"result_generation_ms":0.000166,"rewrite_ms":0.00033299999999999996},"truncated":false}
note: write statement changed nothing; the graph is unchanged
```

The prefix to match on stderr is `note: write statement`; a transaction that persisted nothing prints `note: .commit changed nothing; the transaction applied no changes`.

properties.heading: Control network egress
properties.text:
These commands and flags reach the network, and each one is visible on the command line an agent runs:

| Command or flag               | Reaches                                                                | Limits                                                               | Checks                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--load https://…/<name>.rl`  | Any `https://` host; plain `http://` only for a loopback host          | 1 GiB and 300 seconds; the downloaded copy is deleted after the load | No signature and no host allowlist; `--safe` refuses it                                                                                        |
| `--fetch-params <name>=<url>` | Any `http://` or `https://` URL                                        | 64 MiB and 60 seconds                                                | No allowlist; `--safe` does not refuse it                                                                                                      |
| `relate upgrade`              | `releases.json` on relatedb.ai, then the release's files on GitHub     | —                                                                    | The checksum list's signature against the key pinned in the binary, then the binary's checksum; any failure stops it before the binary changes |
| `relate extension install`    | The signed first-party channel, a GitHub release, or the `--url` given | —                                                                    | Per trust tier; see the [permission matrix](#permission-matrix)                                                                                |
| `relate pull`, `relate push`  | The Neo4j or Aura server named on the command line                     | —                                                                    | —                                                                                                                                              |
| Usage metrics                 | Mixpanel, with anonymous usage events                                  | —                                                                    | `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns them off ([Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/))                           |

For a store published at a URL, the checked path is to download it, compare its SHA-256 with the published value, and load the local copy. A `--load` into the default in-memory store is read-only. In this block `<sha256>` is the published value, and `relate` runs only when it matches; `--strict` also fails a malformed checksum line. Where `sha256sum` is missing, `shasum -a 256 --strict -c -` stands in for it:

```bash
curl -sSfL -o graph.rl https://<host>/<path>/graph.rl
echo "<sha256>  graph.rl" | sha256sum --strict -c - && relate --load ./graph.rl --mode envelope 'MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes'
```

properties.heading: Create the example store
properties.text:
This writes a new single-file [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) named `team.rl` that holds three people and two projects. Every later command opens it with `--read-only` unless the step says it writes:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
```

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < team.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.927083,"execute_ms":1.609875,"lex_parse_ms":0.015000000000000001,"lower_ms":0.020458999999999998,"parse_ms":0.298333,"plan_ms":0.012416,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.000542},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …`** (exit code 6): a write reached a read-only open. When the write is intended, back up the store and run it in a separate command without `--read-only` ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-write-on-read-only)).
- **`syntax error: SafeModeViolation: This statement is not allowed in safe mode: …`** (exit code 6): the statement has one of the refused shapes. Add the label, the `LIMIT`, or a reducing aggregate; safe mode is a policy, so reopening without `--safe` also allows it ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-safe-mode-violation)).
- **`LOAD CSV file unavailable`** (exit code 1): no `--load-csv-dir` was given, or the file is outside it, a symlink escape, or a special file. Put the file under the directory and pass `--load-csv-dir <dir>` ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-load-csv-unavailable)).
- **`Error: --safe refuses a remote --load source — …`** (exit code 2): safe mode never loads a store from the network. Download the file, check its SHA-256, and pass the local path to `--load`.

properties.heading: Keep LOAD CSV inside one directory
properties.text:
`LOAD CSV` reads no local file by default. `--load-csv-dir <dir>`, or `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR` when the flag is absent, allows regular files under that one directory, up to 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) each. A path outside it, a symlink that escapes it, a special file, and a URL all fail the same way: the exit code is 1, and the message names no path. The first command writes a CSV file under `imports/`:

```bash verify
mkdir -p imports
printf 'name,role\nOla,engineer\n' > imports/people.csv
```

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS FROM 'people.csv' AS row RETURN row.name AS name"
```

```text
LOAD CSV file unavailable
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"execution","message":"LOAD CSV file unavailable","retryable":false}}
```

With the directory named, the same statement reads the file:

```bash verify
relate --load-csv-dir ./imports --mode envelope "LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS FROM 'people.csv' AS row RETURN row.name AS name"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING"],"columns":["name"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Ola"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.445625,"execute_ms":0.269958,"lex_parse_ms":0.0050420000000000005,"lower_ms":0.003791,"parse_ms":0.16458299999999998,"plan_ms":0.006,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.000417},"truncated":false}
```

`relate serve` has no `--load-csv-dir` flag: `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR` in the server's environment is its only switch. Over MCP, `read_cypher` refuses `LOAD CSV`, and `write_cypher` runs it when the directory is set and the store is writable.

properties.heading: Open the store read-only
properties.text:
`--read-only` opens a store [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only): relate never writes it, never runs a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint) on it, and never migrates it. A write fails before anything changes, with exit code 6:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Eve'})"
```

The first line is stderr, the second is stdout:

```text
semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.","retryable":false}}
```

| Store      | With `--read-only`                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Directory  | Opens beside a running writer; `--read-only=live` follows the writer's commits |
| `.rl` file | Opens only while no writer holds it                                            |
| `:memory:` | Rejects writes and creates nothing                                             |

The MCP server takes the same flag. Opened read-only, it lists `read_cypher` and `get_schema` and leaves out `write_cypher`:

```bash
relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`. `read_cypher` refuses writes and schema changes either way, with `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query`.

A client handle takes the same guard: [Use relate with the Vercel AI SDK](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/integrations/vercel-ai-sdk/) opens the store with `{ readOnly: true }` behind an agent tool and plans each statement with `EXPLAIN` before it runs.

properties.heading: Permission matrix
properties.text:
What each control does on each surface. MCP stdio is `relate serve --mcp stdio`, and MCP HTTP is `relate serve --mcp <port>`. "n/a" means the control does not exist on that surface.

| Control                              | CLI                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | MCP stdio                                                                                                                                         | MCP HTTP          |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `--read-only`                        | Off by default. Writes fail with exit code 6; a directory store opens beside its writer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Off by default. With it, `write_cypher` is not listed; `read_cypher` refuses writes and schema changes in every mode                              | Same as MCP stdio |
| `--safe`                             | Off by default (`RELATE_SAFE_MODE`). Refuses a new named node without a label, an unbounded `MATCH` read, and a remote `--load`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | `relate serve --safe`: the same statement refusals on every tool call, and a remote `--load` refused at startup                                   | Same as MCP stdio |
| `LOAD CSV` policy                    | Denied by default. `--load-csv-dir <dir>` or `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR` allows regular files under one directory, 8 MiB each; no URLs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | No flag; `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR` in the server's environment only. `read_cypher` refuses `LOAD CSV`; `write_cypher` runs it                         | Same as MCP stdio |
| `--fetch-params` and `--load` egress | `--fetch-params`: `http` or `https` URL or file, 64 MiB, 60 seconds, no allowlist. `--load`: `https` (or loopback `http`) `.rl` URL, 1 GiB, 300 seconds                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `--fetch-params` is not a `serve` flag; parameters arrive in the tool call. `relate serve --load` fetches once, at startup, under the CLI's rules | Same as MCP stdio |
| Extension tiers                      | `relate extension install`: first-party (signed channel, checked against the release key), GitHub pin (`--github`: tag, commit and asset SHA-256 recorded; a moved tag is refused), third party (`--url`: `https`, or `http` to a loopback host), local (`--from <dir>`). `relate run` runs installed packages only; an uninstalled name fails without fetching anything | n/a: the server's tools are `read_cypher`, `write_cypher`, and `get_schema`                                                                       | n/a               |
| `upgrade`                            | `relate upgrade` installs the latest release after its signature and checksum pass, on macOS and Linux; `--check` changes nothing. It reinstalls the skill for every detected agent without asking once any of them holds a relate copy; with none, it asks first (`--yes` skips the question)                                                                           | n/a                                                                                                                                               | n/a               |

MCP over HTTP also asks for HTTP Basic authentication by default: `relate serve` generates a token, prints it at startup, and keeps it in a `<store>.auth-token` file beside the store. MCP over stdio has no authentication, because the host that starts the server is its only client.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A store to protect. The steps build a small one, `team.rl`.

properties.text:

- [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/): read-only config blocks for each agent host.

- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#safety): `--read-only`, `--safe`, `--load-csv-dir`, and their environment variables.
