properties.heading: Retry only retryable errors
properties.text:
The error object's `retryable` is `true` for a write-write conflict (exit 5) and for a `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` refusal while other statements hold the shared pool (exit 1, kind `resource`; reachable when statements run concurrently, as under `relate serve`). A one-shot CLI run meets only the first. Every other error repeats when the same statement runs again:

| Error                                                                                                                              | Exit code | `retryable` | Remedy                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Write-write conflict, kind `conflict`                                                                                              | 5         | `true`      | Run the statement again in a fresh transaction                                                                                 |
| `resource limit exceeded: concurrent-logical-workspace-limit limit=<bytes>`, kind `resource`, while other statements hold the pool | 1         | `true`      | Run it again once other statements finish, or raise `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit`                                     |
| `storage locked: <path>`, kind `locked`                                                                                            | 5         | `false`     | Wait for the other process to exit; a directory store can also be opened `--read-only` beside its writer, a `.rl` store cannot |
| `Error: query timed out after <duration>`                                                                                          | 7         | `false`     | Bound the statement with `LIMIT` or a narrower pattern, or raise `--timeout`                                                   |
| Any rejected statement: syntax, parameter, type, safe mode, read-only                                                              | 6         | `false`     | Fix the statement                                                                                                              |
| A runtime failure: missing store, I/O, capacity, `LOAD CSV`                                                                        | 1         | `false`     | Read `message` and fix the cause                                                                                               |

[Drive relate from an agent](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/drive-relate-from-an-agent/#branch-on-the-exit-code-and-the-error-object) shows the whole error object.

properties.heading: Turn on safe mode
properties.text:
`--safe` refuses statement shapes that agents commonly get wrong, before anything runs, as `SafeModeViolation` with exit code 6. It is off unless asked for: `--safe` or `RELATE_SAFE_MODE=1` turns it on, and `--no-safe` or `RELATE_SAFE_MODE=0` turns it off. `relate serve --safe` applies it to every statement the server runs.

| Safe mode refuses                                                                                                                              | It allows                                                                                                     | Fix                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE` or `MERGE` of a new named node without a label                                                                                        | Anonymous `()` endpoints of a relationship, and nodes bound earlier in the statement                          | Give the node a label: `CREATE (n:Person)`                                                    |
| A `MATCH` read whose final `RETURN` or `WITH` has no `LIMIT` and no reducing aggregate; `collect()` does not count, because it keeps every row | A `RETURN` of constants only, `SHOW` and `CALL`-only statements, and `MATCH … SET` or `MATCH … DELETE` writes | Add `LIMIT <n>`, or return only reducing aggregates, such as `count(*)`, with no grouping key |
| A remote `--load` source, with exit code 2, before any network request                                                                         | A local `--load` source, and `--fetch-params`                                                                 | Download the file, check its SHA-256, and load the local copy                                 |

A new named node without a label, on an in-memory store that nothing keeps:

```bash verify
relate --safe --mode envelope "CREATE (n {name: 'Eve'}) RETURN n.name AS name"
```

```text
syntax error: SafeModeViolation: This statement is not allowed in safe mode: CREATE or MERGE of a new node `n` without a label. Safe mode refuses shapes an agent commonly gets wrong — give the node a label, e.g. `CREATE (n:Person)`, so the write is self-describing. This is a policy, not a database limit; reopen without --safe to allow it.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: SafeModeViolation: This statement is not allowed in safe mode: CREATE or MERGE of a new node `n` without a label. Safe mode refuses shapes an agent commonly gets wrong — give the node a label, e.g. `CREATE (n:Person)`, so the write is self-describing. This is a policy, not a database limit; reopen without --safe to allow it.","retryable":false}}
```

A `collect()` with no `LIMIT`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --safe --mode envelope 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN collect(p.name) AS names'
```

```text
syntax error: SafeModeViolation: This statement is not allowed in safe mode: an unbounded read (`MATCH … RETURN` or `MATCH … WITH` without `LIMIT`). Safe mode refuses shapes an agent commonly gets wrong — add `LIMIT <n>` (collect() buffers every row, so it does not count as a bound even beside count() or another reducing aggregate; use count() for a bounded total). This is a policy, not a database limit; reopen without --safe to allow it.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: SafeModeViolation: This statement is not allowed in safe mode: an unbounded read (`MATCH … RETURN` or `MATCH … WITH` without `LIMIT`). Safe mode refuses shapes an agent commonly gets wrong — add `LIMIT <n>` (collect() buffers every row, so it does not count as a bound even beside count() or another reducing aggregate; use count() for a bounded total). This is a policy, not a database limit; reopen without --safe to allow it.","retryable":false}}
```

Safe mode judges the shape of a statement, not its effect. It cannot see the store's size, so it refuses an unbounded read of a small store too, and a labeled `MATCH (p:Person) DETACH DELETE p` passes it. A grouping aggregate such as `RETURN p.name, count(*)` is still unbounded and is refused. A `CALL { … }` subquery is checked on its own, so a `MATCH … RETURN` inside one needs its own `LIMIT`. For an agent that only reads, `--read-only` is the fence and `--safe` keeps its reads bounded.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
With `--read-only` and `--safe` together, a destructive statement from an agent fails and the store stays as it was:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --safe --mode envelope 'MATCH (p:Person) DETACH DELETE p'
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.","retryable":false}}
exit=6
```

All three people are still there, and a bounded count passes safe mode:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --safe --mode envelope 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.334542,"execute_ms":0.16141699999999998,"lex_parse_ms":0.030000000000000002,"lower_ms":0.04375,"parse_ms":0.108167,"plan_ms":0.055958,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.008792},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Connect over MCP
properties.text: This guide shows you how to connect an agent host to a relate store over [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) (the Model Context Protocol), with the store opened [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only). Every host on this page starts the same command, `relate serve --mcp stdio --database <store> --read-only`; only the file it lives in differs.

properties.heading: Add the server to your host
properties.text:
Each block starts relate on stdio against `graph.rl`, read-only. Host configuration formats change between releases. Each host's block follows that host's own documentation as of 2026-11-07.

A relative store path resolves against the directory the host starts the server in, which is not the same for every host. Blocks for a host that starts servers from your project folder use `./graph.rl`; the others use `<absolute-path>/graph.rl`, which works everywhere.

properties.heading: Choose a transport
properties.text:
`relate serve --mcp` takes either the keyword `stdio` or a port number. Both serve the same tools.

|                  | `--mcp stdio`                                                            | `--mcp <port>`                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Who starts it    | The host, as a child process, until it closes stdin                      | You, as a long-running process, until SIGINT or SIGTERM                                                        |
| Authentication   | None: the host spawned the process. `--auth` with stdio is a usage error | One basic-auth credential from `--auth` or `RELATE_AUTH`; without either, a generated token printed at startup |
| Where it listens | stdin and stdout                                                         | `127.0.0.1:<port>` by default (`--host`); plaintext HTTP, no TLS                                               |
| Which hosts      | Every host on this page                                                  | Hosts that connect to a URL                                                                                    |

Opened with `--read-only`, the server lists two tools, `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, and takes no writer lease. `write_cypher` is listed only when the store is writable. A directory store can be served read-only beside a process that writes it; a `.rl` file opens only while no writer holds it. [relate serve flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-serve) lists every flag.

properties.heading: Claude Code
properties.text:
A person adds the server with `claude mcp add`. An agent working in the repository writes the same server into `.mcp.json` at the project root, a file the person can review and commit.

#### At a terminal

```bash
claude mcp add relate -- relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

That adds the server for you in the current project (the default `local` scope, kept in `~/.claude.json`). With `--scope project`, Claude Code writes the same entry to `.mcp.json` at the project root instead, so it can be committed.

#### From an agent

```json title=".mcp.json"
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "relate": {
      "command": "relate",
      "args": ["serve", "--mcp", "stdio", "--database", "./graph.rl", "--read-only"]
    }
  }
}
```

To allow writes, remove `"--read-only"` from `args`.

The entry is the one `claude mcp add --scope project` writes. Claude Code asks before it uses a project-scoped server from `.mcp.json`, so the person approves the server the agent added.

`claude mcp list` shows each server with its health status, and `/mcp` inside a session shows its tools.

properties.heading: Claude Desktop
Cline
Codex
properties.text:
The file is `~/.codex/config.toml`, or `.codex/config.toml` in a trusted project. The Codex CLI, the IDE extension and the ChatGPT desktop app share it.

```toml title="config.toml"
[mcp_servers.relate]
command = "relate"
args = ["serve", "--mcp", "stdio", "--database", "<absolute-path>/graph.rl", "--read-only"]
```

To allow writes, remove `"--read-only"` from `args`.

The CLI writes the same entry:

```bash
codex mcp add relate -- relate serve --mcp stdio --database <absolute-path>/graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`. `codex mcp list` and `/mcp` show the configured servers.

properties.heading: Cursor
Gemini CLI
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**The host reports the server failed, and its log shows `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage error: database not found: <path>`.** The read-only open never creates a store, and a relative path resolved against a directory you did not expect. Put the store's absolute path in the block, or create the store first.

**The host cannot start `relate` at all.** The host's `PATH` does not include the directory relate is installed in (`~/.local/bin` for `install.sh`), which is common for desktop apps. Put the binary's absolute path in `command`.

**A write fails with `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query`, or `unknown tool 'write_cypher'`.** The store is open read-only, as configured. To let the agent write, remove `--read-only`; [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/) covers what to put in place first.

**HTTP answers `401 Unauthorized` or `415 Unsupported Media Type`.** A 401 carries `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="relate"`: the request has no credential, or the wrong one. A 415 means the `POST` had no `Content-Type`, or a browser-simple one (`text/plain` or a form type).

**`relate serve` exits 2 with an error that begins `Error: serve --mcp stdio skips auth`.** `--auth` applies to the port listeners only. Drop it from a stdio block.

properties.heading: OpenCode
Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH`: `relate --version` prints its version ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) that already exists, a `.rl` file or a directory. A read-only open never creates one.
- One of the hosts in [Add the server to your host](#add-the-server-to-your-host).

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Connect your agent to relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/): install, rehearse a change, then connect over MCP.
- [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/): read-only opens, safe mode, and backups before an agent writes.
- [MCP errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#mcp-read-query-only): every MCP refusal and JSON-RPC error code.
- [Run relate in a sandbox](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/run-in-a-sandbox/): what to allow when the host runs inside one.
- [CLI reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/): `relate serve` and its flags.
- [Use relate with the Claude Agent SDK](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/integrations/claude-agent-sdk/): the same read-only server, started by the SDK.

properties.heading: Serve over HTTP
properties.text:
If your host connects to a URL, or several clients share one server, start relate yourself on a port as in [Serve over HTTP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/mcp/#serve-over-http): `relate serve --mcp 8000 --database ./graph.rl --read-only` listens on `127.0.0.1:8000` and checks a credential from `RELATE_AUTH` or `--auth`, or else a token it generates for the user `relate` and saves beside the store as `<store>.auth-token`. The [MCP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/) describes the transport and every answer.

In another terminal, register the URL with your host. For Claude Code, `<credential>` is the base64 of `<user>:<password>` (`printf '%s' '<user>:<password>' | base64` prints it):

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http relate http://127.0.0.1:8000 --header "Authorization: Basic <credential>"
```

The server opened the store read-only, so this entry cannot write.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Check the server from a shell before a host is involved. This step creates a small `graph.rl` to check against, the shared example graph of three people and two projects:

```bash verify
relate --database ./graph.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

Then send three JSON-RPC messages the way a host does, one per line: `initialize`, `tools/list`, and a write sent to `read_cypher`. The `2>/dev/null` drops relate's startup lines on stderr:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"shell","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"CREATE (:Person {name: \"Eve\"})"}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","serverInfo":{"name":"relate-mcp","version":"1.0.1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"annotations":{"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true,"title":"Read Cypher"},"description":"Execute one read-only Cypher statement. Returns the result's rows. Write and schema (DDL) statements are rejected.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"parameters":{"default":{},"description":"The statement's parameters; a `rows` array feeds `$rows`.","type":"object"},"statement":{"description":"The Cypher statement.","type":"string"}},"required":["statement"],"type":"object"},"name":"read_cypher"},{"annotations":{"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true,"title":"Get Schema"},"description":"Get the schema of the graph store: node labels with their property keys and inferred types, and the relationship types between them. `sample_size` bounds how many nodes and relationships are examined per label (larger is slower but more accurate; -1 examines all).","inputSchema":{"properties":{"sample_size":{"description":"The sample size used to infer the graph schema. Larger samples are slower, but more accurate. Smaller samples are faster, but might miss information. -1 samples the whole graph.","type":"integer"}},"type":"object"},"name":"get_schema"}]}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"content":[{"text":"Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
```

The tool list names `read_cypher` and `get_schema` and no `write_cypher`, and the write came back as a tool error with the store unchanged. In the host, the same two tools appear in its server list (`/mcp` in Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI).

For the HTTP transport, the same `tools/list` with `curl`:

```bash
curl -s -u <user>:<password> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000 -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}'
```

properties.heading: What the agent sees
properties.text:
Once the host has started the server, the agent calls its tools with `tools/call` requests, and each reply carries the result as JSON text. The tryout below sends those calls to an in-browser database on this page that holds the same graph as the `graph.rl` that [Verify](#verify) creates, three people and two projects:

```cypher run name=graph
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

```json data=calls
{"calls": [
  {"tool": "get_schema", "arguments": {}},
  {"tool": "read_cypher", "arguments": {"statement": "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since", "parameters": {"project": "relate"}}},
  {"tool": "write_cypher", "arguments": {"statement": "CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})", "parameters": {"name": "Eve", "role": "engineer"}}}
]}
```

These calls ran when the page was recorded, on a database that holds what this page's cells write, through the same mapping the live tryout uses. Timings show as `<ms>`; live, each reply carries the timings of its own run. The server lists `write_cypher`, `read_cypher`, `get_schema`.

Live, the tryout starts as a server started `--read-only`, as every configuration on this page opens the store; with **Serve read-only** off it lists `write_cypher` as well.

**`get_schema`**: the request a host sends, then the reply.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{}}}
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"Person\":{\"count\":3,\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"role\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"relationships\":{\"KNOWS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Person\"]},\"MAINTAINS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"]},\"WORKS_ON\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"],\"properties\":{\"since\":{\"type\":\"Integer\"}}}},\"type\":\"node\"},\"Project\":{\"count\":2,\"properties\":{\"language\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"type\":\"node\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

| Label   | Nodes | Properties                       | Relationships out                                          |
| ------- | ----- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Person  | 3     | name (String), role (String)     | WORKS_ON to Project; KNOWS to Person; MAINTAINS to Project |
| Project | 2     | language (String), name (String) | -                                                          |

**`read_cypher`**: the request a host sends, then the reply.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since","parameters":{"project":"relate"}}}}
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"columnTypes\":[\"STRING\",\"INTEGER\"],\"columns\":[\"name\",\"since\"],\"elapsed_ms\":<ms>,\"error\":null,\"execute_ms\":<ms>,\"lex_parse_ms\":<ms>,\"lower_ms\":<ms>,\"notifications\":[{\"category\":\"PERFORMANCE\",\"code\":\"Relate.Notification.Statement.MissingIndex\",\"description\":\"the equality predicate on name filters :Project without a range index on (:Project {name})\",\"gql_status\":\"03C91\",\"operator_id\":1,\"remedy\":\"CREATE INDEX relate_Project__name FOR (n:Project) ON (n.name)\",\"severity\":\"INFORMATION\",\"title\":\"Missing index\"}],\"parse_ms\":<ms>,\"plan\":{\"profiled\":false,\"root\":{\"actual\":null,\"children\":[{\"actual\":null,\"children\":[],\"details\":\"(:Project)<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person)\",\"estimated_rows\":null,\"identifiers\":[],\"operator\":\"Expand\",\"warnings\":[{\"category\":\"PERFORMANCE\",\"code\":\"Relate.Notification.Statement.MissingIndex\",\"description\":\"the equality predicate on name filters :Project without a range index on (:Project {name})\",\"gql_status\":\"03C91\",\"remedy\":\"CREATE INDEX relate_Project__name FOR (n:Project) ON (n.name)\",\"severity\":\"INFORMATION\",\"title\":\"Missing index\"}]}],\"details\":\"2 item(s), ordered\",\"estimated_rows\":null,\"identifiers\":[],\"operator\":\"ProduceResults\",\"warnings\":[]},\"schema\":\"relate.plan/v1\",\"statement\":\"MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since\"},\"plan_cache\":\"miss\",\"plan_ms\":<ms>,\"result_generation_ms\":<ms>,\"rewrite_ms\":<ms>,\"rows\":[{\"name\":\"Grace\",\"since\":2023},{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"since\":2024}],\"stats\":{\"constraints_added\":0,\"constraints_removed\":0,\"indexes_added\":0,\"indexes_removed\":0,\"labels_added\":0,\"labels_removed\":0,\"nodes_created\":0,\"nodes_deleted\":0,\"properties_set\":0,\"relationships_created\":0,\"relationships_deleted\":0}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

| name  | since |
| ----- | ----- |
| Grace | 2023  |
| Ada   | 2024  |

**`write_cypher`**: the request a host sends, then the reply.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"write_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})","parameters":{"name":"Eve","role":"engineer"}}}}
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"columnTypes\":[],\"columns\":[],\"elapsed_ms\":<ms>,\"error\":null,\"execute_ms\":<ms>,\"lex_parse_ms\":<ms>,\"lower_ms\":<ms>,\"notifications\":[],\"parse_ms\":<ms>,\"plan\":{\"profiled\":false,\"root\":{\"actual\":null,\"children\":[],\"details\":\"(:Person)\",\"estimated_rows\":null,\"identifiers\":[],\"operator\":\"Create\",\"warnings\":[]},\"schema\":\"relate.plan/v1\",\"statement\":\"CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})\"},\"plan_cache\":\"miss\",\"plan_ms\":<ms>,\"result_generation_ms\":<ms>,\"rewrite_ms\":<ms>,\"rows\":[],\"stats\":{\"constraints_added\":0,\"constraints_removed\":0,\"indexes_added\":0,\"indexes_removed\":0,\"labels_added\":1,\"labels_removed\":0,\"nodes_created\":1,\"nodes_deleted\":0,\"properties_set\":2,\"relationships_created\":0,\"relationships_deleted\":0}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

Counters: `nodes_created` 1, `properties_set` 2, `labels_added` 1; `rows` is empty, as `write_cypher` returns counters.

**`write_cypher` on a server started `--read-only`**: it lists only `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, and answers a `write_cypher` call with a tool error before the engine sees the statement. This run is recorded from relate 1.0.1 (errors.json `mcp-unknown-tool`, replayed against the binary by `docs:cli-check`); the page quotes it as the binary printed it:

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"check","version":"0"}}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"write_cypher","arguments":{"query":"CREATE (:B)"}}}' | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","serverInfo":{"name":"relate-mcp","version":"1.0.1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"text":"unknown tool 'write_cypher'","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
```

Transport answers (HTTP 401, 403 and 415, the body cap, the header deadline) are not part of the tryout; the [MCP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/#errors-and-refusals) lists them.

Live: each call is a button that sends its `tools/call` request to the page's database in your browser and shows the request and the reply, built from the engine's result the way `relate serve --mcp` builds it, with the statement and parameters editable; "Serve read-only" drops `write_cypher` from the tool list, as `--read-only` does, and shows the engine's own refusal of the write on a read-only database beside the server's recorded answer.

In a browser the tryout starts with **Serve read-only** on, because every block in the next section opens the store read-only: the tool list has no `write_cypher`, and a call to it is refused before the engine sees it. Turned off, `write_cypher` writes to this page's in-browser database and nothing else. The rows and the plan come from the engine; apart from the timings, a host gets the same reply from `relate serve`.

properties.heading: Windsurf
Keep a diffable memory in the repo
properties.text: This guide shows you how to keep an agent's memory in the repository as a store a reviewer can read. A directory store created with the `json` [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec) writes the whole graph to one `graph.json` at every checkpoint, so the writes of an agent's session show up in `git diff` as added and removed [nodes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node) and [relationships](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship), and in a pull request as a change to `graph.json`. A bad fact is then caught in review, before it is merged.

properties.heading: Commit the store
properties.text:
```bash verify
git add .gitattributes memory
git commit -q -m "Seed the team memory"
```

Reading the store changes no file. A read-only open writes nothing and runs no checkpoint, so the working tree stays clean:

```bash verify
relate --database ./memory --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
git status --short
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["nodes"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"nodes":5}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.335791,"execute_ms":0.169542,"lex_parse_ms":0.03125,"lower_ms":0.043125,"parse_ms":0.107042,"plan_ms":0.050708,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.008208},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Create the memory store with the json codec
properties.text:
`--snapshot-format json` picks the codec when the store is created, and only then: it applies to an empty directory, and later opens read the codec from the store. This creates `memory/` and writes the shared example graph into it. The CLI checkpoints when a run that opened the store for writing exits:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./memory --snapshot-format json --mode envelope <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
ls -A memory memory/wal memory/.cypherlite/schema
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":3.681333,"execute_ms":3.3569590000000002,"lex_parse_ms":0.013166,"lower_ms":0.017207999999999998,"parse_ms":0.306375,"plan_ms":0.011708999999999999,"result_generation_ms":0.000209,"rewrite_ms":0.0005},"truncated":false}
memory:
.cypherlite
.cypherlite.lock
.cypherlite.writer
graph.json
manifest.json
wal

memory/.cypherlite/schema:
schema.cypher

memory/wal:
.cypherlite.lock
.cypherlite.writer
00000002.log
```

| File                                                                 | Holds                                                                                                                                                                 | In a diff                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `graph.json`                                                         | Every node with its id, labels and properties, every relationship with its type, its start and end node ids and its properties, then the index and constraint catalog | The facts that changed                        |
| `manifest.json`                                                      | The codec and the position of the last checkpoint                                                                                                                     | Two counters that move with each checkpoint   |
| `.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher`                                   | One `CREATE INDEX` or `CREATE CONSTRAINT` statement per entry: the [schema folder](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#schema-folder)                        | A schema change: a line added, or one removed |
| `wal/<n>.log`                                                        | The WAL; after a clean exit it holds only its 8-byte header                                                                                                           | Renamed by each session that commits          |
| `.cypherlite.lock`, `.cypherlite.writer`, and the same two in `wal/` | Markers that make the directory a store                                                                                                                               | Never change                                  |

Commit the whole directory. A read-only open of a fresh clone needs the markers and the WAL segment: without them it fails with `read-only open requires an existing database at <path>` or `read-only open requires an existing WAL at <path>/wal`.

Each node in `graph.json` is one object, and a relationship points at its nodes by id:

```bash verify
jq -c '.nodes[0], .relationships[0]' memory/graph.json
```

```text
{"id":0,"labels":["Person"],"properties":{"name":"Ada","role":"engineer"}}
{"id":0,"type":"WORKS_ON","start_node":0,"end_node":3,"properties":{"since":2024}}
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| What you see                                                                                                                                 | Cause                                                                                | Remedy                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A merge conflict in `graph.json` and `manifest.json`                                                                                         | Two branches each wrote the memory; git cannot merge two versions of a one-line file | Keep one side's `memory/` whole, then replay the other session's statements on it; `MERGE` writes only what is missing                                  |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage error: read-only open requires an existing WAL at <path>/wal` on a fresh clone                               | `wal/` was left out of the commit, or ignored                                        | Commit the whole store directory                                                                                                                        |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is json, requested parquet`, exit code 1                           | `--snapshot-format` given for a store that already exists                            | Drop the flag; to change the codec, `relate clone --to-snapshot-format`                                                                                 |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage error: schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/<file> differs from the schema this store's checkpoint persisted; …` | A file in the schema folder was edited, or resolved by hand in a merge               | Delete `.cypherlite/schema/` and open the store for writing once ([Keep the schema as files](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/schema-as-files/)) |

properties.heading: Know when it stops fitting
properties.text:
Each checkpoint rewrites the whole `graph.json`, and git keeps every version. Measured with relate 0.1.2, nodes with three short properties and one relationship each take about 170 bytes per pair: 167,702 bytes for 1,000 nodes and 999 relationships, 1,733,704 bytes for 10,000 nodes and 9,999 relationships. The file grows with the graph; the diff grows with the session.

| When                                                  | Keep                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A session changes a few dozen facts a person can read | The `json` codec, as on this page                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Reviewers want one file per entity                    | The `markdown` codec: one note per node with its properties and outgoing relationships in YAML frontmatter ([Open a store as an Obsidian vault](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/obsidian-vault/)). Its manifest records each note's modification time, so every checkpoint changes the manifest too |
| The graph is too large to read as text                | The default `parquet` codec, or a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store) (a `.rl` file), which git treats as binary; review the schema folder, and check facts with read-only statements                                                                       |

`relate clone --to-snapshot-format json <source> <destination>` converts an existing store, and the reverse goes back to `parquet`; [Clone and convert a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/clone-and-convert/) has the details.

properties.heading: Make the diff readable
properties.text:
relate writes `graph.json` as one line, so a plain line diff marks the whole file as changed. A git textconv driver prints it through `jq` before diffing, which puts each property on its own line. The driver changes what `git diff` shows, not what is stored:

```bash verify
printf 'memory/graph.json diff=relate-json\n' > .gitattributes
git config diff.relate-json.textconv "jq ."
```

`.gitattributes` is committed with the store; the `git config` line is per clone, so each reviewer runs it once. Without it, git still shows the change, as one replaced line. A hosted pull request view, such as GitHub's, has no clone's `git config`, so it does not run the driver either and shows the one-line file as replaced; reviewers read the change with `git diff` or `git show` in a clone that has the driver configured.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- git, and `jq` to print `graph.json` readably in a diff. GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 runner image includes `jq` 1.7.
- A new, empty directory to work in. The steps create a scratch repository there.

properties.heading: Record a session's writes
properties.text:
An agent's session is any run that opens the store for writing. Build its writes on `MERGE`, so a retried session matches what is already there and writes nothing. This one adds a project Ada works on, and the second run of the same statement changes nothing:

```bash verify
relate --database ./memory --mode envelope "MATCH (ada:Person {name: 'Ada'}) MERGE (docs:Project {name: 'docs', language: 'Markdown'}) MERGE (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(docs)"
relate --database ./memory --mode envelope "MATCH (ada:Person {name: 'Ada'}) MERGE (docs:Project {name: 'docs', language: 'Markdown'}) MERGE (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(docs)"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.5647499999999999,"execute_ms":1.341834,"lex_parse_ms":0.008166,"lower_ms":0.010416,"parse_ms":0.210459,"plan_ms":0.00725,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.0005},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.523666,"execute_ms":0.304166,"lex_parse_ms":0.007209,"lower_ms":0.009000000000000001,"parse_ms":0.206875,"plan_ms":0.007459,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.000334},"truncated":false}
note: write statement changed nothing; the graph is unchanged
```

A `SET` that writes a value a property already holds still counts as a write: that session checkpoints and renames the WAL segment, though `graph.json` stays the same. A `MERGE` pattern that carries the values, as here, keeps a replayed session silent.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Diffable memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#diffable-memory) in the capability catalog.
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#codecs): what each codec writes.
- [Keep the schema as files](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/schema-as-files/): the schema folder and its drift check.
- [Model agent memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/model-agent-memory/): the entities, episodes, and provenance to keep in it.
- [Know what an agent believed, and when](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/bitemporal-decisions/): a session that replays with no change.
- [WAL and checkpoints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/wal-and-checkpoints/): when a checkpoint runs.

properties.heading: Review the diff
properties.text:
Three files changed: the graph, the manifest's counters, and the WAL segment, which the session's checkpoint replaced with a new empty one:

```bash verify
git status --short
git diff --stat
```

```text
 M memory/graph.json
 M memory/manifest.json
 D memory/wal/00000002.log
?? memory/wal/00000003.log
 memory/graph.json       | 2 +-
 memory/manifest.json    | 4 ++--
 memory/wal/00000002.log | 1 -
 3 files changed, 3 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

The diff of `graph.json`, through the driver, is what a reviewer reads. The new node is id 5, and the new relationship runs from node 0 (Ada) to node 5:

```bash verify
git diff memory/graph.json
```

```text
diff --git a/memory/graph.json b/memory/graph.json
index 60b1684..fd6b7d3 100644
--- a/memory/graph.json
+++ b/memory/graph.json
@@ -50,6 +50,16 @@
         "language": "Gherkin",
         "name": "opencypher-tck"
       }
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 5,
+      "labels": [
+        "Project"
+      ],
+      "properties": {
+        "language": "Markdown",
+        "name": "docs"
+      }
     }
   ],
   "relationships": [
@@ -93,6 +103,15 @@
       "start_node": 0,
       "end_node": 1,
       "properties": {}
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 5,
+      "type": "WORKS_ON",
+      "start_node": 0,
+      "end_node": 5,
+      "properties": {
+        "since": 2026
+      }
     }
   ],
   "indexes": [],
@@ -123,8 +142,8 @@
     },
     "derived_constraints": {}
   },
-  "next_node_id": 5,
-  "next_rel_id": 5,
+  "next_node_id": 6,
+  "next_rel_id": 6,
   "graph_type": null,
   "read_only": false
 }
```

Commit the three files together, `git add memory`, so the graph, the manifest and the WAL always describe the same checkpoint. A schema change shows up in the same diff, in `graph.json`'s catalog and as a line of `schema.cypher`; [Keep the schema as files](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/schema-as-files/) covers that folder.

properties.heading: Start a repository
properties.text:
The steps work in a new repository with a local identity, so `git commit` runs anywhere. In your own repository, skip this step:

```bash verify
git init -q
git config user.name "relate docs"
git config user.email "docs@example.com"
```

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
After the commit, a read-only open of the store reads the new fact, and the tree stays clean:

```bash verify
git add memory
git commit -q -m "Ada works on docs"
relate --database ./memory --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(p:Project) RETURN p.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
git status --short
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER"],"columns":["project","since"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"project":"relate","since":2024},{"project":"docs","since":2026}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.471167,"execute_ms":0.25670800000000005,"lex_parse_ms":0.04,"lower_ms":0.044583000000000005,"parse_ms":0.13733399999999998,"plan_ms":0.067,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.009166},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Drive relate from an agent
properties.text: This guide shows you how to drive relate from an agent through the CLI: read the briefing, ask for the [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope), pass values as parameters, branch on the error object and the [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code), read the [row cap](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#row-cap), pick an output mode, and put a time bound on each statement. Each `relate` command is one process that runs one statement or a `;`-separated list and exits, so an agent calls it like any other shell tool.

properties.heading: Ask for the envelope
properties.text:
`--mode envelope` prints one compact JSON object per result set, on one line:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope 'MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(j:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, j.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING","INTEGER"],"columns":["person","project","since"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"person":"Grace","project":"opencypher-tck","since":2022},{"person":"Grace","project":"relate","since":2023},{"person":"Ada","project":"relate","since":2024}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.454708,"execute_ms":0.2725,"lex_parse_ms":0.034041999999999996,"lower_ms":0.042833,"parse_ms":0.113917,"plan_ms":0.059333000000000004,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.008042},"truncated":false}
```

| Key             | Holds                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`       | The column names in query order; present even when there are no rows                                                    |
| `columnTypes`   | One type name per column, taken from the first row; `ANY` when that value is null or there are no rows                  |
| `rows`          | One object per row, with keys sorted alphabetically; `columns` gives the query's order                                  |
| `truncated`     | `true` when the row cap cut the rows, otherwise `false`                                                                 |
| `rowCap`        | Present only when the row cap cut the rows: `{"kept": N, "total": M}`                                                   |
| `notifications` | The query notifications; always present, `[]` when there are none                                                       |
| `plan`          | Present only on an `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` result                                                                        |
| `planCache`     | Whether a cached plan served the statement, such as `miss` or `hit-template`                                            |
| `timings`       | The statement's phase timings in milliseconds, such as `elapsed_ms` and `execute_ms`; the values change from run to run |

The [output modes reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache) defines every timing key and `planCache` value.

An empty result keeps its columns, so "no rows" is distinguishable from "no output":

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Zed'}) RETURN p.role AS role"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["ANY"],"columns":["role"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.42174999999999996,"execute_ms":0.222083,"lex_parse_ms":0.031291,"lower_ms":0.047541,"parse_ms":0.127041,"plan_ms":0.063667,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.009458},"truncated":false}
```

A run of several statements prints one envelope per statement, one per line, so the output is JSON Lines. New keys may be added to the envelope; existing ones keep their names.

properties.heading: Bound each statement
properties.text:
`--timeout` cancels a statement that runs longer than the duration given (`500ms`, `10s`, `2m`; a bare number is seconds) and exits 7. Without it, a statement has no time bound:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --timeout 100ms 'UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS a UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS b RETURN count(*) AS pairs'
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: query timed out after 100ms
{"error":{"code":"timeout","exit_code":7,"kind":"execution","message":"query timed out after 100ms","retryable":false}}
exit=7
```

`--read-only` keeps a reading agent from writing. [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/) adds safe mode, backups before a write, and the permission matrix.

properties.heading: Branch on the exit code and the error object
properties.text:
A failed statement prints its message on stderr and exits with the code of its class. In `--mode envelope`, `--json`, and `--jsonl` it also prints an error object on stdout. This statement uses `$name` without binding it:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope 'MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p.role AS role'
echo "exit=$?"
```

The first line is stderr, the second is stdout:

```text
semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name","retryable":false}}
exit=6
```

The object's `code` names the class and always comes with the same exit code. `retryable` is `true` for a write-write conflict, which a fresh transaction can fix, and for a `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` refusal while other statements hold the workspace pool:

| Exit | `code`             | Remedy                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | `success`          | Read the rows; an empty result is still a success                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 1    | `fatal_error`      | Read `message`: a missing store, an I/O error, a capacity limit, a `LOAD CSV` path outside its directory. The same command fails again, except a workspace pool refusal with `retryable: true` (kind `resource`), which can run again once other statements finish                  |
| 2    | `usage_error`      | Fix the command line: an unknown flag or a bad value. No error object is printed                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 5    | `conflict`         | With `retryable: true` (kind `conflict`), run the statement again in a fresh transaction. With `retryable: false` (kind `locked`), another process holds the store: wait for it to exit. A directory store can also be opened `--read-only` beside its writer; a `.rl` store cannot |
| 6    | `validation_error` | Fix the statement: syntax, a missing parameter, a type error, a safe mode refusal, or a write on a read-only store                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 7    | `timeout`          | Bound the work with `LIMIT` or a narrower pattern, or raise `--timeout`                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

A syntax error adds `column` and `source`, which point at the failing token. A run of several statements that stops partway adds `statement`, `statements`, and `committed`, so the agent knows whether earlier statements already changed the store:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope 'RETURN 1 AS a; RETRN 2; RETURN 3 AS c'
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["a"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"a":1}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.315959,"execute_ms":0.17925,"lex_parse_ms":0.019666,"lower_ms":0.028791,"parse_ms":0.088292,"plan_ms":0.039541,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.006834},"truncated":false}
syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "RETRN"
  RETRN 2
  ^
statement 2 of 3 failed; 1 completed and committed; 1 not run
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","column":1,"committed":1,"exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: parse error: unexpected token \"RETRN\"   RETRN 2   ^","retryable":false,"source":"RETRN 2","statement":2,"statements":3}}
exit=6
```

The first statement printed its envelope and committed, the second failed, and the third never ran. The [exit codes and errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/) lists every field.

properties.heading: Create the example graph
properties.text:
The steps use one small graph: three people and the two projects they work on. This writes a new single-file store, `team.rl`, from a seed script:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
```

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < team.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":3.2087079999999997,"execute_ms":2.911125,"lex_parse_ms":0.01425,"lower_ms":0.021417,"parse_ms":0.279333,"plan_ms":0.012667,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.0005},"truncated":false}
```

Every later command on this page opens `team.rl` with `--read-only`, which opens the store [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only): relate never writes it, and a write fails with exit code 6.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <name>`** (exit code 6): the statement uses `$<name>` and no `--param` or `--fetch-params` binds it. Pass `--param <name>=<value>` ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-parameter-missing)).
- **A syntax error whose `source` has a gap where `$<name>` was** (exit code 6): the statement was in double quotes, so the shell replaced `$<name>` with an empty string before relate saw it. With the parameter inside a map, the message starts `syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "}" (RightBrace)`. Single-quote the statement.
- **`warning: result truncated to 100 rows (the statement returned <n>); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows`** (exit code 0): the row cap cut the output. Pass `--max-rows 0`, or bound the statement with `LIMIT` or an aggregate ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-row-cap-warning)).
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`** on stderr, with the error object message `storage locked: <path>` (exit code 5, `retryable: false`): another process has the store open. Wait for it to exit; a directory store can also be opened `--read-only` beside its writer ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked)).

properties.heading: Pass values as parameters
properties.text:
`--param N=V` binds the parameter `$N`, and repeats for each parameter. `V` is parsed as JSON, so it can be a number, `true`, a quoted string, an array, or a map; a bare word is a string. Single quotes around the statement keep the shell from expanding `$names` before relate sees it:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope --param 'names=["Ada","Noor"]' --param since=2023 'MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(j:Project) WHERE p.name IN $names AND w.since >= $since RETURN p.name AS person, j.name AS project'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING"],"columns":["person","project"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"person":"Ada","project":"relate"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.440333,"execute_ms":0.248584,"lex_parse_ms":0.033417,"lower_ms":0.049166,"parse_ms":0.12237500000000001,"plan_ms":0.060208,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.008542000000000001},"truncated":false}
```

`--fetch-params N=SRC` reads a JSON file, or fetches an `http` or `https` URL, and binds the whole document as `$N`. In this example the document is a map, read from a file the first command writes:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' '{"names": ["Grace"], "since": 2022}' > filter.json
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope --fetch-params filter=./filter.json 'MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(j:Project) WHERE p.name IN $filter.names AND w.since >= $filter.since RETURN p.name AS person, j.name AS project ORDER BY project'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING"],"columns":["person","project"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"person":"Grace","project":"opencypher-tck"},{"person":"Grace","project":"relate"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.475125,"execute_ms":0.269167,"lex_parse_ms":0.036791,"lower_ms":0.050665999999999996,"parse_ms":0.131708,"plan_ms":0.064667,"result_generation_ms":0.000334,"rewrite_ms":0.008792},"truncated":false}
```

A fetch is capped at 64 MiB and 60 seconds and has no URL allowlist. [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/#control-network-egress) lists it with the other flags that reach the network.

properties.heading: Pick an output mode
properties.text:
Without `--mode`, the output depends on where stdout goes: the human table on a terminal, JSON Lines in a pipe, and TOON in a pipe under [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode). TOON is a compact table: one `rows[N]{columns}:` header line, then one line per row, with nested values as inline JSON, closed by the statement's `timings:` and `planCache:` entries.

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate --database ./team.rl --read-only 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role ORDER BY name'
```

```text
rows[3]{name,role}:
  Ada,engineer
  Grace,engineer
  Noor,maintainer
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":0.43470899999999996,"execute_ms":0.252333,"lex_parse_ms":0.032792,"lower_ms":0.044083,"parse_ms":0.11637499999999999,"plan_ms":0.056542,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.008208}
planCache:
  miss
```

To compare the modes on one result, run a statement in the terminal on this page. It runs in your browser on an empty database opened read-only, as `relate --read-only` opens one, and prints the bytes relate prints in `table`, `envelope`, `jsonl` and `toon`, with the exit code; the timings it prints are the engine's in the page, so their numbers differ from a run of the binary. The `row` column holds a map, which TOON and JSON Lines print as inline JSON and the table prints in Cypher's notation:

```cypher run name=pairs
UNWIND [{name: 'Ada', since: 2024}, {name: 'Grace', since: 2023}] AS p RETURN p.name AS person, p.since AS since, p AS row
```

```table
| person  | since | row                          |
|---------|-------|------------------------------|
| "Ada"   | 2024  | {name: "Ada", since: 2024}   |
| "Grace" | 2023  | {name: "Grace", since: 2023} |
2 rows
```

The statement as relate 1.0.1 prints it in four of its output modes, rendered from this page's recorded result by the terminal's renderers, which match the relate 1.0.1 binary byte for byte on the recorded runs, timing values aside. The recording keeps no timings, so each one shows as `<ms>`; relate prints the milliseconds of its own run, and the live terminal prints the engine's. Exit code 0, as relate 1.0.1 returns it.

`--mode table` prints six lines on stdout:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode table "UNWIND [{name: 'Ada', since: 2024}, {name: 'Grace', since: 2023}] AS p RETURN p.name AS person, p.since AS since, p AS row"
```

```text
+---------+-------+------------------------------+
| person  | since | row                          |
+---------+-------+------------------------------+
| "Ada"   | 2024  | {name: "Ada", since: 2024}   |
| "Grace" | 2023  | {name: "Grace", since: 2023} |
+---------+-------+------------------------------+
```

`--mode envelope` prints one line on stdout:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode envelope "UNWIND [{name: 'Ada', since: 2024}, {name: 'Grace', since: 2023}] AS p RETURN p.name AS person, p.since AS since, p AS row"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER","MAP"],"columns":["person","since","row"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"person":"Ada","row":{"name":"Ada","since":2024},"since":2024},{"person":"Grace","row":{"name":"Grace","since":2023},"since":2023}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":<ms>,"execute_ms":<ms>,"lex_parse_ms":<ms>,"lower_ms":<ms>,"parse_ms":<ms>,"plan_ms":<ms>,"result_generation_ms":<ms>,"rewrite_ms":<ms>},"truncated":false}
```

`--mode jsonl` prints two lines on stdout:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode jsonl "UNWIND [{name: 'Ada', since: 2024}, {name: 'Grace', since: 2023}] AS p RETURN p.name AS person, p.since AS since, p AS row"
```

```text
{"person":"Ada","row":{"name":"Ada","since":2024},"since":2024}
{"person":"Grace","row":{"name":"Grace","since":2023},"since":2023}
```

`--mode toon` prints seven lines on stdout:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode toon "UNWIND [{name: 'Ada', since: 2024}, {name: 'Grace', since: 2023}] AS p RETURN p.name AS person, p.since AS since, p AS row"
```

```text
rows[2]{person,since,row}:
  Ada,2024,{"name":"Ada","since":2024}
  Grace,2023,{"name":"Grace","since":2023}
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":<ms>,"execute_ms":<ms>,"lex_parse_ms":<ms>,"lower_ms":<ms>,"parse_ms":<ms>,"plan_ms":<ms>,"result_generation_ms":<ms>,"rewrite_ms":<ms>}
planCache:
  miss
```

Under a detected agent harness, relate prints at most 100 rows per statement; this statement returns two rows, so the cap leaves it whole.

Live: the statement runs in your browser on an empty read-only database, as `relate --read-only` opens one, and the pane shows what relate prints in the mode you pick, with the exit code and, under "Run as an agent harness", the row cap; the statement can be edited or swapped for a preset.

Turn on "Run as an agent harness", pick the 250-row preset and run it to see the cap cut the rows and the warning on stderr; the exit code stays 0.

An explicit `--mode` always wins, so a pipeline that parses JSON pins it:

| Mode       | Prints                                                                          | A row-cap cut shows as                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `envelope` | One JSON object per result set, with column types                               | `"truncated": true` and `rowCap`                |
| `jsonl`    | One JSON object per row; `--timings` adds one timing line per statement         | A `{"rowCap": …}` line after the rows           |
| `json`     | One JSON object per result set, the rows in `data`; one compact line when piped | A `rowCap` key beside `data`                    |
| `toon`     | A header line, one line per row, then `timings:` and `planCache:` entries       | A `rowCap:` entry before `timings:`             |
| `markdown` | A GitHub-flavored Markdown table                                                | A closing `> truncated: N of M rows shown` line |
| `csv`      | CSV; a value starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a leading `'`              | The stderr warning only                         |
| `table`    | The human table                                                                 | The stderr warning only                         |

Agent mode turns on the 100-row cap and the TOON default. It follows one order: `--agent-mode` or `--no-agent-mode`, then `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1` or `0`, then harness detection. The flag and the variable print a one-line notice on stderr; detection is silent. The [agent mode reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#detection) lists the variables that count as a harness.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A shell the agent can run commands in. No server and no configuration file are involved.

properties.heading: Read the briefing
properties.text:
`relate agent-context` prints the commands, query-run flags, and exit codes of the binary that is installed, so an agent works from the version it has rather than one it remembers. `relate agent-context <command>` prints one command's synopsis, flags, and examples.

The briefing ends with the exit codes, the part an agent branches on:

```bash verify
relate agent-context | tail -7
```

```text
Exit codes:
  0  success: success, including an empty result
  1  fatal_error: runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error
  2  usage_error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional
  5  conflict: write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener
  6  validation_error: the statement is rejected: syntax, semantic or type error
  7  timeout: a statement exceeded --timeout
```

Before them it lists the twelve commands and every query-run flag; the [agent quickstart](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#read-the-briefing) shows the whole output.

properties.heading: Read the row cap
properties.text:
Under a detected agent harness, with stdout not a terminal, relate prints at most 100 rows per statement. A cut result says so three ways: a warning on stderr, `"truncated": true` with a `rowCap` object in the envelope, and a `{"rowCap": …}` line after the rows in `--mode jsonl`, just before the statement's timing line. The exit code stays 0. In this command `CLAUDECODE=1` stands in for a harness, and `grep` keeps the `rowCap` line:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate --mode jsonl 'UNWIND range(1, 250) AS x RETURN x' 2>/dev/null | grep '"rowCap"'
```

```text
{"rowCap":{"kept":100,"total":250}}
```

`--max-rows N` sets the cap everywhere, a terminal included, and `--max-rows 0` lifts it. With a cap of 2, the warning comes first on stderr, then the envelope:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate --mode envelope --max-rows 2 'UNWIND range(1, 250) AS x RETURN x'
```

```text
warning: result truncated to 2 rows (the statement returned 250); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["x"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rowCap":{"kept":2,"total":250},"rows":[{"x":1},{"x":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.494834,"execute_ms":0.344042,"lex_parse_ms":0.023459,"lower_ms":0.038375,"parse_ms":0.095,"plan_ms":0.047416,"result_generation_ms":0.001209,"rewrite_ms":0.007292},"truncated":true}
```

The cap limits what is printed, not what the engine computes: the engine builds the whole result first. A `LIMIT` or an aggregate in the statement bounds the work itself.

properties.text:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people'
echo "exit=$?"
```
