properties.heading: Install the agent skill
properties.text: This guide shows you how to install the relate agent skill in one of three ways: with the relate CLI's installer, with the skills CLI from the website, or as a manual copy checked against published checksums. The [skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#skill) is a `SKILL.md` cheat sheet and a set of reference files that a coding agent reads before it uses relate: the CLI and its flags, output modes, [exit codes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code), Cypher, the clients, and the agent rules. All three install the same `SKILL.md`; the relate CLI and a manual copy also install the 15 reference files.

properties.heading: Choose a way to install
properties.text:
| Way                                                 | Installs                              | Checked by                                                                                        | Network  |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `relate skill install`                              | `SKILL.md` and the 15 reference files | The bytes come from inside the binary; `relate skill check` compares an installed copy with them  | None     |
| `npx skills add https://relatedb.ai --skill relate` | `SKILL.md` only                       | The skills CLI (1.7.6) checks the `sha256:` digest of `SKILL.md` in the website's discovery index | Required |
| Manual copy                                         | `SKILL.md` and the 15 reference files | A script compares each file with its SHA-256 in `/docs/docs-artifacts.json`                       | Required |

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Error: skill: no supported agents detected`** (exit code 1): `relate skill install` found none of the directories in the agent table. Its second line, `valid agents: claude-code, cursor, windsurf, copilot, antigravity, gemini-cli, cline, codex, pi, opencode, junie`, lists the names `--agent` accepts; pass one of them.
- **`Error: skill: unknown agent: '<name>'`** (exit code 2): `--agent` names an agent relate does not know. Use a name from the `valid agents:` line ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-skill-unknown-agent)).
- **`Error: skill: refusing to touch <dest>: no .relate-installed marker present (directory was not created by relate); pass --force to override`** (exit code 1): a `relate` directory that relate did not write is in the way. Move it aside, or pass `--force` to replace it ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-skill-refusing-to-touch)).
- **`relate skill check` prints `drifted`** (exit code 1): an installed copy differs from the binary's bundle, for example after the binary was replaced without `relate upgrade`. `relate skill install` rewrites it.

properties.heading: Install a task skill
properties.text:
Besides the CLI bundle, the website publishes five task skills, one per task family. Each cites the docs pages and cookbook recipes it draws on, and every Cypher statement in it runs on the WebAssembly build the site ships. `relate skill install` does not install them; the binary carries its own bundle only.

| Skill                               | For                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate-agent-memory`               | Long-term agent memory: entities, episodes, facts with provenance and two time axes                |
| `relate-graphrag`                   | Hybrid retrieval: vector and full-text search fused by reciprocal rank, then a graph hop           |
| `relate-schema-design`              | Labels, relationship types, constraints, indexes, schema discovery and the schema folder           |
| `relate-query-tuning`               | `EXPLAIN`, `PROFILE`, the planner's notifications and their remedies, indexes and traversal bounds |
| `relate-migrate-from-vector-search` | Moving records and embeddings from a vector-only store, and checks that nothing was lost           |

The skills CLI installs one by name, the same way as the bundle. For the agent memory skill:

```bash
npx skills add https://relatedb.ai --skill relate-agent-memory
```

As with the bundle, the index entry is `SKILL.md` alone; each task skill's `SKILL.md` names the absolute URL of every reference file, at `https://relatedb.ai/skills/<name>/references/<file>.md`. A URL with a path, such as `https://relatedb.ai/skills/relate-graphrag`, does not select a skill: the skills CLI finds no discovery index under that path and installs nothing. For a copy by hand, put the files that `/docs/docs-artifacts.json` lists under `/skills/<name>/` in a directory named after the skill, beside the `relate` directory below.

properties.heading: Install by hand
properties.text:
A manual copy is a directory named `relate`, holding `SKILL.md` and `references/`, under a skills directory the agent reads. In a project, that is `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`, `.codex/skills/`, or `.agents/skills/`. In your home directory, it is the directory in the agent table. These commands copy the bundle into the current project for Claude Code:

```bash
base=https://relatedb.ai/skills/relate
dest=.claude/skills/relate
mkdir -p "$dest/references"
curl -sSfL "$base/SKILL.md" -o "$dest/SKILL.md"
for f in agent-safety client-c client-extensions client-go client-java client-javascript client-python client-swift client-wasm operations pull push run-git-to-graph spatial vector; do
  curl -sSfL "$base/references/$f.md" -o "$dest/references/$f.md"
done
```

A download by hand has no digest check of its own. `/docs/docs-artifacts.json` lists the SHA-256 of every skill file the website serves; it is not signed yet, and a signature by the release key, `docs-artifacts.json.sig`, is planned beside it. This script compares each downloaded file with its entry there:

```bash
manifest="$(mktemp)"
curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/docs/docs-artifacts.json -o "$manifest"
python3 - "$manifest" "$dest" <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, pathlib, sys
want = {a["path"]: a["sha256"] for a in json.loads(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())["artifacts"]}
dest = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
files = [dest / "SKILL.md", *sorted((dest / "references").glob("*.md"))]
bad = [str(f) for f in files if hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != want.get("/skills/relate/" + f.relative_to(dest).as_posix())]
print("mismatch: " + ", ".join(bad) if bad else f"{len(files)} files match docs-artifacts.json")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
PY
rm -f "$manifest"
```

When every file matches, the script prints `16 files match docs-artifacts.json` and exits 0. On any mismatch it prints `mismatch:` followed by the files that differ, and exits 1. A file that differs is not the one the website published, so delete the copy and download it again.

properties.heading: Install with the relate CLI
properties.text:
`relate skill install` copies the skill into the skills directory of every agent it detects in your home directory; an agent counts as detected when its configuration directory exists. [relate skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/skill/#agents-and-paths) lists the eleven agents, each one's `--agent` name, how it is detected, and where the skill goes.

To install for every detected agent at once:

```bash
relate skill install
```

`--agent <name>` targets one agent, and installs for it even when its directory does not exist yet. For Claude Code:

```bash verify
relate skill install --agent claude-code
```

The path starts with your home directory, shown as `<home>`:

```text
installed relate skill into <home>/.claude/skills/relate
```

Then `relate skill list` prints each detected agent's install state and path. Claude Code's directory exists now, so it is detected:

```bash verify
relate skill list
```

```text
claude-code: installed (<home>/.claude/skills/relate)
```

The installer stamps the binary's version into the `version:` line of `SKILL.md` and writes a `.relate-installed` marker beside it. The marker is how relate knows the directory is its own: it replaces a marked directory or an earlier relate skill, and refuses to overwrite anything else. After `relate upgrade` replaces the binary, it runs `relate skill install` again. If any detected agent already holds a relate copy, this happens without asking and writes into every detected agent, including one detected since the last install. If none holds a copy, it asks first on a terminal, prints a hint otherwise, and `--yes` installs without asking. A `relate` directory that holds neither the marker nor an earlier relate skill is left untouched.

properties.heading: Install with the skills CLI
properties.text:
The website publishes the same skill under the Agent Skills discovery paths, so the skills CLI can install it before relate is on the machine:

```bash
npx skills add https://relatedb.ai --skill relate
```

As of skills 1.7.6 (read and run 2026-11-07), the `https://` prefix is required: given a bare `relatedb.ai`, the skills CLI does not look for the website's discovery index. It reads `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`, checks the `sha256:` digest of `SKILL.md` against it, and writes `SKILL.md` where its own settings say.

The index lists six skills, this bundle and the five task skills listed in `/skill.md`, and `--skill relate` picks this one. Its entry is `SKILL.md`, so this way installs that file without `references/`. The links in `SKILL.md` that point into `references/` then name files that are not on disk. Each reference file is published at `https://relatedb.ai/skills/relate/references/<name>.md`, and the relate CLI and a manual copy both put the reference files on disk.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- For the CLI installer: relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)). The skill ships inside the binary, so this way needs no network.
- For the skills CLI: Node.js with `npx`, and network access to `relatedb.ai`.
- For a manual copy: `curl` and `python3`, and network access to `relatedb.ai`.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Connect your agent to relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/): install a pinned relate and its skill, then rehearse a change.
- [Drive relate from an agent](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/drive-relate-from-an-agent/): the machine output, error object, and exit codes the skill summarizes.
- [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/): read-only opens, safe mode, and the permission matrix.
- [CLI reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/): every `relate skill` action and flag.
- [The skill's landing file, `/skill.md`](https://relatedb.ai/skill.md): the bundle's URLs, its discovery index, and its checksums.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The skill is installed when `SKILL.md` sits in a directory the agent reads. For a copy in a home skills directory, `relate skill check` compares it with the bundle inside the binary:

```bash verify
relate skill check
```

```text
claude-code: up to date (<home>/.claude/skills/relate)
```

`relate skill check` exits 0 when every installed copy matches, and 1 when one has drifted, with a `missing:`, `differs:`, or `extra:` line per file. A manual copy in a home skills directory gets the same check, and `relate skill list` reports it as `installed (legacy bundle)`. A copy in a project directory is outside what `relate skill list` and `relate skill check` read, so check the files themselves. The installed directory holds the marker, `SKILL.md`, and `references`:

```bash verify
ls -A "$HOME/.claude/skills/relate"
```

```text
.relate-installed
SKILL.md
references
```

The frontmatter names the skill and the relate version it describes, which matches what `relate --version` reports:

```bash verify
grep -E '^(name|version):' "$HOME/.claude/skills/relate/SKILL.md"
```

```text
name: relate
version: 1.0.1
```

For a project copy, the same two commands on `.claude/skills/relate` show `SKILL.md` and `references` without the marker, and the same two lines.

properties.heading: Model agent memory
properties.text: This guide shows you how to model an agent's long-term memory as a graph: the entities it knows about, the episodes it learned things in, and facts that carry two time ranges and a link to their evidence. The cells on this page run in order on one in-memory [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), so by the end the page holds a working memory you can query.

properties.heading: Ask what the agent believed
properties.text:
The two time axes answer two questions about 15 March: who reviewed releases then, as the agent knows now, and who the agent thought did, at the time.

```json data=asof
{"slot": "relate/release-reviewer", "on": "2026-03-15T00:00:00Z"}
```

```cypher run name=asof params=asof
MATCH (f:Fact {slot: $slot})
WITH datetime($on) AS t, collect(f) AS facts
RETURN [x IN facts WHERE x.validFrom <= t AND (x.validTo IS NULL OR t < x.validTo) | x.text] AS trueOn,
       [x IN facts WHERE x.recordedAt <= t AND (x.closedAt IS NULL OR t < x.closedAt) | x.text] AS believedOn
```

```table
| trueOn                               | believedOn                             |
|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| ["Ada reviews each relate release."] | ["Grace reviews each relate release."] |
1 row
```

The answers differ, and both are right. That is the audit trail for "why did the agent ask Grace on 15 March?".

The slot's two facts, with their four times, show why on both axes. Ada's fact holds from 10 March, but the agent wrote it only on 20 March, and until then it still believed Grace's:

```cypher run name=slot-facts params=asof
MATCH (f:Fact {slot: $slot})
RETURN f.text AS fact, f.validFrom AS validFrom, f.validTo AS validTo,
       f.recordedAt AS recordedAt, f.closedAt AS closedAt
ORDER BY f.recordedAt
```

```table
| fact                                 | validFrom              | validTo                | recordedAt             | closedAt               |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| "Grace reviews each relate release." | "2026-01-05T00:00:00Z" | "2026-03-10T00:00:00Z" | "2026-03-02T10:00:00Z" | "2026-03-20T09:00:00Z" |
| "Ada reviews each relate release."   | "2026-03-10T00:00:00Z" | null                   | "2026-03-20T09:00:00Z" | null                   |
2 rows
```

The `slot-facts` cell's recorded rows, 2 rows, each on its valid time (`validFrom` to `validTo`) and its record time (`recordedAt` to `closedAt`); `null` is an open end.

| fact                               | validFrom            | validTo              | recordedAt           | closedAt             |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------- |
| Grace reviews each relate release. | 2026-01-05T00:00:00Z | 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z | 2026-03-02T10:00:00Z | 2026-03-20T09:00:00Z |
| Ada reviews each relate release.   | 2026-03-10T00:00:00Z | null                 | 2026-03-20T09:00:00Z | null                 |

Live: the drawing reads its rows again from each run of the statement it draws on the page's database in your browser, so an edit to the statement or its parameters redraws it; Tab reaches the marks and the arrow keys move along a lane and between lanes, each mark read out with its values; where the page names an as-of statement, a time slider runs that statement again with the time as its parameter and lights up the rows it returns.

![The slot-facts cell's rows on both time axes, as recorded](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/model-agent-memory/element-timeline-1-light.svg)

properties.heading: Create the schema
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**A write fails with ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `entity_key` uniqueness``.** Two writes created the same entity. Write entities with `MERGE (e:Entity {key: $key})` so a repeat finds the existing node.

**A write fails with `type error: vector() dimension does not match list`.** An embedding's length differs from the one the statement names. Make the `vector(…, <dimensions>, FLOAT32)` call and the index's `vector.dimensions` match your model.

**Recall fails with `type error: VectorIndexDimensionalityMismatch`.** The question's vector has a different length from the index. Embed the question with the same model as the facts.

**Recall returns fewer than `k` rows.** The `f.closedAt IS NULL` filter sits after `SEARCH`, so it filters the `k` rows the index already chose. Inside the search, on a property declared with `WITH [...]`, it runs before the `LIMIT`.

**Recall returns closed facts.** The search has no `WHERE f.closedAt IS NULL`. Put it inside the search's parentheses.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- Cypher reads and writes with parameters, as in [Your first graph](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/first-graph/).
- Embeddings from your model for each fact and each question. The examples use 4-dimension vectors written by hand, so their results never change; a real model's vectors have hundreds of dimensions.

properties.heading: Recall
properties.text:
A recall takes the question's embedding, finds the nearest current facts, and brings back what each is about, the episode it came from, and what it replaced. The question is "Who reviews relate releases?".

```json data=question
{"vector": [0.88, 0.12, 0.02, 0.22], "k": 2}
```

```cypher run name=recall params=question
MATCH (f:Fact)
SEARCH f IN (VECTOR INDEX fact_embedding FOR $vector WHERE f.closedAt IS NULL LIMIT $k) SCORE AS score
MATCH (f)-[:FROM]->(ep:Episode)
RETURN f.text AS memory, round(score, 4) AS score,
       COLLECT { MATCH (f)-[:ABOUT]->(e:Entity) RETURN e.name ORDER BY e.name } AS about,
       ep.kind AS learnedFrom, ep.text AS evidence,
       COLLECT { MATCH (f)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old:Fact) RETURN old.text } AS replaced
ORDER BY score DESC
```

```table
| memory                                       | score  | about              | learnedFrom | evidence                                            | replaced                               |
|----------------------------------------------|--------|--------------------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| "Ada reviews each relate release."           | 0.999  | ["Ada", "relate"]  | "tool_call" | "read_file CODEOWNERS: release/ @ada"               | ["Grace reviews each relate release."] |
| "Noor triages new relate issues on Mondays." | 0.6178 | ["Noor", "relate"] | "message"   | "Noor goes through new relate issues every Monday." | []                                     |
2 rows
```

Grace's fact is the nearest by meaning, and it does not come back: the filter inside the search drops closed facts before the `LIMIT`. The answer names the tool call it rests on, so an agent can quote its evidence.

properties.heading: Record a correction
properties.text:
On 20 March, in session `s2`, a tool call reads the repository's owners file and finds that Ada took over release review on 10 March. The agent was wrong for ten days, and now it knows.

```json data=correction
{
  "episode": {"id": "e3", "session": "s2", "kind": "tool_call", "at": "2026-03-20T09:00:00Z",
              "text": "read_file CODEOWNERS: release/ @ada", "mentions": ["ada", "relate"]},
  "fact": {"id": "f3", "text": "Ada reviews each relate release.", "slot": "relate/release-reviewer",
           "about": ["ada", "relate"], "validFrom": "2026-03-10T00:00:00Z", "embedding": [0.85, 0.15, 0.05, 0.25]}
}
```

One statement writes the episode and the new fact, then closes the current fact in the same slot: its `validTo` becomes the new fact's `validFrom`, its `closedAt` the time the agent learned it.

```cypher run name=correct params=correction
WITH $episode AS e, $fact AS f
CREATE (ep:Episode {id: e.id, session: e.session, kind: e.kind, at: datetime(e.at), text: e.text})
CREATE (new:Fact {id: f.id, text: f.text, slot: f.slot,
                  validFrom: datetime(f.validFrom), recordedAt: ep.at,
                  embedding: vector(f.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)})-[:FROM]->(ep)
WITH ep, new, e, f
CALL (ep, e) { UNWIND e.mentions AS key MATCH (n:Entity {key: key}) CREATE (ep)-[:MENTIONS]->(n) }
CALL (new, f) { UNWIND f.about AS key MATCH (n:Entity {key: key}) CREATE (new)-[:ABOUT]->(n) }
MATCH (old:Fact {slot: new.slot}) WHERE old <> new AND old.closedAt IS NULL
SET old.validTo = new.validFrom, old.closedAt = new.recordedAt
CREATE (new)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old)
RETURN new.text AS current, old.text AS replaced, old.validTo AS validTo, old.closedAt AS closedAt
```

```table
| current                            | replaced                             | validTo                | closedAt               |
|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| "Ada reviews each relate release." | "Grace reviews each relate release." | "2026-03-10T00:00:00Z" | "2026-03-20T09:00:00Z" |
1 row · nodes created: 2, relationships created: 6, properties set: 13, labels added: 2
```

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Pick up where the last session left off](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/agent-memory/): sessions, slots, and supersession on a larger extraction.
- [Know what an agent believed, and when](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/bitemporal-decisions/): valid time and record time through late corrections and a rejection.
- [Tool-call provenance](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/tool-call-provenance/): every tool call recorded in the graph it touched.
- [Hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/): vector and full-text search fused in one statement.
- [Search by vector similarity](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/): vector indexes and `SEARCH` in depth.
- [Use relate with LangGraph](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/integrations/langgraph/): a reduced form of this model behind a LangGraph agent's tools.

properties.heading: Remember a session
properties.text:
In session `s1` the agent hears two messages and extracts one fact from each. The extraction is your model's job; this block holds its output.

```json data=session
{
  "episodes": [
    {"id": "e1", "session": "s1", "kind": "message", "at": "2026-03-02T10:00:00Z",
     "text": "Grace does the release review for relate.", "mentions": ["grace", "relate"]},
    {"id": "e2", "session": "s1", "kind": "message", "at": "2026-03-02T10:05:00Z",
     "text": "Noor goes through new relate issues every Monday.", "mentions": ["noor", "relate"]}
  ],
  "facts": [
    {"id": "f1", "episode": "e1", "text": "Grace reviews each relate release.", "slot": "relate/release-reviewer",
     "about": ["grace", "relate"], "validFrom": "2026-01-05T00:00:00Z", "embedding": [0.9, 0.1, 0.0, 0.2]},
    {"id": "f2", "episode": "e2", "text": "Noor triages new relate issues on Mondays.", "slot": "relate/triage",
     "about": ["noor", "relate"], "validFrom": "2026-02-02T00:00:00Z", "embedding": [0.1, 0.9, 0.2, 0.0]}
  ]
}
```

The first statement writes the episodes and what they mention. The second writes each fact `FROM` its episode and `ABOUT` its entities. A fact's `recordedAt` is its episode's time. `vector(f.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)` stores a typed vector and fails the statement if an embedding has the wrong length.

```cypher run name=remember params=session
UNWIND $episodes AS e
CREATE (ep:Episode {id: e.id, session: e.session, kind: e.kind, at: datetime(e.at), text: e.text})
WITH ep, e
UNWIND e.mentions AS key
MATCH (n:Entity {key: key})
CREATE (ep)-[:MENTIONS]->(n);

UNWIND $facts AS f
MATCH (ep:Episode {id: f.episode})
CREATE (x:Fact {id: f.id, text: f.text, slot: f.slot,
                validFrom: datetime(f.validFrom), recordedAt: ep.at,
                embedding: vector(f.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)})-[:FROM]->(ep)
WITH x, f
UNWIND f.about AS key
MATCH (n:Entity {key: key})
CREATE (x)-[:ABOUT]->(n);

MATCH (x:Fact)-[:FROM]->(ep:Episode)
RETURN ep.id AS episode, x.text AS fact, x.slot AS slot
ORDER BY episode
```

```table
| episode | fact                                         | slot                      |
|---------|----------------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| "e1"    | "Grace reviews each relate release."         | "relate/release-reviewer" |
| "e2"    | "Noor triages new relate issues on Mondays." | "relate/triage"           |
2 rows · nodes created: 4, relationships created: 10, properties set: 22, labels added: 4
```

properties.heading: Serve it to the agent
properties.text:
Recall needs only reads, so an agent that recalls gets the memory store over MCP opened read-only, and only the process that writes memory holds it writable:

```bash
relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./memory.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`. Opened read-only, the server lists `read_cypher` and `get_schema`; the recall statement runs through `read_cypher` with `vector` and `k` as its `parameters`. [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/) has the block for each host.

properties.heading: Start from the graph you have
properties.text:
Memory attaches to the domain graph, in this guide the shared example graph: three people and two projects.

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

Every person and project becomes an entity, with a lowercase `key` that writes can match on:

```cypher run name=entities
MATCH (n) WHERE n:Person OR n:Project
SET n:Entity, n.key = toLower(n.name)
RETURN n.key AS key, labels(n) AS labels
ORDER BY key
```

```table
| key              | labels                |
|------------------|-----------------------|
| "ada"            | ["Person", "Entity"]  |
| "grace"          | ["Person", "Entity"]  |
| "noor"           | ["Person", "Entity"]  |
| "opencypher-tck" | ["Project", "Entity"] |
| "relate"         | ["Project", "Entity"] |
5 rows · properties set: 5, labels added: 5
```

properties.heading: The model
properties.text:
Three node labels and four relationship types. Nothing is ever deleted: a correction closes the old fact and links it from the new one. | Element | Holds | Role | | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `Entity` | `key`, `name`, plus its domain labels | What memory is about. `key` is unique, so every write finds the same node | | `Episode` | `id`, `session`, `kind`, `at`, `text` | Where and when the agent learned something: a message, or a tool call and its result | | `Fact` | `id`, `text`, `slot`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `recordedAt`, `closedAt`, `embedding` | One statement about entities. `slot` names what it answers, and holds one current fact at a time | | `(:Episode)-[:MENTIONS]->(:Entity)` | | The entities an episode names | | `(:Fact)-[:FROM]->(:Episode)` | | Provenance: the evidence for the fact | | `(:Fact)-[:ABOUT]->(:Entity)` | | What the fact describes | | `(:Fact)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(:Fact)` | | A correction and the fact it replaced | A fact has two time axes. Valid time, `validFrom` to `validTo`, is when it held in the world. Record time, `recordedAt` to `closedAt`, is when the agent believed it. A late correction makes them disagree, and the graph keeps both answers. ```mermaid flowchart LR accTitle: Data model: entities, the episodes that mention them, and facts with their evidence accDescr { An Episode MENTIONS the Entity nodes it names. A Fact is ABOUT one or more entities and comes FROM the Episode that is its evidence. A Fact carries valid time and record time, and a newer Fact SUPERSEDES the one it replaced in the same slot. } Episode(("Episode
id · session · kind
at · text")) -- "MENTIONS" --> Entity(("Entity
key · name")) Fact(("Fact
text · slot · embedding
validFrom · validTo
recordedAt · closedAt")) -- "ABOUT" --> Entity Fact -- "FROM" --> Episode Fact -- "SUPERSEDES" --> Fact class Entity l3 class Episode l2 class Fact l4 ``` An Episode MENTIONS the Entity nodes it names. A Fact is ABOUT one or more entities and comes FROM the Episode that is its evidence. A Fact carries valid time and record time, and a newer Fact SUPERSEDES the one it replaced in the same slot. Once the cells on this page have run, the database can report its own model. `CALL db.schema.visualization()` returns one node per label, with its indexes and constraints, and one relationship per type and pair of labels: The figure above is the model as written. `CALL db.schema.visualization()` reports the model the page's database holds once the cells have run: one node per label, one relationship per type and pair of labels, and each label's indexes and constraints. When the page was recorded, those cells wrote 11 nodes, 21 relationships, 2 indexes and 3 constraints. Live: a button runs `CALL db.schema.visualization()` on the page's database in your browser once its cells have run, and draws the labels and relationship types it reports with the code that draws the figure, beside a table of each label's indexes and constraints.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Each slot holds at most one current fact. This check returns no rows while that holds:

```cypher run name=verify
MATCH (f:Fact) WHERE f.closedAt IS NULL
WITH f.slot AS slot, count(*) AS current WHERE current > 1
RETURN slot, current
```

```table
| slot | current |
|------|---------|
0 rows
```

properties.heading: Run relate in a sandbox
properties.text: This guide shows you how to run relate inside an agent sandbox: which hosts to allow, where the binary lands, how to keep usage metrics off, and which [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) to use. Once relate is installed and usage metrics are off, it needs no network, so most sandboxes need egress only while the image is built.

properties.heading: Choose where the store lives
properties.text:
Each `relate` command is its own process, so an in-memory store lasts one command. Work that spans commands needs a file in the workspace, `--database ./work.rl`, which can be committed with the change. Reads open it `--read-only`, so a mistake cannot change it.

relate turns on [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode) when it detects a harness variable such as `CLAUDECODE`, `CODEX_SANDBOX` or `CURSOR_AGENT` and stdout is not a terminal: each statement prints at most 100 rows and says so on stderr. `--max-rows 0` prints them all.

properties.heading: Claude Code sandbox
Codex CLI and Codex cloud
properties.text:
The Codex CLI's default `workspace-write` sandbox lets commands write to the current directory and temporary directories such as `/tmp`, with network access off. Install relate before the session. To let `--load` reach a URL, network access goes on in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml title="config.toml"
[sandbox_workspace_write]
network_access = true
```

Codex cloud runs an environment's setup with network access, and the agent phase offline unless internet access is turned on for that environment, with optional allowed domains. Put the install line and `relate telemetry off` in the environment's install script.

properties.heading: Cursor cloud agents
properties.text:
Cursor cloud agents run on Ubuntu machines with internet access by default. The `install` command in `.cursor/environment.json` runs from the project root when Cursor builds the environment, and must be safe to repeat, as `install.sh` is:

```json title=".cursor/environment.json"
{
  "install": "curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash && ~/.local/bin/relate telemetry off"
}
```

To narrow egress, the Cloud Agents dashboard's network modes are **Allow all network access**, **Default + allowlist** and **Allowlist only**.

properties.heading: Daytona
properties.text: On Daytona's tiers 1 and 2, organization-level network limits apply, and the documented always-reachable services include `github.com` and `*.githubusercontent.com`, the pinned binary's two hosts. `install.sh` also needs `relatedb.ai`. Tiers 3 and 4 have unrestricted internet access by default; `domainAllowList` (domains, wildcards allowed), `networkAllowList` (IPv4 ranges) and `networkBlockAll` replace it at creation.

properties.heading: E2B
properties.text: E2B sandboxes have outbound internet access by default. `allowInternetAccess: false` (Python `allow_internet_access=False`) turns it off at creation, and the `network` option takes `allowOut` and `denyOut` lists. Bake the install into a custom template, set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` with the template's `setEnvs`, and start each sandbox from that template.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**`relate: command not found`.** The install directory is not on the `PATH`; `install.sh` says so with `NOTE: <dir> is not in your PATH.` Add `$HOME/.local/bin` to the `PATH`, or call `$HOME/.local/bin/relate`.

**A `--load` exits 1 with `Error: request failed:` and a network detail.** The sandbox blocked the host, or it does not resolve. Allow `<dataset-host>` (`raw.githubusercontent.com` for a GitHub link), or download the file during setup and `--load` the local copy.

**`--load` exits 2 with an error that begins `Error: --safe refuses a remote --load source`.** Safe mode does not load remote stores. Download the file, check its SHA-256, and load the local copy.

**Results stop at 100 rows with `warning: result truncated to 100 rows (the statement returned <n>); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows`.** relate detected the harness and capped the output. Pass `--max-rows 0`, or `--max-rows <n>`, when the agent needs more.

properties.heading: Install relate into the image
properties.text:
Install at image or setup time, while the sandbox still has egress:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash
```

The script checks the release's signature, its signed version line and the binary's SHA-256 before it installs the latest release to `$HOME/.local/bin`. For an exact version, the [pinned install steps](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#install-a-pinned-relate) make the same checks. If `$HOME/.local/bin` is not on the agent's `PATH`, add it, or call the binary by its absolute path.

> **The agent build**
>
> Release binaries are the `full` build. The `agent` build, built from source with `cargo build -p relate-cli --no-default-features --features agent`, leaves out `serve`, `upgrade` and usage metrics, and keeps statements, `--load` from a URL, `--fetch-params`, the skill and `agent-context`.

properties.heading: Keep served surfaces on loopback
properties.text: `relate serve` binds `127.0.0.1` unless `--host` says otherwise. Bolt, the HTTP Query API and MCP over HTTP check one basic-auth credential, but serve has no TLS, so a non-loopback host sends the credential and every result in plaintext and prints a `WARNING` at startup. Inside a container, bind `0.0.0.0` and publish the port to the host's loopback only (see [plain Docker](#plain-docker)).

properties.heading: Load a dataset from a URL
properties.text:
`--load https://<dataset-host>/<name>.rl` fetches a `.rl` file, so `<dataset-host>` has to be allowed; a GitHub file link is fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com`. relate keeps no copy, so nothing is left to check afterwards. To check what you load, download it, compare its SHA-256 with the one its publisher lists, then load the local file:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://<dataset-host>/<name>.rl
sha256sum <name>.rl
relate --load ./<name>.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
```

`--safe` refuses a remote `--load` source before any network request and exits 2: a downloaded store is untrusted input. The download-and-check form works under `--safe`, because the source is then a local file.

properties.heading: Plain Docker
properties.text:
A Debian-based image with the install's two dependencies:

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl openssh-client \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:${PATH}" DO_NOT_TRACK=1
WORKDIR /work
```

Run statements against a store mounted from the host, with no network at all:

```bash
docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD":/work <image> relate --database ./graph.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
```

To serve Bolt from the container, bind all interfaces inside it and publish the port to the host's loopback:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:7687:7687 -v "$PWD":/work <image> relate serve --database ./graph.rl --read-only --host 0.0.0.0 --bolt 7687
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- A sandbox that runs Linux on amd64 or arm64, or macOS for Claude Code's local sandbox. The Linux binaries are built for glibc (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`), so use a Debian or Ubuntu base rather than Alpine.
- `curl` and `ssh-keygen` (the OpenSSH client) in the image, for the install script's checks.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/): serve a store to the agent host, read-only.
- [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/): read-only opens, safe mode, and backups.
- [Drive relate from an agent](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/drive-relate-from-an-agent/): the envelope, exit codes, and the row cap.
- [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/): what usage metrics hold and every way to turn them off.
- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/): `--load`, `--safe`, `--fetch-params` and `--max-rows`.

properties.heading: Set up each harness
properties.text: The harness side of each section follows that vendor's documentation as of 2026-11-07. Harness settings change between releases.

properties.heading: Turn off usage metrics
properties.text: Set `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` in the sandbox's environment: nothing is sent, and the first run prints no notice on stderr. Where a harness has no place for environment variables, run `relate telemetry off` once at setup; it writes the choice to relate's config folder in the image. The [privacy and telemetry reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/) lists every event.

properties.heading: Vercel Sandbox
properties.text:
Vercel Sandbox runs each sandbox in a Firecracker microVM whose default network policy is `allow-all`. The policy can change at runtime, so install relate first, then tighten it to `deny-all` or a list of domains:

```js title="sandbox.mjs"
await sandbox.update({ networkPolicy: { allow: ["raw.githubusercontent.com"] } });
```

Sandboxes are persistent by default, so a `.rl` file survives to the next session. A snapshot taken after installing skips the install next time. With the CLI, `sandbox exec --env DO_NOT_TRACK=1 <name> -- relate …` sets the variable per command.

With `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` set, usage metrics report disabled:

properties.heading: What relate needs from any sandbox
properties.text:
| Need                            | relate's side                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hosts to allow while installing | `install.sh`: `relatedb.ai`, `github.com` and `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`; since 1.0.1 it makes no GitHub API request and reads no token. The pinned binary: `github.com` and `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`                                       |
| Hosts to allow at run time      | None once usage metrics are off (`DO_NOT_TRACK=1`), except the host of a `--load https://…` or `--fetch-params` URL an agent uses. `relate upgrade` and `relate extension install` reach `relatedb.ai` and GitHub; `pull` and `push` reach the Neo4j server they name |
| Where the binary lands          | `$HOME/.local/bin/relate` for the user that ran `install.sh`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Usage metrics                   | On by default in release binaries; `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns them off and wins over every other setting                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Store                           | `:memory:` (the default) forgets everything when the process exits; a `.rl` file in the workspace persists                                                                                                                                                            |
| Served surfaces                 | `relate serve` binds `127.0.0.1` by default and has no TLS                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The release asset host is where GitHub redirects release downloads, as of 2026-11-07.

properties.heading: Turn questions into Cypher with an LLM
properties.text: This guide shows you how to turn a question into a Cypher [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) with a language model and check that statement before it runs. The model gets three things it cannot guess: this graph's schema, read from the engine; the places where relate's dialect differs from the Neo4j examples it was trained on; and a check that plans the statement with `EXPLAIN`, so a wrong label or a Neo4j-only procedure comes back as a message the model can repair, not as an empty result.

properties.heading: Add the ontology as context
properties.text: The inferred schema says what the data holds today, not what each label means. An [ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#ontology) stored with the store adds that: descriptions of the node and relationship types in words a model can use, and the properties each type must have. `CALL db.ontology.get()` returns the document as YAML or JSON, ready to paste into the prompt. The ontology procedures are a preview feature that runs only with `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` set; [Use an ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/ontology/) covers storing and reading one.

properties.heading: Check each statement with EXPLAIN
properties.text:
`EXPLAIN` plans a statement without running it: writes, procedures and `LOAD CSV` are only planned. The plan comes back with the planner's notifications, and they are the repair signal. A statement that names a label or relationship type the store does not have still plans, and returns no rows when it runs, so without `EXPLAIN` a wrong guess looks like an empty answer. Here a model guessed `WORKS_AT` and `Company`:

```cypher run name=explain-guess
EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company)
RETURN c.name AS company, count(p) AS people
```

```table
(no rows)
```

The cell returns no rows; its JSON view holds the envelope with the notifications. In a terminal, `--mode envelope` prints them on one line:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN c.name AS company, count(p) AS people" | jq -c '.notifications[] | {gql_status, description}'
```

```text
{"gql_status":"01N50","description":"The label `Company` does not exist in this database."}
{"gql_status":"01N51","description":"The relationship type `WORKS_AT` does not exist in this database."}
```

Each notification also carries `severity`, `title` and a `remedy`. `01N50`, `01N51` and `01N52` (an unknown [property](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property) key) are the ones a generated statement trips most; a statement that is valid for this schema plans with no notifications, or only with performance advice such as `03C91` (a missing index). The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#notifications) lists every notification. A syntax error or a Neo4j-only procedure fails the `EXPLAIN` itself: exit code 6, with the error object.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| What you see                                                                                                                 | Cause                                                                                                                         | Remedy                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No rows, and `EXPLAIN` reports `01N50`, `01N51` or `01N52`                                                                   | The statement names a label, relationship type or property key the store does not have                                        | Send the notification back to the model with the schema text                                                                        |
| `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: <name>`, exit code 6                                                                       | A procedure from a Neo4j library, such as APOC                                                                                | The Write instead column of [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/#differences) |
| `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`, exit code 6                                                     | A `USE` clause with a database name; a store has only the fixed namespaces                                                    | Drop the `USE` clause; [Namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/namespaces/) explains the three names                         |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …`, exit code 6, or `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query` from MCP | The model wrote a write: the CLI store is open read-only, as configured, and MCP's `read_cypher` refuses writes on any server | Keep it read-only for questions; a write goes through a separate, reviewed path                                                     |
| `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'ontology' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology`                      | `db.ontology.get()` without the preview opt-in                                                                                | Set `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` in the environment of the process that opens the store                                                |

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- The example graph from [your first graph](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/first-graph/): three people and two projects. The first step creates it in the cells, and the terminal steps write it to `team.rl`.
- For the terminal steps, relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)). The cells run in your browser without it.
- For the program, the Python client (`pip install relate-db`) and a client for the model of your choice. No step on this page calls a model; that call is the one line you supply.

properties.heading: Read the schema from the engine
properties.text:
Three statements give a model what it needs: each [label](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label)'s properties with their types, each [relationship type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type)'s properties, and which labels each type connects. `db.schema.nodeTypeProperties()` infers the first by scanning the data:

```cypher run name=node-schema
CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties() YIELD nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes
RETURN nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes
ORDER BY nodeType, propertyName
```

```table
| nodeType   | propertyName | propertyTypes       |
|------------|--------------|---------------------|
| ":Person"  | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
| ":Person"  | "role"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
| ":Project" | "language"   | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
| ":Project" | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
4 rows
```

`db.schema.relTypeProperties()` does the same for relationships. A type with no properties has one row with a null `propertyName`:

```cypher run name=rel-schema
CALL db.schema.relTypeProperties() YIELD relType, propertyName, propertyTypes
RETURN relType, propertyName, propertyTypes
ORDER BY relType
```

```table
| relType        | propertyName | propertyTypes        |
|----------------|--------------|----------------------|
| "[:KNOWS]"     | null         | []                   |
| "[:MAINTAINS]" | null         | []                   |
| "[:WORKS_ON]"  | "since"      | ["INTEGER NOT NULL"] |
3 rows
```

Neither procedure says which way a relationship points or what it connects, and a model needs that to write a pattern. One statement lists every pattern that occurs:

```cypher run name=patterns
MATCH (a)-[r]->(b)
RETURN DISTINCT labels(a) AS source, type(r) AS type, labels(b) AS target
ORDER BY type
```

```table
| source     | type        | target      |
|------------|-------------|-------------|
| ["Person"] | "KNOWS"     | ["Person"]  |
| ["Person"] | "MAINTAINS" | ["Project"] |
| ["Person"] | "WORKS_ON"  | ["Project"] |
3 rows
```

On a large store the pattern statement reads every relationship; keep its result with the prompt and refresh it when the schema changes. `db.schema.visualization()` returns the same labels and types as one row, for a tool that draws them.

properties.heading: Read the schema over MCP
properties.text:
An agent connected to relate's own MCP server has the same facts in one call. The `get_schema` tool returns each label with its count, its properties and types, and its outgoing relationships with the labels they reach. This sends `initialize` and a `get_schema` call to a read-only stdio server on `team.rl`; `2>/dev/null` drops relate's startup lines:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"shell","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","serverInfo":{"name":"relate-mcp","version":"1.0.1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"Person\":{\"count\":3,\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"role\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"relationships\":{\"KNOWS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Person\"]},\"MAINTAINS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"]},\"WORKS_ON\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"],\"properties\":{\"since\":{\"type\":\"Integer\"}}}},\"type\":\"node\"},\"Project\":{\"count\":2,\"properties\":{\"language\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"type\":\"node\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

`get_schema` takes an optional `sample_size`, the number of nodes and relationships it examines per label; `-1` examines all of them. The [MCP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/) lists both tools a read-only server offers, and [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/) has the host configuration.

properties.heading: Run the checked statement
properties.text:
Once the check passes, run the statement against the store, read-only. A person reads the table; an agent reads the envelope and the exit code, and sends a non-zero exit back into the loop with the error object's `message`:

### At a terminal

```bash
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, count(p) AS people ORDER BY people DESC"
```

### From an agent

Exit code 0 means the rows in the envelope are the answer; 6 means the statement was rejected, and the error object on stdout says why; 7 means it ran past `--timeout`:

```bash
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope --timeout 10s "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, count(p) AS people ORDER BY people DESC"
```

properties.heading: Run the repair loop
properties.text:
This program puts the steps together with the Python client. It writes `team.rl`, opens it `read_only=True`, builds the schema text a prompt carries, and checks two statements as a model might return them: a first guess and its repair. Nothing in it calls a model:

```python run name=loop title="text_to_cypher.py"
import relate

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

writer = relate.connect("./team.rl")
writer.execute(TEAM)
writer.close()


def schema_text(conn):
    """The labels, properties and relationship patterns, one line each."""
    props = {}
    for row in conn.execute(
        "CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties() YIELD nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes "
        "RETURN nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes ORDER BY nodeType, propertyName"
    ).data():
        props.setdefault(row["nodeType"], []).append(f"{row['propertyName']}: {row['propertyTypes'][0]}")
    lines = [f"({label} {{{', '.join(p)}}})" for label, p in props.items()]
    for row in conn.execute(
        "MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) RETURN DISTINCT labels(a)[0] AS source, type(r) AS type, "
        "labels(b)[0] AS target ORDER BY type"
    ).data():
        lines.append(f"(:{row['source']})-[:{row['type']}]->(:{row['target']})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def check(conn, statement):
    """Plan the statement; return the problems a model can repair, or []."""
    try:
        summary = conn.execute("EXPLAIN " + statement).consume()
    except relate.Error as e:
        return [f"{e.gql_status}: {e}"]
    return [f"{n['gql_status']}: {n['description']}" for n in summary.notifications if n["severity"] == "WARNING"]


conn = relate.connect("./team.rl", read_only=True)
print(schema_text(conn))

first_guess = "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN c.name AS company, count(p) AS people"
repaired = "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, count(p) AS people ORDER BY people DESC"

for statement in (first_guess, repaired):
    problems = check(conn, statement)
    print("problems:" if problems else "no problems", *problems, sep="\n  ")

print(conn.execute(repaired).data())
conn.close()
```

```text
(:Person {name: STRING NOT NULL, role: STRING NOT NULL})
(:Project {language: STRING NOT NULL, name: STRING NOT NULL})
(:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(:Person)
(:Person)-[:MAINTAINS]->(:Project)
(:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project)
problems:
  01N50: The label `Company` does not exist in this database.
  01N51: The relationship type `WORKS_AT` does not exist in this database.
no problems
[{'project': 'relate', 'people': 2}, {'project': 'opencypher-tck', 'people': 1}]
```

The loop around it sends the question, the schema text and the Differences table to the model, checks what comes back, and sends the problems back until there are none or a retry budget runs out. `ask_model` stands for your model client:

```python title="loop.py"
def answer(conn, question, ask_model, retries=3):
    prompt = f"Schema:\n{schema_text(conn)}\n\nQuestion: {question}\nReply with one Cypher statement."
    statement = ask_model(prompt)
    for _ in range(retries):
        problems = check(conn, statement)
        if not problems:
            return conn.execute(statement).data()
        statement = ask_model(f"{prompt}\n\nThis statement:\n{statement}\nhas these problems:\n" + "\n".join(problems))
    raise RuntimeError(f"no valid statement after {retries} repairs: {problems}")
```

The store is open read-only, so a generated write fails with `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase` instead of changing the graph. To bound a statement that plans cleanly but runs long, run it from the CLI with `--timeout`.

properties.heading: Tell the model what differs from Neo4j
properties.text:
Most Cypher a model has seen was written for Neo4j, and relate rejects a few of those habits: APOC and Graph Data Science procedures, `CREATE DATABASE` and `USE` with a database name, colon commands such as `:param`, index procedures, and a `SEARCH` score read without `SCORE AS`. [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/#differences) lists each one with the error relate returns and the form to write instead. Put that table in the prompt, or let the checks catch the habit and hand the model the row it broke.

A Neo4j-only procedure fails with a message that names it:

```cypher run name=apoc expect=error
CALL apoc.meta.schema()
```

```table
error: syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: apoc.meta.schema
```

properties.text:
The repaired statement returns one row per project with its head count, and planning it reports no unknown names:

```cypher run name=verify
MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
RETURN proj.name AS project, count(p) AS people
ORDER BY people DESC
```

```table
| project          | people |
|------------------|--------|
| "relate"         | 2      |
| "opencypher-tck" | 1      |
2 rows
```

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, count(p) AS people ORDER BY people DESC" | jq -c '.notifications'
```
