properties.heading: Use relate in CI
properties.text: This guide shows you how to run relate in a GitHub Actions job: install one exact release and check its signature, keep usage metrics off, and gate the build on a Cypher [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) that returns no rows when the build may pass. The example check is the advisory gate from the [dependency blast radius recipe](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/dependency-blast-radius/), run against a store committed to the repository and opened `--read-only`.

properties.heading: Accept reviewed findings
properties.text:
A finding a reviewer accepts goes into `$allow`, in the workflow or a file beside `gate.cypher`. With both ids allowed, the result is empty and the gate passes:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./deps.rl --read-only --mode json --max-rows 0 --timeout 30s --param minCvss=7.5 --param 'allow=["ADV-2026-0007","ADV-2026-0012"]' < gate.cypher > findings.json
jq -e '.data | length == 0' findings.json
echo "gate exit=$?"
```

```text
true
gate exit=0
```

properties.heading: Add the workflow
properties.text:
The workflow installs relate 1.0.1 with the three checks `install.sh` makes, from the [pinned install steps](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#install-a-pinned-relate): the signature on `SHA256SUMS` against the release signing key, the signed first line naming the release, and the binary's SHA-256. Releases up to and including 0.16.1 were published under the project's earlier name, so their assets, signer and manifest header say `cypherlite`; from 0.1.0 on they say `relate`, with the same key ([Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/#release-signing-key)). The gate's `.data` filter needs 0.1.0 or later, where `--json` wraps the rows in `data`.

```yaml title=".github/workflows/graph-check.yml"
name: Graph check

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  DO_NOT_TRACK: '1'
  RELATE_VERSION: 1.0.1
  RELATE_ASSET: relate-linux-amd64
  RELATE_SIGNER: relate-release

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      # The download, cached by version and asset; the checks below run on every job.
      - name: Restore the relate download
        id: relate-cache
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: relate-download
          key: relate-${{ env.RELATE_VERSION }}-${{ env.RELATE_ASSET }}

      - name: Download relate
        if: steps.relate-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p relate-download && cd relate-download
          BASE="https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases/download/v$RELATE_VERSION"
          curl -sSfLO "$BASE/$RELATE_ASSET"
          curl -sSfLO "$BASE/SHA256SUMS"
          curl -sSfLO "$BASE/SHA256SUMS.sig"

      - name: Verify and install relate
        working-directory: relate-download
        run: |
          echo "$RELATE_SIGNER ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHgv/GHY5mtv/HopH/J/T7KrTT7eOVFEG2ueT4iRKwbK $RELATE_SIGNER" > allowed_signers
          ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I "$RELATE_SIGNER" -n "$RELATE_SIGNER" -s SHA256SUMS.sig < SHA256SUMS
          test "$(head -n 1 SHA256SUMS)" = "# $RELATE_SIGNER-version: v$RELATE_VERSION"
          grep "  $RELATE_ASSET\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c -
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
          install -m 0755 "$RELATE_ASSET" "$HOME/.local/bin/relate"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Check the version
        run: relate --version

      - name: Gate on reachable advisories
        run: |
          relate query --database ./deps.rl --read-only --mode json --max-rows 0 --timeout 30s \
            --param minCvss=7.5 --param 'allow=[]' < gate.cypher > findings.json
          jq . findings.json
          jq -e '.data | length == 0' findings.json
```

What each part does:

- **`env`** applies to every step: `DO_NOT_TRACK` turns usage metrics off, and the three `RELATE_` values are the pin. Moving to a new release changes them together, in the same change that moves any `AGENTS.md` pin.
- **`shell: bash`** runs each step with `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`, so the first failing command, a failed check or a non-zero relate exit, fails the step. A step with no `shell` on an Ubuntu runner runs `bash -e`, without `pipefail` (GitHub's workflow syntax reference, read 2026-11-08).
- **`actions/checkout`** v7 (as its README describes v7.0.1, the latest release on 2026-11-08) checks out the repository, store and `gate.cypher` included.
- **The cache** (`actions/cache` v6, as its README describes v6.1.0) keeps the three downloaded files under a key made of the version and the asset, so a new pin downloads again. The cache stores the files, not the trust: the verify step checks the signature, the header and the checksum on every job, cached or not, and needs no network.
- **The verify step** stops the job at the first check that fails, before anything is installed.
- **The gate step** prints the findings to the log with `jq .`, then fails the job when relate exits non-zero or when the result has rows.

properties.heading: Build a fixture store
properties.text:
The check reads a dependency graph: package versions that `DEPENDS_ON` each other, and advisories that affect some of them, as in the recipe's data model. This writes a small one into a new [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store), `deps.rl`, with invented package names. In a real repository the store is built by your own tooling and committed:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./deps.rl --mode envelope <<'EOF'
CREATE (app:Version:Root {key: 'NPM/team-api@1.4.0', name: 'team-api', version: '1.4.0'}),
       (router:Version {key: 'NPM/route-kit@2.3.1', name: 'route-kit', version: '2.3.1'}),
       (parser:Version {key: 'NPM/path-match@0.1.7', name: 'path-match', version: '0.1.7'}),
       (signer:Version {key: 'NPM/token-sign@8.5.1', name: 'token-sign', version: '8.5.1'}),
       (app)-[:DEPENDS_ON {requirement: '^2.3.0'}]->(router),
       (router)-[:DEPENDS_ON {requirement: '0.1.7'}]->(parser),
       (app)-[:DEPENDS_ON {requirement: '^8.5.0'}]->(signer),
       (parser)-[:AFFECTED_BY]->(:Advisory {id: 'ADV-2026-0007', title: 'Backtracking on crafted paths', cvss3: 7.5}),
       (signer)-[:AFFECTED_BY]->(:Advisory {id: 'ADV-2026-0012', title: 'Weak default algorithm', cvss3: 8.1}),
       (router)-[:AFFECTED_BY]->(:Advisory {id: 'ADV-2026-0019', title: 'Verbose error pages', cvss3: 4.3});
EOF
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":2.5163339999999996,"execute_ms":2.190625,"lex_parse_ms":0.017499999999999998,"lower_ms":0.019792,"parse_ms":0.30762500000000004,"plan_ms":0.012125,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.0012920000000000002},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| What you see                                                                                                              | Cause                                                                                                             | Remedy                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The verify step fails at `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, with no `Good "relate-release" signature` line                           | The downloaded `SHA256SUMS` or its signature is not the release's, or a value in `env` does not match the release | Check the three `RELATE_` values against the pinned install steps; never skip the check                  |
| The verify step fails at `test` or `sha256sum -c -`                                                                       | The manifest names another release, or the binary does not match its line                                         | Delete the cache entry for the key and run again; a second failure means the download is not the release |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage error: database not found: <path>`, exit code 1                                           | The store path is wrong, or the file was not checked out (Git LFS without `lfs: true` on the checkout)            | Fix the `--database` path                                                                                |
| `semantic error: …` or `syntax error: …`, exit code 6                                                                     | `gate.cypher` does not parse or plan, or it writes on a read-only store                                           | Run it locally with the same flags; the message names the problem                                        |
| `Error: query timed out after <duration>`, exit code 7                                                                    | The statement ran past `--timeout`                                                                                | Bound the pattern, or raise `--timeout`                                                                  |
| `findings.json` holds at most 100 findings and a `rowCap` key, and stderr shows `warning: result truncated to 100 rows …` | `--max-rows 0` is missing and an agent harness variable is set in the job                                         | Add `--max-rows 0`                                                                                       |

properties.heading: Keep usage metrics off
properties.text:
The relate CLI sends anonymous [usage metrics](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#telemetry) unless a setting turns them off ([Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/)). `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` in the job's environment turns them off for every step, sends nothing, and prints no first-run notice. `relate telemetry status` names the setting that decided:

```bash verify
DO_NOT_TRACK=1 relate telemetry status
```

```text
disabled (DO_NOT_TRACK)
```

properties.heading: Open the workspace store read-only
properties.text:
The checkout puts the store in the workspace, and every step that reads it passes `--read-only`: relate writes nothing, runs no checkpoint, and leaves the file byte for byte as committed. A `.rl` store opens read-only only while no process writes it, which holds in a job where nothing else opens it; otherwise the open fails with `Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5.

A check that needs to write, such as one that derives data before it gates, works on a copy. `--load ./deps.rl --database ./scratch.rl` copies the store and opens the copy for writing; `--load ./deps.rl` alone loads it into an in-memory store that is itself read-only and gone when the step ends.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- A GitHub repository with Actions enabled. The workflow runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, whose image (version 20261101.360.1) includes `jq` 1.7 and the OpenSSH client.
- A store in the repository for the check to read, such as a `.rl` file. The steps build a small one, `deps.rl`.
- relate on your `PATH`, to run the check locally first ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Fresh graph per test run](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#fresh-graph-per-test-run) and [Dependency analysis](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#dependency-analysis) in the capability catalog.
- [Trace how vulnerabilities reach your app](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/dependency-blast-radius/): the gate on real dependency graphs, with its data.
- [Connect your agent to relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#install-a-pinned-relate): the pinned install steps.
- [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/): the signing key, its fingerprint, and what each check proves.
- [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/): every exit code and the error object.
- [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/): the defaults a harness variable changes.

properties.heading: Turn the findings into an exit code
properties.text:
relate's own exit code says whether the statement ran: 0 for success, including an empty result, 6 for a rejected statement, 1 for a store that cannot be opened, 5 for one another process holds. The findings are rows, so a second command turns rows into a failure. `--mode json` prints the result as one JSON object with the rows in `data`, beside the statement's [timings](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache), and `jq -e '.data | length == 0'` exits 1 when `data` has anything in it:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./deps.rl --read-only --mode json --max-rows 0 --timeout 30s --param minCvss=7.5 --param 'allow=[]' < gate.cypher > findings.json
echo "relate exit=$?"
cat findings.json
jq -e '.data | length == 0' findings.json
echo "gate exit=$?"
```

```text
relate exit=0
{"data":[{"advisory":"ADV-2026-0012","cvss":8.1,"path":["team-api","token-sign"],"version":"NPM/token-sign@8.5.1"},{"advisory":"ADV-2026-0007","cvss":7.5,"path":["team-api","route-kit","path-match"],"version":"NPM/path-match@0.1.7"}],"planCache":"miss","timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.26275,"execute_ms":1.0196669999999999,"lex_parse_ms":0.025,"lower_ms":0.060458000000000005,"parse_ms":0.16883299999999998,"plan_ms":0.067625,"result_generation_ms":0.000375,"rewrite_ms":0.007208}}
false
gate exit=1
```

Two findings fail the gate; the 4.3 advisory is under the threshold. Every flag on that command is there for CI:

| Flag                           | Why                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate query … < gate.cypher` | `query` reads the statement from stdin. Without the word `query`, a redirected file is not read: relate prints its help and exits 0                                                           |
| `--read-only`                  | The check cannot change the store, and a write in the statement fails with exit code 6                                                                                                        |
| `--mode json`                  | One JSON object with the rows in `data`, whatever stdout is; with `--max-rows 0` its shape does not change under [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode) either |
| `--max-rows 0`                 | Every finding is printed, even when the job runs under an agent harness, where the default caps output at 100 rows                                                                            |
| `--timeout 30s`                | A statement that runs longer is cancelled with exit code 7 instead of holding the job                                                                                                         |

[Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/) covers each one, and [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/) lists every exit code.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Run the gate locally against the committed store before pushing: exit code 1 and the findings on a failing graph, exit code 0 and an empty `data` array on a passing one, as in [Turn the findings into an exit code](#turn-the-findings-into-an-exit-code). In the Actions log, the `Check the version` step prints:

```bash verify
relate --version
```

```text
Relate v1.0.1
License: Apache 2.0 (binary)
```

properties.heading: Write the check as a statement
properties.text:
A gate is a statement whose rows are the findings: no rows, the build passes. This one lists every advisory with a score of at least `$minCvss` that a root package can reach, with the shortest chain to it, minus the ids in `$allow` that a reviewer accepted. Keep it in the repository as `gate.cypher`:

```bash verify
cat > gate.cypher <<'EOF'
MATCH p = SHORTEST 1 (r:Root)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->{0,12}(v:Version)
MATCH (v)-[:AFFECTED_BY]->(a:Advisory)
WHERE a.cvss3 >= $minCvss AND NOT a.id IN $allow
RETURN a.id AS advisory, a.cvss3 AS cvss, v.key AS version,
       [n IN nodes(p) | n.name] AS path
ORDER BY cvss DESC, advisory, version;
EOF
```

The thresholds are [parameters](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter), so the workflow changes them with `--param` and the statement stays the same file. The recipe explains the pattern and runs it on 89 real package versions.

properties.heading: Use the interactive shell
properties.text:
This guide shows you how to work in the `relate` interactive shell: start it on a store, run statements that span several lines, edit and recall what you typed, bind parameters, use the dot commands, group writes in a transaction, and leave. The shell opens when `relate` runs on a terminal with no statement to run. It reads one [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) at a time, runs it when it sees the closing `;`, and prints the result as a table.

The transcripts on this page come from a terminal session with relate 1.0.1 and are not replayed by the docs checks. Each is followed by the same statements as a piped script, which the checks replay; a script and the shell share the statement splitter and the dot commands.

properties.heading: Bind parameters for the session
properties.text:
Pass `--param name=value` when you start the shell, once per [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter). Every statement in the session can use `$name`; the shell has no command to set one later:

```bash
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --param name=Grace
```

```text
cypher> MATCH (p:Person {name: $name})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
   ...> RETURN proj.name AS project, w.since AS since
   ...> ORDER BY since;
+------------------+-------+
| project          | since |
+------------------+-------+
| "opencypher-tck" | 2022  |
| "relate"         | 2023  |
+------------------+-------+
```

The same statement, piped with the same flag:

```bash verify
printf 'MATCH (p:Person {name: $name})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)\nRETURN proj.name AS project, w.since AS since\nORDER BY since;\n' | relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --param name=Grace --mode table
```

```text
+------------------+-------+
| project          | since |
+------------------+-------+
| "opencypher-tck" | 2022  |
| "relate"         | 2023  |
+------------------+-------+
```

[Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/#pass-parameters) covers value types and quoting.

properties.heading: Build the example store
properties.text:
Write the seed to a file and run it into a new store. This step writes `team.rl`:

```bash verify
cat > seed.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl < seed.cypher
```

properties.heading: Edit and recall input
properties.text:
On a terminal, the prompt is a line editor:

| Key                      | Effect                                                           |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left, Right, Home, End   | Move within the current line                                     |
| Emacs-style editing keys | Edit the current line                                            |
| Up, Down                 | Walk back and forward through what you submitted in this session |
| Ctrl-C                   | Drop the statement you are typing and return to `cypher>`        |
| Ctrl-D                   | Leave the shell (on an empty line)                               |

A statement you submitted over several lines comes back as one history entry. History lasts for the session only: the shell writes no history file, and there is no tab completion. Ctrl-C at the `   ...>` prompt discards every line typed so far:

```text
cypher> MATCH (n)
   ...>
cypher>
```

properties.heading: Group writes in a transaction
properties.text:
This section writes to `team.rl`, so start the shell without `--read-only`. Removing `--read-only` is what allows writes:

```bash
relate --database ./team.rl
```

Outside a transaction, each statement that writes commits as soon as it succeeds. To make several statements one unit, open a [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction) with `.begin`, check the result inside it, then `.commit`. This one adds Ines to the `relate` project:

```text
cypher> .begin
cypher> MATCH (proj:Project {name: 'relate'})
   ...> MERGE (i:Person {name: 'Ines', role: 'engineer'})
   ...> MERGE (i)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(proj);
cypher> MATCH (:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN count(*) AS people;
+--------+
| people |
+--------+
| 3      |
+--------+
cypher> .commit
```

The write prints nothing. Statements inside the transaction see its writes, so the count is 3 before `.commit`. `.rollback` in place of `.commit` discards them. If a statement fails inside the transaction, every later statement prints `semantic error: transaction failed; rollback required` until you run `.rollback`.

The same transaction as a piped script. `MERGE` makes it safe to run after the session, because a second run finds Ines already there:

```bash verify
cat > ines.cypher <<'EOF'
.begin
MATCH (proj:Project {name: 'relate'})
MERGE (i:Person {name: 'Ines', role: 'engineer'})
MERGE (i)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(proj);
.commit
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < ines.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.46883400000000003,"execute_ms":0.249917,"lex_parse_ms":0.00625,"lower_ms":0.008791,"parse_ms":0.207125,"plan_ms":0.006917,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.00033299999999999996},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| What you see                                                                                                                                                 | Cause                                                                          | Remedy                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The `relate` help text instead of a prompt                                                                                                                   | stdin is piped or redirected, so there is no terminal to read from             | Run `relate` from a terminal, or pipe the script to `relate query`                                                                             |
| The `   ...>` prompt keeps coming back                                                                                                                       | The statement has no closing `;`, or an open quote or comment is swallowing it | Type `;` and Enter, or press Ctrl-C to start over                                                                                              |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.` | The shell was started with `--read-only`                                       | Leave and start it again without `--read-only` to write                                                                                        |
| `semantic error: transaction failed; rollback required`                                                                                                      | A statement failed inside a `.begin` transaction                               | Run `.rollback`, then the transaction again                                                                                                    |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5                                                                                                 | Another process holds the store for writing                                    | Wait for it to exit, or open with `--read-only` (a directory store can be read beside its writer; a `.rl` store only while no writer holds it) |
| `warning: line editor unavailable (<reason>); falling back to plain stdin`                                                                                   | The terminal doesn't support the line editor                                   | The shell still works; arrow keys and history are off for the session                                                                          |

properties.heading: Leave the shell
properties.text:
Type `.quit` or `.exit`, or press Ctrl-D on an empty line. At the `   ...>` prompt, Ctrl-D first runs the lines entered so far, then leaves. On a line with text, Ctrl-D edits the line and does not leave. The shell exits 0, even after a statement failed in the session.

On a store opened for writing, the shell writes a checkpoint as it exits. A transaction still open at exit is rolled back, and the shell says so on stderr before it exits:

```text
cypher> .begin
cypher> .quit
Warning: exiting with an open transaction; rolling back uncommitted changes. Use .commit before exiting to persist them.
```

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- `relate` on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A terminal. With stdin redirected or piped, `relate` with no statement prints its help instead of opening the shell.
- An empty working directory. The first step writes the team graph shared across the docs to `team.rl` there.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Dot commands](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/dot-commands/): every dot command with its output and errors
- [Output modes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/): the `--mode` values a session can start with
- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/): `--param`, `--read-only`, `--timeout` and the rest
- [Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/): the same statements and dot commands from a file

properties.heading: Run a statement over several lines
properties.text:
Type the statement over as many lines as you like and end it with `;`. Until the `;`, the prompt changes to `   ...>` and the shell keeps reading:

```text
cypher> MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
   ...> WHERE w.since >= 2023
   ...> RETURN p.name AS person, proj.name AS project
   ...> ORDER BY person;
+---------+----------+
| person  | project  |
+---------+----------+
| "Ada"   | "relate" |
| "Grace" | "relate" |
+---------+----------+
```

Only a `;` at the end of the statement submits it. A blank line doesn't, and a `;` inside a string or a comment doesn't end the statement. The same lines as a piped script print the same table:

```bash verify
printf 'MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)\nWHERE w.since >= 2023\nRETURN p.name AS person, proj.name AS project\nORDER BY person;\n' | relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table
```

```text
+---------+----------+
| person  | project  |
+---------+----------+
| "Ada"   | "relate" |
| "Grace" | "relate" |
+---------+----------+
```

A statement that fails prints its error and returns to `cypher>`. Unlike a script, the shell keeps going after a failure.

properties.heading: Start the shell
properties.text:
Open the store [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) for exploring, so nothing you type can change it:

```bash
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only
```

The shell prints a banner and the `cypher>` prompt:

```text
Relate 1.0.1. End statements with ;  (.quit to exit)
cypher>
```

`relate` with no `--database` opens the shell on an in-memory [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), which is gone when the shell exits. `relate query --database <path>` opens the same shell. Flags given at the start apply to the whole session: `--mode` changes the output, `--timeout` bounds each statement, and `--read-only` refuses every write.

properties.heading: Use dot commands
properties.text:
A line that starts with `.` is a shell command, not Cypher. It runs when you press Enter and needs no `;`:

| Command                          | Effect                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.help`                          | Lists what the shell accepts                                                               |
| `.begin`, `.commit`, `.rollback` | Open, commit, or discard an explicit transaction                                           |
| `.checkpoint`                    | Writes a checkpoint of a persistent store now                                              |
| `.info`                          | Prints the store's metadata, node and relationship counts, and its indexes and constraints |
| `.timer on`, `.timer off`        | Prints each statement's run time after its result                                          |
| `.quit`, `.exit`                 | Leaves the shell                                                                           |

Any other dot command prints `Error: unknown command <name>`. Output format, headers and width are flags given at the start, not dot commands. The [dot commands reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/dot-commands/) has each command's output and errors.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Read the store back, read-only. Ines works on `relate` after the transaction committed:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name"
```

```text
+---------+
| name    |
+---------+
| "Ada"   |
| "Grace" |
| "Ines"  |
+---------+
```

properties.heading: Choose an output format
properties.text:
This guide shows you how to pick the `relate` output mode that fits the job, one step per job: rows for `jq`, results for a program, a spreadsheet, a notes file, an agent, and a query profile. The table names the mode for each, [TOON](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#toon) for an agent among them. Pass the mode on every command whose output something else reads. Without one, relate prints a table on a terminal and JSON Lines into a pipe, so the same command prints differently in each place.

| Job                                                               | Mode         | Flag                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| Read results at a terminal                                        | `table`      | none on a terminal, or `--mode table` |
| Filter or reshape rows with `jq`                                  | `jsonl`      | `--jsonl`                             |
| Parse results in a program, with types and an empty-result signal | `envelope`   | `--mode envelope`                     |
| Open the rows in a spreadsheet                                    | `csv`        | `--csv`                               |
| Paste a table into notes or a pull request                        | `markdown`   | `--markdown`                          |
| Hand rows to an agent in few characters                           | `toon`       | `--toon`                              |
| Look at where a statement spends its time                         | `speedscope` | `--mode speedscope` with `PROFILE`    |

properties.heading: Build the example store
properties.text:
Write the seed to a file and run it into a new store. This step writes `team.rl`; every later step opens it `--read-only`:

```bash verify
cat > seed.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl < seed.cypher
```

properties.heading: Export CSV for a spreadsheet
properties.text:
Use `--csv` and redirect to a file. The first line is the header:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --csv "MATCH (p:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role, count(proj) AS projects ORDER BY name" > people.csv
cat people.csv
```

```text
name,role,projects
Ada,engineer,1
Grace,engineer,2
Noor,maintainer,0
```

To leave the header out, for appending to an existing file, add `--noheader`. A field that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a `'` in front, so a spreadsheet shows it as text instead of running it as a formula; a negative number prints as `'-5`.

properties.heading: Give an agent TOON
properties.text:
Use `--toon` for rows an agent reads. The header names the row count and the columns once, then each row is one line of values, and the `timings:` and `planCache:` entries close the block:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --toon "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, proj.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
rows[3]{person,project,since}:
  Grace,opencypher-tck,2022
  Grace,relate,2023
  Ada,relate,2024
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":0.428167,"execute_ms":0.247,"lex_parse_ms":0.031291,"lower_ms":0.0425,"parse_ms":0.111333,"plan_ms":0.061,"result_generation_ms":0.00029099999999999997,"rewrite_ms":0.008291999999999999}
planCache:
  miss
```

Under [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode), `toon` is already the default when stdout is piped. It prints no error object: a failure shows only as the stderr message and the exit code. If the agent branches on failures in its output, pass `--mode envelope` instead.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| What you see                                                                                                                                   | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Remedy                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `jq` reports a parse error on piped output                                                                                                     | Agent mode is on (a detected agent harness, `--agent-mode` or `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1`), so the piped default is `toon`                                                                                                         | Pass `--jsonl` or `--mode envelope` explicitly                                      |
| `speedscope mode requires a PROFILE statement: per-operator times are what it exports (the statement carries no plan tree)`, exit code 1       | The statement has no `PROFILE` prefix. The statement still ran: its writes are committed                                                                                                                                     | Start the statement with `PROFILE`                                                  |
| `speedscope mode requires a PROFILE statement: per-operator times are what it exports (the plan tree carries no PROFILE metrics)`, exit code 1 | The plan's top operator recorded no metrics; as of 1.0.1, a `count()` over an `Expand`, such as `MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN count(p)`, does this. The statement still ran: its writes are committed | Profile the statement without its aggregation, or read the plan with `--mode table` |
| A spreadsheet column shows `'-5`                                                                                                               | The CSV formula guard prefixes a field that starts with `-`                                                                                                                                                                  | Strip the leading `'` on import, or export with `--jsonl`                           |
| `Error: invalid mode '<name>' (expected one of: table, csv, json, jsonl, envelope, markdown, cypher, toon, speedscope)`, exit code 2           | A mode name relate doesn't have                                                                                                                                                                                              | Use one of the nine names the message lists                                         |

properties.heading: Parse results in a program
properties.text:
Use `--mode envelope` when a program reads the output. Each result set is one JSON object, the [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope), with the column order in `columns`, a type per column in `columnTypes`, the rows, and `truncated`, which says whether a row cap cut them:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, count(p) AS people ORDER BY project" | jq -c '{columns, columnTypes, truncated, rows: (.rows | length)}'
```

```text
{"columns":["project","people"],"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER"],"truncated":false,"rows":2}
```

A read with no rows still prints an envelope with its `columns`, where `jsonl` prints nothing. A failed statement prints an [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object) on stdout in place of the envelope, so a program can tell no rows, no output, and a failure apart.

properties.heading: Paste a Markdown table into notes
properties.text:
Use `--markdown` for a table that renders in a Markdown file, an issue or a pull request:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --markdown "MATCH (proj:Project)<-[:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person) RETURN proj.name AS project, collect(p.name) AS people ORDER BY project"
```

```text
| project          | people           |
|------------------|------------------|
| "opencypher-tck" | ["Grace"]        |
| "relate"         | ["Grace", "Ada"] |
```

Strings keep their quotes, and a `|` inside a value is escaped, so a value can't add a column. Append to a notes file with `>> notes.md`.

properties.heading: Pipe rows to jq
properties.text:
Use `--jsonl` for a stream of rows: one JSON object per row, each on its own line, which `jq` reads one at a time. Each statement ends with one more line, its [timings and plan-cache outcome](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache); a filter on a row's key, such as `.role`, passes over it. This keeps the engineers' names:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --jsonl "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role ORDER BY name" | jq -r 'select(.role == "engineer") | .name'
```

```text
Ada
Grace
```

`jsonl` is also the default when stdout is a pipe, but pass it anyway: under a detected agent harness the piped default is `toon`, which `jq` can't read.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- `relate` on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- `jq`, for the JSON steps.
- An empty working directory. The first step writes the team graph shared across the docs to `team.rl` there.

properties.heading: Profile a statement in speedscope
properties.text:
Use `--mode speedscope` with a `PROFILE` statement and save the output to a file. It holds the statement's [plan](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#plan), one frame per operator, with the time each one took:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode speedscope "PROFILE MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, proj.name AS project" > profile.json
jq -r '.shared.frames[].name' profile.json
```

```text
ProduceResults 0
Expand 1
```

Open `profile.json` in the speedscope viewer at [speedscope.app](https://www.speedscope.app). The times change from run to run; the frames and their nesting don't. To read the plan as a table instead, run the `PROFILE` statement with `--mode table`. [Tune a query](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/tune-a-query/) covers reading plans.

properties.text:

- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#output): the output flags and `--width`
- [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/): the piped `toon` default and the row cap

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Check that each file holds what its consumer expects: a CSV header for the spreadsheet, and an evented profile for speedscope:

```bash verify
head -n 1 people.csv
jq -r '.profiles[0].type, .profiles[0].unit' profile.json
```

```text
name,role,projects
evented
nanoseconds
```

properties.heading: Script the CLI
properties.text: This guide shows you how to run relate from shell scripts: statements from a file or stdin, output a program can parse, parameters, a time bound per statement, all-or-nothing scripts, and exit codes to branch on. Each command opens the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), runs, and exits, so a script is a sequence of ordinary commands.

properties.heading: Apply scripts in a loop
properties.text:
A script stops at its first failing statement and exits with that statement's code. Statements before it are already committed, unless the script opens a transaction with `.begin` and ends it with `.commit`: then a failure rolls back everything since `.begin`. The [shell dot commands](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/dot-commands/) lists `.begin`, `.commit`, `.rollback` and the others a script can use.

This example applies a directory of migration scripts in order. Each one is a transaction, and the second has a typo:

```bash verify
mkdir -p migrations
cat > migrations/001-ines.cypher <<'EOF'
.begin
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ines'}), (proj:Project {name: 'relate'})
MERGE (p)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(proj);
.commit
EOF
cat > migrations/002-teams.cypher <<'EOF'
.begin
MATCH (p:Person) SET p.team = 'core';
MATCH (p:Person) RETRUN count(p) AS people;
.commit
EOF
```

The loop runs under `set -e`, so the first migration that fails stops it, and the shell exits with relate's code:

```bash verify
cat > migrate.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
for f in migrations/*.cypher; do
  echo "applying $f"
  relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < "$f"
done
echo "all migrations applied"
EOF
bash migrate.sh
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
applying migrations/001-ines.cypher
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.500167,"execute_ms":0.278458,"lex_parse_ms":0.006166,"lower_ms":0.008542000000000001,"parse_ms":0.20925,"plan_ms":0.007458,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.000375},"truncated":false}
applying migrations/002-teams.cypher
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.404584,"execute_ms":0.2205,"lex_parse_ms":0.003708,"lower_ms":0.006709,"parse_ms":0.174375,"plan_ms":0.005,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.00029099999999999997},"truncated":false}
syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "RETRUN"
  MATCH (p:Person) RETRUN count(p) AS people
                   ^
statement 3 of 4 failed; 2 completed, not committed (open transaction); 1 not run
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","column":18,"committed":0,"exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: parse error: unexpected token \"RETRUN\"   MATCH (p:Person) RETRUN count(p) AS people                    ^","retryable":false,"source":"MATCH (p:Person) RETRUN count(p) AS people","statement":3,"statements":4}}
Warning: exiting with an open transaction; rolling back uncommitted changes. Use .commit before exiting to persist them.
exit=6
```

The progress line and the error object's `statement`, `statements` and `committed` say how far the script got. `.begin` counts as statement 1, and `"committed":0` means none of the migration's statements are durable: its `SET` was rolled back. "all migrations applied" never printed.

properties.heading: Bound each statement with a timeout
properties.text:
`--timeout` cancels any statement that runs longer than the duration: `500ms`, `10s`, `2m`, or a bare number of seconds. The bound applies to each statement of a script on its own, and a timed-out statement exits 7:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --timeout 100ms "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS a UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS b RETURN count(*) AS pairs"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: query timed out after 100ms
{"error":{"code":"timeout","exit_code":7,"kind":"execution","message":"query timed out after 100ms","retryable":false}}
exit=7
```

The first line is stderr; the error object is stdout. Without `--timeout`, a statement has no time bound.

properties.heading: Branch on exit codes
properties.text:
Every failure exits with the [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) of its class. When a statement or the store open fails, `--mode envelope` also prints an error object on stdout whose `code` names the class. A usage error (exit 2: an unknown flag, or a bad `--param` or `--timeout` value) or a `--fetch-params` failure (exit 1) prints only its stderr line and leaves stdout empty, so branch on the exit code, not on stdout.

The `case` at the end of this section branches on these codes:

| Exit code | `code`             | Meaning                                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`       | —                  | Success, including an empty result                                                                           |
| `5`       | `conflict`         | Write-write conflict, or another process holds the store                                                     |
| `6`       | `validation_error` | The statement was rejected: syntax, semantic, argument or type error, including a write on a read-only store |
| `7`       | `timeout`          | A statement exceeded `--timeout`                                                                             |

`retryable` is `true` for a write-write conflict (exit 5) and for a `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` refusal while other statements hold the shared pool (exit 1, kind `resource`; reachable when statements run concurrently, as under `relate serve`). A one-shot CLI run meets only the first. Running the same statement again can succeed after either. A locked store also exits 5, with `"retryable":false` until the other process exits. [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/) lists every code, including `1` and `2`, and the error object's fields.

Capture the code with `|| status=$?`, which also keeps `set -e` from stopping the script, then branch on it:

```bash verify
status=0
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope --timeout 5s "MATCH (p:Person) RETRUN p.name" > result.jsonl 2> error.txt || status=$?
case "$status" in
  0) echo "ok" ;;
  5) echo "conflict" ;;
  6) echo "rejected: $(head -n 1 error.txt)" ;;
  7) echo "timed out" ;;
  *) echo "failed with exit code $status" ;;
esac
```

```text
rejected: syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "RETRUN"
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| What you see                                                                                             | Cause                                                                                                                                           | Remedy                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The `relate` help text, and exit code 0, instead of results                                              | A script was redirected into `relate` without the word `query`                                                                                  | Run `relate query --database <path> --mode envelope < <script>`                                                                               |
| `Error: invalid --param value: parameter <name>: …`, exit code 2                                         | A `--param` value that starts like JSON (a digit, `-`, `"`, `[` or `{`) doesn't parse; a date such as `2026-11-07` counts                       | Quote the whole argument in single quotes and fix the JSON, or JSON-quote a string: `'since="2026-11-07"'`                                    |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5                                             | Another process holds the store                                                                                                                 | Wait for it to exit, or read with `--read-only` (a directory store can be read beside its writer; a `.rl` file only while no writer holds it) |
| `warning: result truncated to 100 rows (the statement returned <total>); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows` | With agent mode on (a detected agent harness, for example), a piped statement prints at most 100 rows, and the envelope says `"truncated":true` | Pass `--max-rows 0` to print every row, or bound the result with `LIMIT`                                                                      |
| `note: write statement changed nothing; the graph is unchanged` on stderr                                | Not an error: a write matched nothing, often a `MATCH` with no rows                                                                             | Check the `MATCH`; the exit code stays 0                                                                                                      |

properties.heading: Open the store read-only for reads
properties.text:
A script step that only reads opens the store with `--read-only`. relate never writes or checkpoints a [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) store, and a write fails before it changes anything:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Zed'})"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.","retryable":false}}
exit=6
```

properties.heading: Pass parameters
properties.text:
`--param name=value` binds `$name`, and repeats for each parameter. A value that parses as JSON keeps its JSON type. A value that starts like JSON (a digit, `-`, `"`, `[` or `{`) but doesn't parse exits 2. Any other bare word is a string:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --param name=Ines --param since=2026 --param 'tags=["graph","cli"]' 'RETURN $name AS name, $since AS since, $tags AS tags'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER","LIST"],"columns":["name","since","tags"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Ines","since":2026,"tags":["graph","cli"]}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.34808300000000003,"execute_ms":0.194666,"lex_parse_ms":0.021084,"lower_ms":0.043250000000000004,"parse_ms":0.107333,"plan_ms":0.037875,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.01025},"truncated":false}
```

Single quotes keep the shell from expanding `$name` in the statement. To pass a string that starts like a number, such as a date or a version, JSON-quote it: `--param 'since="2026-11-07"'` binds the string `2026-11-07`, where a bare `since=2026-11-07` exits 2. A string that reads as a boolean or `null` needs the same quoting.

For data in a JSON file, `--fetch-params name=<path>` reads the file, parses it, and binds the result. It also accepts an `http(s)` URL. This file holds two people, and the statement merges them into the store:

```bash verify
printf '[{"name": "Ines", "role": "engineer"}, {"name": "Kofi", "role": "maintainer"}]\n' > people.json
relate --database ./team.rl --mode envelope --fetch-params people=people.json 'UNWIND $people AS p MERGE (n:Person {name: p.name}) SET n.role = p.role RETURN count(n) AS merged'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["merged"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"merged":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":2.125458,"execute_ms":1.924125,"lex_parse_ms":0.005458,"lower_ms":0.008334,"parse_ms":0.18954200000000002,"plan_ms":0.005,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.000375},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Pin the output mode
properties.text:
Pass `--mode` on every scripted command. Without it, relate picks the output from where stdout goes, and a script can run in all three places:

| Where stdout goes                                                                                                                                                   | Default output                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A terminal                                                                                                                                                          | `table`                                                                           |
| A pipe or a file                                                                                                                                                    | `jsonl`, one JSON object per row (`--timings` adds one timing line per statement) |
| A pipe or a file, with [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode) on (a detected agent harness, `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1` or `--agent-mode`) | `toon`                                                                            |

For a program, use `--mode envelope`: one JSON object per result set, the [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope), with `columns`, `columnTypes`, `rows` and `truncated`, plus the statement's `timings` and `planCache` ([timings and the plan cache](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache)). An empty result still lists its columns. The [output modes table](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#output) lists the others.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- `relate` on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- `bash`, or another POSIX shell.
- The examples build `team.rl`, the people-and-projects store from [Your first graph in the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/first-graph/), in a new, empty directory. The first step creates it there.

properties.heading: Run statements from a file or stdin
properties.text:
Make a new directory for the examples and move into it, so the first step starts from an empty store:

```bash
mkdir relate-scripting && cd relate-scripting
```

Write the statements to a file, each ending with `;`:

```bash verify
cat > seed.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes;
EOF
```

Then redirect the file into `relate query`. With no statement argument, `query` reads a script from stdin:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < seed.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.884792,"execute_ms":1.53525,"lex_parse_ms":0.060958,"lower_ms":0.022833,"parse_ms":0.328208,"plan_ms":0.014167,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.000458},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["nodes"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"nodes":5}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.08841700000000001,"execute_ms":0.012792000000000001,"lex_parse_ms":0.013417,"lower_ms":0.020583,"parse_ms":0.044417,"plan_ms":0.026875,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.001708},"truncated":false}
```

Each statement prints its own envelope, so the output is JSON Lines. A pipe works the same way as a file:

```bash verify
printf 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people;\nMATCH (p:Project) RETURN count(p) AS projects;\n' | relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.35266699999999995,"execute_ms":0.17525000000000002,"lex_parse_ms":0.031916,"lower_ms":0.048583,"parse_ms":0.11541699999999999,"plan_ms":0.053625,"result_generation_ms":0.000375,"rewrite_ms":0.009458},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["projects"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"projects":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.040834,"execute_ms":0.0029579999999999997,"lex_parse_ms":0.006625,"lower_ms":0.010458,"parse_ms":0.024208,"plan_ms":0.011292,"result_generation_ms":0.000083,"rewrite_ms":0.00075},"truncated":false}
```

For a short list, `-c` takes the statements as one argument, separated by `;`.

Keep the word `query` in a command that reads stdin. Without it, a redirected script is not read at all: relate prints its help and exits 0, so the script looks like it succeeded.

```bash
# Avoid: prints the help text and exits 0; seed.cypher never runs
relate --database ./team.rl < seed.cypher
# Instead:
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < seed.cypher
```

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Read the store back, read-only, with two statements in one `-c` argument. Ines works on `relate` from the first migration, and no one has a `team` from the second:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope -c "MATCH (:Person {name: 'Ines'})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, w.since AS since; MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.team IS NOT NULL RETURN count(p) AS with_team"
```
