properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
List what the store holds after the drops:

```cypher run name=verify
SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type, owningConstraint, state
RETURN name, type, owningConstraint, state
ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name               | type     | owningConstraint | state    |
|--------------------|----------|------------------|----------|
| "index_1b9dcc97"   | "LOOKUP" | null             | "ONLINE" |
| "index_460996c0"   | "LOOKUP" | null             | "ONLINE" |
| "person_role"      | "RANGE"  | null             | "ONLINE" |
| "project_language" | "TEXT"   | null             | "ONLINE" |
| "project_name"     | "RANGE"  | "project_name"   | "ONLINE" |
5 rows
```

Three `ONLINE` indexes besides the two lookup indexes, one of them owned by `project_name`, and the `NodeIndexSeek` plan in the terminal mean the indexes are in place and serve the lookups they were made for.

properties.heading: Load JSON from a URL or a file
properties.text:
This guide shows you how to load a JSON document into a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) with `--fetch-params <name>=<source>`: the CLI reads a file or fetches an `http://` or `https://` URL, parses it as JSON, and binds the whole document as the [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter) `$<name>`. One statement then walks it with `UNWIND` and writes nodes and relationships. The steps write to the store, and each says so.

`--fetch-params` is a flag of the CLI process, not a Cypher clause. The cells on other pages, the clients and `relate serve` have no equivalent: there, read the document in your program and pass it as an ordinary parameter ([use parameters](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/parameters/)).

properties.heading: Fetch the document from a URL
properties.text:
A source that starts with `http://` or `https://` is fetched instead of read. Nothing else changes.

> **Warning: Egress**
>
> A `--fetch-params` URL is a network request made by the CLI process. A sandbox has to allow the host first. A fetched document is untrusted input: a statement that writes what it holds writes whatever the server sent. The [agent safety](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/) guide covers both.

This command writes to `team.rl`:

```bash
relate --database ./team.rl --mode table \
  --fetch-params 'team=https://<host>/<path>/team.json' \
  'UNWIND $team.people AS row MERGE (p:Person {name: row.name}) SET p.role = row.role RETURN count(p) AS people'
```

Quote the whole `<name>=<source>` argument when the URL holds `&` or `?`, so the shell passes it as one word.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
Each of these failures exits before the statement runs and prints one line on stderr, with no error object:

```bash verify
relate --read-only --fetch-params team=missing.json 'RETURN size($team.people) AS people'
```

```text
Error: --fetch-params team: reading missing.json: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

| Message                                                                                                                                                          | Exit code | Cause                                                           | Remedy                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Error: --fetch-params team: reading missing.json: No such file or directory (os error 2)`                                                                       | 1         | The path does not exist, relative to the working directory.     | Check the path, or give an absolute one.                       |
| `Error: --fetch-params team: invalid JSON: trailing characters at line 2 column 1`                                                                               | 1         | The source is not one JSON document, such as a JSON Lines file. | Wrap the lines in one array, or load each line with `--param`. |
| `Error: --fetch-params team: HTTP 404`                                                                                                                           | 1         | The server answered with an error status.                       | Check the URL in a browser or with `curl`.                     |
| `Error: --fetch-params team: reading team.json: source exceeded the 64 MiB cap` (a file) or `Error: --fetch-params team: source exceeded the 64 MiB cap` (a URL) | 1         | The document is larger than 64 MiB.                             | Split it into several files and load each.                     |
| `Error: invalid --fetch-params value: expected name=value`                                                                                                       | 2         | The argument has no `=`.                                        | Write `--fetch-params <name>=<source>` as one argument.        |
| `Error: invalid --fetch-params value: unsupported source (only http, https, and file paths): ftp://x/team.json`                                                  | 2         | A scheme other than `http`, `https` or `file`.                  | Download the file and pass its path.                           |

properties.heading: Know the limits and the egress rules
properties.text:
| Rule            | Value                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sources         | A file path (relative to the working directory, or absolute), a `file://` URL, or an `http://` or `https://` URL. Any other scheme exits with code 2                                              |
| Size            | At most 64 MiB per source; a larger one fails with `source exceeded the 64 MiB cap` and nothing runs                                                                                              |
| Time            | 60 seconds per fetch                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Content         | One JSON document: a map, list, string, number, boolean or null. JSON Lines (one document per line) fails as invalid JSON                                                                         |
| Several sources | `--fetch-params` is repeatable and combines with `--param`. Assignments resolve in command-line order, and the last one for a name wins; a source that a later assignment overrides is never read |
| Network         | No URL allowlist and no signature check: the document has the same trust as a value passed with `--param`. Plain `http://` is accepted for any host                                               |
| Safe mode       | `--safe` does not affect `--fetch-params`: it binds a parameter, not a store. `--safe` refuses a remote `--load` source, which is a store                                                         |
| Failure         | The command exits before the statement runs, so nothing is written                                                                                                                                |

Safe mode leaves the flag working, so a `--safe` run can still load a document:

```bash verify
relate --read-only --safe --mode table --fetch-params team=team.json 'UNWIND $team.projects AS p RETURN p.name AS project LIMIT 5'
```

```text
+------------------+
| project          |
+------------------+
| "relate"         |
| "opencypher-tck" |
+------------------+
```

properties.heading: Look at the document before you write
properties.text:
Bind the file as `$team` and read it without writing anything. `--read-only` on the default in-memory store refuses every write, so this run can only look:

```bash verify
relate --read-only --mode table --fetch-params team=team.json 'UNWIND $team.people AS p RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role, size(p.works_on) AS projects'
```

```text
+---------+--------------+----------+
| name    | role         | projects |
+---------+--------------+----------+
| "Ada"   | "engineer"   | 1        |
| "Grace" | "engineer"   | 2        |
| "Noor"  | "maintainer" | 0        |
+---------+--------------+----------+
```

The parameter has the document's JSON types: objects become maps, arrays lists, and numbers stay numbers. Single quotes around the statement keep the shell from expanding `$team`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([install](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A JSON document: one value per file or response, of up to 64 MiB. The first step writes a small one, so you can follow along in an empty directory.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#fetch-params): `--fetch-params` and `--param`, with their recorded runs.
- [Use parameters](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/parameters/): how a parameter's JSON maps to Cypher types, and the typed constructors.
- [Import a CSV](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/import-csv/): `LOAD CSV` for tabular files.
- [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fetch-params-failed): the `--fetch-params` failures at a stable anchor.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Read the loaded graph back, read-only:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table 'MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, proj.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since'
```

```text
+---------+------------------+-------+
| person  | project          | since |
+---------+------------------+-------+
| "Grace" | "opencypher-tck" | 2022  |
| "Grace" | "relate"         | 2023  |
| "Ada"   | "relate"         | 2024  |
+---------+------------------+-------+
```

Three `WORKS_ON` relationships, as many as the file lists, mean every entry arrived.

properties.heading: Write a JSON file
properties.text:
This file holds the people and projects of the shared example graph: two projects, three people, and who works on which project since when.

```bash verify
cat > team.json <<'JSON'
{"projects": [{"name": "relate", "language": "Rust"},
              {"name": "opencypher-tck", "language": "Gherkin"}],
 "people": [{"name": "Ada", "role": "engineer", "works_on": [{"project": "relate", "since": 2024}]},
            {"name": "Grace", "role": "engineer", "works_on": [{"project": "relate", "since": 2023},
                                                              {"project": "opencypher-tck", "since": 2022}]},
            {"name": "Noor", "role": "maintainer", "works_on": []}]}
JSON
```

properties.heading: Write nodes and relationships
properties.text:
This command writes to a new single-file store, `team.rl`. The first statement creates the projects; the second creates the people and a `WORKS_ON` relationship for each entry in their `works_on` list. Both statements see the same `$team`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --mode table --fetch-params team=team.json 'UNWIND $team.projects AS row
MERGE (proj:Project {name: row.name})
SET proj.language = row.language;
UNWIND $team.people AS row
MERGE (p:Person {name: row.name})
SET p.role = row.role
WITH p, row
UNWIND row.works_on AS w
MATCH (proj:Project {name: w.project})
MERGE (p)-[r:WORKS_ON]->(proj)
SET r.since = w.since
RETURN count(r) AS works_on'
```

```text
+----------+
| works_on |
+----------+
| 3        |
+----------+
```

`MERGE` on each name makes the load repeatable: a second run with the same file updates the same nodes instead of adding copies. Noor has no projects, so `UNWIND` of her empty list produces no row, and she is written by the `MERGE` before it.

properties.heading: Use an ontology
properties.text:
This guide shows you how to store, read, apply and drop an [ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#ontology) with the four `db.ontology.*` procedures, a [preview feature](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#preview-feature) that runs only when `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` is set in the environment of the process that opens the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). In relate, an ontology is one document per store, in the Ontology Graph Spec 1.1.0 shape, written in YAML or JSON. It describes the node and relationship types of the `neo4j` graph in words an agent or a person can read, and its enforceable parts become the store's [graph type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#graph-type) when you apply it.

The steps run in a terminal. The in-browser cells on other pages cannot run them: the WebAssembly (WASM) build has no process environment, so nothing can switch the preview on there.

properties.heading: Apply it as the graph type
properties.text:
`db.ontology.apply()` turns the enforceable parts of the stored document into the graph type and replaces the current one. It checks the existing data first, and fails without changing anything when a node or relationship breaks the result. This command writes to `team.rl`:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl "CALL db.ontology.apply()"
```

The graph type shows up as constraints, which hold without the opt-in:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "SHOW CONSTRAINTS YIELD name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties RETURN name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties ORDER BY labelsOrTypes, type"
```

```text
+-----------------------+------------------------------+---------------+--------------+
| name                  | type                         | labelsOrTypes | properties   |
+-----------------------+------------------------------+---------------+--------------+
| "constraint_bda177ce" | "NODE_KEY"                   | ["Person"]    | ["name"]     |
| "constraint_786ac02f" | "NODE_PROPERTY_EXISTENCE"    | ["Person"]    | ["role"]     |
| "constraint_7d617092" | "NODE_PROPERTY_TYPE"         | ["Person"]    | ["name"]     |
| "constraint_819770c5" | "NODE_PROPERTY_TYPE"         | ["Person"]    | ["role"]     |
| "constraint_1a7131b"  | "NODE_KEY"                   | ["Project"]   | ["name"]     |
| "constraint_18daa608" | "NODE_PROPERTY_TYPE"         | ["Project"]   | ["language"] |
| "constraint_77b97d24" | "NODE_PROPERTY_TYPE"         | ["Project"]   | ["name"]     |
| "constraint_acbf0f7c" | "RELATIONSHIP_PROPERTY_TYPE" | ["WORKS_ON"]  | ["since"]    |
| "constraint_a4500cf5" | "RELATIONSHIP_SOURCE_LABEL"  | ["WORKS_ON"]  | <null>       |
| "constraint_f500c307" | "RELATIONSHIP_TARGET_LABEL"  | ["WORKS_ON"]  | <null>       |
+-----------------------+------------------------------+---------------+--------------+
```

A person without a role now fails, and the statement writes nothing:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --mode table "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Eli'})"
```

```text
semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `constraint_786ac02f` requires properties
```

Descriptions, aliases, `one_of` lists and the other descriptive fields are never applied; `get` keeps returning them. `SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE` prints the graph type as Cypher, and [indexes and constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/indexes-and-constraints/) covers the constraints it holds.

properties.heading: Create the store
properties.text:
This command writes the example graph to a new single-file store, `team.rl`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

Without the opt-in, every procedure call fails with exit code 6, and `SHOW PROCEDURES` does not list them:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "CALL db.ontology.get() YIELD ontology RETURN ontology"
```

```text
semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'ontology' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology
```

properties.heading: Drop the ontology
properties.text:
`db.ontology.drop()` removes the document. The graph type it applied stays until a statement replaces it, such as `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET {}`. This command writes to `team.rl`:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl "CALL db.ontology.drop()"
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                                                                                         | Cause                                                          | Remedy                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'ontology' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` (exit code 6)                                                                           | The process that opened the store has no opt-in.               | Set `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` in that process's environment.      |
| `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: SemanticError: invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature '<name>' (known features: …)` (exit code 1)                                        | A misspelled feature name; the store does not open.            | Spell it `ontology`; separate several features with commas.       |
| `semantic error: Unsupported ontology spec version: '<uri>'. This version of Relate supports up to Ontology Graph Spec 1.1.0 ('https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json').` | The `schema` field names another spec version.                 | Rewrite the document in the 1.1.0 shape with that exact `schema`. |
| ``type error: InvalidArgumentType: db.ontology.set argument `ontology` expects STRING``                                                                                                         | A JSON document passed with `--param` was parsed into a map.   | Pass the document in YAML, or as a JSON-quoted string.            |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.`                                    | `set`, `apply` or `drop` on a store opened with `--read-only`. | Run it without `--read-only`.                                     |
| ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `<constraint>` violated by element `<element id>`: …``                                                                                            | `apply` found existing data that breaks the ontology.          | Fix the element the message names, then apply again.              |
| `semantic error: SemanticError: Ontologies can only be stored for the user database 'neo4j'.`                                                                                                   | The procedure ran on the `system` namespace.                   | Run it on `neo4j`, the default.                                   |

properties.heading: Know where the document lives
properties.text:
The document belongs to the `neo4j` [namespace](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#namespace), the graph that holds user data. `SHOW DATABASES` also lists `system_ontologies`, which no statement can query, reads included:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --namespace system_ontologies --mode table "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
```

```text
semantic error: SemanticError: This database is not queryable. Use the db.ontology.* procedures on the user database 'neo4j' instead.
```

The procedures are the only way to the document. [Namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/namespaces/) explains the three fixed graphs of a store.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([install](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` in the environment of each command that calls a procedure. The steps put it in front of the command, so it applies to that command only.

> **Warning: Served stores**
>
> The opt-in is read once, when the store opens, and is not a per-caller check. On `relate serve`, it exposes all four procedures to every connected client, including `db.ontology.set` and `db.ontology.drop`, which replace or remove the store's document.

properties.heading: Read it back
properties.text:
`db.ontology.get()` returns the stored document: the bytes as stored when the format matches (`'yaml'`, the default), or converted when it does not (`'json'`). This is the query an agent runs before it writes Cypher against the store ([text to Cypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/text-to-cypher/)):

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode jsonl "CALL db.ontology.get('json') YIELD ontology RETURN ontology"
```

```text
{"ontology":"{\"schema\":\"https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json\",\"id\":\"team\",\"version\":\"1\",\"description\":\"Who works on which project, and since when.\",\"nodes\":{\"Person\":{\"label\":\"Person\",\"description\":\"Someone on the team.\",\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"STRING\",\"key\":true},\"role\":{\"type\":\"STRING\",\"must_exist\":true,\"description\":\"engineer or maintainer\"}}},\"Project\":{\"label\":\"Project\",\"description\":\"A code repository the team works on.\",\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"STRING\",\"key\":true},\"language\":{\"type\":\"STRING\"}}}},\"relationships\":{\"WORKS_ON\":{\"type\":\"WORKS_ON\",\"description\":\"A person contributes to a project.\",\"from\":{\"node\":\"Person\"},\"to\":{\"node\":\"Project\"},\"properties\":{\"since\":{\"type\":\"INTEGER\",\"description\":\"the year the person started\"}}}}}"}
```

| Procedure                                    | Mode    | Returns                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `db.ontology.set(ontology :: STRING)`        | `WRITE` | Nothing; stores the document after checking it                            |
| `db.ontology.get(format = "yaml" :: STRING)` | `READ`  | One row, `ontology`: the document as a string, or `null` when none is set |
| `db.ontology.apply()`                        | `WRITE` | Nothing; replaces the graph type with the one the document describes      |
| `db.ontology.drop()`                         | `WRITE` | Nothing; removes the document, and succeeds when none is set              |

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Procedures](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/procedures/): the `db.ontology.*` signatures, the document shape, and the transaction rules.
- [Namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/namespaces/): `neo4j`, `system` and `system_ontologies`.
- [Text to Cypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/text-to-cypher/): give a model the schema before it writes a statement.
- [Indexes and constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/indexes-and-constraints/): the constraints a graph type adds, and how to list them.

properties.heading: Store the ontology
properties.text:
`db.ontology.set` takes the document as a string, checks it against the 1.1.0 schema, and stores it byte for byte, replacing any earlier one. Pass it as a parameter: a YAML document does not look like JSON, so `--param` binds it as a string. This command writes to `team.rl`:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl --param "ontology=$(cat team.yaml)" 'CALL db.ontology.set($ontology)'
```

The double quotes let the shell insert the file; the single quotes keep it from expanding `$ontology`. `set` and `drop` run only as a statement of their own, outside an explicit transaction.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
After the drop, `get` returns `null`:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "CALL db.ontology.get() YIELD ontology RETURN ontology IS NULL AS unset"
```

```text
+-------+
| unset |
+-------+
| true  |
+-------+
```

Before the drop, the `get` output and the `ConstraintValidationFailed` refusal showed the document stored and its graph type in force.

properties.heading: Write the ontology
properties.text:
This file describes the shared example graph: people with a unique name and a required role, projects with a unique name, and who works on which project. The `description` fields are for readers; the `key`, `must_exist` and `type` fields are enforceable.

```bash verify
cat > team.yaml <<'YAML'
schema: https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json
id: team
version: "1"
description: Who works on which project, and since when.
nodes:
  Person:
    label: Person
    description: Someone on the team.
    properties:
      name: {type: STRING, key: true}
      role: {type: STRING, must_exist: true, description: "engineer or maintainer"}
  Project:
    label: Project
    description: A code repository the team works on.
    properties:
      name: {type: STRING, key: true}
      language: {type: STRING}
relationships:
  WORKS_ON:
    type: WORKS_ON
    description: A person contributes to a project.
    from: {node: Person}
    to: {node: Project}
    properties:
      since: {type: INTEGER, description: "the year the person started"}
YAML
```

`schema` must be exactly `https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json`, and `version` is a string. A member the 1.1.0 schema does not define fails at `set`, including the older spellings `mustExist` and `constraint_type`.

properties.heading: Use parameters
properties.text: This guide shows you how to pass values to a [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) as [parameters](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter): the statement names each value `$name`, and the caller binds the values separately, with `--param` on the command line, a JSON block in the cells on this page, or a dict or object in the Python and Node.js [clients](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client). A parameter is always a value and never Cypher, so the statement text stays the same whatever the value holds.

properties.heading: Bind parameters on the command line
properties.text:
`--param <name>=<value>` binds one parameter; repeat it for more, and the last one for a name wins. This step writes the example graph to a new single-file store, `team.rl`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

Then read it with a parameter. Single quotes around the statement keep the shell from expanding `$name` itself:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table --param name=Grace 'MATCH (p:Person {name: $name})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since'
```

```text
+------------------+-------+
| project          | since |
+------------------+-------+
| "opencypher-tck" | 2022  |
| "relate"         | 2023  |
+------------------+-------+
```

The value after `=` is read as JSON when it parses as JSON, and as a string otherwise:

| `--param` value                          | Binds                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name=Grace`, `name='hello world'`, `x=` | A string. A value that does not start with a digit, `-`, `"`, `[` or `{` and is not JSON binds as the string as written; `x=` binds the empty string |
| `n=3`, `f=1.5`, `big=1e3`                | `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `FLOAT`; an integer outside the 64-bit range exits with code 2                                                                   |
| `flag=true`, `none=null`                 | `BOOLEAN`, `NULL`. Only the lowercase JSON words: `TRUE` binds the string `"TRUE"`                                                                   |
| `'tags=["graph", "rust"]'`               | `LIST`                                                                                                                                               |
| `'meta={"source": "cli", "rank": 1}'`    | `MAP`                                                                                                                                                |
| `'day="2026-11-08"'`                     | The string `"2026-11-08"`, JSON-quoted because it starts with a digit                                                                                |
| `day=2026-11-08`                         | Exit code 2: it starts with a digit and is not JSON                                                                                                  |

The last row is the one that bites. A date starts with a digit, so relate tries it as a JSON number and refuses it before the statement runs, with [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) 2:

```bash verify
relate --read-only --param day=2026-11-08 'RETURN date($day) AS day'
```

```text
Error: invalid --param value: parameter day: invalid parameter JSON: trailing characters at line 1 column 5
```

Quote it as a JSON string, inside the shell's single quotes:

```bash verify
relate --read-only --mode table --param 'day="2026-11-08"' 'RETURN date($day) AS day'
```

```text
+------------+
| day        |
+------------+
| 2026-11-08 |
+------------+
```

The [flags reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#param) has `--param` with its recorded runs. To bind a whole JSON document from a file or a URL, use `--fetch-params` ([load JSON from a URL or a file](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/load-json-from-a-url/)).

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                     | Cause                                                                                                        | Remedy                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name` (exit code 6)                                               | The statement names `$name` and nothing binds it. relate never binds a missing parameter as `null`.          | Bind every parameter the statement names, or remove the reference. |
| `syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "}" (RightBrace) at line 1, col 24`                                            | The statement was in double quotes, so the shell replaced `$name` with an empty string before relate saw it. | Put the statement in single quotes.                                |
| `Error: invalid --param value: parameter day: invalid parameter JSON: trailing characters at line 1 column 5` (exit code 2) | The value starts with a digit, `-`, `"`, `[` or `{` and is not valid JSON.                                   | JSON-quote it: `--param 'day="2026-11-08"'`.                       |
| `Error: invalid --param value: parameter x: $: integer exceeds i64 range` (exit code 2)                                     | An integer beyond the 64-bit range.                                                                          | Pass it as a JSON string.                                          |
| `syntax error: parse error: expected a label name, got "label"`                                                             | A parameter in a label position.                                                                             | Write `$($label)`.                                                 |
| `relate.exceptions.ProgrammingError: query parameters must be a dict mapping string keys to values, got 'list'`             | The Python client got the parameters as a list.                                                              | Pass a `dict` with string keys.                                    |
| `TypeError: query params: "d" must be a plain object`                                                                       | The Node.js client got a `Date`, a `Map` or a class instance.                                                | Use the typed classes, such as `CypherDateTime`, or plain values.  |

properties.heading: Keep values out of the statement text
properties.text:
Building a statement by pasting a value into its text makes the value part of the Cypher. A value that holds a quote then changes what the statement does:

```python
# The input becomes part of the statement text
conn.execute(f"MATCH (p:Person {{name: '{name}'}}) RETURN p.role AS role")
# The input is bound as a value
conn.execute("MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p.role AS role", {"name": name})
```

As a parameter, the same input is only a name that matches nobody:

```json data=tricky
{"name": "Ada'}) OR true //"}
```

```cypher run name=tricky params=tricky
MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name = $name
RETURN count(p) AS matches
```

```table
| matches |
|---------|
| 0       |
1 row
```

A parameter also keeps its type: `3` stays an `INTEGER` and `"3"` a `STRING`, where text formatting turns both into the same characters.

Labels, relationship types and property keys are names, not values, so `MATCH (p:$label)` is a parse error. The dynamic forms take a parameter: `$(<expr>)` for a label or type, and `p[$key]` for a property key.

```json data=names
{"label": "Project", "key": "language"}
```

```cypher run name=dynamic params=names
MATCH (n:$($label))
RETURN n.name AS name, n[$key] AS value
ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name             | value     |
|------------------|-----------|
| "opencypher-tck" | "Gherkin" |
| "relate"         | "Rust"    |
2 rows
```

properties.heading: Load the example graph
properties.text:
The cells on this page run in page order on one in-memory [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). This cell writes the shared graph: Ada, Grace and Noor, the `relate` and `opencypher-tck` projects, and who works on what.

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

properties.heading: Pass a list of rows
properties.text:
A list of maps and `UNWIND` write many rows with one statement. This cell writes two more people:

```json data=newcomers
{"people": [{"name": "Ines", "role": "engineer"}, {"name": "Kofi", "role": "reviewer"}]}
```

```cypher run name=unwind params=newcomers
UNWIND $people AS row
MERGE (p:Person {name: row.name})
SET p.role = row.role
RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role
```

```table
| name   | role       |
|--------|------------|
| "Ines" | "engineer" |
| "Kofi" | "reviewer" |
2 rows · nodes created: 2, properties set: 4, labels added: 2
```

properties.heading: Pass typed values
properties.text:
On the command line and in the cells, a parameter arrives as a JSON value: a string, number, boolean, null, list or map. A point, a temporal value or a vector is built inside the statement from one of those with its constructor. The clients can also send most of them as typed values.

| Type      | CLI and cells: the JSON value and the constructor                                         | Python                                                                  | Node.js                                                                                       |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Point     | `{"latitude": 45.5231, "longitude": -122.6765}` or `{"x": 1, "y": 2}`, then `point($loc)` | `relate.Point(4326, -122.6765, 45.5231)` (`x` is the longitude)         | `new CypherPoint(4326, -122.6765, 45.5231)`                                                   |
| Date      | `"2026-11-08"`, then `date($day)`                                                         | `datetime.date`                                                         | `new CypherDate(2026, 11, 8)`                                                                 |
| Datetime  | `"2026-11-08T09:30:00Z"`, then `datetime($at)`                                            | `datetime.datetime`                                                     | `new CypherDateTime(2026, 11, 8, 9, 30, 0, 0, 0)`: the last argument is the offset in seconds |
| Duration  | `"PT90M"`, then `duration($span)`                                                         | `relate.Duration(seconds=5400)` or `datetime.timedelta`                 | `new CypherDuration(0, 0, 5400, 0)`: months, days, seconds, nanoseconds                       |
| Vector    | a list, then `vector($focus, 3, FLOAT32)`                                                 | a list and `vector()`; a vector read from a result binds back unchanged | a list and `vector()`; a `CypherVector` read from a result binds back unchanged               |
| List, map | a JSON array or object                                                                    | `list` or `tuple`, `dict`                                               | an array, a plain object                                                                      |

A map stays a map on every surface: `{"latitude": 45.5231, "longitude": -122.6765}` is a `MAP` until `point()` turns it into a point. The cell builds each type from the JSON values and reports what arrived:

```json data=typed
{"loc": {"latitude": 45.5231, "longitude": -122.6765},
 "day": "2026-11-08", "at": "2026-11-08T09:30:00Z", "span": "PT90M",
 "focus": [0.9, 0.1, 0.2], "tags": ["graph", "rust"], "meta": {"source": "cell", "rank": 1}}
```

```cypher run name=typed params=typed
RETURN valueType(point($loc)) AS loc, valueType(date($day)) AS day,
       valueType(datetime($at)) AS at, valueType(duration($span)) AS span,
       valueType(vector($focus, 3, FLOAT32)) AS focus,
       valueType($tags) AS tags, valueType($meta) AS meta
```

```table
| loc              | day             | at                        | span                | focus                                  | tags                             | meta           |
|------------------|-----------------|---------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------|----------------|
| "POINT NOT NULL" | "DATE NOT NULL" | "ZONED DATETIME NOT NULL" | "DURATION NOT NULL" | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL" | "LIST<STRING NOT NULL> NOT NULL" | "MAP NOT NULL" |
1 row
```

The same values from each surface. Each program prints the type every parameter arrived as:

### CLI

```bash verify
relate --read-only --mode table --param 'loc={"latitude": 45.5231, "longitude": -122.6765}' --param 'day="2026-11-08"' --param 'at="2026-11-08T09:30:00Z"' --param 'span="PT90M"' --param 'focus=[0.9, 0.1, 0.2]' --param 'tags=["graph", "rust"]' --param 'meta={"source": "cli", "rank": 1}' 'RETURN valueType(point($loc)) AS loc, valueType(date($day)) AS day, valueType(datetime($at)) AS at, valueType(duration($span)) AS span, valueType(vector($focus, 3, FLOAT32)) AS focus, valueType($tags) AS tags, valueType($meta) AS meta'
```

```text
+------------------+-----------------+---------------------------+---------------------+----------------------------------------+----------------------------------+----------------+
| loc              | day             | at                        | span                | focus                                  | tags                             | meta           |
+------------------+-----------------+---------------------------+---------------------+----------------------------------------+----------------------------------+----------------+
| "POINT NOT NULL" | "DATE NOT NULL" | "ZONED DATETIME NOT NULL" | "DURATION NOT NULL" | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL" | "LIST<STRING NOT NULL> NOT NULL" | "MAP NOT NULL" |
+------------------+-----------------+---------------------------+---------------------+----------------------------------------+----------------------------------+----------------+
```

### Python

```python run name=typed-python
import datetime

import relate

conn = relate.connect(":memory:", read_only=True)
row = conn.execute(
    """
    RETURN valueType($loc) AS loc, valueType($day) AS day, valueType($at) AS at,
           valueType($span) AS span, valueType(vector($focus, 3, FLOAT32)) AS focus,
           valueType($tags) AS tags, valueType($meta) AS meta
    """,
    {
        "loc": relate.Point(4326, -122.6765, 45.5231),
        "day": datetime.date(2026, 11, 8),
        "at": datetime.datetime(2026, 11, 8, 9, 30, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc),
        "span": relate.Duration(seconds=90 * 60),
        "focus": [0.9, 0.1, 0.2],
        "tags": ["graph", "rust"],
        "meta": {"source": "python", "rank": 1},
    },
).single()
for key, value in row.items():
    print(f"{key}: {value}")
conn.close()
```

```text
loc: POINT NOT NULL
day: DATE NOT NULL
at: ZONED DATETIME NOT NULL
span: DURATION NOT NULL
focus: VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL
tags: LIST<STRING NOT NULL> NOT NULL
meta: MAP NOT NULL
```

### Node.js

```js run name=typed-node
const { Database, CypherPoint, CypherDate, CypherDateTime, CypherDuration } = require("@relate/relate");

const conn = Database.open(":memory:", { readOnly: true }).connect();
const row = conn.query(
  `RETURN valueType($loc) AS loc, valueType($day) AS day, valueType($at) AS at,
          valueType($span) AS span, valueType(vector($focus, 3, FLOAT32)) AS focus,
          valueType($tags) AS tags, valueType($meta) AS meta`,
  {
    loc: new CypherPoint(4326, -122.6765, 45.5231),
    day: new CypherDate(2026, 11, 8),
    at: new CypherDateTime(2026, 11, 8, 9, 30, 0, 0, 0),
    span: new CypherDuration(0, 0, 90 * 60, 0),
    focus: [0.9, 0.1, 0.2],
    tags: ["graph", "rust"],
    meta: { source: "node", rank: 1 },
  },
).single();
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(row)) console.log(`${key}: ${value}`);
```

```text
loc: POINT NOT NULL
day: DATE NOT NULL
at: ZONED DATETIME NOT NULL
span: DURATION NOT NULL
focus: VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL
tags: LIST<STRING NOT NULL> NOT NULL
meta: MAP NOT NULL
```

A JavaScript `Date` is refused rather than guessed at, because its UTC or local reading is ambiguous; build a `CypherDateTime`. The [types reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/types-and-values/) lists every value type.

properties.heading: Refer to a value with $name
properties.text:
Write `$name` where the value goes. A cell takes its parameters from the JSON block it names with `params=`:

```json data=who
{"name": "Grace"}
```

```cypher run name=projects-of params=who
MATCH (p:Person {name: $name})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
RETURN proj.name AS project, w.since AS since
ORDER BY since
```

```table
| project          | since |
|------------------|-------|
| "opencypher-tck" | 2022  |
| "relate"         | 2023  |
2 rows
```

To ask about Ada, change the value; the statement stays as it is. A parameter can stand anywhere a value can: in a property map, a `WHERE` comparison, a `LIMIT`, a list to `UNWIND`, or the query of a `SEARCH`.

properties.heading: Tune a query
properties.text: This guide shows you how to read the [plan](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#plan) relate chooses for a statement, act on the [notification](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#notification) the planner attaches to it, and prove with a second plan that the fix worked. `EXPLAIN` plans a statement without running it; `PROFILE` runs it and adds what each step did. The example is a lookup by name on the shared graph, planned once without an [index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#index) and once with one.

properties.heading: Act on the notification
properties.text:
Each notification line reads `<severity> <GQLSTATUS> <code>: <description> Remedy: <remedy>`, with `Id <n>:` in front when it concerns one operator. In the envelope, the same entry has the keys `code`, `gql_status`, `severity`, `category`, `title`, `description` and `remedy`, plus `operator_id`. The remedy for a missing index is the statement to run, with the index name derived from the label and the property:

```cypher run name=create-index
CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)
```

```table
(no rows) · indexes added: 1
```

The same remedy in the terminal writes the index to `team.rl`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)"
```

The planner emits these performance notifications. The descriptions are quoted from runs on relate's engine; the parts that name your labels, properties, and counts vary.

| GQLSTATUS | Title                             | Fires on                                                                                                                                 | Example description                                                                                  | Remedy                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `03C91`   | Missing index                     | An equality predicate on a label's property with no range index on that pair                                                             | `the equality predicate on name filters :Person without a range index on (:Person {name})`           | `CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)`                                                                                                                              |
| `03C90`   | All nodes scan                    | A label-less node pattern while the store has a property index                                                                           | `the scan matches every node; consider the property index (:Person(name))`                           | ``Name the label the scan intends (`MATCH (n:<Label>)`); on the index's label the scan becomes an index-backed lookup.``                                                                   |
| `03N90`   | Cartesian product                 | Patterns in one `MATCH` that share no variable                                                                                           | `the MATCH patterns share no join anchor`                                                            | `Give the patterns a join anchor: reuse a node variable across them, or add a pattern that relates their endpoints; otherwise run them as separate queries.`                               |
| `03N91`   | Unbounded variable-length pattern | A variable-length pattern with no upper bound                                                                                            | `the variable-length pattern (p:Person)-[:KNOWS*1..]->(q) has no upper bound`                        | ``Bound the expansion (`[:R*1..5]`) where arbitrary length is not required, or add a selective endpoint/label predicate and a `LIMIT`.``                                                   |
| `03C92`   | Eager aggregation                 | An aggregation whose input is estimated at 100,000 rows or more                                                                          | `the aggregation buffers an estimated 100000 input rows, at or above the 100000-row eager threshold` | ``Reduce the rows reaching the aggregation with a selective label/property predicate or a `LIMIT` before it; profile again to confirm the buffered input shrank.``                         |
| `03C93`   | Estimation miss                   | `PROFILE` only: an operator whose estimate is 10 times its actual rows or more                                                           | `estimated rows 10x or more above the actual rows`                                                   | `Rework the operator's input so the estimate can see the filter (add the selective predicate at the scan, or reorder the join); the estimate is a planner assumption, not a runtime fact.` |
| `03C94`   | Label disjunction scan            | An equality on a property of a label disjunction, such as `(p:Model OR p:Source) AND p.id = 1`, that no range index on each label serves | `the disjunction scan answers per label; consider the property index (:Model(id), :Source(id))`      | `Create a range index on each disjunct label's filtered property: the disjunction then serves as per-label keyed lookups instead of per-label scans.`                                      |

In `--mode table`, the four plan warnings (`03C90`, `03N90`, `03C93` and `03C94`) print in the plan's `Warnings` column and a `Warnings:` line instead of the `Notifications:` block; the envelope carries all of them. A plain run without `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` derives no notifications. The planner also reports a label, relationship type or property key the store does not have (`01N50` to `01N52`), a `CALL` subquery without a scope clause (`01N00`) and a deprecated function or procedure (`01N01`); the [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#notifications) lists every notification with its code and severity, at a stable anchor.

properties.heading: Compare the plans
properties.text:
Plan the same statement again:

```cypher run name=explain-after
EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
RETURN proj.name AS project
```

```table
(no rows)
```

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project"
```

```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project
Plan:
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
| Operator          | Id | Details                                                                               | Estimated Rows |
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
| + ProduceResults  | 0  | 1 item(s)                                                                             | -              |
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
| | + NodeIndexSeek | 1  | RANGE INDEX p:Person(name) WHERE name = 'Ada', (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) | 1              |
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
```

`Expand` became `NodeIndexSeek`: the walk now starts from the one node the index finds, and the plan estimates one row. The `Notifications:` block is gone, and the envelope's `notifications` is an empty list.

The plan viewer holds both recorded plans and what changed between them. In a browser it draws each plan as a tree. **Compare with the index** creates `relate_Person__name` on this page's database, plans the statement without it and with it, and shows the two side by side; pressed again, it drops the index it created (an index the `create-index` cell made stays). **PROFILE** runs the statement for each plan and adds the rows, time and database hits of every operator.

The plan recorded for cell `explain-before`, as `relate --mode table` prints it:

```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project
Plan:
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
| Operator         | Id | Details                                |
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
| + ProduceResults | 0  | 1 item(s)                              |
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
| | + Expand       | 1  | (proj:Project)<-[:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person) |
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
Notifications:
Id 1: INFORMATION 03C91 Relate.Notification.Statement.MissingIndex: the equality predicate on name filters :Person without a range index on (:Person {name}) Remedy: CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)
```

The plan recorded for cell `explain-after`, later on the page:

```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project
Plan:
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
| Operator          | Id | Details                                                                               | Estimated Rows |
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
| + ProduceResults  | 0  | 1 item(s)                                                                             | -              |
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
| | + NodeIndexSeek | 1  | RANGE INDEX p:Person(name) WHERE name = 'Ada', (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) | 1              |
+-------------------+----+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+----------------+
```

What changed between `explain-before` and `explain-after`:

| Measure                              | `explain-before`       | `explain-after`               | Change  |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------- |
| Operators, root first                | ProduceResults, Expand | ProduceResults, NodeIndexSeek | changed |
| Estimated rows where the plan starts | -                      | 1                             | -       |
| Notifications                        | 03C91                  | none                          | 1 fewer |

Notifications on `explain-before`, each with its remedy:

- [`03C91` Missing index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#notif-03c91) on operator 1: the equality predicate on name filters :Person without a range index on (:Person {name}). Remedy: `CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)`

Notifications on `explain-after`: none.

In a browser, the viewer's comparison runs `CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)` on the page's in-memory database only.

Live: the plan is drawn as a tree, and PROFILE runs the statement on the page's database in your browser and adds each operator's rows, time and database hits as bars; the index button creates the index on the page's database, plans the statement with and without it side by side with the changes, and drops it again; a PROFILE downloads as a speedscope file.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Symptom                                                                  | Cause                                                                                                                                          | Remedy                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `semantic error: IndexAlreadyExists` (exit code 6)                       | An index with that name exists.                                                                                                                | Add `IF NOT EXISTS` after the name, or check `SHOW INDEXES` first.                                |
| The plan still shows `Expand` or `NodeByLabelScan` after the index       | The index is on another label or property than the predicate, or the predicate is not an equality or range comparison on the indexed property. | Compare `SHOW INDEXES` with the `03C91` description, which names the label and property it wants. |
| A `01N50`, `01N51` or `01N52` warning, and the statement returns no rows | A label, type or property key is misspelled.                                                                                                   | Correct the name the description quotes.                                                          |
| `03N90` in the envelope, but no `Notifications:` block in the terminal   | Plan warnings print in the table's `Warnings` column.                                                                                          | Read the `Warnings:` line under the plan, or use `--mode envelope`.                               |

properties.heading: Read the plan with EXPLAIN
properties.text:
Prefix the statement with `EXPLAIN`. Nothing runs: writes, procedures and `LOAD CSV` are only planned, so `EXPLAIN` is safe on any statement.

```cypher run name=explain-before
EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
RETURN proj.name AS project
```

```table
(no rows)
```

The cell returns no rows. Its JSON view holds the [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope): `plan` is the operator tree and `notifications` is the planner's advice. In a terminal, `--mode table` prints the same plan as a table and the notifications as text:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project"
```

```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN proj.name AS project
Plan:
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
| Operator         | Id | Details                                |
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
| + ProduceResults | 0  | 1 item(s)                              |
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
| | + Expand       | 1  | (proj:Project)<-[:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person) |
+------------------+----+----------------------------------------+
Notifications:
Id 1: INFORMATION 03C91 Relate.Notification.Statement.MissingIndex: the equality predicate on name filters :Person without a range index on (:Person {name}) Remedy: CREATE INDEX relate_Person__name FOR (n:Person) ON (n.name)
```

Read the table from the bottom up. Each row is an operator; `| +` nests it under the row before it, and the root, `ProduceResults`, returns the rows. `Details` names what the operator works on: here `Expand` starts from every `Project` node, walks `WORKS_ON` backward, and keeps the person named Ada. Nothing narrows the start, so the work grows with the number of nodes that carry the label.

properties.heading: Search by vector similarity
properties.text: This guide shows you how to store embeddings on [nodes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node), index them, and find the nearest nodes with the [SEARCH clause](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#search). The cells run in page order on one [in-memory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#in-memory-store), in your browser and in the docs build, so each step sees what the steps before it wrote.

properties.heading: Combine with full-text search
properties.text: A vector search finds what is near in meaning; a full-text search finds the exact words. To use both, chain one `MATCH … SEARCH` per index through `WITH`, so the second search keeps only what the first found, or fuse the two ranked lists by reciprocal rank. [Hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/) builds the fused version over 40 notes in one statement, and the [search reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#hybrid-search) has both forms.

properties.heading: Create a vector index
properties.text:
Create the index on the property, with the vector length and the similarity function in `OPTIONS`. `WITH [p.role]` declares a [property](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property) that a search can filter on before it ranks.

```cypher run name=create-index
CREATE VECTOR INDEX person_focus IF NOT EXISTS
FOR (p:Person) ON (p.focus) WITH [p.role]
OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 3, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}
```

```table
(no rows) · indexes added: 1
```

The `indexConfig` keys contain dots, so quote them in backticks or single quotes; an unquoted `vector.dimensions` is a parse error. The similarity function is `'cosine'` (the default) or `'euclidean'`. The [search reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#vector-index-options) lists every option and its default.

properties.heading: Filter inside the search
properties.text:
Put the filter inside the parentheses. It runs before the ranking and the `LIMIT`, so the search still returns two people when one of the nearest neighbors does not match:

```cypher run name=filtered params=question
MATCH (p:Person)
SEARCH p IN (VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR $question WHERE p.role = 'engineer' LIMIT 2) SCORE AS score
RETURN p.name AS name, round(score, 4) AS score
ORDER BY score DESC
```

```table
| name    | score  |
|---------|--------|
| "Grace" | 0.989  |
| "Ada"   | 0.6184 |
2 rows
```

Noor, the second nearest, is a maintainer, so Ada takes the second place. The filter may name only the properties in the index's `WITH [...]` list, compared with simple comparisons or `IN` a list, joined by `AND`. A `WHERE` after the `SEARCH` clause filters only the rows the search already returned, so it can leave fewer than `LIMIT`.

The result is an ordinary match, so the next clause can walk the graph from it:

```cypher run name=then-traverse
MATCH (p:Person)
SEARCH p IN (VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR [0.2, 0.2, 0.9] LIMIT 1) SCORE AS score
MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_ON|MAINTAINS]->(proj:Project)
RETURN p.name AS name, collect(proj.name) AS projects
```

```table
| name   | projects   |
|--------|------------|
| "Noor" | ["relate"] |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Find the nearest nodes
properties.text:
The question vector leans hard on tests. `SEARCH` binds `p` to the nearest people and `SCORE AS` names the similarity:

```json data=question
{"question": [0.1, 0.9, 0.1]}
```

```cypher run name=nearest params=question
MATCH (p:Person)
SEARCH p IN (VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR $question LIMIT 2) SCORE AS score
RETURN p.name AS name, round(score, 4) AS score
ORDER BY score DESC
```

```table
| name    | score  |
|---------|--------|
| "Grace" | 0.989  |
| "Noor"  | 0.7151 |
2 rows
```

Three rules shape the clause:

- `LIMIT` is required: it is the number of neighbors the index returns.
- The score exists only under the name `SCORE AS` gives it; there is no implicit `score` variable.
- The variable after `SEARCH` is the one the `MATCH` pattern declares, and the query vector cannot refer to it.

A higher score means more similar. The search uses the index's similarity function, so these scores are the ones `vector.similarity.cosine` returns.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
A query vector whose length differs from `vector.dimensions` fails:

```cypher run name=wrong-length expect=error
MATCH (p:Person)
SEARCH p IN (VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR [0.1, 0.9] LIMIT 2) SCORE AS score
RETURN p.name AS name, score
```

```table
error: type error: VectorIndexDimensionalityMismatch
```

| Message                                                           | Cause                                                                                       | Remedy                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type error: VectorIndexDimensionalityMismatch`                   | The query vector's length is not the index's `vector.dimensions`.                           | Embed the question with the same model as the stored vectors.                                                                          |
| `syntax error: UndefinedVariable: variable 'score' not defined`   | The query reads `score` without `SCORE AS`.                                                 | Add `SCORE AS score` after the closing parenthesis.                                                                                    |
| `syntax error: parse error: expected LIMIT, got ")" (RightParen)` | The search has no `LIMIT`.                                                                  | Add `LIMIT <k>` inside the parentheses.                                                                                                |
| `WrongPropertyForVectorSearchFilter`                              | The `WHERE` inside the search names a property the index does not declare.                  | Add the property to the index's `WITH [...]` list, or filter after the search.                                                         |
| A node never comes back, and nothing fails                        | Its property holds a list or vector of another length: the index skips it without an error. | Store vectors with `vector(list, <dimensions>, FLOAT32)` at the index's dimensions; it refuses a list of another length at write time. |

properties.text:

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- The example graph from [your first graph](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/first-graph/): three people and the two projects they work on. The first step creates it, so this page runs on its own.
- Embeddings from the model of your choice. This guide uses three-dimensional vectors so the numbers stay readable; a model's vectors have hundreds of dimensions, and every step works the same way.

properties.heading: Read the score
properties.text:
The two similarity functions return a rebounded score, not a raw cosine or distance. Thresholds belong on these scales:

| Function                            | Range                                                 | Closer means | Examples                                                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vector.similarity.cosine(a, b)`    | 0 to 1                                                | higher       | `1.0` same direction, `0.5` orthogonal, `0.0` opposite            |
| `vector.similarity.euclidean(a, b)` | greater than 0, up to 1: `1 / (1 + squared distance)` | higher       | `1.0` identical; `[0, 0]` and `[3, 4]` give `0.03846153989434242` |
| `vector_distance(a, b, <metric>)`   | the raw metric                                        | lower        | `EUCLIDEAN` for `[0, 0]` and `[3, 4]` gives `5.0`                 |

```cypher run name=scores
RETURN vector.similarity.cosine([1, 0], [1, 0]) AS same,
       vector.similarity.cosine([1, 0], [0, 1]) AS orthogonal,
       vector.similarity.cosine([1, 0], [-1, 0]) AS opposite,
       vector.similarity.euclidean([0, 0], [3, 4]) AS euclidean,
       vector_distance(vector([0, 0], 2, FLOAT32), vector([3, 4], 2, FLOAT32), EUCLIDEAN) AS distance
```

```table
| same | orthogonal | opposite | euclidean           | distance |
|------|------------|----------|---------------------|----------|
| 1.0  | 0.5        | 0.0      | 0.03846153989434242 | 5.0      |
1 row
```

The similarity functions take a list or a typed vector; `vector_distance` takes typed vectors only. The [search reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#functions) lists the metrics.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/): index DDL, every `SEARCH` form, options and defaults, and the functions.
- [Hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/): vector and full-text search fused in one statement.
- [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/): the procedure forms and what to write instead.

properties.heading: See the search on 40 real vectors
properties.text:
Three readable vectors hide what a search does among hundreds of dimensions. The 40 notes in this cell come from the [hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/) recipe, with the same text and vectors: notes from three working sessions of one project, each with the 384-dimension vector that recipe's `hash-384` embedder computed. That embedder [hashes lowercased words and character trigrams](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/#embeddings-computed-ahead-of-time), so it measures shared words rather than meaning, which is enough to see the mechanics. The cell stores each note with its session and its first topic, and creates a cosine index that can filter on the session:

```json data=notes src=https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/data/notes.json
{
  "data_block": "notes",
  "inline": false,
  "url": "https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/data/notes.json",
  "media_type": "application/json",
  "bytes": 76107,
  "sha256": "f70448d164c694ffaf673a17e903f036fc01f5af037eba68d390c5c6ee0790e8",
  "shape": {"notes":"array of 40 objects"},
  "first": {"notes":{"id":"n01","session":"session-1","topics":["planning"],"text":"Relay kickoff: ticket intake, the agent console and billing all live in one monorepo.","e":"array of 384 numbers"}}
}
```

```cypher run name=load-notes params=notes
UNWIND $notes AS r
CREATE (:Note {id: r.id, text: r.text, session: r.session, topic: r.topics[0],
               embedding: vector(r.e, 384, FLOAT32)});
CREATE VECTOR INDEX note_embedding IF NOT EXISTS
FOR (n:Note) ON (n.embedding) WITH [n.session]
OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 384, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}};
MATCH (n:Note)
RETURN count(n) AS notes, count(DISTINCT n.session) AS sessions
```

```table
| notes | sessions |
|-------|----------|
| 40    | 3        |
1 row · nodes created: 40, properties set: 200, labels added: 40, indexes added: 1
```

SEARCH n IN (VECTOR INDEX note_embedding FOR $v WHERE n.session = $session LIMIT $k) SCORE AS score
RETURN n.id AS id, n.session AS session, round(score, 4) AS score, n.text AS text
ORDER BY score DESC, id

An index ranks with the similarity function it was created with. To rank with the other one without a second index, order by the function; this statement reads every note instead of using the index:

```cypher run name=recall-euclidean params=recall
MATCH (n:Note)
WITH n, vector.similarity.euclidean(n.embedding, $v) AS score
ORDER BY score DESC, n.id LIMIT $k
RETURN n.id AS id, n.session AS session, round(score, 4) AS score, n.text AS text
```
