The top 5 by `recall` for "what did we decide about oauth tokens", as recorded with k = 5:

| Rank | id  | session   | score  | text                                                                          |
| ---- | --- | --------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | n02 | session-1 | 0.6252 | Customer login goes through Auth0; refresh tokens live in HttpOnly cookies.   |
| 2    | n25 | session-2 | 0.5692 | Refresh tokens rotate on every use once Okta is live.                         |
| 3    | n03 | session-1 | 0.5585 | OAuth callbacks are published to Kafka so the audit service sees every login. |
| 4    | n15 | session-2 | 0.5536 | Migrate customer login from Auth0 to Okta before the April renewal.           |
| 5    | n04 | session-1 | 0.5435 | Each tenant gets its own Kafka topic for ticket events.                       |

The picture places the 40 vectors of the `notes` block (384 dimensions) on their first two principal components, which hold 7.2% and 6.4% of the variance, computed when the page was recorded. The cross is the question vector `v`, and the rings mark the top 5, numbered by rank.

Live: a k slider runs the page's search statements on its database in your browser with that k, and the view marks the ids the engine returns.

![The 40 vectors of notes on two principal components, with the question and its top 5](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/element-vector-explorer-1-light.svg)

Three things to notice:

- The picture flattens 384 dimensions into two, so a ringed note can sit farther from the cross than one the search skipped. The engine ranks in all 384 dimensions; the picture only shows which notes it returned.
- With the pre-filter on, the notes outside session 3 grey out and the search still returns `k` notes, all from session 3: the filter runs before the ranking and the `LIMIT`.
- The `hash-384` vectors have length 1, so cosine and euclidean rank the notes in the same order and only the scores differ. For unit vectors the squared distance is `2 - 2 * cosine`, and both scores fall as it grows.

A question can only be searched against vectors from the model that embeds it, so a sentence of your own cannot join these notes. The recipe [Turn a question into the relate docs you need](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/query-the-relate-docs/#ask-your-own-question) searches docs sections embedded with the bge-small-en-v1.5 model, and in a browser it can download that model, embed a question you type, and search with it.

properties.heading: Store the vectors
properties.text:
Give each person a `focus` vector: how much of their work goes to the engine, the tests, and the docs. Pass the vectors as a [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter) and store each one with `vector(list, dimensions, FLOAT32)`. The typed vector is also a guard: a list of the wrong length fails the statement with `type error: vector() dimension does not match list` instead of being stored.

```json data=focus
{"people": [
  {"name": "Ada", "focus": [0.9, 0.1, 0.2]},
  {"name": "Grace", "focus": [0.3, 0.9, 0.1]},
  {"name": "Noor", "focus": [0.2, 0.3, 0.9]}
]}
```

```cypher run name=store-vectors params=focus
UNWIND $people AS row
MATCH (p:Person {name: row.name})
SET p.focus = vector(row.focus, 3, FLOAT32)
RETURN p.name AS name, valueType(p.focus) AS type
ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name    | type                                   |
|---------|----------------------------------------|
| "Ada"   | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL" |
| "Grace" | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL" |
| "Noor"  | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL" |
3 rows · properties set: 3
```

The coordinate type is a bare keyword, such as `FLOAT32`, `FLOAT64`, `INT8` or `INT64`; the [search reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#functions) lists every accepted spelling.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
`SHOW INDEXES` lists the index, the properties it covers (the vector property, then the `WITH` properties) and its state:

```cypher run name=verify
SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, state
WHERE type = 'VECTOR'
RETURN name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, state
```

```table
| name             | type     | labelsOrTypes | properties               | state    |
|------------------|----------|---------------|--------------------------|----------|
| "note_embedding" | "VECTOR" | ["Note"]      | ["embedding", "session"] | "ONLINE" |
| "person_focus"   | "VECTOR" | ["Person"]    | ["focus", "role"]        | "ONLINE" |
2 rows
```

Two `ONLINE` indexes, `person_focus` and `note_embedding`, and two rows from the nearest-node search mean the index serves the query.

properties.heading: Use relate from a web page
properties.text: This guide shows you how to embed relate in a web app through the `@relate/relate-wasm` package: serve the engine as static files, run it in a module worker, keep a graph in the Origin Private File System (OPFS), and read what comes back. [Run relate in the browser](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/browser/) builds the same pieces step by step. The calls and messages here come from the WebAssembly (WASM) build this site ships, run in Chrome 157 and in Node.js, and from its `relate.d.ts`.

properties.heading: Add the client
properties.text:
The package is `@relate/relate-wasm`. Its glue, `relate.js`, fetches `relate_bg.wasm` from beside itself and imports its `snippets/` directory the same way. Install the package, then serve the four entries as files, unchanged, from one directory:

```bash
npm install @relate/relate-wasm
mkdir -p public/relate
cp -R node_modules/@relate/relate-wasm/{relate.js,relate_bg.wasm,trap.js,snippets} public/relate/
```

Vite copies `public/` to the built site as it is. Load the glue at runtime, by URL, so the bundler never rewrites it:

```js
const engine = (file) => new URL(`/relate/${file}`, self.location.origin).href;
const relate = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ engine('relate.js'));
await relate.default();
```

This site does the same with `/wasm/relate.js`. Serve `relate_bg.wasm` with `Content-Type: application/wasm`. With another type, the glue logs a warning and falls back to a slower load.

To pass the engine's location yourself, `relate.default({ module_or_path: <url> })` takes a URL, a `Response`, bytes or a compiled `WebAssembly.Module`. Passing the URL on its own still works, and logs a deprecation warning.

properties.heading: Bind parameters and read typed values
properties.text:
`execute(statement, params_json)` returns the [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope) as JSON text. The queries in this section run on the team graph that every embed guide uses, which one `CREATE` writes:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

A write returns no rows; its envelope's `stats` holds the eleven counters, with `nodes_created` at `5` here. A read's `rows` hold one object per row, keyed by the column names in `RETURN`.

```cypher run name=read
MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'})
RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since
ORDER BY since
```

```table
| name    | since |
|---------|-------|
| "Grace" | 2023  |
| "Ada"   | 2024  |
2 rows
```

From a worker, with the project as a [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter):

```js
const result = JSON.parse(db.execute(
  'MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since',
  JSON.stringify({ project: 'relate' }),
));
// result.columns      ["name","since"]
// result.columnTypes  ["STRING","INTEGER"]
// result.rows         [{"name":"Grace","since":2023},{"name":"Ada","since":2024}]
// result.error        null
```

Parameters go in as one JSON object, or `null` for none. A nested object is an ordinary map, even with a `__type` key, so build typed values in Cypher: `date($d)`, `point($p)`.

Values come back as JSON. A node is `{"id", "kind": "node", "labels", "properties"}`, a relationship `{"id", "kind": "relationship", "type", "start_node", "end_node", "properties"}`, and a path a list of them in order. Dates, times and durations are ISO 8601 strings. A point is `{"crs", "srid", "x", "y"}` when cartesian, plus `"z"` in 3D, or `{"crs", "srid", "longitude", "latitude"}` when geographic, plus `"height"` in 3D. The JSON text carries every integer exactly, but `JSON.parse` rounds one beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (9007199254740991). [Value shapes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/api/wasm/#value-shapes) lists each type.

properties.heading: Choose the thread
Group writes in a transaction
Handle errors
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**`Error: storage error: OPFS needs a dedicated worker`.** `RelateDb.open()` ran on the page's thread, or in a shared or service worker. Move the engine into a dedicated worker.

**`storage locked: opfs://<name>`.** Another worker of the same site holds the store, in this tab or another. Send it every statement instead of opening a second handle, or close the other handle with `free()`.

**`OPFS name must be 1-64 characters from [A-Za-z0-9_-]`.** The name after `opfs://` has a dot, a slash or another character outside that set: `opfs://team.rl` fails, `opfs://team` opens.

**`OPFS open requires an opfs://name URI; use new RelateDb() for :memory:`.** `RelateDb.open()` got a path, a `file://` URL or `:memory:`. The browser build opens only OPFS stores and in-memory ones; a `.rl` file cannot be opened.

**`failed to fetch Wasm: 404 Not Found fetching '<url>'`.** `relate_bg.wasm` is not beside `relate.js` at the URL the glue resolved; another failing status shows in place of `404 Not Found`. Copy the four entries into one served directory, or pass the file's URL as `module_or_path`.

**The console warning starts with `` `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` failed because your server does not serve Wasm with `application/wasm` MIME type. ``** The engine still loads, more slowly, through `WebAssembly.instantiate`. Configure the server to send that type for `.wasm`.

**`null pointer passed to rust`.** The handle was used after `free()`. Open a new one.

properties.heading: Open a store
properties.text:
`new RelateDb()` opens an in-memory store. To keep the graph in OPFS, open the store by name in the worker instead. This open is writable, because the app writes to it; `RelateDb.open('opfs://team', true)` opens it [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only):

```js
const db = await relate.RelateDb.open('opfs://team');
```

The name is 1 to 64 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`. The [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) is created when it does not exist, and its files live under `relate/<name>/` in the site's OPFS root. Each statement is durable when `execute()` returns, so a reload, or a terminated worker, keeps every write.

| To                            | Call                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Open read-only                | `RelateDb.open('opfs://team', true)`: every write fails with `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase` |
| Empty the store               | `db.reset()`: wipes `opfs://team` and reopens it empty; a reload stays empty                 |
| Release it in the same worker | `db.free()`, then `RelateDb.open()` again                                                    |

One open handle holds a store at a time, read-only or not. A second open of the same name from any worker of the site, while the first is open, rejects with `storage locked: opfs://team`. A worker that ends, including on a reload, releases it.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- A project that a bundler builds. The bundling facts on this page were checked with Vite 5.4.21.
- For an OPFS store: a browser with module workers, OPFS, and its synchronous access handles. Chrome 157 was checked; this page makes no claim about other browsers.

properties.heading: Read result metadata
properties.text:
The rest of the envelope describes the statement. `notifications` and `plan` are filled on `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`: the notifications say what the planner noticed, such as a label that does not exist, and `plan` holds the operator tree; on a plain run they are `[]` and `null`. `elapsed_ms`, `parse_ms`, `plan_ms` and `execute_ms` time the statement and change on every run. [The envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/api/wasm/#the-envelope) lists every key.

`renderResult(envelopes)` turns a list of envelope texts into the text table this site's cells print.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [WebAssembly API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/api/wasm/): every export, the envelope, the OPFS rules and what the browser build leaves out.
- [Run relate in the browser](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/browser/): a page that keeps the team graph in OPFS, step by step.
- [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-storage-locked): the storage and engine messages, with their causes.
- [Limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/): what the engine does not do on any surface.
- [Embedded graph in an app](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#embedded-graph-in-an-app): the problem the browser build solves.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
From the page, send the worker a statement that reads the engine's version:

```cypher run name=version
CALL dbms.components() YIELD name, versions
WHERE name = 'Relate'
RETURN versions[0] AS version
```

```table
| version |
|---------|
| "1.0.1" |
1 row
```

The envelope's `rows` hold `[{"version":"1.0.1"}]`. For an OPFS store, write one node, reload the page, and count the nodes again: the count includes it.

properties.heading: Use the C ABI
properties.text: This guide shows you how to embed relate in a C program through its C application binary interface (ABI): link the library, open a store, run statements, read typed values, pass parameters, group writes in transactions, and handle both halves of the error channel. The ABI is `relate.h` plus `librelate_ffi`, and the Node.js, Java, Go and Swift [clients](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) are built on the same library. Each program on this page writes to a store it creates, and each one runs on its own.

properties.heading: Add the client
properties.text:
Each release attaches a `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` archive (`cypherlite-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` up to and including 0.16.1) per platform to the [releases page](https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases), with `<target>` one of `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`. The archive holds `include/relate.h` and the static and shared libraries.

Compile against the header and link the shared library. An rpath lets the program find the library when it runs. On macOS, the release library's install name is the absolute path it was built at, so an rpath finds it only after `install_name_tool` gives it an rpath-relative name, once per unpacked archive:

```bash
install_name_tool -id @rpath/librelate_ffi.dylib <dir>/librelate_ffi.dylib   # macOS only
cc -I<dir>/include app.c -L<dir> -lrelate_ffi -Wl,-rpath,<dir> -o app
```

`<dir>` is where you unpacked the archive. Every program on this page was built with that command. `relate_abi_version()` returns `2`, the ABI the header describes.

properties.heading: Bind parameters and read typed values
properties.text: A result's cells are typed value handles, and a statement's parameters go in through a builder of the same kinds.

properties.heading: Follow the ownership rules
properties.text:
The return type is the rule: a `char *` belongs to the caller, and a `const char *` belongs to relate.

| Thing                                                             | Owner      | Freed by                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate_database`, `relate_connection`, `relate_query_result`     | Caller     | `relate_database_close`, `relate_disconnect`, `relate_destroy_result` |
| Every `relate_value` handle                                       | The result | `relate_destroy_result`; there is no per-value free                   |
| Every `const char *` a result or value accessor returns           | The result | `relate_destroy_result`                                               |
| A `char **error_json` string, and `relate_conn_commit`'s bookmark | Caller     | `relate_free_string`                                                  |
| A params builder root and its children                            | Caller     | `relate_params_free` on the root                                      |

Copy anything you keep before destroying its result. A `relate_database` can be shared across threads, but a `relate_connection` cannot: serialize every call on one connection, or give each thread its own.

properties.heading: Group writes in a transaction
Handle errors
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Symptom                                                                                                                                                              | Cause                                                                                                                            | Remedy                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cells read as `NULL` after a `RELATE_OK`                                                                                                                             | The statement failed, and the error rode the result.                                                                             | Test `relate_result_is_error(r)` and read `relate_result_error_json(r)`.                                                                                                                                   |
| `{"code":"Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError","gql_status":"42000","stage":"internal","retryable":false,"message":"internal error"}` from `relate_database_open` | A storage failure, most often another writable open of the same store.                                                           | Set `RELATE_FFI_LOG=1` to see the original message on stderr; close the other handle, or open with `relate_database_open_read_only`.                                                                       |
| `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <names>` in an error result                                                                                | The statement names a `$parameter` the builder does not hold.                                                                    | Put every named value; a bound null counts.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `null out pointer` from `relate_conn_commit`                                                                                                                         | `bookmark_out` was `NULL`; the transaction did not commit.                                                                       | Pass the address of a `char *` and free the bookmark afterwards.                                                                                                                                           |
| The loader cannot find `librelate_ffi` when the program starts                                                                                                       | The shared library is not on the runtime search path; on macOS, `dyld` names the absolute path the release library was built at. | Link with `-Wl,-rpath,<dir>` (on macOS, after `install_name_tool -id @rpath/librelate_ffi.dylib <dir>/librelate_ffi.dylib`), or add `<dir>` to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` on Linux or `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` on macOS. |

The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists every engine message with its codes.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text: Run the `open` program, or your own, against a fresh directory. It prints `ABI version 2`, two counter objects with `"nodes_created":5`, and `rows=3` from the read-only reopen. The `team.rl` it leaves behind opens in the CLI too: `relate --database ./team.rl --read-only "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"` counts three people.

properties.heading: Walk the result
Use the Go client
properties.text: This guide shows you how to use the relate Go [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) in an app: the module, how cgo finds the C library, which store to open and how, which Go types values arrive as, how to group writes and retry a conflict, what a result reports about itself, and how to branch on an error. The client calls the engine in your process through cgo; there is no server. Every program on this page writes to a store it creates, using the team graph from the [Go tutorial](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/go/).

properties.heading: Add the client
properties.text:
The module path is `github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go` and the package name is `relate`:

```bash
go get github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go@ef436ce
```

```go
import relate "github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go"
```

Go resolves the module from the repository. It has no version tag of its own, so `go.mod` records a pseudo-version of the commit: `ef436ce`, the commit of relate 1.0.1, is `v0.0.0-20261112130637-ef436ce10a54`. Without `@<commit>`, `go get` takes the newest commit on the default branch, which can be ahead of the release's C library; [Project](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/project/#platforms) lists what each release publishes.

properties.heading: Bind parameters and read typed values
properties.text:
`conn.QueryParams(statement, params)` takes a `map[string]any`; `conn.Query(statement)` is the same with a nil map. Signed and unsigned integers bind as `INTEGER` (an unsigned value above `math.MaxInt64` is refused), strings as `STRING`, slices and arrays as `LIST`, string-keyed maps as `MAP`, and a struct as a `MAP` of its exported fields, keyed by their `json` tag names. A temporal, point or vector has no Go type to bind from: pass its parts and build it in the statement, with `date($joined)` or `vector($focus, 3, FLOAT32)`. `time.Time` is refused, because it has no exported fields. Cells decode to `int64`, `float64`, `string`, `[]any`, `map[string]any`, and the package's own types for graph and temporal values:

```go run name=params
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"

	relate "github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go"
)

const team = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)`

type profile struct {
	Joined string    `json:"joined"`
	Focus  []float64 `json:"focus"`
	Note   string    `json:"note,omitempty"`
}

func main() {
	db, err := relate.Open(":memory:")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer db.Close()
	conn, err := db.Connect()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()
	if _, err := conn.Query(team); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	res, err := conn.QueryParams(`
		MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project})
		RETURN p, w.since AS since ORDER BY since`,
		map[string]any{"project": "relate"})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, row := range res.Rows {
		person := row[0].(relate.Node)
		since := row[1].(int64)
		fmt.Println(person.Properties["name"], person.Labels, "since", since)
	}

	res, err = conn.QueryParams(`
		MATCH (p:Person {name: $name})
		SET p.joined = date($profile.joined), p.focus = vector($profile.focus, 3, FLOAT32)
		RETURN p.joined AS joined, p.focus AS focus, elementId(p) AS id`,
		map[string]any{"name": "Noor", "profile": profile{Joined: "2025-03-01", Focus: []float64{0.25, 0.5, 1}}})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	joined := res.Rows[0][0].(relate.Date)
	focus := res.Rows[0][1].(relate.Vector)
	fmt.Printf("joined %04d-%02d-%02d\n", joined.Year, joined.Month, joined.Day)
	fmt.Println("focus", focus.DType, focus.Floats)

	byID, err := conn.QueryParams("MATCH (p) WHERE elementId(p) = $id RETURN p.name AS name",
		map[string]any{"id": res.Rows[0][2]})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("by element id:", byID.Rows[0][0])
}
```

```text
Grace [Person] since 2023
Ada [Person] since 2024
joined 2025-03-01
focus FLOAT32 [0.25 0.5 1]
by element id: Noor
```

A refused value fails before the statement runs, with a plain `error` that names the parameter, such as `parameter "x": struct type time.Time has no exported fields to bind`. An element id round-trips through a parameter. The [Go API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/api/go/#values) has the Go type of every Cypher kind in both directions.

properties.heading: Group writes in a transaction
Handle errors
properties.text:
A failure the engine reports is a `*relate.Error`, whether it comes from a statement or from the call itself. Match it with `errors.As` and branch on its fields, never on `Message`:

| Field       | Holds                                                                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Code`      | The Neo4j status code, such as `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ParameterMissing`        |
| `GQLStatus` | The five-character GQLSTATUS                                                       |
| `Stage`     | `StageCompile`, `StageRuntime`, or `StageInternal` for a failure at the C boundary |
| `Retryable` | True exactly when re-running the same work can succeed                             |
| `Message`   | The engine's message; `Error()` returns it                                         |

The client's own refusals, a parameter it cannot bind or a result shape that breaks the C contract, are plain `error` values, not `*relate.Error`.

```go run name=errors
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log"

	relate "github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go"
)

const team = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)`

const roleOf = "MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p.role AS role"

func main() {
	db, err := relate.Open(":memory:")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer db.Close()
	conn, err := db.Connect()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()
	if _, err := conn.Query(team); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	_, err = conn.Query(roleOf)
	var e *relate.Error
	if errors.As(err, &e) {
		fmt.Println("message:", e.Message)
		fmt.Println("code:", e.Code)
		fmt.Println("gql_status:", e.GQLStatus, "stage:", e.Stage, "retryable:", e.Retryable)
	}

	_, err = db.ConnectNamespace("archive")
	if errors.As(err, &e) {
		fmt.Println("connect:", e.Message)
	}

	_, err = conn.QueryParams(roleOf, map[string]any{"name": make(chan int)})
	fmt.Println("plain error:", err, "| *relate.Error:", errors.As(err, &e))

	res, err := conn.QueryParams(roleOf, map[string]any{"name": "Noor"})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println(res.Rows[0][0])
}
```

```text
message: semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name
code: Neo.ClientError.Statement.ParameterMissing
gql_status: 42N02 stage: compile retryable: false
connect: semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: archive
plain error: parameter "name": unsupported parameter type chan int | *relate.Error: false
maintainer
```

After a `StageInternal` failure the handle may be unusable: close it and open a new one. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-parameter-missing) lists every engine message with its cause and codes.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Error                                                                                                                      | Cause                                                                                                                | Remedy                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fatal error: 'relate.h' file not found`                                                                                   | cgo has no include path to the header                                                                                | Set `CGO_CFLAGS="-I<directory holding relate.h>"`                                           |
| `ld: library 'relate_ffi' not found`                                                                                       | The linker has no path to the library                                                                                | Set `CGO_LDFLAGS="-L<directory> -lrelate_ffi"`                                              |
| `undefined: relate.Open`                                                                                                   | cgo is off (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, or cross-compiling)                                                                     | Build with `CGO_ENABLED=1` and a C compiler for the target                                  |
| On macOS, `dyld[<pid>]: Library not loaded: <absolute build path>/librelate_ffi.dylib` when the binary starts              | The binary looks for the shared library at the absolute path it was built at, and the library is not there           | Set `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the library's directory, or link the static library              |
| `*relate.Error` `internal error` (`Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, `StageInternal`) from `Open` or `OpenReadOnly` | Another process or an unclosed `*Database` holds the store for writing, or `OpenReadOnly` named a path with no store | Close the other writer, open a directory store read-only beside its writer, or fix the path |
| `*relate.Error` `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …` (`42N18`)                                               | A write or `Checkpoint` on a database opened with `OpenReadOnly`                                                     | Open with `relate.Open` for writes                                                          |

properties.heading: Open a store
properties.text:
`relate.Open(path)` opens a store for writing and creates it when it is missing; `relate.OpenReadOnly(path)` loads an existing one once. The path decides the layout:

| Call                            | Opens                                                                                  | Notes                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate.Open(":memory:")`       | An in-memory store                                                                     | Gone when the database closes                                                         |
| `relate.Open("./team")`         | A directory store                                                                      | Created when missing; another process may read it with `OpenReadOnly` while you write |
| `relate.Open("./team.rl")`      | A single-file store                                                                    | Created when missing; opens only while no other process writes it                     |
| `relate.OpenReadOnly(path)`     | An existing store, [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) | Refuses writes and `Checkpoint`; a missing store is an error, never created           |
| `db.ConnectNamespace("system")` | A connection in another namespace                                                      | `Connect()` is `ConnectNamespace("neo4j")`; names match case-insensitively            |

> **Warning: Close each handle once**
>
> `Close` frees the native handle at once, and the client keeps no record of it. A second `Close`, or any call on a closed `*Database` or `*Connection`, uses freed memory and can crash the process. There is no finalizer either: a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) file stays locked until its `Close`.

Defer `Close` right after a successful open, connections before their database. This program writes `team.rl`, closes it, and reads it back read-only:

```go run name=open
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"

	relate "github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go"
)

const team = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)`

func write(path string) error {
	db, err := relate.Open(path)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer db.Close()
	conn, err := db.Connect()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer conn.Close()
	_, err = conn.Query(team)
	return err
}

func main() {
	if err := write("./team.rl"); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, statErr := os.Stat("team.rl")
	fmt.Println("team.rl exists:", statErr == nil)

	db, err := relate.OpenReadOnly("./team.rl")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer db.Close()
	conn, err := db.Connect()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	res, err := conn.Query("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("people:", res.Rows[0][0])

	_, err = conn.Query("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Lin'})")
	var e *relate.Error
	if errors.As(err, &e) {
		fmt.Println("refused:", e.GQLStatus, e.Code)
	}
}
```

```text
team.rl exists: true
people: 3
refused: 42N18 Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError
```

A `*Database` may be shared between goroutines. A `*Connection` serves one call at a time and the client adds no lock, so serialize the calls that share one, or open one connection per goroutine.

properties.heading: Point cgo at the C library
properties.text:
The package is cgo code that includes `relate.h` and links `-lrelate_ffi`. Its own search paths exist only inside the relate source repository, so a project of yours tells cgo where the extracted archive is:

```bash
export CGO_CFLAGS="-I<directory holding relate.h>"
export CGO_LDFLAGS="-L<directory holding librelate_ffi> -lrelate_ffi"
go build ./...
```

A binary linked that way loads the shared library at run time. On Linux, put its directory in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, or add `-Wl,-rpath,<directory>` to `CGO_LDFLAGS`. On macOS the library's install name is the absolute path it was built at, so an rpath does not help: put its directory in `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`. To ship one self-contained binary instead, on either system, link the static library: put `librelate_ffi.a` alone in a directory, since the linker prefers a shared library when both are present, and on macOS add the framework it needs:

```bash
export CGO_LDFLAGS="-L<directory holding only librelate_ffi.a> -lrelate_ffi -framework CoreFoundation"
go build ./...
```

On Windows, cgo links with MinGW, so generate a MinGW import library from `relate_ffi.dll` first, with `gendef` and `dlltool`. The package needs cgo: with `CGO_ENABLED=0` its files are left out, and the build fails with `undefined: relate.Open`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- Go 1.22 or later and a C compiler, so cgo can build. The programs on this page were built with Go 1.27.3 on macOS.
- The relate C library for your platform: `librelate_ffi` and its header, `relate.h`. Each release attaches them as `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` (`cypherlite-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` up to and including 0.16.1), holding the shared library, the static library, and the header.

properties.heading: Read result metadata
properties.text:
A `*relate.Result` holds every row, decoded before the call returns, and these fields beside `Columns` and `Rows`:

| Field           | Value                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `QueryType`     | `QueryTypeRead` (`"r"`), `QueryTypeWrite` (`"w"`), `QueryTypeReadWrite` (`"rw"`) or `QueryTypeSchema` (`"s"`)                          |
| `Namespace`     | The namespace the statement ran in: its `USE` target, else the connection's                                                            |
| `Bookmark`      | An auto-commit write's bookmark, `"relate:<n>"`; the [Go API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/api/go/#result) lists when it is `""` |
| `Stats`         | The 11 mutation counters, zeros included                                                                                               |
| `Notifications` | The planner's notifications, filled by `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`; an empty slice on a plain run                                          |
| `Plan`          | The plan document under `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE`, else `nil`                                                                             |

The result has no column types or timings.

```go run name=metadata
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"log"

	relate "github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go"
)

const team = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)`

func run(conn *relate.Connection, label, statement string) *relate.Result {
	res, err := conn.Query(statement)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	fmt.Printf("%s: type=%s namespace=%s bookmark=%q columns=%v\n", label, res.QueryType, res.Namespace, res.Bookmark, res.Columns)
	return res
}

func main() {
	db, err := relate.Open(":memory:")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer db.Close()
	conn, err := db.Connect()
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	created := run(conn, "create", team)
	s := created.Stats
	fmt.Println("  nodes", s.NodesCreated, "relationships", s.RelationshipsCreated, "properties", s.PropertiesSet, "labels", s.LabelsAdded)
	run(conn, "read", "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name")
	updated := run(conn, "update", "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'}) SET p.role = 'lead' RETURN p.role AS role")
	fmt.Println("  properties", updated.Stats.PropertiesSet)
	index := run(conn, "index", "CREATE INDEX person_name FOR (p:Person) ON (p.name)")
	fmt.Println("  indexes", index.Stats.IndexesAdded)
	run(conn, "routed", "USE system SHOW DATABASES YIELD name RETURN name")

	explained := run(conn, "explain", "EXPLAIN MATCH (a:Person), (b:Project) RETURN a.name, b.name")
	fmt.Println("plan root:", explained.Plan.Root.Operator)
	for _, n := range explained.Notifications {
		fmt.Println(n.GQLStatus, n.Severity, n.Title)
		fmt.Println("remedy:", n.Remedy)
	}
}
```

```text
create: type=w namespace=neo4j bookmark="relate:1" columns=[]
  nodes 5 relationships 5 properties 13 labels 5
read: type=r namespace=neo4j bookmark="" columns=[name]
update: type=rw namespace=neo4j bookmark="relate:2" columns=[role]
  properties 1
index: type=s namespace=neo4j bookmark="relate:3" columns=[]
  indexes 1
routed: type=r namespace=system bookmark="" columns=[name]
explain: type=r namespace=neo4j bookmark="" columns=[]
plan root: ProduceResults
03N90 INFORMATION Cartesian product
remedy: Give the patterns a join anchor: reuse a node variable across them, or add a pattern that relates their endpoints; otherwise run them as separate queries.
```

The counters follow Neo4j's counting: one per label on each node and one per property written, with schema statements in the index and constraint counters. `EXPLAIN` plans without running, so its counters are all zero. [Notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/notifications/) lists every notification kind.

properties.heading: Verify
Use the Java client
properties.text: This guide shows you how to use the relate Java [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) in an app: the Maven or Gradle dependency, how the jar loads its native engine, which store to open and how, which Java types values arrive as, how to group writes and retry a conflict, what a result reports about itself, and how to branch on an exception. The client runs the engine inside your Java virtual machine (JVM) through JNA (Java Native Access). Every program on this page writes to a store it creates, using the team graph from the [Java tutorial](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/java/).

properties.heading: Add the client
properties.text:
The artifact is `com.relate:relate` and the package is `com.relate`. The jars are attached to each release on the [releases page](https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases), not published to Maven Central, so a build resolves them from the local Maven repository. Each jar carries its POM; install the plain jar with `mvn install:install-file -Dfile=relate-<release>.jar`, and a classifier jar with `-Dclassifier=<classifier>` added. The plain jar carries the engine for all five platforms, about 40 MB; in these blocks `<release>` is the release version:

```xml title="pom.xml"
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.relate</groupId>
  <artifactId>relate</artifactId>
  <version><release></version>
</dependency>
```

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
repositories { mavenLocal(); mavenCentral() }
dependencies { implementation("com.relate:relate:<release>") }
```

For a smaller deployable, depend on one classifier jar instead, which carries one platform's engine. Depend on the plain jar or one classifier jar, never both:

| Classifier       | Platform            |
| ---------------- | ------------------- |
| `osx-aarch_64`   | macOS arm64         |
| `osx-x86_64`     | macOS x86-64        |
| `linux-aarch_64` | Linux arm64, glibc  |
| `linux-x86_64`   | Linux x86-64, glibc |
| `windows-x86_64` | Windows x86-64      |

The names follow the vocabulary of the `os-maven-plugin` build extension for Maven and of `com.google.osdetector` for Gradle. With the extension, `<classifier>${os.detected.classifier}</classifier>` picks the build host's; in a Gradle build that applies `com.google.osdetector`, `"com.relate:relate:<release>:${osdetector.classifier}"` does. A container image built for another platform names its classifier literally. [Project](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/project/#platforms) lists what each release publishes, and where.

Handle errors
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Error                                                                                                                            | Cause                                                                                                                           | Remedy                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RelateException`: `relate: no bundled native library for platform <key> …`                                                      | The classpath has a classifier jar for another platform                                                                         | Depend on the plain jar, or add the classifier the message names                            |
| `RelateException`: `relate: unsupported platform os.name=<name>, os.arch=<arch>; …`                                              | No jar carries an engine for this operating system and architecture                                                             | Run on one of the five platforms in [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)                         |
| `RelateException`: `relate: cannot extract the bundled native library …`                                                         | The cache directory is not writable                                                                                             | Pass `-Drelate.native.cache=<writable directory>`                                           |
| `RelateException`: `incompatible librelate_ffi at <path> …`                                                                      | `RELATE_LIB` points at a library of another C application binary interface (C ABI) version; the client needs version 2          | Unset `RELATE_LIB` to load the jar's engine, or rebuild the library from the same release   |
| `DatabaseException`: `internal error` (`Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, stage `INTERNAL`) from `open` or `openReadOnly` | Another process or an unclosed `Database` in this JVM holds the store for writing, or `openReadOnly` named a path with no store | Close the other writer, open a directory store read-only beside its writer, or fix the path |
| `ClientException`: `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …` (`42N18`)                                                  | A write or `checkpoint()` on a database opened with `openReadOnly`                                                              | Open with `Database.open` for writes                                                        |

properties.heading: Load the native engine
properties.text:
The first use of `Database` in a JVM resolves the engine once:

1. When `RELATE_LIB` is set and not empty, its path is loaded. It is a development override for a library you built, not a deployment mechanism.
2. Otherwise the jar's engine for the running platform is extracted to a cache directory and loaded from there.
3. Otherwise the call throws `RelateException`, naming the platform and the classifier to add.

The system library path, `java.library.path` and `jna.library.path` are never searched. The extracted file is reused by every later JVM:

| Platform | Cache root                                                                                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| macOS    | `~/Library/Caches/relate/native`                                                                 |
| Linux    | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/relate/native` when `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is absolute, else `~/.cache/relate/native` |
| Windows  | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\relate\native`                                                                   |

On a read-only home directory or a `noexec` mount, pass `-Drelate.native.cache=<dir>` to move the cache. On Java 24 or later, pass `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` to the JVM: JNA loads through JNI, and without the flag the JVM prints `WARNING: A restricted method in java.lang.System has been called` on first use.

properties.heading: Add the client
properties.text:
The package is `@relate/relate`:

```bash
npm install @relate/relate
```

npm installs the engine library as the platform package for your system, `@relate/relate-<platform>-<arch>`, with no install script. On a platform without one, `RELATE_LIB` names a library built from source. The client checks the library's ABI version when it loads and refuses one it was not built for.

If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Error                                                                                                                                                                | Cause                                                                                       | Remedy                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Error`: `librelate_ffi not found; looked in (1) the RELATE_LIB environment variable, (2) the platform package @relate/relate-<platform>-<arch> (lib/ directory), …` | npm did not install the platform package, or the platform has none                          | Reinstall without `--omit=optional`, or set `RELATE_LIB` to a library built from source |

| `RelateError`: `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …` (`gqlStatus` `42N18`)                                                                              | A write through a read-only handle                                                          | Open without `readOnly` for writes                                                      |
| `TypeError`: `query params: "<name>" must be a plain object`                                                                                                         | A `Date`, `Map`, `Set` or class instance as a parameter                                     | Pass a `CypherDateTime`, an array, or a plain object                                    |
| `RelateError`: `a synchronous query cannot start while an async query is in flight on this connection`                                                               | A synchronous call while a `queryAsync()` on the same connection is running                 | Await the Promise first, or use a second connection                                     |

properties.heading: Run statements off the main thread
Verify
properties.text:
Write the graph to a directory store and read it back through a read-only handle:

```js run name=verify
const { Database } = require("@relate/relate");

const TEAM = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
`;

Database.open("./team").connect().query(TEAM);

const reader = Database.open("./team", { readOnly: true }).connect();
const row = reader
  .query("MATCH (n) OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[r]->() RETURN count(DISTINCT n) AS nodes, count(r) AS relationships")
  .single();
console.log("nodes:", row.nodes, "relationships:", row.relationships);
```

```text
nodes: 5 relationships: 5
```

Five nodes and five relationships from the read-only handle mean the store was written and read back through the client.

properties.heading: Write statements as tagged templates
properties.text:
`query` is also a template tag. Each `${value}` becomes a parameter (`$p0`, `$p1`, …), never statement text, so a value holding quotes or Cypher stays data:

```js run name=templates
const { Database } = require("@relate/relate");

const TEAM = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
`;

const conn = Database.open(":memory:").connect();
conn.query(TEAM);

const name = "Grace";
const rows = conn.query`
  MATCH (:Person {name: ${name}})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(p:Project)
  RETURN p.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since
`.rows;
for (const row of rows) console.log(row.project, row.since);

const hostile = "Grace'}) DETACH DELETE p //";
console.log("matches:", conn.query`MATCH (p:Person {name: ${hostile}}) RETURN count(p) AS n`.single().n);
console.log("people:", conn.query`MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n`.single().n);
```

```text
opencypher-tck 2022
relate 2023
matches: 0
people: 3
```

A template interpolates values only. To build a clause from parts, assemble the string and pass the values in `params`.

properties.heading: Use the Python client
properties.text: This guide shows you how to use the relate Python [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client), the `relate-db` package, in an app: which store to open and how, which Python types a value arrives as, how to group writes, what a result tells you about itself, how to branch on an error, and how to use a connection from a threaded server. The client runs the engine inside your Python process. Every program on this page uses the same team graph as the [Python tutorial](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/python/), which covers the first program step by step.

properties.heading: Add the client
properties.text:
The package is `relate-db`; the import is `import relate`.

```bash
pip install relate-db
```

`cursor.to_df()` needs pandas and `cursor.to_arrow()` needs pyarrow. Each is an extra: `pip install 'relate-db[pandas]'` or `pip install 'relate-db[arrow]'`.

properties.heading: Bind parameters and read typed values
properties.text:
`execute(statement, params)` takes a dict with string keys, and each value converts to a Cypher value. Results convert back to the most exact Python type available:

| Cypher value                                                           | As a parameter                                                              | In a result                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `STRING`, `BOOLEAN`, `NULL`                        | `int` (64-bit), `float`, `str`, `bool`, `None`                              | The same types                                                                      |
| `DATE`, `LOCAL DATETIME`, `ZONED DATETIME`, `LOCAL TIME`, `ZONED TIME` | `datetime.date`; a naive or an aware `datetime.datetime` or `datetime.time` | The same types, or `relate.Temporal` when the value has nanoseconds or a named zone |
| `DURATION`                                                             | `relate.Duration`, or `datetime.timedelta`                                  | `relate.Duration`, always                                                           |
| `POINT`                                                                | `relate.Point(srid, x, y)`                                                  | `relate.Point`                                                                      |
| `VECTOR`                                                               | A `relate.Vector` from an earlier result                                    | `relate.Vector`                                                                     |
| `LIST`, `MAP`                                                          | `list` or `tuple`, `dict`                                                   | `list`, `dict`                                                                      |

A plain dict stays a map, even with `srid`, `x` and `y` keys; build a point with `relate.Point` or `point($coords)`. `relate.Vector` has no constructor: create a vector in Cypher with `vector($values, <dimensions>, FLOAT32)`. This program stores a start date, a release cycle and an office location on the `relate` project, then reads them back:

```python run name=typed-values
import datetime

import relate

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

conn = relate.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute(TEAM)
conn.execute(
    "MATCH (p:Project {name: 'relate'}) "
    "SET p.started = $started, p.cycle = $cycle, p.office = $office",
    {
        "started": datetime.date(2023, 3, 1),
        "cycle": relate.Duration(days=42),
        "office": relate.Point(4326, 13.4, 52.5),
    },
)
row = conn.execute(
    "MATCH (p:Project {name: 'relate'}) "
    "RETURN p.started AS started, p.cycle AS cycle, p.office AS office, "
    "p.started + p.cycle AS next_release, "
    "datetime('2026-11-08T09:30:00.123456789Z') AS tagged_at, "
    "vector([1.0, 0.5, 0.25], 3, FLOAT32) AS focus"
).single()
for name, value in row.items():
    print(f"{name}: {type(value).__name__} {value}")
conn.close()
```

```text
started: date 2023-03-01
cycle: Duration P42D
office: Point Point(srid=4326, x=13.4, y=52.5)
next_release: date 2023-04-12
tagged_at: Temporal 2026-11-08T09:30:00.123456789Z
focus: Vector vector([1.0, 0.5, 0.25], 3, FLOAT32 NOT NULL)
```

`tagged_at` has nanoseconds, which `datetime.datetime` cannot hold, so it arrives as `relate.Temporal`; its `.text` keeps every digit and `.to_native()` gives the microsecond `datetime`. A `relate.Duration` keeps months, days, seconds and nanoseconds apart, so `PT36H` and `P1DT12H` stay different values.

properties.heading: Group writes in a transaction
properties.text:
A connection commits each statement as its own [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction). Set `conn.autocommit = False` and the first statement opens a transaction; `conn.commit()` keeps it and returns its [bookmark](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bookmark), `relate:<n>`, and `conn.rollback()` discards it. An auto-commit write's bookmark is on `cursor.consume().bookmark`.

```python run name=transaction
import relate

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

conn = relate.connect(":memory:")
print("seed bookmark:", conn.execute(TEAM).consume().bookmark)

conn.autocommit = False
conn.execute(
    "MATCH (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'}) "
    "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Lin', role: 'engineer'})-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(tck)"
)
conn.execute("MATCH (noor:Person {name: 'Noor'}) SET noor.role = 'lead'")
print("commit bookmark:", conn.commit())

conn.execute("MATCH (p:Project) DETACH DELETE p")
conn.rollback()
print("projects:", conn.execute("MATCH (p:Project) RETURN count(p) AS n").single()["n"])
conn.close()
```

```text
seed bookmark: relate:1
commit bookmark: relate:2
projects: 2
```

Setting `autocommit` back to `True` commits an open transaction first. Closing a connection with a transaction open rolls it back.

properties.heading: Handle errors
properties.text:
Every error the engine reports raises a subclass of `relate.Error`, following Python's database API: `ProgrammingError` for a statement mistake, `DataError` for a bad value, `IntegrityError` for a constraint violation, `OperationalError` for opening, locking, namespaces and read-only refusals. Each carries the engine's own classification as attributes:

```python run name=errors
import relate

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

conn = relate.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute(TEAM)

for statement in [
    "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name +",
    "MATCH (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[w:WORKS_ON]->() RETURN w.since / 0",
    "MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p.role AS role",
]:
    try:
        conn.execute(statement)
    except relate.Error as e:
        print(type(e).__name__, e.gql_status, e.stage, e.retryable)

try:
    conn.execute("RETURN $n AS n", {"n": 2**63})
except relate.DataError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e)
conn.close()
```

```text
ProgrammingError 42N06 compile False
DataError 22G03 runtime False
ProgrammingError 42N02 compile False
DataError integer parameter is out of range for a 64-bit Relate integer
```

`gql_status` and `neo4j_code` are the codes to branch on; the [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#python-exception-classes) lists every class and code. `retryable` is `True` only for a failure that a retry of the whole transaction can fix, such as a write-write conflict. An error the Python layer raises itself, like the out-of-range integer, has `None` in all four engine attributes.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Error                                                                                                          | Cause                                                                                                              | Remedy                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OperationalError`: `storage locked: <path>` (for a directory store, `<path>` is `<store>/.cypherlite.writer`) | Another connection or process holds the store for writing                                                          | Close the other writer, or open with `read_only=True` (a directory store allows a reader beside its writer; a `.rl` store does not) |
| `ProgrammingError` with `kind` `WrongThread`                                                                   | The connection was used from a thread other than the one that opened it                                            | Route calls to the owning thread, as in [Use a connection from one thread](#use-a-connection-from-one-thread)                       |
| `OperationalError`: `storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`                    | `read_only=True` on a directory path with no store (a `.rl` path says `storage error: database not found: <path>`) | Create the store with a writable open first, or fix the path                                                                        |
| `OperationalError`: `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …` (`gql_status` `42N18`)                  | A write on a read-only connection                                                                                  | Open without `read_only=True` for writes                                                                                            |
| `ProgrammingError`: `query parameters must be a dict mapping string keys to values, got 'list'`                | `params` was not a dict                                                                                            | Pass `{"name": value}` and refer to it as `$name`                                                                                   |
| `ImportError`: `to_df() needs pandas: pip install 'relate-db[pandas]'`                                         | pandas is not installed                                                                                            | Install the extra named in the message                                                                                              |

properties.heading: Open a store
properties.text:
`relate.connect(database, namespace="neo4j", read_only=False)` opens a store and returns a connection. The path decides the layout:

| Call                                       | Opens                                                                                 | Notes                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate.connect(":memory:")`               | An in-memory store                                                                    | The default; gone when the connection closes                                            |
| `relate.connect("./team")`                 | A directory store                                                                     | Created when missing; another process may read it with `read_only=True` while you write |
| `relate.connect("./team.rl")`              | A [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store) | Created when missing; opens only while no other process writes it                       |
| `relate.connect(path, read_only=True)`     | An existing store, read-only                                                          | Loads once and refuses writes; a missing store is an error, never created               |
| `relate.connect(path, namespace="system")` | The same store, another namespace                                                     | `neo4j` (default), `system` or `system_ontologies`                                      |

A new directory store writes its snapshot with the codec in `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` (`parquet` by default, `json` or `markdown`); an existing store keeps its own. The client has no codec argument. This program creates a directory store with the `json` codec, then reads it back through a read-only connection:

```python run name=open
import os

import relate

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

os.environ["RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT"] = "json"

with relate.connect("./team") as conn:
    conn.execute(TEAM)
print("graph.json written:", os.path.exists("team/graph.json"))

reader = relate.connect("./team", read_only=True)
print("people:", reader.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n").single()["n"])
try:
    reader.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Lin'})")
except relate.OperationalError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e.gql_status)
reader.close()
```

```text
graph.json written: True
people: 3
OperationalError 42N18
```

The `with` block closes the connection, which checkpoints a file-backed store. A read-only connection sees the store as it was when it opened. To change namespaces later, call `conn.set_namespace(name)` between transactions, or name the target in the statement with `USE system`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text: - Python 3.9 or later, and the steps of [Embed relate in a Python app](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/python/) or the equivalent experience.

properties.heading: Read result metadata
properties.text:
A cursor holds every row at once. Beyond the rows, `cur.description` gives a type code per column, `cur.consume()` returns a `ResultSummary` (counters, `query_type`, `namespace`, `bookmark`, timings, `notifications`, `plan`), and `cur.graph()` collects the distinct nodes and relationships the rows carry. Each node and relationship has an [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id), the string `elementId()` returns, which finds it again with `WHERE elementId(n) = $id`.

```python run name=metadata
import relate

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

conn = relate.connect(":memory:")
conn.execute(TEAM)

graph = conn.execute("MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN p, w, proj").graph()
print("nodes:", sorted(n["name"] for n in graph.nodes))
print("relationships:", len(graph.relationships))
ada = graph.nodes[0]
print(ada["name"], ada.element_id, ada.labels)

found = conn.execute(
    "MATCH (n) WHERE elementId(n) = $id RETURN n.name AS name", {"id": ada.element_id}
).single()
print("found by element id:", found.name)

summary = conn.execute("EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person), (q:Project) RETURN p, q").consume()
print("query type:", summary.query_type)
for n in summary.notifications:
    print(n["gql_status"], n["title"])
conn.close()
```

```text
nodes: ['Ada', 'Grace', 'opencypher-tck', 'relate']
relationships: 3
Ada 4:rl-id:n0 ['Person']
found by element id: Ada
query type: r
03N90 Cartesian product
```

A plain run leaves `notifications` empty and `plan` set to `None`; `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` fill both. Rows are `relate.Record` dicts, so `row["name"]` and `row.name` read the same value.
