properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The tool's output already shows what it read. To see the links it followed, ask the store from the CLI, read-only, in the directory the program ran in:

```bash
relate --database ./memory --read-only --mode table "MATCH (e:Episode)-[:MENTIONS]->(x) RETURN e.seq AS seq, x.name AS mentions ORDER BY seq, mentions"
```

```text
+-----+----------+
| seq | mentions |
+-----+----------+
| 1   | "Ada"    |
| 1   | "relate" |
| 2   | "Grace"  |
| 2   | "relate" |
+-----+----------+
```

Each episode links to the person and the project it names, which is the path `recall` follows from `relate` back to both episodes.

properties.heading: Write the tool
properties.text:
The program opens `./memory`, a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store), for writing in a setup block that stands in for the app: it writes the team graph and two episodes from two stand-ups. The `recall` tool opens its own read-only connection on each call. The last lines print the tool as the model sees it and call it twice, the way the agent does, with a name that exists and one that doesn't:

```python run name=recall-tool title="recall_tool.py"
import relate
from langchain.tools import ToolException, tool

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

REMEMBER = """
MERGE (c:Conversation {id: $conversation})
CREATE (e:Episode {seq: $seq, text: $text})-[:IN_CONVERSATION]->(c)
WITH e
UNWIND $mentions AS name
MATCH (x {name: name})
MERGE (e)-[:MENTIONS]->(x)
"""

STORE = "./memory"

# Setup: the app that owns ./memory writes the team graph and two episodes, on a writable connection.
with relate.connect(STORE) as owner:
    if owner.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n").single()["n"] == 0:
        owner.execute(TEAM)
        owner.execute(REMEMBER, {"conversation": "standup-monday", "seq": 1, "text": "Ada fixed the CSV import bug in relate.", "mentions": ["Ada", "relate"]})
        owner.execute(REMEMBER, {"conversation": "standup-tuesday", "seq": 2, "text": "Grace will review the relate release notes.", "mentions": ["Grace", "relate"]})


@tool(parse_docstring=True)
def recall(name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return what memory holds about a person or project: the episodes that mention it, oldest first, then who works on it.

    Args:
        name: The exact name of a person or project, such as "Ada" or "relate".
    """
    # Read-only: the engine refuses every write on this connection.
    with relate.connect(STORE, read_only=True) as conn:
        if conn.execute("MATCH (x {name: $name}) RETURN count(x) AS n", {"name": name}).single()["n"] == 0:
            raise ToolException(f"Nothing in memory is named {name!r}.")
        episodes = conn.execute(
            """
            MATCH (x {name: $name})<-[:MENTIONS]-(e:Episode)-[:IN_CONVERSATION]->(c:Conversation)
            RETURN c.id AS conversation, e.text AS text
            ORDER BY e.seq
            """,
            {"name": name},
        ).fetchall()
        people = conn.execute(
            """
            MATCH (x {name: $name})<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person)
            RETURN p.name AS person, w.since AS since
            ORDER BY since
            """,
            {"name": name},
        ).fetchall()
    return [f"[{r['conversation']}] {r['text']}" for r in episodes] + [
        f"{r['person']} has worked on {name} since {r['since']}" for r in people
    ]


# A ToolException goes back to the model as the tool's answer instead of ending the run.
recall.handle_tool_error = True

# Check: what the model sees, then two calls the way an agent makes them.
print(recall.name, recall.args)
for line in recall.invoke({"name": "relate"}):
    print(line)
print(recall.invoke({"name": "relate-engine"}))
```

```text
recall {'name': {'description': 'The exact name of a person or project, such as "Ada" or "relate".', 'title': 'Name', 'type': 'string'}}
[standup-monday] Ada fixed the CSV import bug in relate.
[standup-tuesday] Grace will review the relate release notes.
Grace has worked on relate since 2023
Ada has worked on relate since 2024
Nothing in memory is named 'relate-engine'.
```

The first call returns both episodes about `relate`, oldest first, and then two lines that no episode stated: they come from the team graph's `WORKS_ON` relationships. The second call returns the `ToolException` message as the tool's answer. The parts that matter:

- **A connection per call.** `create_agent` runs a synchronous tool on a worker thread, and a relate connection belongs to the thread that opened it. Opening inside the tool keeps the open and the statements on one thread, and each call sees every episode the app committed before it.
- **`parse_docstring=True`** takes the `name` argument's description from the docstring's `Args:` section, so the model gets it in the tool's schema; the first line printed shows it.
- **`handle_tool_error = True`** turns a `ToolException` into the tool's answer, so a misspelled name gets a sentence the model can act on instead of ending the run.
- **Every value is a `$parameter`.** The model chooses only `name`; the Cypher is fixed, and the read-only connection refuses a write even if a statement tried one.

properties.heading: Use relate with LangGraph
properties.text: This guide shows you how to give a LangGraph graph long-term memory in a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), from Python. LangGraph's checkpointer keeps each conversation's state; relate keeps what should outlive the conversation, as a graph of episodes linked to the people and projects they mention. Two LangChain tools wrap the relate client, and two nodes call them: one writes an episode, the other recalls what memory holds. relate is reached through those tools, not as LangGraph's `BaseStore` or as its checkpointer. A `BaseStore` gets items by namespace and key, while the tools let recall follow the graph's relationships.

properties.heading: Hand the tools to a model
properties.text:
`remember` and `recall` are LangChain tools, so a chat model can call them itself. Bind them to the model with its `bind_tools` method and run the calls with LangGraph's `ToolNode`:

```python
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode

tools = [remember, recall]
model_with_tools = model.bind_tools(tools)  # model: any LangChain chat model
tool_node = ToolNode(tools)
```

`ToolNode` runs each call on a worker thread, which `Memory` already allows for.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Cause                                                                                                        | Remedy                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Relate connection used from a thread other than the one that opened it: connections are thread-affine (DB-API threadsafety = 1). Create the connection on the thread that uses it.` (`relate.ProgrammingError`) | A connection opened on one thread was used from another, such as a `ToolNode` call or a node under `ainvoke` | Route every statement through one owning thread, as `Memory` does.                                                                               |
| `storage locked: <path>` (`relate.OperationalError`)                                                                                                                                                             | A second process, or a second writable connection, opened `./memory.rl` while the program holds it           | Keep one writer per store. To read while the program runs, use a directory store (`Memory("./memory")`) and open it read-only beside the writer. |
| `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name` (`relate.ProgrammingError`)                                                                                                                      | A tool ran a statement without one of its `$parameters`                                                      | Pass every parameter the statement names in the `params` dict.                                                                                   |

The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists the Python exception class for each engine error.

properties.heading: Lay out the memory graph
properties.text:
Memory attaches to the small team graph the Get started pages use. Each turn becomes an `Episode` node in a `Conversation`, one per LangGraph thread id. The episode `MENTIONS` the people and projects it names, so recall can follow the team graph's own relationships to facts no episode stated. This is a reduced form of the model in [Model agent memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/model-agent-memory/): the thread id sits on a `Conversation` node instead of in `Episode.session`, an episode's `seq` takes the place of its `id` and `at`, and the team graph's `Person` and `Project` nodes stand in for `Entity`. Facts, their two time axes and supersession are left out; that guide adds them for an agent that has to track what is currently true. ```mermaid flowchart LR accTitle: Data model: episodes attach to the team graph accDescr { Each Episode is IN_CONVERSATION of one Conversation, keyed by the LangGraph thread id. An Episode MENTIONS the Person and Project nodes it names. The team graph's WORKS_ON relationships connect people to projects, so recall can add what no episode said. } Episode(("Episode
seq · text")) -- "IN_CONVERSATION" --> Conversation(("Conversation
id")) Episode -- "MENTIONS" --> Person(("Person
name · role")) Episode -- "MENTIONS" --> Project(("Project
name · language")) Person -- "WORKS_ON" --> Project ``` Each Episode is IN_CONVERSATION of one Conversation, keyed by the LangGraph thread id. An Episode MENTIONS the Person and Project nodes it names. The team graph's WORKS_ON relationships connect people to projects, so recall can add what no episode said.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- Python 3.10 or later, with the relate client and LangGraph: `pip install relate-db langgraph`. The package is `relate-db`; the import is `import relate`. The LangGraph code on this page was checked against `langgraph` 1.2.20 and `langchain-core` 1.7.6, as of 2026-11-07.
- No model and no credential. The nodes call the tools directly, so the program runs offline; [Hand the tools to a model](#hand-the-tools-to-a-model) shows where a model fits.

properties.text:

- [Model agent memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/model-agent-memory/): choosing labels and relationships for what an agent remembers.
- [Agent memory](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/agent-memory/): a fuller memory graph, with facts and decisions that supersede older ones.

properties.heading: Write the program
properties.text:
The program opens `./memory.rl`, a single-file store, for writing, and seeds the team graph on its first run. It defines the `remember` and `recall` tools and a two-node graph, then runs two turns in two conversations and prints what memory holds about `relate`. The `finally` closes the store even when a node raises. The last lines read the episodes back on a new [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) connection:

```python run name=memory-graph title="memory_graph.py"
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import TypedDict

import relate
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""


class Memory:
    """A relate store that one dedicated thread opens and runs every statement on."""

    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self._thread = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
        self._conn = self._thread.submit(relate.connect, path).result()

    def run(self, statement: str, params: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
        def execute():
            return [dict(row) for row in self._conn.execute(statement, params or {}).fetchall()]
        return self._thread.submit(execute).result()

    def close(self) -> None:
        self._thread.submit(self._conn.close).result()
        self._thread.shutdown()


# Writable on purpose: the graph's nodes write episodes.
memory = Memory("./memory.rl")
if memory.run("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n")[0]["n"] == 0:
    memory.run(TEAM)


@tool
def remember(conversation: str, text: str, mentions: list[str]) -> int:
    """Store one episode and link it to the people and projects it names."""
    rows = memory.run(
        """
        MERGE (c:Conversation {id: $conversation})
        WITH c
        OPTIONAL MATCH (earlier:Episode)
        WITH c, count(earlier) AS seen
        CREATE (e:Episode {seq: seen + 1, text: $text})-[:IN_CONVERSATION]->(c)
        WITH e
        UNWIND $mentions AS name
        MATCH (x {name: name})
        MERGE (e)-[:MENTIONS]->(x)
        RETURN count(x) AS linked
        """,
        {"conversation": conversation, "text": text, "mentions": mentions},
    )
    return rows[0]["linked"] if rows else 0


@tool
def recall(name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return what memory holds about a person or project, oldest episode first."""
    episodes = memory.run(
        """
        MATCH (x {name: $name})<-[:MENTIONS]-(e:Episode)-[:IN_CONVERSATION]->(c:Conversation)
        RETURN c.id AS conversation, e.text AS text
        ORDER BY e.seq
        """,
        {"name": name},
    )
    people = memory.run(
        """
        MATCH (x {name: $name})<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person)
        RETURN p.name AS person, w.since AS since
        ORDER BY since
        """,
        {"name": name},
    )
    return [f"[{r['conversation']}] {r['text']}" for r in episodes] + [
        f"{r['person']} has worked on {name} since {r['since']}" for r in people
    ]


class State(TypedDict):
    message: str
    mentions: list[str]
    subject: str
    context: list[str]


def write_episode(state: State, config: RunnableConfig) -> dict:
    remember.invoke({
        "conversation": config["configurable"]["thread_id"],
        "text": state["message"],
        "mentions": state["mentions"],
    })
    return {}


def recall_context(state: State) -> dict:
    return {"context": recall.invoke({"name": state["subject"]})}


builder = StateGraph(State)
builder.add_node("write_episode", write_episode)
builder.add_node("recall_context", recall_context)
builder.add_edge(START, "write_episode")
builder.add_edge("write_episode", "recall_context")
builder.add_edge("recall_context", END)
graph = builder.compile(checkpointer=InMemorySaver())

try:
    graph.invoke(
        {"message": "Ada fixed the CSV import bug in relate.", "mentions": ["Ada", "relate"], "subject": "relate"},
        {"configurable": {"thread_id": "standup-monday"}},
    )
    state = graph.invoke(
        {"message": "Grace will review the relate release notes.", "mentions": ["Grace", "relate"], "subject": "relate"},
        {"configurable": {"thread_id": "standup-tuesday"}},
    )
    for line in state["context"]:
        print(line)
finally:
    memory.close()

# Check: the episodes outlive the program's connection.
reader = relate.connect("./memory.rl", read_only=True)
episodes = reader.execute(
    "MATCH (e:Episode)-[:IN_CONVERSATION]->(c:Conversation) RETURN c.id AS conversation, e.seq AS seq ORDER BY seq"
).fetchall()
print(f"{len(episodes)} episodes:", ", ".join(f"{row['seq']} in {row['conversation']}" for row in episodes))
reader.close()
```

```text
[standup-monday] Ada fixed the CSV import bug in relate.
[standup-tuesday] Grace will review the relate release notes.
Grace has worked on relate since 2023
Ada has worked on relate since 2024
2 episodes: 1 in standup-monday, 2 in standup-tuesday
```

The second turn recalls both episodes, though each came from a different conversation. The two lines after them come from the team graph, not from any episode. The parts that matter:

- **One thread owns the connection.** A relate connection is thread-affine: only the thread that opened it may use it. LangGraph runs a `ToolNode`'s calls on worker threads, and under `ainvoke` it runs synchronous nodes there too. So `Memory` opens the store on a dedicated thread and sends every statement there. The same tools then work under `invoke`, `ainvoke` and `ToolNode`.
- **`remember`** merges one `Conversation` per LangGraph thread id, numbers the episode, and links it to every node whose `name` it mentions. Every value goes in as a `$parameter`.
- **`recall`** reads the episodes that mention a subject, oldest first, then follows `WORKS_ON` to who works on it.
- **The mentions are given, not extracted.** In a real agent a model picks them out of the message; in this program they're fixed, so the run is the same every time.

properties.heading: Use relate with LlamaIndex
properties.text: This guide shows you how to put a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) behind a LlamaIndex retriever. Notes live in the store as [nodes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node) with their embeddings as vector [properties](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property), a [vector index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#vector-index) finds the nearest notes to a question, and the retriever follows each hit to the project it's about and the people who work on it. The retriever opens the store read-only on every call. The whole program runs without a model or a credential, LlamaIndex's query engine included.

properties.heading: Answer with a model
properties.text:
Replace the query-engine check at the end of `notes_retriever.py` with a real LLM. `llm` is any LlamaIndex LLM, which comes from that provider's integration package and needs its credential:

```python
engine = RetrieverQueryEngine.from_args(retriever, llm=llm)  # llm: any LlamaIndex LLM
print(engine.query("Where is the release?"))
```

For an agent that decides when to look things up, wrap the retriever as a tool instead and give it to the agent:

```python
from llama_index.core.agent.workflow import FunctionAgent
from llama_index.core.tools import RetrieverTool

notes_tool = RetrieverTool.from_defaults(
    retriever,
    name="team_notes",
    description="Find notes about the team's projects, with each note's project and the people who work on it.",
)
agent = FunctionAgent(tools=[notes_tool], llm=llm)
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                             | Cause                                                                                                                             | Remedy                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type error: VectorIndexDimensionalityMismatch` (`relate.DataError`, `gql_status` `22G03`)          | The question's embedding has a different length from the index's `vector.dimensions`, usually because the embedding model changed | Embed questions with the model that embedded the notes. After a model change, re-embed the notes and recreate the index with the new length. |
| `type error: vector() dimension does not match list` (`relate.DataError`, `gql_status` `22G03`)     | The ingestion step stored an embedding whose length isn't `$dimensions`                                                           | Set the dimensions from the embedding model's output length, as `DIMENSIONS` does.                                                           |
| `storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>` (`relate.OperationalError`) | The retriever's store path names a directory that holds no store; a read-only open never creates one                              | Run the ingestion step first, or fix the path.                                                                                               |
| `storage locked: <path>` (`relate.OperationalError`)                                                | The store is a single-file `.rl` store that the ingestion step holds for writing, and a read-only open refuses it                 | Keep the notes in a directory store, as `./notes` is, so retrieval runs beside ingestion.                                                    |

[Search by vector similarity](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/#if-it-goes-wrong) lists the other `SEARCH` mistakes and their messages.

properties.heading: Lay out the notes
properties.text:
The notes attach to the small team graph the Get started pages use. Each `Note` node holds its text and its embedding and is `ABOUT` one `Project`; the team graph's `WORKS_ON` relationships say who works on that project. The vector index `note_embedding` covers the `embedding` property of every `Note`. ```mermaid flowchart LR accTitle: Data model: notes about the team's projects accDescr { A Note has an id, its text and an embedding, and is ABOUT one Project. A Person WORKS_ON a Project, so the retriever can add who works on the project each note is about. The vector index note_embedding covers the embedding property of every Note. } Note(("Note
id · text · embedding")) -- "ABOUT" --> Project(("Project
name · language")) Person(("Person
name · role")) -- "WORKS_ON" --> Project ``` A Note has an id, its text and an embedding, and is ABOUT one Project. A Person WORKS_ON a Project, so the retriever can add who works on the project each note is about. The vector index note_embedding covers the embedding property of every Note.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- Python 3.10 or later, with the relate client and LlamaIndex's core package: `pip install relate-db llama-index-core`. The package is `relate-db`; the import is `import relate`. The LlamaIndex code on this page was checked against `llama-index-core` 0.14.25, as of 2026-11-08, and uses nothing outside that package.
- An embedding model for your own data: any LlamaIndex embedding model, which is a `BaseEmbedding`. The program's `KeywordEmbedding` stands in for one so the page runs offline.
- For [Answer with a model](#answer-with-a-model) only: a LlamaIndex LLM (large language model) from its integration package, with that provider's credential.
- relate on your `PATH` for [Verify](#verify) ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The setup block wrote four notes with their embeddings. Check them from the CLI, read-only, in the directory the program ran in:

```bash
relate --database ./notes --read-only --mode table "MATCH (n:Note)-[:ABOUT]->(p:Project) RETURN n.id AS id, p.name AS project, valueType(n.embedding) AS embedding ORDER BY id"
```

```text
+------+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| id   | project          | embedding                              |
+------+------------------+----------------------------------------+
| "n1" | "relate"         | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(7) NOT NULL" |
| "n2" | "relate"         | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(7) NOT NULL" |
| "n3" | "opencypher-tck" | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(7) NOT NULL" |
| "n4" | "relate"         | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(7) NOT NULL" |
+------+------------------+----------------------------------------+
```

Every embedding is a typed vector of 7 coordinates, the stand-in model's length. Then check that the index serves them:

```bash
relate --database ./notes --read-only --mode table "SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, state WHERE type = 'VECTOR' RETURN name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, state"
```

```text
+------------------+----------+---------------+---------------+----------+
| name             | type     | labelsOrTypes | properties    | state    |
+------------------+----------+---------------+---------------+----------+
| "note_embedding" | "VECTOR" | ["Note"]      | ["embedding"] | "ONLINE" |
+------------------+----------+---------------+---------------+----------+
```

An `ONLINE` index on `Note.embedding` and two hits per question mean the retriever's search runs on the index.

properties.heading: Write the retriever
properties.text:
The program opens `./notes`, a directory store, for writing in a setup block that stands in for your ingestion step: it writes the team graph, embeds four notes with the embedding model, stores each vector with `vector(…, FLOAT32)`, and creates the index. `NotesRetriever` reads the store on its own read-only connections. The last lines retrieve for two questions, then run the same retriever inside LlamaIndex's query engine:

```python run name=notes-retriever title="notes_retriever.py"
import re

import relate
from llama_index.core.embeddings import BaseEmbedding
from llama_index.core.llms import MockLLM
from llama_index.core.query_engine import RetrieverQueryEngine
from llama_index.core.retrievers import BaseRetriever
from llama_index.core.schema import NodeWithScore, QueryBundle, TextNode

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

NOTES = [
    {"id": "n1", "project": "relate", "text": "Ada fixed the CSV import bug."},
    {"id": "n2", "project": "relate", "text": "Grace will review the release notes."},
    {"id": "n3", "project": "opencypher-tck", "text": "Grace added test scenarios for CSV headers."},
    {"id": "n4", "project": "relate", "text": "Noor tagged the release candidate."},
]

VOCABULARY = ["csv", "import", "release", "notes", "test", "scenarios"]
DIMENSIONS = len(VOCABULARY) + 1


class KeywordEmbedding(BaseEmbedding):
    """Stands in for an embedding model: counts vocabulary words, plus a constant so no vector is zero."""

    def _embed(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        words = re.findall(r"[a-z]+", text.lower())
        return [float(words.count(w)) for w in VOCABULARY] + [0.5]

    def _get_text_embedding(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
        return self._embed(text)

    def _get_query_embedding(self, query: str) -> list[float]:
        return self._embed(query)

    async def _aget_query_embedding(self, query: str) -> list[float]:
        return self._embed(query)


RECALL = """
MATCH (n:Note)
SEARCH n IN (VECTOR INDEX note_embedding FOR $vector LIMIT $k) SCORE AS score
MATCH (n)-[:ABOUT]->(p:Project)
OPTIONAL MATCH (person:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(p)
RETURN n.id AS id, n.text AS text, p.name AS project, collect(person.name) AS people, score
ORDER BY score DESC, id
"""


class NotesRetriever(BaseRetriever):
    """Retrieves notes from a relate store by vector search, with each note's project and its people."""

    def __init__(self, store: str, embed_model: BaseEmbedding, top_k: int = 2):
        super().__init__()
        self._store = store
        self._embed_model = embed_model
        self._top_k = top_k

    def _retrieve(self, query_bundle: QueryBundle) -> list[NodeWithScore]:
        vector = self._embed_model.get_query_embedding(query_bundle.query_str)
        # Read-only: the engine refuses every write on this connection.
        with relate.connect(self._store, read_only=True) as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(RECALL, {"vector": vector, "k": self._top_k}).fetchall()
        return [
            NodeWithScore(
                node=TextNode(id_=r["id"], text=r["text"], metadata={"project": r["project"], "people": sorted(r["people"])}),
                score=r["score"],
            )
            for r in rows
        ]


embed_model = KeywordEmbedding()

# Setup: the app that owns ./notes writes the team graph, the notes and their embeddings, on a writable connection.
with relate.connect("./notes") as owner:
    if owner.execute("MATCH (n:Note) RETURN count(n) AS n").single()["n"] == 0:
        owner.execute(TEAM)
        embeddings = embed_model.get_text_embedding_batch([note["text"] for note in NOTES])
        owner.execute(
            """
            UNWIND $notes AS note
            MATCH (p:Project {name: note.project})
            CREATE (n:Note {id: note.id, text: note.text, embedding: vector(note.embedding, $dimensions, FLOAT32)})-[:ABOUT]->(p)
            """,
            {"notes": [dict(note, embedding=e) for note, e in zip(NOTES, embeddings)], "dimensions": DIMENSIONS},
        )
        owner.execute(
            "CREATE VECTOR INDEX note_embedding IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n:Note) ON (n.embedding) "
            f"OPTIONS {{indexConfig: {{`vector.dimensions`: {DIMENSIONS}, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}}}}"
        )

retriever = NotesRetriever("./notes", embed_model)

# Check: retrieve for two questions, without a model.
for question in ["Where is the release?", "Who worked on CSV import?"]:
    print(question)
    for hit in retriever.retrieve(question):
        print(f"  {hit.score:.4f} {hit.node.node_id} [{hit.node.metadata['project']}; {', '.join(hit.node.metadata['people'])}] {hit.node.get_content()}")

# Check: the same retriever behind LlamaIndex's query engine; MockLLM answers without a model.
engine = RetrieverQueryEngine.from_args(retriever, llm=MockLLM())
response = engine.query("Where is the release?")
print("query engine sources:", ", ".join(hit.node.node_id for hit in response.source_nodes))
```

```text
Where is the release?
  1.0000 n4 [relate; Ada, Grace] Noor tagged the release candidate.
  0.8727 n2 [relate; Ada, Grace] Grace will review the release notes.
Who worked on CSV import?
  1.0000 n1 [relate; Ada, Grace] Ada fixed the CSV import bug.
  0.7311 n3 [opencypher-tck; Grace] Grace added test scenarios for CSV headers.
query engine sources: n4, n2
```

Each hit carries its similarity score, the note, its project, and the people on that project. The score is cosine similarity rescaled to 0 to 1, higher is closer, so `1.0000` is a note whose words match the question's exactly. The query engine retrieves the same two notes for the same question. The parts that matter:

- **One statement per retrieval.** `RECALL` runs the vector [search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#search) with the `SEARCH` clause and walks from each hit to its project and that project's people, so the node LlamaIndex gets back already holds the graph context in its `metadata`.
- **The embedding model sets the dimensions.** The index's `vector.dimensions` and every stored vector must have the model's length. `vector(…, $dimensions, FLOAT32)` refuses a list of another length when it is stored, instead of leaving a note the index skips.
- **A connection per call.** A relate connection belongs to the thread that opened it, and a read-only connection sees the store as it was when it opened. Opening inside `_retrieve` keeps the open and the statement on the thread that runs the retrieval, and each retrieval sees every note committed before it.
- **`MockLLM`** is LlamaIndex's own stand-in for an LLM, in the core package, so the check proves the retriever plugs into `RetrieverQueryEngine` without a model call.

To rank by keywords as well as meaning, add a full-text index and fuse the two result lists by reciprocal rank in the same statement; [Hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/) builds that fused statement.

properties.heading: Use relate with Mastra
properties.text: This guide shows you how to back a Mastra tool with relate from Node.js, behind a read-only guard. The tool's handle opens the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only), so the engine refuses every write on it, and the tool plans each [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) with `EXPLAIN` before it runs only the reads. A Mastra agent gets the tool like any other: the model writes the Cypher, and relate decides what touches the graph.

properties.heading: Give the tool to an agent
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                                                                                           | Cause                                                                                                          | Remedy                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.` (`RelateError`, `gqlStatus` `42N18`) | A write reached the read-only handle                                                                           | Expected: the guard held. Writes belong on a separate, writable handle that the app owns.       |
| `Tool input validation failed for read-graph. …` (the tool result has `error: true`)                                                                                                              | The model's input does not match `inputSchema`                                                                 | Nothing to fix in relate. The model reads the message, which names each field, and calls again. |
| `internal error` (`RelateError`, `stage` `internal`) from `Database.open`                                                                                                                         | The read-only open found no store at the path, or found a single-file `.rl` store that a writable handle holds | Create the store first, or fix the path. To read beside a writer, use a directory store.        |
| `Could not find API key process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for model id anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`                                                                                                     | The agent's provider credential is not in the environment                                                      | Export the provider's key before `generate` runs.                                               |
| `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `@relate/relate`                                                                                                                                                       | The program is an ES module, and ES modules ignore `NODE_PATH`                                                 | Install the packages in the project's own `node_modules`.                                       |

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- Node.js 22.13 or later (`@mastra/core` 1.82.0 requires it), with the relate [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client), Mastra and Zod: `npm install @relate/relate @mastra/core zod`. The Mastra code on this page was checked against `@mastra/core` 1.82.0 and `zod` 4.6.7, as of 2026-11-08.
- For the agent in [Give the tool to an agent](#give-the-tool-to-an-agent) only: a model provider's credential, such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment for an `anthropic/…` model id. Everything before that runs without one.

properties.heading: Write the tool
Use relate with the OpenAI Agents SDK
properties.text: This guide shows you how to back an OpenAI Agents SDK function tool with relate, so a model can write Cypher against a graph and can't change it. The tool opens the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) on each call, plans the model's [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) with `EXPLAIN`, and runs it only when the [plan](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#plan) says it reads. Engine errors go back to the model as data, so it can correct its statement. Everything before the agent loop runs without a credential.

properties.heading: Connect over MCP instead
properties.text:
The SDK can also reach relate's MCP server, which gives the agent relate's own read tool instead of one you write. `MCPServerStdio` starts `relate serve` as a child process when the `async with` block opens, and stops it when the block ends:

```python
import asyncio

from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStdio


async def main():
    async with MCPServerStdio(params={
        "command": "relate",
        "args": ["serve", "--mcp", "stdio", "--database", "./team", "--read-only"],
    }) as relate_mcp:
        team_agent = Agent(name="Team analyst", instructions="Answer questions about the team graph.", mcp_servers=[relate_mcp])
        result = await Runner.run(team_agent, "How many people are on the team?")
        print(result.final_output)


asyncio.run(main())
```

To allow writes, remove `"--read-only"`.

Opened read-only, the server lists two tools, `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, and leaves out `write_cypher`; `read_cypher` takes the Cypher as `statement` and refuses writes either way. [The MCP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/) lists each tool's arguments and refusals.

properties.heading: Give the tool to an agent
properties.text:
Replace the check block at the end of `graph_tool.py` with an agent and a run. This part needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`:

```python
from agents import Agent, Runner

team_agent = Agent(
    name="Team analyst",
    instructions="Answer questions about the team graph with the read_graph tool. Pass every value as a parameter.",
    tools=[read_graph],
)
result = Runner.run_sync(team_agent, "Who works on relate, and since when?")
print(result.final_output)
```

`Agent` uses the SDK's default model unless `model` names one; in 0.24.0 the default is `gpt-5.6-luna`, and `OPENAI_DEFAULT_MODEL` changes it. The runner stops after 10 turns by default (`max_turns`), so a model that keeps retrying a refused statement ends the run with `MaxTurnsExceeded` instead of looping.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Cause                                                                             | Remedy                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `additionalProperties should not be set for object types. This could be because you're using an older version of Pydantic, or because you configured additional properties to be allowed. If you really need this, update the function or output tool to not use a strict schema.` (`agents.exceptions.UserError`, when the tool is defined) | A function tool takes a `dict` parameter, which a strict schema can't describe    | Take a list of name-and-value objects, as `Param` does.                                |
| ``Missing credentials. Please pass an `api_key`, `workload_identity`, `admin_api_key`, or set the `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY` environment variable.`` (`openai.OpenAIError`)                                                                                                                                                      | The runner called the model with no credential set                                | Set `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The check block needs none.                                      |
| `{"error": "semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name", "gql_status": "42N02"}` (the tool's answer)                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The model's statement names a `$parameter` it didn't pass in `params`             | Nothing to fix in the tool: the model reads the error and calls again with the value.  |
| `storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>` (in the tool's `error`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `STORE` names a directory that holds no store; a read-only open never creates one | Create the store with a writable open first, as the setup block does, or fix the path. |

The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists every engine error with its GQLSTATUS code.

properties.heading: Write the tool
properties.text:
The program has three parts. A setup block writes the small team graph the Get started pages use into `./team`, a directory store, standing in for the app that owns the data. The `read_graph` tool takes a statement and its parameters from the model. The last block invokes the tool the way the SDK's runner does, with no model, three times: a read, a delete, and a read that forgets its parameter:

```python run name=graph-tool title="graph_tool.py"
import asyncio
import json

import relate
from agents import function_tool
from agents.tool_context import ToolContext
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

STORE = "./team"
MAX_ROWS = 50

# Setup: the app that owns ./team writes the team graph once, on a writable connection.
with relate.connect(STORE) as owner:
    if owner.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n").single()["n"] == 0:
        owner.execute(TEAM)


class Param(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="The parameter's name, without the $")
    value: str | int | float | bool


@function_tool
def read_graph(statement: str, params: list[Param]) -> str:
    """Run one read-only Cypher statement against the team graph and return its rows as JSON.

    The graph has Person and Project nodes and WORKS_ON, MAINTAINS and KNOWS relationships.

    Args:
        statement: One Cypher statement that only reads.
        params: Values for the statement's $parameters.
    """
    values = {p.name: p.value for p in params}
    try:
        # Read-only: the engine refuses every write on this connection.
        with relate.connect(STORE, read_only=True) as conn:
            # EXPLAIN plans the statement without running it; query type "r" is a pure read.
            kind = conn.execute(f"EXPLAIN {statement}", values).consume().query_type
            if kind != "r":
                return json.dumps({"error": f'refused: the statement\'s query type is "{kind}", and this tool runs only reads ("r")'})
            cur = conn.execute(statement, values)
            rows = [row.data() for row in cur.fetchmany(MAX_ROWS + 1)]
    except relate.Error as e:
        return json.dumps({"error": str(e), "gql_status": e.gql_status})
    return json.dumps({"columns": cur.columns, "rows": rows[:MAX_ROWS], "truncated": len(rows) > MAX_ROWS}, default=str)


async def call(tool, arguments: dict) -> str:
    """Invoke a function tool the way the Runner does, without a model."""
    args = json.dumps(arguments)
    ctx = ToolContext(context=None, tool_name=tool.name, tool_call_id="check", tool_arguments=args)
    return await tool.on_invoke_tool(ctx, args)


# Check: what the model sees, then three calls.
print(read_graph.name, json.dumps(read_graph.params_json_schema["required"]))
print(asyncio.run(call(read_graph, {
    "statement": "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since",
    "params": [{"name": "project", "value": "relate"}],
})))
print(asyncio.run(call(read_graph, {
    "statement": "MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) DETACH DELETE p",
    "params": [{"name": "name", "value": "Ada"}],
})))
print(asyncio.run(call(read_graph, {"statement": "MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p.role AS role", "params": []})))

with relate.connect(STORE, read_only=True) as conn:
    print("people:", conn.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people").single()["people"])
```

```text
read_graph ["statement", "params"]
{"columns": ["name", "since"], "rows": [{"name": "Grace", "since": 2023}, {"name": "Ada", "since": 2024}], "truncated": false}
{"error": "refused: the statement's query type is \"w\", and this tool runs only reads (\"r\")"}
{"error": "semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name", "gql_status": "42N02"}
people: 3
```

The read returns its rows. The delete never runs: its plan says it writes, so the tool refuses it. The third call names `$name` without a value, and the engine's error comes back as the tool's answer with its GQLSTATUS code. The count shows all three people, Ada included. The parts that matter:

- **`params` is a list of `Param`.** The SDK builds a strict JSON schema for every function tool, and a strict schema can't describe a `dict` of arbitrary keys. A list of name-and-value objects can, and the tool turns it back into the dict the client takes.
- **A connection per call.** The SDK runs a synchronous tool with `asyncio.to_thread`, on a worker thread, and a relate connection belongs to the thread that opened it. Opening inside the tool keeps the open, the plan and the run on one thread, and each call sees every commit the app made before it.
- **`call`** builds the `ToolContext` the runner would pass and awaits the tool's `on_invoke_tool`, so the check exercises the same argument parsing and validation a model's call goes through.

Each layer of the guard refuses something different:

| Layer                                            | Refuses                                                               | Enforced by |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `relate.connect(path, read_only=True)`           | Every write and checkpoint on that connection; a path with no store   | The engine  |
| The `EXPLAIN` check (`query_type` must be `"r"`) | Writes (`"w"`, `"rw"`) and schema statements (`"s"`), before they run | The tool    |
| `MAX_ROWS`                                       | Rows beyond the first 50, with `"truncated": true` in the result      | The tool    |

A narrower tool skips model-written Cypher altogether: a fixed statement whose arguments are only the values, such as a project name for `$project`. Keep the read-only connection either way.

properties.heading: Use relate with PydanticAI
properties.text: This guide shows you how to give a PydanticAI agent a tool that reads a relate graph. The tool opens the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) on every call and runs one fixed [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) with a parameter, so the model supplies a value, never Cypher, and the engine refuses any write on the connection. Everything before the model call runs without a credential, because PydanticAI's `FunctionModel` stands in for the model and drives the agent through the tool.

properties.heading: Connect over MCP instead
properties.text:
For an agent that writes its own reads instead of calling one fixed statement, give it relate's MCP server as a toolset. `MCPToolset` takes a FastMCP client; `pip install pydantic-ai` installs FastMCP with it (`fastmcp-slim`, from 3.3 up to but not including 5, with `pydantic-ai` 2.66.0; checked with 4.1.6):

```python
from fastmcp import Client
from fastmcp.client.transports import StdioTransport
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.mcp import MCPToolset

relate_mcp = MCPToolset(Client(StdioTransport(
    "relate", ["serve", "--mcp", "stdio", "--database", "./team", "--read-only"],
)))
agent = Agent("anthropic:claude-opus-5-5", toolsets=[relate_mcp])
print(agent.run_sync("How many people are on the team?").output)
```

To allow writes, remove `"--read-only"`.

The agent starts `relate serve` when a run begins and stops it when the run ends. Opened read-only, the server lists two tools, `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, and leaves out `write_cypher`; `read_cypher` takes the Cypher as `statement` and refuses writes either way. [The MCP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/) lists each tool's arguments and refusals.

properties.heading: Give the tool to a model
properties.text:
Replace the check block at the end of `team_agent.py` with a run on a real model. This part needs the model's credential:

```python
result = agent.run_sync(
    "Who works on relate, and since when?",
    model="anthropic:claude-opus-5-5",
    deps=TeamGraph("./team"),
)
print(result.output)
```

`model` takes any model name PydanticAI accepts, as `<provider>:<model>`. The model can call `team_of`, read the rows, and answer in its own words.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Cause                                                                                                             | Remedy                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>` (`relate.OperationalError`)                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `TeamGraph.path` names a directory that holds no store; a read-only open never creates one                        | Create the store with a writable open first, as the setup block does, or fix the path.   |
| `storage locked: <path>` (`relate.OperationalError`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | The store is a single-file `.rl` store that another connection holds for writing, and a read-only open refuses it | Keep the data in a directory store, as `./team` is, so the tool reads beside the writer. |
| ``Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable or pass it via `AnthropicProvider(api_key=...)` to use the Anthropic provider. To try Pydantic AI without an API key, use the built-in test model: `Agent('test')`. See https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/guides/testing/`` (`pydantic_ai.exceptions.UserError`) | The run names an Anthropic model and no credential is set                                                         | Set the credential, or keep `FunctionModel` for runs that must not call a model.         |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.` (`relate.OperationalError`, `gql_status` `42N18`)                                                                                                 | A write reached the read-only connection                                                                          | Expected: the guard held. Writes belong on the app's own writable connection.            |
| `Tool 'team_of' exceeded max retries count of 1. Consider raising the retry limit, or see the docs on tool retries: https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/tools-advanced/#tool-retries` (`pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnexpectedModelBehavior`)                                                               | The model asked for a project that doesn't exist on two calls in a row, and a tool gets one retry by default      | Raise the limit with `@agent.tool(retries=3)`, or with `retries=` on `Agent`.            |

The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists the Python exception class for each engine error.

The package is `relate-db`; the import is `import relate`. The PydanticAI code on this page was checked against `pydantic-ai` 2.66.0, as of 2026-11-08.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The program's last line already counts the people on a read-only connection. The same check from the CLI, read-only, in the directory the program ran in, also shows the rows the tool returned:

```bash
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode table "MATCH (p:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY name"
```

```text
+---------+--------+
| name    | since  |
+---------+--------+
| "Ada"   | 2024   |
| "Grace" | 2023   |
| "Noor"  | <null> |
+---------+--------+
```

Three people: the refused write left no `Mallory` behind. Ada and Grace work on `relate`, as the agent's answer said. Noor has no `WORKS_ON` relationship to it, because she maintains it.

properties.heading: Write the tool
properties.text:
The program has three parts. A setup block writes the small team graph the Get started pages use into `./team`, a directory store, standing in for the app that owns the data. A directory store lets the tool read while the app writes; a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store) that a writer holds refuses a read-only open. The agent declares `TeamGraph` as its dependency type, and the `team_of` tool reads the store's path from `ctx.deps`. The last block runs the agent with a scripted stand-in for the model, then tries a write on a read-only connection:

```python run name=team-agent title="team_agent.py"
from dataclasses import dataclass

import relate
from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelRetry, RunContext
from pydantic_ai.messages import ModelMessage, ModelResponse, TextPart, ToolCallPart, ToolReturnPart
from pydantic_ai.models.function import AgentInfo, FunctionModel

TEAM = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

TEAM_OF = """
MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project})
RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role, w.since AS since
ORDER BY since
"""

# Setup: the app that owns ./team writes the team graph once, on a writable connection.
with relate.connect("./team") as owner:
    if owner.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n").single()["n"] == 0:
        owner.execute(TEAM)


@dataclass
class TeamGraph:
    path: str


agent = Agent(deps_type=TeamGraph, instructions="Answer questions about the team with the team_of tool.")


@agent.tool
def team_of(ctx: RunContext[TeamGraph], project: str) -> list[dict]:
    """List the people who work on a project, with their role and the year they started.

    Args:
        project: The project's exact name, such as "relate".
    """
    # Read-only: the engine refuses every write on this connection.
    with relate.connect(ctx.deps.path, read_only=True) as conn:
        rows = [row.data() for row in conn.execute(TEAM_OF, {"project": project})]
        if not rows:
            names = [r["name"] for r in conn.execute("MATCH (p:Project) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name")]
            raise ModelRetry(f"No one works on a project named {project!r}. Projects: {', '.join(names)}.")
    return rows


def scripted(messages: list[ModelMessage], info: AgentInfo) -> ModelResponse:
    """Stands in for a model: asks for an unknown project, then for relate, then answers."""
    last = messages[-1].parts[-1]
    if isinstance(last, ToolReturnPart) and isinstance(last.content, list):
        people = ", ".join(f"{p['name']} since {p['since']}" for p in last.content)
        return ModelResponse(parts=[TextPart(f"On relate: {people}.")])
    if len(messages) == 1:
        tool = info.function_tools[0]
        print("tool:", tool.name, "|", tool.description, "|", tool.parameters_json_schema["properties"])
        return ModelResponse(parts=[ToolCallPart("team_of", {"project": "relate-engine"})])
    print("retry:", last.content)
    return ModelResponse(parts=[ToolCallPart("team_of", {"project": "relate"})])


# Check: run the agent with the scripted stand-in, so no model is called.
result = agent.run_sync("Who works on relate?", model=FunctionModel(scripted), deps=TeamGraph("./team"))
print(result.output)

# Check: a write on a read-only connection fails in the engine.
with relate.connect("./team", read_only=True) as conn:
    try:
        conn.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Mallory'})")
    except relate.OperationalError as e:
        print(e.gql_status, e)
    print("people:", conn.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people").single()["people"])
```

```text
tool: team_of | List the people who work on a project, with their role and the year they started. | {'project': {'description': 'The project\'s exact name, such as "relate".', 'type': 'string'}}
retry: No one works on a project named 'relate-engine'. Projects: opencypher-tck, relate.
On relate: Grace since 2023, Ada since 2024.
42N18 semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
people: 3
```

The scripted model prints the tool as the model sees it, asks for a project that doesn't exist, reads the retry message, asks again, and answers from the rows. The write fails in the engine with `42N18`, and the count shows the three people the setup wrote. The parts that matter:

- **A connection per call.** PydanticAI runs a synchronous tool on a worker thread, and a relate connection belongs to the thread that opened it. Opening inside the tool keeps the open and the statement on one thread, and each call sees every commit the app made before it. Each open reads the store from disk. For a large store, one connection owned by a dedicated thread avoids that cost, as the `Memory` class in [the LangGraph guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/integrations/langgraph/#write-the-program) does. A long-lived read-only connection sees only the commits made before it opened.
- **The docstring is the schema.** PydanticAI takes the tool's description and the `project` parameter's description from the docstring; the `tool:` line shows both.
- **`ModelRetry`** sends its message back to the model as the tool's answer, in this program with the projects that do exist, so the model can correct itself; the `retry:` line shows it. A tool gets one retry by default; `@agent.tool(retries=3)` allows more.
- **`FunctionModel`** is a model in name only: a Python function that receives the messages and the tool definitions and returns the next response. A test can drive the agent through every tool path with it and never make a model call.

Each layer of the guard refuses something different:

| Layer                                  | Refuses                                                                                 | Enforced by |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `relate.connect(path, read_only=True)` | Every write and checkpoint on that connection; a path with no store                     | The engine  |
| The fixed statement `TEAM_OF`          | Any Cypher the model writes: the model passes only `project`, which binds as `$project` | The tool    |

A read-only connection sees the graph as it was when it opened, which is why the tool opens one per call instead of keeping one for the life of the agent.

properties.heading: Use relate with the Vercel AI SDK
properties.text: This guide shows you how to back a Vercel AI SDK tool with relate from Node.js, behind a read-only guard. The tool's handle opens the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only), so the engine refuses every write on it. The tool also plans each statement with `EXPLAIN` first and runs only reads. The model writes the Cypher; relate decides what touches the graph.

properties.heading: Give the tool to a model
If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                                                                                           | Cause                                                                                                          | Remedy                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.` (`RelateError`, `gqlStatus` `42N18`) | A write reached the read-only handle                                                                           | Expected: the guard held. Writes belong on a separate, writable handle that the app owns.            |
| `internal error` (`RelateError`, `stage` `internal`) from `Database.open`                                                                                                                         | The read-only open found no store at the path, or found a single-file `.rl` store that a writable handle holds | Create the store first, or fix the path. To read beside a writer, use a directory store.             |
| `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt`                                                                                                                                                | A row holds an integer outside ±(2^53 − 1), which the client returns as a `bigint`                             | Convert `bigint` values before returning them, as the `JSON.stringify` replacer in `readGraph` does. |
| The tool's answers miss recent writes (no error)                                                                                                                                                  | The read-only handle sees the graph as it was when it opened                                                   | Open a new read-only handle per request, or on a schedule.                                           |

properties.text:
- Node.js 22 or later (the AI SDK's `ai` 7 and `@ai-sdk/anthropic` 4 require it), with the relate client, the AI SDK and Zod: `npm install @relate/relate ai zod`. The AI SDK code on this page was checked against `ai` 7.0.165 and `zod` 4.6.7, as of 2026-11-07.
- For the model call in [Give the tool to a model](#give-the-tool-to-a-model) only: a provider package and its credential, such as `@ai-sdk/anthropic` (checked against 4.0.99, as of 2026-11-07) with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment. Everything before that runs without one.

properties.heading: Replay the calls over MCP
properties.text:
relate's MCP server offers the same kind of tool without code. `relate serve --mcp stdio --read-only` lists `read_cypher`, which plans each statement with `EXPLAIN` and refuses one whose plan writes, and `get_schema`, which reads the labels and relationship types from the store instead of from a description written by hand. [Use relate with the Claude Agent SDK](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/integrations/claude-agent-sdk/) registers that server with an agent framework.

The trace below replays this page's read as the `tools/call` requests an agent host sends to that server. It is a replay of the calls, not a transcript of a model run: no model chose them. It runs in your browser, on an in-memory store holding the team graph from the setup block:

```cypher run name=team
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

The program's first check call, with its statement and `params`, as a cell:

```json data=project
{"project": "relate"}
```

```cypher run name=works-on params=project
MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since
```

```table
| name    | since |
|---------|-------|
| "Grace" | 2023  |
| "Ada"   | 2024  |
2 rows
```

The trace sends the schema request, then that read:

```json data=mcp-calls
{"steps": [
  {"tool": "get_schema",
   "note": "The labels, property keys and relationship types that `readGraph`'s description names by hand, read from the store.",
   "arguments": {}},
  {"tool": "read_cypher",
   "note": "The statement and `params` of the program's first `readGraph.execute` call, sent as `read_cypher`.",
   "arguments": {"statement": "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since",
    "parameters": {"project": "relate"}}}
]}
```

The trace starts on the database the cells up to `team` build. Each step below ran when the page was recorded, one after another on that database, through the mapping the MCP tryout uses; each result is what relate serve's tool returns for that call, built from the engine's result. No agent and no server took part in the recording.

**Step 1 of 2: `get_schema`.** The labels, property keys and relationship types that `readGraph`'s description names by hand, read from the store.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{}}}
```

| Label   | Nodes | Properties                       | Relationships out                                          |
| ------- | ----- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Person  | 3     | name (String), role (String)     | WORKS_ON to Project; KNOWS to Person; MAINTAINS to Project |
| Project | 2     | language (String), name (String) | -                                                          |

**Step 2 of 2: `read_cypher`.** The statement and `params` of the program's first `readGraph.execute` call, sent as `read_cypher`.

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since","parameters":{"project":"relate"}}}}
```

| name  | since |
| ----- | ----- |
| Grace | 2023  |
| Ada   | 2024  |

The rows match cell `works-on`'s recording.

Live: Step sends the next call and Play all sends the rest, each to the page's database in your browser on the store the cells build up to the trace's starting cell, and each step shows the result `relate serve`'s tool returns for that call, built from the engine's live result; a trace that would write twice starts on an emptied database, and the database is emptied again when the trace ends, so the page's cells run on what they write.

The rows are the ones `readGraph` returned, in the server's reply instead of the tool's `{ columns, rows, truncated }`. The delete the program sends is refused by `read_cypher` too, with the server's own message; the [Claude Agent SDK page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/integrations/claude-agent-sdk/#replay-the-agents-calls) replays that refusal.

The program's last line already counts the people on a fresh read-only handle. The same check from the CLI, read-only, in the directory the program ran in:
