```bash
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"rows":[{"people":3}],"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Write the tool
Migrate from a vector store
properties.text: This guide shows you how to move retrieval from a vector store, such as Chroma, LanceDB or pgvector, into relate. Each record of an id, a text, some metadata, and an embedding becomes a [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node): the embedding a typed vector [property](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property) under a [vector index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#vector-index), the metadata properties and [relationships](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship). The top-k query becomes a `SEARCH` clause with the same filter, and nothing is re-embedded. The cells run in page order on one in-memory store, in your browser and in the docs build, on a five-record export; the sources themselves are described here, not run.

properties.heading: Create the schema
properties.text:
Create the keys and the indexes before the first row arrives. `vector.dimensions` is the model's dimension count; this export uses 4 so the numbers stay readable. `WITH [c.source, c.year]` declares the two metadata fields a search can filter on:

```cypher run name=schema
CREATE CONSTRAINT chunk_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (c:Chunk) REQUIRE c.id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT document_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (d:Document) REQUIRE d.id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE VECTOR INDEX chunk_embedding IF NOT EXISTS
  FOR (c:Chunk) ON (c.embedding) WITH [c.source, c.year]
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 4, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'}};
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX chunk_text IF NOT EXISTS FOR (c:Chunk) ON EACH [c.text]
```

```table
(no rows) · indexes added: 2, constraints added: 2
```

A source that ranks by inner product (dot product) over vectors of length 1 ranks them as `'cosine'` does. Over vectors of other lengths the two orders can differ, because the inner product also weighs each vector's length.

properties.heading: Follow the graph from each hit
properties.text:
The search binds `c` like any `MATCH`, so the same statement walks from each hit: here, to its document and the document's other chunks, the context a passage on its own lacks:

```cypher run name=expand
MATCH (c:Chunk)
SEARCH c IN (VECTOR INDEX chunk_embedding FOR [0.15, 0.85, 0.2, 0.05] LIMIT 1) SCORE AS score
MATCH (c)-[:PART_OF]->(d:Document)
RETURN c.id AS hit, d.id AS document,
       COLLECT { MATCH (d)<-[:PART_OF]-(s:Chunk) WHERE s <> c RETURN s.text ORDER BY s.id } AS context
```

```table
| hit  | document     | context                                                                    |
|------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| "c3" | "incident-7" | ["Splitting the suite across four runners brought build times back down."] |
1 row
```

The same nodes answer keyword search through the full-text index, so exact words and codes that an embedding blurs still match:

```cypher run name=keywords
MATCH (c:Chunk)
SEARCH c IN (FULLTEXT INDEX chunk_text FOR 'suite runners' LIMIT 3) SCORE AS score
RETURN c.id AS id, score
ORDER BY score DESC, id
```

```table
| id   | score               |
|------|---------------------|
| "c4" | 0.9790317299047325  |
| "c3" | 0.41168875365010643 |
2 rows
```

[Hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/) fuses the two ranked lists by reciprocal rank in one statement and hops from each note to its topic.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
An embedding of the wrong length fails the import, and nothing from that statement is written:

```json data=short
{"rows": [{"id": "c6", "doc": "onboarding", "source": "wiki", "year": 2026, "text": "Pairing rotates every month.", "embedding": [0.7, 0.2, 0.1]}]}
```

```cypher run name=wrong-length params=short expect=error
UNWIND $rows AS r
MERGE (c:Chunk {id: r.id})
  ON CREATE SET c.text = r.text, c.embedding = vector(r.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)
RETURN count(c) AS imported
```

```table
error: type error: vector() dimension does not match list
```

| Message                                                                                                     | Cause                                                                                                  | Remedy                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type error: vector() dimension does not match list`                                                        | An exported embedding's length is not the `vector()` call's dimensions                                 | Re-export that record, or check that every record came from the same model.                                       |
| `type error: VectorIndexDimensionalityMismatch`                                                             | The question vector's length is not the index's `vector.dimensions`                                    | Embed the question with the model that embedded the records.                                                      |
| `syntax error: SyntaxError: InvalidSearchFilterPredicate: invalid predicate for vector search filtering. …` | The filter inside the search uses `OR` or `<>`                                                         | Split an `OR` into one search per branch and combine the rows, or filter after the search.                        |
| `WrongPropertyForVectorSearchFilter`                                                                        | The filter names a property missing from the index's `WITH [...]` list                                 | Drop the index and create it again with the property in `WITH [...]`, or filter after the search.                 |
| A record never comes back, and nothing fails                                                                | Its embedding, a typed vector or a plain list, has a length other than the index's `vector.dimensions` | Run the type predicate in [Verify](#verify), then store the vectors with `vector(<list>, <dimensions>, FLOAT32)`. |

properties.heading: Import the records
properties.text:
The export arrives as one parameter. This cell writes a `Chunk` per record and a `Document` per distinct `doc` value, linked by `PART_OF`. `MERGE` on the id makes a rerun a no-op, and `vector(r.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)` fails the whole statement on an embedding of another length:

```json data=export
{"rows": [
  {"id": "c1", "doc": "onboarding", "source": "wiki", "year": 2025, "text": "New engineers pair with a maintainer for their first week.", "embedding": [0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.0]},
  {"id": "c2", "doc": "onboarding", "source": "wiki", "year": 2026, "text": "The first week ends with a small fix merged to main.", "embedding": [0.8, 0.2, 0.0, 0.1]},
  {"id": "c3", "doc": "incident-7", "source": "tickets", "year": 2026, "text": "Builds slowed after the test suite doubled in size.", "embedding": [0.2, 0.9, 0.1, 0.0]},
  {"id": "c4", "doc": "incident-7", "source": "tickets", "year": 2026, "text": "Splitting the suite across four runners brought build times back down.", "embedding": [0.1, 0.8, 0.3, 0.1]},
  {"id": "c5", "doc": "style-guide", "source": "wiki", "year": 2024, "text": "Headings use sentence case and no trailing punctuation.", "embedding": [0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.9]}
]}
```

```cypher run name=import params=export
UNWIND $rows AS r
MERGE (c:Chunk {id: r.id})
  ON CREATE SET c.text = r.text, c.source = r.source, c.year = r.year,
                c.embedding = vector(r.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)
MERGE (d:Document {id: r.doc})
MERGE (c)-[:PART_OF]->(d)
RETURN count(c) AS imported
```

```table
| imported |
|----------|
| 5        |
1 row · nodes created: 8, relationships created: 5, properties set: 28, labels added: 8
```

On the CLI, the same two steps write to a `.rl` file. `relate query` with no statement reads a script from stdin, so the schema statements above, saved as `schema.cypher`, run first. Then `--fetch-params` binds the export file as the parameter. Both commands write to `./chunks.rl`:

```bash
relate query --database ./chunks.rl < schema.cypher
relate --database ./chunks.rl --fetch-params export=./export.json 'UNWIND $export.rows AS r MERGE (c:Chunk {id: r.id}) ON CREATE SET c.text = r.text, c.source = r.source, c.year = r.year, c.embedding = vector(r.embedding, 4, FLOAT32) MERGE (d:Document {id: r.doc}) MERGE (c)-[:PART_OF]->(d) RETURN count(c) AS imported'
```

A read opens the store with `--read-only`, and the indexes are there:

```bash
relate --database ./chunks.rl --read-only --mode table "SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type RETURN name, type ORDER BY name"
```

[Migrate from JSON files](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/migrate/from-json-files/) covers loading files with keyed `MERGE` statements and a check against the files.

properties.heading: Know what changes
properties.text:
The ranking keeps its order; the numbers, the filter grammar and a few features do not carry over:

| Topic                | In relate                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Score direction      | `SCORE AS` is a similarity: higher is closer. A store that ranks by distance sorts ascending; the recall query sorts `DESC`                                                                                                             |
| Cosine scale         | 0 to 1: `1.0` same direction, `0.5` orthogonal, `0.0` opposite. A threshold tuned on another store's numbers needs converting; a raw cosine `t` becomes `(1 + t) / 2`                                                                   |
| Similarity functions | `'cosine'` and `'euclidean'` only; any other `vector.similarity_function` fails with `semantic error: InvalidInputValue`                                                                                                                |
| Dimensions           | 1 to 4096 per index; `4097` fails with `semantic error: NumberOutOfRange`                                                                                                                                                               |
| Filters              | Equality, `IN` a list, or a range per property, joined by `AND`, on the properties in `WITH [...]` only. `OR` and `<>` fail with `InvalidSearchFilterPredicate`; another property fails with `WrongPropertyForVectorSearchFilter`       |
| Paging               | `LIMIT` is required, and a vector search takes no `SKIP` or `OFFSET`: `syntax error: InvalidUseOfCommand: SKIP cannot be used together with VECTOR INDEX`                                                                               |
| Embeddings           | relate stores the vectors the application computes; it has no embedding function                                                                                                                                                        |
| Search               | Exact nearest neighbors: every search scores each indexed vector and keeps the top `LIMIT`. Ties go to the lower element id. The `vector.hnsw.*` options are accepted and `SHOW INDEXES` reports them, but they don't change the search |
| Memory               | The whole graph, vectors and indexes included, is held in memory ([sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/))                                                                                                 |
| Writers              | One process writes a store at a time ([limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/#process-model))                                                                                                                     |

The [search reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/) has every rule with its error.

properties.heading: Map the records
properties.text:
| In a vector store                                             | In relate                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A collection or table                                         | A [label](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label) (`:Chunk`) with a vector index on it |
| A record id                                                   | A property with a uniqueness constraint, so the import can `MERGE` and a rerun adds nothing        |
| The document text                                             | A string property, with a full-text index for keyword search                                       |
| The embedding                                                 | A typed vector property: `vector(<list>, <dimensions>, FLOAT32)`                                   |
| Scalar metadata used in filters                               | Properties declared in the vector index's `WITH [...]` list                                        |
| Metadata that names another record, such as a parent document | A relationship to that record's node                                                               |
| The distance metric                                           | `vector.similarity_function`: `'cosine'` or `'euclidean'`                                          |

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- An export of the records as JSON, each with its id, text, metadata and embedding. Every vector store has its own export route; this guide starts from the JSON.
- The embedding model's dimension count and the distance metric the source ranks by.
- [Search by vector similarity](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/) for the `SEARCH` clause itself.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/): index options and defaults, every `SEARCH` rule, and the vector functions.
- [Search by vector similarity](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/vector-search/): typed vectors, filters inside the search, and the score scales.
- [Hybrid recall](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/hybrid-recall/): vector and full-text search fused in one statement.
- [Hybrid retrieval for RAG](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#hybrid-retrieval-for-rag) in the capability catalog.
- The `relate-migrate-from-vector-search` task skill, which gives an agent this mapping and the verification probes as reference text, at `https://relatedb.ai/skills/relate-migrate-from-vector-search/SKILL.md` ([install a task skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/install-the-skill/#install-a-task-skill)).
- [Migration rehearsal](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/migration-rehearsal/): fingerprints before and after a change, for the first schema change on the new store.

properties.heading: Rewrite the recall query
properties.text:
A top-k search with a metadata filter becomes `SEARCH` with the filter inside the parentheses, where it runs before `LIMIT`. `SCORE AS` names the similarity, and higher is closer:

```json data=question
{"question": [0.85, 0.15, 0.05, 0.05], "k": 2, "sources": ["wiki"], "since": 2025}
```

```cypher run name=recall params=question
MATCH (c:Chunk)
SEARCH c IN (VECTOR INDEX chunk_embedding FOR $question
             WHERE c.source IN $sources AND c.year >= $since LIMIT $k) SCORE AS score
RETURN c.id AS id, round(score, 4) AS score, c.text AS text
ORDER BY score DESC, id
```

```table
| id   | score  | text                                                         |
|------|--------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| "c1" | 0.9975 | "New engineers pair with a maintainer for their first week." |
| "c2" | 0.997  | "The first week ends with a small fix merged to main."       |
2 rows
```

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Compare what arrived with what the source held. The source's counts per metadata value go in as a parameter, and every row should say `true`:

```json data=source
{"bySource": {"wiki": 3, "tickets": 2}}
```

```cypher run name=counts params=source
UNWIND keys($bySource) AS source
RETURN source, $bySource[source] AS expected,
       COUNT { MATCH (c:Chunk) WHERE c.source = source } AS actual,
       $bySource[source] = COUNT { MATCH (c:Chunk) WHERE c.source = source } AS ok
ORDER BY source
```

```table
| source    | expected | actual | ok   |
|-----------|----------|--------|------|
| "tickets" | 2        | 2      | true |
| "wiki"    | 3        | 3      | true |
2 rows
```

A search skips, without an error, a property whose length differs from `vector.dimensions`, so counts stay right while recall loses the node. A type predicate finds every such node, and any embedding stored as a plain list rather than a typed vector. No rows means none:

```cypher run name=types
MATCH (c:Chunk)
WHERE NOT c.embedding IS :: VECTOR<FLOAT32>(4)
RETURN c.id AS id, valueType(c.embedding) AS stored
```

```table
| id | stored |
|----|--------|
0 rows
```

Every chunk searched with its own embedding comes back first, with a score of 1.0, unless two chunks' embeddings point the same way (under `'cosine'`) or are equal (under `'euclidean'`). Then the tie goes to the lower element id. A chunk missing from its own result is one the index does not hold:

```cypher run name=self-recall
MATCH (x:Chunk)
CALL (x) {
  MATCH (c:Chunk)
  SEARCH c IN (VECTOR INDEX chunk_embedding FOR x.embedding LIMIT 1) SCORE AS s
  RETURN c.id AS top, s
}
RETURN x.id AS id, top, round(s, 4) AS score, top = x.id AS ok
ORDER BY id
```

```table
| id   | top  | score | ok   |
|------|------|-------|------|
| "c1" | "c1" | 1.0   | true |
| "c2" | "c2" | 1.0   | true |
| "c3" | "c3" | 1.0   | true |
| "c4" | "c4" | 1.0   | true |
| "c5" | "c5" | 1.0   | true |
5 rows
```

The strongest check replays questions whose answers the old store gave, with the same vectors and `k`, and compares the ids. relate's search is exact, so the ids match except where two scores tie, which relate orders by element id, or where the old store's index was approximate. An id missing from the top of the list is a missing node.

properties.heading: Migrate from JSON files
properties.text: This guide shows you how to move records an application keeps in JSON files into a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). A script file creates a uniqueness [constraint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#constraint) per record type, writes each record with `MERGE` on its id, and turns every id reference into a [relationship](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship). `--fetch-params` binds each file as a [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter), so the script needs no code around it, and running it twice leaves the same graph. The steps write to `./team.rl`, and each says so.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
A field that holds an object can't be stored as one property. This run on the default in-memory store writes nothing:

```bash verify
relate --mode table --param 'row={"name": "Ada", "address": {"city": "Lyon"}}' 'CREATE (p:Person {name: $row.name}) SET p.address = $row.address'
```

```text
type error: InvalidPropertyType
```

| Message                                                                                     | Exit code | Cause                                                                                 | Remedy                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `type error: InvalidPropertyType`                                                           | 6         | A `SET` stores a map, a list of maps, a nested list, or a list that mixes types       | Flatten the object into properties (`SET p.city = row.address.city`), or `MERGE` a node for it and link it.                                                                         |
| ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `person_id` uniqueness``                      | 6         | A `CREATE` wrote a second node with an id the store already holds                     | Write the record with `MERGE` on its id.                                                                                                                                            |
| A `false` in the reference check, and no error                                              | 0         | A reference names an id that no record in the files has                               | Fix the reference in the source file, or load the missing record, and run the script again.                                                                                         |
| `Error: --fetch-params people: reading people.json: No such file or directory (os error 2)` | 1         | The path does not exist, relative to the working directory                            | Check the path, or give an absolute one. The [load JSON guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/load-json-from-a-url/#if-it-goes-wrong) lists every `--fetch-params` failure. |
| `Error: --fetch-params people: invalid JSON: …`                                             | 1         | The file is not one JSON document, such as a JSON Lines file with one record per line | Wrap the records in one array.                                                                                                                                                      |

properties.heading: Plan the mapping
properties.text:
| In the JSON files                                                         | In relate                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A file of records of one kind                                             | A [label](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label), such as `:Person`                                             |
| A record's id                                                             | A property with a uniqueness constraint: the `MERGE` key                                                                     |
| A field holding a string, number, boolean, or a list of one of those      | A property of the same type                                                                                                  |
| A field holding an id of another record                                   | A relationship to that record's node                                                                                         |
| A list of objects that each name another record, with fields of their own | One relationship per object, with the fields as its properties                                                               |
| A nested object                                                           | Its fields flattened into properties, or a node of its own. A map is not a property value: `type error: InvalidPropertyType` |
| `null` or a missing field                                                 | No property: `SET p.x = null` leaves `x` off the node                                                                        |

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- The JSON files, each one JSON document of at most 64 MiB, the `--fetch-params` limit per source. The first step writes two small ones, so you can follow along in an empty directory.
- Each record type with an id field that is unique within its file. Records that point at each other by id become relationships.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Load JSON from a URL or a file](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/load-json-from-a-url/): `--fetch-params` on its own, its limits, and its egress rules.
- [Flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#fetch-params): `--fetch-params` and `--param`, with their recorded runs.
- [Indexes and constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/indexes-and-constraints/): the uniqueness constraints that back the `MERGE` keys.
- [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fetch-params-failed): the `--fetch-params` failures at a stable anchor.
- [Migration rehearsal](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/migration-rehearsal/): fingerprints before and after a change, for the first change to the migrated graph.

properties.heading: Run it again
properties.text:
A second run with the same files matches every key instead of creating anything. It writes to `./team.rl` again:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode table --fetch-params people=people.json --fetch-params projects=projects.json < load.cypher
```

```text
note: write statement 1 of 6 changed nothing; the graph is unchanged
note: write statement 2 of 6 changed nothing; the graph is unchanged
+--------+
| people |
+--------+
| 3      |
+--------+
+----------+
| works_on |
+----------+
| 3        |
+----------+
+-----------+
| maintains |
+-----------+
| 1         |
+-----------+
note: write statement 5 of 6 changed nothing; the graph is unchanged
+-------+
| knows |
+-------+
| 1     |
+-------+
note: write statement 6 of 6 changed nothing; the graph is unchanged
```

The notes, on stderr, name the statements that wrote nothing; the exit code stays 0. Statements 3 and 4 have no note because their `SET` writes the same values again. When a file changes, the same run updates those properties in place and adds the new records and references.

properties.heading: Run the load
properties.text:
This command writes to `./team.rl`, a single-file store it creates. `relate query` reads the script from stdin, and each `--fetch-params <name>=<file>` binds one file:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode table --fetch-params people=people.json --fetch-params projects=projects.json < load.cypher
```

```text
+--------+
| people |
+--------+
| 3      |
+--------+
+----------+
| works_on |
+----------+
| 3        |
+----------+
+-----------+
| maintains |
+-----------+
| 1         |
+-----------+
+-------+
| knows |
+-------+
| 1     |
+-------+
```

The two constraint statements print nothing. Each count is the number of rows its statement wrote or matched.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Count each record type in the files and in the store, in one statement. The store opens read-only, and the files are bound as parameters again:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table --fetch-params people=people.json --fetch-params projects=projects.json 'RETURN size($people) AS people_in_files, COUNT { MATCH (p:Person) } AS people_in_store, size($projects) AS projects_in_files, COUNT { MATCH (p:Project) } AS projects_in_store'
```

```text
+-----------------+-----------------+-------------------+-------------------+
| people_in_files | people_in_store | projects_in_files | projects_in_store |
+-----------------+-----------------+-------------------+-------------------+
| 3               | 3               | 2                 | 2                 |
+-----------------+-----------------+-------------------+-------------------+
```

Node counts miss a reference whose id matched no record, because its `MATCH` drops the row without an error. Check every reference in the files against the relationships in the store; `false` marks one that did not arrive:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table --fetch-params projects=projects.json 'UNWIND $projects AS proj
UNWIND proj.contributors AS c
OPTIONAL MATCH (p:Person {id: c.person})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {id: proj.id})
RETURN proj.id AS project, c.person AS person, w IS NOT NULL AS loaded
ORDER BY project, person'
```

```text
+----------+--------+--------+
| project  | person | loaded |
+----------+--------+--------+
| "relate" | "p1"   | true   |
| "relate" | "p2"   | true   |
| "tck"    | "p2"   | true   |
+----------+--------+--------+
```

properties.heading: Write the example files
properties.text:
The application keeps people and projects in two files. Projects name their maintainer and contributors by person id, and people name who they know. Together they hold the team graph the Get started pages use:

```bash verify
cat > people.json <<'JSON'
[{"id": "p1", "name": "Ada", "role": "engineer", "knows": ["p2"]},
 {"id": "p2", "name": "Grace", "role": "engineer", "knows": []},
 {"id": "p3", "name": "Noor", "role": "maintainer", "knows": []}]
JSON
cat > projects.json <<'JSON'
[{"id": "relate", "name": "relate", "language": "Rust", "maintainer": "p3",
  "contributors": [{"person": "p1", "since": 2024}, {"person": "p2", "since": 2023}]},
 {"id": "tck", "name": "opencypher-tck", "language": "Gherkin", "maintainer": null,
  "contributors": [{"person": "p2", "since": 2022}]}]
JSON
```

properties.heading: Write the load script
properties.text:
The script runs in order: the constraints, then the nodes, then the relationships, so every `MATCH` on an id finds a node that already exists. Each file arrives whole as a list, `$people` or `$projects`, and `UNWIND` turns it into one row per record:

```bash verify
cat > load.cypher <<'CYPHER'
CREATE CONSTRAINT person_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) REQUIRE p.id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT project_id IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Project) REQUIRE p.id IS UNIQUE;

UNWIND $people AS row
MERGE (p:Person {id: row.id})
SET p.name = row.name, p.role = row.role
RETURN count(p) AS people;

UNWIND $projects AS row
MERGE (proj:Project {id: row.id})
SET proj.name = row.name, proj.language = row.language
WITH proj, row
UNWIND row.contributors AS c
MATCH (p:Person {id: c.person})
MERGE (p)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj)
SET w.since = c.since
RETURN count(w) AS works_on;

UNWIND $projects AS row
MATCH (proj:Project {id: row.id}), (m:Person {id: row.maintainer})
MERGE (m)-[r:MAINTAINS]->(proj)
RETURN count(r) AS maintains;

UNWIND $people AS row
UNWIND row.knows AS other
MATCH (a:Person {id: row.id}), (b:Person {id: other})
MERGE (a)-[k:KNOWS]->(b)
RETURN count(k) AS knows;
CYPHER
```

Three choices make the script safe to rerun:

- `MERGE` on the id alone, then `SET` for the other fields. A `MERGE` on every field would create a second node when one field changes.
- The constraint backs each key: a `CREATE` of a second node with the same id fails instead of adding a copy.
- A `null` reference matches nothing. The `opencypher-tck` project has no maintainer, so its `MATCH` returns no row and the statement writes no `MAINTAINS` for it.

properties.heading: Migrate from Kuzu
properties.text:
This guide shows you how to move a graph from Kuzu, another embedded graph database that speaks a Cypher dialect, into a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). A short Python script exports each node and relationship table as JSON. In relate, a [graph type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#graph-type) declares the same tables, keys and endpoints, and one script loads the files with `--fetch-params` and keyed `MERGE` statements. The last sections translate the statements that differ between the two dialects, each with the relate form runnable on this page.

The Kuzu GitHub repository is archived, and its last release is 0.11.3, published 2025-10-10 ([kuzudb/kuzu](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu)); its README says earlier releases keep working without changes. The Kuzu steps here ran on 0.11.3, through the `kuzu` Python package. The relate steps run in a terminal and write to `./team.rl`; the cells run in page order on one in-memory store, in your browser and in the docs build.

properties.heading: Assign the next id
properties.text:
A `SERIAL` column numbers new rows on its own. In relate, the statement that creates the node reads the largest id and adds one, and the node key refuses a duplicate if two writes ever pick the same number:

```cypher run name=next-id
MATCH (i:Issue)
WITH coalesce(max(i.id), -1) + 1 AS next
MATCH (p:Project {name: 'relate'})
CREATE (:Issue {id: next, title: 'Document SERIAL columns', opened: date('2026-11-02'), labels: ['docs']})-[:FILED_IN]->(p)
RETURN next AS id
```

```table
| id |
|----|
| 3  |
1 row · nodes created: 1, relationships created: 1, properties set: 4, labels added: 1
```

`coalesce(…, -1) + 1` starts an empty label at 0, as `SERIAL` does. A key that need not be a number can come from `randomUUID()` instead.

properties.heading: Convert the exported values
properties.text:
The JSON export keeps `INT64`, `DOUBLE`, `BOOLEAN` and lists as JSON values, which arrive as relate's types; `DATE` and `TIMESTAMP` arrive as strings and need a conversion. This row has the shape the export writes:

```json data=exported
{"row": {"since": 2024, "score": 1.5, "active": true, "opened": "2026-10-02", "updated": "2026-10-02 09:30:00", "labels": ["bug", "planner"]}}
```

```cypher run name=types params=exported
RETURN valueType($row.since) AS int64, valueType($row.score) AS double,
       valueType($row.active) AS boolean, valueType($row.labels) AS list,
       date($row.opened) AS date, localdatetime($row.updated) AS timestamp
```

```table
| int64              | double           | boolean            | list                             | date         | timestamp             |
|--------------------|------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------|
| "INTEGER NOT NULL" | "FLOAT NOT NULL" | "BOOLEAN NOT NULL" | "LIST<STRING NOT NULL> NOT NULL" | "2026-10-02" | "2026-10-02T09:30:00" |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Declare the schema as a graph type
properties.text:
A graph type holds what Kuzu's `CREATE NODE TABLE` and `CREATE REL TABLE` statements hold: each label's properties and their types, the primary keys as `IS KEY`, and each relationship type's endpoints. Setting it creates the constraints, so every later write is checked. This step writes the script and runs it on `./team.rl`, a single-file store it creates:

```bash verify
cat > schema.cypher <<'CYPHER'
CREATE GRAPH TYPE team {
  (person:Person => {name :: STRING NOT NULL IS KEY, role :: STRING}),
  (project:Project => {name :: STRING NOT NULL IS KEY, language :: STRING}),
  (issue:Issue => {id :: INTEGER NOT NULL IS KEY, title :: STRING, opened :: DATE, labels :: LIST<STRING NOT NULL>}),
  (person)-[:WORKS_ON => {since :: INTEGER}]->(project),
  (person)-[:MAINTAINS =>]->(project),
  (person)-[:KNOWS =>]->(person),
  (issue)-[:FILED_IN =>]->(project)
};
ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET GRAPH TYPE team;
CYPHER
relate query --database ./team.rl < schema.cypher
```

The statements print nothing. A graph type is open where a Kuzu schema is closed: a label, a property or a relationship type it doesn't declare is accepted, not refused ([Translate the statements](#translate-the-statements) shows both).

properties.heading: Export the tables from Kuzu
Find a shortest path
properties.text:
Kuzu writes the shortest-path keyword inside the relationship pattern; relate writes `SHORTEST` before the pattern, as GQL does. For this graph, Kuzu's `MATCH p = (a:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[* SHORTEST 1..5]-(b:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'}) RETURN length(p) AS hops` returned 2:

```cypher run name=shortest
MATCH path = SHORTEST 1 (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[*1..5]-(:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'})
RETURN [n IN nodes(path) | n.name] AS route, length(path) AS hops
```

```table
| route                              | hops |
|------------------------------------|------|
| ["Ada", "Grace", "opencypher-tck"] | 2    |
1 row
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
The Kuzu forms with no relate counterpart fail before they run. Kuzu's schema statements:

```cypher run name=node-table expect=error
CREATE NODE TABLE Person(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, role STRING)
```

```table
error: syntax error: parse error: expected a pattern
  CREATE NODE TABLE Person(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, role STRING)
         ^
```

Kuzu's shortest-path form:

```cypher run name=kuzu-shortest expect=error
MATCH p = (a:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[* SHORTEST 1..5]-(b:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'})
RETURN length(p) AS hops
```

```table
error: syntax error: InvalidRelationshipPattern: parse error: expected RightBracket, got "SHORTEST" (Identifier)
  MATCH p = (a:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[* SHORTEST 1..5]-(b:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'})
                                        ^
```

`CAST`:

```cypher run name=cast expect=error
RETURN CAST('2024' AS INT64) AS year
```

```table
error: syntax error: parse error: expected RightParen, got "AS" (AS)
  RETURN CAST('2024' AS INT64) AS year
                     ^
```

`label()`:

```cypher run name=label expect=error
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Grace'}) RETURN label(p) AS label
```

```table
error: syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function label()
```

| Message                                                                                                     | Cause                                                                      | Remedy                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax error: parse error: expected a pattern`                                                             | A `CREATE NODE TABLE` or `CREATE REL TABLE` statement                      | Declare the tables in a graph type, as in [Declare the schema as a graph type](#declare-the-schema-as-a-graph-type), or leave them undeclared. |
| `syntax error: InvalidRelationshipPattern: parse error: expected RightBracket, got "SHORTEST" (Identifier)` | Kuzu's `-[* SHORTEST 1..5]-`                                               | Write `SHORTEST 1` before the pattern: `MATCH path = SHORTEST 1 (a)-[*1..5]-(b)`.                                                              |
| `syntax error: parse error: expected RightParen, got "AS" (AS)`                                             | `CAST(<value> AS <type>)`                                                  | Use `toInteger()`, `toFloat()`, `toBoolean()`, `toString()`, `date()` or `localdatetime()`.                                                    |
| `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function label()`                                                   | Kuzu's `label(n)`                                                          | Use `labels(n)[0]`, or test a label with `n:Person`.                                                                                           |
| ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `<name>` property type``                                      | A `DATE` or `TIMESTAMP` written as the exported string                     | Wrap it in `date()` or `localdatetime()`.                                                                                                      |
| `ConstraintValidationFailed: endpoint label presence verification failed: expected Person`                  | A relationship whose endpoints the graph type doesn't declare for its type | Check the direction of the `MATCH` and `MERGE` against the relationship table's `FROM` and `TO`.                                               |
| `Error: --fetch-params <name>: invalid JSON: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0`                  | An export file is empty                                                    | Check that the export script finished for that table, and run it again.                                                                        |

properties.heading: Load the files
properties.text:
The load script writes the nodes first, then the relationships, so every `MATCH` on a key finds a node that already exists. Each file arrives whole as a list, and `UNWIND` turns it into one row per record. `date(row.opened)` turns the exported string back into a `DATE`, which the graph type requires:

```bash verify
cat > load.cypher <<'CYPHER'
UNWIND $person AS row
MERGE (p:Person {name: row.name})
SET p.role = row.role;

UNWIND $project AS row
MERGE (p:Project {name: row.name})
SET p.language = row.language;

UNWIND $issue AS row
MERGE (i:Issue {id: row.id})
SET i.title = row.title, i.opened = date(row.opened), i.labels = row.labels;

UNWIND $works_on AS row
MATCH (a:Person {name: row.source}), (b:Project {name: row.target})
MERGE (a)-[r:WORKS_ON]->(b)
SET r.since = row.since;

UNWIND $maintains AS row
MATCH (a:Person {name: row.source}), (b:Project {name: row.target})
MERGE (a)-[:MAINTAINS]->(b);

UNWIND $knows AS row
MATCH (a:Person {name: row.source}), (b:Person {name: row.target})
MERGE (a)-[:KNOWS]->(b);

UNWIND $filed_in AS row
MATCH (a:Issue {id: row.source}), (b:Project {name: row.target})
MERGE (a)-[:FILED_IN]->(b);
CYPHER
```

This command writes to `./team.rl`. Each `--fetch-params <name>=<file>` binds one export file as a [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter). `MERGE` on each key makes a second run match instead of create:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl \
  --fetch-params person=export/Person.json \
  --fetch-params project=export/Project.json \
  --fetch-params issue=export/Issue.json \
  --fetch-params works_on=export/WORKS_ON_Person_Project.json \
  --fetch-params maintains=export/MAINTAINS_Person_Project.json \
  --fetch-params knows=export/KNOWS_Person_Person.json \
  --fetch-params filed_in=export/FILED_IN_Issue_Project.json \
  < load.cypher
```

The load prints nothing: no statement returns rows, and the exit code is 0. The issues arrived with their types intact. The store opens read-only:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "MATCH (i:Issue)-[:FILED_IN]->(p:Project)
RETURN i.id AS id, i.opened AS opened, valueType(i.opened) AS type, i.labels AS labels, p.name AS project
ORDER BY id"
```

```text
+----+------------+-----------------+--------------------+------------------+
| id | opened     | type            | labels             | project          |
+----+------------+-----------------+--------------------+------------------+
| 0  | 2026-10-02 | "DATE NOT NULL" | ["bug", "planner"] | "relate"         |
| 1  | 2026-09-14 | "DATE NOT NULL" | []                 | "opencypher-tck" |
| 2  | 2026-10-20 | "DATE NOT NULL" | ["docs"]           | "relate"         |
+----+------------+-----------------+--------------------+------------------+
```

properties.heading: Plan the mapping
properties.text:
| In Kuzu                                                  | In relate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE NODE TABLE Person(...)`                          | A [label](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label), declared in a graph type as `(:Person => {...})`. Outside a graph type, a label needs no declaration                                                                          |
| `PRIMARY KEY`                                            | `IS KEY` on the property: a node key constraint, unique and required                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `CREATE REL TABLE WORKS_ON(FROM Person TO Project, ...)` | A [relationship type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type) with its endpoints: `(:Person =>)-[:WORKS_ON => {...}]->(:Project =>)`                                                                                 |
| A relationship table with several `FROM … TO` pairs      | One relationship type. A graph type declares one endpoint pair per type, and a second fails with `semantic error: SyntaxError: duplicate identifying label`; leave that type out of the graph type, and relate accepts it between any labels |
| `INT64`, `DOUBLE`, `STRING`, `BOOLEAN`                   | `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `STRING`, `BOOLEAN`                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `DATE`, `TIMESTAMP`                                      | `DATE` with `date()`, `LOCAL DATETIME` with `localdatetime()`: the JSON export writes both as strings                                                                                                                                        |
| `STRING[]`                                               | `LIST<STRING NOT NULL>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `SERIAL`                                                 | An `INTEGER` key. relate has no sequences: a statement assigns the next value ([Assign the next id](#assign-the-next-id))                                                                                                                    |
| One table per node                                       | Any number of labels per node                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- Python with the `kuzu` package at the version that opens your database, for the export.
- Each table's JSON export at most 64 MiB, the `--fetch-params` limit per file.
- The whole graph, its indexes included, fits in memory ([size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/)).

properties.heading: Read a node's label and convert strings
properties.text:
`labels(n)` returns a list, because a node can carry several labels. `toInteger()` and the other conversion functions take the place of `CAST`:

```cypher run name=labels
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Grace'})
RETURN labels(p) AS labels, labels(p)[0] AS label, toInteger('2024') AS year, toFloat('1.5') AS score
```

```table
| labels     | label    | year | score |
|------------|----------|------|-------|
| ["Person"] | "Person" | 2024 | 1.5   |
1 row
```

properties.text:

properties.heading: Translate the statements
properties.text:
Most of Kuzu's Cypher runs on relate unchanged: `MATCH`, `CREATE`, `MERGE`, `WHERE`, `WITH`, `UNWIND`, aggregation and `COUNT { }` subqueries. The table lists what differs, with what Kuzu 0.11.3 returned; the cells after it run the relate form. They start from the same graph type and rows, in an in-memory store:

| Task                                                                        | In Kuzu                                                                                                        | In relate                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Declare the schema                                                          | `CREATE NODE TABLE`, `CREATE REL TABLE`, required before any write                                             | `CREATE GRAPH TYPE`, optional                                                                                                                                             |
| A write to an undeclared label, property or relationship type               | Refused: `Binder exception: Table Team does not exist.`, `Binder exception: Cannot find property email for a.` | Accepted, also under a graph type                                                                                                                                         |
| A second label on a node                                                    | Refused: `Binder exception: Table Maintainer does not exist.`                                                  | Accepted                                                                                                                                                                  |
| A value of another type                                                     | `CREATE (:Person {name: 'Zed', role: 7})` stores the string `'7'`                                              | Refused under the graph type's type constraint                                                                                                                            |
| A duplicate or missing primary key, a relationship between the wrong tables | Refused                                                                                                        | Refused under the graph type                                                                                                                                              |
| Assign the next id                                                          | `SERIAL`, starting at 0                                                                                        | `max(id) + 1` in the creating statement                                                                                                                                   |
| A shortest path                                                             | `-[* SHORTEST 1..5]-`                                                                                          | `SHORTEST 1 (…)-[*1..5]-(…)`                                                                                                                                              |
| A node's label                                                              | `label(n)` and `labels(n)` both return the string `'Person'`                                                   | `labels(n)` returns a list, `['Person']`; `labels(n)[0]` is the string                                                                                                    |
| Convert a string                                                            | `CAST('2024' AS INT64)`; `toInteger()` fails with `Catalog exception: function TOINTEGER does not exist.`      | `toInteger('2024')`, `toFloat()`, `toBoolean()`, `date()`, `localdatetime()`                                                                                              |
| Read a CSV file                                                             | `LOAD FROM 'people.csv' (header = true) RETURN *`                                                              | `LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS FROM 'file:///people.csv' AS row`, from the directory `--load-csv-dir` allows ([import a CSV](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/import-csv/)) |

The graph type from [Declare the schema as a graph type](#declare-the-schema-as-a-graph-type):

```cypher run name=graph-type
CREATE GRAPH TYPE team {
  (person:Person => {name :: STRING NOT NULL IS KEY, role :: STRING}),
  (project:Project => {name :: STRING NOT NULL IS KEY, language :: STRING}),
  (issue:Issue => {id :: INTEGER NOT NULL IS KEY, title :: STRING, opened :: DATE, labels :: LIST<STRING NOT NULL>}),
  (person)-[:WORKS_ON => {since :: INTEGER}]->(project),
  (person)-[:MAINTAINS =>]->(project),
  (person)-[:KNOWS =>]->(person),
  (issue)-[:FILED_IN =>]->(project)
};
ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET GRAPH TYPE team
```

```table
(no rows) · constraints added: 23
```

The rows the load wrote:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace),
       (:Issue {id: 0, title: 'Plan cache misses on quoted labels', opened: date('2026-10-02'), labels: ['bug', 'planner']})-[:FILED_IN]->(relate),
       (:Issue {id: 1, title: 'Scenario for OPTIONAL MATCH ordering', opened: date('2026-09-14'), labels: []})-[:FILED_IN]->(tck),
       (:Issue {id: 2, title: 'Add a Kuzu migration guide', opened: date('2026-10-20'), labels: ['docs']})-[:FILED_IN]->(relate)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 8, relationships created: 8, properties set: 25, labels added: 8
```

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Count the records in each export file and the nodes and relationships in the store, then compare. The store opens read-only, and the files are bound as parameters again:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table \
  --fetch-params person=export/Person.json \
  --fetch-params project=export/Project.json \
  --fetch-params issue=export/Issue.json \
  --fetch-params works_on=export/WORKS_ON_Person_Project.json \
  --fetch-params maintains=export/MAINTAINS_Person_Project.json \
  --fetch-params knows=export/KNOWS_Person_Person.json \
  --fetch-params filed_in=export/FILED_IN_Issue_Project.json \
  'UNWIND [["Person", size($person)], ["Project", size($project)], ["Issue", size($issue)],
         ["WORKS_ON", size($works_on)], ["MAINTAINS", size($maintains)],
         ["KNOWS", size($knows)], ["FILED_IN", size($filed_in)]] AS t
WITH t[0] AS name, t[1] AS in_export
RETURN name, in_export,
       COUNT { MATCH (n) WHERE name IN labels(n) } + COUNT { MATCH ()-[r]->() WHERE type(r) = name } AS in_relate
ORDER BY name'
```

```text
+-------------+-----------+-----------+
| name        | in_export | in_relate |
+-------------+-----------+-----------+
| "FILED_IN"  | 3         | 3         |
| "Issue"     | 3         | 3         |
| "KNOWS"     | 1         | 1         |
| "MAINTAINS" | 1         | 1         |
| "Person"    | 3         | 3         |
| "Project"   | 2         | 2         |
| "WORKS_ON"  | 3         | 3         |
+-------------+-----------+-----------+
```

Equal columns mean every record arrived and every relationship found both of its endpoints. A relationship count lower than its file's is a `source` or `target` whose `MATCH` found no node, which drops the row without an error. Then run each statement the application sends with `EXPLAIN` in front: it plans without running, and a Kuzu-only form fails at planning.

properties.heading: Write the export files
properties.text:
These are the files the script wrote for the example, byte for byte, so the remaining steps run without Kuzu. With your own export, skip this step. This step writes the directory `./export`:

```bash verify
mkdir export
cat > export/Person.json <<'JSON'
[
{"name":"Ada","role":"engineer"},
{"name":"Grace","role":"engineer"},
{"name":"Noor","role":"maintainer"}
]
JSON
cat > export/Project.json <<'JSON'
[
{"name":"relate","language":"Rust"},
{"name":"opencypher-tck","language":"Gherkin"}
]
JSON
cat > export/Issue.json <<'JSON'
[
{"id":0,"title":"Plan cache misses on quoted labels","opened":"2026-10-02","labels":["bug","planner"]},
{"id":1,"title":"Scenario for OPTIONAL MATCH ordering","opened":"2026-09-14","labels":[]},
{"id":2,"title":"Add a Kuzu migration guide","opened":"2026-10-20","labels":["docs"]}
]
JSON
cat > export/WORKS_ON_Person_Project.json <<'JSON'
[
{"source":"Ada","target":"relate","since":2024},
{"source":"Grace","target":"opencypher-tck","since":2022},
{"source":"Grace","target":"relate","since":2023}
]
JSON
cat > export/MAINTAINS_Person_Project.json <<'JSON'
[
{"source":"Noor","target":"relate"}
]
JSON
cat > export/KNOWS_Person_Person.json <<'JSON'
[
{"source":"Ada","target":"Grace"}
]
JSON
cat > export/FILED_IN_Issue_Project.json <<'JSON'
[
{"source":0,"target":"relate"},
{"source":1,"target":"opencypher-tck"},

```

properties.heading: Writes the graph type accepts
properties.text:
A second label, an undeclared property, an undeclared relationship type and an undeclared label, each of which Kuzu refuses, all succeed in one statement:

```cypher run name=open-schema
MATCH (ada:Person {name: 'Ada'})
SET ada:Maintainer, ada.email = 'ada@example.com'
CREATE (ada)-[:MEMBER_OF]->(team:Team {name: 'core'})
RETURN labels(ada) AS labels, ada.email AS email, labels(team) AS team
```

```table
| labels                   | email             | team     |
|--------------------------|-------------------|----------|
| ["Person", "Maintainer"] | "ada@example.com" | ["Team"] |
1 row · nodes created: 1, relationships created: 1, properties set: 2, labels added: 2
```

To refuse these too, declare them: a property in the graph type with `NOT NULL` is required, and a constraint can require any property ([indexes and constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/indexes-and-constraints/)).

properties.heading: Writes the graph type refuses
properties.text:
The three writes Kuzu refuses for its primary key and its relationship table, the graph type refuses too. A second person named Ada:

```cypher run name=duplicate-key expect=error
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'designer'})
```

```table
error: semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `constraint_bda177ce` uniqueness
```

A person without a name:

```cypher run name=missing-key expect=error
CREATE (:Person {role: 'designer'})
```

```table
error: semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `constraint_238af3a3` requires properties
```

A `WORKS_ON` from a project to a person:

```cypher run name=wrong-endpoints expect=error
MATCH (p:Project {name: 'relate'}), (a:Person {name: 'Noor'})
CREATE (p)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2020}]->(a)
```

```table
error: ConstraintValidationFailed: endpoint label presence verification failed: expected Person
```

A number where the graph type declares a string, which Kuzu stored as the string `'7'`:

```cypher run name=wrong-type expect=error
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Zed', role: 7})
```

```table
error: semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `constraint_819770c5` property type
```

properties.heading: Migrate from Neo4j
properties.text: This guide shows you how to move a graph and the application that queries it from Neo4j to relate. relate runs Neo4j's [Cypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#cypher) inside one process, on one machine, so most statements carry over unchanged. What doesn't carry over is the server around them: procedure libraries, several databases, user accounts, and clustering. The first section lists each of those with what relate offers instead, so you can decide before you copy anything.

properties.heading: Check the application's statements
properties.text:
Run each statement the application sends with `EXPLAIN` in front, against the copy. `EXPLAIN` plans without running, and an unknown function or procedure fails at planning. The pull and the driver connection are described here, not run in the docs build; the cells run on one in-memory store holding the team graph, standing in for the copy:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

A GDS call fails before anything runs:

```cypher run name=gds expect=error
EXPLAIN CALL gds.degree.stream('team') YIELD nodeId, score
RETURN nodeId, score
```

```table
error: syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: gds.degree.stream
```

Degree, the simplest centrality, is a `COUNT` subquery:

```cypher run name=degree
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.name AS person, COUNT { (p)--() } AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC, person
```

```table
| person  | degree |
|---------|--------|
| "Grace" | 3      |
| "Ada"   | 2      |
| "Noor"  | 1      |
3 rows
```

A shortest path is a pattern:

```cypher run name=shortest
MATCH path = SHORTEST 1 (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[*]-(:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'})
RETURN [n IN nodes(path) | n.name] AS route, length(path) AS hops
```

```table
| route                              | hops |
|------------------------------------|------|
| ["Ada", "Grace", "opencypher-tck"] | 2    |
1 row
```

APOC's list and text helpers have built-in counterparts. This statement does with `string.join`, `coll.sort` and `coll.distinct` what `apoc.text.join`, `apoc.coll.sort` and `apoc.coll.toSet` would:

```cypher run name=builtins
MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
WITH proj, collect(p.name) AS names, collect(p.role) AS roles
RETURN proj.name AS project, string.join(coll.sort(names), ', ') AS people, coll.distinct(roles) AS roles
ORDER BY project
```

```table
| project          | people       | roles        |
|------------------|--------------|--------------|
| "opencypher-tck" | "Grace"      | ["engineer"] |
| "relate"         | "Ada, Grace" | ["engineer"] |
2 rows
```

A statement that plans cleanly can still return different results where the dialect differs; [differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) lists each case with the form to write instead.

properties.heading: Check what you'd miss
properties.text:
Each row is something a Neo4j deployment commonly relies on. The relate column says what happens when a statement or a deployment reaches for it, quoting the error where there is one:

| Neo4j feature                                                  | In relate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | What to use instead                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The APOC library                                               | None. `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function apoc.text.join()`; `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: apoc.meta.schema`                                                                                                                         | Built-in functions such as `string.join`, `string.regexReplace`, `coll.sort`, `coll.distinct` and `coll.flatten`; `CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties()` for the schema; `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` for batched writes; the CLI's `--fetch-params` to load a JSON file or URL. `SHOW FUNCTIONS` and `SHOW PROCEDURES` list what exists |
| The Graph Data Science (GDS) library                           | None. `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: gds.pageRank.stream`                                                                                                                                                                                          | Cypher patterns and aggregation: degree with a `COUNT { }` subquery, paths with `SHORTEST`. Other algorithms run in the application's own code over a query result                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Several databases per server (`CREATE DATABASE`, `USE <name>`) | Three fixed [namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#namespace) per store, `neo4j`, `system` and `system_ontologies`. `semantic error: UnsupportedAdministrationCommand: Unsupported administration command: CREATE DATABASE movies` | One store per graph: a directory or a `.rl` file each                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Users, roles, and privileges                                   | None. `CREATE USER bob SET PASSWORD 'secret'` fails with `syntax error: parse error: expected a pattern`                                                                                                                                              | File permissions on the store; `--read-only` opens, which refuse every write; on a served store, one Basic-auth credential for every surface, from `relate serve --auth <user>:<password>`                                                                                                                                              |
| Clustering: replicas, failover, sharding                       | None. One process writes a store, and nothing replicates it to another machine                                                                                                                                                                        | On the same machine, readers beside the writer with `--read-only` on a directory store, or `--read-only=live` to follow its commits; `relate serve` for many clients of one process; `relate clone` for a copy                                                                                                                          |
| Several processes writing one database                         | One writing process per store. A second fails at open with `storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5                                                                                                                                                      | Route every writer through one `relate serve` process ([two processes, one store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/))                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Graphs larger than memory                                      | The whole graph and its indexes are held in memory, with no paging                                                                                                                                                                                    | Measure first ([size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/)); `--logical-graph-size-limit` fails a growing write instead of exhausting memory                                                                                                                                              |
| Encrypted connections                                          | `relate serve` has no TLS. Every surface binds to `127.0.0.1` unless `--host` names another address                                                                                                                                                   | A TLS-terminating proxy in front of `relate serve` ([auth and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/))                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `LOAD CSV` from a URL                                          | Local files under the `--load-csv-dir` directory only, denied by default; anything else fails with `LOAD CSV file unavailable`                                                                                                                        | Download the file, then `--load-csv-dir <dir>` ([import a CSV](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/import-csv/))                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

If a row is a requirement, relate is the wrong home for that workload, and [where relate fits](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/where-relate-fits/) says what to use instead. The [limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/) page lists every limit, and [differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) every statement-level habit.

properties.heading: Connect the application
properties.text:
Two routes, depending on how much of the application should change:

| Route                 | What changes                                                                                                                             | Start here                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Embed relate          | The Neo4j driver gives way to the relate client for the language, which opens the store in the application's process. No server, no port | [Python](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/python/), [Node.js](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/node/), or the other [clients](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/api/) |
| Keep the Neo4j driver | Nothing in the code but the URI. `relate serve --bolt <port>` speaks Bolt, and a `neo4j://` driver gets a single-server routing table    | [Serve a store over Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/bolt/)                                                                                                         |

The served form, with the copy opened read-only:

```bash
relate serve --database ./mirror --bolt 7687 --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`. Without `--auth` or `RELATE_AUTH`, relate generates a token, prints it at startup, and keeps it in `./mirror.auth-token` for the next start.

properties.heading: Copy the data
properties.text:
`relate pull` runs your statements against Neo4j over its HTTP Query API and writes the nodes and relationships they return into a new local [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), with the source's constraints and its range, text, and point indexes. This command writes to `./mirror`, which must not exist yet or be empty:

```bash
relate pull --from neo4j.env --query "MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN n, r, m" --database ./mirror
```

That statement copies every node with at least one relationship; add `MATCH (n) WHERE NOT EXISTS { (n)--() } RETURN n` as a second statement, separated by `;`, for nodes without any. Two things don't come across:

- Full-text and vector indexes. The pull skips them with a warning on stderr; create them again with `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` or `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` ([search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/)).
- [Element ids](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id). Every node and relationship gets a new one, so an application that stored Neo4j's element ids needs its own key property instead.

[Pull a subgraph from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/neo4j/pull-from-neo4j/) covers the connection file, the value types, and every error.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                           | Cause                                                                            | Remedy                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function apoc.<name>()` or `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: apoc.<name>` | The statement calls APOC                                                         | Use the built-in from [Check what you'd miss](#check-what-youd-miss); `SHOW FUNCTIONS` lists them.                |
| `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: gds.<name>`                                                                     | The statement calls GDS                                                          | Write the measure in Cypher, or compute it in the application from a query result.                                |
| `Error: destination database is not empty; pull writes into an empty database only (ADR-0158)`                    | `relate pull` targets a store that holds data                                    | Pull into a new path.                                                                                             |
| `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`                                                       | The statement or driver session names a database other than the three namespaces | Drop the `USE` clause or the session's database name; put each graph in its own store.                            |
| `Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5                                                      | A second process opened the store for writing                                    | Send every writer through one `relate serve` process, or open the reader with `--read-only` on a directory store. |
| A search returns nothing on the copy                                                                              | The pull skipped the source's full-text and vector indexes                       | Create them with `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` or `CREATE VECTOR INDEX`.                                                |

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A Neo4j or Aura database that answers the HTTP Query API, for the copy. [Pull a subgraph from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/neo4j/pull-from-neo4j/) has the connection file and every refusal.
- The application's Cypher statements, collected in one place, to check against the dialect.

properties.heading: Rehearse the cut-over
properties.text:
Run any change the move needs, such as replacing APOC calls in stored data or renaming a relationship type, on a clone of the copy, so the pull stays as it came. This writes the new store `./rehearsal`:

```bash
relate clone ./mirror ./rehearsal
```

The [migration rehearsal recipe](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/migration-rehearsal/) is the pattern for checking the result: fingerprint the graph before the change, write down what the change may touch, and compare afterwards. It catches a migration that keeps every node count right while it deletes 352 relationships.
