properties.heading: Share one store between two processes
properties.text: This guide shows you how to reach one store from more than one process. A [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) has one writer: the first process that opens it for writing owns it until that process exits. A second writable open fails with [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) 5, and on a `.rl` store so does a read-only one. A read-only open beside the writer, a read-only open that follows the writer's commits, or one process that serves the store to the others are the three ways to share it.

properties.heading: Follow the writer's commits
properties.text:
`--read-only=live` opens a directory store read-only and keeps applying the writer's commits as they reach its WAL. A statement that is already running keeps the view it started with. The value is attached with `=`; `--read-only live` is a usage error.

A one-shot run reads once and exits, so following pays off in a process that stays up. This server answers HTTP statements from `team` while another process writes to it:

```bash
relate serve --database ./team --read-only=live --http 7474
```

Without `--read-only=live`, the server opens the store for writing and needs the writer lock itself. While another process writes, it stops at startup with `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>` and exit code 1.

The server prints a generated password for the user `relate` at startup and keeps it in `team.auth-token` beside the store. A statement sent while the writer adds a person returns the new count as soon as that commit lands, with no restart. `relate serve --read-only`, without `=live`, serves a frozen view taken at startup (freshness `snapshot`) instead.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5, on a `--read-only` open of a `.rl` store.** A writer holds the file, and a `.rl` store can't be read beside it. Wait for the writer to exit, read through the writer's `relate serve`, or move the store to a directory with `relate clone`.
- **`Error: Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 1, when `relate serve` starts.** Another process holds the store for writing. For a directory store, start the server with `--read-only` or `--read-only=live` beside that writer. For a `.rl` store, stop the writer and let the server be the one writer.
- **`Failed to open Relate: semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases`, exit code 1.** `--read-only=live` was given a `.rl` store or `:memory:`. Follow a directory store instead.
- **`semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.`, exit code 6.** A write went to a read-only open. Send writes to the process that owns the store ([write on a read-only store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-write-on-read-only)).
- **`{"errors":[{"code":"42NFF","message":"authentication required"}]}` from the HTTP server.** The request had no password. Pass `-u "relate:<token>"` with the password from the server's startup output, or `-u "$(cat <store>.auth-token)"`, since that file holds the whole `relate:<token>` credential.

properties.heading: Pick a way to share the store
properties.text:
| You need                                     | Use                                                                                                 | Works on                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reads while another process writes           | `--read-only`: a frozen view of the store as it was at open (freshness `snapshot`)                  | A directory store at any time; a `.rl` store only while no writer holds it |
| Reads that keep up with the writer's commits | `--read-only=live` in a long-running process, such as `relate serve`                                | A directory store only                                                     |
| Writes from more than one process            | One `relate serve` process owns the store; the others send statements to it over HTTP, Bolt, or MCP | Any store                                                                  |

A `.rl` store is one file that its writer locks whole, so only the third answer shares it with a running writer. `relate clone ./team.rl ./team` copies it into a directory store, which allows the first two ([Choose a store layout](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/choose-a-store-layout/)).

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- `relate` on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A store. To follow along, create the shared example graph as `team.rl`:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl < team.cypher
```

properties.heading: Read beside a writer
properties.text:
Copy the example into a directory store, `team`:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team.rl ./team
```

A [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) open never writes, checkpoints, or migrates the store, so it takes no writer lock. With a first process holding `team` open for writing, a second reads it read-only:

```bash verify
# a first process keeps the team directory open for 3 seconds
sleep 3 | relate query --database ./team > /dev/null &
sleep 1
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
echo "exit=$?"
wait
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.536833,"execute_ms":0.3705,"lex_parse_ms":0.030875,"lower_ms":0.0415,"parse_ms":0.106875,"plan_ms":0.051333,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.008459},"truncated":false}
exit=0
```

The read sees the store as it was when the read opened. Several read-only processes can share a directory store with its writer, and a second writable open still fails with exit code 5.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Errors: storage locked](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked): the locked-store entry with its exit code.
- [`--read-only`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#read-only) in the flags reference.
- [Choose a store layout](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/choose-a-store-layout/): directory store or `.rl`, and what each allows.
- [Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/): one writer, many readers, and write-write conflicts.

properties.heading: See what the second process gets
properties.text:
A `relate` run holds its store only while it runs: a one-shot statement opens the store, runs, checkpoints if it opened for writing, and exits. Two processes collide only when their runs overlap. This step keeps `team.rl` open in a first process for 3 seconds and opens it read-only from a second:

```bash verify
# a first process keeps team.rl open for 3 seconds
sleep 3 | relate query --database ./team.rl > /dev/null &
sleep 1
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
echo "exit=$?"
wait
```

The path starts with the working directory, shown as `<dir>`. The first line is stderr, the second the error object on stdout:

```text
Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <dir>/team.rl
{"error":{"code":"conflict","exit_code":5,"kind":"locked","message":"storage locked: <dir>/team.rl","retryable":false}}
exit=5
```

Even a read-only open is refused: a `.rl` store can't be read beside its writer. The error has code `conflict` and kind `locked`. `retryable` is `false`: running the same command again fails the same way until the first process exits. For a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store), the path in the message is the writer lock file inside it, `.cypherlite.writer`. In the Python client, `relate.connect()` raises `OperationalError` with the same `storage locked: <path>` message.

properties.heading: Serve one store to several writers
properties.text:
One process owns the store and every other process sends it statements. This server is writable on purpose: it is the one writer, and its clients' writes go through it. It holds `team.rl` until it stops:

```bash
relate serve --database ./team.rl --http 7474
```

The generated password differs on every new store, so it's shown as `<token>`:

```text
auth: generated token for user relate: <token>
auth: persisted at ./team.rl.auth-token (reused on restart)
serve: HTTP Query API v2 listening on http://127.0.0.1:7474 (auth: basic)
```

Any process with the password can write through the HTTP Query API. This one adds a person:

```bash
curl -s -u "relate:<token>" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})", "parameters": {"name": "Ines", "role": "engineer"}}'
```

The same server takes `--bolt <port>` for Neo4j drivers and tools, and `--mcp <port>` or `--mcp stdio` for agent hosts ([Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/)). It listens on `127.0.0.1` unless `--host` says otherwise. Statements from all clients run in the one engine, and two [transactions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction) that write the same data at once get a write-write conflict, which is retryable ([Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/)).

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Once the process that held the store exits, the open that failed in [See what the second process gets](#see-what-the-second-process-gets) succeeds:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.541167,"execute_ms":0.372417,"lex_parse_ms":0.029791,"lower_ms":0.044166,"parse_ms":0.108083,"plan_ms":0.052667000000000005,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.0085},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Upgrade a store
properties.text: This guide shows you how to take a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) to a newer relate release. Migration is automatic and forward-only: the first writable open by a newer binary rewrites an older store in the current format before it runs a statement, and no release converts a store back. Once migrated, the older binary refuses the store, so the backup comes first.

properties.heading: Back up with the release you have
properties.text:
Make the copy before the new binary touches the store. `relate clone` reads the source without writing it and creates a new store at the destination, which must not exist yet:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team.rl ./team-backup.rl
```

The backup keeps the current format, so the release you have now can open it. Keep it until the new release has run against the store for a while ([Back up and restore a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/)).

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage error: unsupported snapshot version <n>`, or `storage error: unsupported graph value encoding: <n>` for a JSON store, exit code 1.** A newer relate wrote the store, or already migrated it. For a Parquet store, `relate info` fails too, with `Failed to read store info:` before the same detail. Open the store with that newer release, or restore the backup for the older one.
- **The older release refuses the store after the upgrade.** That is the forward-only rule. Restore the backup made before the upgrade, and open the migrated store only with the new release.
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5.** Another process has the store open, so the migration can't start. Stop it and open the store again ([Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/)).
- **`relate upgrade` fails.** Install the new release with the install script or the pinned binary steps instead ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).

properties.heading: Open the store once for writing
properties.text:
The first writable open migrates the store, then runs the statement. This step opens `team.rl` for writing on purpose, so the migration happens now and not in the middle of other work; the statement itself only reads:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["nodes"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"nodes":5}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.339666,"execute_ms":0.175167,"lex_parse_ms":0.027917,"lower_ms":0.041208999999999996,"parse_ms":0.10241700000000001,"plan_ms":0.053291000000000005,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.008624999999999999},"truncated":false}
```

relate prints nothing when it migrates: the output is the statement's, and the store is in the new format by the time it runs. A `--read-only` open never migrates; it reads an older store as it is. A crash in the middle of a migration leaves the old store as it was, and the next writable open migrates it again.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- `relate` on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- No process has the store open. To follow along, create the shared example graph as `team.rl`:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl < team.cypher
```

properties.heading: Read the store's format version
properties.text:
`relate info` reads a store's metadata without opening it, so it doesn't migrate anything:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team.rl
```

```text
layout: .rl bundle
superblock version: 1
codec: parquet
format version: 5
checkpoint LSN: 1
commit timestamp: 1
total bytes: 36864
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
relationships (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
indexes: 0
constraints: 0
```

`format version` is the version of the Parquet [snapshot](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#snapshot), and `superblock version` that of the `.rl` file around it. `relate info --json` prints the same fields as `format_version` and `superblock_version`. A store with the JSON [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec) prints `format version: unavailable`, because its version is inside `graph.json`, which a cold read doesn't parse.

Where each part's version shows:

| Part              | Where the version shows                         |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Parquet snapshot  | `format version` in `relate info`               |
| JSON snapshot     | `value_encoding` in `graph.json`                |
| Markdown snapshot | `value_encoding` in `.cypherlite/manifest.json` |
| `.rl` file        | `superblock version` in `relate info`           |

[Version markers](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#version-markers) lists the versions this release writes and reads for each part.

A store whose versions are all readable but not all current is migrated on its next writable open. A store with a version this release can't read is refused before anything is written to it.

From 0.1.2 to 1.0.0, the one part that changes is the Parquet snapshot: format version `3` becomes `5` at the store's first checkpoint, which a writable open writes at the latest when it closes, not before the statement runs. relate 0.1.2 reads format version `5`, so it still opens the store after the upgrade.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Keep relate up to date](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/#keep-relate-up-to-date): `relate upgrade` and how it checks a release.
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/): directory stores, `.rl` files and the codecs.
- [Back up and restore a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/): copies to restore from.
- [Changelog](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/changelog/): what each release changed, including formats.

properties.heading: Upgrade the binary
properties.text:
`relate upgrade --check` compares your version with the latest release and changes nothing. `relate upgrade` downloads the newer release, checks its signature and checksum, and replaces the binary. It runs on macOS and Linux; on Windows, download the new binary instead ([Keep relate up to date](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/#keep-relate-up-to-date)).

```bash
relate upgrade --check
relate upgrade
```

Then confirm the version that opens the store from now on. The first line names the release you installed; this run shows 1.0.1, the version this page is verified against:

```bash verify
relate --version
```

```text
Relate v1.0.1
License: Apache 2.0 (binary)
```

The [changelog](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/changelog/) says what changed between the two releases. A repository that pins a relate version in its `AGENTS.md` moves the pin in the same change.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Read the format version again. It is the one the new release writes:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team.rl --json
```

```text
{"checkpoint_lsn":1,"codec":"parquet","commit_ts":1,"constraints":[],"format_version":5,"indexes":[],"layout":"bundle","node_count":5,"rel_count":5,"superblock_version":1,"total_bytes":36864,"wal_segments":1}
```

Between two releases with the same format, the version stays the same and there is nothing to migrate.

properties.heading: Authentication and TLS for relate serve
properties.text: This guide shows you how to control who can reach a store that `relate serve` hosts. The server checks one HTTP Basic credential on every port it listens on: a generated token by default, or a `user:password` you set. It binds `127.0.0.1` by default and has no TLS of its own; to encrypt traffic, a TLS-terminating proxy goes in front.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**HTTP answers `401` with `authentication required`.** The request carries no credential, or not the server's. With a generated token, send `-u "$(cat <store>.auth-token)"`; a `:memory:` store's token is only in its startup line and changes on every start.

**A Bolt driver raises `Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized` with `The client is unauthorized due to authentication failure.`** The driver's user or password does not match. Split the token file's line at its first colon: the user is `relate`, the password is the token.

**`relate serve` exits 2 with an error that begins `Error: serve --mcp stdio skips auth`.** The stdio transport has no authentication, so `--auth` with only `--mcp stdio` is a usage error. Drop `--auth`, or serve a port listener beside stdio, such as `--http <port>`, which then uses the credential.

**`relate serve` exits 1 with `Error: --auth: expected user:password or 'none'`.** The value has no colon. Pass `<user>:<password>`, or `none`.

properties.heading: Keep the loopback default
properties.text: `--host` sets the bind address for every surface, and its default is `127.0.0.1`, so nothing outside the machine can connect. Any other value, such as `--host 0.0.0.0`, exposes the surfaces in plaintext: the credential and every result travel unencrypted. relate starts anyway and prints a warning first, beginning `serve: WARNING: --host 0.0.0.0 exposes the PLAINTEXT HTTP/MCP/Bolt surfaces to the network — serve has no TLS`. A container is the usual exception, because it must bind all interfaces to be reachable ([Run relate serve in a container](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/docker/)).

properties.heading: Know what each surface checks
properties.text:
One credential covers every listener of one `relate serve` process. What each [surface](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#surface) does with it:

| Surface                                                                                         | Credential                                                                   | Without a valid one                                                 | TLS            | Browser origins                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#http-query-api) (`--http <port>`) | `Authorization: Basic` on every route except `GET /`                         | `401`, code `42NFF`, with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="relate"`  | None           | Loopback, `https://browser.neo4j.io` and `https://console.neo4j.io`; `--origin <url>` replaces the list                                                                   |
| [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) over HTTP (`--mcp <port>`)              | `Authorization: Basic` on every request                                      | `401` with the same challenge                                       | None           | Loopback only, fixed                                                                                                                                                      |
| MCP on stdio (`--mcp stdio`)                                                                    | None: the host started the process                                           | Not applicable                                                      | Not applicable | Not applicable                                                                                                                                                            |
| [Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bolt) (`--bolt <port>`)                     | The driver's basic auth token, in `LOGON` at Bolt 5.4 or `HELLO` at Bolt 4.4 | `Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized`, then the connection closes | None           | WebSocket upgrades: loopback, `https://browser.neo4j.io` and `https://console.neo4j.io`, or loopback only with `--auth none`; `--ws-allow-origin <url>` replaces the list |

A failed credential waits 1 second before the server answers, on every surface. There is one credential, not users or roles: whoever holds it can do anything the open mode allows, so a server that only needs to answer reads opens the store `--read-only`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH`: `relate --version` prints its version ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- `curl`, for the checks.
- A [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) to serve. `graph.rl` in the examples holds the shared example graph; [Serve the HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/http-query-api/#create-a-store-to-serve) shows the command that creates it.

properties.heading: Put TLS in front
properties.text:
`relate serve` has no TLS and no certificate flags. To encrypt traffic, run a TLS-terminating proxy on the same machine: it holds the certificate, accepts encrypted connections, and forwards plaintext to the server's loopback port.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  accTitle: TLS in front of relate serve
  accDescr {
    A driver or an HTTP client connects to a TLS-terminating proxy over an encrypted connection.
    The proxy runs on the same machine and forwards plaintext to relate serve on 127.0.0.1.
    relate serve checks the Basic-auth credential on each of its listeners, which share one store.
  }
  Client["Driver or HTTP client"] -->|"bolt+s:// or https://"| Proxy["TLS proxy"]
  Proxy -->|"plaintext on 127.0.0.1"| Bolt["Bolt listener"]
  Proxy -->|"plaintext on 127.0.0.1"| HTTP["HTTP and MCP listeners"]
  Bolt --> Store["One store"]
  HTTP --> Store
```

A driver or an HTTP client connects to a TLS-terminating proxy over an encrypted connection. The proxy runs on the same machine and forwards plaintext to relate serve on 127.0.0.1. relate serve checks the Basic-auth credential on each of its listeners, which share one store.

| Client                                               | Connects to the proxy with |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| A Neo4j driver, certificate from a trusted authority | `bolt+s://<host>:<port>`   |
| A Neo4j driver, self-signed certificate              | `bolt+ssc://<host>:<port>` |
| An HTTP Query API or MCP client                      | `https://<host>:<port>`    |

What the proxy needs:

- One TLS listener per relate listener, each forwarding to the matching port on `127.0.0.1`.
- For Bolt, termination at the TCP level: Bolt is not HTTP, so the proxy decrypts the stream and passes the bytes through unchanged.
- For the HTTP Query API and MCP, TCP-level termination works the same way. An HTTP reverse proxy, not run for this page, has to pass the `Authorization` and `Content-Type` headers through, because the server answers `401` or `415` without them.
- The server left on `--host 127.0.0.1`, so the plaintext hop never leaves the machine.

This page gives no configuration for a named proxy, because none was run for it. The setup was checked with a small TCP proxy written for the test, which terminated TLS with a self-signed certificate and forwarded to the loopback ports: the Neo4j Python driver 5.28.2 connected with `bolt+ssc://`, and `curl` with `https://` and the certificate as its CA. The proxy keeps the certificate; relate never reads it, so a new certificate needs only a proxy reload.

properties.text:
- [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/#served-surfaces): the served surfaces' defaults in one table.
- [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/): `--auth`, `--host`, `--origin`, `--ws-allow-origin` and the connection limits.
- [Serve the HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/http-query-api/), [Serve a store over Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/bolt/) and [Serve a store over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/mcp/): each surface with the credential in use.
- [Run relate serve in a container](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/docker/): the container's bind address and where its token goes.

properties.heading: Set your own credential
properties.text:
Set `RELATE_AUTH` in the server's environment to a `user:password` of your choice:

```bash
RELATE_AUTH=<user>:<password> relate serve --http 7474 --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

The startup line reads `auth: basic (from RELATE_AUTH)`. `--auth <user>:<password>` does the same and wins over the variable, and its startup line reads `auth: basic (from --auth)`; on a shared machine the variable is the better place, because the process list shows a flag's value to every user. Neither writes a token file.

The value must hold a colon with something on both sides:

| Value                     | Result                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--auth ada`              | Exit code 1: `Error: --auth: expected user:password or 'none'`                      |
| `RELATE_AUTH=ada`         | Exit code 1: `Error: RELATE_AUTH: expected user:password or 'none'`                 |
| `RELATE_AUTH=:<password>` | Exit code 1: `Error: RELATE_AUTH: expected user:password with both sides non-empty` |
| `--auth` with no value    | Exit code 2: `Error: --auth requires USER:PASSWORD or none`                         |

A malformed value never falls back to no authentication.

properties.heading: Turn authentication off on loopback
properties.text: `--auth none` (or `RELATE_AUTH=none`) checks no credential on any surface. The startup line reads `auth: none (no credentials checked — publish ports only on trusted networks)`, and the Bolt WebSocket origins narrow to loopback. It fits a server on `127.0.0.1` that only local processes reach, or one behind a proxy that does its own authentication. A Bolt driver then connects with `auth=None`, and an HTTP client sends no `Authorization` header.

properties.heading: Use the generated token
properties.text:
With no `--auth` flag and no `RELATE_AUTH` variable, `relate serve` generates a token for the user `relate` at startup:

```bash
relate serve --http 7474 --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

On stderr, relate prints `auth: generated token for user relate: <token>` and `auth: persisted at ./graph.rl.auth-token (reused on restart)`. The token file sits beside the store, never inside it, with mode `0600`, and holds one line, `relate:<token>`. A restart reuses it and prints `auth: basic (token reused from ./graph.rl.auth-token)`. A `:memory:` store gets a new token on every start and no file; its startup line says so: `auth: connect with auth=(relate, <token>) — :memory: generates a fresh token every start`.

A client reads the credential from the file:

```bash
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "RETURN 1 AS ok"}' http://127.0.0.1:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2
```

```text
{"data":{"fields":["ok"],"values":[[1]]},"bookmarks":[]}
```

The token never appears on a command line, so the process list does not show it. Anyone who can read the token file can connect, which is why relate creates it readable by its owner only.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
This step writes a one-node `graph.rl`, then starts the server read-only on port 8842 and stops it, which generates the token. It shows the token file's mode and user, starts the server again, and sends one request with the credential and one with a wrong password. Last, it shows the second start's authentication line and a malformed `--auth`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./graph.rl "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'})" > /dev/null
relate serve --http 8842 --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2> first.log &
server=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8842/; do sleep 0.1; done
kill $server
wait $server
ls -l graph.rl.auth-token | cut -c1-10
cut -d: -f1 graph.rl.auth-token
relate serve --http 8842 --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2> second.log &
server=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8842/; do sleep 0.1; done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"statement": "RETURN 1 AS ok"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/neo4j/query/v2
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -u relate:wrong \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"statement": "RETURN 1 AS ok"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/neo4j/query/v2
kill $server
wait $server
grep '^auth:' second.log
relate serve --http 8842 --database ./graph.rl --read-only --auth ada
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
-rw-------
relate
200
401
auth: basic (token reused from ./graph.rl.auth-token)
Error: --auth: expected user:password or 'none'
exit=1
```

The token file is readable by its owner only and names the user `relate`. The token got `200`, the wrong password `401`, the second start reused the token, and the malformed credential stopped the server before it listened.

properties.heading: Serve a store over Bolt
properties.text: This guide shows you how to serve a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) over [Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bolt), Neo4j's binary protocol, with `relate serve --bolt <port>`, so Neo4j's official drivers and tools can run Cypher against it. The server speaks Bolt 4.4 and Bolt 5.4. The examples use the Neo4j Python driver; the other official drivers connect the same way.

properties.heading: Connect from a driver
properties.text:
The driver reads the credential from the token file and runs a [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) with a [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter). `database_` names the namespace; `neo4j` is the default, and `system` and `system_ontologies` are the other two.

```python title="team.py"
from pathlib import Path

from neo4j import GraphDatabase

# The token file beside the store holds one line: relate:<token>
user, password = Path("graph.rl.auth-token").read_text().strip().split(":", 1)

with GraphDatabase.driver("bolt://127.0.0.1:7687", auth=(user, password)) as driver:
    records, summary, keys = driver.execute_query(
        "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) "
        "RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name",
        project="relate",
        database_="neo4j",
    )
    print([record["name"] for record in records])
    print(summary.server.agent, summary.server.protocol_version)
```

Run it from the directory that holds `graph.rl`:

```text
['Ada', 'Grace']
Neo4j/5.26.0 5.4
```

The second line is the agent string `--bolt-identity` set and the Bolt version the two sides agreed; a 6.x driver prints that line as `Neo4j/5.26.0 (5, 4)`. The `neo4j://` scheme works too: the server answers routing requests with itself as the only member.

properties.heading: Connect Neo4j Browser
properties.text:
Neo4j Browser speaks Bolt over WebSocket, which the server answers on the Bolt port, so Browser needs no extra listener. Its version check reads `dbms.components()`, not the agent string, so it connects with or without `--bolt-identity`. The hosted Browser's origin, `https://browser.neo4j.io`, is on the server's default WebSocket allow list whenever authentication is on.

1. Start the server as in [Start the server](#start-the-server).
2. Open `https://browser.neo4j.io`, choose the `neo4j://` protocol, and enter `127.0.0.1:7687` as the connection URL.
3. Enter the user `relate` and, as the password, the token from `graph.rl.auth-token`, then connect.

Browser connects over `ws://127.0.0.1:7687` and opens the `neo4j` namespace. With `--auth none` the allow list narrows to loopback origins, so the hosted Browser also needs `--ws-allow-origin https://browser.neo4j.io`.

For this page, `https://browser.neo4j.io` in Chrome 157, on November 8, 2026, was connected to a server started with `--auth none --ws-allow-origin https://browser.neo4j.io` and no `--bolt-identity`, so no credential was entered. Chrome refused the connection until the site held Chrome's local network access permission; once granted, Browser reported `Connected to neo4j://127.0.0.1:8845`, and the statement from `team.py`, with `'relate'` in place of `$project`, returned `"Ada"` and `"Grace"`. With authentication on, the hosted origin was checked at the WebSocket upgrade: the server answered `101`, and `403` to an origin off the list.

properties.heading: Create a store to serve
properties.text:
This command writes a new `graph.rl` holding the shared example graph: three people, two projects, and who works on what.

```bash verify
relate --database ./graph.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**A Neo4j Python driver 5.x or a Java driver raises `UnsupportedServerProduct: Relate/1.0.1` or `UntrustedServerException`.** The driver checks the agent string. Start the server with `--bolt-identity Neo4j/5.26.0`.

**The driver raises `AuthError` with `Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized` and `The client is unauthorized due to authentication failure.`** The user or password does not match the server's credential. Read both from `<store>.auth-token`, or use the `user:password` from `--auth` or `RELATE_AUTH`.

**A write fails with `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` and a message that begins `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase`.** The server opened the store `--read-only`. Restart it without `--read-only` to accept writes.

**The driver raises `ServiceUnavailable` with `Connection refused`.** No server listens on that address: check the port in the startup line and that the server is still running.

properties.heading: Know which Bolt versions answer
properties.text:
| Item           | What relate does                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Versions       | Bolt 4.4 and Bolt 5.4 only. The first version in the driver's proposal list that covers one of them wins, so a driver that offers a 5.x range gets 5.4                                                             |
| Authentication | At 5.4, in the `LOGON` message; at 4.4, in `HELLO`                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Transactions   | `BEGIN`, `COMMIT` and `ROLLBACK` are real transactions; a `RUN` outside one commits on its own                                                                                                                     |
| Not served     | The Bolt 5.7 manifest handshake (drivers fall back to a version list), reactive sessions, and byte arrays stored as properties                                                                                     |
| WebSocket      | Served on the same port. Browser origins allowed by default: loopback, `https://browser.neo4j.io` and `https://console.neo4j.io`, or loopback only with `--auth none`; `--ws-allow-origin <url>` replaces the list |

The relate project's compatibility probes compared these behaviors with Neo4j 2026.09.0 (Community) at Bolt 4.4 and Bolt 5.4. The [Bolt server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/bolt/) lists every message.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH`: `relate --version` prints its version ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A Neo4j driver. The examples use the Neo4j Python driver (`pip install neo4j`, which installs a 6.x release). Their output comes from driver 5.28.2; drivers 6.0.3 through 6.4.0, also run for this page, print the same, except the protocol version, which 6.x prints as `(5, 4)`.
- A store to serve. The first step creates `graph.rl`.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Bolt server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/bolt/): every message, field, and failure code.
- [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/): every flag, including `--bolt-identity` and the WebSocket limits.
- [Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/): credentials, and `bolt+s://` through a TLS proxy.
- [Serve the HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/http-query-api/): the same store over JSON and HTTP.
- [Bolt errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#bolt-unauthorized): each failure a driver can raise.
- [Shared store across processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#shared-store-across-processes): one server owning a store for several clients.

properties.heading: Set the server identity
properties.text:
Some Neo4j drivers check the server's agent string when they connect and refuse one that does not start with `Neo4j/`. relate's own is `Relate/<version>`, so without `--bolt-identity` the Python driver 5.28.2 stops with `neo4j.exceptions.UnsupportedServerProduct: Relate/1.0.1`. The Python driver 6.x does not check: 6.0.3 through 6.4.0 connected without the flag and reported `Relate/1.0.0` as the agent. `--bolt-identity Neo4j/5.26.0` (or `RELATE_IDENTITY`) makes the server send that string instead. It is sent as written and claims no Neo4j feature parity; the Cypher relate runs is its own ([differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/)).

Per driver, from relate's compatibility notes as of relate 1.0.1 and the runs for this page:

| Driver                  | Versions named                                            | Needs `--bolt-identity` |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| Neo4j Python driver 5.x | 5.23 through 5.28; this page ran 5.28.2                   | Yes                     |
| Neo4j Python driver 6.x | 6.0.3, 6.1.0, 6.2.0, 6.3.1 and 6.4.0, run for this page   | No                      |
| Neo4j Java driver       | 5.28.5; every 5.x and 6.x release checks the agent string | Yes                     |
| Neo4j Go driver         | v5.28.5                                                   | No                      |

`cypher-shell` checks the agent string too, and the same flag admits it.

properties.heading: Start the server
properties.text:
Give `--bolt` a port; it has no default, and `7687` is the port Neo4j tools try first. The server binds `127.0.0.1` and runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM:

```bash
relate serve --bolt 7687 --database ./graph.rl --read-only --bolt-identity Neo4j/5.26.0
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

On stderr, relate prints that the store is open read-only, then `auth: generated token for user relate: <token>`, `auth: persisted at ./graph.rl.auth-token (reused on restart)`, and `serve: Bolt listening on bolt://127.0.0.1:7687 (auth: basic)`. The token file holds one line, `relate:<token>`: the user name and the password a driver sends. [Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/) covers setting your own credential.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
A driver is not needed to check that the port speaks Bolt. This step starts the server read-only on port 8843, with the HTTP Query API beside it on port 8842. It reads the HTTP discovery document, which names the Bolt address, then sends the Bolt handshake from bash, offering 5.4 and then 4.4, and compares the server's 4-byte answer with version 5.4. Then it stops the server:

```bash verify
relate serve --bolt 8843 --http 8842 --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2> serve.log &
server=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8842/; do sleep 0.1; done
curl -s -w '\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/
exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8843
printf '\x60\x60\xb0\x17\x00\x00\x04\x05\x00\x00\x04\x04\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00' >&3
head -c 4 <&3 > reply.bin
exec 3>&-
printf '\x00\x00\x04\x05' | cmp -s - reply.bin && echo "Bolt 5.4 agreed"
kill $server
wait $server
```

```text
{"query":"http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/{databaseName}/query/v2","transaction":"http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/{databaseName}/query/v2/tx","neo4j_version":"1.0.1","neo4j_edition":"community","auth_config":{"oidc_providers":[]},"bolt_direct":"bolt://127.0.0.1:8843"}
Bolt 5.4 agreed
```

`bolt_direct` names the Bolt listener, and the handshake agreed on Bolt 5.4. With a driver, `team.py` printing `['Ada', 'Grace']` is the same check end to end.

properties.heading: Write, and read the bookmark
properties.text:
A [bookmark](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bookmark) marks a commit's place in the store's commit sequence, `relate:<n>`. The server returns one after an auto-commit write and after the `COMMIT` of a transaction that wrote. Bookmarks a driver sends back are accepted and ignored: there is one store, and every commit is visible to the next statement on any connection.

Writes need a server started without `--read-only`. This command opens `graph.rl` for writing:

```bash
relate serve --bolt 7687 --database ./graph.rl --bolt-identity Neo4j/5.26.0
```

This program writes a new person in one explicit transaction, with a date and a date-time from Python as parameters, then reads them back:

```python title="writes.py"
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from neo4j import GraphDatabase

user, password = Path("graph.rl.auth-token").read_text().strip().split(":", 1)

with GraphDatabase.driver("bolt://127.0.0.1:7687", auth=(user, password)) as driver:
    with driver.session(database="neo4j") as session:
        # An explicit transaction: both statements commit together.
        with session.begin_transaction() as tx:
            tx.run(
                "MATCH (p:Project {name: $project}) "
                "CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: 'engineer', joined: $joined})-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(p)",
                project="relate", name="Lin", joined=date(2026, 11, 7),
            )
            tx.run("MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Lin'}) SET p.seen = $seen",
                   seen=datetime(2026, 11, 7, 9, 30, tzinfo=timezone.utc))
            tx.commit()
        print(session.last_bookmarks())

        record = session.run(
            "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Lin'}) "
            "RETURN p.joined AS joined, p.joined + duration('P1D') AS next_day, p.seen AS seen"
        ).single()
        print(type(record["joined"]).__name__, record["joined"], record["next_day"])
        print(type(record["seen"]).__name__, record["seen"])
```

The number in the bookmark depends on how many commits the store has seen:

```text
<Bookmarks values={'relate:2'}>
Date 2026-11-07 2026-11-08
DateTime 2026-11-07T09:30:00.000000000+00:00
```

The date and the date-time crossed the wire as Bolt temporal structures, were stored as a `DATE` and a `ZONED DATETIME`, and came back as the driver's `neo4j.time` types. Times, local date-times, durations, and points cross the same way. When two transactions write the same data, the later commit fails with the transient error `Neo.TransientError.Transaction.Outdated`; the server never retries, and a driver's managed transaction (`execute_write`, `execute_query`) retries it.

properties.heading: Run relate serve in a container
properties.text: This guide shows you how to run `relate serve` in a container, with the Dockerfile that ships in the relate source repository. One container serves [Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bolt) on port 7687, the [HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#http-query-api) on 7474 and [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) over HTTP on 7475, from one [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) kept on a volume, with one credential for all three. No prebuilt image is published: you build it from a checkout of the source. For this page, the `relate serve` commands the image runs and the endpoints it answers on were checked against the relate 1.0.1 binary on the host, and the Compose file was parsed by Docker Compose 5.6.1. The image itself was not built or run.

properties.heading: Build the image
properties.text:
From the root of the checkout:

```bash
docker build -t relate-bolt:1.0.1 .
```

The Dockerfile compiles `relate` in a Rust build stage and copies the static binaries into an image built `FROM scratch`. The repository's `make docker` runs the same build and tags it `relate-bolt:<version>` and `relate-bolt:latest`. What the image holds:

| Item                | Value                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Base                | `scratch`: no shell, no package manager, no HTTP client                                                                                          |
| Binaries            | `/bin/relate` and `/bin/entrypoint`, the process that starts `relate serve`                                                                      |
| User                | UID and GID `1000`                                                                                                                               |
| Volume              | `/data`; the default store is the directory store `/data/graph`                                                                                  |
| Ports               | `7687` (Bolt), `7474` (HTTP Query API), `7475` (MCP over HTTP)                                                                                   |
| Effective arguments | `--host 0.0.0.0 --database /data/graph --bolt 7687` (the image's `CMD`); the entrypoint appends `--http 7474 --mcp 7475` when they are not given |

Arguments after the image name go to `relate serve` in place of the defaults, and the entrypoint adds back any of `--host`, `--database`, `--bolt`, `--http` and `--mcp` they leave out. So `docker run relate-bolt:1.0.1 --read-only` serves the default store read-only on all three ports.

properties.heading: Check its health
properties.text: The image has no shell and no HTTP client, so a Docker `HEALTHCHECK` or a Compose `healthcheck`, which run inside the container, have nothing to run. Probe from outside instead: `GET /` on the HTTP port needs no credential and answers `200` with the discovery document while the server is up, which suits an HTTP probe from an orchestrator or a load balancer.

properties.heading: Create the store on a volume
properties.text:
The first run creates the store and serves it writable. This command writes to the volume `relate-data`: `RELATE_QUERY` is a statement the entrypoint runs once, when the store does not exist yet, before the server starts.

```bash
docker run -d --name relate-seed \
  -p 127.0.0.1:7687:7687 -p 127.0.0.1:7474:7474 -p 127.0.0.1:7475:7475 \
  -v relate-data:/data \
  -e DO_NOT_TRACK=1 \
  -e RELATE_AUTH \
  -e RELATE_QUERY="UNWIND ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Noor'] AS name CREATE (:Person {name: name})" \
  relate-bolt:1.0.1
```

| Setting                      | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-p 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>` | Inside the container the server must bind `0.0.0.0` to be reachable, and prints a plaintext warning at startup. Publishing on the host's `127.0.0.1` keeps the ports off the network                          |
| `-v relate-data:/data`       | A named volume starts as a copy of the image's `/data`, owned by UID 1000, so the server can write the store there. A host directory mounted instead must be writable by UID 1000                             |
| `-e DO_NOT_TRACK=1`          | `relate serve` sends one usage-metrics event when it exits unless metrics are off; the statements it serves send nothing ([Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/)) |
| `-e RELATE_AUTH`             | Passes your shell's `RELATE_AUTH=<user>:<password>` to the server. Without it, the server generates a token                                                                                                   |

Without `RELATE_AUTH`, the token is in the container's log, on the line that starts `auth: generated token for user relate:`, and on the volume as `/data/graph.auth-token`, where a restart reuses it:

```bash
docker logs relate-seed 2>&1 | grep 'auth:'
```

[Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/) covers the credential on each surface. Once the store holds what it should, stop and remove the writable container with `docker stop relate-seed` and `docker rm relate-seed`.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**The container exits at once, and `docker logs` shows `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at /data/graph`.** The volume holds no store and the container runs `--read-only`, which never creates one. Run the seeding container first, or mount the volume that holds the store.

**The log shows a `WARNING` that begins `serve: WARNING: --host 0.0.0.0 exposes the PLAINTEXT`.** That is expected in a container, which must bind all interfaces. The `127.0.0.1:` prefix on each `-p` keeps the ports on the host's loopback; for traffic across a network, put a TLS-terminating proxy in front ([Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/#put-tls-in-front)).

**A client gets `401`, or a driver `Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized`.** The client's credential is not the container's. Use the `RELATE_AUTH` value the container was started with, or the token from `docker logs`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- Docker Engine 23.0 or later, where BuildKit is the default builder. This page parsed its Compose file with Docker Compose 5.6.1 on Docker 29.9.2.
- A checkout of the relate source repository, `github.com/relatedb/relate`, at the release you want to serve: `git clone --branch v1.0.1 --depth 1 https://github.com/relatedb/relate`.
- relate on your `PATH` for the last check, optional ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/): the credential, the bind address, and TLS in front.
- [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/): every flag the container's arguments can carry.
- [Serve the HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/http-query-api/), [Serve a store over Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/bolt/) and [Serve a store over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/mcp/): connecting to each port.
- [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/): what `relate serve` sends and how `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` stops it.

properties.heading: Run it with docker compose
properties.text:
The same read-only service as a Compose file. `RELATE_AUTH` comes from your shell or an `.env` file beside it, and Compose refuses to start without it:

```yaml title="compose.yaml"
services:
  relate:
    image: relate-bolt:1.0.1
    command: ["--read-only"]
    environment:
      DO_NOT_TRACK: "1"
      RELATE_AUTH: ${RELATE_AUTH:?set RELATE_AUTH to user:password}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:7687:7687"
      - "127.0.0.1:7474:7474"
      - "127.0.0.1:7475:7475"
    volumes:
      - relate-data:/data
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  relate-data:
    external: true
```

To allow writes, remove the `command` line. `external: true` uses the `relate-data` volume the seeding run created, instead of a new empty one, which a read-only start cannot open.

properties.heading: Serve the store read-only
properties.text:
Run the image again on the same volume with `--read-only`, a [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) open. The server takes no writer lease and refuses every write, on every surface:

```bash
docker run -d --name relate \
  -p 127.0.0.1:7687:7687 -p 127.0.0.1:7474:7474 -p 127.0.0.1:7475:7475 \
  -v relate-data:/data \
  -e DO_NOT_TRACK=1 \
  -e RELATE_AUTH \
  relate-bolt:1.0.1 --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`. A read-only open never creates a store, so on an empty volume this container exits at once. The same flags with the host binary show the message it prints, with the path the container would name in place of `<dir>/data/graph`:

```bash verify
relate serve --database ./data/graph --read-only --http 8842
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: Failed to open Relate: storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <dir>/data/graph
exit=1
```

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The container was not run for this page. This check runs the command the read-only container runs, with the host binary on loopback ports: it creates a store, serves it read-only on port 8842 with Bolt on 8843, probes `GET /` without a credential, runs a read with the generated token, and stops the server.

```bash verify
relate --database ./data/graph "UNWIND ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Noor'] AS name CREATE (:Person {name: name})" > /dev/null
relate serve --database ./data/graph --read-only --http 8842 --bolt 8843 --mcp 8844 2> serve.log &
server=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8842/; do sleep 0.1; done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/
curl -s -u "$(cat data/graph.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"}' \
  -w '\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/neo4j/query/v2
kill $server
wait $server
```

```text
200
{"data":{"fields":["people"],"values":[[3]]},"bookmarks":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.529209,"execute_ms":0.350083,"lex_parse_ms":0.032125,"lower_ms":0.043042,"parse_ms":0.110791,"plan_ms":0.056208999999999995,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.007375},"planCache":"miss"}
```

Against the container, the same two `curl` commands go to `http://127.0.0.1:7474/`, with `-u "$RELATE_AUTH"` or the token from `docker logs`.

properties.heading: Serve the HTTP Query API
properties.text: This guide shows you how to serve a relate store over the [HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#http-query-api) with `relate serve --http <port>`. A client sends one `POST` holding a Cypher [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) as JSON to `/db/<namespace>/query/v2` and gets one JSON answer back. The request and the answer follow Neo4j's Query API v2, so any HTTP client works, `curl` included, with no driver.

properties.heading: Create a store to serve
properties.text:
This command writes a new `graph.rl` holding the shared example graph: three people, two projects, and who works on what.

```bash verify
relate --database ./graph.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**`401` with code `42NFF` and `authentication required`.** The request has no credential or the wrong one. Send `-u "$(cat <store>.auth-token)"`, or the `user:password` from `--auth` or `RELATE_AUTH`.

**`415` with a message that begins `the request content type is browser-"simple"`.** The `POST` has no JSON content type; `curl -d` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` unless told otherwise. Add `-H 'Content-Type: application/json'`.

**`400` with code `42N18` and `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase`.** The server opened the store `--read-only`. Restart it without `--read-only` to accept writes.

**`404` with code `42N00` and `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`.** The path names a namespace other than `neo4j`, `system` or `system_ontologies`.

properties.heading: Pass parameters
properties.text:
Put the values in `parameters` and refer to them as `$name`:

```bash
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role ORDER BY name", "parameters": {"project": "relate"}}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2
```

```text
{"data":{"fields":["name","role"],"values":[["Ada","engineer"],["Grace","engineer"]]},"bookmarks":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.37425,"execute_ms":0.25945900000000005,"lex_parse_ms":0.019792,"lower_ms":0.02575,"parse_ms":0.064625,"plan_ms":0.042792,"result_generation_ms":0.000334,"rewrite_ms":0.002167},"planCache":"miss"}
```

Under `application/json`, a parameter is plain JSON: a string, a number, a boolean, a list, or a map. A date arrives as its string, so build the typed value in Cypher: `RETURN date($day) AS day` with `{"day": "2026-11-07"}`. The other request type, `application/vnd.neo4j.query.v1.2`, also takes the typed form Neo4j's official clients send, such as `{"$type": "Integer", "_value": "41"}`. A statement that names a parameter the request leaves out fails with `400` and code `42N02`; it is never bound as `null`.

To get typed values back, ask for them with `Accept: application/vnd.neo4j.query`. Each value then arrives as `{"$type": …, "_value": …}`, such as `{"$type":"Date","_value":"2026-11-07"}`, with integers as strings inside `_value`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH`: `relate --version` prints its version ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- `curl`, or any HTTP client.
- A store to serve. The first step creates `graph.rl`.

properties.heading: Read the status codes
properties.text:
A failed request answers with a status code and an `errors` array holding one `code` and `message`:

| Status | `code`  | Cause                                                                  |
| ------ | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `400`  | `42N06` | A body that is not JSON or lacks `statement`, or a Cypher syntax error |
| `400`  | `42N02` | A parameter the statement names is missing from `parameters`           |
| `400`  | `22G03` | A type error, such as `type error: / by zero`                          |
| `400`  | `42N18` | A write on a server started `--read-only`                              |
| `400`  | `42000` | Any other statement error                                              |
| `401`  | `42NFF` | No credential, or the wrong one                                        |
| `404`  | `42N00` | An unknown namespace or route                                          |
| `404`  | `42000` | An unknown transaction id                                              |
| `404`  | `42N90` | A transaction that expired while idle                                  |
| `405`  | `42000` | The wrong method for the route                                         |
| `415`  | `42000` | A `POST` without a JSON content type                                   |
| `429`  | `42N91` | A new transaction while 128 are open                                   |

The [HTTP errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#http-unauthorized) list every code with its message.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [HTTP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/http/): every route, header, and status code.
- [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/): every flag, such as the transaction limits.
- [Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/): credentials and TLS in front of the server.
- [Serve over Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/bolt/): the same store for Neo4j drivers.
- [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/): when one server should own the store.
- [Shared store across processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#shared-store-across-processes): the problem this page solves.

properties.heading: Run a statement
properties.text:
`POST` a JSON body with `Content-Type: application/json` to `/db/neo4j/query/v2`. `neo4j` is the default namespace; `system` and `system_ontologies` are the other two.

```bash
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "MATCH (p:Person {name: \"Ada\"}) RETURN p"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2
```

```text
{"data":{"fields":["p"],"values":[[{"elementId":"0","labels":["Person"],"properties":{"name":"Ada","role":"engineer"}}]]},"bookmarks":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.410167,"execute_ms":0.235459,"lex_parse_ms":0.030125,"lower_ms":0.039292,"parse_ms":0.111916,"plan_ms":0.052542,"result_generation_ms":0.000209,"rewrite_ms":0.006541},"planCache":"miss"}
```

`data.fields` names the columns and `data.values` holds one array per row, in column order. A [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node) is an object with its `elementId`, `labels` and `properties`; a [relationship](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship) adds `startNodeElementId`, `endNodeElementId` and `type`; a [path](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#path) is an array that alternates nodes and relationships. Temporal values are ISO 8601 strings.

| Request field     | Required                  | Meaning                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `statement`       | Required                  | One Cypher statement                                        |
| `parameters`      | Optional                  | An object holding a value for each `$name` in the statement |
| `includeCounters` | Optional, default `false` | Adds `counters` to an answer that changed nothing           |

| Answer field                     | When it is present                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data`                           | Always: `fields` and `values`                                                                                                               |
| `counters`                       | After a statement that changed the graph, or with `includeCounters`: the 11 mutation counters, such as `nodes_created` and `properties_set` |
| `bookmarks`                      | Always, and always `[]`: there is no bookmark manager, because every commit is visible to the next request                                  |
| `notifications`                  | Only for an `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` statement that raised one                                                                                |
| `queryPlan`, `profiledQueryPlan` | Only for an `EXPLAIN` or a `PROFILE` statement                                                                                              |
| `timings`                        | Whenever a statement ran: its phase timings in milliseconds, such as `parse_ms`, `plan_ms` and `execute_ms`                                 |
| `planCache`                      | Whenever a statement ran: the plan cache's outcome, such as `miss`                                                                          |

`timings` and `planCache` come after the members of Neo4j's Query API v2 shape, and their values differ on every request. Unlike the CLI's envelope, the answer carries no column types.

properties.heading: Start the server
properties.text:
Give `--http` a port; it has no default. The server binds `127.0.0.1` and runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM:

```bash
relate serve --http 7474 --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

On stderr, relate prints that the store is open read-only, then `auth: generated token for user relate: <token>`, `auth: persisted at ./graph.rl.auth-token (reused on restart)`, and `serve: HTTP Query API v2 listening on http://127.0.0.1:7474 (auth: basic)`. Every request to a statement route needs that credential as HTTP Basic authentication. The token file holds one line, `relate:<token>`, which is the form `curl -u` takes. [Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/) covers setting your own credential.

`GET /` is the one route that needs no credential. It returns the discovery document: the statement endpoint under `query`, the transaction endpoint under `transaction`, the relate version under `neo4j_version`, `neo4j_edition` `community`, and `bolt_direct` when the same process also serves Bolt. [Verify](#verify) shows a whole one.

properties.heading: Use it from Neo4j tools
properties.text:
The request and answer shapes are those of Neo4j's Query API v2 statement and transaction endpoints. A client built for that API talks to relate unchanged, within the Cypher relate supports ([differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/)). relate adds one thing, gzip compression for an answer of 1 KiB or more when the request sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. It leaves out batching, a bookmark manager, and JSON Lines answers.

A browser page may call the server only from an allowed origin. By default those are the loopback origins and the hosted Neo4j Browser and Neo4j Console, `https://browser.neo4j.io` and `https://console.neo4j.io`. `--origin <url>` replaces that list and repeats for each origin.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
This step starts the server read-only on port 8842, reads the discovery document, runs a statement with a parameter, tries a write, and sends a request without a credential. Then it stops the server:

```bash verify
relate serve --http 8842 --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2> serve.log &
server=$!
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8842/; do sleep 0.1; done
curl -s -w '\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name", "parameters": {"project": "relate"}}' \
  -w '\n%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/neo4j/query/v2
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "CREATE (:Person {name: $name})", "parameters": {"name": "Eve"}}' \
  -w '\n%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/neo4j/query/v2
curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"statement": "RETURN 1 AS ok"}' \
  -w '\n%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/neo4j/query/v2
kill $server
wait $server
```

```text
{"query":"http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/{databaseName}/query/v2","transaction":"http://127.0.0.1:8842/db/{databaseName}/query/v2/tx","neo4j_version":"1.0.1","neo4j_edition":"community","auth_config":{"oidc_providers":[]}}
{"data":{"fields":["name"],"values":[["Ada"],["Grace"]]},"bookmarks":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.608958,"execute_ms":0.41325,"lex_parse_ms":0.03216599999999999,"lower_ms":0.045292,"parse_ms":0.121875,"plan_ms":0.062041,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.006167000000000001},"planCache":"miss"}
200
{"errors":[{"code":"42N18","message":"semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance."}]}
400
{"errors":[{"code":"42NFF","message":"authentication required"}]}
401
```

The read returned Ada and Grace with `200`, the write was refused with `400` and the store is unchanged, and the request without a credential got `401`.

properties.heading: Write in a transaction
properties.text:
Each request to `/db/neo4j/query/v2` runs as its own transaction and commits when it succeeds. To group several statements, use the transaction routes. A read-only server serves them too, but a write staged in a transaction there fails at the commit with `400` and code `42N18`, and the store is unchanged. This command opens `graph.rl` for writing:

```bash
relate serve --http 7474 --database ./graph.rl
```

Begin a transaction with a `POST` to `…/query/v2/tx`. The body's statement is optional, and the answer is `201` with a `transaction` block:

```bash
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"statement": "CREATE (:Person {name: \"Tess\", role: \"engineer\"})"}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2/tx
```

```text
{"data":{"fields":[],"values":[]},"counters":{"constraints_added":0,"constraints_removed":0,"indexes_added":0,"indexes_removed":0,"labels_added":1,"labels_removed":0,"nodes_created":1,"nodes_deleted":0,"properties_set":2,"relationships_created":0,"relationships_deleted":0},"bookmarks":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.4075,"execute_ms":0.23766600000000002,"lex_parse_ms":0.004958,"lower_ms":0.004916,"parse_ms":0.162292,"plan_ms":0.002125,"result_generation_ms":0.000166,"rewrite_ms":0.00033299999999999996},"planCache":"miss","transaction":{"expires":"2026-11-10T01:58:10.021Z","id":"tx-0"}}
```

The `id`, the `expires` time and the `timings` differ on every run. Use the `id` in the routes that follow:

| Method and path                                | Does                                                                        | Answers                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `POST /db/<namespace>/query/v2/tx`             | Begins a transaction, running the body's statement if it has one            | `201`, with `transaction.id` and `transaction.expires` |
| `POST /db/<namespace>/query/v2/tx/<id>`        | Runs a statement in the transaction; an empty body `{}` only keeps it alive | `200`, with the `transaction` block                    |
| `POST /db/<namespace>/query/v2/tx/<id>/commit` | Runs the body's statement if it has one, then commits                       | `200`, with no `transaction` block                     |
| `DELETE /db/<namespace>/query/v2/tx/<id>`      | Rolls back                                                                  | `202`                                                  |

Inside the transaction, its own writes are visible; to other requests they are not, until the commit. A transaction idle for 60 seconds expires and rolls back (`--tx-idle-timeout-secs`), and at most 128 can be open at once (`--max-open-transactions`). With `"accessMode": "READ"` in the body of the request that begins a transaction, a write in it fails with `writing is not allowed in a READ transaction` and the transaction stays open.

properties.heading: Serve a store over MCP
properties.text: This guide shows you how to serve a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) over [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) (the Model Context Protocol) with `relate serve --mcp`: on stdio, for an agent host that starts the server itself, or on a port over HTTP, for clients that connect to a URL. The store opens [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) unless the agent is meant to write. The configuration block for each agent host is in [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/); this page is about the server those blocks start.

properties.heading: Choose read-only or writable
properties.text:
What an agent can do depends on how the store is opened, not on the host's settings. Opened `--read-only`, the server takes no writer lease, never creates the store, and lists two tools. One JSON-RPC `tools/list` request shows them; `grep` keeps only the tool names:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -o '"name":"[a-z_]*"'
```

```text
"name":"read_cypher"
"name":"get_schema"
```

Opened writable, the server also lists `write_cypher`. This command opens `graph.rl` for writing, though the request it sends writes nothing:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -o '"name":"[a-z_]*"'
```

```text
"name":"write_cypher"
"name":"read_cypher"
"name":"get_schema"
```

The three tools, with the fields of the server's `tools/list` answer:

| Tool           | Listed                          | Input                                                                                                | Answer                                                                                                                                                      | Annotations                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `read_cypher`  | Always                          | `statement` (string, required), `parameters` (object, default `{}`)                                  | The result as a JSON envelope in the text content: `columns`, `columnTypes`, `rows`, `stats`, `notifications`, `plan`, `error`, and timings in milliseconds | `title: "Read Cypher"`, `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`   |
