| `get_schema`   | Always                          | `sample_size` (integer, optional; the nodes and relationships examined per label; `-1` examines all) | A map keyed by label: each label's `count`, its property keys with inferred types, and its outgoing relationship types                                      | `title: "Get Schema"`, `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`    |
| `write_cypher` | Only when the store is writable | `statement` (string, required), `parameters` (object, default `{}`)                                  | The same envelope with empty `rows`; the mutation counters are under `stats`                                                                                | `title: "Write Cypher"`, `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: true`, `idempotentHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false` |

Every call is classified with `EXPLAIN` before it runs, and the tools hold to that class whatever the open mode:

| The call                                                             | What happens                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A write or a schema statement (`CREATE INDEX`) sent to `read_cypher` | Refused with `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query`; the store is unchanged |
| A read sent to `write_cypher`                                        | Refused with `Only write queries are allowed for write-query`                        |
| `write_cypher` on a read-only server                                 | Refused with `unknown tool 'write_cypher'`                                           |

The message about `MATCH` is the wording the server keeps for compatibility; any pure read passes `read_cypher`, `OPTIONAL MATCH` and `RETURN` without `MATCH` included. A refusal is a tool result with `isError: true`, not a JSON-RPC error, so the host shows it to the agent as a failed call.

Two more flags narrow what the server allows:

- `--safe`, for a writable server, refuses a `CREATE` or `MERGE` of a new node bound to a variable without a label (an anonymous `()` passes), and a `MATCH` read whose final `RETURN` or `WITH` has neither `LIMIT` nor a reducing aggregate (`collect()` does not count). The refusal arrives as a tool error that starts `Error: syntax error: SafeModeViolation:`.
- `--read-only=live`, on a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store), serves a store another process is writing and follows that writer's commits ([live read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#live-read-only)). `write_cypher` is not listed. A `.rl` store and `:memory:` refuse `--read-only=live`.

[Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/) covers backups and the other controls to put in place before an agent writes.

properties.heading: Create a store to serve
properties.text:
This command writes a new `graph.rl` holding the shared example graph: three people, two projects, and who works on what.

```bash verify
relate --database ./graph.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
**The server exits 1 with `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage error: database not found: <path>`.** A read-only open never creates a store, and a relative path resolves against the directory the server starts in. Use the store's absolute path, or create the store first.

**A call fails with `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query` or `unknown tool 'write_cypher'`.** The statement writes, and the server only reads: either the store is open `--read-only` or the statement went to `read_cypher`. Send writes to `write_cypher` on a server started without `--read-only`.

**`relate serve` exits 2 with an error that begins `Error: serve --mcp stdio skips auth`.** `--auth` applies to the port listeners only. Drop it from a stdio command.

**`relate serve` exits 1 with an error that begins `Error: serve --mcp 8000: cannot bind 127.0.0.1:8000: Address already in use`.** Another process holds the port. Ports have no defaults, so pick another one.

**HTTP answers `401` or `415`.** The request lacked the credential (`curl -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)"`), or it had no `Content-Type` or a browser-simple one (`text/plain` or a form type, which is what `curl -d` sends without `-H`); `Content-Type: application/json` clears it.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH`: `relate --version` prints its version ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A store to serve. A read-only open never creates one, so the first step creates `graph.rl`.
- `curl`, for the HTTP transport.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/): the configuration block for each agent host.
- [MCP server reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/): the protocol, the tools, and every answer.
- [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/): every flag of the command.
- [Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/): credentials, the token file, and TLS in front.
- [MCP errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#mcp-read-query-only): each refusal and JSON-RPC error code.
- [Graph queries over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#graph-queries-over-mcp): the problem this page solves.

properties.heading: Serve on stdio
properties.text:
Pass the keyword `stdio` to `--mcp`:

```bash
relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

The server reads newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 messages on stdin and writes one response per request on stdout. It runs in the foreground until the host closes stdin, then exits 0. Its startup lines go to stderr, so stdout carries nothing but JSON-RPC. There is no authentication challenge on stdio: the host spawned the process, and `--auth` on a stdio-only run is a usage error (exit code 2).

This is the command every block in [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/) starts: the blocks under [Claude Code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/#claude-code), [Claude Desktop](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/#claude-desktop), and [Cursor](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/#cursor), which also has an install link.

properties.heading: Serve over HTTP
properties.text:
Pass a port number to `--mcp` and the server takes the MCP streamable HTTP transport on `127.0.0.1:<port>`. It runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM. Every request needs a credential: without `--auth` or `RELATE_AUTH`, relate generates a token for the user `relate`.

> **Warning: Plaintext on the network**
>
> `relate serve` has no TLS. Keep the default `--host 127.0.0.1`, or put a TLS-terminating proxy in front ([Authentication and TLS](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/)).

```bash
relate serve --mcp 8000 --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

To allow writes, remove `--read-only`.

On stderr, relate prints that the store is open read-only, then `auth: generated token for user relate: <token>` and `auth: persisted at ./graph.rl.auth-token (reused on restart)`, and last `serve: MCP (streamable HTTP) listening on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (auth: basic)`. The token file holds one line, `relate:<token>`, with mode `0600`; a restart reuses it and prints `auth: basic (token reused from ./graph.rl.auth-token)` instead. A `:memory:` store gets a fresh token on every start and no file.

In another terminal, send one JSON-RPC message per `POST`, with `Content-Type: application/json` and the credential. The token file's line is already in the `user:password` form `curl -u` takes:

```bash
curl -s -u "$(cat graph.rl.auth-token)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{}}}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"Person\":{\"count\":3,\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"role\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"relationships\":{\"KNOWS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Person\"]},\"MAINTAINS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"]},\"WORKS_ON\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"],\"properties\":{\"since\":{\"type\":\"Integer\"}}}},\"type\":\"node\"},\"Project\":{\"count\":2,\"properties\":{\"language\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"type\":\"node\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

The transport is stateless: there is no `Mcp-Session-Id`, so the requests need no `initialize` first and can come in any order. A notification gets `202 Accepted` with an empty body. How the HTTP transport answers what it does not serve:

| Request                                                                        | Status                                                                       | Body                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A `POST` with no `Content-Type`, `text/plain`, or a form type (browser-simple) | `415`, before the credential check                                           | `{"error":"the request content type is browser-\"simple\" — a cross-origin form cannot send a non-simple type without a preflight"}` |
| No credential, or the wrong one                                                | `401`, with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="relate"`, after a 1-second delay | `{"error":"authentication required"}`                                                                                                |

[Errors and refusals](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/#errors-and-refusals) in the MCP server reference lists every status, including the `403` for a browser origin that is not loopback and the `405` for any method but `POST`, and the order the checks run in.

The MCP transport allows only loopback browser origins and has no `--origin` setting; the `--origin` flag is for the HTTP Query API. To register the URL with Claude Code, use [Serve over HTTP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/#serve-over-http) in the host guide.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
Run a read through `read_cypher` on the read-only server, the way a host does. The tool's answer is a JSON string inside the JSON-RPC response, so its quotes arrive escaped; `grep` keeps the `rows` member, because the rest of the envelope holds timings that change on every run:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name","parameters":{"project":"relate"}}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -o '\\"rows\\":\[[^]]*\]'
```

```text
\"rows\":[{\"name\":\"Ada\"},{\"name\":\"Grace\"}]
```

Ada and Grace work on `relate`, so the server opened the store, ran the [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) with its parameter, and answered on stdout.

properties.heading: Back up and restore a store
properties.text: This guide shows you how to back up a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), check that the backup opens, and restore from it. The backup command is `relate clone`: it opens the source read-only, never writes it, and writes the committed state into a new store. A [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store) can be cloned while another process writes to it; a `.rl` file can be cloned or copied while no process has it open.

properties.heading: Back up a directory store
properties.text:
Clone the store into a new path. A destination ending in `.rl` gives a backup that is one file; any other path gives a directory store. When the source is a directory store, the destination's parent folder must exist; the destination itself must never exist:

```bash verify
mkdir backups
relate clone ./team ./backups/team-2026-11-07.rl
```

`relate clone` prints nothing on success. It reads the state committed at the moment it opens the source and does not follow later commits, so the copy is consistent even if a writer keeps going. The writer keeps its lock and keeps committing: a directory store allows read-only opens beside its writer, and `clone` opens the source that way.

If the store keeps its [write-ahead log](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal) (WAL) outside its folder (opened with `--wal-dir`), pass the same `--wal-dir` to `relate clone`.

properties.heading: Back up a single-file store
properties.text:
A `.rl` file allows no second opener while a writer holds it, so `relate clone` and `--read-only` opens are both refused until the writer exits. Back up a `.rl` store while no process has it open:

```bash
relate clone ./app.rl ./backups/app-2026-11-07.rl
```

A `.rl` file holds its WAL inside it, so a plain copy of the file (`cp`) taken while nothing has it open is a complete backup too. `relate clone` writes a compact copy: a `.rl` file keeps the space it once needed, and the clone holds only the current state.

properties.heading: Check that the backup opens
properties.text:
Open the backup [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) and count what it holds. A read-only open never writes, checkpoints or migrates the store, so checking a backup leaves it as it was:

```bash verify
relate --database ./backups/team-2026-11-07.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["nodes"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"nodes":5}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.46954199999999996,"execute_ms":0.309667,"lex_parse_ms":0.027375,"lower_ms":0.038708,"parse_ms":0.100791,"plan_ms":0.05025,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.008042},"truncated":false}
```

`relate info` reads the backup's metadata without opening it, including the node and relationship counts at its last [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint):

```bash verify
relate info --database ./backups/team-2026-11-07.rl
```

```text
layout: .rl bundle
superblock version: 1
codec: parquet
format version: 5
checkpoint LSN: 1
commit timestamp: 1
total bytes: 32768
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
relationships (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
indexes: 0
constraints: 0
```

Compare the counts with the source, and run a statement your application depends on. A backup is only as good as the last time it opened.

properties.heading: Copy files only when nothing has the store open
properties.text:
A directory store keeps two things: the snapshot files, which hold the state at the last checkpoint, and the WAL folder (`wal/`, or `.cypherlite/wal/` in a markdown store), which holds every commit since. The WAL is the only copy of those recent commits until the next checkpoint: every 300 seconds by default, after 64 MiB of WAL or 10,000 commits, and when the store closes.

That has two consequences for a file copy:

- A file copy is consistent only when no commit is in progress, and `cp` cannot tell. `relate clone` reads only complete commits.
- A copy without its WAL folder holds the state at the last checkpoint. Commits made since are missing from it, and a read-only open of it fails.

When no process has the store open, a copy of the whole folder is a complete backup. The copy holds the snapshot files and the WAL folder:

```bash verify
cp -R ./team ./backups/team-folder-copy
ls ./backups/team-folder-copy
```

```text
manifest.json
nodes
relationships
wal
```

The CLI checkpoints every time a writable run exits, so a store last written from the CLI has its state in the snapshot. A long-running process, such as an application using a client or `relate serve`, keeps recent commits in the WAL between checkpoints. [Recover from a crash](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/crash-and-recovery/) explains what the WAL gives back after a crash.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination already exists`** (exit code 1). `relate clone` never overwrites. Cloning onto an existing backup fails:

  ```bash verify
  relate clone ./team ./backups/team-2026-11-07.rl
  ```

  ```text
  Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination already exists
  ```

  Use a new destination name, such as one with the date and hour in it.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination parent does not exist: <path>`** (exit code 1). The source is a directory store and the destination's folder does not exist. Create it first (`mkdir -p`); a `.rl` source creates the folders itself.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage locked: <path>`** (exit code 1). The source is a `.rl` file and a process holds it. Back it up when that process exits, or keep the store as a directory store so it can be cloned while in use ([Choose a store layout](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/choose-a-store-layout/)).

- **`storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`** (exit code 1). Nothing at that directory path is a store. Check the path.

- **`storage error: database not found: <path>`** (exit code 1). A `--read-only` open of a `.rl` path where no file exists. Check the backup's path.

- **`storage error: read-only open requires an existing WAL at <path>`** (exit code 1). A copied directory store is missing its WAL folder, named in the message. Copy the whole folder again, or take the backup with `relate clone`.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: clone source must be a native directory or .rl bundle path`** (exit code 1). The source was `:memory:`. An in-memory store has nothing on disk to back up; write the data into a directory store or a `.rl` file to keep it.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A store to back up. The commands on this page use a directory store named `team`, created from a small seed graph:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team --mode envelope < team.cypher
```

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/): what a directory store and a `.rl` file hold.
- [Choose a store layout](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/choose-a-store-layout/): which layout can be backed up while in use.
- [Recover from a crash](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/crash-and-recovery/): what the WAL restores on its own.
- [Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/): back up before a newer release migrates the store.

properties.heading: Restore from a backup
properties.text:
Stop every process that has the store open. Move the damaged store aside rather than deleting it, then clone the backup to the store's path:

```bash verify
mv ./team ./team-damaged
relate clone ./backups/team-2026-11-07.rl ./team
```

`relate clone` writes either layout from either layout, so a `.rl` backup restores into a directory store, as `./team` does, or into a `.rl` file. For a `.rl` store, copying the backup file into place works too. Start the application again once the restored store opens.

properties.heading: Schedule backups
properties.text:
Run `relate clone` from a scheduler with a dated destination, keep several generations, and open one now and then. A crontab entry (`crontab -e`) for an hourly clone of a directory store, with `%` escaped because cron treats it as a newline:

```text
0 * * * * relate clone <store> <backup-dir>/team-$(date +\%Y\%m\%d-\%H).rl
```

Take a backup before a newer relate release opens the store writable as well: that open migrates the store forward, and older releases can't open it afterward. [Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/) covers that.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The restored store opens and holds the graph:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING"],"columns":["name"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Ada"},{"name":"Grace"},{"name":"Noor"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.549375,"execute_ms":0.380625,"lex_parse_ms":0.030459,"lower_ms":0.040791,"parse_ms":0.10675000000000001,"plan_ms":0.053209,"result_generation_ms":0.000209,"rewrite_ms":0.007958000000000002},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Choose a store layout
properties.text: This guide shows you how to choose where a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) lives and how it is written to disk. The path you pass to `--database` picks the layout: `:memory:` keeps the graph in the process, a path ending in `.rl` is one file, and any other path is a directory. Use `:memory:` for throwaway work, a `.rl` file for a store you copy or hand to someone, and a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store) when a second process reads beside the writer or you want a text snapshot you can diff.

properties.heading: Compare the layouts
properties.text:
Every layout runs the same engine: the whole graph lives in memory while the store is open, and every commit goes to the store's write-ahead log ([WAL](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal)) first. The layouts differ in what sits on disk.

|                          | In memory                         | `.rl` file                                                                                | Directory store                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--database` value       | `:memory:` (the default)          | a path ending in `.rl`                                                                    | any other path                                                                                  |
| Survives the process     | No                                | Yes                                                                                       | Yes                                                                                             |
| On disk                  | Nothing                           | One file                                                                                  | A folder: snapshot files and a WAL folder                                                       |
| A reader beside a writer | Not possible: one process owns it | No: a `--read-only` open is refused while a writer holds the file                         | Yes, with `--read-only`                                                                         |
| Size on disk             | None                              | Grows to the most space it has needed and reuses it; `relate clone` writes a compact copy | The snapshot plus the WAL since the last checkpoint                                             |
| Diffable                 | No                                | No                                                                                        | With the JSON [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec): `graph.json` is text |
| Startup                  | Starts empty                      | Loads the whole graph, then replays the WAL                                               | Loads the whole graph, then replays the WAL                                                     |

Startup grows with the size of the graph in every durable layout, because relate loads all of it into memory before the first statement runs. The [storage formats reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/) has the file layout of each and measured sizes.

properties.heading: Create a directory store
properties.text:
Any path that does not end in `.rl` becomes a directory store:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team --mode envelope < team.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.223083,"execute_ms":0.926084,"lex_parse_ms":0.015042,"lower_ms":0.021459,"parse_ms":0.28016599999999997,"plan_ms":0.010917000000000001,"result_generation_ms":0.000209,"rewrite_ms":0.0005},"truncated":false}
```

The folder holds the snapshot (`manifest.json` and the Parquet files under `nodes/` and `relationships/`) and the WAL:

```bash verify
ls team
```

```text
manifest.json
nodes
relationships
wal
```

Choose a directory store when another process needs to read while one writes: a `--read-only` open of a directory works beside its writer, and a `.rl` file refuses it. [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/) covers that setup.

properties.heading: Create a single-file store
properties.text:
The rest of this guide uses one small graph. Save its seed statement as `team.cypher`:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
```

Run it into a path that ends in `.rl`. relate creates the file on the first open:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --mode envelope < team.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":2.00025,"execute_ms":1.69775,"lex_parse_ms":0.01425,"lower_ms":0.02775,"parse_ms":0.283083,"plan_ms":0.013583,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.000583},"truncated":false}
```

`relate info` reads a store's metadata without opening it:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team.rl
```

```text
layout: .rl bundle
superblock version: 1
codec: parquet
format version: 5
checkpoint LSN: 1
commit timestamp: 1
total bytes: 36864
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
relationships (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
indexes: 0
constraints: 0
```

What sits inside `team.rl`, and what a commit and a checkpoint change there.

**One `.rl` file.** A single-file store keeps in one file the same tree a directory store spreads over a folder, WAL included. Its parts, in logical order rather than by byte position:

| Part            | Holds                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Superblock      | The container's version marker: magic `MDBCLB01`, version `1` (`relate info` prints `superblock version: 1`)                                              |
| Snapshot        | `manifest.json` and the codec's files (with the default `parquet` codec, the files under `nodes/` and `relationships/`): the state at the last checkpoint |
| WAL             | `wal/NNNNNNNN.log` segments: every commit since the last checkpoint                                                                                       |
| Space it reuses | The most space the snapshot and WAL have needed at once; later writes reuse what they no longer hold, and the file does not shrink                        |

A commit appends its record to the open segment inside the file. A checkpoint writes the new snapshot files inside it, publishes them with `manifest.json` last, and deletes the segments the snapshot covers. A writer holds the file itself, with no lock files beside it, so a `--read-only` open is refused while a writer has it, and `--wal-dir` is refused for a `.rl` path. `relate clone` writes a compact copy that holds only the current state.

Live: Commit, Checkpoint and Crash step through what relate does with the WAL, the in-memory graph and the snapshot (inside one `.rl` file in the file view), and a mode switch with a crash slider shades what `full`, `everysecond` and `snapshot` can lose; under reduced motion each step waits for Next. It is a diagram of documented behaviour: no engine runs.

![The parts of one .rl file, as relate documents it](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/choose-a-store-layout/element-rl-file-light.svg)

Choose a `.rl` file when the store travels: one file to copy, attach, or check in. To read it into memory without holding the file, pass it to `--load`; the in-memory copy is read-only:

```bash verify
relate --load ./team.rl --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.363917,"execute_ms":0.18412499999999998,"lex_parse_ms":0.03225,"lower_ms":0.043709,"parse_ms":0.11108299999999999,"plan_ms":0.060209,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.00825},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is json, requested parquet`** (exit code 1). `--snapshot-format` named a codec other than the one the directory was created with. Asking for Parquet on the JSON store fails:

  ```bash verify
  relate --database ./team-json --snapshot-format parquet --read-only --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
  ```

  ```text
  Failed to open Relate: storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is json, requested parquet
  {"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"storage","message":"storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is json, requested parquet","retryable":false}}
  ```

  Drop the flag, or make a copy in another codec with `relate clone --to-snapshot-format <codec> <source> <dest>`.

- **`storage locked: <path>`** (exit code 5). Another process holds the store. A `.rl` file can't be opened at all while a writer holds it, even `--read-only`. If a reader has to run beside the writer, move to a directory store with `relate clone`. The [locked error](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked) has the details.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination already exists`** (exit code 1). `relate clone` never overwrites. Pick a new destination path.

properties.heading: Open a store from Python or Node.js
properties.text:
The clients take the same three spellings: `":memory:"`, a directory path, or a path ending in `.rl`. Each opens writable by default and creates a missing store. In Python, `relate.connect(path)` opens one, as in the [Python tutorial](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/python/), and `read_only=True` opens it read-only. This program writes the graph into each layout, then opens the `.rl` file [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only):

```python run name=open-layouts title="layouts.py"
import relate

seed = """
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
"""

for path in [":memory:", "./team", "./team.rl"]:
    conn = relate.connect(path)
    conn.execute(seed)
    people = conn.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people").fetchone()["people"]
    print(f"{path}: {people} people")
    conn.close()

reader = relate.connect("./team.rl", read_only=True)
rows = reader.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name").fetchall()
print("read-only:", [row["name"] for row in rows])
reader.close()
```

```text
:memory:: 3 people
./team: 3 people
./team.rl: 3 people
read-only: ['Ada', 'Grace', 'Noor']
```

In Node.js, `Database.open` takes the same paths, and `{ readOnly: true }` opens a store read-only. The Node.js handles in this program stay open until it exits, so the read-only open goes to the directory store, which allows a reader beside its writer:

```js run name=open-layouts-js title="layouts.cjs"
const { Database } = require("@relate/relate");

const seed = `
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)`;

for (const path of [":memory:", "./team", "./team.rl"]) {
  const db = Database.open(path);
  const conn = db.connect();
  conn.query(seed);
  const people = conn.query("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people").rows[0].people;
  console.log(`${path}: ${people} people`);
}

const reader = Database.open("./team", { readOnly: true }).connect();
const names = reader.query("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name").rows;
console.log("read-only:", names.map((row) => row.name));
```

```text
:memory:: 3 people
./team: 3 people
./team.rl: 3 people
read-only: [ 'Ada', 'Grace', 'Noor' ]
```

properties.heading: Pick a codec for a directory store
properties.text:
A codec is the encoding a checkpoint writes the snapshot in. The default is Parquet: compact, binary columnar files. JSON writes the whole graph as one readable `graph.json`, which a code review can diff. Pass `--snapshot-format json` when you create the store:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team-json --snapshot-format json --mode envelope < team.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.260125,"execute_ms":0.930708,"lex_parse_ms":0.013375,"lower_ms":0.061,"parse_ms":0.313042,"plan_ms":0.010166000000000001,"result_generation_ms":0.000042,"rewrite_ms":0.001084},"truncated":false}
```

```bash verify
ls team-json
```

```text
graph.json
manifest.json
wal
```

The codec is fixed when the store is created and recorded in `manifest.json`, so later opens need no flag:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-json --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING"],"columns":["name"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Ada"},{"name":"Grace"},{"name":"Noor"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.536292,"execute_ms":0.376833,"lex_parse_ms":0.029833000000000002,"lower_ms":0.038042,"parse_ms":0.10087499999999999,"plan_ms":0.050334000000000004,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.008},"truncated":false}
```

`RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT=json` makes the same choice for a new store, including from the clients. A third codec, `markdown`, writes one note per node for a folder people edit by hand; the [formats reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/) describes it.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- For the client section: the Python client (`relate-db`) or the Node.js client (`@relate/relate`).

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:

- [Back up and restore a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/): `relate clone` as the backup command.
- [Storage and durability](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/storage-and-durability/): the write path every layout shares.
- [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/): a writer and readers on one directory store.

properties.heading: Start in memory
properties.text:
With no `--database`, a statement runs against an in-memory store that is gone when the process exits:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["ok"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"ok":1}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.356541,"execute_ms":0.20325000000000001,"lex_parse_ms":0.020542,"lower_ms":0.02775,"parse_ms":0.09895799999999999,"plan_ms":0.042292,"result_generation_ms":0.000209,"rewrite_ms":0.007292},"truncated":false}
```

Use it for tests, scratch statements and anything you rebuild from a script.

properties.heading: Switch layouts later
properties.text:
`relate clone` copies a store into a new store of either layout, and `--to-snapshot-format` changes the codec on the way. The source is opened read-only and never written; the destination must not exist yet. Turn the `.rl` file into a directory store:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team.rl ./team-copy
```

Then make a JSON copy of that:

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team-copy ./team-copy-json
```

Switch when the job changes:

| If                                          | Move to                               |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| A second process must read while one writes | A directory store                     |
| The store is shipped, attached, or archived | A `.rl` file                          |
| Reviewers diff the graph in pull requests   | A directory store with the JSON codec |
| The `.rl` file is larger than its content   | A fresh `.rl` from `relate clone`     |

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
`relate info` names the layout and codec of a store. The JSON copy reports both on its first two lines:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team-copy-json | head -n 2
```

```text
layout: native directory
codec: json
```

properties.heading: Clone and convert a store
properties.text: This guide shows you how to copy a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) into a new one, change its layout or its codec on the way, and check that the copy holds the same graph. The command is `relate clone <source> <dest>`: the destination's path picks the layout (a path ending in `.rl` is one file, any other path a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store)), and `--to-snapshot-format parquet|json|markdown` picks the codec. The source is opened read-only and never written.

properties.heading: Change the codec
properties.text:
Without `--to-snapshot-format`, the destination keeps the source's codec. With it, the destination's first checkpoint is written in the codec it names. Write a `json` copy and a `markdown` copy of the directory store:

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team ./team-json
relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown ./team ./team-md
```

`relate info` reads a store's layout and codec without opening it:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team-md | head -n 2
```

```text
layout: native directory
codec: markdown
```

The `json` copy holds the graph in one `graph.json`. The `markdown` copy holds one note per node, in a folder per label, with an index note per folder, a root `index.md` and a `log.md`:

```bash verify
ls team-json team-md team-md/Person
```

```text
team-json:
graph.json
manifest.json
wal

team-md:
Person
Project
index.md
log.md

team-md/Person:
Ada.md
Grace.md
Noor.md
index.md
```

The `markdown` codec names each note after a key property of its label, `name` here, so every node of a label needs that property, and its value must be unique within the label. `--markdown-body-properties` chooses the properties written as each note's body; [Open a store as an Obsidian vault](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/obsidian-vault/) covers both.

properties.heading: Change the layout
properties.text:
Clone the `.rl` file into a directory, then the directory back into a second `.rl` file. `relate clone` prints nothing on success:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team.rl ./team
relate clone ./team ./team-copy.rl
```

The destination must not exist yet; `relate clone` never overwrites. It reads the state committed when it opens the source and does not follow later commits. A directory source can be cloned while another process writes to it; a [.rl file](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#rl) only while no process holds it open for writing.

properties.heading: Check that the copy holds the same graph
properties.text:
Compare what a statement returns from the source and from the copy. This check writes every node's labels and properties and every relationship to a file, sorted, once for the source and once for a store that went from `.rl` to `markdown` and back to a `parquet` `.rl` file. The `jsonl` mode ends each statement with a line of its timings, which change on every run, so `grep -v '"timings"'` drops those lines before the comparison:

```bash verify
cat > graph-check.cypher <<'EOF'
MATCH (n) RETURN labels(n) AS labels, properties(n) AS props ORDER BY n.name;
MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) RETURN a.name AS from, type(r) AS type, properties(r) AS props, b.name AS to ORDER BY from, type, to;
EOF
relate clone --to-snapshot-format parquet ./team-md ./team-roundtrip.rl
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode jsonl < graph-check.cypher | grep -v '"timings"' > before.jsonl
relate query --database ./team-roundtrip.rl --read-only --mode jsonl < graph-check.cypher | grep -v '"timings"' > after.jsonl
cmp before.jsonl after.jsonl && echo "same graph: $(wc -l < after.jsonl | tr -d ' ') rows"
```

```text
same graph: 10 rows
```

Five nodes and five relationships come back identical. The way back names its codec: in relate 1.0.1, a `.rl` destination refuses the body-property configuration a `markdown` store records, so `relate clone ./team-md ./team-roundtrip.rl` without `--to-snapshot-format`, or with `--to-snapshot-format markdown`, exits 1 with `Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored`. A `markdown` store clones into a `.rl` file with `--to-snapshot-format parquet` or `json`, and into a directory store with any codec. Order the rows by a property your graph has on every node. Values without a YAML form keep their type in a `markdown` note: a date or a point is written as a small map tagged `__type` and reads back as a date or a point. One difference to expect from a `markdown` round trip: a node with two or more labels can return them from `labels(n)` in another order, so sort them before comparing such a graph.

properties.heading: Decide when to convert
properties.text:
A store's layout and [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec) are fixed when it is created: `--snapshot-format` applies only to an empty directory. To change either, write a new store with [relate clone](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#clone):

| If                                                                | Convert to                                  | Command                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A second process must read while one writes, or follow the writer | A directory store                           | `relate clone ./team.rl ./team`                               |
| The store is attached, shipped, or archived as one file           | A `.rl` file                                | `relate clone ./team ./team.rl`                               |
| Reviewers diff the graph in pull requests                         | A directory store with the `json` codec     | `relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team ./team-json`   |
| People read and edit the graph as notes                           | A directory store with the `markdown` codec | `relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown ./team ./team-md` |
| A `.rl` file is far larger than what it holds                     | A fresh `.rl` file                          | `relate clone ./team.rl ./team-compact.rl`                    |

The [storage formats reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/) has the files each layout and codec writes.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Error: unexpected argument to clone: --snapshot-format`** (exit code 2). The flag on `relate clone` is `--to-snapshot-format`:

  ```bash verify
  relate clone --snapshot-format json ./team ./team-json2
  ```

  ```text
  Error: unexpected argument to clone: --snapshot-format
  Did you mean '--to-snapshot-format'?
  Usage: relate clone [--wal-dir DIR] [--to-snapshot-format F] [--markdown-body-properties LIST] SOURCE DEST
  Run 'relate clone --help' for more information.
  ```

  A `--snapshot-format` placed before the verb, as in `relate --snapshot-format json clone …`, does not change the destination's codec: the copy keeps the source's. Put `--to-snapshot-format` after `clone`.

- **`Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored`** (exit code 1). The destination is a `.rl` path and the source is a `markdown` store, or the command passes `--markdown-body-properties`. In relate 1.0.1 a `.rl` destination refuses that configuration, even with `--to-snapshot-format markdown`. Pass `--to-snapshot-format parquet` or `json` for a `.rl` copy of a vault, or clone it into a directory store.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination already exists`** (exit code 1). `relate clone` never overwrites. Pick a new destination path.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: markdown vault: node <id> of label <Label> has no '<property>' property; the markdown vault requires a non-null unique '<property>' on :<Label>`** (exit code 1). A `markdown` destination names each note after a key property, and a node of that label lacks it. Set the property on every node of the label first. A failed clone removes the destination it created.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage error: markdown vault: two nodes of label <Label> share the key value '<value>'; the vault filename would collide`** (exit code 1). Two nodes of one label have the same key value. Make the values unique, or keep the store in `parquet` or `json`.

- **`Error: invalid --to-snapshot-format: storage error: unknown snapshot codec '<value>' (expected parquet, json, markdown or rkyv)`** (exit code 2). The codec name is misspelled.

- **`Failed to clone database: storage locked: <path>`** (exit code 1). The source is a `.rl` file that a process holds open for writing. Clone it when that process exits ([storage locked](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-clone-locked)).

properties.heading: Measure the sizes
properties.text:
A `.rl` file grows to the most space it has needed and reuses it; it does not shrink when data is deleted. `relate clone` writes only the current state. To see it, add 20,000 draft nodes to `team.rl`, delete them again, and clone it:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team.rl | grep 'total bytes'
relate --database ./team.rl --mode envelope "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS i CREATE (:Draft {id: i, text: 'draft note ' + toString(i)})"
relate --database ./team.rl --mode envelope "MATCH (d:Draft) DELETE d"
relate clone ./team.rl ./team-compact.rl
```

```text
total bytes: 36864
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":66.759917,"execute_ms":66.566792,"lex_parse_ms":0.006292,"lower_ms":0.007292,"parse_ms":0.182708,"plan_ms":0.005332999999999999,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.000375},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":21.065709,"execute_ms":20.903374999999997,"lex_parse_ms":0.002333,"lower_ms":0.0029579999999999997,"parse_ms":0.154167,"plan_ms":0.003583,"result_generation_ms":0.000417,"rewrite_ms":0.00020800000000000001},"truncated":false}
```

The method: `relate info` prints each store's size on disk as `total bytes`, read without opening the store. The loop prints it for the bloated file, its clone, and the three copies made in [Change the codec](#change-the-codec) and [Change the layout](#change-the-layout):

```bash verify
for store in team.rl team-compact.rl team team-json team-md; do printf '%s: ' "$store"; relate info --database "./$store" | grep 'total bytes'; done
```

```text
team.rl: total bytes: 3100672
team-compact.rl: total bytes: 32768
team: total bytes: 4032
team-json: total bytes: 1385
team-md: total bytes: 2926
```

| Store                                   | Measured        | What it shows                                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `team.rl` before the drafts             | 36,864 bytes    | A new `.rl` file for 5 nodes and 5 relationships                             |
| `team.rl` after the drafts were deleted | 3,203,072 bytes | The file kept the space the 20,000 drafts needed                             |
| `team-compact.rl`                       | 32,768 bytes    | The clone holds only the current state                                       |
| `team` (`parquet` directory)            | 3,556 bytes     | Columnar files plus a manifest                                               |
| `team-json`                             | 1,385 bytes     | One JSON file plus a manifest; on this graph the smallest                    |
| `team-md`                               | 2,926 bytes     | One note per node, an index per label, and the `log.md` and `index.md` notes |

These numbers are for this 5-node graph. At 100,000 nodes the `json` codec is about 3.4 times the size of `parquet` ([measured in the formats reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#size-on-disk)), so the sizes on a small graph don't predict the order on a large one.

properties.text:

- A store to copy. The commands on this page start from the shared example graph in a single-file store, `team.rl`:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl < team.cypher
```
