- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/): the files each layout and codec writes, and sizes at 100,000 nodes.
- [Choose a store layout](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/choose-a-store-layout/): which layout and codec fit a job.
- [Back up and restore a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/): `relate clone` as the backup command.
- [Single-file graph](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#single-file-graph) in the capability catalog.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The converted store opens and answers statements. The `markdown` copy returns who works on what:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-md --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) RETURN p.name AS name, proj.name AS project ORDER BY name, project"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING"],"columns":["name","project"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Ada","project":"relate"},{"name":"Grace","project":"opencypher-tck"},{"name":"Grace","project":"relate"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.55875,"execute_ms":0.382,"lex_parse_ms":0.033417,"lower_ms":0.039709,"parse_ms":0.1085,"plan_ms":0.058542000000000004,"result_generation_ms":0.000375,"rewrite_ms":0.008291999999999999},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Open a store as an Obsidian vault
properties.text: This guide shows you how to open a folder of markdown notes, such as an Obsidian vault, as a relate store, query and write it with Cypher, and keep editing the same files by hand. With the `markdown` [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec), the notes are the store: each note is a [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node), each top-level folder a [label](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label), and each `[[wikilink]]` under a frontmatter key a relationship. The engine keeps its own state in a hidden `.cypherlite/` folder and two hidden lock files, `.cypherlite.lock` and `.cypherlite.writer`, at the vault root.

properties.heading: Edit notes by hand
properties.text:
Edit the notes in Obsidian or any editor while no relate process has the vault open; the next open reads them. Noor's note gains a second project and a body:

```bash verify
cat > team-vault/Person/Noor.md <<'EOF'
---
type: Person
name: Noor
role: maintainer
MAINTAINS:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
  - "[[Project/opencypher-tck]]"
---

Reviews every release.
EOF
relate --database ./team-vault --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Noor'})-[:MAINTAINS]->(x) RETURN p.body AS body, collect(x.name) AS maintains"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","LIST"],"columns":["body","maintains"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"body":"Reviews every release.","maintains":["opencypher-tck","relate"]}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.481791,"execute_ms":0.28125,"lex_parse_ms":0.033958,"lower_ms":0.049208,"parse_ms":0.125375,"plan_ms":0.065667,"result_generation_ms":0.000334,"rewrite_ms":0.00825},"truncated":false}
```

While a process holds the vault open, it is the one writer: an edit made to the files then is refused at its next checkpoint ([If it goes wrong](#if-it-goes-wrong)).

properties.heading: How notes map to the graph
properties.text:
| In the vault                                                                     | In the graph                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A top-level folder, such as `Person/`                                            | A label                                                                                                                          |
| A note in it, such as `Person/Ada.md`                                            | A node with that label; the filename is its key, stored as `name`                                                                |
| A note at the vault root                                                         | A node with the label `Vault`                                                                                                    |
| A frontmatter key holding a scalar or a list of values, such as `role: engineer` | A [property](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property)                                                              |
| A frontmatter key holding `[[Folder/note]]` links, such as `WORKS_ON:`           | Relationships of that [type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type), from this note to each linked note |
| A link to a missing note                                                         | A node with only its key, written as a new note at the next checkpoint                                                           |
| The note's text after the frontmatter                                            | The `body` property, or the properties `--markdown-body-properties` names                                                        |

A link with properties takes a map form, `- since: 2024` with `target: "[[Project/relate]]"`; its key counts as a relationship type once some note uses it with a bare link.

> **Warning: The first open rewrites the notes**
>
> The first writable open adds `type` and `name` to every note's frontmatter, sorts its keys, writes a note for every link that points nowhere, and adds an `index.md` per folder, a root `index.md` and a `log.md`. Commit the vault to git, or copy it, before the first open, so the change is a diff you can read and undo.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage error: ambiguous legacy storage role at <path>; explicit offline migration required`** (exit code 1). A folder of notes was opened without `--snapshot-format markdown`. Nothing in it changed; open it again with the flag.
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`** (exit code 1). The first open was `--read-only`. Open the vault once without `--read-only`, after committing it to git.
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage error: markdown vault: <note>: '<KEY>' holds map-form link entries but no file declares the relationship type with a bare wikilink; declare it or use a bare link`** (exit code 1). A key holds links with properties and no note declares that relationship type with a plain `- "[[Folder/note]]"` link. Add a bare link under that key in one note.
- **`Error: final checkpoint failed: storage error: markdown vault: node <id> of label <Label> has no 'name' property; the markdown vault requires a non-null unique 'name' on :<Label>`** (exit code 1). A statement created a node without its key. The write committed, and every writable open fails its checkpoint the same way until the key is set:

  ```bash verify
  relate --database ./team-vault --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {role: 'reviewer'})"
  echo "exit=$?"
  ```

  ```text
  {"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":2.6516669999999998,"execute_ms":2.385125,"lex_parse_ms":0.008209000000000001,"lower_ms":0.006791,"parse_ms":0.253625,"plan_ms":0.002333,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.000542},"truncated":false}
  Error: final checkpoint failed: storage error: markdown vault: node 7 of label Person has no 'name' property; the markdown vault requires a non-null unique 'name' on :Person
  exit=1
  ```

  Give the node its key, and the next checkpoint writes its note:

  ```bash verify
  relate --database ./team-vault --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name IS NULL SET p.name = 'Jun'"
  ls team-vault/Person
  ```

  ```text
  {"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":12.825,"execute_ms":12.275584,"lex_parse_ms":0.21241700000000002,"lower_ms":0.013875,"parse_ms":0.522375,"plan_ms":0.017249999999999998,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.001167},"truncated":false}
  Ada.md
  Grace.md
  Ines.md
  Jun.md
  Noor.md
  index.md
  ```

  Two nodes of one label with the same key fail the same way, with `two nodes of label <Label> share the key value '<value>'; the vault filename would collide`; rename or delete one.
- **`Error: final checkpoint failed: storage error: markdown vault: the vault changed on disk while the database was open; close the database, let your edits in, and reopen (concurrent writers are not merged)`** (exit code 1). A note was edited while a relate process held the vault. If that process had written, the next open fails with `storage error: markdown vault: the markdown vault changed on disk while uncheckpointed writes were pending; reopen without the edits or recover from a checkpointed state`. Put the edited notes back as they were (`git checkout` on those files), open the vault so relate applies its pending writes, then make the edit again with no relate process running.

properties.heading: Open the vault
properties.text:
Name the codec on the first open with `--snapshot-format markdown`; relate never takes a folder of notes for a store on its own. The first open must be writable, because it creates the `.cypherlite/` folder:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-vault --snapshot-format markdown --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN labels(n)[0] AS label, n.name AS name ORDER BY label, name"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING"],"columns":["label","name"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"label":"Person","name":"Ada"},{"label":"Person","name":"Grace"},{"label":"Person","name":"Noor"},{"label":"Project","name":"opencypher-tck"},{"label":"Project","name":"relate"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.545708,"execute_ms":0.362875,"lex_parse_ms":0.005791999999999999,"lower_ms":0.045417,"parse_ms":0.130916,"plan_ms":0.045958000000000006,"result_generation_ms":0.000166,"rewrite_ms":0.007416},"truncated":false}
```

`opencypher-tck` is a node because Grace's note links it. The codec is now recorded in `.cypherlite/manifest.json`, so later opens need no flag.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A folder of markdown notes with YAML frontmatter. This guide makes a small one from the shared example graph: three people and the project they work on, one note each, with relationships as wikilinks:

```bash verify
mkdir -p team-vault/Person team-vault/Project
cat > team-vault/Person/Ada.md <<'EOF'
---
role: engineer
WORKS_ON:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
KNOWS:
  - "[[Person/Grace]]"
---

Writes the planner.
EOF
cat > team-vault/Person/Grace.md <<'EOF'
---
role: engineer
WORKS_ON:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
  - "[[Project/opencypher-tck]]"
---

Keeps the conformance tests green.
EOF
cat > team-vault/Person/Noor.md <<'EOF'
---
role: maintainer
MAINTAINS:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
---
EOF
cat > team-vault/Project/relate.md <<'EOF'
---
language: Rust
---

An embedded graph database.
EOF
```

properties.heading: Put more properties in the note body
properties.text:
By default a note's body is the `body` property. `--markdown-body-properties` takes a list: the first property is the text right after the frontmatter, and each further one becomes a `## <property>` section. Editing the text under a section heading changes that property. `Label=list` sets a list for one label, and `;` separates entries. Add a `notes` section:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-vault --markdown-body-properties "body,notes" --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'}) SET p.notes = 'Prefers small commits.'"
cat team-vault/Person/Ada.md
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.363583,"execute_ms":1.1715,"lex_parse_ms":0.0047090000000000005,"lower_ms":0.004125,"parse_ms":0.18016700000000002,"plan_ms":0.006625,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.000334},"truncated":false}
---
type: Person
name: Ada
role: engineer
KNOWS:
  - "[[Person/Grace]]"
WORKS_ON:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
---

Writes the planner.

## notes

Prefers small commits.
```

The list is recorded in `.cypherlite/manifest.json`, so later opens use it without the flag; other properties stay in the frontmatter. After a change to the list, the text of a section no longer listed becomes part of the first property's value, and none is lost.

properties.heading: Query and write the vault
properties.text:
The vault answers Cypher like any store. Who works on what:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-vault --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person)-[r]->(x) RETURN p.name AS person, type(r) AS rel, x.name AS target ORDER BY person, rel, target"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING","STRING"],"columns":["person","rel","target"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"person":"Ada","rel":"KNOWS","target":"Grace"},{"person":"Ada","rel":"WORKS_ON","target":"relate"},{"person":"Grace","rel":"WORKS_ON","target":"opencypher-tck"},{"person":"Grace","rel":"WORKS_ON","target":"relate"},{"person":"Noor","rel":"MAINTAINS","target":"relate"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.451625,"execute_ms":0.27304199999999995,"lex_parse_ms":0.03275,"lower_ms":0.045583,"parse_ms":0.113375,"plan_ms":0.057374999999999995,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.0085},"truncated":false}
```

A write becomes a note at the checkpoint. This statement adds Ines, with a body, working on `relate`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-vault --mode envelope "MATCH (r:Project {name: 'relate'}) CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ines', role: 'engineer', body: 'Joined to work on the planner.'})-[:WORKS_ON]->(r)"
cat team-vault/Person/Ines.md
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.515666,"execute_ms":1.318625,"lex_parse_ms":0.006333,"lower_ms":0.006791,"parse_ms":0.186708,"plan_ms":0.0052499999999999995,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.00033299999999999996},"truncated":false}
---
type: Person
name: Ines
role: engineer
WORKS_ON:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
---

Joined to work on the planner.
```

Every node of a label needs its key, `name` here, unique within the label: it is the note's filename. Deleting a node deletes its note.

properties.heading: Read the file layout
properties.text:
The checkpoint at exit wrote the stub note, an index note per folder, and the two root notes. `ls` leaves out the hidden `.cypherlite/` folder and lock files:

```bash verify
ls team-vault team-vault/Person team-vault/Project
```

```text
team-vault:
Person
Project
index.md
log.md

team-vault/Person:
Ada.md
Grace.md
Noor.md
index.md

team-vault/Project:
index.md
opencypher-tck.md
relate.md
```

Ada's note now carries its label and key in the frontmatter, with the relationship keys after the properties:

```bash verify
cat team-vault/Person/Ada.md
```

```text
---
type: Person
name: Ada
role: engineer
KNOWS:
  - "[[Person/Grace]]"
WORKS_ON:
  - "[[Project/relate]]"
---

Writes the planner.
```

`index.md` and `log.md` are views relate rewrites at every checkpoint, so edits to them are lost. Other dot folders, such as Obsidian's `.obsidian/`, are left alone.

properties.heading: Related
properties.text:
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#codecs): the `markdown` codec's files beside `parquet` and `json`.
- [`--markdown-body-properties`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#markdown-body-properties) in the flags reference.
- [Clone and convert a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/clone-and-convert/): copy a vault into another codec and back.
- [Keep a diffable memory in the repo](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/diffable-memory/): notes an agent writes, reviewed as diffs.
- [Diffable memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#diffable-memory) in the capability catalog.

properties.heading: Round-trip through another codec
properties.text:
`relate clone` copies the vault into another layout and codec, and back. A `.rl` copy of a vault names its codec, `parquet` or `json`: in relate 1.0.1 a `.rl` destination refuses the body list a vault records. A `parquet` copy does not record the body list, so pass it again when cloning back to markdown, and the notes come back the same:

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format parquet ./team-vault ./team.rl
relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown --markdown-body-properties "body,notes" ./team.rl ./team-vault-copy
diff -r team-vault/Person team-vault-copy/Person && diff -r team-vault/Project team-vault-copy/Project && echo "same notes"
```

```text
same notes
```

Without the flag, the copy keeps the same values but puts `notes` in the frontmatter. [Clone and convert a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/clone-and-convert/) covers cloning in general.

properties.heading: Verify
properties.text:
The vault opens without the flag and holds the four people and two projects:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team-vault --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (n) RETURN labels(n)[0] AS label, count(*) AS notes ORDER BY label"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER"],"columns":["label","notes"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"label":"Person","notes":4},{"label":"Project","notes":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.622666,"execute_ms":0.442458,"lex_parse_ms":0.005958000000000001,"lower_ms":0.046542,"parse_ms":0.128,"plan_ms":0.046459,"result_generation_ms":0.00029099999999999997,"rewrite_ms":0.006541},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Open a store read-only and follow a writer
properties.text: This guide shows you how to open a relate store so that nothing can change it, and how to keep a second process reading while a writer commits. `--read-only` opens a frozen view of the store as it was at open. `--read-only=live` opens a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store) read-only and follows the writer's commits as they land. Neither writes, checkpoints or migrates the store, and every write statement on either fails with exit code 6.

properties.heading: Choose a freshness
properties.text:
`--read-only` takes an optional freshness, attached with `=`:

| Flag                                           | What a statement sees                                                                                                                               | Works on                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--read-only` (same as `--read-only=snapshot`) | The store as it was when the process opened it; later commits stay invisible until the process opens the store again                                | A directory store, beside its writer; a `.rl` file, only while no writer holds it; `:memory:` |
| `--read-only=live`                             | The writer's commits as they reach the store's [write-ahead log](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal) (WAL), applied in the background | A directory store only                                                                        |

A [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) open takes no writer lock, so on a directory store it runs beside the one process that writes. A `.rl` file is one file its writer locks whole, so a read-only open of it fails with exit code 5 while a writer holds it ([Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/)).

properties.heading: Follow a writer's commits
properties.text:
`--read-only=live` turns the same reader into a follower. It opens like a frozen reader, then applies each complete commit that reaches the WAL. The same steps, with Jun as the new person:

```bash verify
# the follower opens team now and runs its statement after 2 seconds
{ sleep 2; echo "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people;"; } | relate query --database ./team --read-only=live --mode envelope &
sleep 1
relate --database ./team --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Jun', role: 'engineer'})"
wait
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":4.0413749999999995,"execute_ms":3.8890000000000002,"lex_parse_ms":0.003625,"lower_ms":0.007333,"parse_ms":0.14558400000000002,"plan_ms":0.001583,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.000167},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":5}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.474458,"execute_ms":0.292416,"lex_parse_ms":0.032208,"lower_ms":0.047625,"parse_ms":0.115041,"plan_ms":0.058,"result_generation_ms":0.000458,"rewrite_ms":0.008667},"truncated":false}
```

The follower counts 5: Ines from the step before and Jun, who committed after it opened. A [live read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#live-read-only) open has these rules:

- A statement reads one consistent view: one that is already running keeps the view it started with, and the next statement sees the commits applied since.
- When the writer's checkpoint recycles WAL the follower has not applied yet, the follower loads the current snapshot and the WAL that remains, then keeps following.
- The follower never writes, checkpoints or trims the WAL, and it does not hold back the writer's checkpoints.

Following pays off in a process that stays up and answers many statements, such as a server. `relate serve --database ./team --read-only=live --http <port>` answers HTTP statements from `team` while another process writes it; [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/#follow-the-writers-commits) walks through that setup.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  accTitle: A frozen reader and a live reader beside one writer
  accDescr {
    Both readers open the directory store and see the people it holds at that moment.
    The writer then commits another person to the write-ahead log.
    The frozen reader still sees only the people at open; the live reader applies the new commit from the log and sees it too.
  }
  Open["Store at open"] --> Frozen["Frozen reader, --read-only: the people at open"]
  Open --> Live["Live reader, --read-only=live: the people at open plus the new commit"]
  Writer["Writer"] -->|"commits another person"| WAL["WAL of the directory store"]
  WAL -->|"applies the new commit"| Live
```

Both readers open the directory store and see the people it holds at that moment. The writer then commits another person to the write-ahead log. The frozen reader still sees only the people at open; the live reader applies the new commit from the log and sees it too.

properties.heading: Follow only a directory store
properties.text:
Only a directory store has a WAL folder another process can tail. A `.rl` file keeps its WAL inside the one file, so `--read-only=live` refuses it, and `:memory:` has nothing to follow. Make a `.rl` copy and try:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team ./team.rl
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only=live --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases","retryable":false}}
exit=1
```

To follow a store that lives in a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store), copy it into a directory with `relate clone ./team.rl ./team-dir` and have the writer use the directory ([Clone and convert a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/clone-and-convert/)).

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.`, exit code 6.** A statement that writes ran on a read-only open. Send the write to the process that owns the store, or open without `--read-only` when the write is intended.
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`, exit code 1.** Nothing at that directory path is a store, and a read-only open never creates one. Check the path. For a missing `.rl` path the message is `storage error: database not found: <path>`.
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5, on a `.rl` store.** A writer holds the file, and a `.rl` file can't be read beside it. Wait for the writer to exit. To read beside a writer next time, move the store to a directory with `relate clone` once the writer has exited ([storage locked](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked)).
- **`Failed to open Relate: semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases`, exit code 1.** `--read-only=live` was given a `.rl` file or `:memory:`. Follow a directory store, or use `--read-only`.
- **`Error: --read-only takes its value attached: --read-only=live`, exit code 2.** The freshness was passed as a separate word. Write `--read-only=live`.

properties.heading: Open a store read-only
properties.text:
Add `--read-only` to any statement run. The store must exist:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING"],"columns":["name"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Ada"},{"name":"Grace"},{"name":"Noor"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.412167,"execute_ms":0.24537499999999998,"lex_parse_ms":0.030042000000000003,"lower_ms":0.039417,"parse_ms":0.104584,"plan_ms":0.053167,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.00925},"truncated":false}
```

A write on a read-only open fails before it changes anything. The first line is stderr, the second the error object on stdout:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ines', role: 'engineer'})"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.","retryable":false}}
exit=6
```

The error code is `validation_error` and `retryable` is `false`: the same statement fails the same way on every read-only open. The [write on a read-only store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-write-on-read-only) entry has the details. A read-only open also never checkpoints, so opening a backup or a store written by an older release read-only leaves its files as they were.

properties.heading: Open read-only from Python
properties.text:
The Python client takes `read_only=True` on `relate.connect()`; it opens a frozen view, like `--read-only`, and a write raises `relate.OperationalError` with the same message. This program writes from one connection and reads from a read-only one on the same directory store:

```python run name=python-reader title="reader.py"
import relate

writer = relate.connect("./team")
writer.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}), (:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'})")

reader = relate.connect("./team", read_only=True)
count = "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
print("reader at open:", reader.execute(count).fetchone()["people"])

writer.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'})")
print("writer after a commit:", writer.execute(count).fetchone()["people"])
print("reader after the commit:", reader.execute(count).fetchone()["people"])

try:
    reader.execute("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ines'})")
except relate.OperationalError as err:
    print(type(err).__name__, err.kind, err.retryable)

reader.close()
writer.close()
```

```text
reader at open: 2
writer after a commit: 3
reader after the commit: 2
OperationalError WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase False
```

The Node.js client opens a frozen view with `Database.open(path, { readOnly: true })`. Following a writer is a CLI open: `--read-only=live` on a statement run, `relate query` or `relate serve`.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A store that already exists: a read-only open never creates one. To follow along, create the shared example graph as a directory store, `team`:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team < team.cypher
```

properties.heading: Read beside a writer
properties.text:
A frozen reader keeps the view it opened with. Here a reader opens `team` and waits 2 seconds before it counts. In the meantime a second process adds Ines and exits:

```bash verify
# the reader opens team now and runs its statement after 2 seconds
{ sleep 2; echo "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people;"; } | relate query --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope &
sleep 1
relate --database ./team --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ines', role: 'engineer'})"
wait
```

The first line is the writer's empty result, the second the reader's count:

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.9636660000000001,"execute_ms":1.814541,"lex_parse_ms":0.002667,"lower_ms":0.003375,"parse_ms":0.142209,"plan_ms":0.0015,"result_generation_ms":0.000166,"rewrite_ms":0.00020800000000000001},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.702875,"execute_ms":0.509875,"lex_parse_ms":0.038458,"lower_ms":0.047875,"parse_ms":0.12504099999999999,"plan_ms":0.059458,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.009125},"truncated":false}
```

The reader counts 3 people although the store now holds 4: Ines committed after the reader opened. A one-shot run opens, reads and exits, so it sees the latest commit each time. A long-running reader opened with `--read-only` sees it only after it opens the store again.

properties.text:
A read-only open of the store shows every committed write, and the files are unchanged by it. After the steps on this page `team` holds 5 people:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"
```

properties.heading: Keep the schema as files
properties.text: This guide shows you how to read a store's schema from files, review a schema change in a pull request, and apply the same schema to a new store. Every checkpoint of a durable store writes its indexes and constraints as Cypher text into the [schema folder](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#schema-folder), `.cypherlite/schema/`, inside a directory store. The files are a copy for reading and diffing: the schema changes only through Cypher statements, and an edited file stops the store from opening.

properties.heading: Apply the schema to a new store
properties.text:
Each line of `schema.cypher` is a statement that ends with `;`, so the file runs as a script. Pipe it into a new, empty store to give that store the same indexes and constraints, then compare the two copies:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team-staging --mode envelope < team/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
cmp team/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher team-staging/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher && echo "same schema"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.1729170000000002,"execute_ms":1.0586659999999999,"lex_parse_ms":0.002959,"lower_ms":0.000833,"parse_ms":0.109833,"plan_ms":0.001,"result_generation_ms":0.00029099999999999997,"rewrite_ms":0.000166},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.855208,"execute_ms":0.804625,"lex_parse_ms":0.003167,"lower_ms":0.000833,"parse_ms":0.049459,"plan_ms":0.00075,"result_generation_ms":0.000041,"rewrite_ms":0.000167},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.8208329999999999,"execute_ms":0.79225,"lex_parse_ms":0.002208,"lower_ms":0.0007080000000000001,"parse_ms":0.027375,"plan_ms":0.0007080000000000001,"result_generation_ms":0.000041,"rewrite_ms":0.000084},"truncated":false}
same schema
```

Apply the schema before loading data, so a uniqueness constraint checks every row as it arrives. The statements in the file carry no `IF NOT EXISTS`, so running them against a store that already has the same index fails at the first one ([If it goes wrong](#if-it-goes-wrong)).

properties.heading: Diff the data too
properties.text:
The schema folder covers indexes and constraints. To review changes to nodes and relationships as well, keep the store in the `json` codec, whose checkpoint writes the whole graph to one `graph.json` beside the same schema folder:

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team ./team-json
ls -A team-json team-json/.cypherlite/schema
```

```text
team-json:
.cypherlite
.cypherlite.lock
.cypherlite.writer
graph.json
manifest.json
wal

team-json/.cypherlite/schema:
schema.cypher
```

`graph.json` is written as one line of JSON, so a line diff marks the whole file as changed; pass it through a JSON formatter before diffing to see which nodes and relationships changed. [Keep a diffable memory in the repo](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/diffable-memory/) applies this to an agent's memory, and the [formats reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#codecs) shows what `graph.json` holds.

properties.heading: Find the schema folder
properties.text:
The folder holds one file for a store without a schema, `schema.cypher`, and it is empty:

```bash verify
ls -A team/.cypherlite/schema
```

```text
schema.cypher
```

| File                               | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Present                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `schema.cypher`                    | One `CREATE INDEX` or `CREATE CONSTRAINT` statement per line, as the `createStatement` column of `SHOW INDEXES` and `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` renders it: indexes first, then constraints, each group in name order | Always; empty when the store has no index or constraint                                                                                                                        |
| `graph-type.cypher`                | The store's [graph type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#graph-type), as the body of its declaration, such as ``(:`Person` => {`name` :: STRING NOT NULL})``                                    | When the store has a graph type                                                                                                                                                |
| `ontology.json` or `ontology.yaml` | The [ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#ontology) document, byte for byte as it was set                                                                                                  | When an ontology is set; the `db.ontology.*` procedures are a preview feature (`RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology`, [Use an ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/ontology/)) |

A `markdown` store keeps the same folder beside its other engine files, in `.cypherlite/schema/` under the vault root. A constraint that a graph type manages, and an index that has no standalone `CREATE` form, is left out of `schema.cypher`; the graph type and the store's manifest carry it.

properties.heading: If it goes wrong
properties.text:
- **`Failed to open Relate: storage error: schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/<file> differs from the schema this store's checkpoint persisted; …`**, **`… schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/<file> is missing from the mirror this store's checkpoint wrote; …`** or **`… schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/<file> is not part of this store's schema mirror; …`** (exit code 1). A file in the folder was edited, deleted or added, or copied from another store, or a crash interrupted a checkpoint between writing the store and rewriting the folder. Delete `.cypherlite/schema/` and open the store for writing once; nothing in the store is lost.
- **`semantic error: IndexAlreadyExists`** (exit code 6) when piping `schema.cypher` into a store. The store already has an index of that name; the script stops at the first failing statement and runs none after it. Apply the file to an empty store, or run only the statements for the entries the store lacks.
- **The folder shows an old schema.** A long-running process has not checkpointed since the change. The folder catches up at its next checkpoint, or when the process closes the store.

properties.heading: Keep the files read-only
properties.text:
The folder is a mirror of the schema the last checkpoint wrote, never a source. Each open compares it byte for byte with that schema, and a changed, missing or extra file fails the open, read-only included. An index added by hand to the file is refused:

```bash verify
cp -R team team-edited
echo "CREATE INDEX person_age FOR (n:Person) ON (n.age);" >> team-edited/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
relate --database ./team-edited --read-only --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: storage error: schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher differs from the schema this store's checkpoint persisted; it was edited by hand or copied from another store; delete the .cypherlite/schema/ directory and reopen: the next checkpoint regenerates it from the store's schema
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"storage","message":"storage error: schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher differs from the schema this store's checkpoint persisted; it was edited by hand or copied from another store; delete the .cypherlite/schema/ directory and reopen: the next checkpoint regenerates it from the store's schema","retryable":false}}
exit=1
```

The refusal touched nothing else in the store. The repair is in the message: delete the folder and open the store for writing once, so its checkpoint at exit writes the folder again from the store's schema:

```bash verify
rm -r team-edited/.cypherlite/schema
relate --database ./team-edited --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
cat team-edited/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["ok"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"ok":1}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.463208,"execute_ms":0.34041699999999997,"lex_parse_ms":0.019625,"lower_ms":0.027542,"parse_ms":0.080667,"plan_ms":0.033541999999999995,"result_generation_ms":0.000084,"rewrite_ms":0.0067079999999999996},"truncated":false}
CREATE RANGE INDEX `person_role` FOR (n:`Person`) ON (n.`role`);
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX `project_search` FOR (n:`Project`) ON EACH [n.`name`, n.`language`] OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`fulltext.analyzer`: 'standard-no-stop-words',`fulltext.eventually_consistent`: false}};
CREATE CONSTRAINT `person_name` FOR (n:`Person`) REQUIRE (n.`name`) IS UNIQUE;
```

The hand-added `person_age` index is gone: to add an index, run its `CREATE INDEX` statement. A schema change committed since the last checkpoint is not drift; it waits in the WAL, and the next checkpoint writes it to the folder. A store with no `.cypherlite/schema/` folder at all, such as one written by an older release, opens normally and gains the folder at its next checkpoint.

properties.heading: Prerequisites
properties.text:
- relate on your `PATH` ([Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)).
- A directory store. A `.rl` file keeps its contents inside one file, so to read its schema folder, clone it into a directory first ([Clone and convert a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/clone-and-convert/)). To follow along, create the shared example graph as `team`:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team < team.cypher
```

properties.heading: Read the schema
properties.text:
Create a uniqueness [constraint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#constraint) and a range index. Each statement runs in its own process, and the CLI checkpoints when a run that opened the store for writing exits:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team --mode envelope "CREATE CONSTRAINT person_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) REQUIRE p.name IS UNIQUE"
relate --database ./team --mode envelope "CREATE INDEX person_role IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) ON (p.role)"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.233292,"execute_ms":1.121125,"lex_parse_ms":0.004583,"lower_ms":0.001,"parse_ms":0.106709,"plan_ms":0.001042,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.000167},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":1.2614589999999999,"execute_ms":1.154958,"lex_parse_ms":0.003708,"lower_ms":0.000959,"parse_ms":0.101458,"plan_ms":0.001083,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.000167},"truncated":false}
```

One file read now answers what the schema is, with no store opened and no `SHOW` statement run:

```bash verify
cat team/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
```

```text
CREATE RANGE INDEX `person_role` FOR (n:`Person`) ON (n.`role`);
CREATE CONSTRAINT `person_name` FOR (n:`Person`) REQUIRE (n.`name`) IS UNIQUE;
```

The folder changes at a checkpoint, not at each commit. A one-shot CLI run checkpoints as it exits. A long-running process, such as `relate serve` or an application on a client, checkpoints every 300 seconds by default, after 64 MiB of WAL or 10,000 commits, and when it closes the store; until then the folder shows the schema of the last checkpoint.

properties.heading: Review a schema change
properties.text:
Commit the store folder, or at least `.cypherlite/schema/`, to the repository. A schema change then shows up in a pull request as added and removed lines. To see the same diff without git, keep a copy of the file, add a full-text [index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#index), and compare:

```bash verify
cp team/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher schema-before.cypher
relate --database ./team --mode envelope "CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX project_search IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Project) ON EACH [p.name, p.language]"
diff schema-before.cypher team/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.9976670000000001,"execute_ms":0.89025,"lex_parse_ms":0.0041659999999999996,"lower_ms":0.001042,"parse_ms":0.10291600000000001,"plan_ms":0.000917,"result_generation_ms":0.000375,"rewrite_ms":0.000167},"truncated":false}
1a2
> CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX `project_search` FOR (n:`Project`) ON EACH [n.`name`, n.`language`] OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`fulltext.analyzer`: 'standard-no-stop-words',`fulltext.eventually_consistent`: false}};
```

The rendered statement spells out every option, defaults included, so a reviewer sees every setting the index runs with. An agent reads the same file to learn which indexes a statement can use before it writes one.

properties.text:
The store's own catalog lists the same three entries the file holds, after the two lookup indexes that `SHOW INDEXES` lists on every store and the file leaves out. `SHOW INDEXES` includes the range index that backs the uniqueness constraint, under the constraint's name:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team --read-only --mode envelope "SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type RETURN name, type ORDER BY name"
```

properties.heading: API reference
properties.text: relate is one engine with several front doors, and each front door is a [surface](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#surface). The Rust crate is the engine. The C library, `librelate_ffi`, exposes it through a C application binary interface (C ABI), which the Node.js, Java, Go and Swift [clients](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) call; the Python client and the WebAssembly (WASM) browser build carry the engine themselves. The `relate` CLI links the engine too, and `relate serve` hosts [Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bolt), the HTTP Query API and [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) over one [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). Every surface runs the same engine, so a statement means the same thing on each; the surfaces differ in what they expose around it, which the matrix on this page records.

Checked on 2026-11-11 against relate 1.0.0: runs of the CLI binary and `relate serve` (Bolt, HTTP and MCP), the WebAssembly build this site ships, and the Python, Node.js, C, Java, Go, Swift and Rust clients, and each surface's upstream reference. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C ABI library as the Node.js client.

Each row is a feature and each column a surface; every row has a stable anchor, `#matrix-<feature>`, such as `#matrix-read-only`. A cell holds one of four values, then a note:

| Value     | Meaning                                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `yes`     | The surface has the feature; the note names the call, flag, or field |
| `no`      | The surface lacks it; the note says why, or what it offers instead   |
| `partial` | The surface has part of it; the note names the part                  |
| `unknown` | Nobody has checked the cell; the matrix never guesses                |

A cell is checked against a run of the surface or its upstream reference, and the note says what the surface does, not how the cell was checked. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C library as the Node.js client, so a statement-level cell such as vector search is checked once through that library; the Bolt and MCP cells of statement-level features are checked on the store all three served surfaces share. The reference page of each language client shows its own column alone.

properties.heading: C ABI
properties.text: The C application binary interface (ABI) is the header `relate.h` and the library `librelate_ffi`: opaque handles for a database, a connection, a result, a value and a parameter builder, and 81 functions over them. The ABI version is 2, and `relate_abi_version()` returns it. The Node.js, Java, Go and Swift [clients](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) wrap this library, and the library wraps the Rust crate's `Database`. The header is the contract; this page groups its declarations as of relate 1.0.1. The guide [Use the C ABI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/embed/c/) covers the same calls with runnable programs.

properties.text:
| Variable                                                                                                                                                                    | Effect                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_FFI_LOG`                                                                                                                                                            | `1` logs an internal failure's original message to stderr; read once per process                                                                                  |

properties.heading: Error shape
properties.text:
Every failure carries one JSON object, delivered with the call that failed. There is no thread-local error slot, so a call on a worker thread reports its own error.

```json
{"code":"Neo.ClientError.Statement.ArithmeticError","gql_status":"22G03","stage":"runtime","retryable":false,"message":"type error: / by zero"}
```

| Key          | Type    | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`       | string  | The Neo4j status code                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `gql_status` | string  | The five-character GQLSTATUS code                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `stage`      | string  | `compile` (rejected before any work), `runtime` (found while executing) or `internal` (not the statement's fault: a storage, I/O or engine failure, a `NULL` or poisoned handle, a refused argument)                  |
| `retryable`  | boolean | `true` only when running the same work again can succeed, such as after a write-write conflict                                                                                                                        |
| `message`    | string  | The engine's message for a `compile` or `runtime` failure; the boundary's own text for a refused argument or handle; the fixed `internal error` for storage, I/O, lock and engine-internal failures and caught panics |

| Failure                                                                                                         | Status                                    | Where the shape is                                                    | Owner                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| A statement fails                                                                                               | `relate_query_params` returns `RELATE_OK` | `relate_result_error_json(r)`, with `relate_result_is_error(r)` = `1` | The result                   |
| `relate_query_params` itself fails (a `NULL` or poisoned connection, invalid UTF-8, a list builder as `params`) | `RELATE_ERROR`, `*out` = `NULL`           | The `char **error_json` out-param                                     | Caller: `relate_free_string` |
| Any other fallible call: open, connect, set namespace, begin, commit, rollback, checkpoint, every putter        | `RELATE_ERROR`                            | The `char **error_json` out-param                                     | Caller: `relate_free_string` |
| A value accessor refuses                                                                                        | `NULL`, `-1` or `RELATE_ERROR`            | None: the accessor's result is the whole report                       | —                            |
| `relate_database_close(NULL)`, `relate_disconnect(NULL)`                                                        | `RELATE_ERROR`                            | None                                                                  | —                            |

An `error_json` out-param is written only on failure; `NULL` in its place drops the detail, and the status alone reports the failure. The classification comes from the engine's one table, the same one the CLI, the clients, Bolt, and HTTP use. With `RELATE_FFI_LOG=1` set in the environment (read once per process), the original message of an internal failure goes to the host's stderr, prefixed `ffi internal error: `.

properties.heading: Example
Lifecycle
properties.text:
| Function                                                                                                    | Returns | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `int relate_abi_version(void)`                                                                              | `2`     | The ABI version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `relate_database_open(const char *uri, relate_database *out, char **error_json)`                            | status  | Opens `":memory:"`, a `.rl` path (a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store); the legacy `.cl` too), any other path or `file://` URI (a directory store); creates a missing store. On failure `*out` is `NULL`. |
| `relate_database_open_read_only(const char *uri, relate_database *out, char **error_json)`                  | status  | Opens an existing store without writing, checkpointing or creating it; writes and checkpoints then fail with `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase`                                                                                                               |
| `relate_database_close(relate_database db)`                                                                 | status  | Frees the handle, poisoned or not; `NULL` gives `RELATE_ERROR`                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `relate_connect_namespace(relate_database db, const char *name, relate_connection *out, char **error_json)` | status  | Opens a connection whose session namespace is `name`: `neo4j`, `system` or `system_ontologies`, matched case-insensitively; `NULL` selects `neo4j`. Another name fails with a message ending `Graph not found: <name>`.                                    |
| `relate_conn_set_namespace(relate_connection conn, const char *name, char **error_json)`                    | status  | Changes the session namespace between transactions; inside one, fails with a message ending `Cannot change the namespace while a transaction is open.`; a `NULL` name is refused                                                                           |
| `relate_disconnect(relate_connection conn)`                                                                 | status  | Frees the connection, poisoned or not; `NULL` gives `RELATE_ERROR`                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `relate_checkpoint(relate_database db, char **error_json)`                                                  | status  | Writes a snapshot and recycles closed WAL segments; not the commit durability boundary                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `void relate_free_string(char *s)`                                                                          | —       | Frees a caller-owned string; `NULL` is a no-op                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

properties.heading: Limits
properties.text: The limits come from the engine and are the same on every surface: a statement's text is at most 4194304 bytes (`syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`), one value a statement builds is bounded by the expression memory cap, and a file-backed store has one writing open across every process. [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/) lists each limit with its default and the setting that changes it.

properties.heading: Ownership
properties.text:
The return type is the rule: a `char *` belongs to the caller, a `const char *` to relate.

| Handle or pointer                                                                      | Owner      | Freed by                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `relate_database`                                                                      | Caller     | `relate_database_close`                                |
| `relate_connection`                                                                    | Caller     | `relate_disconnect`                                    |
| `relate_query_result`                                                                  | Caller     | `relate_destroy_result`                                |
| Every `relate_value` handle, roots and children                                        | The result | `relate_destroy_result`; no per-value free exists      |
| Every `const char *` from a result or value accessor                                   | The result | `relate_destroy_result`                                |
| `char *` from an `error_json` out-param, or from `relate_conn_commit`'s `bookmark_out` | Caller     | `relate_free_string`                                   |
| A `relate_params` root and its children                                                | Caller     | `relate_params_free` on the root                       |
| Strings and arrays passed to a putter                                                  | Caller     | Copied at the call; released whenever the caller likes |

properties.heading: Params builder
properties.text:
`relate_params_new()` returns a root: the statement's map of named parameters. `_put_list` and `_put_map` insert a nested container and write its child builder, which takes the same putters. A map takes a unique, non-`NULL` UTF-8 name; a list takes a `NULL` name and appends. Every putter copies its input and returns a status; a refusal returns `RELATE_ERROR` with an `internal`-stage shape and leaves the builder unchanged and usable.

| Function                                                                                                              | Binds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate_params relate_params_new(void)`                                                                               | A new root; never `NULL`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `void relate_params_free(relate_params p)`                                                                            | Frees a root and every child; `NULL` or a child is a no-op                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_params_put_null(p, name, &err)`                                                                               | `null`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `relate_params_put_bool(p, name, uint8_t v, &err)`                                                                    | A boolean; `0` is false, any other value true                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_params_put_int(p, name, int64_t v, &err)`                                                                     | An integer, the whole `int64_t` range                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `relate_params_put_float(p, name, double v, &err)`                                                                    | A float, `NaN` and infinities included                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `relate_params_put_string(p, name, const char *v, size_t len, &err)`                                                  | `len` bytes of UTF-8; invalid UTF-8 refuses. A `NULL` `v` with `len` 0 binds the empty string; a `NULL` `v` with a nonzero `len` refuses with `null string value`                                                                                                           |
| `relate_params_put_date(p, name, year, month, day, &err)`                                                             | A date that exists in the calendar                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `relate_params_put_local_time(p, name, hour, minute, second, nanosecond, &err)`                                       | A local time                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `relate_params_put_time(p, name, hour, minute, second, nanosecond, offset_seconds, zone, &err)`                       | A zoned time; a non-`NULL` zone supplies the offset at the current instant, and the time keeps no zone id                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `relate_params_put_local_datetime(p, name, year, month, day, hour, minute, second, nanosecond, &err)`                 | A local datetime                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `relate_params_put_datetime(p, name, year, month, day, hour, minute, second, nanosecond, offset_seconds, zone, &err)` | A zoned datetime. `NULL` zone: the offset alone. A time zone name such as `Europe/Berlin`: kept with the value, its offset resolved at that wall clock and `offset_seconds` ignored; a daylight-saving overlap takes the earlier offset, and a wall clock in a gap refuses. |
| `relate_params_put_duration(p, name, months, days, seconds, nanos, &err)`                                             | A duration from any `int64_t` components                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `relate_params_put_point(p, name, int32_t srid, double x, double y, const double *z, &err)`                           | A point: `srid` 7203 (Cartesian) or 4326 (WGS-84) with `z` `NULL`, or 9157 (3D Cartesian) or 4979 (3D WGS-84) with `z` pointing at the third coordinate; any other pairing refuses                                                                                          |
| `relate_params_put_vector_float(p, name, const char *dtype, const double *values, size_t dim, &err)`                  | A `FLOAT16`, `BFLOAT16`, `FLOAT32` or `FLOAT` vector; each value exactly representable in the dtype                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `relate_params_put_vector_int(p, name, const char *dtype, const int64_t *values, size_t dim, &err)`                   | An `INTEGER8`, `INTEGER16`, `INTEGER32` or `INTEGER` vector; each value within the dtype's width                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `relate_params_put_list(p, name, relate_params *child, &err)`                                                         | An empty list, with its child builder in `*child`                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `relate_params_put_map(p, name, relate_params *child, &err)`                                                          | An empty map, with its child builder in `*child`                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| Limit                                            | Value                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Entries per list or map                          | 100000                                                                                                                                       |
| Bytes per parameter name                         | 4096                                                                                                                                         |
| Bytes per builder, across every nested container | 16 MiB                                                                                                                                       |
| Components                                       | Month 1 to 12, day 1 to 31, hour 0 to 23, minute 0 to 59, second 0 to 59, nanosecond 0 to 999999999, `offset_seconds` within ±64800 (±18:00) |

Each limit refuses one past its value. A `len` or `dim` argument is trusted: a buffer shorter than it is undefined behavior. A statement that references a parameter the builder does not hold fails as an error result with `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <names>`.

properties.heading: Results
properties.text:
Every string a result or value accessor returns belongs to the result and lives until `relate_destroy_result`. A `NULL` result gives `0`, `0.0` or `NULL`; an error result gives `NULL` from the string accessors, `0.0` from the timings and `0` rows.

| Function                                                                                              | Returns        | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate_column_count(result)`                                                                         | `long long`    | The number of columns                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `relate_row_count(result)`                                                                            | `long long`    | The number of rows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `relate_column_name(result, long long col)`                                                           | `const char *` | Column `col`'s name; `NULL` out of range                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_result_is_error(result)`                                                                      | `uint8_t`      | `1` for an error result, else `0`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `relate_result_error_json(result)`                                                                    | `const char *` | The [error shape](#error-shape) of an error result; `NULL` on a good result                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_result_bookmark(result)`                                                                      | `const char *` | An auto-commit write's bookmark, `relate:<n>`; `NULL` for a read, an `EXPLAIN`, a write whose counters are all zero (it changed nothing), and any statement inside an explicit transaction, and an error result                                                                           |
| `relate_result_query_type(result)`                                                                    | `const char *` | `r`, `w` (a write returning no columns), `rw` (a write returning columns) or `s` (schema), from the plan; `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` report the statement they wrap                                                                                                                          |
| `relate_result_namespace(result)`                                                                     | `const char *` | The namespace the statement ran in: its `USE` target, else the session namespace                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `relate_result_stats(result)`                                                                         | `const char *` | A JSON object of 11 counters, zeros included: `nodes_created`, `nodes_deleted`, `relationships_created`, `relationships_deleted`, `properties_set`, `labels_added`, `labels_removed`, `indexes_added`, `indexes_removed`, `constraints_added`, `constraints_removed`                      |
| `relate_result_notifications(result)`                                                                 | `const char *` | A JSON array of [notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#notification), each with `code`, `gql_status`, `severity`, `category`, `title`, `description` and `remedy`, plus `operator_id` for an operator's own; `[]` on a plain run, filled by `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` |
| `relate_result_plan_json(result)`                                                                     | `const char *` | The plan as a `relate.plan/v1` document after `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE`; `NULL` on a plain run                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_result_elapsed_ms(result)`                                                                    | `double`       | The engine's wall-clock time for the statement: parse, plan and run, excluding row handling                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_result_parse_ms(result)`, `relate_result_plan_ms(result)`, `relate_result_execute_ms(result)` | `double`       | Three disjoint parts of the elapsed time; their sum never exceeds it                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The plan document is `{schema, profiled, statement, root}`. Each node holds `operator`, `details`, `identifiers`, `estimated_rows` (or `null`), `actual` (`null` under `EXPLAIN`; rows, time, database hits and memory under `PROFILE`), `children` and `warnings` (the remedy-bearing notifications raised for that operator). Keys are `snake_case`, and a breaking change bumps the `schema` version.
