properties.heading: Statements and transactions
properties.text:
| Function                                                                                                                                   | Returns | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `relate_query_params(relate_connection conn, const char *cypher, const relate_params params, relate_query_result *out, char **error_json)` | status  | Runs one statement. `params` is a builder root, a `put_map` child, or `NULL` for none; it is read, never changed, and can back later statements. A list builder is refused. A statement failure returns `RELATE_OK` with an error result.                                            |
| `void relate_destroy_result(relate_query_result result)`                                                                                   | —       | Frees the result and every value handle and string it owns; `NULL` is a no-op                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `relate_conn_begin(relate_connection conn, char **error_json)`                                                                             | status  | Starts an explicit transaction; one per connection, and a second fails with `semantic error: already in a transaction`                                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_conn_commit(relate_connection conn, char **bookmark_out, char **error_json)`                                                       | status  | Commits. `RELATE_OK`: `*bookmark_out` is the bookmark, caller-owned, or `NULL` when the transaction wrote nothing. `RELATE_ERROR`: the commit failed and `*bookmark_out` is `NULL`. A `NULL` `bookmark_out` is refused with `null out pointer` and the transaction is not committed. |
| `relate_conn_rollback(relate_connection conn, char **error_json)`                                                                          | status  | Discards the transaction; with none open, fails with `semantic error: no transaction`                                                                                                                                                                                                |

A [bookmark](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bookmark) is `relate:<n>`, `n` being the store's commit sequence across every connection and surface. Bookmarks order by the parsed `n`, not as strings: as strings, `relate:10` sorts before `relate:9`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
#include "relate.h"

relate_database_open(uri, &db, &err)              -> relate_status
relate_connect_namespace(db, NULL, &conn, &err)   -> relate_status
relate_query_params(conn, cypher, params, &r, &err) -> relate_status
  relate_result_is_error(r) ? relate_result_error_json(r)
                            : relate_value_at(r, row, col) -> relate_value
relate_destroy_result(r)
relate_disconnect(conn)
relate_database_close(db)
```

Each release attaches a `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` archive per platform (`aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) holding `include/relate.h` and the static and shared libraries. A program links with `-lrelate_ffi`. After the first public release the ABI changes only by addition; a version bump means symbols were removed or signatures changed.

properties.heading: Threading and panic safety
properties.text:
| Rule            | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Databases       | A `relate_database` may be shared across threads                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Connections     | A `relate_connection` must not be: calls on one connection are serialized by the caller; distinct connections may run on distinct threads                                                                                                      |
| Params builders | One thread at a time, as for a connection                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Panics          | Every entry point catches a panic at the boundary. The handle it happened on is then poisoned: every later call on it returns `RELATE_ERROR` with an `internal`-stage shape, or `0` or `NULL`. Close and destroy still free a poisoned handle. |

properties.heading: Types
properties.text:
| Type                     | Kind          | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate_database`        | Opaque handle | An open store; may be shared across threads                                              |
| `relate_connection`      | Opaque handle | One session on a database, with a session namespace; never used from two threads at once |
| `relate_query_result`    | Opaque handle | One statement's result or error                                                          |
| `relate_value`           | Opaque handle | One value inside a result, owned by that result                                          |
| `relate_params`          | Opaque handle | A params builder: a root or a nested list or map                                         |
| `relate_status`          | Enum          | `RELATE_OK = 0`, `RELATE_ERROR = 1`                                                      |
| `enum relate_value_kind` | Enum          | The 18 value kinds in [Value kinds](#value-kinds)                                        |

properties.heading: Value accessors
properties.text:
An accessor called on another kind, on a `NULL` handle, or with a `NULL` out-param refuses without side effects: a pointer return gives `NULL`, a count return gives `-1`, and a status return gives `RELATE_ERROR` with the out-params untouched. A refusal never poisons anything. Every handle and string belongs to the result.

| Function                                                                                                               | Serves                                             | Contract                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate_value_at(result, long long row, long long col)`                                                                | —                                                  | The cell's root handle; `NULL` for an index out of range, an error result or a `NULL` result                                                                                |
| `relate_value_kind(v)`                                                                                                 | any                                                | The `enum relate_value_kind` enumerator as an `int`; `-1` for a `NULL` handle                                                                                               |
| `relate_value_bool(v, uint8_t *out)`                                                                                   | `BOOL`                                             | `0` or `1`                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_value_int(v, int64_t *out)`                                                                                    | `INT`                                              | The 64-bit integer                                                                                                                                                          |
| `relate_value_float(v, double *out)`                                                                                   | `FLOAT`                                            | The double, `NaN` and infinities included                                                                                                                                   |
| `relate_value_is_nan(v, uint8_t *out)`, `relate_value_is_inf(v, uint8_t *out)`                                         | `FLOAT`                                            | `1` when `NaN`, or infinite of either sign                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_value_string(v, size_t *len)`                                                                                  | `STRING`, `RELATIONSHIP`                           | NUL-terminated UTF-8 (a relationship's type); `*len`, when not `NULL`, is the byte length, so a string with an interior NUL crosses whole                                   |
| `relate_value_element_id(v)`                                                                                           | `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`                             | The [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id) as `elementId()` spells it, such as `4:rl-id:n0`; `NULL` in the `system` namespace                |
| `relate_value_start_element_id(v)`, `relate_value_end_element_id(v)`                                                   | `RELATIONSHIP`                                     | The end nodes' element ids                                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_value_id(v, int64_t *out)`                                                                                     | `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`                             | The numeric id `id()` returns                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_value_start_id(v, int64_t *out)`, `relate_value_end_id(v, int64_t *out)`                                       | `RELATIONSHIP`                                     | The end nodes' numeric ids                                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_value_list_len(v)`                                                                                             | `LIST`, `PATH`, `NODE`                             | The items, the path's elements, or the node's labels                                                                                                                        |
| `relate_value_list_get(v, long long i)`                                                                                | `LIST`, `PATH`, `NODE`                             | Item `i`; `NULL` past the end                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_value_map_len(v)`                                                                                              | `MAP`, `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`                      | The entries, or the entity's properties, in the engine's order                                                                                                              |
| `relate_value_map_key(v, long long i, size_t *len)`                                                                    | `MAP`, `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`                      | Key `i`; `NULL` past the end                                                                                                                                                |
| `relate_value_map_get(v, const char *key)`                                                                             | `MAP`, `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`                      | The value under `key`; `NULL` when absent, a `RELATE_V_NULL` handle when present and null                                                                                   |
| `relate_value_year(v, int64_t *out)`, `relate_value_month(…)`, `relate_value_day(…)`                                   | `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `LOCAL_DATETIME`               | Month 1 to 12, day 1 to 31                                                                                                                                                  |
| `relate_value_hour(v, int64_t *out)`, `relate_value_minute(…)`, `relate_value_second(…)`, `relate_value_nanosecond(…)` | `TIME`, `LOCAL_TIME`, `DATETIME`, `LOCAL_DATETIME` | The local wall clock; nanosecond 0 to 999999999                                                                                                                             |
| `relate_value_offset_seconds(v, int64_t *out)`                                                                         | `TIME`, `DATETIME`                                 | The UTC offset in seconds                                                                                                                                                   |
| `relate_value_zone(v)`                                                                                                 | `TIME`, `DATETIME`                                 | The time zone name, or `""` when the value carries only an offset (always for `TIME`)                                                                                       |
| `relate_value_duration(v, int64_t *months, int64_t *days, int64_t *seconds, int64_t *nanos)`                           | `DURATION`                                         | The four components, losslessly; every out-param required                                                                                                                   |
| `relate_value_point(v, int32_t *srid, int32_t *dim, double *x, double *y, double *z)`                                  | `POINT`                                            | `dim` is 2 or 3; `x` and `y` are longitude and latitude for a geographic spatial reference identifier (`srid`); `*z` written only when `dim` is 3; every out-param required |
| `relate_value_vector_dtype(v)`                                                                                         | `VECTOR`                                           | `INTEGER8`, `INTEGER16`, `INTEGER32`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT16`, `BFLOAT16`, `FLOAT32` or `FLOAT`                                                                                |
| `relate_value_vector_dim(v)`                                                                                           | `VECTOR`                                           | The dimension                                                                                                                                                               |
| `relate_value_vector_float(v, long long i, double *out)`                                                               | `VECTOR`                                           | Coordinate `i` of a `FLOAT*` vector; another dtype or an index out of range refuses                                                                                         |
| `relate_value_vector_int(v, long long i, int64_t *out)`                                                                | `VECTOR`                                           | Coordinate `i` of an `INTEGER*` vector; another dtype or an index out of range refuses                                                                                      |

properties.heading: Value kinds
properties.text:
| Enumerator                | Value | Read with                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_V_NULL`           | 0     | Nothing: a Cypher `null` is a handle of this kind, never a `NULL` handle                                                                                                               |
| `RELATE_V_BOOL`           | 1     | `relate_value_bool`                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `RELATE_V_INT`            | 2     | `relate_value_int`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `RELATE_V_FLOAT`          | 3     | `relate_value_float`, `relate_value_is_nan`, `relate_value_is_inf`                                                                                                                     |
| `RELATE_V_STRING`         | 4     | `relate_value_string`; a UUID reads as a string                                                                                                                                        |
| `RELATE_V_NODE`           | 5     | `relate_value_element_id`, `relate_value_id`; labels through the list accessors, properties through the map accessors                                                                  |
| `RELATE_V_RELATIONSHIP`   | 6     | `relate_value_element_id`, `_start_element_id`, `_end_element_id`, `relate_value_id`, `_start_id`, `_end_id`; type through `relate_value_string`, properties through the map accessors |
| `RELATE_V_PATH`           | 7     | The list accessors: 2n + 1 elements for n hops, node, relationship, …, node                                                                                                            |
| `RELATE_V_LIST`           | 8     | `relate_value_list_len`, `relate_value_list_get`; a byte array reads as a list of `INT`                                                                                                |
| `RELATE_V_MAP`            | 9     | `relate_value_map_len`, `relate_value_map_key`, `relate_value_map_get`; always a map, even when shaped like a node                                                                     |
| `RELATE_V_POINT`          | 10    | `relate_value_point`                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `RELATE_V_DATE`           | 11    | `relate_value_year`, `_month`, `_day`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `RELATE_V_TIME`           | 12    | `relate_value_hour`, `_minute`, `_second`, `_nanosecond`, `_offset_seconds`; `relate_value_zone` is `""`                                                                               |
| `RELATE_V_LOCAL_TIME`     | 13    | `relate_value_hour`, `_minute`, `_second`, `_nanosecond`                                                                                                                               |
| `RELATE_V_DATETIME`       | 14    | The date and time components, `_offset_seconds`, and `relate_value_zone` (a named time zone such as `Europe/Berlin`, or `""` for an offset only)                                       |
| `RELATE_V_LOCAL_DATETIME` | 15    | The date and time components                                                                                                                                                           |
| `RELATE_V_DURATION`       | 16    | `relate_value_duration`                                                                                                                                                                |
| `RELATE_V_VECTOR`         | 17    | `relate_value_vector_dtype`, `_vector_dim`, `_vector_float`, `_vector_int`                                                                                                             |

A kind that a later, additive ABI introduces is a number a program does not know; the header asks clients to treat it as a reportable case.

properties.heading: Go API
properties.text: The Go [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) is the module `github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go`, package `relate`, for Go 1.22 or later. It is cgo code over the relate C library, `librelate_ffi`, whose C application binary interface (C ABI) is version 2: values cross through the library's typed value walker and parameter builder, with no JSON. Every call is synchronous. This page lists the package's exported identifiers as `go doc` reports them for relate 1.0.1.

properties.heading: Capabilities
properties.text:
| Feature                                                                                                | Go                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| In-memory store. A store that lives only in the process.                                               | yes: `relate.Open(":memory:")`                                        |
| Directory store. A store in a directory on disk.                                                       | yes: `relate.Open(path)`                                              |
| Single-file .rl store. A store in one `.rl` file.                                                      | yes: `relate.Open("graph.rl")`                                        |
| Read-only open. An open that loads the store once and refuses every write.                             | yes: `relate.OpenReadOnly(uri)`                                       |
| Explicit transactions. Several statements committed or rolled back together.                           | yes: `Begin()`, `Commit()`, `Rollback()`                              |
| Parameters. `$name` values passed beside the statement.                                                | yes: `QueryParams(statement, map)`                                    |
| Column types, counters and timings. Metadata returned with each result.                                | partial: `Stats`, `QueryType`, `Plan`; no column types or timings     |
| Notifications. The engine's query notifications (for example a Cartesian product), each with a remedy. | yes: `Notifications`                                                  |
| Arrow output. Results as Apache Arrow.                                                                 | no: no Arrow call in the client                                       |
| Change data capture. Reading committed changes from a slot.                                            | no: no change-data-capture call in the client                         |
| Vector search. Vector indexes and `SEARCH`.                                                            | yes: `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` and `SEARCH` through the C ABI             |
| Full-text search. Full-text indexes and their queries.                                                 | yes: `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` and full-text `SEARCH` through the C ABI |
| LOAD CSV from local files. Local `LOAD CSV` under a configured directory (denied unless one is set).   | yes: `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`, read by the C ABI's open                  |
| Load a store from a URL. Opening a `.rl` store fetched over https.                                     | no: no open from a URL in the client                                  |
| Agent mode. The CLI's agent defaults: the 100-row cap and the piped `toon` output.                     | no: A CLI setting                                                     |

Each cell is yes, no, partial or unknown, with the call, flag or reason. Checked on 2026-11-11 against relate 1.0.0: runs of the CLI binary and `relate serve` (Bolt, HTTP and MCP), the WebAssembly build this site ships, and the Python, Node.js, C, Java, Go, Swift and Rust clients, and each surface's upstream reference. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C ABI library as the Node.js client.

properties.heading: Connection
properties.text:
| Method                        | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Query(cypher)`               | `QueryParams` with a nil map                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `QueryParams(cypher, params)` | Runs one statement; auto-commits outside an explicit transaction; a nil map binds no parameters                                                                                                                  |
| `SetNamespace(name)`          | Changes the session namespace; refused inside a transaction                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Begin()`                     | Opens an explicit [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction); transactions do not nest                                                                                              |
| `Commit()`                    | Commits; returns the [bookmark](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bookmark) `"relate:<n>"`, or `""` when the transaction wrote nothing; a failure returns `""` and the error and ends the transaction |
| `Rollback()`                  | Discards the explicit transaction                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Close()`                     | Disconnects; an open transaction rolls back                                                                                                                                                                      |

A statement failure returns a nil `*Result` and the `*Error`. A connection's own refusals, each with code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` and GQLSTATUS `42000`:

| Call                                           | Message                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Begin()` inside a transaction                 | `semantic error: already in a transaction`                                                   |
| `Commit()` or `Rollback()` with no transaction | `semantic error: no transaction`                                                             |
| `SetNamespace(…)` inside a transaction         | `semantic error: TransactionError: Cannot change the namespace while a transaction is open.` |

The package holds no lock. A `*Database` may be shared between goroutines; calls that share a `*Connection` are serialized by the caller, one at a time, and distinct connections may run concurrently.

properties.heading: Database
properties.text:
| Function or method       | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Open(uri)`              | Opens `:memory:`, a directory store or a `.rl` store for writing; creates a missing store                                                                                             |
| `OpenReadOnly(uri)`      | Loads an existing store once; refuses writes and checkpoints; a missing store is an error                                                                                             |
| `Connect()`              | A connection in the `neo4j` namespace                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ConnectNamespace(name)` | A connection in `neo4j`, `system` or `system_ontologies`, matched case-insensitively                                                                                                  |
| `Checkpoint()`           | Writes a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint), folding the write-ahead log into a fresh snapshot of committed state; refused on a read-only database |
| `Close()`                | Frees the native handle                                                                                                                                                               |

A failed `Open` or `OpenReadOnly` returns a `*Error` with message `internal error`, code `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, GQLSTATUS `42000` and stage `internal`, whether the store is locked by another writer or missing. An unknown namespace returns `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`.

`Close` on a `*Database` or a `*Connection` frees the native handle and keeps no closed state: a second `Close`, or any later call on the value, uses freed memory. The package sets no finalizers, so a handle never closed keeps its store open, and a `.rl` store locked, until the process exits.

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| Field       | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Code`      | The Neo4j status code, such as `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ArithmeticError`                                                                                                                |
| `GQLStatus` | The five-character GQLSTATUS, such as `22G03`                                                                                                                                             |
| `Stage`     | `StageCompile` (parse or plan), `StageRuntime` (execution) or `StageInternal` (the C boundary: a poisoned handle, a caught panic, a refused argument)                                     |
| `Retryable` | `true` exactly when running the same work again can succeed: a write-write conflict (`Neo.TransientError.Transaction.Outdated`, message `write-write conflict`) or a retryable memory cap |
| `Message`   | The engine's message                                                                                                                                                                      |

Every failure the engine or the C boundary reports is a `*Error`, from a statement's result or from the call's own error channel; `errors.As(err, &e)` with `var e *relate.Error` matches it. The client's own refusals are plain `error` values: the parameter refusals, `ABI contract violated: …` for a result that breaks the C contract, and `unsupported value kind <n>`. A write on a read-only database returns code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` and GQLSTATUS `42N18`. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists the engine's messages.

properties.heading: Example
Exported identifiers
properties.text:
| Identifier                                                           | Kind                      | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Database`                                                           | struct, unexported fields | An open store                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Connection`                                                         | struct, unexported fields | One session on a store                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `Result`                                                             | struct                    | `Columns`, `Rows`, `QueryType`, `Namespace`, `Bookmark`, `Stats`, `Notifications`, `Plan`                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Stats`                                                              | struct                    | The 11 mutation counters                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `QueryType`                                                          | `string` type             | `QueryTypeRead` `"r"`, `QueryTypeWrite` `"w"`, `QueryTypeReadWrite` `"rw"`, `QueryTypeSchema` `"s"`                                                                                                                                           |
| `Namespace`                                                          | `string` type             | `NamespaceNeo4j` `"neo4j"`, `NamespaceSystem` `"system"`, `NamespaceSystemOntologies` `"system_ontologies"`                                                                                                                                   |
| `Error`                                                              | struct                    | `Code`, `GQLStatus`, `Stage`, `Retryable`, `Message`; `Error()` returns `Message`                                                                                                                                                             |
| `Stage`                                                              | `string` type             | `StageCompile` `"compile"`, `StageRuntime` `"runtime"`, `StageInternal` `"internal"`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Node`, `Relationship`, `Path`                                       | struct, struct, `[]any`   | Graph values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Point`, `Vector`                                                    | struct                    | Spatial and vector values                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Date`, `Time`, `LocalTime`, `DateTime`, `LocalDateTime`, `Duration` | struct                    | Temporal values as their components                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `Notification`                                                       | struct                    | One planner notification                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Severity`, `Category`                                               | `string` types            | A notification's severity (`SeverityInformation`, `SeverityWarning`) and category (`CategoryPerformance`, `CategoryUnrecognized`, `CategoryDeprecation`, `CategorySchema`, `CategoryHint`); typed since 0.1.3, where 0.1.2 used plain strings |
| `PlanDocument`, `PlanNode`, `PlanActual`, `PlanStart`                | struct                    | The structured plan                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

properties.heading: Limits
properties.text: The limits come from the engine and are the same on every surface: a statement's text is at most 4194304 bytes (`syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`), one value a statement builds is bounded by the expression memory cap, and a file-backed store has one writing open across every process. [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/) lists each limit with its default and the setting that changes it.

properties.heading: Linking
properties.text:
The package's cgo directives include `relate.h` and link `-lrelate_ffi`, searching the `surfaces/relate-ffi/include`, `target/debug` and `target/release` directories of the relate source repository. Outside that repository the build reads cgo's environment:

| Variable                                               | Value                                                                                                                                                                                          | Without it                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CGO_ENABLED`                                          | `1`                                                                                                                                                                                            | The package's files are excluded: `undefined: relate.Open`                                                        |
| `CGO_CFLAGS`                                           | `-I<directory holding relate.h>`                                                                                                                                                               | `fatal error: 'relate.h' file not found`                                                                          |
| `CGO_LDFLAGS`                                          | `-L<directory holding librelate_ffi> -lrelate_ffi`; for a static link on macOS, add `-framework CoreFoundation`                                                                                | `ld: library 'relate_ffi' not found`                                                                              |
| `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` (macOS), `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (Linux) | The shared library's directory, at run time. On Linux an rpath at link time does the same; on macOS the library's install name is the absolute path it was built at, so an rpath does not help | The binary does not start: on macOS, `dyld[<pid>]: Library not loaded: <absolute build path>/librelate_ffi.dylib` |

Each release attaches `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz`, holding the shared library, the static library, and the header. On Windows, cgo links with MinGW, which needs an import library generated from `relate_ffi.dll` with `gendef` and `dlltool`.

properties.heading: Notifications and plans
properties.text:
`Notification` has the fields `Code`, `GQLStatus`, `Severity`, a `Severity` (`SeverityInformation` or `SeverityWarning`, whose strings are `INFORMATION` and `WARNING`), `Category`, a `Category` (`CategoryPerformance`, `CategoryUnrecognized`, `CategoryDeprecation`, `CategorySchema` or `CategoryHint`, each the upper-case name), `Title`, `Description`, `Remedy` and `OperatorID`, an `*int64` that is nil on a statement-scoped notification. A severity or category outside those values, or a missing one, fails the result's decoding with an error that begins `ABI contract violated:` and names the key and the value.

| Struct         | Fields                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PlanDocument` | `Schema` (`relate.plan/v1`), `Profiled`, `Statement *string`, `Root PlanNode`                                                 |
| `PlanNode`     | `Operator`, `Details`, `Identifiers`, `EstimatedRows *int64`, `Actual *PlanActual`, `Children`, `Warnings []Notification`     |
| `PlanActual`   | `Rows`, `TimeMs`, `DbHits`, `MemoryBytes`, `Hops`, `NeighborWalks`, `NodeReads`, `Start *PlanStart`; nil on an `EXPLAIN` plan |
| `PlanStart`    | `Element`, `Backward`, `Reason`                                                                                               |

properties.heading: Parameters
properties.text:
`QueryParams` binds each map entry as one Cypher value:

| Go value                                          | Binds as                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nil`, or a nil pointer, interface, slice, or map | `NULL`                                                                                                           |
| `bool`                                            | `BOOLEAN`                                                                                                        |
| any signed or unsigned integer                    | `INTEGER`; an unsigned value greater than `math.MaxInt64` is refused                                             |
| `float32`, `float64`                              | `FLOAT`                                                                                                          |
| `string`                                          | `STRING`                                                                                                         |
| slice or array, `[]byte` included                 | `LIST`                                                                                                           |
| `map[string]T`                                    | `MAP`                                                                                                            |
| struct                                            | `MAP` of its exported fields, keyed by `json` tag name; `json:"-"` is skipped and `omitempty` drops a zero value |

The package's own value types are structs, so they bind as maps of their fields; a temporal, point or vector parameter is built in the statement from its parts, as `date($day)` or `vector($v, 3, FLOAT32)`. A value the builder refuses fails before the statement runs, as a plain `error` prefixed `parameter "<name>": `:

| Case                                                    | Message after the prefix                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Unsigned integer greater than `math.MaxInt64`           | `unsigned value <n> exceeds the INT range`          |
| Map with a non-string key type                          | `map key type <type> is not a string`               |
| Struct with no exported fields, `time.Time` among them  | `struct type <type> has no exported fields to bind` |
| Any other type: a channel, a function, a complex number | `unsupported parameter type <type>`                 |

A nested value adds its position (`item <n>`, `field "<name>"`, `key "<name>"`). A name holding a NUL byte fails with `parameter "<name>" holds an interior NUL and cannot cross the C boundary`, and a statement holding one with `statement holds an interior NUL and cannot cross the C boundary`.

properties.heading: Result
properties.text:
| Field           | Type             | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Columns`       | `[]string`       | The column names, in `RETURN` order                                                                                                                                                      |
| `Rows`          | `[][]any`        | One slice per row, cells typed as in [Values](#values)                                                                                                                                   |
| `QueryType`     | `QueryType`      | The plan-time classification; `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` report the wrapped statement's type                                                                                                |
| `Namespace`     | `Namespace`      | The statement's `USE` target, else the session namespace                                                                                                                                 |
| `Bookmark`      | `string`         | An auto-commit write's bookmark, `relate:<n>`; `""` for a read, an `EXPLAIN`, a write whose counters are all zero (it changed nothing), and any statement inside an explicit transaction |
| `Stats`         | `Stats`          | The mutation counters; all zero for a read, an `EXPLAIN` or a write that matched no rows                                                                                                 |
| `Notifications` | `[]Notification` | Filled by `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`; an empty, non-nil slice on a plain run                                                                                                                |
| `Plan`          | `*PlanDocument`  | The `relate.plan/v1` plan document under `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE`; `nil` on a plain run                                                                                                    |

A `Result` has no column types or timings. A bookmark's `<n>` grows across every connection of the store and orders as a number: as strings, `"relate:10"` sorts before `"relate:9"`.

`Stats` has 11 `int64` fields, always present: `NodesCreated`, `NodesDeleted`, `RelationshipsCreated`, `RelationshipsDeleted`, `PropertiesSet`, `LabelsAdded`, `LabelsRemoved`, `IndexesAdded`, `IndexesRemoved`, `ConstraintsAdded`, `ConstraintsRemoved`. The counting follows Neo4j: one label per node it is added to, one property per write, and schema statements in the index and constraint counters.
