properties.heading: Synopsis
Values
properties.text:
Each result cell decodes to one Go type per Cypher kind:

| Cypher kind      | Go type                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NULL`           | `nil`                                                                                                                                                     |
| `BOOLEAN`        | `bool`                                                                                                                                                    |
| `INTEGER`        | `int64`, lossless                                                                                                                                         |
| `FLOAT`          | `float64`, NaN and infinities included                                                                                                                    |
| `STRING`         | `string`, an interior NUL kept                                                                                                                            |
| `LIST`           | `[]any`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `MAP`            | `map[string]any`; Go maps keep no order                                                                                                                   |
| node             | `Node{ElementID string, ID int64, Labels []string, Properties map[string]any}`                                                                            |
| relationship     | `Relationship{ElementID, StartElementID, EndElementID string, ID, StartID, EndID int64, Type string, Properties map[string]any}`                          |
| path             | `Path`, a `[]any` alternating `Node` and `Relationship`                                                                                                   |
| `POINT`          | `Point{SRID, Dimension int32, X, Y, Z float64}`; `Z` set only when `Dimension` is 3                                                                       |
| `DATE`           | `Date{Year, Month, Day int64}`                                                                                                                            |
| `ZONED TIME`     | `Time{Hour, Minute, Second, Nanosecond, OffsetSeconds int64}`                                                                                             |
| `LOCAL TIME`     | `LocalTime{Hour, Minute, Second, Nanosecond int64}`                                                                                                       |
| `ZONED DATETIME` | `DateTime{Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Nanosecond, OffsetSeconds int64, Zone string}`; `Zone` is the zone id, or `""` for an offset-only value |
| `LOCAL DATETIME` | `LocalDateTime{Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, Second, Nanosecond int64}`                                                                                 |
| `DURATION`       | `Duration{Months, Days, Seconds, Nanos int64}`                                                                                                            |
| `VECTOR`         | `Vector{DType string, Ints []int64, Floats []float64}`; the slice of the other family is nil                                                              |
| byte array       | `[]any` of `int64`                                                                                                                                        |

A zoned value reports its local wall clock. An [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id) is the string `elementId()` returns, such as `4:rl-id:n0`, and is `""` in the `system` namespace. The `ID` fields are the deprecated numeric ids `id()` returns. A value kind the client does not know is an error, never `nil`.

properties.heading: Java API
properties.text: The Java [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) is the artifact `com.relate:relate`, package `com.relate`, for Java 17 or later. It calls the relate C library, `librelate_ffi`, through JNA (Java Native Access), and its jar carries that library; the library's C application binary interface (C ABI) is version 2. Its two dependencies are JNA and Jackson databind. Every call is synchronous, and every failure is an unchecked exception. This page describes the client of relate 1.0.1.

properties.heading: Capabilities
properties.text:
| Feature                                                                                                | Java                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| In-memory store. A store that lives only in the process.                                               | yes: `Database.open(":memory:")`                                                                                             |
| Directory store. A store in a directory on disk.                                                       | yes: `Database.open(path)`                                                                                                   |
| Single-file .rl store. A store in one `.rl` file.                                                      | yes: `Database.open("graph.rl")`                                                                                             |
| Read-only open. An open that loads the store once and refuses every write.                             | yes: `Database.openReadOnly(uri)`                                                                                            |
| Explicit transactions. Several statements committed or rolled back together.                           | yes: `begin()`, `commit()`, `rollback()`                                                                                     |
| Parameters. `$name` values passed beside the statement.                                                | yes: `query(statement, Map)`                                                                                                 |
| Column types, counters and timings. Metadata returned with each result.                                | partial: query type (a typed `QueryType`), namespace, bookmark, notifications and plan; no column types, counters or timings |
| Notifications. The engine's query notifications (for example a Cartesian product), each with a remedy. | yes: `getNotifications()`                                                                                                    |
| Arrow output. Results as Apache Arrow.                                                                 | no: no Arrow call in the client                                                                                              |
| Change data capture. Reading committed changes from a slot.                                            | no: no change-data-capture call in the client                                                                                |
| Vector search. Vector indexes and `SEARCH`.                                                            | yes: `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` and `SEARCH` through the C ABI                                                                    |
| Full-text search. Full-text indexes and their queries.                                                 | yes: `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` and full-text `SEARCH` through the C ABI                                                        |
| LOAD CSV from local files. Local `LOAD CSV` under a configured directory (denied unless one is set).   | yes: `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`, read by the C ABI's open                                                                         |
| Load a store from a URL. Opening a `.rl` store fetched over https.                                     | no: no open from a URL in the client                                                                                         |
| Agent mode. The CLI's agent defaults: the 100-row cap and the piped `toon` output.                     | no: A CLI setting                                                                                                            |

Each cell is yes, no, partial or unknown, with the call, flag or reason. Checked on 2026-11-11 against relate 1.0.0: runs of the CLI binary and `relate serve` (Bolt, HTTP and MCP), the WebAssembly build this site ships, and the Python, Node.js, C, Java, Go, Swift and Rust clients, and each surface's upstream reference. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C ABI library as the Node.js client.

properties.heading: Connection
properties.text:
`Database.Connection`, a static nested class, has these methods:

| Method                                        | Returns  | Behavior                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query(String cypher)`                        | `Result` | Runs one statement with no parameters; auto-commits outside an explicit transaction                                                                 |
| `query(String cypher, Map<String, ?> params)` | `Result` | Runs one statement with named parameters; a `null` map binds none                                                                                   |
| `setNamespace(String namespace)`              | `void`   | Changes the session namespace; refused inside a transaction                                                                                         |
| `begin()`                                     | `void`   | Opens an explicit transaction; transactions do not nest                                                                                             |
| `commit()`                                    | `String` | Commits; returns the [bookmark](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bookmark) `"relate:<n>"`, or `null` when the transaction wrote nothing |
| `rollback()`                                  | `void`   | Discards the explicit transaction                                                                                                                   |
| `close()`                                     | `void`   | Disconnects; idempotent                                                                                                                             |

Every method is `synchronized`: a connection serves one call at a time, and concurrent callers wait. A connection's own refusals, each a `ClientException` with code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` and GQLSTATUS `42000`:

| Call                                           | Message                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `begin()` inside a transaction                 | `semantic error: already in a transaction`                                                   |
| `commit()` or `rollback()` with no transaction | `semantic error: no transaction`                                                             |
| `setNamespace(…)` inside a transaction         | `semantic error: TransactionError: Cannot change the namespace while a transaction is open.` |

A failed `commit()` ends the transaction. A call on a closed connection or database throws `RelateException` with message `connection is closed` or `database is closed` and a `null` code.

properties.heading: Database
properties.text:
| Method                      | Returns      | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open(String uri)`          | `Database`   | Opens `:memory:`, a directory store or a `.rl` store for writing; creates a missing store                                                                                             |
| `openReadOnly(String uri)`  | `Database`   | Loads an existing store once; refuses writes and checkpoints; a missing store is an error                                                                                             |
| `connect()`                 | `Connection` | A connection in the `neo4j` namespace                                                                                                                                                 |
| `connect(String namespace)` | `Connection` | A connection in `neo4j`, `system` or `system_ontologies`, matched case-insensitively; `null` selects `neo4j`                                                                          |
| `checkpoint()`              | `void`       | Writes a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint), folding the write-ahead log into a fresh snapshot of committed state; refused on a read-only database |
| `close()`                   | `void`       | Closes the store; idempotent; required before the same file store opens again in this Java virtual machine (JVM)                                                                      |

A failed `open` or `openReadOnly` throws `DatabaseException` with message `internal error`, code `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, GQLSTATUS `42000` and stage `INTERNAL`, whether the store is locked by another writer or missing. An unknown namespace throws `ClientException`: `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`.

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| Class                | Thrown when                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `isRetryable()` |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `TransientException` | The engine marks the failure retryable: a write-write [conflict](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#conflict), `Neo.TransientError.Transaction.Outdated`, message `write-write conflict`, or the retryable workspace cap | `true`          |
| `ClientException`    | The code starts `Neo.ClientError.`: syntax, types, a missing parameter, an unknown namespace, a write on a read-only store                                                                                                         | `false`         |
| `DatabaseException`  | The code starts `Neo.DatabaseError.`: engine failures, a failed open, and the C boundary's `INTERNAL` stage                                                                                                                        | `false`         |
| `RelateException`    | Any other code, and the client's own failures: native loading, a closed handle, a malformed C ABI payload, such as a query type, namespace, notification severity, or category outside its enum                                    | `false`         |

Every class has these getters:

| Getter           | Returns                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getMessage()`   | The engine's message                                                                                                                                                         |
| `getCode()`      | The Neo4j status code, such as `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ArithmeticError`; `null` on a client-side failure                                                                  |
| `getGqlStatus()` | The five-character GQLSTATUS, such as `22G03`; `null` on a client-side failure                                                                                               |
| `getStage()`     | `COMPILE` (parse or plan), `RUNTIME` (execution) or `INTERNAL` (the C boundary: a poisoned handle, a caught panic, an undecodable argument); `null` on a client-side failure |
| `isRetryable()`  | `true` exactly when running the same work again can succeed                                                                                                                  |

A conflict surfaces on an auto-commit statement or on `commit()`. After an `INTERNAL` failure the handle may be poisoned; `close()` still works on it. A write on a read-only database throws `ClientException` with code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` and GQLSTATUS `42N18`. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists the engine's messages.

properties.heading: Example
Limits
properties.text: The limits come from the engine and are the same on every surface: a statement's text is at most 4194304 bytes (`syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`), one value a statement builds is bounded by the expression memory cap, and a file-backed store has one writing open across every process. [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/) lists each limit with its default and the setting that changes it.

properties.heading: Native library
properties.text:
The first use of `Database` in a JVM resolves the library once, in this order:

| Step | Source                                                                                                                   |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1    | `RELATE_LIB`, when set and not empty: a path to a library, for development                                               |
| 2    | The jar's resource `native/<key>/<library>` for the running platform, extracted to the cache and loaded by absolute path |
| 3    | Neither: the first call throws `RelateException` beginning `relate: no bundled native library for platform <key>`        |

The system library path, `java.library.path` and `jna.library.path` are never searched. The platforms:

| `os.name`, `os.arch`  | Key            | Library               | Classifier       |
| --------------------- | -------------- | --------------------- | ---------------- |
| `Mac OS X`, `aarch64` | `darwin-arm64` | `librelate_ffi.dylib` | `osx-aarch_64`   |
| `Mac OS X`, `x86_64`  | `darwin-x64`   | `librelate_ffi.dylib` | `osx-x86_64`     |
| `Linux`, `aarch64`    | `linux-arm64`  | `librelate_ffi.so`    | `linux-aarch_64` |
| `Linux`, `amd64`      | `linux-x64`    | `librelate_ffi.so`    | `linux-x86_64`   |
| `Windows*`, `amd64`   | `win32-x64`    | `relate_ffi.dll`      | `windows-x86_64` |

`arm64` and `x86_64` are accepted spellings of the same architectures. Any other platform throws `RelateException` beginning `relate: unsupported platform os.name=`. The plain jar carries all five libraries; each classifier jar carries one.

| Setting                              | Default                                                                                                                                           | Effect                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-Drelate.native.cache=<dir>`        | macOS `~/Library/Caches/relate/native`; Linux `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/relate/native` or `~/.cache/relate/native`; Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\relate\native` | The cache root; the library lands in `<root>/<version>/<key>-<first 16 hex digits of its SHA-256>/` |
| `RELATE_LIB`                         | unset                                                                                                                                             | A library path that replaces the jar's                                                              |
| `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` | off                                                                                                                                               | On Java 24 or later, silences the JVM's restricted-method warning when JNA loads                    |

The extraction writes a temporary file and renames it into place, so concurrent JVMs never load a partial file. Old versions' directories stay until removed. A library of another C ABI version throws `RelateException` beginning `incompatible librelate_ffi at <path>`. Every jar also carries the skill file `.agents/skills/relate/SKILL.md`.

properties.heading: Notifications and plans
properties.text:
`Notification` has the getters `getCode()`, `getGqlStatus()`, `getSeverity()` (a `Severity`: `INFORMATION` or `WARNING`), `getCategory()` (a `Category`: `PERFORMANCE`, `UNRECOGNIZED`, `DEPRECATION`, `SCHEMA` or `HINT`), `getTitle()`, `getDescription()`, `getRemedy()` and `getOperatorId()`, a `Long` that is `null` on a statement-scoped notification. The list follows plan pre-order, then statement-scoped entries.

The plan classes have public fields:

| Class          | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PlanDocument` | `schema` (`relate.plan/v1`), `profiled`, `statement`, `root`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `PlanNode`     | `operator`, `details`, `identifiers`, `estimatedRows`, `actual`, `children`, `warnings` (the operator's notifications)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `PlanActual`   | `rows`, `timeMs`, `totalTimeMs` (the operator's time plus its descendants'), `dbHits`, `seekMs`, `walkMs`, `loops` (a `Long`, `null` on an operator with no input clause), `memoryBytes`, `expressionBuiltBytes`, `hops`, `neighborWalks`, `nodeReads`, `batched`, `zoneSkips`, `frontier`, `frontierDecline` (`null` when the frontier never declined), `start`, `kernel` (`null` when no kernel served the walk); the whole object is `null` on an `EXPLAIN` plan |
| `PlanStart`    | `element`, `backward`, `reason`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `PlanFrontier` | `edgeVisits`, `levels`, `endpoints`, `cells`, `memoHits`, `memoMisses`, `representativeProofs`, `searchProven`, `searchDisproven`, `declinedExhausted`, `budgetFraction`; all zeros when the operator walks no frontier                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `PlanKernel`   | `rung`: `chain`, `hub-star`, `frontier-nfa` or `walker`; `hops`, a `Long` that only `chain` sets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

properties.heading: Parameters
properties.text:
`query(cypher, params)` binds each map entry as one Cypher value, with no JSON in between:

| Java type                                 | Binds as                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `null`                                    | `NULL`                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Boolean`                                 | `BOOLEAN`                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Byte`, `Short`, `Integer`, `Long`        | `INTEGER`                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `Float`, `Double`                         | `FLOAT`                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `String`                                  | `STRING`                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, `LocalDateTime` | `DATE`, `LOCAL TIME`, `LOCAL DATETIME`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `OffsetTime`                              | `ZONED TIME`                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `OffsetDateTime`, `ZonedDateTime`         | `ZONED DATETIME`; a `ZonedDateTime` keeps its zone id, one zoned at a `ZoneOffset` crosses as the offset form                                                                                                     |
| `DurationValue`                           | `DURATION`                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `java.time.Duration`                      | `DURATION` with zero months and days                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `Point`                                   | `POINT`                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `VectorValue`                             | `VECTOR`; `dtype` is one of `INTEGER8`, `INTEGER16`, `INTEGER32`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT16`, `BFLOAT16`, `FLOAT32`, `FLOAT`; coordinates must be `Long` for the `INTEGER*` dtypes and `Double` for the `FLOAT*` dtypes |
| `List`                                    | `LIST`, in order                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Map`                                     | `MAP`, nested to any depth; keys must be `String`                                                                                                                                                                 |

Any other type throws `IllegalArgumentException` before the statement runs, such as `cannot bind parameter "x": unsupported Java type java.lang.Object`. So do a vector coordinate of the wrong box type, as in `cannot bind vector parameter with dtype INTEGER8: coordinate 0 is java.lang.Integer, expected Long`, and a map key that is not a `String`, as in `cannot bind nested map parameter "m": key 1 is java.lang.Integer, expected String`. A value the engine refuses, such as an impossible date or an unknown zone, throws `RelateException` with stage `INTERNAL`. A statement that refers to a parameter the map lacks fails with `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <names>`.

properties.text:

| `Path`                                                                              | record                               | `elements`: node, relationship, …, node                                                       |
| `Point`                                                                             | record                               | `srid`, `x`, `y`, `z` (`null` on a 2D point)                                                  |
| `DurationValue`                                                                     | record                               | `months`, `days`, `seconds`, `nanos`                                                          |
| `VectorValue`                                                                       | record                               | `dtype`, `coordinates`                                                                        |
| `QueryType`                                                                         | enum                                 | `READ`, `WRITE`, `READ_WRITE`, `SCHEMA`                                                       |
| `Namespace`                                                                         | enum                                 | `NEO4J`, `SYSTEM`, `SYSTEM_ONTOLOGIES`                                                        |
| `Notification`                                                                      | final class                          | One planner notification                                                                      |
| `Severity`, `Category`                                                              | enums                                | A notification's severity and category                                                        |
| `PlanDocument`, `PlanNode`, `PlanActual`, `PlanStart`, `PlanFrontier`, `PlanKernel` | classes with public fields           | The structured plan                                                                           |
| `RelateException`                                                                   | `RuntimeException`                   | The base of every client exception                                                            |
| `TransientException`, `ClientException`, `DatabaseException`                        | subclasses of `RelateException`      | The engine's classification of a failure                                                      |
| `RelateException.Stage`                                                             | enum                                 | `COMPILE`, `RUNTIME`, `INTERNAL`                                                              |

properties.heading: Result
properties.text:
`Database.Result`, a static nested class, holds every row, copied out of the engine before `query` returns.

| Method               | Returns                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `columns()`          | The column names, in `RETURN` order                                                                                                                                                        |
| `rows()`             | One `List<Object>` per row, cells in column order, typed as in [Values](#values)                                                                                                           |
| `getQueryType()`     | A `QueryType`: `READ`, `WRITE` (a write with no columns), `READ_WRITE` (a write with columns) or `SCHEMA`; `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` report the wrapped statement's type                     |
| `getNamespace()`     | A `Namespace`: `NEO4J`, `SYSTEM` or `SYSTEM_ONTOLOGIES`; the statement's `USE` target, else the session namespace                                                                          |
| `getBookmark()`      | An auto-commit write's bookmark, `relate:<n>`; `null` for a read, an `EXPLAIN`, a write whose counters are all zero (it changed nothing), and any statement inside an explicit transaction |
| `getNotifications()` | The statement's notifications; filled by `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`, empty on a plain run                                                                                                     |
| `getPlan()`          | The `relate.plan/v1` plan document under `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE`; `null` on a plain run                                                                                                     |

`QueryType`, `Namespace`, `Severity` and `Category` each have `wire()`, the string the C ABI carries: `QueryType.READ_WRITE.wire()` is `"rw"`, `Namespace.NEO4J.wire()` is `"neo4j"`, and a `Severity` or `Category` constant's string is its name. A `Result` carries no mutation counters, column types, or timings. A bookmark's `<n>` grows across every connection of the store and orders as a number: as strings, `"relate:10"` sorts before `"relate:9"`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
Values
properties.text:
Each result cell is decoded into one Java type per Cypher kind:

| Cypher kind                            | Java type                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `NULL`                                 | `null`                                                                                                 |
| `BOOLEAN`                              | `Boolean`                                                                                              |
| `INTEGER`                              | `Long`, any 64-bit value                                                                               |
| `FLOAT`                                | `Double`, NaN and infinities included                                                                  |
| `STRING`                               | `String`, interior NUL characters kept                                                                 |
| `LIST`                                 | `List<Object>`                                                                                         |
| `MAP`                                  | `Map<String, Object>`, in engine order                                                                 |
| node                                   | `Node`                                                                                                 |
| relationship                           | `Relationship`                                                                                         |
| path                                   | `Path`, its elements alternating `Node` and `Relationship`                                             |
| `POINT`                                | `Point`; `srid` 7203 or 4326 in 2D, 9157 or 4979 in 3D                                                 |
| `DATE`, `LOCAL TIME`, `LOCAL DATETIME` | `LocalDate`, `LocalTime`, `LocalDateTime`                                                              |
| `ZONED TIME`                           | `OffsetTime`; a time keeps an offset, never a zone id                                                  |
| `ZONED DATETIME`                       | `ZonedDateTime` when the value has a zone id, `OffsetDateTime` when it has only an offset              |
| `DURATION`                             | `DurationValue`; `duration('P1Y2M')` has `months` 14                                                   |
| `VECTOR`                               | `VectorValue`; `coordinates` holds `Long` for the `INTEGER*` types and `Double` for the `FLOAT*` types |
| byte array                             | `List<Long>`, each 0 to 255                                                                            |

An [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id) is the string `elementId()` returns, such as `4:rl-id:n0`, so it round-trips through a parameter. The `long` ids are the deprecated numeric ids `id()` returns. A map key holding a NUL character, or a value kind the client does not know, throws `RelateException` instead of returning a value.

properties.heading: Node.js API
properties.text: The relate Node.js [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) is the `@relate/relate` package: it loads the engine as a native library (`librelate_ffi`, the C ABI version 2) and runs it in the calling process against a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). `query()` is synchronous and `queryAsync()` returns a Promise of the same result. The package ships TypeScript types in `index.d.ts`; the signatures on this page are read from those types and the package source, and checked against `@relate/relate` 1.0.1 on Node.js 26; the package requires Node.js 18 or later.

properties.heading: Capabilities
properties.text:
| Feature                                                                                                | Node.js                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| In-memory store. A store that lives only in the process.                                               | yes: `Database.open(":memory:")`                                                                                  |
| Directory store. A store in a directory on disk.                                                       | yes: `Database.open(path)`                                                                                        |
| Single-file .rl store. A store in one `.rl` file.                                                      | yes: `Database.open("graph.rl")`                                                                                  |
| Read-only open. An open that loads the store once and refuses every write.                             | yes: `Database.open(uri, { readOnly: true })`                                                                     |
| Explicit transactions. Several statements committed or rolled back together.                           | yes: `begin()`, `commit()`, `rollback()`                                                                          |
| Parameters. `$name` values passed beside the statement.                                                | yes: `query(statement, { x: 3 })`                                                                                 |
| Column types, counters and timings. Metadata returned with each result.                                | partial: counters, query type, elapsed and its phase split; no per-column type list (each value carries its type) |
| Notifications. The engine's query notifications (for example a Cartesian product), each with a remedy. | yes: `result.notifications`                                                                                       |
| Arrow output. Results as Apache Arrow.                                                                 | no: no Arrow call in the client                                                                                   |
| Change data capture. Reading committed changes from a slot.                                            | no: no change-data-capture call in the client                                                                     |
| Vector search. Vector indexes and `SEARCH`.                                                            | yes: `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` and `SEARCH`                                                                           |
| Full-text search. Full-text indexes and their queries.                                                 | yes: `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` and full-text `SEARCH`                                                               |
| LOAD CSV from local files. Local `LOAD CSV` under a configured directory (denied unless one is set).   | yes: `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`                                                                                        |
| Load a store from a URL. Opening a `.rl` store fetched over https.                                     | no: no open from a URL in the client                                                                              |
| Agent mode. The CLI's agent defaults: the 100-row cap and the piped `toon` output.                     | no: A CLI setting                                                                                                 |

Each cell is yes, no, partial or unknown, with the call, flag or reason. Checked on 2026-11-11 against relate 1.0.0: runs of the CLI binary and `relate serve` (Bolt, HTTP and MCP), the WebAssembly build this site ships, and the Python, Node.js, C, Java, Go, Swift and Rust clients, and each surface's upstream reference. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C ABI library as the Node.js client.

properties.heading: Connection
properties.text:
| Member                                                           | Returns           | Behavior                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query(cypher: string, params?: { [name: string]: ParamValue })` | `Result`          | Runs one statement; auto-commit unless `begin()` is open                                                                                             |
| `` query`…${value}…` ``                                          | `Result`          | The tagged-template form: each interpolated value becomes a parameter `$p0`, `$p1`, …; the same primitive value twice maps to one parameter          |
| `queryAsync(cypher, params?)`, `` queryAsync`…` ``               | `Promise<Result>` | The same, on a worker thread; calls on one connection run one at a time, in order                                                                    |
| `begin()`                                                        | `void`            | Opens an explicit transaction; a second `begin()` throws `semantic error: already in a transaction`                                                  |
| `commit()`                                                       | `string \| null`  | Commits and returns the bookmark, `relate:<n>`; `null` when the transaction wrote nothing. Without a transaction: `semantic error: no transaction`   |
| `rollback()`                                                     | `void`            | Discards the transaction. Without one: `semantic error: no transaction`                                                                              |
| `setNamespace(name: string)`                                     | `void`            | Changes the session namespace between transactions; inside one it throws a message ending `Cannot change the namespace while a transaction is open.` |

While a `queryAsync()` is in flight, `query`, `begin`, `commit`, `rollback` and `setNamespace` on the same connection throw `RelateError: a synchronous <call> cannot start while an async query is in flight on this connection`, with `code`, `gqlStatus` and `stage` `null`. A synchronous call in the same tick as `queryAsync()` runs first, because the async statement starts on the next microtask.

properties.heading: Database
properties.text:
| Member                                                         | Returns      | Behavior                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Database.open(uri: string, options?: { readOnly?: boolean })` | `Database`   | Opens a store; see [Open options](#open-options)                                        |
| `db.connect(namespace?: string)`                               | `Connection` | A new connection; `"neo4j"` (default), `"system"` or `"system_ontologies"`, in any case |
| `db.checkpoint()`                                              | `void`       | Writes the current state to the snapshot                                                |

There is no close method. Each statement is durable when `query()` returns; the store stays open until the process exits.

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| Thrown                 | When                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RelateError`          | Every failure the engine reports, from `open`, `connect`, `query`, `queryAsync` (as a rejection), `begin`, `commit`, `rollback`, `setNamespace` and `checkpoint`                                      | `message`, `code` (the Neo4j status code), `gqlStatus` (the GQLSTATUS code), `stage` (`"compile"`, `"runtime"` or `"internal"`), `retryable`, and `isRetriable` (the same as `retryable`) |
| `TypeError`            | A wrong argument shape, or a parameter the client cannot convert                                                                                                                                      | `message`: one of the [`TypeError` messages](#value-mapping), naming the value's path where there is one                                                                                  |
| `ResultNotSingleError` | `result.single()` with zero or several rows                                                                                                                                                           | `message`, `rowCount`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `Error`                | The library is missing or has another ABI version, at `require` time; or the library sent a malformed error shape, or a query type or namespace outside the fixed values (`ABI contract violated: …`) | `message`                                                                                                                                                                                 |

`retryable` is `true` only when re-running the same work can succeed, such as after a write-write conflict, which can surface on a statement or on `commit()`. A `stage` of `"internal"` marks a failure outside the statement. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists every engine message with its codes.

properties.heading: Example
Exports
properties.text:
| Export                                                                                                                                  | Kind            | What it is                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `Database`                                                                                                                              | class           | An open store                            |
| `Connection`                                                                                                                            | class           | Runs statements in one session namespace |
| `Result`, `ResultSummary`, `ResultGraph`                                                                                                | classes         | What a statement returns                 |
| `RelateError`                                                                                                                           | class           | The error every engine failure throws    |
| `ResultNotSingleError`                                                                                                                  | class           | Thrown by `result.single()`              |
| `CypherFloat`, `float(value)`                                                                                                           | class, function | A number bound as `FLOAT`                |
| `CypherDate`, `CypherTime`, `CypherLocalTime`, `CypherDateTime`, `CypherLocalDateTime`, `CypherDuration`, `CypherPoint`, `CypherVector` | classes         | Typed values for parameters and results  |

The types file also exports the TypeScript types `QueryType`, `Namespace`, `Int64`, `NodeValue`, `RelationshipValue`, `PathValue`, `Row`, `Stats`, `Notification`, `PlanDocument`, `PlanNode`, `PlanStartReason`, `PlanActual` and `ParamValue`.

properties.heading: Limits
properties.text:
| Limit                                | Value                              | When exceeded                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Integer parameter                    | A signed 64-bit integer            | `TypeError: query params: <path> is an integer outside the int64 range`                              |
| Statement text                       | 4194304 bytes                      | `RelateError: syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes` |
| One value a statement builds         | The engine's expression memory cap | `RelateError: This statement tried to build a single value of <size>. …`                             |
| Writing opens of a file-backed store | One                                | `RelateError` from `Database.open()`: `internal error`                                               |
| Calls in flight per connection       | One; `queryAsync()` calls queue    | A synchronous call during an async one throws                                                        |

properties.heading: Loading
properties.text:
`require("@relate/relate")` finds the library in this order: the path in `RELATE_LIB`; the platform package `@relate/relate-<platform>-<arch>` that npm installs as an optional dependency (`darwin-arm64`, `darwin-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `win32-x64`); then a source checkout's build directories. It then checks the library's ABI version.

| Failure at `require` time            | Error message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No library found                     | `librelate_ffi not found; looked in (1) the RELATE_LIB environment variable, (2) the platform package @relate/relate-<platform>-<arch> (lib/ directory), (3) the repo target/debug and target/release directories. Set RELATE_LIB to the library path.` |
| A library with another ABI version   | `incompatible librelate_ffi: ABI version <n>; this client requires 2`                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| A library without the version symbol | `incompatible librelate_ffi: no relate_abi_version symbol (the library predates the ABI version symbol); this client requires ABI v2`                                                                                                                   |

properties.heading: Open options
properties.text:
| Option     | Default  | Accepted values                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `uri`      | required | `":memory:"`; a directory path (a directory store); a path ending in `.rl` (a single-file store). A missing store is created, unless `readOnly` is set |
| `readOnly` | `false`  | `true` loads the store once and refuses writes and checkpoints; a missing store throws                                                                 |

| Environment variable     | Effect                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_LIB`             | The library path, checked first at `require` time                                                                     |
| `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` | The codec of a new, empty directory store: `parquet` (default), `json` or `markdown`; an existing store keeps its own |
| `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`    | The directory local `LOAD CSV` may read                                                                               |

A file-backed store has one writing open at a time. A directory store also opens `readOnly: true` beside its writer; a `.rl` store does not. A failed open throws a `RelateError` whose message is `internal error`, with `stage` `"internal"`, `gqlStatus` `42000` and `code` `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`; the message does not say whether the store was locked or missing.

properties.heading: Result
properties.text:
A `Result` holds every row from the moment `query()` returns.

| Member          | Type                                         | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`       | `string[]`                                   | Column names in `RETURN` order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `rows`          | `Row[]`                                      | Rows as objects keyed by column name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `stats`         | `Stats`                                      | The 11 mutation counters, zeros included: `nodes_created`, `nodes_deleted`, `relationships_created`, `relationships_deleted`, `properties_set`, `labels_added`, `labels_removed`, `indexes_added`, `indexes_removed`, `constraints_added`, `constraints_removed`                         |
| `queryType`     | `"r" \| "w" \| "rw" \| "s"`                  | A read, a write with no columns, a write that returns columns, a schema statement; `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` report the wrapped statement's type                                                                                                                                           |
| `namespace`     | `"neo4j" \| "system" \| "system_ontologies"` | The namespace the statement ran in: its `USE` target, else the session namespace                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `bookmark`      | `string \| null`                             | An auto-commit write's bookmark, `relate:<n>`; `null` for a read, an `EXPLAIN`, a write whose counters are all zero (it changed nothing), and any statement inside an explicit transaction                                                                                               |
| `notifications` | `Notification[]`                             | `[]` on a plain run; filled by `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`. Keys: `code`, `gql_status`, `severity` (`INFORMATION` or `WARNING`), `category` (`PERFORMANCE`, `UNRECOGNIZED`, `DEPRECATION`, `SCHEMA` or `HINT`), `title`, `description`, `remedy`, and `operator_id` on operator-scoped kinds |
| `plan`          | `PlanDocument \| null`                       | `null` on a plain run; for `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`, a `relate.plan/v1` document with `schema`, `profiled`, `statement` and `root`                                                                                                                                                        |
| `single()`      | `Row`                                        | The one row; zero or several throw `ResultNotSingleError: expected exactly one row, got <n>`, with `rowCount`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `consume()`     | `ResultSummary`                              | The summary; repeated calls return the same object                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `graph()`       | `ResultGraph`                                | The distinct nodes and relationships in the rows, nested values included                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

| `ResultSummary` field                                         | Type           | Meaning                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `counters`                                                    | `Stats`        | As `result.stats`                                                 |
| `namespace`, `queryType`, `bookmark`, `notifications`, `plan` | as on `Result` | As on `Result`                                                    |
| `elapsedMs`                                                   | `number`       | Engine time for parse, plan and run, in milliseconds              |
| `parseMs`, `planMs`, `executeMs`                              | `number`       | The three phases of `elapsedMs`; their sum is at most `elapsedMs` |

| `ResultGraph` member | Type                  | Meaning                                                               |
| -------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nodes`              | `NodeValue[]`         | Distinct nodes, in the order the rows first carry them, by element id |
| `relationships`      | `RelationshipValue[]` | Distinct relationships, in the same order                             |
| `size`               | `number`              | Nodes plus relationships                                              |
