properties.heading: Staged runs
properties.text:
Upstream documents these entry points for network transports, which report planning failures and execution failures at different points; relate's Bolt server is their in-tree user.

| Item                                                                       | Contract                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Connection::query_staged(cypher, params, CancelToken, Option<Heartbeat>)` | `Err` for a failure before execution (parse, planning, a missing parameter); `Ok(Executed::Rows(QueryResult))` for a finished result; `Ok(Executed::Failed(ExecutionFailure))` for a failure while executing, with the planned `header` and the `error`. `Executed::into_result()` gives the `query` shape. |
| `Connection::commit_with_heartbeat(Heartbeat)`                             | `commit()`, ticking the heartbeat on the calling thread while the flush runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `Heartbeat::every(interval, tick)`                                         | A callback run once per elapsed `interval` while a statement or commit runs on the query worker; a zero interval fails with `semantic error: heartbeat interval must be non-zero`                                                                                                                           |

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
use relate::{Database, OpenOptions, Value};

Database::open(uri) -> Result<Database>
Database::open_with(uri, OpenOptions) -> Result<Database>
Database::clone(source, dest, CloneOptions) -> Result<()>
db.connect() -> Result<Connection>
conn.query(cypher) -> Result<QueryResult>
conn.query_with_params(cypher, BTreeMap<String, Value>) -> Result<QueryResult>
conn.begin() -> Result<()>
conn.commit() -> Result<Option<String>>
conn.rollback() -> Result<()>
relate::error_info(&Error) -> ErrorInfo
```

`relate::Result<T>` is `std::result::Result<T, relate::Error>`. A `uri` is `":memory:"`, a filesystem path or a `file://` URI: a path ending in `.rl` (or the legacy `.cl`) is a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store), any other path a directory store. An `s3://` URI is refused at open.

properties.heading: Value
properties.text:
A parameter or a result cell. `Value` is `Send`, `Sync` and `Clone`; strings, lists, maps, vectors and byte arrays share their payload behind an `Arc`, so a clone never copies it.

| Variant                                                                                   | Cypher type                                                                                       | Column type    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `Null`                                                                                    | `null`                                                                                            | `ANY`          |
| `Bool(bool)`                                                                              | `BOOLEAN`                                                                                         | `BOOLEAN`      |
| `Int(i64)`                                                                                | `INTEGER`                                                                                         | `INTEGER`      |
| `Float(f64)`                                                                              | `FLOAT`                                                                                           | `FLOAT`        |
| `String(Arc<str>)`                                                                        | `STRING`                                                                                          | `STRING`       |
| `List(Arc<Vec<Value>>)`                                                                   | `LIST`                                                                                            | `LIST`         |
| `Map(Arc<BTreeMap<String, Value>>)`                                                       | `MAP`                                                                                             | `MAP`          |
| `Node(Arc<Node>)`                                                                         | `NODE`: `id`, `labels`, `properties`                                                              | `NODE`         |
| `Relationship(Arc<Relationship>)`                                                         | `RELATIONSHIP`: `id`, `start`, `end`, `rel_type`, `properties`                                    | `RELATIONSHIP` |
| `Path(Arc<Path>)`                                                                         | `PATH`: `nodes`, `rels`                                                                           | `PATH`         |
| `Temporal(Temporal::Date)`                                                                | `DATE`                                                                                            | `DATE`         |
| `Temporal(Temporal::Time { time, offset })`, `Temporal(Temporal::LocalTime)`              | `ZONED TIME`, `LOCAL TIME`                                                                        | `TIME`         |
| `Temporal(Temporal::DateTime { utc, offset, zone })`, `Temporal(Temporal::LocalDateTime)` | `ZONED DATETIME`, `LOCAL DATETIME`                                                                | `DATETIME`     |
| `Temporal(Temporal::Duration { months, days, nanos })`                                    | `DURATION`                                                                                        | `DURATION`     |
| `Point(PointValue)`                                                                       | `POINT`: `srid`, `x`, `y`, `z`                                                                    | `POINT`        |
| `Vector { coord, values }`                                                                | `VECTOR`                                                                                          | `VECTOR`       |
| `Uuid(u128)`                                                                              | A UUID; `column_types` reports it as `STRING`                                                     | `STRING`       |
| `Bytes(Arc<[u8]>)`                                                                        | A byte array; it enters only as a parameter, and storing it as a property fails with a type error | `BINARY`       |

`Temporal::CivilDate` and `Temporal::CivilDateTime` hold dates outside the range of the standard date types. `node_element_id`, `rel_element_id`, `parse_node_element_id` and `parse_rel_element_id` convert between numeric ids and [element ids](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id), the strings `elementId()` returns.

properties.heading: Swift API
properties.text: The Swift [client](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#client) is the package `Relate`, from the repository `github.com/relatedb/relate`, for iOS 16 or later and macOS 13 or later in the Swift 6 language mode. It is a Swift layer over the relate C library, linked in as the static XCFramework `RelateFFI`, whose C application binary interface (C ABI) is version 2: values cross through the library's typed value walker and parameter builder, with no JSON. Every call is synchronous and throws `RelateError`. This page describes the package of relate 1.0.1.

properties.heading: Capabilities
properties.text:
| Feature                                                                                                | Swift                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| In-memory store. A store that lives only in the process.                                               | yes: `Database.inMemory()`                                                      |
| Directory store. A store in a directory on disk.                                                       | yes: `Database(path:)`                                                          |
| Single-file .rl store. A store in one `.rl` file.                                                      | yes: `Database(path: "graph.rl")`                                               |
| Read-only open. An open that loads the store once and refuses every write.                             | yes: `Database(readOnlyPath:)`                                                  |
| Explicit transactions. Several statements committed or rolled back together.                           | yes: `begin()`, `commit()`, `rollback()`, `transaction { }`                     |
| Parameters. `$name` values passed beside the statement.                                                | yes: `query(statement, [String: CypherValue])`                                  |
| Column types, counters and timings. Metadata returned with each result.                                | partial: `stats`, `elapsedMs` and its phase split, `queryType`; no column types |
| Notifications. The engine's query notifications (for example a Cartesian product), each with a remedy. | yes: `notifications`                                                            |
| Arrow output. Results as Apache Arrow.                                                                 | no: no Arrow call in the client                                                 |
| Change data capture. Reading committed changes from a slot.                                            | no: no change-data-capture call in the client                                   |
| Vector search. Vector indexes and `SEARCH`.                                                            | yes: `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` and `SEARCH` through the C ABI                       |
| Full-text search. Full-text indexes and their queries.                                                 | yes: `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` and full-text `SEARCH` through the C ABI           |
| LOAD CSV from local files. Local `LOAD CSV` under a configured directory (denied unless one is set).   | yes: `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`, read by the C ABI's open                            |
| Load a store from a URL. Opening a `.rl` store fetched over https.                                     | no: no open from a URL in the client                                            |
| Agent mode. The CLI's agent defaults: the 100-row cap and the piped `toon` output.                     | no: A CLI setting                                                               |

Each cell is yes, no, partial or unknown, with the call, flag or reason. Checked on 2026-11-11 against relate 1.0.0: runs of the CLI binary and `relate serve` (Bolt, HTTP and MCP), the WebAssembly build this site ships, and the Python, Node.js, C, Java, Go, Swift and Rust clients, and each surface's upstream reference. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C ABI library as the Node.js client.

properties.heading: Concurrency
properties.text:
| Rule                           | Detail                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Database` is `Sendable`       | One database may be shared across tasks and actors                                                                  |
| `Connection` is not `Sendable` | The Swift 6 compiler refuses code that shares one between isolation domains; concurrent work opens more connections |
| Calls block                    | Every call is synchronous while the engine runs                                                                     |
| Errors travel with the call    | A call from any task reports its own error; nothing depends on the calling thread                                   |
| One writer per store           | Only one process holds a store writable at a time                                                                   |

properties.heading: Connection
properties.text:
| Member             | Behavior                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query(_:_:)`      | Runs one statement; auto-commits outside an explicit transaction; an empty dictionary binds no parameters                                          |
| `setNamespace(_:)` | Changes the session namespace; refused inside a transaction                                                                                        |
| `begin()`          | Opens an explicit transaction; transactions do not nest                                                                                            |
| `commit()`         | Commits; returns the [bookmark](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bookmark) `"relate:<n>"`, or `nil` when the transaction wrote nothing |
| `rollback()`       | Discards the explicit transaction                                                                                                                  |
| `transaction(_:)`  | Begins, runs the body, and commits when it returns; when the body or the commit throws, rolls back and rethrows that error                         |

A `Connection` disconnects when it is released. Its own refusals, each `.engine` with code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` and GQLSTATUS `42000`:

| Call                                           | Message                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `begin()` inside a transaction                 | `semantic error: already in a transaction`                                                   |
| `commit()` or `rollback()` with no transaction | `semantic error: no transaction`                                                             |
| `setNamespace(_:)` inside a transaction        | `semantic error: TransactionError: Cannot change the namespace while a transaction is open.` |

properties.heading: Database
properties.text:
| Member                | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init(path:)`         | Opens `:memory:`, a directory store or a `.rl` store for writing; creates a missing store                                                                                             |
| `init(readOnlyPath:)` | Loads an existing store once; refuses writes and checkpoints; a missing store is an error                                                                                             |
| `inMemory()`          | `Database(path: ":memory:")`                                                                                                                                                          |
| `path`, `isReadOnly`  | The path the database was opened with, and whether it is read-only                                                                                                                    |
| `connect()`           | A connection in the `neo4j` namespace                                                                                                                                                 |
| `connect(namespace:)` | A connection in `neo4j`, `system` or `system_ontologies`, matched case-insensitively; `nil` selects `neo4j`                                                                           |
| `checkpoint()`        | Writes a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint), folding the write-ahead log into a fresh snapshot of committed state; refused on a read-only database |

A `Database` closes its [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) when its last reference is released; there is no `close()`. Every `Connection` keeps its `database`, so the store outlives its connections. A failed open throws `.engine` with message `internal error`, code `Neo.DatabaseError.General.UnknownError`, GQLSTATUS `42000` and stage `.internal`, whether the store is locked by another writer or missing. An unknown namespace throws `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`.

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| `RelateError` case          | Thrown when                                                                                                                                                                            | `description`                         |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `.engine(EngineError)`      | The engine or the C boundary refused the call                                                                                                                                          | `Relate: [<code>] <message>`          |
| `.invalidParameter(String)` | A parameter cannot cross the C boundary                                                                                                                                                | `Relate invalid parameter: <message>` |
| `.decoding(String)`         | A result broke the C contract, such as a query type or namespace outside its enum (`ABI contract violated: query type '<value>'`), or `scalar()` met other than one row and one column | `Relate decoding error: <message>`    |

`error.message` is the message of any case and `error.engineError` the `EngineError` of the `.engine` case, else `nil`.

| `EngineError` property | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`                 | The Neo4j status code, such as `Neo.ClientError.Statement.ArithmeticError`                                                                                                                     |
| `gqlStatus`            | The five-character GQLSTATUS, such as `22G03`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `stage`                | `.compile` (parse or plan), `.runtime` (execution) or `.internal` (the C boundary: a poisoned handle, a caught panic, a refused argument)                                                      |
| `retryable`            | `true` exactly when running the same work again can succeed: a write-write conflict (`Neo.TransientError.Transaction.Outdated`, message `write-write conflict`) or the retryable workspace cap |
| `message`              | The engine's message                                                                                                                                                                           |

A statement failure throws from `query`; a conflict in an explicit transaction throws from `commit()`. After a `.internal` failure the handle may be poisoned: later calls throw `.internal` too, and only a new handle recovers. A write on a read-only database throws code `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError` with GQLSTATUS `42N18`. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists the engine's messages.

properties.heading: Example
properties.text:
This program writes two `Person` nodes and a `KNOWS` relationship to an in-memory store and prints the `CypherValue` kind of each returned value:

```swift run name=values
import Relate

let conn = try Database.inMemory().connect()
let result = try conn.query("""
    CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[k:KNOWS {since: 2024}]->(grace:Person {name: 'Grace'})
    RETURN ada, k, 9007199254740993 AS big, 1.5 AS ratio, date('2024-05-06') AS day,
           datetime('2024-05-06T09:30:00[Europe/Berlin]') AS meeting, duration('P1Y2M') AS term,
           point({x: 1, y: 2}) AS spot, vector([1, 2, 3], 3, INT8) AS counts
    """)
for (column, value) in zip(result.columns, result.rows[0]) {
    print("\(column): \(value.kind) \(value)")
}
```

```text
ada: node (4:rl-id:n0:Person {name: 'Ada'})
k: relationship (4:rl-id:n0)-[5:rl-id:r0:KNOWS {since: 2024}]->(4:rl-id:n1)
big: int 9007199254740993
ratio: float 1.5
day: date 2024-05-06
meeting: dateTime 2024-05-06T09:30:00+02:00[Europe/Berlin]
term: duration duration(months: 14, days: 0, seconds: 0, nanoseconds: 0)
spot: point point({srid: 7203, x: 1.0, y: 2.0})
counts: vector vector<INTEGER8>[1, 2, 3]
```

properties.heading: Limits
properties.text: The limits come from the engine and are the same on every surface: a statement's text is at most 4194304 bytes (`syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`), one value a statement builds is bounded by the expression memory cap, and a file-backed store has one writing open across every process. [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/) lists each limit with its default and the setting that changes it.

properties.heading: Notifications and plans
properties.text:
`Notification` has the properties `code`, `gqlStatus`, `severity`, a `Severity` (`.information` or `.warning`, raw values `INFORMATION` and `WARNING`), `category`, a `Category` (`.performance`, `.unrecognized`, `.deprecation`, `.schema` or `.hint`, raw values the upper-case names), `title`, `description`, `remedy` and `operatorId`, an `Int64?` that is `nil` on a statement-scoped notification. A severity or category outside those cases, or a missing one, is a `.decoding` error that begins `ABI contract violated:` and names the key and the value.

| Struct         | Properties                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PlanDocument` | `schema` (`relate.plan/v1`), `profiled`, `statement: String?`, `root: PlanNode`                                                  |
| `PlanNode`     | `operator`, `details`, `identifiers`, `estimatedRows: Int64?`, `actual: PlanActual?`, `children`, `warnings: [Notification]`     |
| `PlanActual`   | `rows`, `timeMs`, `dbHits`, `memoryBytes`, `hops`, `neighborWalks`, `nodeReads`, `start: PlanStart?`; `nil` on an `EXPLAIN` plan |
| `PlanStart`    | `element`, `backward`, `reason`                                                                                                  |

properties.heading: Parameters
properties.text:
`query(_:_:)` binds each dictionary entry as one value. `CypherValue` conforms to `ExpressibleByNilLiteral`, `…BooleanLiteral`, `…IntegerLiteral`, `…FloatLiteral`, `…StringLiteral`, `…ArrayLiteral` and `…DictionaryLiteral`, so `["n": 1, "tags": ["a"], "m": ["k": true]]` needs no wrapping. A variable binds through `CypherValue(_:)` for `Int`, `Double`, `String` and `Bool`; the struct payloads of the point, temporal, duration and vector cases have public initializers. Non-finite floats and every `Int64` value bind directly.

| Refusal                                                                                                            | Error                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A `.node`, `.relationship` or `.path` value                                                                        | `.invalidParameter`: `nodes, relationships and paths cannot be passed as parameters; pass their element id or properties` |
| A statement, path, namespace, parameter name or map key holding a NUL byte                                         | `.invalidParameter`: `<what> contains a NUL byte`                                                                         |
| A value the engine's builder refuses: an impossible date, an unknown zone, a srid that does not fit the dimensions | `.engine` with stage `.internal`                                                                                          |
| A parameter the statement refers to and the dictionary lacks                                                       | `.engine`: `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <names>`                                             |

properties.heading: QueryResult
properties.text:
A `QueryResult` is a plain value, copied out of the engine before `query` returns.

| Member                           | Type                      | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`                        | `[String]`                | The column names, in `RETURN` order                                                                                                                                                       |
| `rows`                           | `[[CypherValue]]`         | One array per row, cells in column order                                                                                                                                                  |
| `records`                        | `[[String: CypherValue]]` | The rows keyed by column name; for a repeated name, the last column's value                                                                                                               |
| `scalar()`                       | `CypherValue`             | The one value of a one-row, one-column result; otherwise throws `.decoding`                                                                                                               |
| `queryType`                      | `QueryType`               | The plan-time classification; `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` report the wrapped statement's type                                                                                                 |
| `namespace`                      | `Namespace`               | The statement's `USE` target, else the session namespace                                                                                                                                  |
| `bookmark`                       | `String?`                 | An auto-commit write's bookmark, `relate:<n>`; `nil` for a read, an `EXPLAIN`, a write whose counters are all zero (it changed nothing), and any statement inside an explicit transaction |
| `stats`                          | `QueryStats`              | The mutation counters; all zero for a read or an `EXPLAIN`                                                                                                                                |
| `notifications`                  | `[Notification]`          | Filled by `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`; empty on a plain run                                                                                                                                   |
| `plan`                           | `PlanDocument?`           | The `relate.plan/v1` plan document under `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE`; `nil` on a plain run                                                                                                     |
| `elapsedMs`                      | `Double`                  | The engine's parse, plan and execute time, in milliseconds                                                                                                                                |
| `parseMs`, `planMs`, `executeMs` | `Double`                  | The phases of `elapsedMs`; their sum never exceeds it                                                                                                                                     |

A `QueryResult` has no column types. `QueryStats` has 11 `Int` properties: `nodesCreated`, `nodesDeleted`, `relationshipsCreated`, `relationshipsDeleted`, `propertiesSet`, `labelsAdded`, `labelsRemoved`, `indexesAdded`, `indexesRemoved`, `constraintsAdded`, `constraintsRemoved`. A bookmark's `<n>` grows across every connection of the store and orders as a number: as strings, `"relate:10"` sorts before `"relate:9"`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
Values
properties.text:
Every cell, and every element of a list or map, is a `CypherValue` that keeps its kind at any depth:

| Case             | Cypher kind      | Payload                                                                                                       |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.null`          | `NULL`           |                                                                                                               |
| `.bool`          | `BOOLEAN`        | `Bool`                                                                                                        |
| `.int`           | `INTEGER`        | `Int64`                                                                                                       |
| `.float`         | `FLOAT`          | `Double`, NaN and infinities included                                                                         |
| `.string`        | `STRING`         | `String`, interior NUL characters kept                                                                        |
| `.list`          | `LIST`           | `[CypherValue]`                                                                                               |
| `.map`           | `MAP`            | `[String: CypherValue]`; a map shaped like a node stays `.map`                                                |
| `.node`          | node             | `Node`: `id`, `elementId`, `labels`, `properties`                                                             |
| `.relationship`  | relationship     | `Relationship`: `id`, `elementId`, `type`, `startId`, `endId`, `startElementId`, `endElementId`, `properties` |
| `.path`          | path             | `Path`: `nodes`, `relationships`, with one more node than relationships                                       |
| `.point`         | `POINT`          | `Point`: `srid`, `x`, `y`, `z` (`nil` in 2D); `x` and `y` are longitude and latitude for srid 4326 and 4979   |
| `.date`          | `DATE`           | `Date`: `year`, `month`, `day`                                                                                |
| `.time`          | `ZONED TIME`     | `Time`: `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `nanosecond`, `offsetSeconds`                                             |
| `.localTime`     | `LOCAL TIME`     | `LocalTime`: `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `nanosecond`                                                         |
| `.dateTime`      | `ZONED DATETIME` | `DateTime`: the date and time parts, `offsetSeconds`, `zone` (`nil` for an offset-only value)                 |
| `.localDateTime` | `LOCAL DATETIME` | `LocalDateTime`: the date and time parts                                                                      |
| `.duration`      | `DURATION`       | `Duration`: `months`, `days`, `seconds`, `nanoseconds`                                                        |
| `.vector`        | `VECTOR`         | `Vector`: `.floats(dtype:values:)` or `.ints(dtype:values:)`                                                  |

`Vector.DType` has the cases `.integer8`, `.integer16`, `.integer32`, `.integer`, `.float16`, `.bfloat16`, `.float32` and `.float`, whose raw values are the engine's names (`INTEGER8` … `FLOAT`). UUIDs arrive as `.string`, byte arrays as a `.list` of `.int`. An [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id) is the string `elementId()` returns, such as `4:rl-id:n0`; the `Int64` ids are the deprecated numeric ids `id()` returns. A value kind the package does not know throws `.decoding`.

| Accessor                                                                                                          | Returns                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `kind`                                                                                                            | The `CypherValueKind`                                                    |
| `isNull`                                                                                                          | `true` for `.null`                                                       |
| `boolValue`, `intValue`, `stringValue`, `listValue`, `mapValue`                                                   | The payload, or `nil` for another case                                   |
| `doubleValue`                                                                                                     | A `.float`, or an `.int` widened to `Double`                             |
| `nodeValue`, `relationshipValue`, `pathValue`, `pointValue`                                                       | The graph or spatial payload, or `nil`                                   |
| `dateValue`, `timeValue`, `localTimeValue`, `dateTimeValue`, `localDateTimeValue`, `durationValue`, `vectorValue` | The temporal or vector payload, or `nil`                                 |
| `subscript(key:)`                                                                                                 | A map entry, or a node or relationship property; `nil` otherwise         |
| `description`                                                                                                     | A Cypher-like rendering for logs, map keys sorted; not a format to parse |

properties.heading: WebAssembly API
properties.text: The `@relate/relate-wasm` package is relate compiled to WebAssembly (WASM) for the browser: an ES module, `relate.js`, that loads the engine from `relate_bg.wasm` and exports one class, `RelateDb`. A `RelateDb` is one [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), in memory or in the Origin Private File System (OPFS), with one connection. Each [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) returns its result as the [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope), JSON text. This page describes the build this site ships in `public/wasm/`, the engine behind its cells, the cookbook and the playground; its `relate.d.ts` is the source of the signatures.

properties.heading: Capabilities
properties.text:
The capability matrix, narrowed to this surface:

| Feature                                                                                                | Browser (WASM)                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| In-memory store. A store that lives only in the process.                                               | yes: `new RelateDb()`                                                                                         |
| Directory store. A store in a directory on disk.                                                       | no: no filesystem paths; `RelateDb.open("opfs://<name>")` is the durable browser store, in a dedicated worker |
| Single-file .rl store. A store in one `.rl` file.                                                      | no: opens `:memory:` and `opfs://` only                                                                       |
| Read-only open. An open that loads the store once and refuses every write.                             | yes: `new RelateDb(true)`                                                                                     |
| Explicit transactions. Several statements committed or rolled back together.                           | no: each statement commits on its own; `BEGIN` is a syntax error                                              |
| Parameters. `$name` values passed beside the statement.                                                | yes: `execute(statement, paramsJson)`                                                                         |
| Column types, counters and timings. Metadata returned with each result.                                | yes: `columnTypes`, `stats`, `elapsed_ms` and its phase split, `plan_cache` in the envelope                   |
| Notifications. The engine's query notifications (for example a Cartesian product), each with a remedy. | yes: `notifications` in the envelope; filled on `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`                                       |
| Arrow output. Results as Apache Arrow.                                                                 | no: no Arrow call in the package                                                                              |
| Change data capture. Reading committed changes from a slot.                                            | no: `CALL db.cdc.current()` is `ProcedureNotFound`                                                            |
| Vector search. Vector indexes and `SEARCH`.                                                            | yes: `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` and `SEARCH`                                                                       |
| Full-text search. Full-text indexes and their queries.                                                 | yes: `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` and full-text `SEARCH`                                                           |
| LOAD CSV from local files. Local `LOAD CSV` under a configured directory (denied unless one is set).   | no: no CSV directory can be set; a local file is `LOAD CSV file unavailable`                                  |
| Load a store from a URL. Opening a `.rl` store fetched over https.                                     | no: opens `:memory:` and `opfs://` only                                                                       |
| Agent mode. The CLI's agent defaults: the 100-row cap and the piped `toon` output.                     | no: A CLI setting                                                                                             |

Each cell is yes, no, partial or unknown, with the call, flag or reason. Checked on 2026-11-11 against relate 1.0.0: runs of the CLI binary and `relate serve` (Bolt, HTTP and MCP), the WebAssembly build this site ships, and the Python, Node.js, C, Java, Go, Swift and Rust clients, and each surface's upstream reference. The C, Java, Go and Swift clients load the same C ABI library as the Node.js client.

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
Thrown errors are `Error` objects; statement errors arrive in the envelope instead.

| Call                       | Message                                                                                                                                                                 | When                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `init`                     | `failed to fetch Wasm: <status> <statusText> fetching '<url>'`                                                                                                          | `relate_bg.wasm` answered with a non-2xx status, such as `404 Not Found` when the file was not copied beside `relate.js` |
| `RelateDb.open`            | `storage error: OPFS needs a dedicated worker`                                                                                                                          | Called outside a dedicated worker                                                                                        |
| `RelateDb.open`            | `OPFS name must be 1-64 characters from [A-Za-z0-9_-]`                                                                                                                  | The name is empty, too long, or has another character (`opfs://team.rl`, `opfs://a/b`)                                   |
| `RelateDb.open`            | `OPFS open requires an opfs://name URI; use new RelateDb() for :memory:`                                                                                                | The URI is a path, a `file://` URL or `:memory:`                                                                         |
| `RelateDb.open`            | `storage locked: opfs://<name>`                                                                                                                                         | Another handle holds the store                                                                                           |
| `RelateDb.open`            | `storage error: OPFS is not available in this browser`                                                                                                                  | The worker has no `navigator.storage.getDirectory`                                                                       |
| `reset`                    | `database is read-only`                                                                                                                                                 | The handle was opened read-only                                                                                          |
| any method                 | `null pointer passed to rust`                                                                                                                                           | The handle was freed                                                                                                     |
| `renderResult`             | The JSON parser's message, such as `expected ident at line 1 column 2`                                                                                                  | An entry is not JSON                                                                                                     |
| `renderResult`             | ``envelope <i>: no `columns` array``                                                                                                                                    | Entry `<i>`, counted from 0, is JSON without a `columns` array, such as `{}`                                             |
| `execute`, `executeScript` | (envelope) `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.` | A write on a read-only handle                                                                                            |
| `execute`, `executeScript` | (envelope) `LOAD CSV file unavailable`                                                                                                                                  | `LOAD CSV` from a file                                                                                                   |

The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) lists the engine's statement errors, which are the same on every surface.

properties.heading: Limits
properties.text: The limits come from the engine and are the same on every surface: a statement's text is at most 4194304 bytes (`syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`), and one value a statement builds is bounded by the expression memory cap. [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/) lists each limit with its default and the setting that changes it.

properties.heading: Module exports
properties.text:
| Export                                     | Signature                                                                                  | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` (`init`)                         | `init(options?: { module_or_path: InitInput \| Promise<InitInput> }): Promise<InitOutput>` | Loads and instantiates the engine. `InitInput` is a `RequestInfo`, `URL`, `Response`, `BufferSource` or `WebAssembly.Module`; with no argument, the URL beside `relate.js`. Passing `InitInput` directly instead of the object still works and logs a deprecation warning. A response whose type is not `application/wasm` logs a warning and falls back to `WebAssembly.instantiate` |
| `initSync`                                 | `initSync(options: { module: BufferSource \| WebAssembly.Module }): InitOutput`            | Instantiates from bytes or a compiled module, synchronously. Passing the module directly still works and logs a deprecation warning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `RelateDb`                                 | class                                                                                      | One store and one connection ([RelateDb](#relatedb))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `renderResult`                             | `renderResult(envelopes: string[]): string`                                                | Renders a script's envelopes as a recording ([Recordings](#recordings))                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `__start`                                  | `__start(): void`                                                                          | The engine's start function; `init()` and `initSync()` run it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `InitInput`, `InitOutput`, `SyncInitInput` | types                                                                                      | The loader's argument and result types; `InitOutput` holds the instance's exports, including `memory`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Every export except `default`, `initSync` and the types needs a finished `init()` or `initSync()`.

properties.heading: Not in this build
properties.text:
| Absent                                                   | In its place                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A version export                                         | `CALL dbms.components() YIELD name, versions WHERE name = 'Relate' RETURN versions[0]` returns the engine version (`1.0.1`) |
| Opening a `.rl` file, a directory store, or a URL        | `new RelateDb()` in memory, or `RelateDb.open('opfs://<name>')`                                                             |
| A statement deadline or timeout                          | None; a page that runs the engine in a worker ends a statement with `worker.terminate()`                                    |
| Explicit transactions                                    | Each statement commits on its own                                                                                           |
| `LOAD CSV` from a file                                   | None; parameters carry the rows                                                                                             |
| Arrow output, change data capture, the `apoc` procedures | None: `CALL db.cdc.current()` and `CALL apoc.version()` are `ProcedureNotFound`                                             |
| Bolt, the HTTP Query API, MCP                            | The CLI's `relate serve`                                                                                                    |
| Agent mode, row caps, output modes                       | CLI settings                                                                                                                |

properties.heading: OPFS stores
properties.text:
| Property          | Value                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| URI               | `opfs://<name>`                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Name              | 1 to 64 characters from `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_`, `-`; one path segment                                                                                                           |
| Where it can open | A dedicated worker; the page thread, a shared worker and a service worker are refused                                                                                             |
| Files             | `relate/<name>/catalog` and `relate/<name>/slot-00` to `slot-63`, in the origin's OPFS root                                                                                       |
| Durability        | Each statement is durable when it returns; a terminated worker or a reload keeps every acknowledged write                                                                         |
| Concurrency       | One open handle per store, read-only or not; a second open from any worker of the origin rejects with `storage locked: opfs://<name>` until the first is freed or its worker ends |
| Snapshot codec    | JSON; the WASM build has no Parquet codec                                                                                                                                         |
| Background work   | None: no checkpoint timer, no threads                                                                                                                                             |
| Browsers checked  | Chrome 157 (this site's run of the shipped build); no other browser has been checked                                                                                              |

properties.heading: Package files
properties.text:
| File                                     | Holds                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate.js`                              | The ES module: `init`, `initSync`, `RelateDb`, `renderResult`, `__start`                           |
| `relate_bg.wasm`                         | The engine; `init()` with no argument fetches it from `new URL('relate_bg.wasm', import.meta.url)` |
| `relate.d.ts`, `relate_bg.wasm.d.ts`     | TypeScript declarations for `relate.js` and the engine's exports                                   |
| `snippets/relate-wasm-<hash>/js/opfs.js` | The OPFS helper; `relate.js` imports it by that relative path                                      |
| `opfs.js`                                | The same OPFS helper, at the top level ([The OPFS helper](#the-opfs-helper))                       |
| `trap.js`                                | `isWasmTrap(err)` ([Traps](#traps))                                                                |
| `trap.d.ts`, `opfs.d.ts`                 | TypeScript declarations for `trap.js` and `opfs.js`                                                |
| `package.json`                           | The manifest: name, version, `exports` map, `types`                                                |
| `README.md`                              | The package's readme                                                                               |

`relate.js` and `snippets/` resolve their imports relative to `relate.js`, so the files sit together, unchanged, in one directory. The package's `exports` map names `.` (`relate.js`, types `relate.d.ts`), `./trap.js` (types `trap.d.ts`), `./opfs.js` (types `opfs.d.ts`) and `./relate_bg.wasm`. The site's own copy in `public/wasm/` holds the files a page loads, without `trap.d.ts`, `opfs.d.ts`, `package.json` and `README.md`.

properties.heading: Parameters
properties.text:
| `params_json`                          | Result                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `null`, omitted, or blank              | No [parameters](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter)               |
| A JSON object, as text                 | Each key is a parameter; a nested object is a map, even with a `__type` key           |
| JSON that does not parse               | An error envelope: `invalid params JSON: <detail>`                                    |
| JSON that is not an object             | An error envelope: `params must be a JSON object`                                     |
| A missing parameter the statement uses | An error envelope: `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <names>` |

Parameters carry JSON values only. Typed values (dates, points, durations) are built in the statement: `date($d)`, `point($p)`.

properties.heading: Recordings
properties.text:
`renderResult(envelopes)` takes the JSON texts `executeScript()` returned and returns JSON text, the form this site's cells record:

| Key     | Value                                                                                                             |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`  | `"gram"` when a row holds a node, relationship or path; `"table"` otherwise                                       |
| `text`  | The last statement's result as text, followed by the counters summed over the script                              |
| `table` | `{columns, rows, numeric, summary}` for a table with rows, each cell a Cypher literal; `null` for gram or no rows |
| `graph` | `{nodes, rels}` for gram, each node and relationship once in the order met; `null` for a table                    |
| `stats` | The eleven counters, summed over the script                                                                       |

An empty array renders as `(no rows)`. An entry that is not envelope JSON throws.

properties.heading: RelateDb
properties.text:
| Member             | Signature                                                     | Returns             | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| constructor        | `new RelateDb(read_only?: boolean \| null)`                   | `RelateDb`          | An in-memory store. `read_only` `true` opens it [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only), refusing every write; such a store starts empty and stays empty, since nothing can be written to it or loaded into it. Omitted, `null` or `false`, the store is writable. Works on the page thread and in a worker. Throws when the open fails |
| `open`             | `RelateDb.open(uri: string, read_only?: boolean \| null)`     | `Promise<RelateDb>` | An OPFS store, `opfs://<name>`, created when it does not exist ([OPFS stores](#opfs-stores)). Dedicated worker only. `read_only` `true` refuses every write. Rejects with the messages in [Errors](#errors)                                                                                                                                                         |
| `execute`          | `execute(query: string, params_json?: string \| null)`        | `string`            | Runs one statement and returns its envelope as JSON text. A second statement in `query` is a syntax error. Never throws for an error in the statement; the envelope's `error` holds it                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `executeScript`    | `executeScript(script: string, params_json?: string \| null)` | `string[]`          | Runs a script of statements separated by `;` and returns one envelope per statement run, in order. A `;` inside a string, a backquoted identifier or a comment does not split. Stops after the first envelope whose `error` is set; the statements before it stay committed. Every statement gets the same parameters. A blank or comment-only script returns `[]`  |
| `reset`            | `reset(): void`                                               | `undefined`         | In memory: drops the store and opens a new empty one. OPFS: wipes the store and reopens it empty, so a reload finds it empty. Throws `database is read-only` on a read-only handle                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `free`             | `free(): void`                                                | `undefined`         | Releases the handle and, for OPFS, its file handles. A later call on it throws `null pointer passed to rust`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `[Symbol.dispose]` | `[Symbol.dispose](): void`                                    | `undefined`         | The same as `free()`, for `using` declarations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

properties.heading: Synopsis
The envelope
properties.text:
`execute()` returns, and `executeScript()` returns per statement, one JSON object as text. A successful statement:

| Key                                               | Type             | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`                                         | `string[]`       | Column names, in `RETURN` order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `columnTypes`                                     | `string[]`       | The engine's type name for each column: `STRING`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `BOOLEAN`, `LIST`, `MAP`, `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`, `PATH`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `DATETIME`, `DURATION`, `POINT`, `VECTOR`, `BINARY`, `ANY` and the other type names ([Value shapes](#value-shapes)) |
| `rows`                                            | `object[]`       | One object per row, keyed by column name; `[]` for a statement with no rows                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `stats`                                           | object           | Eleven counters: `constraints_added`, `constraints_removed`, `indexes_added`, `indexes_removed`, `labels_added`, `labels_removed`, `nodes_created`, `nodes_deleted`, `properties_set`, `relationships_created`, `relationships_deleted`                             |
| `notifications`                                   | `object[]`       | Each with `code`, `gql_status`, `severity`, `category`, `title`, `description`, `remedy`, and `operator_id` on operator-scoped kinds; filled on `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`, `[]` on a plain run                                                                        |
| `plan`                                            | object or `null` | On `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`: `{schema: "relate.plan/v1", statement, profiled, root}`, each operator with `operator`, `details`, `identifiers`, `estimated_rows`, `actual` (filled under `PROFILE`), `warnings` and `children`; `null` otherwise                      |
| `elapsed_ms`, `parse_ms`, `plan_ms`, `execute_ms` | number           | Timings in milliseconds; different on every run                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `error`                                           | `null`           | `null` on success                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

A failed statement has only four keys: `columns` (`[]`), `rows` (`[]`), `stats` (`{}`) and `error`, a string. An engine error starts with its kind (`syntax error`, `semantic error`, `type error`) and, for a typed engine error, its name. The parameter-decoding errors (`invalid params JSON: <detail>`, `params must be a JSON object`) and `LOAD CSV file unavailable` carry no kind.

```json
{"columns":[],"error":"semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): name","rows":[],"stats":{}}
```

properties.heading: The OPFS helper
properties.text:
`opfs.js` is the code `RelateDb.open()` calls to reach OPFS; `relate.js` imports its copy in `snippets/`. It is internal to the engine.

| Export                                                                        | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OPFS_SLOT_COUNT`                                                             | `64`, the number of slot files per store                                                                                                                                                      |
| `prepareOpfs(name)`                                                           | Creates `relate/<name>/` and takes a synchronous access handle on `catalog` and each slot file; throws `storage locked: opfs://<name>` (`name` `RelateLocked`) when a handle is already taken |
| `slotSize`, `slotTruncate`, `slotFlush`, `slotClose`, `slotRead`, `slotWrite` | Synchronous file operations on a handle taken by `prepareOpfs`                                                                                                                                |

properties.heading: Transactions
properties.text: The build has no transaction API. Every statement commits on its own when `execute()` returns, and `BEGIN` is a syntax error. Within one statement, all of its writes apply or none do.

properties.heading: Traps
properties.text: A crash inside the engine (a Rust panic, stack exhaustion, an out-of-bounds access) traps the WebAssembly instance: the call throws, and the instance cannot be used again. `isWasmTrap(err)` in `trap.js` returns `true` when `err` is a `WebAssembly.RuntimeError` or its message matches `unreachable`, `memory access out of bounds`, `call stack exhausted` or `maximum call stack size`, ignoring case, and `false` for any other error, after which the instance is still usable. After a trap, a new instance means a new worker or a page reload. An OPFS store reopens with every write it acknowledged.

properties.heading: Value shapes
properties.text:
| Cypher type                          | In `rows`                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `INTEGER`                            | A JSON number with every digit; `JSON.parse` rounds one beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (9007199254740991)                                                            |
| `FLOAT`, `STRING`, `BOOLEAN`, `NULL` | The JSON value                                                                                                                                                         |
| `LIST`, `MAP`                        | A JSON array, a JSON object                                                                                                                                            |
| `NODE`                               | `{"id": <n>, "kind": "node", "labels": […], "properties": {…}}`                                                                                                        |
| `RELATIONSHIP`                       | `{"id": <n>, "kind": "relationship", "type": "<TYPE>", "start_node": <n>, "end_node": <n>, "properties": {…}}`                                                         |
| `PATH`                               | An array: node, relationship, node, … in path order                                                                                                                    |
| `DATE`, `DURATION`                   | An ISO 8601 string: `"2026-01-02"`, `"P1D"`                                                                                                                            |
| `DATETIME` (zoned)                   | An ISO 8601 string with its offset, and its zone when it has one: `"2026-01-02T03:04:05Z"`, `"2026-01-02T03:04:05+01:00[Europe/Paris]"`                                |
| `LOCAL DATETIME`                     | An ISO 8601 string without an offset: `"2026-01-02T03:04:05"`; its `columnTypes` entry is `DATETIME`                                                                   |
| `TIME` (zoned), `LOCAL TIME`         | An ISO 8601 string: `"03:04:05Z"`, `"03:04:05"`; both have the `columnTypes` entry `TIME`                                                                              |
| `POINT` (cartesian)                  | `{"crs": "cartesian", "srid": 7203, "x": 1.0, "y": 2.0}`; in 3D, `"crs": "cartesian-3d"`, `"srid": 9157` and a `"z"` key                                               |
| `POINT` (geographic)                 | `{"crs": "wgs-84", "srid": 4326, "longitude": 1.0, "latitude": 2.0}`; in 3D, `"crs": "wgs-84-3d"`, `"srid": 4979` and a `"height"` key                                 |
| `VECTOR`                             | `{"dim": <n>, "type": "<coordinate type>", "values": […]}`, such as `{"dim": 2, "type": "FLOAT32", "values": [1.0, 2.0]}`                                              |
| `BINARY` (byte array)                | A list of integers from 0 to 255. A byte array enters only through Bolt or a Rust parameter, never through this build's parameters, and cannot be stored as a property |

The JSON text writes a float with its decimal point (`1.0`); `JSON.parse` reads it as the number `1`.

properties.heading: relate CLI
properties.text: `relate` is one binary with two kinds of run. A query run executes Cypher statements against one [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) and prints their results; a command (`relate <command>`) does one job, such as copying a store or serving it, and exits. This page lists the invocation forms, every command the binary's `relate --help` prints, the query-run flags by family and the shell dot commands, with a link to the page that holds each detail.

properties.heading: Commands
properties.text:
The twelve commands of the binary these pages are verified against, in the order `relate --help` prints them. The second column is the binary's own one-line summary.

| Command                                                                  | Summary from `relate --help`                                   | Its flags                                                                            | Guide                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`query`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/query/)                 | Run a statement session (oneshot, stdin, or shell)             | [Query-run flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#query-run-flags)     | [Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/)                            |
| [`clone`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/clone/)                 | Copy a database into a new store and exit                      | [`relate clone`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-clone)         | [Back up and restore](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/)          |
| [`info`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/info/)                   | Print store metadata for a database without opening it         | [`relate info`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-info)           | [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/)                      |
| [`pull`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/pull/)                   | Copy a Neo4j/Aura subgraph into a database                     | [`relate pull`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-pull)           | [Pull from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/neo4j/pull-from-neo4j/)                   |
| [`push`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/push/)                   | Copy a database subgraph into Neo4j/Aura                       | [`relate push`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-push)           | [Push to Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/neo4j/push-to-neo4j/)                       |
| [`skill`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/skill/)                 | Install, inspect, or remove the embedded agent skill bundle    | [`relate skill`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-skill)         | [Install the agent skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/install-the-skill/)        |
| [`upgrade`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/upgrade/)             | Update the relate binary (alias: update)                       | [`relate upgrade`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-upgrade)     | —                                                                                           |
| [`telemetry`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/telemetry/)         | Manage anonymous usage metrics (on, off, status)               | none                                                                                 | [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/)          |
| [`run`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/run/)                     | Run an installed extension action into a store the host owns   | [`relate run`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-run)             | [Install and run an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/install-and-run/) |
| [`serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/)                 | Host the HTTP Query API and MCP surfaces on a database         | [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-serve)         | [Connect over MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/connect-over-mcp/)                |
| [`agent-context`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-context/) | Print the compact agent briefing (commands, flags, exit codes) | none                                                                                 | [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#the-agent-context-briefing) |
| [`extension`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/extension/)         | Scaffold, install, check, list, or remove command extensions   | [`relate extension`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-extension) | [Write an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/write-an-extension/)        |

Each command's name links to its reference page. A dash in the Guide column means no guide covers the command; `relate <command> --help` and `relate agent-context <command>` describe it on any machine. `relate --help` lists only the commands compiled into the binary. A command left out of a build exits 2 with `Error: the '<command>' command is not included in this build of relate`.
