properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
A one-statement query run on the default in-memory store, printed as an [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope):

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["ok"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"ok":1}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.351167,"execute_ms":0.203625,"lex_parse_ms":0.023166000000000003,"lower_ms":0.0295,"parse_ms":0.09595899999999999,"plan_ms":0.040874999999999995,"result_generation_ms":0.00041600000000000003,"rewrite_ms":0.006667},"truncated":false}
```

`relate query` with no statement reads a script from piped stdin, one envelope per statement:

```bash verify
printf 'RETURN 1 AS a;\nRETURN 2 AS b;\n' | relate query --mode envelope
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["a"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"a":1}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.331042,"execute_ms":0.19675,"lex_parse_ms":0.020125,"lower_ms":0.027959,"parse_ms":0.087084,"plan_ms":0.038167,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.006583},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["b"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"b":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.02425,"execute_ms":0.004041,"lex_parse_ms":0.003792,"lower_ms":0.003416,"parse_ms":0.01325,"plan_ms":0.0051660000000000005,"result_generation_ms":0.000083,"rewrite_ms":0.000417},"truncated":false}
```

The version line names the release:

```bash verify

```

```text
Relate v1.0.1
License: Apache 2.0 (binary)
```

properties.heading: Shell dot commands
properties.text: A line that starts with a dot is a shell command, not Cypher: `.begin`, `.commit`, `.rollback`, `.checkpoint`, `.info`, `.timer`, `.help` and `.quit`. They work in the interactive shell and in a script piped to `relate query`, one per line; `.begin` opens an explicit [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction) and `.checkpoint` writes a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint). [Dot commands](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/dot-commands/) gives each one's effect, output, failure and exit code.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]
relate <COMMAND> [ARGS]
relate query [STATEMENT] [--database PATH]
```

| Form                       | What runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate [OPTIONS] [QUERY]` | The path-first query run. `QUERY` (or `-c`, `--command`) is one statement or a `;`-separated list. With no `QUERY`, a terminal opens the interactive shell; piped or redirected stdin prints the top-level help and exits 0. |
| `relate query [STATEMENT]` | The same query session as a command word. With no `STATEMENT`, it reads a script from stdin, or opens the interactive shell on a terminal.                                                                                   |
| `relate <COMMAND> [ARGS]`  | A command: it does its job and exits. Each command takes its own flags, listed on the [flags page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#command-flags).                                                             |

`--database` (short form `-d`) names the store: a directory, a single-file `.rl` store, or `:memory:`, the default. The word `query` as the first positional is the command; a directory named `query` is `--database ./query`.

properties.heading: relate agent-context
properties.text: `relate agent-context` prints a compact plain-text briefing of the binary that runs it: its version, one line per command it contains, the names of its query-run flags, and its exit code table. With a command word, it prints that command's usage line, flags, examples, and the exit code table instead. The briefing is built from the same command table as `--help`, so it describes the installed binary and no other: the version it prints is the version that answers. It reads no store, needs no network, and takes no flags beyond `--help`.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code                                                                 | When                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| [0](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-0) | The briefing printed                           |
| [2](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-2) | An unknown command word, or more than one word |

An unknown word, or anything that is not a command word, exits 2:

```bash verify
relate agent-context --json
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: agent-context: unknown command '--json' (expected one of: query, clone, info, pull, push, skill, upgrade, telemetry, run, serve, agent-context, extension)
Usage: relate agent-context [COMMAND]
Run 'relate agent-context --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

A second word exits 2 with `Error: unexpected argument to agent-context: <word>` and the same two lines.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
A command with no flags of its own, such as `telemetry`, prints no `Flags:` list:

```bash verify
relate agent-context telemetry
```

```text
telemetry — Manage anonymous usage metrics (on, off, status)
Usage: relate telemetry on|off|status
Examples:
  # See whether anonymous usage metrics are on
  relate telemetry status
Exit codes:
  0  success: success, including an empty result
  1  fatal_error: runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error
  2  usage_error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional
  5  conflict: write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener
  6  validation_error: the statement is rejected: syntax, semantic or type error
  7  timeout: a statement exceeded --timeout
```

properties.heading: One command
properties.text:
A command word narrows the briefing to that command:

```bash verify
relate agent-context info
```

```text
info — Print store metadata for a database without opening it
Usage: relate info --database PATH [--json]
Flags:
  --database
  --json
Examples:
  # Describe a database without opening it, as JSON
  relate info --database ./mydata --json
Exit codes:
  0  success: success, including an empty result
  1  fatal_error: runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error
  2  usage_error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional
  5  conflict: write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener
  6  validation_error: the statement is rejected: syntax, semantic or type error
  7  timeout: a statement exceeded --timeout
```

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate agent-context [COMMAND]
```

| Argument  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `COMMAND` | Optional. One command word: `query`, `clone`, `info`, `pull`, `push`, `skill`, `upgrade`, `telemetry`, `run`, `serve`, `agent-context` or `extension`. `update` names `upgrade`, its alias |

| Run                              | Prints                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate agent-context`           | The version line, the command index, the query-run flag names, the exit code table                                                    |
| `relate agent-context <command>` | `<command> — <summary>`, the usage line, a `Flags:` list when the command has its own flags, an `Examples:` list, the exit code table |
| `relate agent-context --help`    | The command's help page, exit code 0                                                                                                  |

The output is plain text in every run, with [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode) on or off. `RELATE_HELP_EXAMPLES=0`, which drops the examples from every `--help` page, leaves the briefing's `Examples:` list in place.

properties.heading: The briefing
properties.text:
These examples run in a new, empty directory. The whole briefing, 26 lines:

```bash verify
relate agent-context
```

```text
relate v1.0.1 — agent context

Commands (detail: relate agent-context <COMMAND>):
  query          Run a statement session (oneshot, stdin, or shell)
  clone          Copy a database into a new store and exit
  info           Print store metadata for a database without opening it
  pull           Copy a Neo4j/Aura subgraph into a database
  push           Copy a database subgraph into Neo4j/Aura
  skill          Install, inspect, or remove the embedded agent skill bundle
  upgrade        Update the relate binary (alias: update)
  telemetry      Manage anonymous usage metrics (on, off, status)
  run            Run an installed extension action into a store the host owns
  serve          Host the HTTP Query API and MCP surfaces on a database
  agent-context  Print the compact agent briefing (commands, flags, exit codes)
  extension      Scaffold, install, check, list, or remove command extensions

Query-run flags (relate [OPTIONS] [QUERY]):
  --help --version --database --json --csv --markdown --jsonl --toon --noheader --mode --format --pretty --timings --param --fetch-params --snapshot-format --markdown-body-properties --wal-dir --checkpoint-interval-secs --durability-mode --logical-graph-size-limit --expression-memory-limit --concurrent-logical-workspace-limit --max-traversal-depth --safe --no-safe --agent-mode --no-agent-mode --max-rows --width --timeout --load --read-only --load-csv-dir --namespace --command

Exit codes:
  0  success: success, including an empty result
  1  fatal_error: runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error
  2  usage_error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional
  5  conflict: write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener
  6  validation_error: the statement is rejected: syntax, semantic or type error
  7  timeout: a statement exceeded --timeout
```

| Section           | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Version line      | `relate v<version> — agent context`: the version of the binary that printed it                                                                                                                           |
| `Commands`        | Each command compiled into this binary, with the one-line summary `relate --help` prints. A build without a command leaves its line out                                                                  |
| `Query-run flags` | The names of the flags that the path-first form and `relate query` accept; no arguments or defaults                                                                                                      |
| `Exit codes`      | Each [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code), its `code` name as the [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object) carries it, and what it means |

The flag list names flags only. `relate agent-context query` repeats them with the usage line, the [relate query page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/query/) describes the session they apply to, and the [flags page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#query-run-flags) gives each one's argument, default, and environment variable.

The briefing needs no network and names the release that answers; the [agent quickstart](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#read-the-briefing) and [Drive relate from an agent](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/drive-relate-from-an-agent/) use it, and the [skill bundle](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/install-the-skill/) lists it among its commands.

properties.heading: Agent mode
properties.text: [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode) is a pair of default changes the CLI makes for a query run under an agent harness: at most 100 rows printed per statement, with the cut reported, and `toon` instead of `jsonl` as the output mode when stdout is piped. It turns on when relate detects a harness and stdout is not a terminal, or when `--agent-mode` or `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1` asks for it. An explicit `--mode` or `--max-rows` overrides either default. Agent mode never blocks a write, changes the envelope's shape, or changes an exit code, but its piped `toon` default prints no [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object) on stdout: a failure there shows only as the stderr message and the exit code.

properties.heading: Detection
properties.text:
An agent harness is detected when any of these environment variables is set to a non-empty value. The value itself does not matter: `AI_AGENT=0` counts, and an empty value does not.

| Variables                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AI_AGENT`, `AGENT`                                                                    |
| `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE`                                                            |
| `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`                             |
| `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`                                                     |
| `CURSOR_AGENT`, `GEMINI_CLI`, `OPENCODE`, `AUGMENT_AGENT`, `GOOSE_PROVIDER`, `REPL_ID` |

Three patterns also count, each matched case-insensitively:

| Variable       | Contains    |
| -------------- | ----------- |
| `EDITOR`       | `devin`     |
| `TERM_PROGRAM` | `kiro`      |
| `PATH`         | `.pi/agent` |

properties.heading: Forcing it on or off
properties.text:
Under a detected harness with stdout piped, the output mode is `toon`, with no announcement:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate "UNWIND [1, 2] AS x RETURN x"
```

```text
rows[2]{x}:
  1
  2
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":0.378,"execute_ms":0.220834,"lex_parse_ms":0.031875,"lower_ms":0.031792,"parse_ms":0.1065,"plan_ms":0.041665999999999995,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.0067079999999999996}
planCache:
  miss
```

`--no-agent-mode` beats detection, so the piped default is `jsonl` again:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate --no-agent-mode "UNWIND [1, 2] AS x RETURN x"
```

```text
{"x":1}
{"x":2}
```

An explicit `--mode` beats agent mode's default without turning agent mode off:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate --mode jsonl "UNWIND [1, 2] AS x RETURN x"
```

```text
{"x":1}
{"x":2}
```

`RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1` turns it on without a harness, and says so on stderr:

```bash verify
RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1 relate "UNWIND [1, 2] AS x RETURN x"
```

```text
relate agent mode on: RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1 (--no-agent-mode to turn off)
rows[2]{x}:
  1
  2
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":0.47974999999999995,"execute_ms":0.335833,"lex_parse_ms":0.023125,"lower_ms":0.032541,"parse_ms":0.095875,"plan_ms":0.038583,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.005667}
planCache:
  miss
```

A value other than `1` or `0` is a usage error, before any statement runs:

```bash verify
RELATE_AGENT_MODE=yes relate "RETURN 1 AS x"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: invalid RELATE_AGENT_MODE: 'yes' is neither 1 nor 0
exit=2
```

properties.heading: Notifications
properties.text:
A plain run produces no notifications. `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` derive them beside the plan: an unknown label or property key, a missing index, a pattern with no join anchor. Agent mode does not change them; the output mode decides where they go. Under agent mode's piped `toon` default, they print as a `notifications:` entry after `plan:`, one inline JSON array, before the `timings:` and `planCache:` entries:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate "EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Persn) RETURN p.name AS name" | tail -6 | head -2
```

```text
notifications:
  [{"category":"UNRECOGNIZED","code":"Neo.ClientNotification.Statement.UnknownLabelWarning","description":"The label `Persn` does not exist in this database.","gql_status":"01N50","remedy":"Check the spelling; the label exists after the first write that creates it, and no index or constraint uses the unknown name.","severity":"WARNING","title":"Unknown label"},{"category":"UNRECOGNIZED","code":"Neo.ClientNotification.Statement.UnknownPropertyKeyWarning","description":"The property key `name` does not exist in this database.","gql_status":"01N52","remedy":"Check the spelling; the key exists after the first write that sets it.","severity":"WARNING","title":"Unknown property key"}]
```

Each entry has `category`, `code`, `description`, `gql_status`, `remedy`, `severity` and `title`, plus `operator_id` when it concerns one plan operator. The `envelope` mode carries the same list in `notifications`; `json` prints one `{"notifications":[…],"plan":{…},"planCache":…,"timings":{…}}` object; `jsonl` prints one `{"notifications":[…],"plan":{…}}` line, then the timing line with `--timings`; `table` and `markdown` print a `Notifications:` block; `csv` and `cypher` print none. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#notifications) lists every notification.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate --agent-mode [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
relate --no-agent-mode [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1 relate [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
RELATE_AGENT_MODE=0 relate [OPTIONS] [QUERY]
```

| Setting                                                              | Agent mode off    | Agent mode on                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Output mode, stdout piped or redirected, no output flag              | `jsonl`           | `toon`                                                                       |
| Output mode, stdout a terminal, no output flag                       | `table`           | `table`                                                                      |
| Rows printed per statement, no `--max-rows` or `RELATE_MAX_ROWS`     | unlimited         | at most 100; the cut is reported on stderr and in-band                       |
| An explicit `--mode` or `--max-rows`                                 | applies           | applies                                                                      |
| Error object on stdout, stdout piped, no output flag                 | printed (`jsonl`) | not printed: `toon` prints none; the stderr message and the exit code remain |
| Writes, the envelope's fields, the error object's fields, exit codes | unchanged         | unchanged                                                                    |

properties.heading: The agent-context briefing
properties.text:
`relate agent-context` prints a compact text briefing of the installed binary: its version, one line per command, the query-run flag names, and the exit code table. `relate agent-context <command>` prints one command's usage line, its flags, an example, and the exit code table. The output is plain text in every run, agent mode or not, and it comes from the same command table as `--help`, so it describes the binary that prints it.

```bash verify
relate agent-context clone
```

```text
clone — Copy a database into a new store and exit
Usage: relate clone [--wal-dir DIR] [--to-snapshot-format F] [--markdown-body-properties LIST] SOURCE DEST
Flags:
  --wal-dir
  --to-snapshot-format
  --markdown-body-properties
Examples:
  # Copy a database into a new store
  relate clone ./mydata ./backup
Exit codes:
  0  success: success, including an empty result
  1  fatal_error: runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error
  2  usage_error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional
  5  conflict: write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener
  6  validation_error: the statement is rejected: syntax, semantic or type error
  7  timeout: a statement exceeded --timeout
```

An unknown command word exits 2 with `Error: agent-context: unknown command '<name>'`, followed by the list of commands it accepts. The briefing with no command word is recorded in the [agent quickstart](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#read-the-briefing).

properties.heading: The envelope
properties.text:
`--mode envelope` prints one compact JSON object per result set, on one line, so a multi-statement run is JSON Lines of [envelopes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope). Agent mode changes nothing in it except the row cap's two fields. Keys are sorted alphabetically, at the top level and inside each row; `columns` gives the column order.

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS a, [1, 2] AS l, {k: 'v'} AS m, null AS z"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER","LIST","MAP","ANY"],"columns":["a","l","m","z"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"a":1,"l":[1,2],"m":{"k":"v"},"z":null}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.3515,"execute_ms":0.198667,"lex_parse_ms":0.02425,"lower_ms":0.030792,"parse_ms":0.1025,"plan_ms":0.040958,"result_generation_ms":0.000334,"rewrite_ms":0.007084},"truncated":false}
```

| Field           | Type             | Present                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columnTypes`   | array of strings | always                        | One type name per column, from the first row: `STRING`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `BOOLEAN`, `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`, `PATH`, `LIST`, `MAP`, `POINT`, `DATETIME`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `DURATION`, `VECTOR`, `UUID`, `BINARY` or `ANY`. A `null` first value, or no rows, gives `ANY`. |
| `columns`       | array of strings | always                        | The result columns in order, even when there are no rows                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `notifications` | array of objects | always                        | The statement's notifications; `[]` on a plain run                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `plan`          | object           | `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` only  | The plan tree                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `planCache`     | string           | always                        | The plan-cache outcome: `miss`, `hit-raw-fastpath`, `hit-template`, `replan-generation-mismatch` or `bypassed`                                                                                                                                                             |
| `rowCap`        | object           | when the row cap cut the rows | `{"kept":N,"total":M}`: the rows printed and the rows the statement returned                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `rows`          | array of objects | always                        | One object per row, values as `--json` prints them                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `timings`       | object           | always                        | The statement's phase timings in milliseconds: `elapsed_ms`, `execute_ms`, `lex_parse_ms`, `lower_ms`, `parse_ms`, `plan_ms`, `result_generation_ms` and `rewrite_ms`; the values change from run to run                                                                   |
| `truncated`     | boolean          | always                        | `true` when the row cap cut the rows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

The [output modes page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache) defines each timing key and each `planCache` value.

An empty result keeps its columns, so no rows is told apart from no output:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["ANY"],"columns":["p"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.382083,"execute_ms":0.227458,"lex_parse_ms":0.027834,"lower_ms":0.04075,"parse_ms":0.098458,"plan_ms":0.048708,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.007500000000000001},"truncated":false}
```

A cut result has `rowCap` and `"truncated":true`. In this run `--max-rows 2` sets the cap; agent mode's default cut looks the same with `"kept":100`:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --max-rows 2 "UNWIND range(1, 5) AS x RETURN x"
```

```text
warning: result truncated to 2 rows (the statement returned 5); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["x"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rowCap":{"kept":2,"total":5},"rows":[{"x":1},{"x":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.34175,"execute_ms":0.20358400000000001,"lex_parse_ms":0.021709,"lower_ms":0.032666,"parse_ms":0.08629200000000001,"plan_ms":0.044333,"result_generation_ms":0.0011250000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.007042},"truncated":true}
```

A failed statement in `envelope`, `json`, `jsonl` or `speedscope` prints the error object instead, with the same keys in each; its fields are on the [exit codes page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#the-error-object). New envelope fields may be added; existing ones are never renamed.

`toon` prints no error object. Under a detected harness with stdout piped, a failed statement leaves the stderr message and the exit code, and nothing on stdout:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate "RETURN 1/0 AS x"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
type error: / by zero
exit=6
```

With `--mode envelope` or `--mode jsonl`, the same run prints the error object on stdout, agent mode on or off.

properties.heading: The row cap
properties.text:
With agent mode on and no `--max-rows` or `RELATE_MAX_ROWS`, a statement prints at most 100 rows. The cap limits what is printed, not what runs: the engine computes the whole result first, so a Cypher `LIMIT` is what bounds the work. `--max-rows N` sets the cap in any run, on a terminal too, and `--max-rows 0` prints every row.

A cut result still exits 0. The CLI writes one line to stderr:

```text
warning: result truncated to 100 rows (the statement returned 250); pass --max-rows 0 for all rows
```

The machine modes also carry the cut in-band, after the rows or inside the envelope, so a capped result never reads as a complete one:

| Mode                     | The in-band record                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `envelope`               | `"truncated":true` and `"rowCap":{"kept":100,"total":250}`                                                              |
| `jsonl`                  | A `{"rowCap":{"kept":100,"total":250}}` line after the rows, before the statement's timing line when `--timings` is set |
| `json`                   | A `rowCap` key beside `data`: `{"data":[…],"planCache":…,"rowCap":{"kept":100,"total":250},"timings":{…}}`              |
| `toon`                   | A `rowCap:` entry after the rows, the counts as inline JSON, before the `timings:` and `planCache:` entries             |
| `markdown`               | A footer line `> truncated: 100 of 250 rows shown`                                                                      |
| `table`, `csv`, `cypher` | None; the stderr line is the only report                                                                                |

Each statement of a multi-statement run is capped and reported on its own. Under a detected harness, the `toon` header names the rows kept, and the `rowCap:` entry after the last row names both counts. The `timings:` and `planCache:` entries close the block; the [output modes page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache) describes them, and their digits change from run to run:

```bash verify
CLAUDECODE=1 relate "UNWIND range(1, 250) AS x RETURN x" 2>/dev/null | head -2
CLAUDECODE=1 relate "UNWIND range(1, 250) AS x RETURN x" 2>/dev/null | tail -7
```

```text
rows[100]{x}:
  1
  100
rowCap:
  {"kept":100,"total":250}
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":0.44983399999999996,"execute_ms":0.30124999999999996,"lex_parse_ms":0.024457999999999997,"lower_ms":0.033833,"parse_ms":0.093125,"plan_ms":0.047667,"result_generation_ms":0.001209,"rewrite_ms":0.007833}
planCache:
  miss
```

properties.heading: What agent mode leaves alone
properties.text: Agent mode changes output defaults only. Writes go through as in any other run; the opt-ins that refuse statements are separate flags: `--read-only` opens the store [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only), and `--safe` refuses an unbounded `MATCH` read and a new named node without a label. Neither turns on by detection. Every [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) and the error object's fields are the same with agent mode on or off. `toon`, agent mode's piped default, prints no error object on stdout; `--mode envelope` or `--mode jsonl` prints it.

properties.heading: What turns it on
properties.text:
The CLI decides once per run, from the first rule that applies:

| Order | Rule                                                                                                                                                       | Applies on a terminal | Announced on stderr |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- |
| 1     | `--agent-mode` turns it on, `--no-agent-mode` off; of the two, the last one given wins                                                                     | yes                   | yes, when on        |
| 2     | `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1` turns it on, `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=0` off, with surrounding whitespace ignored; an empty value counts as unset; any other value exits 2 | yes                   | yes, when on        |
| 3     | Detection: on when an agent harness is detected and stdout is not a terminal                                                                               | no                    | no                  |

The two announcements, one line on stderr before any output:

```text
relate agent mode on: --agent-mode (--no-agent-mode to turn off)
relate agent mode on: RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1 (--no-agent-mode to turn off)
```

Detection is silent, so a harness that runs one statement per process sees no banner. On a terminal, an explicit on-state applies the row cap, and the output mode stays `table`.

properties.heading: relate clone
properties.text: `relate clone SOURCE DEST` copies a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) into a new store and exits. Each side is a [directory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#directory-store), or a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store) when its path ends in `.rl`, so one command copies, packs a directory into a `.rl` file, or unpacks one. The destination keeps the source's [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec) unless `--to-snapshot-format` names another. [Clone](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#clone) opens the source read-only, copies the state visible when it opened, and never writes the source; it creates the destination, which must not exist yet, and prints nothing on success.

properties.heading: Codecs
properties.text:
Without `--to-snapshot-format`, the destination keeps the source's codec. With it, clone writes the state visible when it opened, which is the last checkpoint plus the WAL commits after it, in the `parquet`, `json` or `markdown` codec; the layout and the codec are chosen independently.

| Source codec | `--to-snapshot-format` | Layouts in the example                     |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `parquet`    | `json`                 | directory to directory, `.rl` to `.rl`     |
| `parquet`    | `markdown`             | directory to directory, `.rl` to directory |
| `parquet`    | `parquet`              | directory to directory                     |
| `json`       | `parquet`              | directory to directory                     |
| `markdown`   | `parquet`              | directory to directory, directory to `.rl` |

Any other value exits 2 with `Error: invalid --to-snapshot-format: storage error: unknown snapshot codec '<value>' (expected parquet, json, markdown or rkyv)`. `rkyv` is not compiled into the release binary: `--to-snapshot-format rkyv` exits 1 with `Failed to clone database: storage error: rkyv snapshot codec is not compiled into this build (enable the "rkyv-codec" feature)`. [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#codecs) describes each codec's files.

Each pairing in the table, with the codec `relate info` reports for every result:

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team ./team-json
relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown ./team ./team-vault
relate clone --to-snapshot-format parquet ./team ./team-parquet
relate clone --to-snapshot-format parquet ./team-json ./from-json
relate clone --to-snapshot-format parquet ./team-vault ./from-vault
relate clone --to-snapshot-format parquet ./team-vault ./team-vault.rl
relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team.rl ./team-json.rl
relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown ./team.rl ./vault-from-rl
for store in team-json team-vault team-parquet from-json from-vault team-vault.rl team-json.rl vault-from-rl; do
  printf '%s: ' "$store"
  relate info --database "./$store" | grep '^codec:'
done
```

```text
team-json: codec: json
team-vault: codec: markdown
team-parquet: codec: parquet
from-json: codec: parquet
from-vault: codec: parquet
team-vault.rl: codec: parquet
team-json.rl: codec: json
vault-from-rl: codec: markdown
```

The graph survives a round trip through the text codecs:

```bash verify
relate --database ./from-vault --read-only --mode jsonl "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(r:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, r.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
{"person":"Grace","project":"opencypher-tck","since":2022}
{"person":"Grace","project":"relate","since":2023}
{"person":"Ada","project":"relate","since":2024}
```

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code                                                                 | Meaning for `relate clone`                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [0](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-0) | The destination was created; nothing is printed                                                  |
| [1](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-1) | The copy did not run or did not finish: a refusal in the table, or a storage or I/O error        |
| [2](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-2) | Usage error: a missing or extra argument, an unknown flag, or a bad `--to-snapshot-format` value |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
An existing destination is never overwritten:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team ./team-copy
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination already exists
exit=1
```

properties.heading: Layouts
properties.text:
Every pairing of the two durable layouts works; the in-memory store is refused on either side. One pairing depends on the codec: in relate 1.0.1 a `.rl` destination refuses markdown body properties, so a `markdown` source reaches a `.rl` path only with `--to-snapshot-format parquet` or `json` ([Codecs](#codecs)).

| Source          | Destination     | Result                                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Directory store | Directory store | A copy                                                                                                                  |
| Directory store | `.rl` path      | The store packed into one file                                                                                          |
| `.rl` file      | Directory store | The file unpacked into a folder                                                                                         |
| `.rl` file      | `.rl` path      | A copy                                                                                                                  |
| `:memory:`      | Any             | Exit code 1: `Failed to clone database: storage error: clone source must be a native directory or .rl bundle path`      |
| Any             | `:memory:`      | Exit code 1: `Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination must be a native directory or .rl bundle path` |

These examples run in a new, empty directory. This first command writes: it creates the directory store `./team` with three people, two projects and three `WORKS_ON` relationships:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

The four layout pairings, then a read-only count of the relationships in each copy:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team ./team-copy
relate clone ./team ./team.rl
relate clone ./team.rl ./team-unpacked
relate clone ./team.rl ./team-copy.rl
for store in team-copy team.rl team-unpacked team-copy.rl; do
  relate --database "./$store" --read-only --mode jsonl "MATCH (:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project) RETURN '$store' AS store, count(w) AS works"
done
```

```text
{"store":"team-copy","works":3}
{"store":"team.rl","works":3}
{"store":"team-unpacked","works":3}
{"store":"team-copy.rl","works":3}
```

properties.heading: Markdown body properties
properties.text:
`--markdown-body-properties` names the properties a `markdown` destination writes as each note's body instead of its frontmatter: a comma-separated list for every label, or `Label=LIST` for one label, with several entries separated by `;` (`Person=role,bio;Project=language`). The first listed property is written as the bare body and the rest as `##` sections. Without the flag, the destination uses the source's recorded configuration, else the single property `body`. On a directory destination whose codec is not `markdown`, it exits 1 with `Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored` (the codec named is the destination's).

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown --markdown-body-properties 'Person=role' ./team ./team-notes
cat team-notes/Person/Ada.md
```

```text
---
type: Person
name: Ada
KNOWS:
  - "[[Person/Grace]]"
WORKS_ON:
  - since: 2024
    target: "[[Project/relate]]"
---

engineer
```

properties.heading: Markdown into a .rl file
properties.text:
In relate 1.0.1 a `.rl` destination refuses markdown body properties, whether they come from `--markdown-body-properties` or from the configuration a `markdown` source records. Cloning a `markdown` store into a `.rl` path therefore needs `--to-snapshot-format parquet` or `json`; without it, or with `--to-snapshot-format markdown`, the clone exits 1 and creates nothing. The message names `parquet` whatever codec the command asked for:

```bash verify
relate clone ./team-vault ./vault-kept.rl
echo "exit=$?"
relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown ./team-vault ./vault-md.rl
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored
exit=1
Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored
exit=1
```

A `parquet` or `json` source with no body properties clones into a `markdown` `.rl` file: `relate clone --to-snapshot-format markdown ./team.rl ./team-md.rl` succeeds, and `relate info` reports `codec: markdown` for it. A `markdown` store clones into a directory store with any codec.

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
| Flag                         | Argument                  | Default                                        | Scope          | Since | Description                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--wal-dir`                  | `DIR`                     | `<SOURCE>/wal`                                 | `relate clone` | —     | Source WAL of a directory source; fails with a `.rl` source.                                       |
| `--to-snapshot-format`       | `parquet\|json\|markdown` | the source codec                               | `relate clone` | —     | Destination snapshot codec (`parquet`, `json` or `markdown`); transcodes the published checkpoint. |
| `--markdown-body-properties` | `LIST`                    | the source's recorded configuration, else body | `relate clone` | —     | Body properties of a markdown destination (`LIST` or `Label=LIST`; entries separated by `;`).      |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

`relate clone` takes only these three flags. A query-run flag after `clone`, such as `--read-only` or `--json`, exits 2 with `Error: unexpected argument to clone: <flag>`; `--read-only` before `clone` exits 2 with `Error: clone cannot be combined with a query or an access flag (--read-only)`.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/): the layouts and codecs clone converts between
- [Back up and restore a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/): clone as a backup that opens
- [relate info](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/info/): the layout, codec and counts of a clone, read without opening it
- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#relate-clone): the clone flags beside every other command's

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate clone [--wal-dir DIR] [--to-snapshot-format F] [--markdown-body-properties LIST] SOURCE DEST
```

| Argument | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SOURCE` | The store to copy: a directory store, or a path ending in `.rl`. Required. `:memory:` is refused                                                                                     |
| `DEST`   | The new store: a path ending in `.rl` makes a single-file store, any other path a directory store. Required. It must not exist, and its parent directory must. `:memory:` is refused |

A directory store can be cloned while another process writes it: the clone takes the state committed when it opened and does not follow later commits. A `.rl` source is refused while another process holds it for writing. The destination's write-ahead log (WAL) starts at `<DEST>/wal` for a directory destination; a `.rl` destination holds its own.

properties.heading: WAL directory
properties.text: `--wal-dir DIR` names the source's WAL when it is not at `<SOURCE>/wal`. It applies to a directory source only; with a `.rl` source, which holds its own WAL, it exits 1 with `Failed to clone database: storage error: wal_dir is not supported for .rl single-file databases (ADR-0074)`. It does not move the destination's WAL.

properties.heading: What clone refuses
properties.text:
| Input                                                                                                                                                 | Exit code | Message                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `DEST` exists                                                                                                                                         | 1         | `Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination already exists`                                                                                              |
| `DEST`'s parent directory does not exist                                                                                                              | 1         | `Failed to clone database: storage error: clone destination parent does not exist: <path>`                                                                               |
| A directory `SOURCE` that does not exist                                                                                                              | 1         | `Failed to clone database: storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`                                                                        |
| A `.rl` `SOURCE` that does not exist                                                                                                                  | 1         | `Failed to clone database: storage error: database not found: <path>`                                                                                                    |
| A `.rl` `SOURCE` another process holds for writing                                                                                                    | 1         | `Failed to clone database: storage locked: <path>`                                                                                                                       |
| `:memory:` on either side                                                                                                                             | 1         | `clone source must be a native directory or .rl bundle path`, or `clone destination …`, after `Failed to clone database: storage error: `                                |
| A `.rl` `DEST` with markdown body properties: a `markdown` `SOURCE` without `--to-snapshot-format parquet` or `json`, or `--markdown-body-properties` | 1         | `Failed to clone database: semantic error: markdown body properties are set but the store's snapshot codec is parquet, not markdown; the configuration would be ignored` |
| `--wal-dir` with a `.rl` source                                                                                                                       | 1         | `Failed to clone database: storage error: wal_dir is not supported for .rl single-file databases (ADR-0074)`                                                             |
| Fewer than two paths                                                                                                                                  | 2         | `Error: clone requires SOURCE and DEST`                                                                                                                                  |
| A third path, or a flag clone does not take                                                                                                           | 2         | `Error: unexpected argument to clone: <argument>`                                                                                                                        |

A runtime refusal (exit code 1) prints one line on stderr and no error object. A usage error (exit code 2) prints the error line, the usage line and `Run 'relate clone --help' for more information.`

properties.heading: Dot commands
properties.text: A dot command is a line that starts with `.` and that the `relate` CLI handles itself instead of running as Cypher. There are eight: `.help`, `.quit` (also `.exit`), `.begin`, `.commit`, `.rollback`, `.checkpoint`, `.info` and `.timer`. They work the same in the interactive shell and in a script piped to `relate query`. A dot command ends at the end of its line and needs no `;`. Any other word starting with `.` fails with `Error: unknown command <name>`.

properties.heading: .begin, .commit, and .rollback
properties.text:
Without `.begin`, each statement that writes commits on its own when it succeeds. `.begin` opens an explicit [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction): the statements after it see its writes, and nothing is committed until `.commit`. `.rollback` discards everything since `.begin`. All three print nothing on success. This example writes two `Note` nodes to a new directory store, `./notes`; later examples on this page read it `--read-only`.

```bash verify
printf ".begin\nCREATE (:Note {text: 'kept'});\nCREATE (:Note {text: 'also kept'});\n.commit\n" | relate query --database ./notes
relate --database ./notes --read-only --mode jsonl "MATCH (n:Note) RETURN count(n) AS notes"
```

```text
{"notes":2}
```

Transactions do not nest, and `.commit` or `.rollback` needs an open one:

| Situation                                | Message on stderr                          | Exit code in a script                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.begin` while a transaction is open     | `semantic error: already in a transaction` | 1                                                                              |
| `.commit` or `.rollback` with none open  | `semantic error: no transaction`           | 1                                                                              |
| A statement fails inside the transaction | The statement's own error                  | The statement's exit code; the script stops and the transaction is rolled back |

```bash verify
printf '.commit\n' | relate query
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
semantic error: no transaction
exit=1
```

In the interactive shell a failed statement does not end the session. It rolls back its own partial writes and leaves the transaction failed: every later statement and `.commit` print `semantic error: transaction failed; rollback required` until `.rollback`. The [transactions concept page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/) explains what a transaction sees and when it commits.

properties.heading: .checkpoint
properties.text:
`.checkpoint` writes a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint) now: the snapshot is rewritten to the current state and the WAL segments it covers are recycled. It prints nothing. On `:memory:` it succeeds without writing anything. A store opened `--read-only` refuses it with exit code 1:

```bash verify
printf '.checkpoint\n' | relate query --database ./notes --read-only
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
exit=1
```

A persistent store also checkpoints on a timer (`--checkpoint-interval-secs`, default `300`) and when a session ends. The [WAL and checkpoints page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/wal-and-checkpoints/) covers what a checkpoint writes.

properties.heading: Commands that do not exist
properties.text:
Many shells have more dot commands. relate has only the eight on this page, and every other word fails with `Error: unknown command <name>`, exit code 1 in a script. The jobs those commands do elsewhere are done this way:

| Job                                                           | In relate                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Output format, headers, width (`.mode`, `.headers`, `.width`) | The `--mode`, `--noheader` and `--width` flags, set when the session starts ([output modes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/)) |
| Writing results to a file (`.output`, `.once`)                | Shell redirection: `relate query --database <path> --read-only --mode csv < <script> > <file>`                                                     |
| Schema and counts (`.schema`, `.indexes`, `.labels`)          | `.info`, or Cypher: `SHOW INDEXES`, `SHOW CONSTRAINTS`, `CALL db.labels()`                                                                         |
| Running a script file (`.read`)                               | Piped stdin: `relate query --database <path> --read-only < <script>`; without `--read-only`, the script can write                                  |
| Switching stores (`.open`)                                    | One store per process, named once with `--database`                                                                                                |
| Plans (`.explain`)                                            | The `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` prefixes on a statement                                                                                                |

```bash verify
printf '.mode csv\n' | relate query
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: unknown command .mode
exit=1
```

properties.heading: Every command
properties.text:
| Command                   | Effect                                                | Prints on success                     | Fails with                                                  |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.help`                   | Lists the commands                                    | Five summary lines                    | —                                                           |
| `.quit`, `.exit`          | Ends the session; lines after it are not read         | Nothing                               | —                                                           |
| `.begin`                  | Opens an explicit transaction                         | Nothing                               | `semantic error: already in a transaction`                  |
| `.commit`                 | Commits the open transaction                          | Nothing                               | `semantic error: no transaction`                            |
| `.rollback`               | Discards the open transaction's writes                | Nothing                               | `semantic error: no transaction`                            |
| `.checkpoint`             | Writes a checkpoint of a persistent store now         | Nothing                               | The store's write error, on a read-only store               |
| `.info`                   | Prints the store's metadata, live counts, and catalog | A key/value block and two result sets | —                                                           |
| `.timer on`, `.timer off` | Turns per-statement timing on or off                  | `Timer: on` or `Timer: off`           | `Usage: .timer on\|off`, printed on stdout with exit code 0 |

properties.heading: .help
properties.text:
`.help` prints the summary of what the session accepts:

```bash verify
printf '.help\n' | relate query
```

```text
  Cypher statement ending with ;
  .begin / .commit / .rollback / .checkpoint
  .info
  .timer on|off
  .quit
```

properties.heading: .info
properties.text:
`.info` prints a read-only report on the open store, in three parts:

| Part           | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                 | Source                                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Store metadata | The store path as given, layout, the superblock version for a `.rl` store, codec, format version, checkpoint LSN, commit timestamp, total bytes, and WAL segments past the checkpoint | Read from disk, the same fields `relate info` prints; on `:memory:`, the line `store: :memory: (store metadata not applicable)` |
| Live counts    | `nodes:` and `relationships:`                                                                                                                                                         | The open session, so writes not yet checkpointed count                                                                          |
| Catalog        | `indexes:` and `constraints:`, each followed by the `SHOW INDEXES` or `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` result                                                                                       | The open session, printed in the session's output mode                                                                          |

On `:memory:` with `--mode csv`, the indexes result holds the two lookup indexes every store lists, and the constraints result is its header line:

```bash verify
printf '.info\n' | relate query --mode csv
```

```text
store:                        :memory: (store metadata not applicable)
nodes:                        0
relationships:                0
indexes:
id,name,state,populationPercent,type,entityType,labelsOrTypes,properties,indexProvider,owningConstraint,lastRead,readCount
0,index_1b9dcc97,ONLINE,100.0,LOOKUP,RELATIONSHIP,,,token-lookup-1.0,,,0
0,index_460996c0,ONLINE,100.0,LOOKUP,NODE,,,token-lookup-1.0,,,0
constraints:
id,name,type,entityType,labelsOrTypes,properties,ownedIndex,propertyType,enforcedLabel
```

On a directory store, the metadata lines come first. Sizes and timestamps differ from store to store, so this example keeps five lines:

```bash verify
printf '.info\n' | relate query --database ./notes --read-only --mode csv | grep -E '^(layout|codec|checkpoint LSN|nodes|relationships):'
```

```text
layout:                       native directory
codec:                        parquet
checkpoint LSN:               1
nodes:                        2
relationships:                0
```

A store that has never been checkpointed reports a `snapshot:` line reading `none yet (no checkpoint since creation)` in place of the codec and checkpoint fields. A `json` codec store reports `unavailable` as its format version, with a `note:` line saying the format version lives in its `graph.json`; its live counts and catalog print as usual.

properties.heading: .quit and .exit
properties.text:
`.quit` and `.exit` end the session with exit code 0. In a script, the lines after it are never read:

```bash verify
printf ".quit\nCREATE (:Note {text: 'never runs'});\n" | relate query --mode envelope
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
exit=0
```

On a persistent [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) opened for writing, the session takes a final checkpoint before it exits. If that fails, it prints `Error: final checkpoint failed: <reason>` and exits 1. End of input, or Ctrl-D on an empty line in the interactive shell, ends the session the same way.

A session that ends with a transaction open discards that transaction's writes and prints a warning on stderr. The exit code depends on the session:

| Session                                     | Exit code with a transaction open                        |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| A piped script or a one-shot statement list | 1, or the higher code of a statement that already failed |
| The interactive shell                       | 0                                                        |

```bash verify
printf '.begin\nCREATE (:Note);\n.quit\n' | relate query
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Warning: exiting with an open transaction; rolling back uncommitted changes. Use .commit before exiting to persist them.
exit=1
```

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Use the interactive shell](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/interactive-shell/): multi-line statements, history, and leaving the shell
- [Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/): `.begin` and `.commit` around a migration script
- [relate CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/#shell-dot-commands): the invocation forms and the dot commands in brief
- [Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/): what an explicit transaction sees

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
cypher> .<command> [argument]
printf '.<command>\n' | relate query [--database PATH]
```

| Rule                  | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Where                 | The interactive shell, a script on stdin to `relate query`, and a one-shot statement list (`-c` or the positional argument)                                                                                                                         |
| Ending                | The end of the line; a trailing `;` is accepted. A dot command can follow a statement on the same line: `RETURN 1 AS x; .help`                                                                                                                      |
| Case                  | Lowercase only: `.HELP` is an unknown command. The bare words `exit` and `EXIT` also end the session                                                                                                                                                |
| Arguments             | Only `.timer` reads one; the other commands ignore anything after the command word                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Output                | Results go to stdout in the session's output mode; errors go to stderr                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Exit code in a script | A failed dot command stops the script with [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) 1, like a failed [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement); in the interactive shell the session continues |

properties.heading: .timer
properties.text:
`.timer on` turns on per-statement timing, and `.timer off` turns it off; it is off when a session starts. Each prints its new state. While it is on, every statement that succeeds prints one line on stdout after its result: `Time: <total>ms (parse <ms> / plan <ms> / execute <ms>)`. The times change from run to run. Any argument other than `on` or `off`, in lowercase, prints the usage line and leaves the state unchanged:

```bash verify
printf '.timer on\n.timer off\n.timer ON\n' | relate query
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Timer: on
Timer: off
Usage: .timer on|off
exit=0
```

properties.heading: Environment variables
properties.text: The `relate` CLI reads environment variables for five jobs: default values for its flags, detecting an [agent harness](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-harness), turning off usage metrics, turning on preview features, and finding its config directory. A flag always beats its variable, and a variable beats the built-in default. A variable set to an empty or blank value counts as unset, with two exceptions the synopsis table names. An invalid value stops the run before any statement executes, with exit code 2 or 1 depending on the variable; a few variables fall back to their default instead, and the tables on this page say which. `RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES` is the exception to that order: it is read at the checkpoint, after the run's statements have run and committed.

properties.heading: Command variables
properties.text:
Each of these is read by one or two commands, and its row in [every variable](#every-variable) names them (`NEO4J_USER` appears inside the `NEO4J_USERNAME` row):

| Command                              | Variables                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Detail                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate serve`                       | `RELATE_AUTH`, `RELATE_IDENTITY`, `RELATE_TX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `RELATE_MAX_OPEN_TRANSACTIONS`, `RELATE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `RELATE_WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `RELATE_HEADER_DEADLINE_SECS`, `RELATE_BODY_DEADLINE_SECS` | [`relate serve`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/)                                                                              |
| `relate pull`                        | `NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USERNAME` (or `NEO4J_USER`), `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, `NEO4J_DATABASE`, read when `--from` is not given                                                                                               | [`relate pull`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/pull/)                                                                                |
| `relate push`                        | `NEO4J_USERNAME` (or `NEO4J_USER`), `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, `NEO4J_DATABASE`, read when `--to` is a Query API URI rather than an env file                                                                                | [`relate push`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/push/)                                                                                |
| `relate upgrade`, `relate extension` | `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL`, `RELATE_EXTENSIONS_JSON_URL`, `RELATE_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_URL`, `RELATE_GITHUB_API_URL`                                                                                   | [`relate upgrade`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/upgrade/), [`relate extension`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/extension/) |
| Every `--help` page                  | `RELATE_HELP_EXAMPLES`: `0`, `false`, `off` or `no`, in any case, drops the `Examples:` section; any other value keeps it                                                                                          | [relate CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/)                                                                                        |

The four URL variables are for development and testing. Each replaces one default URL, and an empty value means the default.

properties.heading: Durability and storage
properties.text:
These set the defaults for a persistent store's write path and snapshot. `:memory:` has no WAL or snapshot, so only `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` is checked there.

| Variable                          | Flag                         | Accepted values                                                                                          | An invalid value                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE`          | `--durability-mode`          | `full` (default), `everysecond`, `snapshot`                                                              | Exit 2: `Error: invalid RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE: semantic error: invalid durability mode "<value>"; expected full, everysecond, or snapshot`                                                                                            |
| `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS` | `--checkpoint-interval-secs` | Whole seconds, default `300`; `0` turns the timer off                                                    | Ignored: the default `300` applies                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`          | `--snapshot-format`          | `parquet` (default), `json`, `markdown`, for an empty directory                                          | Exit 1: `Failed to open Relate: storage error: unknown snapshot codec '<value>' (expected parquet, json, markdown or rkyv)`                                                                                                            |
| `RELATE_MARKDOWN_BODY_PROPERTIES` | `--markdown-body-properties` | The flag's list grammar; default `body`                                                                  | Exit 1: `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: invalid markdown body properties '<value>': an entry names no property`                                                                                                                |
| `RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES`       | none                         | The target size of one Parquet shard written at a checkpoint, `1` to `1073741824` bytes; default 256 MiB | The checkpoint fails, exit 1, after the run's statements have committed to the WAL: `Error: final checkpoint failed: storage error: RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES must be an integer in 1..=1073741824`; an empty value fails the same way |

On an existing store, `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` must name the store's recorded [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec), or the open fails with exit 1: `Failed to open Relate: storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is <codec>, requested <codec>`. The message lists `rkyv`, which the release binary is not built with: `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT=rkyv` fails the open with exit 1 and `Failed to open Relate: storage error: rkyv snapshot codec is not compiled into this build (enable the "rkyv-codec" feature)`. `relate serve` takes no `--checkpoint-interval-secs` flag, so `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS` is how a server's checkpoint timer is set. Only a checkpoint that writes Parquet shards reads `RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES`, so a run on `:memory:`, a `--read-only` open, and a `json` codec store never check it. The [durability modes guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/durability-modes/) covers each mode's loss window.

properties.heading: Engine diagnostics
properties.text:
Three variables tune the query engine and are read once at open. They exist for measurement, not for routine tuning.

| Variable                      | Accepted values                                                                                                     | An invalid value                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_PATTERN_ENGINE`       | `auto` (default), `nfa`, `walk`: which pattern-matching engine serves a clause                                      | Exit 1: `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: invalid RELATE_PATTERN_ENGINE: semantic error: invalid pattern engine "<value>"; expected auto, nfa, or walk` |

| `RELATE_BULK_BATCH_BUDGET`    | A positive integer, default `25000`: the estimated entities per batch commit                                        | Exit 1: `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: invalid RELATE_BULK_BATCH_BUDGET '<value>'`                                                                   |
