properties.heading: Limits
properties.text:
These bound one run's memory, traversal depth, printed rows, and local file access. Each is a safety limit, not a store property: a different run can open the same store with different limits.

| Variable                                    | Flag                                   | Accepted values                                                                           | An invalid value                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT`           | `--logical-graph-size-limit`           | A size: bytes, or a number with `mb`, `mib`, `gb` or `gib`; `0` is unlimited, the default | Exit 2: `Error: invalid RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT: semantic error: invalid memory limit '<value>'`                                       |
| `RELATE_EXPRESSION_MEMORY_LIMIT`            | `--expression-memory-limit`            | A size, or `none` or `0` for no cap; default 256 MiB                                      | Exit 2: `Error: invalid RELATE_EXPRESSION_MEMORY_LIMIT: invalid memory limit '<value>'`                                                        |
| `RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT` | `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` | A positive size turns query admission on; unset leaves it off                             | Exit 2: `Error: invalid RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT: must be positive` for `0`                                                   |
| `RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH`                | `--max-traversal-depth`                | `1` through `2000`; default `500`                                                         | Exit 2: `Error: invalid RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH: must be between 1 and 2000`                                                                |
| `RELATE_MAX_ROWS`                           | `--max-rows`                           | A non-negative integer; `0` is unlimited                                                  | Exit 2: `Error: invalid RELATE_MAX_ROWS: '<value>' is not a non-negative integer`                                                              |
| `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`                       | `--load-csv-dir`                       | A directory local `LOAD CSV` may read; unset denies every local file                      | Exit 1 at open: `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: LOAD CSV invalid configuration`, for a directory that does not exist or an empty value |

[Size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/) works through the memory limits.

properties.heading: Paths and terminal
properties.text:
| Variable          | Read by                                           | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Usage metrics, `relate extension`, `relate skill` | The config directory is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/` when the value is set, non-empty and an absolute path; otherwise `$HOME/.config/relate/`; without `HOME`, `$APPDATA/relate/`, then `$USERPROFILE/.config/relate/` (each only as an absolute path). It holds `config.json`, `state.json` and installed extensions. `relate skill` also resolves agent directories under it |
| `HOME`            | The same                                          | The base of `~/.config/relate/` and of the agent directories `relate skill install` writes to                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `COLUMNS`         | The `table` output mode                           | The wrap width when stdout is not a terminal and `--width` is not given; a value under `20` is ignored, and the table keeps its natural width                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

The config directory follows `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. In this run, the config file in `./cfg/relate/` turns metrics off, and `DO_NOT_TRACK` is removed from the command's environment so the file is the layer that decides:

```bash verify
mkdir -p cfg/relate
printf '{"telemetry":false}\n' > cfg/relate/config.json
env -u DO_NOT_TRACK XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$PWD/cfg" relate telemetry status
```

```text
disabled (config file)
```

`COLUMNS` wraps a piped table. The widest column shrinks, and its cell continues on the next line:

```bash verify
COLUMNS=20 relate --mode table "UNWIND ['engineer', 'maintainer'] AS role RETURN role, size(role) AS len"
```

```text
+------------+-----+
| role       | len |
+------------+-----+
| "engineer" | 8   |
| "maintaine | 10  |
| r"         |     |
+------------+-----+
```

properties.heading: Precedence
Preview features
properties.text:
`RELATE_PREVIEW` turns on [preview features](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#preview-feature): a comma-separated list of feature names, read once when the store opens. Unset or empty turns on nothing. With `coll-zip` named, the `coll.zip` function exists:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=coll-zip relate --mode envelope "RETURN coll.zip([1, 2], ['a', 'b']) AS pairs"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["LIST"],"columns":["pairs"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"pairs":[[1,"a"],[2,"b"]]}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.500958,"execute_ms":0.357792,"lex_parse_ms":0.024290999999999997,"lower_ms":0.034375,"parse_ms":0.092541,"plan_ms":0.042917000000000004,"result_generation_ms":0.000959,"rewrite_ms":0.007333},"truncated":false}
```

An unknown name fails the open with exit 1, and the message lists every name the binary knows:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=bogus relate --mode jsonl "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: semantic error: SemanticError: invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature 'bogus' (known features: hybrid-search, local-callables, graph-type-opt-props, graph-type-default-values, graph-type-implied-labels, ontology, obfuscated-literals, mixed-label-syntax, float16-coordinate-types, chronological-comparisons, complex-search-patterns, coll-zip, coll-has, gql-stddev-aliases)
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: SemanticError: invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature 'bogus' (known features: hybrid-search, local-callables, graph-type-opt-props, graph-type-default-values, graph-type-implied-labels, ontology, obfuscated-literals, mixed-label-syntax, float16-coordinate-types, chronological-comparisons, complex-search-patterns, coll-zip, coll-has, gql-stddev-aliases)","retryable":false}}
exit=1
```

On `relate serve`, the variable is the server process's setting: a feature it turns on is on for every connected client.

properties.heading: Retired names
properties.text:
Three retired names are refused rather than ignored, because an unset limit means unlimited and a store would otherwise open uncapped. Setting one fails the open with exit 1:

| Retired name                         | Message                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_MEMORY_LIMIT`                | `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: RELATE_MEMORY_LIMIT is set but ignored; set RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT`                          |
| `RELATE_TOKEN_ADMISSION`             | `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: RELATE_TOKEN_ADMISSION is set but ignored; set RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT`             |
| `RELATE_CONCURRENT_PEAK_TOKEN_LIMIT` | `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: RELATE_CONCURRENT_PEAK_TOKEN_LIMIT is set but ignored; set RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT` |

Any variable whose name starts with `CYPHERLITE_`, the product's former prefix, is refused too when its value is not empty or blank, even a name relate never read. The check runs before anything else, so every command fails with exit 1, `--help` and `--version` included, and the message names the matching `RELATE_` name:

```bash verify
CYPHERLITE_MAX_ROWS=1 relate "RETURN 1 AS x"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: semantic error: CYPHERLITE_MAX_ROWS is set but ignored; set RELATE_MAX_ROWS
exit=1
```

properties.heading: Safety and agent mode
properties.text:
`RELATE_SAFE_MODE` and `RELATE_AGENT_MODE` take `1` or `0`, with surrounding whitespace ignored. Any other value exits 2 before a statement runs.

| Variable            | Flags                             | `1`                                                                                      | `0`                                | An invalid value                                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RELATE_SAFE_MODE`  | `--safe`, `--no-safe`             | Safe mode on: an unbounded `MATCH` read and a new named node without a label are refused | Off, the default                   | `Error: invalid RELATE_SAFE_MODE: '<value>' is not 1 or 0`       |
| `RELATE_AGENT_MODE` | `--agent-mode`, `--no-agent-mode` | Agent mode on, announced on stderr                                                       | Off, even under a detected harness | `Error: invalid RELATE_AGENT_MODE: '<value>' is neither 1 nor 0` |

With `RELATE_AGENT_MODE` unset, agent mode turns on when stdout is not a terminal and one of these variables is set to a non-empty value: `AI_AGENT`, `AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE`, `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID`, `REPL_ID`, `GEMINI_CLI`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `OPENCODE`, `AUGMENT_AGENT`, `GOOSE_PROVIDER` or `CURSOR_AGENT`. It also turns on when `EDITOR` contains `devin`, `TERM_PROGRAM` contains `kiro`, or `PATH` contains `.pi/agent`, each matched case-insensitively. Detection prints nothing. Agent mode, whether set or detected, turns on neither `--read-only` nor safe mode. The [agent mode page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#detection) has the detection ladder and the two defaults agent mode changes.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
<NAME>=<value> relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]
<NAME>=<value> relate <COMMAND> [ARGS]
```

| Rule                  | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Precedence            | Flag, then environment variable, then built-in default                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Empty value           | An empty or blank value counts as unset, except `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR` (the open fails, exit 1) and `RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES` (the checkpoint fails, exit 1)                                                             |
| When it is read       | Once per run, before the first statement; engine variables are read when the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) opens; `RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES` at each checkpoint that writes Parquet shards |
| Invalid value         | Exit 2 for a variable the CLI parses, exit 1 for one the engine parses at open; the messages are in the tables on this page, and an open failure prints `Failed to open Relate: ` before its message                      |
| `--help`, `--version` | Still print and exit 0 when a variable holds an invalid value, except a set `CYPHERLITE_*` variable ([retired names](#retired-names))                                                                                     |
| Scope                 | The CLI process and every store it opens; `relate serve` reads the engine variables when it opens the store it serves                                                                                                     |

properties.heading: Usage metrics
properties.text:
The CLI's anonymous usage metrics, its [telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#telemetry), are on by default. The first layer that decides wins:

| Order | Setting                                                                           | Turns metrics off     | Turns metrics on    |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------- |
| 1     | `DO_NOT_TRACK`                                                                    | `1` or `true`         | —                   |
| 2     | `RELATE_TELEMETRY`                                                                | `0`, `false` or `off` | `1`, `true` or `on` |
| 3     | `config.json` in the config directory, written by `relate telemetry off` and `on` | `false`               | `true`              |
| 4     | The default                                                                       | —                     | on                  |

A `RELATE_TELEMETRY` value outside those six falls through to the next layer. `relate telemetry status` names the layer that decided:

```bash verify
DO_NOT_TRACK=1 RELATE_TELEMETRY=1 relate telemetry status
```

```text
disabled (DO_NOT_TRACK)
```

Two more variables exist for development and testing: `RELATE_MIXPANEL_ENDPOINT` replaces the `/track` URL (an `https://` URL, or `http://` for a loopback host only; a rejected value turns metrics off for the run with one warning on stderr), and `RELATE_MIXPANEL_TOKEN` replaces the project token. Since relate 0.1.0 an exit writes its events to the spool instead of waiting for a delivery, so `RELATE_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_MS` is gone. Each event's `invoker` property is `agent` when `CLAUDECODE`, `CURSOR_AGENT`, `GEMINI_CLI` or `OPENCODE` is set, else `ci` when `CI` is set to a value other than empty, `0` or `false`, else `human`. The [privacy and telemetry page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/#turning-usage-metrics-off) lists every event and property.

properties.heading: Exit codes and errors
properties.text: Every `relate` run ends with an [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) from one closed table, and each code has an anchor on this page, `https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors#exit-<n>`. A failed query run prints its message on stderr; in the `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope` and `speedscope` output modes it also prints one [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object) on stdout, whose `code` names the class and whose `exit_code` equals the process exit code. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/) holds one row per error message.

properties.heading: A failure in four output modes
properties.text:
The statement in this cell divides by zero, which the engine rejects as a type error:

```cypher run name=divide expect=error
RETURN 1/0 AS x
```

```table
error: type error: / by zero
```

The terminal prints what relate prints for the same statement in `table`, `envelope`, `jsonl` and `toon`, with the exit code. The statement runs in the browser on the engine the page loads, on an empty database opened read-only, as `relate --read-only` opens one. The exit code and the error's class follow from the error kind through the classes in the errors reference. Its presets include a syntax error, a missing parameter, a refused write and a run of three statements that stops at the second.

The statement as relate 1.0.1 prints it in four of its output modes, rendered from this page's recorded result by the terminal's renderers, which match the relate 1.0.1 binary byte for byte on the recorded runs, timing values aside. The recording keeps no timings, so each one shows as `<ms>`; relate prints the milliseconds of its own run, and the live terminal prints the engine's. Exit code 6, as relate 1.0.1 returns it.

relate classes this failure as `validation_error`, kind `type`, retryable `false` ([engine-division-by-zero](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-division-by-zero)).

`--mode table` prints one line on stderr:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode table 'RETURN 1/0 AS x'
```

```text
type error: / by zero
```

`--mode envelope` prints one line on stderr, then one on stdout:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode envelope 'RETURN 1/0 AS x'
```

```text
type error: / by zero
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"type","message":"type error: / by zero","retryable":false}}
```

`--mode jsonl` prints one line on stderr, then one on stdout:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode jsonl 'RETURN 1/0 AS x'
```

```text
type error: / by zero
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"type","message":"type error: / by zero","retryable":false}}
```

`--mode toon` prints one line on stderr:

```bash
relate --read-only --mode toon 'RETURN 1/0 AS x'
```

```text
type error: / by zero
```

Live: the statement runs in your browser on an empty read-only database, as `relate --read-only` opens one, and the pane shows what relate prints in the mode you pick, with the exit code and, under "Run as an agent harness", the row cap; the statement can be edited or swapped for a preset.

properties.heading: A multi-statement run that stops
properties.text:
When a run of several statements stops at a failure, stderr gains one line saying how far it got, and the error object gains `statement`, `statements` and `committed`:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "CREATE (:T {n: 1}); RETRN 2; RETURN 3 AS x"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.539084,"execute_ms":0.388542,"lex_parse_ms":0.003583,"lower_ms":0.003083,"parse_ms":0.1435,"plan_ms":0.001583,"result_generation_ms":0.000167,"rewrite_ms":0.00025},"truncated":false}
syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "RETRN"
  RETRN 2
  ^
statement 2 of 3 failed; 1 completed and committed; 1 not run
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","column":1,"committed":1,"exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: parse error: unexpected token \"RETRN\"   RETRN 2   ^","retryable":false,"source":"RETRN 2","statement":2,"statements":3}}
exit=6
```

The first statement's write is committed; the third statement never ran. A run of several statements has no all-or-nothing flag, so `committed` is what a caller reads to know what changed.

properties.heading: Exit 0: success
properties.text:
An empty result is a success too: the envelope keeps its columns and `rows` is `[]`.

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
relate --mode envelope "MATCH (n:Nope) RETURN n.p AS p"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["ok"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"ok":1}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.34937500000000005,"execute_ms":0.201167,"lex_parse_ms":0.029709,"lower_ms":0.029207999999999998,"parse_ms":0.09624999999999999,"plan_ms":0.042583,"result_generation_ms":0.000292,"rewrite_ms":0.0065},"truncated":false}
exit=0
{"columnTypes":["ANY"],"columns":["p"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.352833,"execute_ms":0.205334,"lex_parse_ms":0.026416,"lower_ms":0.036291000000000004,"parse_ms":0.093209,"plan_ms":0.047166,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.007292},"truncated":false}
exit=0
```

properties.heading: Exit 1: a store that does not exist
properties.text:
A `--read-only` open never creates a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), so a missing path fails the open with the error kind `storage`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./missing.rl --read-only --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: storage error: database not found: <dir>/missing.rl
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"storage","message":"storage error: database not found: <dir>/missing.rl","retryable":false}}
exit=1
```

The stderr line carries the prefix `Failed to open Relate:`; the object's `message` does not.

properties.heading: Exit 2: a usage error
properties.text:
An unknown flag exits before the store opens, so even `--mode envelope` prints no error object:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --bogus "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: unknown flag: --bogus
Usage: relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]
Run 'relate --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

A command's usage error names that command's usage line and help. The [flags page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#how-flags-are-parsed) lists the parsing rules behind these errors.

properties.heading: Exit 5: a locked store
properties.text:
A second process opening a store another process holds for writing fails with the error kind `locked`. This run is recorded with a second `relate query` holding `s.rl` open:

```text
Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <dir>/s.rl
{"error":{"code":"conflict","exit_code":5,"kind":"locked","message":"storage locked: <dir>/s.rl","retryable":false}}
```

`retryable` is `false`: the same open fails until the other process exits. A directory store can be opened with `--read-only` beside its writer; [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/) covers the options.

properties.heading: Exit 6: a rejected statement
properties.text:
The error kinds `syntax`, `semantic`, `argument` and `type` exit 6. A type error raised while the statement runs is one of them:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "RETURN 1/0 AS x"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
type error: / by zero
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"type","message":"type error: / by zero","retryable":false}}
exit=6
```

A syntax error adds `column` and `source`, shown in the [synopsis](#synopsis). A write on a `--read-only` store is a `semantic` error, also exit 6.

properties.heading: Exit 7: a timeout
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --timeout 100ms "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS a UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS b RETURN count(*) AS pairs"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: query timed out after 100ms
{"error":{"code":"timeout","exit_code":7,"kind":"execution","message":"query timed out after 100ms","retryable":false}}
exit=7
```

properties.heading: Exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code | Code               | Meaning                                                                                                                     | Error kinds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Retry                                                               |
| --------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`       | `success`          | Success, including an empty result. `--help` and `--version` also exit 0.                                                   | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                                                                   |
| `1`       | `fatal_error`      | Runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error, failed final checkpoint. | [`execution`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-execution), [`capacity`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-capacity), [`resource`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-resource), [`storage`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-storage), [`semantic`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-live-freshness-unsupported), [`io`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-io), [`internal`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-internal) | No: `retryable` is `false`.                                         |
| `2`       | `usage_error`      | Unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional.                                                                       | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                                                                   |
| `3`       | `not_found`        | Reserved (shared with neo4j-cli); not produced.                                                                             | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                                                                   |
| `4`       | `auth_error`       | Reserved (shared with neo4j-cli); not produced.                                                                             | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                                                                   |
| `5`       | `conflict`         | Write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener.                                                             | [`conflict`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-conflict), [`locked`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Only kind `conflict` (`retryable` is `true`); kind `locked` is not. |
| `6`       | `validation_error` | The statement is rejected: syntax, semantic, argument or type error, including a write on a `--read-only` database.         | [`syntax`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-validation-error-syntax), [`semantic`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-validation-error-semantic), [`argument`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-validation-error-argument), [`type`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-validation-error-type)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | No: `retryable` is `false`.                                         |
| `7`       | `timeout`          | A statement exceeded `--timeout`.                                                                                           | [`execution`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-timeout)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | No: `retryable` is `false`.                                         |
| `8`       | `upstream_error`   | Reserved (shared with neo4j-cli); not produced.                                                                             | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | —                                                                   |

The kinds and the retry advice come from the CLI entries of the [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/); a query run's error object carries them as `kind` and `retryable`.

Exit codes 3, 4 and 8 are reserved and never produced.

`relate agent-context` prints the same table for the installed binary, without the reserved rows. Each entry in the Error kinds column links that kind's own anchor in the errors reference, such as [`#cli-validation-error-syntax`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-validation-error-syntax) for a syntax error and [`#cli-timeout`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-timeout) for a timeout.

properties.heading: How the exit code and the error object relate
properties.text:
`code` and `exit_code` always name the same row. `kind` says which engine error variant produced it, so one exit code covers several kinds:

| `kind`                                                                                           | `code`             | Exit code | `retryable`                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `syntax`, `semantic`, `argument`, `type`                                                         | `validation_error` | 6         | `false`                                                                                                |
| `execution`, `capacity`, `storage`, `io`, `internal`                                             | `fatal_error`      | 1         | `false`                                                                                                |
| `semantic`, for a store that fails to open on an invalid engine setting such as `RELATE_PREVIEW` | `fatal_error`      | 1         | `false`                                                                                                |
| `resource`, a `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` refusal                                     | `fatal_error`      | 1         | `true` while other statements hold the shared pool; `false` when the statement alone exceeds the limit |
| `execution`, for a statement cancelled by `--timeout`                                            | `timeout`          | 7         | `false`                                                                                                |
| `conflict`                                                                                       | `conflict`         | 5         | `true`                                                                                                 |
| `locked`                                                                                         | `conflict`         | 5         | `false`                                                                                                |

Exit codes 0 and 2 never come with an error object: 0 is success, and a usage error is caught before any statement runs. The message of each error, with its cause and remedy, is in the [CLI errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-errors) and [engine errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-errors) tables.

properties.heading: Recorded runs
properties.text: Each run shows stderr and stdout as one stream, in the order relate wrote them, then the exit code. A path inside the run's directory prints as `<dir>`.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/): every message, with its cause, remedy, retry advice, and exit code
- [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/): the envelope a successful run prints
- [Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/): branching on exit codes in a shell script
- [Drive relate from an agent](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/drive-relate-from-an-agent/): reading the error object from an agent

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
A failed statement in `--mode envelope`, with the exit code echoed:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "MATCH (n RETURN n"
echo "exit=$?"
```

The first three lines are stderr, the fourth is stdout:

```text
syntax error: parse error: expected RightParen, got "RETURN" (RETURN)
  MATCH (n RETURN n
           ^
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","column":10,"exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: parse error: expected RightParen, got \"RETURN\" (RETURN)   MATCH (n RETURN n            ^","retryable":false,"source":"MATCH (n RETURN n"}}
exit=6
```

| Run                                                                                                  | stderr                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | stdout                                             | Exit code     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Query run that succeeds                                                                              | Diagnostics only: warnings, notes, `table`-mode plans                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | The results                                        | 0             |
| Query run that fails, in `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope` or `speedscope`                                 | The message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Any results already printed, then one error object | 1, 5, 6, or 7 |
| Query run that fails, in `table`, `csv`, `markdown`, `cypher` or `toon` (agent mode's piped default) | The message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Nothing extra                                      | 1, 5, 6, or 7 |
| Usage error, in any mode                                                                             | `Error: <message>`. An unknown flag, an unexpected argument, a missing value, a `--read-only` value not attached, or an unknown `--namespace` adds the usage line and a `--help` hint; a value rejected after parsing (`--mode`, `--timeout`, `--width`, `--max-rows`, `--param`, `--command` with a positional query, `RELATE_AGENT_MODE`) prints the `Error:` line alone | Nothing                                            | 2             |
| A command (`clone`, `skill`, `info`, …)                                                              | Its own messages                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Its own output; never an error object              | 0, 1, or 2    |

A run of several statements stops at the first one that fails and exits with that statement's code.

properties.heading: The error object
properties.text:
A query run (a one-shot statement or a piped script) that fails in `--mode json`, `--mode jsonl`, `--mode envelope` or `--mode speedscope` prints one compact JSON object on stdout, after any results already written, on one line. It carries no `timings` or `planCache`. Its keys are sorted alphabetically, as in every JSON mode.

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: …","retryable":false}}
```

| Field        | Type    | Present                                                           | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `code`       | string  | always                                                            | The class name from the exit code table: `fatal_error`, `conflict`, `validation_error` or `timeout`                                                                                               |
| `exit_code`  | number  | always                                                            | The process exit code, equal to the table row of `code`                                                                                                                                           |
| `kind`       | string  | always                                                            | The engine's error variant: `syntax`, `semantic`, `argument`, `type`, `execution`, `conflict`, `capacity`, `resource`, `storage`, `locked`, `io` or `internal`                                    |
| `message`    | string  | always                                                            | The text also printed on stderr, sanitized to one line                                                                                                                                            |
| `retryable`  | boolean | always                                                            | `true` for a write-write conflict and for a `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` refusal while other statements hold the workspace pool; a locked store is `false` until its other opener exits |
| `statement`  | number  | multi-statement runs                                              | The 1-based index of the failed statement                                                                                                                                                         |
| `statements` | number  | with `statement`                                                  | How many statements the input held                                                                                                                                                                |
| `committed`  | number  | with `statement`                                                  | How many earlier statements are durable; `0` inside an open `.begin` transaction                                                                                                                  |
| `column`     | number  | syntax errors, when known                                         | The 1-based character column within `source`                                                                                                                                                      |
| `source`     | string  | syntax errors, when known                                         | The statement line the parser echoed                                                                                                                                                              |
| `line`       | number  | syntax errors, when the parser gave a position but no source line | The 1-based line within the statement                                                                                                                                                             |

A position field is left out, never `null` or `0`, when the position is unknown. New fields may be added; existing fields and `code` values are never renamed or given a new meaning.

The CLI error object carries no GQL status code. Where an engine error has one, its row in the errors reference names it, and the [GQL status index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#gql-status-index) lists every status at its own anchor (`#gql-42n02`). The Python exception classes and the HTTP, Bolt and MCP errors are on the same page.

properties.heading: relate extension
properties.text: `relate extension` manages [extensions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#extension): packages that add an action to the CLI, run as [`relate run <name>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/run/). It has five actions. `init` scaffolds a new package, `check` tests a package directory without installing it, `install` puts a package on the machine from one of four sources, `list` prints what is installed, and `remove` uninstalls one. Only `install` and `list --available` use the network; the other actions read and write local files, and none of them opens a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store).

properties.heading: check
properties.text:
`relate extension check <dir>` runs the package through six stages, in the order a mount uses them, printing one line per stage and stopping at the first failure:

| Stage                       | Passes when                                                                                                                                                  | Exit code on failure |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `manifest`                  | `extension.json` decodes, its executable stays inside the directory, its name is not a reserved command word, and its protocol is the one this binary serves | 2                    |
| `executable`                | The file exists, is a regular file, and is executable                                                                                                        | 2                    |
| `spawn`                     | The executable starts and takes its flag defaults on stdin                                                                                                   | 1                    |
| `initialize`                | Its first request is `initialize`, for the protocol this binary serves                                                                                       | 1                    |
| `notifications/initialized` | It confirms the handshake                                                                                                                                    | 1                    |
| `tools/list`                | Any tool it calls is one of the five the mount serves                                                                                                        | 1                    |

A package that passes every stage gets a seventh line about its GitHub pin (`pin: approved`, `pin: drifted`, `pin: not from a GitHub source (<tier>)` or `pin: unknown`), which never changes the exit code. `check` opens no store, installs nothing and fetches nothing, but the `spawn` stage starts the package's executable, so any code the package runs when it starts runs with the user's permissions; it is not a sandbox. Each stage waits at most ten seconds. It exits 0 when the package would mount.

properties.heading: Environment
properties.text:
| Variable                      | Effect                                                                                                                     | Default                                                | Used by                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`                | Optional bearer token for release-asset downloads; required while the repository is internal.                              | —                                                      | `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install`                    |
| `RELATE_EXTENSIONS_JSON_URL`  | Override the extension channel-index URL (dev and test).                                                                   | `https://relatedb.ai/extensions.json`                  | `relate extension install`, `relate extension list --available` |
| `RELATE_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_URL` | Override the base of the direct release-download route (dev and test).                                                     | `https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases/download` | `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install`                    |
| `RELATE_GITHUB_API_URL`       | Override the base of the GitHub API asset route (dev and test).                                                            | `https://api.github.com`                               | `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install`                    |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`             | When set, non-empty and absolute, the config directory is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/`.                                      | —                                                      | usage metrics, `relate extension`, `relate skill`               |
| `HOME`                        | The fallback config directory `~/.config/relate/`, and the base of the agent directories `relate skill install` writes to. | —                                                      | usage metrics, `relate extension`, `relate skill`               |

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
Every action ends with one of three [exit codes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code).

| Exit code | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 0         | The action completed; for `check`, the package would mount                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 1         | A runtime failure: an existing `init` directory, a source that cannot be read or fetched, a failed verification, a tier or name conflict, a missing marker on `remove`, a name that is not installed, a `check` stage that fails when the package runs |
| 2         | A usage error, or a `check` failure in the manifest or the executable. A usage error is followed by the five usage lines and `Run 'relate extension --help' for more information.`                                                                     |

| Message on stderr                                                                                                                                                               | Exit code |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| `Error: extension requires an action (init, install, list, remove or check)`                                                                                                    | 2         |
| `Error: extension init: <dir>/<name> already exists (init writes a new package directory)`                                                                                      | 1         |
| `Error: extension init: '<name>' is not a valid package name (a single directory name, no path separators)`                                                                     | 2         |
| `Error: extension init: unknown --lang value '<value>' (expected sh, py, ts or rust)`                                                                                           | 2         |
| `Error: extension name '<name>' collides with the reserved command word '<word>'`                                                                                               | 2         |
| `Error: extension install: --url accepts only https URLs (or plain http to the loopback interface); '<url>' is neither`                                                         | 2         |
| `Error: extension install: --github '<value>' needs a pin: owner/repo@tag or owner/repo@<full-commit-sha> (an untagged repository is a moving target)`                          | 2         |
| `Error: extension install: --url and --from are mutually exclusive (they both name the install source)`                                                                         | 2         |
| `Error: extension install: --github is mutually exclusive with --url and --from (each names the install source)`                                                                | 2         |
| `Error: extension install: --re-approve and --approve <commit-sha> only apply to --github installs`                                                                             | 2         |
| `Error: extension install --approve requires a full 40-hex commit sha`                                                                                                          | 2         |
| `Error: extension install: the package's manifest names '<manifest name>' but the install was for '<name>'`                                                                     | 1         |
| `Error: extension install: extension '<name>' is installed <tier> (source: <source>); refusing a third-party install over it — remove it first: relate extension remove <name>` | 1         |
| `Error: extension remove: no installed extension '<name>' (relate extension list prints the installed set)`                                                                     | 1         |
| `Error: extension remove: refusing to remove <path>: no .relate-provenance.json marker present (the directory was not installed by relate; remove it manually)`                 | 1         |
| `Error: extension list: --trust and --available ask different questions (recorded pins vs the channel catalog)`                                                                 | 2         |

When the channel index cannot be read, the message names its URL. This run had `RELATE_EXTENSIONS_JSON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8874/extensions.json` with nothing listening; the text after `io:` comes from the operating system, and this recording is from macOS:

```text
Error: extension list: could not read the extension channel index from http://127.0.0.1:8874/extensions.json: GET http://127.0.0.1:8874/extensions.json: io: Connection refused (os error 61)
```

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The examples run in a fresh directory, written `<dir>`, with a fresh home, written `<home>`, and no `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Nothing is installed yet, so `list` prints nothing and exits 0:

```bash verify
relate extension list
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
exit=0
```

`init` scaffolds a package with a shell executable:

```bash verify
relate extension init team-import --lang sh
```

```text
created sh extension 'team-import' in <dir>/team-import
  extension.json  the manifest (mount name, MCP revision, flag table)
  team-import.sh  the executable: generated glue plus your walk()
  README.md       the quickstart for this package

next:
  relate extension install team-import --from <dir>/team-import
  relate run team-import -d ./store
```

`check` runs it through the six stages without installing it. The `initialize` line names the binary's version:

```bash verify
relate extension check team-import
```

```text
manifest: ok (team-import 0.1.0, protocol 2025-06-18)
executable: ok (team-import.sh)
spawn: ok
initialize: ok (MCP 2025-06-18, server relate 1.0.1)
notifications/initialized: ok
tools/list: ok (the shared tool table: 5 tools; the extension calls 'write_cypher')
pin: not from a GitHub source (unmarked)
```

`install --from` installs it as a local package, and `list` shows the tier and the source:

```bash verify
relate extension install team-import --from ./team-import
relate extension list
```

```text
installed local extension team-import 0.1.0 from ./team-import
team-import 0.1.0 local ./team-import
```

A plain `http` URL to another host is refused before any fetch:

```bash verify
relate extension install other-import --url http://example.com/other-import.tar.gz
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: extension install: --url accepts only https URLs (or plain http to the loopback interface); 'http://example.com/other-import.tar.gz' is neither
exit=2
```

`remove` deletes the installed package:

```bash verify
relate extension remove team-import
```

```text
removed extension team-import (<home>/.config/relate/extensions/team-import)
```

properties.heading: init
properties.text:
`relate extension init <name>` creates `./<name>/` with three items (four for `--lang rust`) and prints them, with the two commands that install and run the package:

| File             | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extension.json` | A manifest with version `0.1.0`, the protocol revision this binary serves, one sample flag `--name` (default `there`), and `commit: per-batch`                                                                      |
| The executable   | `<name>.sh`, `<name>.py` (the default) or `<name>.ts`; for `--lang rust`, a Cargo project (`Cargo.toml`, `src/main.rs`) whose built binary, copied into the package directory, is the executable the manifest names |
| `README.md`      | The package's quickstart                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The `sh`, `py` and `ts` executables hold a generated protocol client inline, so they depend on no client library; the Rust project depends on the `relate-wire` crate instead. Each has a `walk()` function to edit. The sample writes one `:Scaffold` node and reports a greeting built from `--name`. An existing directory of that name is refused (exit code 1); a name with a path separator, a reserved command word as the name, or an unknown `--lang` is a usage error (exit code 2).

properties.heading: install
properties.text:
`relate extension install <name>` takes the package from one source. The source is the trust decision, and the marker records it as the package's tier:

| Tier          | Source flag                              | What is checked before anything lands                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `first-party` | None                                     | The channel index, `extensions.json`, verifies against the release signing key `relate upgrade` uses, and the package's SHA-256 matches its signed row; `--version V` picks a listed version, default the newest           |
| `github-pin`  | `--github OWNER/REPO@TAG` or `@<commit>` | The tag's commit and the asset's SHA-256 are recorded on the first install; a later install whose tag moved or whose asset changed is refused before any download unless `--re-approve` or `--approve <commit>` accepts it |
| `third-party` | `--url URL`                              | Nothing beyond the transport: `https` only, or plain `http` to the loopback interface; any other URL is refused before any fetch                                                                                           |
| `local`       | `--from DIR`                             | Nothing beyond the package rules: the directory is the trust act, and its executable must resolve inside it                                                                                                                |

Every tier then runs the same package rules (the manifest decodes, the executable stays inside the package, the protocol matches, the name collides with no command and no installed extension) in a staging directory beside the destination, writes the marker, and renames the package into place. A failed install leaves nothing behind. On success it prints one line naming the tier, the name, the version and the source, such as `installed local extension team-import 0.1.0 from ./team-import`.

| Case                                      | Behavior                                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The name is installed from the same tier  | Reinstalled                                                                                       |
| The name is installed from another tier   | Refused, naming the installed tier and source; the refusal names `relate extension remove <name>` |
| The manifest's name differs from `<name>` | Refused                                                                                           |
| A target directory without a marker       | Refused unless `--force`                                                                          |

The [extension install guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/install-and-run/) walks through each tier, and the [security reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/) covers the signing key.

properties.heading: list
properties.text:
| Form               | Prints, one line per entry                                                                                                                         | Network                                          |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `list`             | `<name> <version> <tier> <source>`; a package placed by hand, without a marker, prints `<name> <version> unmarked`; nothing when none is installed | None                                             |
| `list --trust`     | The recorded GitHub pins: name, repository, tag, commit and asset SHA-256                                                                          | None                                             |
| `list --available` | The channel's catalog: name, newest version, protocol, and whether it is installed; a package marked hidden is left out                            | Required; offline, it fails naming the index URL |

`--available` and `--trust` together are a usage error.

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
| Flag           | Argument           | Default           | Scope              | Since | Description                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ------------------ | ----------------- | ------------------ | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--lang`       | `sh\|py\|ts\|rust` | `py`              | `relate extension` | —     | `init`: the template language.                                                                         |
| `--github`     | `REPO@TAG\|@SHA`   | unset             | `relate extension` | —     | `install`: a GitHub release pinned to a commit; the tag's commit and the asset's SHA-256 are recorded. |
| `--url`        | `URL`              | unset             | `relate extension` | —     | `install`: the tarball at an `https` URL (third party).                                                |
| `--from`       | `DIR`              | unset             | `relate extension` | —     | `install`: an unpacked package directory (local; no network, no signature).                            |
| `--version`    | `V`                | the newest listed | `relate extension` | —     | `install`: the channel version.                                                                        |
| `--force`      | —                  | off               | `relate extension` | —     | `install`: clobber a target directory without the install marker.                                      |
| `--re-approve` | —                  | off               | `relate extension` | —     | `install --github`: re-approve whatever the pin resolves to now.                                       |
| `--approve`    | `SHA`              | unset             | `relate extension` | —     | `install --github`: re-approve only this commit.                                                       |
| `--available`  | —                  | off               | `relate extension` | —     | `list`: the channel's catalog (the signed `extensions.json` index); fails closed offline.              |
| `--trust`      | —                  | off               | `relate extension` | —     | `list`: the recorded GitHub pins.                                                                      |
| `--forget-pin` | —                  | off               | `relate extension` | —     | `remove`: also clear the name's recorded GitHub pin.                                                   |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

Each flag belongs to one action, named in its row; a flag given to another action is a usage error. Of the `install` sources, `--github`, `--url` and `--from` name where the package comes from, and two of them together are a usage error; with none, the source is the first-party channel.

properties.heading: remove
properties.text: `relate extension remove <name>` deletes the package directory and prints `removed extension <name> (<path>)`. It requires the provenance marker: a directory without one, such as a package copied by hand, is refused with a message naming the path, and `remove` has no `--force`. A GitHub pin outlives the package, so a reinstall is still compared with it; `--forget-pin` clears the pin too.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [`relate run`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/run/): running an installed extension into a store
- [Install and run an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/install-and-run/): the tiers in practice
- [Write an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/write-an-extension/): from `init` to a working import
- [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/): the release signing key the first-party channel shares with `relate upgrade`
- [Problems relate solves: offline and sandboxed use](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#offline-and-sandboxed-use): the commands that reach the network

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate extension init <name> [--lang sh|py|ts|rust]
relate extension install <name> [--github REPO@TAG|@SHA] [--url URL] [--from DIR] [--version V] [--force] [--re-approve | --approve SHA]
relate extension list [--available | --trust]
relate extension remove <name> [--forget-pin]
relate extension check <dir>
```

| Action             | Does                                                                     | Network              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `init <name>`      | Creates the package directory `./<name>/`                                | None                 |
| `check <dir>`      | Runs a package directory through the stages a mount needs                | None                 |
| `install <name>`   | Verifies a package and installs it under the extensions directory        | Except with `--from` |
| `list`             | Prints the installed packages; `--trust` prints the recorded GitHub pins | None                 |
| `list --available` | Prints the first-party channel's catalog                                 | Required             |
| `remove <name>`    | Deletes an installed package                                             | None                 |

properties.heading: Where packages live
properties.text:
| Path                                            | Holds                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/extensions/<name>/`    | One installed package: `extension.json`, its executable, and the provenance marker `.relate-provenance.json` |
| `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/extensions-trust.json` | The recorded GitHub pins, one per extension name                                                             |

When `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset, empty or a relative path, `~/.config` takes its place. This directory is the only place relate looks for extensions: never the working directory, so a cloned repository cannot add an action to the CLI.

The manifest, `extension.json`, declares the package: `kind` (`command`), `name` (the action's name after `relate run`), `version`, `protocol` (the Model Context Protocol revision it speaks, `2025-06-18`), the `flags` table, `commit` (`per-batch` or `whole-import`) and `executable`, a path inside the package directory, and the optional `positional`, `requires-fresh-store` and `hidden`. The [`relate run` reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/run/#the-action-and-its-flags) covers the flags table, and [Write an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/write-an-extension/) the rest.

properties.heading: CLI flags
properties.text: Each flag of the `relate` CLI has a row on this page at a stable anchor, `https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags#<flag>` (`#read-only`, `#max-rows`); a command's own flag carries the command's name (`#serve-mcp`, `#clone-wal-dir`). A row gives the flag's other spellings, its argument, its default, where it applies, and the environment variable that sets its default. The tables are generated from the data file the CLI facts are recorded in, so the page and its markdown twin list the same flags.

properties.heading: Agent ergonomics
properties.text: `--agent-mode` and `--no-agent-mode` turn [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-mode) on or off: the 100-row cap default and the piped `toon` default. `--max-rows N` sets the cap directly; `0` prints every row. The [agent mode page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/) has the detection rules and what each output mode prints when the cap cuts a result.

properties.heading: Command flags
properties.text: Each command's own flags. `relate query` takes the query-run flags; `relate telemetry` and `relate agent-context` take no flags beyond `--help`.

properties.heading: Environment variables
properties.text:
