properties.heading: How flags are parsed
properties.text:
| Rule                   | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Values                 | A flag's value is the next argument: `--mode envelope`. The `=` form is an unknown flag (`--mode=envelope` exits 2).                                                                                                         |
| The one attached value | `--read-only` takes its optional value attached, `--read-only=live`. `--read-only live` exits 2 with `Error: --read-only takes its value attached: --read-only=live`.                                                        |
| Position               | Query-run flags may come before or after the statement: `relate "RETURN 1 AS ok" --mode envelope` runs.                                                                                                                      |
| One statement argument | A second positional statement exits 2 with `Error: unexpected argument: <statement>`. `--command` and a positional statement together exit 2 with `Error: --command cannot be combined with a positional query`.             |
| Other spellings        | Short forms `-d` (`--database`), `-c` (`--command`), `-h` (`--help`) and `-v` (`--version`); single-dash forms `-json`, `-csv`, `-jsonl`, `-markdown`, `-noheader`, `-param` and `-version`.                                 |
| Repeated flags         | `--param` and `--fetch-params` repeat, one parameter each; a `--param` name bound twice keeps the last value. `--read-only` may appear once: a second exits 2 with `Error: relate --read-only may be given only once`.       |
| Pairs and output flags | Of `--safe` and `--no-safe`, or `--agent-mode` and `--no-agent-mode`, the last one given wins. Of several output-mode flags (`--mode`, `--format`, `--json`, `--csv`, `--jsonl`, `--markdown`, `--toon`), the last one wins. |
| Precedence             | A flag beats its environment variable, which beats the built-in default.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Unknown flags          | Exit 2 with three lines on stderr: `Error: unknown flag: <flag>`, the usage line, and `Run 'relate --help' for more information.` A close match to a real flag adds `Did you mean '<flag>'?` after the first line.           |
| `--`                   | Every argument after it is positional.                                                                                                                                                                                       |

A misspelled flag gets its suggestion:

```bash verify
relate --readonly "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: unknown flag: --readonly
Did you mean '--read-only'?
Usage: relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]
Run 'relate --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

properties.heading: Memory limits
properties.text:
A `SIZE` is a number of bytes, or a number with `mb`, `mib`, `gb` or `gib`. A statement that exceeds `--logical-graph-size-limit` or `--expression-memory-limit` fails with the error kind `capacity` and exit code 1, and is not retryable.

| Flag                                        | Default       | Bounds                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--logical-graph-size-limit SIZE`           | unlimited     | The live graph plus its indexes, in logical bytes; `0` is unlimited                     |
| `--expression-memory-limit SIZE`            | `256 MiB`     | One value a statement builds; `none` or `0` turns the cap off                           |
| `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE` | admission off | A shared workspace pool; a positive value turns query admission on, and `0` is rejected |

[Size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/) works through a sizing.

properties.heading: Output
properties.text:
[Output modes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/) shows each mode's shape on stdout. Without an output flag, the mode depends on where stdout goes:

| stdout                                                                                     | Default mode |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| A terminal                                                                                 | `table`      |
| A pipe or a file                                                                           | `jsonl`      |
| A pipe or a file, with [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/) on | `toon`       |

An explicit mode always overrides the default. `--json`, `--csv`, `--jsonl`, `--markdown` and `--toon` are shortcuts for `--mode <name>`, and `--format` is an alias of `--mode`. `--output` and `-o` are unknown flags whose suggestion names `--format`.

| Mode         | Prints                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table`      | A human table; control characters escaped                                                                                                |
| `csv`        | RFC 4180 CSV; a value starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a `'` prefix, so `-5` prints as `'-5`                                      |
| `json`       | One JSON array; indented on a terminal, one compact line when piped                                                                      |
| `jsonl`      | One JSON object per row                                                                                                                  |
| `envelope`   | One compact JSON object per result set; fields on the [agent mode page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#the-envelope) |
| `markdown`   | A GitHub-flavored table; `\|` escaped                                                                                                    |
| `cypher`     | Each row as a Cypher `CREATE` statement                                                                                                  |
| `toon`       | One `rows[N]{cols}:` header, then one line per row; nested values as inline JSON                                                         |
| `speedscope` | A `PROFILE` plan tree as one speedscope profile JSON document                                                                            |

`--pretty` indents `json` output when stdout is not a terminal; the other modes ignore it. `--timings` adds each statement's `{"planCache":…,"timings":…}` line to `jsonl` output; it is off by default since 1.0.1, and the other modes ignore it ([timings and the plan cache](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache)). `--noheader` drops the header row of `table` and `csv`; `markdown` and `toon` keep theirs. `--width N` wraps the `table` mode to `N` columns; a value under 20 exits 2, and without it the width is the terminal's, else `COLUMNS`, else the natural width.

HTTP transport only for MCP. Environment: [`RELATE_AUTH`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-auth).               |

properties.heading: Safety
properties.text:
`--read-only` and `--safe` are off unless given, and agent detection switches neither on.

| Flag                      | Default | Refuses or bounds                                                                                                                                                                                              | Exit code                    |
| ------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `--read-only`             | off     | Every write: `WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase`                                                                                                                                                                   | 6                            |
| `--safe`                  | off     | A new named node without a label, and a `MATCH` read whose final `RETURN` or `WITH` has no `LIMIT` and no reducing aggregate (`collect()` does not count): `SafeModeViolation`. Also a remote `--load` source. | 6; 2 for the remote `--load` |
| `--load-csv-dir PATH`     | denied  | Local `LOAD CSV` outside `PATH`; a file over 8 MiB, a limit no flag raises                                                                                                                                     | 1                            |
| `--max-traversal-depth N` | `500`   | An explicit hop bound over `N` (1 through 2000): `TraversalDepthExceeded`                                                                                                                                      | 6                            |
| `--fetch-params N=SRC`    | unset   | A fetched file over 64 MiB, or a fetch over 60 seconds. There is no URL allowlist: the fetch runs in the CLI process with the same trust as `--param`.                                                         | 1                            |

`--no-safe` turns safe mode off, including when `RELATE_SAFE_MODE=1` set it. The errors behind the [exit codes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) are in the [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-safe-mode-violation).

properties.heading: Store and storage
properties.text:
`--database PATH` names the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store): a directory (a snapshot plus a [WAL](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal)), a single-file `.rl` store, or `:memory:`, the default. It is never a URL; a remote store is a `--load` source.

| Flag                              | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--load SOURCE`                   | Loads a store from a local `.rl` file, a directory, or an `https` URL to a `.rl` file. Into `:memory:`, the store opens read-only and the source is released after the load. Into a `--database` path that does not exist yet, the source is copied there and the store opens normally. A URL is fetched to a private temporary copy that is not kept.                                                                                                                                             |
| `--read-only[=snapshot\|live]`    | Opens an existing store without writing, checkpointing or migrating it; every write exits 6. `snapshot`, the default, freezes the state at open; `live` follows a directory store's WAL and is refused for `.rl` and `:memory:`. A directory store can be open read-only beside its writer; a `.rl` store only while no writer holds it.                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--namespace NAME`                | The namespace a statement without `USE` targets: `neo4j` (default), `system` or `system_ontologies`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--wal-dir DIR`                   | The WAL directory of a directory store, default `<DATABASE>/wal`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--snapshot-format F`             | The [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec) of an empty directory store: `parquet` (default), `json` or `markdown`. `parquet` writes one typed column per common property key ([Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#parquet-data-files)). An existing store keeps its recorded codec; naming a different one exits 1 with `storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is <codec>, requested <codec>`. Also accepted by `relate serve`. |
| `--markdown-body-properties LIST` | The properties a `markdown` store writes as note bodies; default `body`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--durability-mode MODE`          | `full` (default) syncs each commit before it is acknowledged. `everysecond` can lose about the last second of acknowledged writes in a crash. `snapshot` can lose every write since the last completed checkpoint.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `--checkpoint-interval-secs N`    | The timed checkpoint period, default `300`; `0` turns the timer off. Persistent stores only. Not accepted by `relate serve`, which reads only `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

The [durability modes guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/durability-modes/) covers choosing a loss window, and [storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/) covers the store forms.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]
relate <COMMAND> [ARGS]
relate query [STATEMENT] [--database PATH]
```

The query-run flags (`OPTIONS`) apply to the path-first form and to `relate query`. A command takes only its own flags, listed under [Command flags](#command-flags); `relate serve` also takes seven query-run flags, named in its table. The sections before the tables explain the flag families whose behavior a one-line row cannot carry.

properties.heading: Timeouts
properties.text:
`--timeout DURATION` bounds each statement's wall-clock time. A bare number is seconds; `ms`, `s` and `m` suffixes and fractions are accepted; `0` turns the bound off, and unset means no bound. A statement that runs longer is cancelled and exits 7 with `Error: query timed out after <duration>` on stderr; the error object's `code` is `timeout`, its `kind` is `execution`, and `retryable` is `false`. A value that is not a duration exits 2:

```bash verify
relate --timeout soon "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: invalid --timeout: 'soon' is not a duration (try 500ms, 10s, 2m)
exit=2
```

`relate serve` has its own deadlines instead: `--tx-idle-timeout-secs` (default `60`), `--header-deadline-secs` (default `10`) and `--body-deadline-secs` (default `60`), in its table.

properties.heading: relate info
properties.text: `relate info --database PATH` prints a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store)'s metadata and exits, without opening the store: no lock, no write-ahead log (WAL) replay, no graph load. It reports the layout, the [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec) and its format version, the last [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint), the size on disk, the WAL segments written since that checkpoint, the node and relationship counts at that checkpoint, and the index and [constraint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#constraint) catalog. The output is a key/value table, or one JSON object with `--json`. Because nothing is opened, `info` runs beside a process that has the store open.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code                                                                 | When                                                                             | Message on stderr                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [0](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-0) | The metadata printed                                                             | None                                                                                        |
| [1](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-1) | The store could not be read: a missing path, or a corrupt or unreadable manifest | `Failed to read store info: <detail>`, such as `storage error: database not found: <path>`  |
| [2](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-2) | No `--database`                                                                  | `Error: info requires --database`                                                           |
| 2                                                                         | `--database :memory:` or an empty path                                           | `Error: info cannot use :memory: or an empty --database path (info reads an on-disk store)` |
| 2                                                                         | `--json` twice                                                                   | `Error: info --json may be given only once`                                                 |
| 2                                                                         | An extra argument or an unknown flag                                             | `Error: unexpected argument to info: <argument>`                                            |
| 2                                                                         | `--read-only` before `info`                                                      | `Error: info cannot be combined with a query or an access flag (--read-only)`               |

Each exit 2 also prints the usage line and `Run 'relate info --help' for more information.` No failure prints an [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object).

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
These examples run in a new, empty directory. This first command writes: it creates the directory store `./team` with three people, two projects, and five relationships. The process checkpoints the store as it exits:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

The table for a directory store:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./team
```

```text
layout: native directory
codec: parquet
format version: 5
checkpoint LSN: 1
commit timestamp: 1
total bytes: 4032
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
relationships (at checkpoint LSN 1): 5
indexes: 0
constraints: 0
```

A `.rl` file with an index and two constraints. These four commands write: they create `catalog.rl` and add the schema, each commit checkpointed as its process exits:

```bash verify
relate --database ./catalog.rl "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(:Project {name: 'relate'})"
relate --database ./catalog.rl "CREATE INDEX person_name FOR (p:Person) ON (p.name)"
relate --database ./catalog.rl "CREATE CONSTRAINT project_name FOR (p:Project) REQUIRE p.name IS NOT NULL"
relate --database ./catalog.rl "CREATE CONSTRAINT works_since FOR ()-[w:WORKS_ON]-() REQUIRE w.since IS :: INTEGER"
```

```bash verify
relate info --database ./catalog.rl
```

```text
layout: .rl bundle
superblock version: 1
codec: parquet
format version: 5
checkpoint LSN: 4
commit timestamp: 4
total bytes: 45056
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 4): 2
relationships (at checkpoint LSN 4): 1
indexes: 1
  person_name: :Person(name)
constraints: 2
  project_name: exists node :Project(name)
  works_since: propertyType relationship :WORKS_ON(since) :: INTEGER
```

The same store as JSON, one line:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./catalog.rl --json
```

```text
{"checkpoint_lsn":4,"codec":"parquet","commit_ts":4,"constraints":[{"enforced_label":null,"kind":"exists","label":"Project","name":"project_name","properties":["name"],"property_type":null,"relationship":false},{"enforced_label":null,"kind":"propertyType","label":"WORKS_ON","name":"works_since","properties":["since"],"property_type":"INTEGER","relationship":true}],"format_version":5,"indexes":[{"label":"Person","name":"person_name","property":"name"}],"layout":"bundle","node_count":2,"rel_count":1,"superblock_version":1,"total_bytes":45056,"wal_segments":1}
```

A `json`-codec copy of `./team`, made with `relate clone`, reports what its manifest holds:

```bash verify
relate clone --to-snapshot-format json ./team ./team-json
relate info --database ./team-json
```

```text
layout: native directory
codec: json
format version: unavailable
checkpoint LSN: 1
commit timestamp: 1
total bytes: 1385
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
note: a JSON-codec store keeps the format version, counts and the index/constraint catalog in graph.json, which a cold info read never parses
nodes: unavailable
relationships: unavailable
indexes: unavailable
constraints: unavailable
```

A path with no store:

```bash verify
relate info --database ./missing
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to read store info: storage error: database not found: ./missing
exit=1
```

properties.heading: Fields
properties.text:
The counts are the checkpoint's, not the live graph's: commits since the last checkpoint sit in the WAL, which `info` does not replay. `wal segments past checkpoint` says how many WAL segments may hold them.

| Table key                               | JSON key             | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `layout`                                | `layout`             | `native directory` (`"native_dir"`) for a directory store, `.rl bundle` (`"bundle"`) for a single-file store                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `superblock version`                    | `superblock_version` | The `.rl` file's container version; a table line only for a `.rl` file, `null` for a directory store                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `codec`                                 | `codec`              | `parquet`, `json` or `markdown`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `format version`                        | `format_version`     | The snapshot format version                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `checkpoint LSN`                        | `checkpoint_lsn`     | The log sequence number (LSN) of the last checkpoint                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `commit timestamp`                      | `commit_ts`          | The commit timestamp of that checkpoint                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `total bytes`                           | `total_bytes`        | The store's size on disk in bytes, WAL included                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `wal segments past checkpoint`          | `wal_segments`       | WAL segment files written since the checkpoint; each may hold newer commits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `nodes (at checkpoint LSN <n>)`         | `node_count`         | Nodes at the checkpoint                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `relationships (at checkpoint LSN <n>)` | `rel_count`          | Relationships at the checkpoint                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `indexes`                               | `indexes`            | The count, then one line per index, `<name>: :<Label>(<property>)`. JSON: an array of `{name, label, property}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `constraints`                           | `constraints`        | The count, then one line per constraint, `<name>: <kind> node\|relationship :<Label>(<properties>)`, with `:: <TYPE>` for a property type constraint. JSON: an array of `{name, kind, label, relationship, properties, property_type, enforced_label}`; `relationship` is a boolean, and a field that does not apply is `null` |

JSON keys are sorted alphabetically. Three states leave fields empty:

| State                                   | Table                                                                                                             | JSON                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A `json` or `markdown` codec store      | `format version`, `nodes`, `relationships`, `indexes` and `constraints` print `unavailable`, after a `note:` line | Those five keys are `null`                                                                 |
| A new store before its first checkpoint | `snapshot: none yet (no checkpoint since creation)` in place of every checkpoint field                            | Every field but `layout`, `superblock_version`, `total_bytes` and `wal_segments` is `null` |
| A directory store                       | No `superblock version` line                                                                                      | `superblock_version` is `null`                                                             |

A `json`-codec store keeps its counts and catalog in `graph.json`, which `info` does not parse, so it reports only what the manifest holds. A store that a writer has created but not yet checkpointed printed this in a run:

```text
layout: native directory
snapshot: none yet (no checkpoint since creation)
total bytes: 55
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
```

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate info --database PATH [--json]
```

| Argument          | Meaning                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--database PATH` | The store: a directory store or a path ending in `.rl`. Required; short form `-d`. `:memory:` and an empty path are refused |
| `--json`          | One JSON object on stdout instead of the table. Optional; at most once                                                      |

properties.heading: Output modes
properties.text: An output mode decides how a query run prints each result set. The `relate` CLI has nine: `table`, `csv`, `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope`, `markdown`, `cypher`, `toon` and `speedscope`. Without an output flag, the mode is `table` when stdout is a terminal and `jsonl` when stdout is a pipe or a file, or `toon` when stdout is piped and agent mode is on. An explicit output flag always wins. The mode changes how results print, never what a [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) does. Its exit code is the same in every mode except `speedscope`, which exits 1 after a statement that has no `PROFILE` metrics; that statement still ran, and its writes committed.

properties.heading: csv
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --csv "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
name,since
Grace,2023
Ada,2024
```

properties.heading: cypher
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode cypher "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
CREATE ({name: 'Grace', since: 2023})
CREATE ({name: 'Ada', since: 2024})
```

`cypher` formats values, not graph elements: a node, relationship or path column has no Cypher literal form and is left out, with a `// column <name> (<TYPE>) omitted: no Cypher literal form` comment line. It is not a way to copy a store; [back up and restore](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/storage/backup-and-restore/) covers that.

properties.heading: Defaults
properties.text:
The CLI picks the mode once per run, from where stdout goes and whether agent mode is on:

| stdout                   | Agent mode off  | Agent mode on   |
| ------------------------ | --------------- | --------------- |
| A terminal               | `table`         | `table`         |
| A pipe or a file         | `jsonl`         | `toon`          |
| Any, with an output flag | the flag's mode | the flag's mode |

Agent mode is on under a detected agent harness with stdout not a terminal, or with `--agent-mode` or `RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1`; the [agent mode page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#what-turns-it-on) has the rules. The interactive shell runs on a terminal, so its default is `table`. A script piped to `relate query` follows the same table: its output is `jsonl` unless something else applies.

properties.heading: Empty results, writes, and several statements
properties.text:
Each statement prints its own result set, in the order the statements run:

| Mode       | Two statements, `RETURN 1 AS a; RETURN 2 AS b`                              | A read with no rows                                            | A write with no `RETURN`                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `table`    | Two tables                                                                  | The header only                                                | Nothing                                         |
| `csv`      | `a`, `1`, `b`, `2` on four lines                                            | The header line                                                | One empty line                                  |
| `json`     | Two objects, one per line                                                   | An object with `"data":[]`                                     | An object with `"data":[]`                      |
| `jsonl`    | Each statement's rows; with `--timings`, each followed by its timing line   | Nothing; with `--timings`, the timing line only                | Nothing; with `--timings`, the timing line only |
| `envelope` | Two envelopes, one per line                                                 | An envelope with `columns` and `"rows":[]`                     | An envelope with `"columns":[]`                 |
| `markdown` | Two tables                                                                  | The header and separator lines                                 | Nothing                                         |
| `cypher`   | One `CREATE` per row                                                        | Nothing                                                        | Nothing                                         |
| `toon`     | Two `rows[1]{…}:` blocks, each with its `timings:` and `planCache:` entries | `rows[0]{name}:`, then the `timings:` and `planCache:` entries | The `timings:` and `planCache:` entries only    |

`jsonl` prints nothing for a read with no rows, the same as for a write, so a statement with N rows prints exactly N lines. `envelope` tells the two apart:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Zed'}) RETURN p.name AS name"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["ANY"],"columns":["name"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.508375,"execute_ms":0.333625,"lex_parse_ms":0.028249999999999997,"lower_ms":0.039916999999999994,"parse_ms":0.110375,"plan_ms":0.054958,"result_generation_ms":0.000125,"rewrite_ms":0.007875},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: envelope
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER"],"columns":["name","since"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"name":"Grace","since":2023},{"name":"Ada","since":2024}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.427292,"execute_ms":0.250583,"lex_parse_ms":0.028833,"lower_ms":0.040375,"parse_ms":0.111167,"plan_ms":0.057292,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.007708},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
A failed statement prints its message on stderr and exits with the exit code of its class, in every mode. In `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope` and `speedscope`, it also prints an [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object) on stdout, after any rows already printed. `table`, `csv`, `markdown`, `cypher` and `toon` print no error object:

```bash verify
relate --mode jsonl "RETRN 1"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "RETRN"
  RETRN 1
  ^
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","column":1,"exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: parse error: unexpected token \"RETRN\"   RETRN 1   ^","retryable":false,"source":"RETRN 1"}}
exit=6
```

The first three lines are stderr; the error object is stdout. Its fields and every exit code are on the [exit codes and errors page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#the-error-object).

properties.heading: Header and width options
properties.text:
`--noheader` drops the header row of `table` and `csv`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --csv --noheader "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
Grace,2023
Ada,2024
```

`markdown` and `toon` keep their header with `--noheader`, because the table or the row count needs it.

`--pretty` indents `json` when stdout is not a terminal, two spaces per level:

```bash verify
relate --json --pretty "RETURN 'Ada' AS name, 2024 AS since"
```

```text
{
  "data": [
    {
      "name": "Ada",
      "since": 2024
    }
  ],
  "planCache": "miss",
  "timings": {
    "elapsed_ms": 0.48633299999999996,
    "execute_ms": 0.35312499999999997,
    "lex_parse_ms": 0.019084,
    "lower_ms": 0.0265,
    "parse_ms": 0.08887500000000001,
    "plan_ms": 0.036167,
    "result_generation_ms": 0.000166,
    "rewrite_ms": 0.006208
  }
}
```

`--width N` wraps `table` output to `N` display columns: the widest columns shrink and their cells continue on the next line. Without it, the width is the terminal's, else an exported `COLUMNS`, else the table's natural width. A value under `20` exits 2 with `Error: invalid --width: a width under 20 columns cannot hold a table; omit --width for the terminal default`.

properties.heading: How values print
properties.text:
The same row in each mode, with a string holding a comma and a pipe, a `null`, a list, a map, a float, a boolean and a date:

| Mode                        | Prints                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table`                     | `"a,b\|c"`, `<null>`, `[1, 2]`, `{k: 1}`, `1.5`, `true`, `2026-11-07`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `csv`                       | `"a,b\|c",,"[1, 2]",{k: 1},1.5,true,2026-11-07`: `null` is an empty field                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope` | `"a,b\|c"`, `null`, `[1,2]`, `{"k":1}`, `1.5`, `true`, `"2026-11-07"`: temporal values are strings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `markdown`                  | As `table`, with each pipe character escaped by a backslash                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `cypher`                    | `{s: 'a,b\|c', n: null, l: [1, 2], m: {k: 1}, f: 1.5, b: true, d: date('2026-11-07')}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `toon`                      | `"a,b\|c",null,[1,2],{"k":1},1.5,true,2026-11-07`: nested values are inline JSON, and a string is quoted, as a JSON string, when it is empty, holds a comma, a double quote, a backslash, or a control or invisible format character, has leading or trailing whitespace, or reads as a number (`NaN` and `Infinity` included), `true`, `false` or `null` |

A node prints as `(:Person {name: "Ada", role: "engineer"})` in `table`, `csv` and `markdown`, and as an object in the JSON modes and `toon`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode jsonl "MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'}) RETURN p"
```

```text
{"p":{"id":0,"kind":"node","labels":["Person"],"properties":{"name":"Ada","role":"engineer"}}}
```

`id` is the node's internal id within this store. A relationship prints with `"kind":"relationship"`.

properties.heading: json
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --json "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
{"data":[{"name":"Grace","since":2023},{"name":"Ada","since":2024}],"planCache":"miss","timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.498208,"execute_ms":0.288125,"lex_parse_ms":0.046125000000000006,"lower_ms":0.043583,"parse_ms":0.137083,"plan_ms":0.062541,"result_generation_ms":0.00033299999999999996,"rewrite_ms":0.008709000000000001}}
```

The rows are in `data`, beside the statement's `planCache` and `timings`. Keys are sorted alphabetically, in each row object and in the outer object, in `json`, `jsonl` and `envelope` alike. The column order is the statement's; `envelope` carries it in `columns`.

properties.heading: jsonl
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --jsonl "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
{"name":"Grace","since":2023}
{"name":"Ada","since":2024}
```

properties.heading: markdown
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --markdown "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
| name    | since |
|---------|-------|
| "Grace" | 2023  |
| "Ada"   | 2024  |
```

properties.heading: One query in every mode
properties.text:
The examples on this page read the team graph shared across the docs: three people, two projects, and who works on what. This step writes it to `team.rl`:

```bash verify
cat > seed.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
EOF
relate query --database ./team.rl < seed.cypher
```

Each example runs the same read, opened `--read-only`: who works on `relate`, and since when.

properties.heading: Output safety
properties.text:
Text modes escape what could change a terminal or a spreadsheet. There is no flag to turn this off.

| Mode                                | What is escaped                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `table`, `markdown`                 | Control characters and invisible format characters, such as a bidi override, in every cell and header: a newline prints as `\n`, a tab as `\t`, others as `\u{<hex>}` in uppercase hex with no padding, such as `\u{7}` and `\u{202E}`; `markdown` also escapes `\|` |
| `csv`                               | Control characters other than a newline or carriage return, then a field starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a `'` prefix, so `-5` prints as `'-5`; a field with a comma, quote or newline is quoted                                                             |
| `cypher`                            | Control and invisible format characters inside string literals, as `\n`, `\t` and `\uXXXX`, such as `\u0007`                                                                                                                                                         |
| `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope`, `toon` | JSON escaping only; values are unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

```bash verify
relate --csv "RETURN -5 AS n, '=1+1' AS formula"
```

```text
n,formula
'-5,'=1+1
```

A program that reads `csv` output handles the `'` prefix on a negative number; `jsonl` or `envelope` keeps numbers as numbers.

properties.text:
- [Choose an output format](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/output-formats/): which mode fits which job
- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#output): the output flags with their defaults
- [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/): the `toon` default, the row cap and the envelope's types

properties.heading: speedscope
properties.text:
`speedscope` needs a `PROFILE` statement, because the per-operator times of the plan are what it exports. The output is one JSON document in the speedscope file format: a frame per plan operator, named `<operator> <id>`, and an open and a close event per operator, in nanoseconds. The times change from run to run, so this example prints only the names:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode speedscope "PROFILE MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name" | grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"'
```

```text
"name":"relate PROFILE"
"name":"ProduceResults 0"
"name":"NodeByLabelScan 1"
```

A statement without `PROFILE` still runs, and its writes commit, but `speedscope` prints nothing on stdout and exits 1, with this message on stderr and no error object:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode speedscope "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
speedscope mode requires a PROFILE statement: per-operator times are what it exports (the statement carries no plan tree)
exit=1
```

A write is the case that matters: the refusal comes after the statement committed, so running it again writes twice. This example writes one `Run` node to a new directory store, `./sp`, then counts it read-only:

```bash verify
relate --database ./sp --mode speedscope "CREATE (:Run)"
echo "exit=$?"
relate --database ./sp --read-only --mode jsonl "MATCH (r:Run) RETURN count(r) AS runs"
```

```text
speedscope mode requires a PROFILE statement: per-operator times are what it exports (the statement carries no plan tree)
exit=1
{"runs":1}
```

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate [OPTIONS] --mode <mode> [--database PATH] [QUERY]
relate query --mode <mode> [STATEMENT] [--database PATH]
```

| Flag                                                 | Effect                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mode MODE`                                        | Selects one of the nine modes; an unknown name exits 2                                                                                                   |
| `--format MODE`                                      | Alias of `--mode`                                                                                                                                        |
| `--json`, `--csv`, `--jsonl`, `--markdown`, `--toon` | Shortcuts for `--mode json`, `csv`, `jsonl`, `markdown` and `toon`; the single-dash forms `-json`, `-csv`, `-jsonl` and `-markdown` are accepted         |
| `--pretty`                                           | Indents `json` output even when stdout is not a terminal; the other modes ignore it                                                                      |
| `--timings`                                          | Adds each statement's timing line to `jsonl` output (default off); `json`, `envelope` and `toon` always carry the timings, and the other modes ignore it |
| `--noheader`                                         | Drops the header row of `table` and `csv`; the other modes keep their headers                                                                            |
| `--width N`                                          | Wraps `table` output to `N` display columns, `20` or more                                                                                                |

Of several output flags, the last one given wins: `relate --mode csv --json …` prints JSON. The flag's value is the next argument; `--mode=csv` is an unknown flag. An unknown mode name exits 2:

```bash verify
relate --mode yaml "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: invalid mode 'yaml' (expected one of: table, csv, json, jsonl, envelope, markdown, cypher, toon, speedscope)
exit=2
```

properties.heading: table
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
+---------+-------+
| name    | since |
+---------+-------+
| "Grace" | 2023  |
| "Ada"   | 2024  |
+---------+-------+
```

properties.heading: The envelope
properties.text:
`--mode envelope` prints one compact [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope) per result set, on one line, with its keys sorted alphabetically:

| Key             | Present                                                                               | Holds                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columnTypes`   | always                                                                                | One type name per column, from the first row; `ANY` for a `null` first value or no rows                  |
| `columns`       | always                                                                                | The column names in the statement's order, even with no rows                                             |
| `notifications` | always                                                                                | The statement's notifications; `[]` on a plain run                                                       |
| `plan`          | `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE` only                                                          | The plan tree                                                                                            |
| `planCache`     | always                                                                                | The plan-cache outcome, one of the [five values](#timings-and-the-plan-cache)                            |
| `rowCap`        | when the [row cap](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#row-cap) cut the rows | `{"kept":N,"total":M}`                                                                                   |
| `rows`          | always                                                                                | One object per row, as `json` prints it                                                                  |
| `timings`       | always                                                                                | The statement's phase timings in milliseconds, one object with [eight keys](#timings-and-the-plan-cache) |
| `truncated`     | always                                                                                | `true` when the row cap cut the rows                                                                     |

The [agent mode page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#the-envelope) lists every `columnTypes` name. New keys may be added; existing ones are never renamed.

properties.heading: The nine modes
properties.text:
| Mode         | Shortcut     | Prints                                                                                                                                                                  | Error object on stdout                                            | Row cap reported in-band |
| ------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `table`      | none         | A boxed text table; strings in double quotes                                                                                                                            | no                                                                | no                       |
| `csv`        | `--csv`      | CSV with RFC 4180 quoting and LF line endings, with a header row                                                                                                        | no                                                                | no                       |
| `json`       | `--json`     | One JSON object per result set: the rows in `data`, with `planCache` and `timings`, and `rowCap` when the row cap cut them; indented on a terminal, one line when piped | yes                                                               | yes                      |
| `jsonl`      | `--jsonl`    | One JSON object per row; with `--timings`, then one `{"planCache":…,"timings":…}` line per result set                                                                   | yes                                                               | yes                      |
| `envelope`   | none         | One JSON object per result set: columns, types, rows, flags, `planCache` and `timings`                                                                                  | yes                                                               | yes                      |
| `markdown`   | `--markdown` | A GitHub-flavored table                                                                                                                                                 | no                                                                | yes                      |
| `cypher`     | none         | One `CREATE` statement per row, values as Cypher literals                                                                                                               | no                                                                | no                       |
| `toon`       | `--toon`     | One `rows[N]{cols}:` header line, one line per row, then `timings:` and `planCache:` entries                                                                            | no                                                                | yes                      |
| `speedscope` | none         | A `PROFILE` plan as one speedscope profile document                                                                                                                     | yes, for a failed statement; the `PROFILE` refusal is stderr only | no                       |

A mode with no error object prints a failure only on stderr, with the exit code; the [error object](#errors) section covers the rest. `json`, `envelope` and `toon` also report each statement's [timings and plan-cache outcome](#timings-and-the-plan-cache), and `jsonl` does with `--timings`; `table`, `csv`, `markdown`, `cypher` and `speedscope` do not. The in-band row cap report for each mode is on the [agent mode page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/#the-row-cap). An `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` result prints a plan object in `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope` and `toon`, in place of the shapes this table lists; [EXPLAIN and PROFILE](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/explain-and-profile/#the-plan-in-each-output-mode) shows each.

properties.heading: Timings and the plan cache
properties.text:
`json`, `envelope` and `toon` report two facts for every statement that runs: where its time went, as a `timings` object, and whether a cached plan served it, as `planCache`. `jsonl` reports them only with `--timings` (default off, since 1.0.1), so that by default it prints rows alone. `table`, `csv`, `markdown`, `cypher` and `speedscope` print neither, with or without `--timings`, and neither does the [error object](#errors) of a failed statement.

| Mode       | Where they print                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `json`     | The `planCache` and `timings` keys of the statement's object, beside `data`, and beside `notifications` and `plan` for `EXPLAIN` and `PROFILE`                                                                                        |
| `jsonl`    | With `--timings` only: one `{"planCache":…,"timings":{…}}` line after the statement's other lines: its rows, then a `{"rowCap":…}` line when the row cap cut them, or its plan object. A statement with no rows prints only this line |
| `envelope` | The `planCache` and `timings` keys of the envelope                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `toon`     | A `timings:` entry, the object as inline JSON, then a `planCache:` entry, as the last two entries of the statement's block, after `rowCap:` and `notifications:`                                                                      |

`timings` holds eight keys, sorted alphabetically like every other object these modes print. Each value is a number of milliseconds, measured on this run, so the digits change from run to run:

| Key                    | Measures                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `elapsed_ms`           | The statement's wall-clock total                          |
| `parse_ms`             | The parse phase                                           |
| `lex_parse_ms`         | Lexing and building the syntax tree, a part of `parse_ms` |
| `rewrite_ms`           | The rewrite pass, a part of `parse_ms`                    |
| `lower_ms`             | Validation and lowering, a part of `parse_ms`             |
| `plan_ms`              | The plan phase                                            |
| `execute_ms`           | The execute phase                                         |
| `result_generation_ms` | Building the result, a part of `execute_ms`               |

On a plan-cache hit, `lex_parse_ms`, `rewrite_ms` and `lower_ms` are `0.0`: the statement was not parsed again. `planCache` is one of five values:

| Value                        | Meaning                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `miss`                       | No cached plan served the statement, so it compiled from the start                                               |
| `hit-raw-fastpath`           | A cached plan served it because the statement text matched an earlier statement exactly                          |
| `hit-template`               | A cached plan served it because the statement matched an earlier one with only its literal values changed        |
| `replan-generation-mismatch` | A cached plan matched, but the store had committed a write since it was compiled, so the statement planned again |
| `bypassed`                   | The cache was not consulted, such as for a parameter whose name starts with the reserved `__AUTO_` prefix        |

The plan cache lives in the open store and starts empty on every CLI run, so a one-shot `relate "…"` reports `miss`. Several statements in one run share it. In this run, the second statement differs from the first only in a literal, and the third repeats the second; `--timings` adds the line that carries `planCache` to the `jsonl` output:

```bash verify
relate --jsonl --timings "RETURN 1 AS a; RETURN 2 AS a; RETURN 2 AS a" | jq -r 'select(.planCache) | .planCache'
```

```text
miss
hit-template
hit-raw-fastpath
```

properties.heading: toon
properties.text:
```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --toon "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'relate'}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since"
```

```text
rows[2]{name,since}:
  Grace,2023
  Ada,2024
timings:
  {"elapsed_ms":0.43375,"execute_ms":0.261625,"lex_parse_ms":0.028458,"lower_ms":0.0405,"parse_ms":0.109291,"plan_ms":0.055292,"result_generation_ms":0.000334,"rewrite_ms":0.007333999999999999}
planCache:
  miss
```

The [TOON](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#toon) header names the row count and the columns once; each row is two spaces, then the values separated by commas. The `timings:` and `planCache:` entries close the statement's block.

properties.heading: relate pull
properties.text: `relate pull` copies the nodes and relationships that one or more Cypher statements return from a Neo4j or Aura database into a local [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store), then exits. It talks to the source over Neo4j's [HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#http-query-api) v2, writes into an empty directory or `.rl` store, carries the source's constraints and indexes across, and checkpoints once at the end. No Neo4j server was available when this page was verified: the refusals and failures shown are recorded runs of the relate binary, and what a successful pull writes is described from relate's CLI specification and its agent skill, not from a run.

properties.heading: Connection and credentials
properties.text:
The credentials are four keys. `--from FILE` reads them from a `KEY=VALUE` file; without `--from`, pull reads the same names from the process environment.

| Key              | Required | Meaning                                                                       |
| ---------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NEO4J_URI`      | yes      | The source's Query API origin, such as `https://<host>:7473`                  |
| `NEO4J_USERNAME` | yes      | The user for HTTP Basic authentication; `NEO4J_USER` is accepted in its place |
| `NEO4J_PASSWORD` | yes      | The password                                                                  |
| `NEO4J_DATABASE` | no       | The source database; default `neo4j`                                          |

Pull sends each statement to `<origin>/db/<NEO4J_DATABASE>/query/v2`. A `--from` file that other local users can read (any group or world permission bit) prints a warning naming the file and its mode, and its credentials still load.

`NEO4J_URI` names the Query API, not a Bolt endpoint. Pull maps the URI schemes it accepts as follows:

| `NEO4J_URI`                                                                                     | Request origin                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `http://<host>:<port>` or `https://<host>:<port>`                                               | Used as written                                                                                                 |
| `neo4j://<host>[:7687]` or `bolt://<host>[:7687]`                                               | `http://<host>:7474`                                                                                            |
| `neo4j://` or `bolt://` on any other port                                                       | Refused: `NEO4J_URI bolt port <port> has no Query API mapping (7687 → 7474); use an explicit http(s) NEO4J_URI` |
| `neo4j+s://<host>[:<port>]`, `neo4j+ssc://` and `bolt+s://`                                     | `https://<host>`, without the port                                                                              |
| A URI with a user and password in it                                                            | Refused: `NEO4J_URI must not contain userinfo; pass credentials via NEO4J_USERNAME/NEO4J_PASSWORD`              |
| Any other scheme                                                                                | Refused: `unsupported NEO4J_URI scheme (use neo4j/bolt/http/https or +s/+ssc)`                                  |
| A host with characters a DNS name or IP address cannot hold, such as a percent-encoded password | Refused: `NEO4J_URI has an invalid host (expected a DNS name or IP literal)`                                    |

The refusals of a malformed `NEO4J_URI` never echo the URI, so a password pasted into it does not reach a log.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | The pull completed and printed its summary line                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 1         | A runtime failure: missing or unreadable credentials, a refused `NEO4J_URI`, plaintext refused, a non-empty destination, a statement whose `RETURN` is not graph elements, no answer from the source, an error the source returned, or a value that cannot be stored |
| 2         | A usage error: `--query` or `--database` missing, `:memory:` as the destination, an unknown flag or argument, or `--namespace`. The message is followed by the usage line and `Run 'relate pull --help' for more information.`                                       |

The messages, each on stderr after `Error: `:

| Message                                                                                                                                                                                | Exit code | Cause                                                                                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pull requires --query`                                                                                                                                                                | 2         | No `--query`                                                                                                         |
| `pull requires --database`                                                                                                                                                             | 2         | No `--database`                                                                                                      |
| `pull cannot target :memory: (--database must persist)`                                                                                                                                | 2         | `--database :memory:`                                                                                                |
| `unexpected argument to pull: <argument>`                                                                                                                                              | 2         | An unknown flag, a flag of the query run, or a positional store path                                                 |
| `--namespace is not valid with pull (pull always writes the neo4j namespace)`                                                                                                          | 2         | `--namespace` before the `pull` word; after it, the message is the unexpected-argument one                           |
| `NEO4J_URI missing from environment`                                                                                                                                                   | 1         | No `--from` and no `NEO4J_URI`; the same message names `NEO4J_USERNAME` or `NEO4J_PASSWORD` when that one is missing |
| `<KEY> missing from env file`                                                                                                                                                          | 1         | The `--from` file lacks `NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USERNAME` (or `NEO4J_USER`) or `NEO4J_PASSWORD`                          |
| `failed to read env file <path>: <reason>`                                                                                                                                             | 1         | The `--from` file cannot be read                                                                                     |
| `refusing to send Basic auth credentials in the clear: Query API URL <url> is http:// to a non-loopback host; pass --allow-plaintext to accept the risk, or use an https:// NEO4J_URI` | 1         | Plain `http://` to another host without `--allow-plaintext`                                                          |
| `destination database is not empty; pull writes into an empty database only (ADR-0158)`                                                                                                | 1         | The destination holds data                                                                                           |
| `shape query RETURN must be graph elements (nodes/rels/paths), not projections/scalars/aggregates; rejected item: <item>`                                                              | 1         | A `RETURN` item that is not a node, relationship, or path                                                            |
| `no statements in --query value`                                                                                                                                                       | 1         | An empty `--query` value                                                                                             |
| `HTTP request to <url> failed: <reason>`                                                                                                                                               | 1         | The source did not answer: a closed port, a name that does not resolve, or a network failure                         |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The examples share one credentials file. Its host is a documentation name, `neo4j.example.com`, and each command fails before it would connect. The file is readable by its owner only, so no warning prints. The setup also writes one `:Person` node into `./team.rl`, so the first example has a destination that holds data:

```bash verify
printf 'NEO4J_URI=https://neo4j.example.com:7473\nNEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j\nNEO4J_PASSWORD=<password>\n' > neo4j.env
chmod 600 neo4j.env
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'})" > /dev/null
```

A destination that already holds data is refused:

```bash verify
relate pull --from neo4j.env --query 'MATCH (n) RETURN n' --database ./team.rl
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: destination database is not empty; pull writes into an empty database only
exit=1
```

A statement that returns a count instead of graph elements is refused before the source is contacted:

```bash verify
relate pull --from neo4j.env --query 'MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes' --database ./mirror.rl
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: shape query RETURN must be graph elements (nodes/rels/paths), not projections/scalars/aggregates; rejected item: count(n)
exit=1
```

A plain `http://` origin on another host is refused, and a credentials file with group read permission gets a warning first:

```bash verify
printf 'NEO4J_URI=http://neo4j.example.com:7474\nNEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j\nNEO4J_PASSWORD=<password>\n' > plain.env
chmod 640 plain.env
relate pull --from plain.env --query 'MATCH (n) RETURN n' --database ./mirror.rl
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
warning: env file plain.env is group/world-readable (mode 0640); credentials may be exposed to other local users — run `chmod 600 plain.env`
Error: refusing to send Basic auth credentials in the clear: Query API URL http://neo4j.example.com:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2 is http:// to a non-loopback host; pass --allow-plaintext to accept the risk, or use an https:// NEO4J_URI
exit=1
```

`:memory:` is a usage error:

```bash verify
relate pull --from neo4j.env --query 'MATCH (n) RETURN n' --database :memory:
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: pull cannot target :memory: (--database must persist)
Usage: relate pull [--from FILE] --query Q [--param N=V] [--allow-plaintext] --database PATH
Run 'relate pull --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

When no server answers, the error names the request URL. This run had `NEO4J_URI=http://127.0.0.1:8873` with nothing listening on that port. The text after `io:` comes from the operating system; this recording is from macOS, and the error number in parentheses differs on Linux:

```bash
relate pull --from local.env --query 'MATCH (n) RETURN n' --database ./mirror.rl
```

```text
Error: HTTP request to http://127.0.0.1:8873/db/neo4j/query/v2 failed: io: Connection refused (os error 61)
```

The pull exits 1, and `./mirror.rl` remains as an empty store that a later pull can write into.

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
