| Flag                | Argument | Default                 | Scope         | Since | Description                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | -------- | ----------------------- | ------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--from`            | `FILE`   | the process environment | `relate pull` | —     | Env file with `NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USERNAME`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, `NEO4J_DATABASE`; omitted, those process environment variables are used.                                 |
| `--query`           | `Q`      | `required`              | `relate pull` | —     | A statement, a `;`-separated list, a file path, or `-` for stdin; every statement must `RETURN` graph elements. All run in one process, with one checkpoint at the end. |
| `--param`           | `N=V`    | unset                   | `relate pull` | —     | Bind a source query parameter (repeatable).                                                                                                                             |
| `--allow-plaintext` | —        | off                     | `relate pull` | —     | Permit Basic auth to a non-loopback `http://` Query API (insecure; prints a warning).                                                                                   |
| `--database`, `-d`  | `PATH`   | `required`              | `relate pull` | —     | Destination directory or `.rl` file; not `:memory:`.                                                                                                                    |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

properties.heading: Plaintext credentials
properties.text:
Pull refuses to send credentials over plain `http://` to a host that is not the local machine, before any network call. A loopback origin (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`) is allowed, and an `https://` origin is never refused.

| Origin                          | Without `--allow-plaintext` | With `--allow-plaintext`             |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `https://`                      | Sent                        | Sent                                 |
| `http://` to a loopback address | Sent                        | Sent                                 |
| `http://` to any other host     | Refused, exit code 1        | Sent, after a warning line on stderr |

The warning `--allow-plaintext` prints names the request URL:

```text
warning: Query API URL http://<host>:7474/db/neo4j/query/v2 is http://; Basic auth credentials will be sent in the clear (--allow-plaintext)
```

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [`relate push`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/push/): the mirror command, which copies from a store into Neo4j or Aura
- [Pull a subgraph from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/neo4j/pull-from-neo4j/): the task, from credentials to a first query on the copy
- [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/): what a statement written for Neo4j may need on the copy
- [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/): the exit codes every command shares
- [Problems relate solves: Neo4j subgraph mirror](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#neo4j-subgraph-mirror)

properties.heading: Selecting the subgraph
properties.text:
`--query` takes one of four forms: a statement, a `;`-separated list of statements, the path of a file that holds them, or `-` to read them from stdin. Every statement's `RETURN` items must be graph elements: nodes, relationships, or paths. A projection, a scalar or an aggregate is refused before the source is contacted:

```text
Error: shape query RETURN must be graph elements (nodes/rels/paths), not projections/scalars/aggregates; rejected item: count(n)
```

All the statements of one pull run in one process against one destination. A relationship returned by a later statement finds its endpoints among the nodes a previous statement copied, so one statement can copy nodes and the next the relationships between them.

`--param N=V` binds a parameter of the source statements; repeat it for more. As in a query run, `V` is parsed as a JSON scalar, a bare word is a string, and a name bound twice keeps the last value.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate pull [--from FILE] --query Q [--param N=V] [--allow-plaintext] --database PATH
```

| Part              | Required | Meaning                                                                                          |
| ----------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--query Q`       | yes      | What to copy: Cypher whose `RETURN` items are nodes, relationships, or paths                     |
| `--database PATH` | yes      | The destination store: a directory or a single-file `.rl` store, either empty or not yet created |
| `--from FILE`     | no       | The credentials file; without it, the credentials come from the process environment              |

[Pull](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#pull) is a command, so it takes only its own flags: the query-run flags such as `--mode` do not apply. `--namespace` is refused in both positions, because pull always writes the `neo4j` namespace.

properties.heading: What it writes
properties.text:
| Property | Behavior | | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Destination | A directory store or a single-file `.rl` store; `:memory:` is a usage error (exit code 2) | | Empty destination | Required. A store that already holds data is refused before the source is contacted: `destination database is not empty; pull writes into an empty database only (ADR-0158)` | | A path that does not exist | Created as a new store once the credentials load, before the URI, plaintext, shape and empty-destination checks; a pull that fails after that leaves it there, empty | | Namespace | Always `neo4j` | | Codec | A new directory store gets the build's default codec, `parquet` in the release binary | | Checkpoint | One, after the last statement | From the CLI specification, not from a run: within one pull, each source element is identified by its Neo4j [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id), so an element that two statements return is written once. Values keep their Cypher type: pull asks for the typed form of the Query API's JSON, so `DATE`, the other temporal types, `DURATION`, `POINT`, `UUID` and `VECTOR` properties are stored as those types. A byte-array property, a value the server could not serialize, or an unrecognized type fails the pull with exit code 1 and an error that names the element and the property, in the form `typed wire decode failed: property "" on element : unsupported typed value ""`. After the data, pull copies the source's schema, also from the specification. It reads `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` and `SHOW INDEXES` on the source and runs each row as a `CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS` statement on the destination: | Source schema | On the destination | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ | | Uniqueness, existence, node key, relationship key and property type [constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#constraint) | Created with the same form | | `RANGE`, `TEXT` and `POINT` indexes | Created | | Indexes that back a constraint, indexes that are not online, `LOOKUP` indexes | Left out | | `FULLTEXT` and `VECTOR` indexes, unrecognized constraint kinds | Skipped with a note on stderr, and counted | A schema row never fails a pull. On success, pull prints one line on stdout and exits 0: ```text pulled new / reused nodes,

new / reused rels (+ constraints, indexes; schema skipped) to ```

properties.heading: relate push
properties.text:
`relate push` copies a subgraph of a local [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) into a Neo4j or Aura database over the HTTP Query API v2, then exits. It is the mirror of [`relate pull`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/pull/): the same credentials file, the same URI rules, the same transport. Push merges each node and relationship on a key taken from the store's constraints, sends batched, parameterized statements, never deletes anything on the remote, and prints a report of what it created, updated, and skipped.

`--dry-run` prints the plan without contacting the remote. No Neo4j server was available when this page was verified: the dry runs and refusals shown are recorded runs of the relate binary, and what a push does against a live remote is described from relate's CLI specification and its agent skill, not from a run.

properties.heading: Against a live remote
properties.text:
From the CLI specification, not from a run:

- Before it writes an entity, push reads the remote's current rows for that entity by the same merge key, so the report can separate created from updated and `--updated-at` can compare timestamps.
- Every value is sent as a typed parameter, so `DATE`, `POINT`, `UUID` and vector properties keep their Cypher type on the remote. A byte-array property fails the push: `push failed: property "<key>": a byte array property …`.
- Rows go in batches of `--batch-size` (default `5000`) per statement.
- Nothing is deleted on the remote.
- Pushing the same scope twice, under `add` or `skip`, with keyed or structural relationships, leaves the remote as one push did.
- A failing batch stops the push, names the entity, the batch and the row range, prints the partial report of what landed, and exits 1.
- The report does not compare the remote's constraints with the local ones: a local merge key that the remote does not enforce still merges, but the remote may already hold duplicates of it.

A failure before any write is a recorded run. With a uniqueness constraint on `Person` only, `--labels Person`, and `NEO4J_URI=http://127.0.0.1:8873` in `local.env`, where nothing was listening, the pre-read fails, the report prints with nothing written, and the push exits 1. The timing and the text after `io:` vary by run and by operating system (this recording is from macOS):

```bash
relate push --to local.env --database ./team.rl --labels Person
```

```text
entity                       total  created  updated  skipped  warn  merge key  policy  batches
Person                           3        0        0        0     0  name       add           0
(Person)-[:KNOWS]->(Person)      1        0        0        0     0             add           0
(dangling)                       4        0        0        4     0             skip          0
pushed 0 rows in 0 statements (0 bytes) in 1 ms
Error: push failed: pre-read of Person failed: HTTP request to http://127.0.0.1:8873/db/neo4j/query/v2 failed: io: Connection refused (os error 61)
```

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | The push completed, or a dry run printed its plan                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 1         | A runtime failure: credentials missing or unreadable, a refused `NEO4J_URI`, plaintext refused, the store locked by another process, no answer from the remote, a remote error, a failing batch, or a value that cannot be pushed                           |
| 2         | A usage error: `--to` or `--database` missing, `:memory:`, two selectors, an invalid value, a repeated single-value flag, an unknown flag, or `--namespace`. The message is followed by the usage line and `Run 'relate push --help' for more information.` |

The usage messages, each on stderr after `Error: `:

| Message                                                                         | Cause                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `push requires --to`                                                            | No `--to`                                                                                                           |
| `push requires --database`                                                      | No `--database`                                                                                                     |
| `push cannot read :memory: (--database must be an on-disk store)`               | `--database :memory:`                                                                                               |
| `push takes one of --query, --labels, or --types (none pushes the whole store)` | Two selectors                                                                                                       |
| `invalid --batch-size "<value>" (expected a number >= 1)`                       | `--batch-size 0` or a value that is not a number                                                                    |
| `unknown update policy "<value>" (expected add, replace or skip)`               | A bad `--nodes-update` or `--rels-update` value                                                                     |
| `unknown --rel-mode "<value>" (expected keyed, structural or create)`           | A bad `--rel-mode`                                                                                                  |
| `unknown --unkeyed-labels "<value>" (expected skip or create)`                  | A bad `--unkeyed-labels`                                                                                            |
| `--namespace is not valid with push (push always reads the neo4j namespace)`    | `--namespace` before the `push` word                                                                                |
| `push <flag> may be given only once`                                            | A single-value flag repeated, such as two `--to` flags, or `--dry-run`, `--json` or `--allow-plaintext` given twice |
| `--merge-key "<value>" must be NAME:PROP[,PROP] (no ':' found)`                 | A `--merge-key` value without a colon; `--rel-key` gives the same message with its own name                         |
| `--merge-key "<value>" has an empty name`                                       | Nothing before the colon; also from `--rel-key`                                                                     |
| `--merge-key "<value>" has an empty property name`                              | Nothing after the colon, or an empty item in its property list; also from `--rel-key`                               |
| `--merge-key names "<label>" twice`                                             | Two `--merge-key` flags for one label                                                                               |
| `--rel-key names "<type>" twice`                                                | Two `--rel-key` flags for one type                                                                                  |
| `--labels has an empty name in "<value>"`                                       | An empty item in a `--labels` list, such as `A,`; `--types` gives the same message with its own name                |
| `--updated-at names "<name>" twice`                                             | One property in two `--updated-at` flags                                                                            |
| `--updated-at "<value>" names "<name>" twice`                                   | One property twice in one `--updated-at` list                                                                       |
| `--updated-at "<value>" has an empty property name`                             | An empty `--updated-at` value, or an empty item in its list                                                         |
| `empty item in policy list`                                                     | An empty `--nodes-update` or `--rels-update` value, or an empty item in its list                                    |
| `policy list has two global policies ("<policy>" twice)`                        | Two bare policies in one list, such as `add,replace`                                                                |
| `empty entity name in policy item "<item>"`                                     | A list item with nothing before the `=`                                                                             |
| `policy list names entity "<entity>" twice`                                     | One entity named twice in one list                                                                                  |
| `unexpected argument to push: <argument>`                                       | An unknown flag, including `--read-only` and `--namespace` after the word                                           |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The setup writes the team graph (five nodes, five relationships) into `./team.rl` and a credentials file that names a documentation host, `neo4j.example.com`; a dry run never contacts it.

```bash verify
printf 'NEO4J_URI=https://neo4j.example.com:7473\nNEO4J_USERNAME=neo4j\nNEO4J_PASSWORD=<password>\n' > neo4j.env
chmod 600 neo4j.env
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)" > /dev/null
```

The store has no constraints yet, so no label has a merge key and the plan skips everything:

```bash verify
relate push --to neo4j.env --database ./team.rl --dry-run
```

```text
entity                                      total  created  updated  skipped  warn  merge key  policy  batches
Person (unkeyed)                                3        0        0        3     0             add           0
Project (unkeyed)                               2        0        0        2     0             add           0
(Person)-[:KNOWS]->(Person) (unkeyed)           1        0        0        1     0             add           0
(Person)-[:MAINTAINS]->(Project) (unkeyed)      1        0        0        1     0             add           0
(Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(Project) (unkeyed)       3        0        0        3     0             add           0
dry run: 5 entities, 10 rows planned; nothing was sent
```

The next two statements write a uniqueness constraint on each label into `./team.rl`, which gives both labels a key. The second dry run plans every row and prints the statements:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE CONSTRAINT person_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) REQUIRE p.name IS UNIQUE" > /dev/null
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE CONSTRAINT project_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Project) REQUIRE p.name IS UNIQUE" > /dev/null
relate push --to neo4j.env --database ./team.rl --dry-run
```

```text
entity                            total  created  updated  skipped  warn  merge key  policy  batches
Person                                3        3        0        0     0  name       add           1
Project                               2        2        0        0     0  name       add           1
(Person)-[:KNOWS]->(Person)           1        1        0        0     0             add           1
(Person)-[:MAINTAINS]->(Project)      1        1        0        0     0             add           1
(Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(Project)       3        3        0        0     0             add           1
Person: UNWIND $rows AS row MERGE (n:`Person` {`name`: row.key.`name`}) SET n += row.props
Project: UNWIND $rows AS row MERGE (n:`Project` {`name`: row.key.`name`}) SET n += row.props
(Person)-[:KNOWS]->(Person): UNWIND $rows AS row MATCH (a:`Person` {`name`: row.start.`name`}) MATCH (b:`Person` {`name`: row.end.`name`}) MERGE (a)-[r:`KNOWS`]->(b) SET r += row.props
(Person)-[:MAINTAINS]->(Project): UNWIND $rows AS row MATCH (a:`Person` {`name`: row.start.`name`}) MATCH (b:`Project` {`name`: row.end.`name`}) MERGE (a)-[r:`MAINTAINS`]->(b) SET r += row.props
(Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(Project): UNWIND $rows AS row MATCH (a:`Person` {`name`: row.start.`name`}) MATCH (b:`Project` {`name`: row.end.`name`}) MERGE (a)-[r:`WORKS_ON`]->(b) SET r += row.props
dry run: 5 entities, 10 rows planned; nothing was sent
```

`--labels Person` keeps the people and the one relationship between two people; the four relationships that reach a project are counted as dangling:

```bash verify
relate push --to neo4j.env --database ./team.rl --dry-run --labels Person
```

```text
entity                       total  created  updated  skipped  warn  merge key  policy  batches
Person                           3        3        0        0     0  name       add           1
(Person)-[:KNOWS]->(Person)      1        1        0        0     0             add           1
(dangling)                       4        0        0        4     0             skip          0
Person: UNWIND $rows AS row MERGE (n:`Person` {`name`: row.key.`name`}) SET n += row.props
(Person)-[:KNOWS]->(Person): UNWIND $rows AS row MATCH (a:`Person` {`name`: row.start.`name`}) MATCH (b:`Person` {`name`: row.end.`name`}) MERGE (a)-[r:`KNOWS`]->(b) SET r += row.props
dry run: 3 entities, 8 rows planned; nothing was sent
```

Two selectors are a usage error:

```bash verify
relate push --to neo4j.env --database ./team.rl --labels Person --types KNOWS
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: push takes one of --query, --labels, or --types (none pushes the whole store)
Usage: relate push --to CREDS --database PATH [--query Q | --labels L1,L2 | --types T1,T2] [--batch-size N] [--nodes-update POLICY] [--rels-update POLICY] [--updated-at NAME[,NAME]] [--rel-mode MODE] [--merge-key LABEL:PROP[,PROP]] [--rel-key TYPE:PROP[,PROP]] [--unkeyed-labels ACTION] [--dry-run] [--json] [--allow-plaintext]
Run 'relate push --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

properties.heading: Merge keys
properties.text:
Push writes a node with `MERGE` on its label's merge key, so pushing twice does not duplicate it. The key comes from the store's uniqueness, node key and relationship key [constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#constraint), composite keys included. `--merge-key LABEL:PROP[,PROP]` sets or overrides one label's key, once per label.

| Case                                                   | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A label with a key                                     | ``UNWIND $rows AS row MERGE (n:`Label` {`key`: row.key.`key`}) SET …``                                                                                                               |
| A label without one, `--unkeyed-labels skip` (default) | Not written; its row in the report says `(unkeyed)` and counts the nodes as skipped                                                                                                  |
| A label without one, `--unkeyed-labels create`         | ``UNWIND $rows AS row CREATE (n:`Label`) SET n += row.props``, where the `SET` follows `--nodes-update` (`SET n = row.props` under `replace`); pushing twice creates the nodes twice |
| A relationship with an unkeyed endpoint                | Not written, counted `(unkeyed)`, under either action                                                                                                                                |

Relationships follow `--rel-mode`:

| `--rel-mode`      | Statement                                                                                                                                                                              | Pushing twice      |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `keyed` (default) | `MERGE` on the type's key: `--rel-key TYPE:PROP[,PROP]`, else the type's relationship uniqueness or key constraint; without either, one relationship of the type between the two nodes | Idempotent         |
| `structural`      | ``MERGE (a)-[r:`TYPE`]->(b)``, even when a key exists; parallel relationships of one type between the same two nodes become one                                                        | Idempotent         |
| `create`          | ``CREATE (a)-[r:`TYPE`]->(b)``                                                                                                                                                         | Creates them again |

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
| Flag                | Argument            | Default                    | Scope         | Since | Description                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--to`              | `CREDS`             | `required`                 | `relate push` | —     | Env file (`NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USERNAME`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, optional `NEO4J_DATABASE`), or a Query API URI with the username and password from the process environment. |
| `--database`, `-d`  | `PATH`              | `required`                 | `relate push` | —     | Source store directory or `.rl` file; not `:memory:`.                                                                                                                  |
| `--query`           | `Q`                 | the whole store            | `relate push` | —     | Push only what the statements return (nodes, relationships, paths); a `;`-list, file path, or `-` for stdin. One of `--query`, `--labels`, `--types`.                  |
| `--labels`          | `L1,L2`             | unset                      | `relate push` | —     | Only nodes with these labels, and the relationships between them.                                                                                                      |
| `--types`           | `T1,T2`             | unset                      | `relate push` | —     | Only relationships of these types, with both their endpoints.                                                                                                          |
| `--batch-size`      | `N`                 | `5000`                     | `relate push` | —     | Rows per batched statement.                                                                                                                                            |
| `--nodes-update`    | `POLICY`            | `add`                      | `relate push` | —     | `add` (`SET +=`, keeps remote-only properties), `replace` (`SET =`) or `skip` (create missing only), per label or global.                                              |
| `--rels-update`     | `POLICY`            | `add`                      | `relate push` | —     | The same policies, per relationship type or global.                                                                                                                    |
| `--updated-at`      | `NAME[,NAME]`       | unset                      | `relate push` | —     | Candidate timestamp properties; when both sides carry one, a strictly newer remote row is skipped.                                                                     |
| `--rel-mode`        | `MODE`              | `keyed`                    | `relate push` | —     | `keyed` (merge on the type's resolved key), `structural` (one relationship of a type between two nodes) or `create` (non-idempotent).                                  |
| `--merge-key`       | `LABEL:PROP[,PROP]` | the constraint-derived key | `relate push` | —     | Merge key for one label (repeatable).                                                                                                                                  |
| `--rel-key`         | `TYPE:PROP[,PROP]`  | the constraint-derived key | `relate push` | —     | Merge key for one relationship type (repeatable).                                                                                                                      |
| `--unkeyed-labels`  | `ACTION`            | `skip`                     | `relate push` | —     | `skip` (reported and counted) or `create` (non-idempotent) for a label with no merge key.                                                                              |
| `--dry-run`         | —                   | off                        | `relate push` | —     | Print the plan without touching the remote.                                                                                                                            |
| `--json`            | —                   | off                        | `relate push` | —     | Print the run report as one JSON object instead of the table.                                                                                                          |
| `--allow-plaintext` | —                   | off                        | `relate push` | —     | Permit Basic auth to a non-loopback `http://` Query API (insecure; prints a warning).                                                                                  |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

A flag that takes one value may appear once: a second `--to`, `--query` or `--rel-mode` is a usage error. `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--allow-plaintext` may also appear once. `--merge-key` and `--rel-key` repeat once per label or type, `--updated-at` repeats but never names a property twice, and `--labels` and `--types` add to their lists when repeated.

properties.heading: Scope
properties.text:
| Selector         | What is pushed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| None             | The whole store                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `--query Q`      | The nodes, relationships and paths the statements `RETURN`, with the endpoints of each relationship. `Q` is a statement, a `;`-separated list, a file path, or `-` for stdin, with the same rule as pull: every `RETURN` item is a graph element |
| `--labels L1,L2` | Nodes with any of these [labels](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label), and the relationships whose two endpoints are both in scope; a relationship with an endpoint out of scope is counted in a `(dangling)` row and not written |
| `--types T1,T2`  | Relationships of these [relationship types](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type), with both their endpoints                                                                                                           |

Two selectors together are a usage error: `push takes one of --query, --labels, or --types (none pushes the whole store)`.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [`relate pull`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/pull/): the mirror command, and the credential and URI tables push shares
- [Push a subgraph to Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/neo4j/push-to-neo4j/): the task, from a dry run to a verified push
- [Schema clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/schema-clauses/): the constraints push takes its merge keys from
- [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/): the exit codes every command shares
- [Problems relate solves: Neo4j subgraph mirror](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#neo4j-subgraph-mirror)

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate push --to CREDS --database PATH [--query Q | --labels L1,L2 | --types T1,T2] [--batch-size N] [--nodes-update POLICY] [--rels-update POLICY] [--updated-at NAME[,NAME]] [--rel-mode MODE] [--merge-key LABEL:PROP[,PROP]] [--rel-key TYPE:PROP[,PROP]] [--unkeyed-labels ACTION] [--dry-run] [--json] [--allow-plaintext]
```

| Part                               | Required | Meaning                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--to CREDS`                       | yes      | The remote: a credentials file, or a Query API URI                       |
| `--database PATH`                  | yes      | The source store: a directory or a single-file `.rl` store               |
| `--query`, `--labels` or `--types` | no       | What to push; at most one of the three, and without any, the whole store |

[Push](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#push) is a command, so it takes only its own flags. `--namespace` is refused in both positions, because push always reads the `neo4j` namespace.

properties.heading: The remote and its credentials
properties.text:
`--to` takes a credentials file in the format `relate pull --from` reads (`NEO4J_URI`, `NEO4J_USERNAME`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, optional `NEO4J_DATABASE`), or a Query API URI. With a URI, the username, password and database come from the process environment; a missing one is an error such as `NEO4J_USERNAME missing from push --to`.

Everything else about the connection is pull's: the URI scheme mapping, the refusal of a URI that carries a password, the warning for a credentials file other users can read, and the refusal of plain `http://` to a non-loopback host unless `--allow-plaintext` is given. The [pull reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/pull/#connection-and-credentials) has the tables.

properties.heading: The report
properties.text:
Push prints one row per entity, then a summary line. The `skipped` column adds up the four reasons: unkeyed, policy, remote-newer and dangling. `warn` counts the `--updated-at` pairs that could not be compared. A dry run also prints each entity's statement shape and ends with `dry run: <n> entities, <m> rows planned; nothing was sent`.

`--json` prints the same report as one JSON object:

| Key                                                    | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dryRun`                                               | `true` for a dry run                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `entities`                                             | One object per entity: `entity`, `kind` (`node` or `relationship`), `total`, `created`, `updated`, `skipped` (`unkeyed`, `policy`, `remoteNewer`, `dangling`), `incomparableWarnings`, `mergeKey`, `policy`, `statement`, `batches` |
| `statementsSent`, `rowsSent`, `bytesSent`, `elapsedMs` | The totals of the run                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

In a dry run nothing is read from the remote, so `created` counts every row in scope.

properties.heading: The source store
properties.text:
| Property                   | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--database`               | A directory store or a single-file `.rl` store; `:memory:` is a usage error (exit code 2)                                                                                 |
| Opening                    | Push opens the store itself, as a writer: a store another process holds for writing fails with `storage locked: <path>` (exit code 1), and push has no `--read-only` flag |
| A path that does not exist | Created as a new, empty store; the push then plans nothing                                                                                                                |
| Namespace                  | Always `neo4j`                                                                                                                                                            |

properties.heading: Update policies
properties.text:
`--nodes-update` and `--rels-update` decide what happens to an entity that already exists on the remote. Each takes a global policy (`add`), a per-entity list (`Person=replace,Project=skip`), or both, where a bare policy in the list is the default for every entity it does not name.

| Policy          | Statement                     | On the remote                                                            |
| --------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `add` (default) | `SET n += row.props`          | Pushed properties are set; properties only the remote has stay           |
| `replace`       | `SET n = row.props`           | The property map is replaced; properties only the remote has are removed |
| `skip`          | Creates missing entities only | Existing entities are left as they are                                   |

`--updated-at NAME[,NAME]` names timestamp properties to compare, the first one present on each side winning. When both the local entity and the remote row carry one, a strictly newer remote row is skipped and counted as remote-newer, and an equal or newer local row is written. Temporal values and numbers compare; any other pair is incomparable, is written under the policy, and adds to the `warn` count.

properties.heading: relate query
properties.text: `relate query` runs a statement session against one store: the statements given as an argument, a script read from stdin, or the interactive shell. It takes every query-run flag. The path-first form, `relate [OPTIONS] [QUERY]`, runs the same session with the same flags; the one difference is that it never reads a script from stdin. Without `--database`, the store is `:memory:`, which is gone when the process exits. A [query](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#query), in these docs, is a statement that reads; the command runs writes too.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
A session exits with the code of the first statement that failed, or 0. An empty result is a success.

| Exit code                                                                 | Meaning in a query session                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [0](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-0) | Every statement ran, including one with no rows                                            |
| [1](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-1) | Runtime failure: the store did not open, a capacity limit, an I/O or internal error        |
| [2](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-2) | Usage error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional; nothing ran             |
| [5](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-5) | Conflict: another process holds the store for writing, or a write-write conflict           |
| [6](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-6) | The statement was rejected: syntax, semantic or type error, or a write on a read-only open |
| [7](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-7) | A statement exceeded `--timeout`                                                           |

The [exit codes page](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/) has the error object's fields and a recorded run for each code.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
Who works on what, written to a CSV file with a header row:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --csv "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(r:Project) RETURN p.name AS person, r.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since" > who.csv
echo "exit=$?"
cat who.csv
```

```text
exit=0
person,project,since
Grace,opencypher-tck,2022
Grace,relate,2023
Ada,relate,2024
```

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
`relate query` takes the query-run flags, the same set as the path-first form. A flag beats its environment variable, which beats the built-in default. Flags may come before or after the statement, a flag's value is the next argument (`--mode envelope`, not `--mode=envelope`), and `--read-only` is the one flag whose value is attached (`--read-only=live`). `--` ends the options: every argument after it is positional, so a statement that starts with `-` can follow it. [How flags are parsed](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#how-flags-are-parsed) has every parsing rule, and [Environment variables](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/environment-variables/) lists the variables.

| Flag                                   | Argument                      | Default                                                                                                    | Scope     | Since | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--database`, `-d`                     | `PATH`                        | `:memory:`                                                                                                 | query run | —     | The store target: a directory, a `.rl` file (legacy `.cl` files still open), or `:memory:`. Never a URL; a remote store is a `--load` source.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--command`, `-c`                      | `CYPHER`                      | unset                                                                                                      | query run | —     | One statement or a `;`-separated list; the same as the positional QUERY, and the two cannot be combined.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--load`                               | `SOURCE`                      | unset                                                                                                      | query run | —     | Load a store's content from a source (a local `.rl` file, a directory, or an http(s) URL to a `.rl` file) into the target: into `:memory:` it is an ephemeral read-only open; into a new `-d PATH` it creates the store.                                                                                                           |
| `--mode`                               | `MODE`                        | table on a terminal; jsonl when stdout is piped or redirected; toon instead of jsonl when agent mode is on | query run | —     | Output mode: `table`, `csv`, `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope`, `markdown`, `cypher`, `toon`, `speedscope`. An explicit mode always overrides the default.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--format`                             | `MODE`                        | as --mode                                                                                                  | query run | —     | Alias of `--mode` (the neo4j-cli spelling). `--output` and `-o` are unknown flags whose did-you-mean names `--format`.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--json`; also `-json`                 | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Shortcut for `--mode json`: one object per result set with the rows in `data`; indented on a terminal, one compact line when piped.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--csv`; also `-csv`                   | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Shortcut for `--mode csv`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--jsonl`; also `-jsonl`               | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Shortcut for `--mode jsonl`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `--markdown`; also `-markdown`         | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Shortcut for `--mode markdown`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--toon`                               | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Shortcut for `--mode toon`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--pretty`                             | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Force indented `json` output when stdout is not a terminal; ignored by the other modes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `--timings`                            | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Append each statement's `{"planCache":…,"timings":…}` line to `jsonl` output; `json`, `envelope` and `toon` always carry the timings, and the other modes ignore it.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--noheader`; also `-noheader`         | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Suppress column headers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--param`; also `-param`               | `N=V`                         | unset                                                                                                      | query run | —     | Bind a Cypher parameter (repeatable). A value that parses as JSON keeps its JSON type (`true`, `null` and numbers included); a value that starts with a digit, `-`, `"`, `[` or `{` and does not parse exits 2; any other value binds as a string.                                                                                 |
| `--fetch-params`                       | `N=SRC`                       | unset                                                                                                      | query run | —     | Fetch an http(s) URL or read a file, parse it as JSON, and bind it as parameter N (repeatable; 64 MiB cap, 60 s timeout). A CLI-process fetch with no URL allowlist.                                                                                                                                                               |
| `--snapshot-format`                    | `parquet\|json\|markdown`     | parquet (json in builds without the parquet feature)                                                       | query run | —     | Snapshot codec for an empty directory; an existing store keeps its recorded codec, and a different codec fails the open (exit 1). `parquet` writes one typed column per common property key (format version 5). Environment: [`RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-snapshot-format). |
| `--markdown-body-properties`           | `LIST`                        | `body`                                                                                                     | query run | —     | Body properties of a markdown-codec store (`LIST` or `Label=LIST`; entries separated by `;`; the first is written bare, the rest as `##` sections).                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--wal-dir`                            | `PATH`                        | `<DATABASE>/wal`                                                                                           | query run | —     | Local WAL directory for a directory store; rejected for `.rl` files.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Persistent stores only. Environment: [`RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-checkpoint-interval-secs).                                                                                                                      |

Environment: [`RELATE_EXPRESSION_MEMORY_LIMIT`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-expression-memory-limit).                                                                                                                                       |
| `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` | `SIZE`                        | admission off                                                                                              | query run | —     | Shared logical-workspace pool; a positive value turns query admission on; `0` is rejected. Environment: [`RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-concurrent-logical-workspace-limit).                                                                                |
| `--max-traversal-depth`                | `N`                           | `500`                                                                                                      | query run | —     | Largest explicit traversal hop bound (1 through 2000); a larger bound fails at admission with `TraversalDepthExceeded`. Environment: [`RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-max-traversal-depth).                                                                                 |
| `--safe`, `--no-safe`                  | —                             | off                                                                                                        | query run | —     | Opt-in safe mode: refuses a new named node without a label, and a `MATCH` read whose final `RETURN`/`WITH` has no `LIMIT` and no reducing aggregate, as `SafeModeViolation` (exit 6). Environment: [`RELATE_SAFE_MODE`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-safe-mode).                                       |

A timed-out statement exits 7 with `code: "timeout"`.                                                                                                                                                            |

Attached form only; once only. A write fails with exit 6.                                                                             |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

properties.heading: Output modes
properties.text:
Without an output flag, the mode depends on where stdout goes:

| stdout                                                                                     | Default mode |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| A terminal                                                                                 | `table`      |
| A pipe or a file                                                                           | `jsonl`      |
| A pipe or a file, with [agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/) on | `toon`       |

`--mode` (alias `--format`) picks one of `table`, `csv`, `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope`, `markdown`, `cypher`, `toon` and `speedscope`; `--json`, `--csv`, `--jsonl`, `--markdown` and `--toon` are shortcuts. Of several output flags, the last one wins. A failed statement prints the error object on stdout in `envelope`, `json`, `jsonl` and `speedscope`; `table`, `csv`, `markdown`, `cypher` and `toon` print nothing on stdout; the stderr message and the exit code remain. [Output modes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/) shows each mode's output.

`--mode table` on the people in `team.rl`:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role ORDER BY name"
```

```text
+---------+--------------+
| name    | role         |
+---------+--------------+
| "Ada"   | "engineer"   |
| "Grace" | "engineer"   |
| "Noor"  | "maintainer" |
+---------+--------------+
```

properties.heading: Parameters
properties.text:
A statement reads a [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter) as `$name`. Two flags bind them, and both repeat, one parameter each:

| Flag                   | Binds                                                                                                                                                  | Limits                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--param N=V`          | `$N` to `V`, parsed as JSON. A value that starts like JSON (a digit, `-`, `"`, `[` or `{`) and does not parse exits 2; any other bare word is a string | A name bound twice keeps the last value                                                                 |
| `--fetch-params N=SRC` | `$N` to the JSON parsed from `SRC`: a file path, or an `http` or `https` URL                                                                           | 64 MiB per source and 60 seconds per fetch. No URL allowlist: the fetch has the same trust as `--param` |

A statement that names a parameter no flag bound fails with `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <name>` and exit code 6. Grace's projects, by parameter, against `team.rl`:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope --param name=Grace 'MATCH (p:Person {name: $name})-[w:WORKS_ON]->(r:Project) RETURN r.name AS project, w.since AS since ORDER BY since'
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","INTEGER"],"columns":["project","since"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"project":"opencypher-tck","since":2022},{"project":"relate","since":2023}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.473833,"execute_ms":0.281583,"lex_parse_ms":0.033209,"lower_ms":0.047208,"parse_ms":0.12095800000000001,"plan_ms":0.06224999999999999,"result_generation_ms":0.00029099999999999997,"rewrite_ms":0.008124999999999999},"truncated":false}
```

Single quotes keep the shell from expanding `$name`. [Script the CLI](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/scripting/#pass-parameters) shows typed values and a JSON file.

properties.heading: Read-only opens
properties.text:
`--read-only` opens an existing store without writing or checkpointing it. It is off unless given, and it may appear once per run.

| Spelling                              | Opens                                                                                                                                              | Refused for                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--read-only`, `--read-only=snapshot` | The store as it was at open: a frozen snapshot. On a directory store it can open beside a writer; a `.rl` file opens only while no writer holds it | —                                                                                                                                       |
| `--read-only=live`                    | A [live read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#live-read-only) open: it tails the WAL and follows the writer's commits            | `.rl` files and `:memory:`: `semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases`, exit code 1 |
| `--read-only live` (a space)          | Nothing: exit code 2 with `Error: --read-only takes its value attached: --read-only=live`                                                          | —                                                                                                                                       |

A read-only open never creates a store. A missing directory fails with `storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>` and a missing `.rl` file with `storage error: database not found: <path>`, each after `Failed to open Relate: ` and with exit code 1. On `:memory:`, `--read-only` rejects writes and creates nothing. A write against a read-only open fails before it changes anything, with exit code 6:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Zed'})"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.","retryable":false}}
exit=6
```
