properties.heading: Session forms
properties.text:
The form depends on whether a statement is given and on what stdin is:

| Form              | Chosen when                                              | Runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Oneshot           | `STATEMENT` or `-c` is given                             | The statement, or each statement of the `;`-separated list in order, then exits                                                                                                                                       |
| Stdin script      | No statement, and stdin is a pipe, a file or `/dev/null` | Every statement on stdin until end of input, then exits. Statements end with `;` (the last one may omit it), may span lines, and `//` starts a comment. Dot commands such as `.begin` and `.commit` work one per line |
| Interactive shell | No statement, and stdin is a terminal                    | A prompt with readline-style editing and the dot commands, until `.quit` or end of input                                                                                                                              |

In the oneshot and stdin forms, each statement prints its own result set and commits on its own, unless a `.begin` in a script opened a [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction). A failed statement stops the run: the statements before it stay committed, and the rest do not run. [Dot commands](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/dot-commands/) lists the shell and script commands, and [Use the interactive shell](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cli/interactive-shell/) covers the shell.

The path-first form with no statement differs only in the stdin case: it prints the top-level help and exits 0 without reading stdin, so a redirected script never runs. A script on stdin needs the word `query`.

| Input                         | Exit code | Message on stderr                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `STATEMENT` and `-c` together | 2         | `Error: --command cannot be combined with a positional query`                  |
| A second positional statement | 2         | `Error: unexpected argument: <statement>`, the usage line, and a `--help` hint |
| Empty stdin                   | 0         | None                                                                           |

These examples run in a new, empty directory. This first command writes: it creates `team.rl`, a single-file store holding three people and two projects, and prints nothing, because a `CREATE` with no `RETURN` has no rows:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

A oneshot read. Stdout is a pipe here, so the output mode is `jsonl`: one JSON object per row, and nothing else unless `--timings` adds the statement's [timings and plan-cache outcome](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/#timings-and-the-plan-cache):

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name"
```

```text
{"name":"Ada"}
{"name":"Grace"}
{"name":"Noor"}
```

`-c` with a `;`-separated list prints one result set per statement, here as envelopes (`--mode envelope`):

```bash verify
relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope -c "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people; MATCH (p:Project) RETURN count(p) AS projects"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.46900000000000003,"execute_ms":0.299875,"lex_parse_ms":0.030875,"lower_ms":0.041832999999999995,"parse_ms":0.106041,"plan_ms":0.055,"result_generation_ms":0.000375,"rewrite_ms":0.008542000000000001},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["projects"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"projects":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.032499999999999994,"execute_ms":0.004459,"lex_parse_ms":0.0055,"lower_ms":0.009209,"parse_ms":0.019167,"plan_ms":0.007541,"result_generation_ms":0.000084,"rewrite_ms":0.00041600000000000003},"truncated":false}
```

The same two statements as a script on stdin:

```bash verify
printf 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people;\nMATCH (p:Project) RETURN count(p) AS projects;\n' | relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.468375,"execute_ms":0.283959,"lex_parse_ms":0.028917,"lower_ms":0.052667000000000005,"parse_ms":0.1175,"plan_ms":0.058708,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.008084},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["projects"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"projects":2}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.043417000000000004,"execute_ms":0.003333,"lex_parse_ms":0.007666999999999999,"lower_ms":0.010875,"parse_ms":0.02575,"plan_ms":0.011916999999999999,"result_generation_ms":0.000083,"rewrite_ms":0.00075},"truncated":false}
```

A script that fails at its second statement. The first statement's result prints, the stderr lines say how far the run got, and the error object names the statement:

```bash verify
printf 'MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people;\nRETURN 1/0 AS boom;\nRETURN 3 AS never;\n' | relate query --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["people"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"people":3}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.315917,"execute_ms":0.148167,"lex_parse_ms":0.028875,"lower_ms":0.042959,"parse_ms":0.104167,"plan_ms":0.055542,"result_generation_ms":0.00025,"rewrite_ms":0.008542000000000001},"truncated":false}
type error: / by zero
statement 2 of 3 failed; 1 completed and committed; 1 not run
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","committed":1,"exit_code":6,"kind":"type","message":"type error: / by zero","retryable":false,"statement":2,"statements":3}}
exit=6
```

properties.heading: Statement timeouts
properties.text:
`--timeout DURATION` bounds each statement's wall-clock time on its own. A bare number is seconds; `ms`, `s` and `m` suffixes and fractions are accepted; `0` turns the bound off. Unset, a statement has no time bound. A statement that runs longer is cancelled and exits 7; the error object's `code` is `timeout` and `retryable` is `false`:

```bash verify
relate query --read-only --mode envelope --timeout 100ms "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS a UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS b RETURN count(*) AS pairs"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: query timed out after 100ms
{"error":{"code":"timeout","exit_code":7,"kind":"execution","message":"query timed out after 100ms","retryable":false}}
exit=7
```

A value that is not a duration exits 2 with `Error: invalid --timeout: '<value>' is not a duration (try 500ms, 10s, 2m)`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate query [STATEMENT] [--database PATH]
```

| Part              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `STATEMENT`       | One Cypher [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement), or a list separated by `;`. Optional. `-c` and `--command` are the flag spelling of the same argument |
| `--database PATH` | The store: a directory, a path ending in `.rl`, or `:memory:` (the default). Never a URL; a remote store is a `--load` source. Short form `-d`                                        |
| `OPTIONS`         | Any query-run flag, before or after `STATEMENT` ([Options](#options))                                                                                                                 |

The word `query` is the command when it is the first positional argument, before or after flags; a later positional `query` is an unexpected argument (exit code 2). A directory named `query` is `--database ./query`.

properties.heading: relate run
properties.text: `relate run <name>` runs an installed [extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#extension) action and imports what it produces into a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). The extension is a separate program: relate starts it, hands it the action's flag values, and answers its requests over the [Model Context Protocol](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) on stdin and stdout. relate alone opens the store, enforces the limits and sets the [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code); the extension never sees the store's path. Without `--database`, the import goes into an [in-memory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#in-memory-store). `relate run` never fetches anything: an action that is not installed fails, and [`relate extension install`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/extension/#install) is the command that installs one.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code | When                                                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | The extension finished and the summary printed                                              |
| 1         | A runtime failure: the work started and failed, or the fresh-store check refused the target |
| 2         | A usage error: before anything ran                                                          |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The examples run in a fresh directory with a fresh home and no `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. With nothing installed, a bare `relate run` names the install command:

```bash verify
relate run
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: run requires an action name (no actions installed; relate extension install <name> adds one)
Usage: relate run <name> [flags]
Run 'relate run --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

The remaining examples use a package scaffolded and installed by [`relate extension`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/extension/). Its one flag is `--name`, and its sample writes one `:Scaffold` node:

```bash verify
relate extension init team-import --lang sh > /dev/null
relate extension install team-import --from ./team-import > /dev/null
```

The run imports into `team.rl`, prints the extension's summary and its starter statement, and exits:

```bash verify
relate run team-import -d ./team.rl --name Ada
```

```text
team-import: Hello Ada world! — wrote 1 sample node(s)
  MATCH (n:Scaffold) RETURN n
```

The store holds what the extension wrote; this command reads it without the right to write:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode envelope "MATCH (n:Scaffold) RETURN n.id AS id, n.note AS note"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["STRING","STRING"],"columns":["id","note"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"id":"example","note":"Ada"}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.547667,"execute_ms":0.38291699999999995,"lex_parse_ms":0.028,"lower_ms":0.041458,"parse_ms":0.104625,"plan_ms":0.051834,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.008},"truncated":false}
```

A misspelled flag gets a suggestion from the action's own flags, and the usage line is the action's:

```bash verify
relate run team-import --nam Ada
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: unexpected argument to run team-import: --nam
Did you mean '--name'?
Usage: relate run team-import [--name VALUE]
Run 'relate run team-import --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

A name that is not installed fails without fetching anything:

```bash verify
relate run git-to-graph
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: no installed action 'git-to-graph' — first-party extension available: relate extension install git-to-graph
Usage: relate run <name> [flags]
Run 'relate run --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
| Flag               | Argument | Default    | Scope        | Since | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | -------- | ---------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--database`, `-d` | `PATH`   | `:memory:` | `relate run` | —     | Store to import into; an explicit `--database` exits after the import, and without it a terminal opens the shell on the in-memory graph. |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

| `--database`                  | After the import                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A path                        | The store takes its final checkpoint and the command exits                               |
| Omitted, stdin a terminal     | The interactive shell opens on the in-memory graph, with the action's starter statements |
| Omitted, stdin not a terminal | The command exits and nothing is kept                                                    |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [`relate extension`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/extension/): scaffold, check, install, list, and remove packages
- [Install and run an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/install-and-run/): the task from install to a first query
- [Write an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/write-an-extension/): the manifest, the protocol and `walk()`
- [The git-to-graph extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/git-to-graph/) and [the fs-to-graph extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/fs-to-graph/): the first-party actions
- [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/): the exit codes every command shares

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate run <name> [-d PATH] [<positional>] [--<flag> VALUE ...]
relate run <name> --help
relate run --help
```

| Input                   | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<name>`                | yes      | The installed action: the `name` in the package's `extension.json`                                                                                |
| `-d`, `--database PATH` | no       | The store to import into; default `:memory:`                                                                                                      |
| `<positional>`          | no       | One positional argument, when the action's manifest declares one                                                                                  |
| `--<flag>`              | no       | The action's own flags, from its manifest                                                                                                         |
| `--help`                | no       | After `<name>`, the action's usage and flags with their kinds and defaults; without a name, the command's page with the list of installed actions |

properties.heading: The action and its flags
properties.text:
The flags an action accepts are its manifest's `flags` table. Each entry has a kind, a name and a default; a flag left off the command line takes its default.

| Kind         | On the command line              | Value                                                                        |
| ------------ | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `string`     | `--<name> VALUE`                 | The text                                                                     |
| `integer`    | `--<name> N`                     | A whole number; anything else is a usage error naming the flag and the value |
| `boolean`    | `--<name>`                       | `true` when present                                                          |
| `repeatable` | `--<name> VALUE`, once per value | A list of the values given                                                   |

A manifest that declares a flag twice, or a flag named `database` or `db`, is refused, because `-d` and `--database` belong to relate. A manifest declares at most one positional argument.

properties.heading: What happens during a run
properties.text:
| Step                      | What relate does                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Find the action        | Reads every package under the extensions directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/extensions/`, else `~/.config/relate/extensions/`). A package that fails to load fails every `relate run`, help pages included |
| 2. Parse the command line | Against the action's manifest                                                                                                                                                                               |
| 3. Open the store         | The `--database` target, or `:memory:`                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 4. Fresh-store check      | An action whose manifest sets `requires-fresh-store` is refused when the target already holds nodes, before the extension starts                                                                            |
| 5. Start the extension    | Runs the manifest's executable with no shell and no arguments, and writes one JSON line to its stdin: each flag's value and the positional, by name                                                         |
| 6. Serve its requests     | Answers `initialize`, then the tool calls `write_cypher`, `read_cypher`, `update_schema`, `batch_cypher` and `report_output`, writing through relate's own store                                            |
| 7. Print the summary      | The text the extension gave `report_output`, then each starter statement on its own line, indented two spaces                                                                                               |

The manifest's `commit` policy frames the writes. Under `whole-import`, the whole run is one transaction, and any failure rolls all of it back. Under `per-batch`, each writing call commits when it lands, so the calls before a failure stay committed.

From the extensions specification, not from a run, relate holds every extension to these limits; a call over a limit is refused before it writes:

| Limit                                     | Value   |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------- |
| One statement, and one line of a response | 8 MiB   |
| Rows in one `write_cypher` call           | 1000    |
| Statements in one `batch_cypher` call     | 4096    |
| Bytes across the whole session            | 128 MiB |

The extension's stderr is kept up to 64 KiB and shown in a failure's error. Usage metrics name the command `run` with the action `extension`, never the action's own name; `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` sends none.

properties.heading: What it refuses
properties.text:
| Case                                                                                                                                   | Exit code | Message                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No action name, nothing installed                                                                                                      | 2         | `Error: run requires an action name (no actions installed; relate extension install <name> adds one)`                                                                                       |
| A name that is not installed                                                                                                           | 2         | `Error: no installed action '<name>' — first-party extension available: relate extension install <name>`, printed for any name the registry does not hold; nothing is fetched to produce it |
| An unknown flag                                                                                                                        | 2         | `Error: unexpected argument to run <name>: <flag>`, with `Did you mean '<flag>'?` when a flag of the action is close                                                                        |
| A positional the action does not declare                                                                                               | 2         | `Error: unexpected argument to run <name>: <argument>`                                                                                                                                      |
| A package that fails to load: a malformed manifest, a name that collides, an executable outside the package, another protocol revision | 2         | The refusal, which names the package                                                                                                                                                        |
| A target that is not fresh, for an action that requires one                                                                            | 1         | `the extension '<name>' requires a fresh store, but the target holds <n> nodes`                                                                                                             |
| The extension breaks the protocol, exceeds a session limit, exits non-zero or is killed                                                | 1         | One `Error:` line                                                                                                                                                                           |

A usage error (exit code 2) is followed by the usage line, the action's own when the name resolved, and `Run 'relate run --help' for more information.` (or the action's help hint). A refused single call, such as an unknown tool or one statement over its limit, is answered to the extension as an error and does not end the run.

properties.heading: relate serve
properties.text: `relate serve` opens one store and hosts relate's network [surfaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#surface) on it until it gets SIGINT or SIGTERM: the [HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#http-query-api) with `--http PORT`, [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) with `--mcp PORT` (streamable HTTP) or `--mcp stdio`, and [Bolt](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#bolt) with `--bolt PORT`. At least one surface flag is required, and ports have no defaults. Every listener binds `127.0.0.1` unless `--host` names another address, and no surface has Transport Layer Security (TLS). Writes are allowed unless the store is opened with `--read-only`.

properties.heading: Authentication
properties.text:
One credential guards every port listener. An HTTP or MCP request without it, or with the wrong one, gets `401 Unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="relate"`; a Bolt client gets `Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized` and the connection closes ([Bolt server](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/bolt/#authentication)). The startup lines on stderr say where the credential came from:

| Credential source                                   | Startup line                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--auth USER:PASSWORD`                              | `auth: basic (from --auth)`                                                                                                                       |
| `RELATE_AUTH=USER:PASSWORD`                         | `auth: basic (from RELATE_AUTH)`                                                                                                                  |
| Neither, a persistent store, first start            | `auth: generated token for user relate: <token>`, then `auth: persisted at <database>.auth-token (reused on restart)`                             |
| Neither, a persistent store whose token file exists | `auth: basic (token reused from <database>.auth-token)`                                                                                           |
| Neither, `:memory:`                                 | `auth: generated token for user relate: <token>`, then `auth: connect with auth=(relate, <token>) — :memory: generates a fresh token every start` |
| `--auth none`                                       | `auth: none (no credentials checked — publish ports only on trusted networks)`                                                                    |
| `--mcp stdio` alone                                 | No `auth:` line; the stdio transport has no challenge, since the MCP host started the process                                                     |

The token file sits beside the store (`./team` gets `./team.auth-token`), holds `relate:<token>`, and has mode `0600`. A value that is not `USER:PASSWORD` or `none` exits 1 with `Error: --auth: expected user:password or 'none'`. A credential on the command line shows in the process list; `RELATE_AUTH` keeps it out. There are no users or roles: the one credential can run every statement the open allows.

properties.heading: Bind host and plaintext
properties.text:
`--host` sets the address every listener binds, `127.0.0.1` by default. No surface has TLS. Any address that is not loopback exposes the credential and every result in plaintext, and the startup lines then include this warning (from the `relate serve` source, with `<host>` for the address):

```text
serve: WARNING: --host <host> exposes the PLAINTEXT HTTP/MCP/Bolt surfaces to the network — serve has no TLS; anyone who can reach the ports can present credentials. Keep 127.0.0.1 or front the server with TLS (ADR-0248).
```

Two more warnings print on a non-loopback `--host`, each when its condition holds. With `--max-connections 0` (unlimited):

```text
WARNING: --max-connections is unlimited on non-loopback --host <host>. Each accepted connection takes a thread before authentication. Set --max-connections to bound it (ADR-0333).
```

With `--http` served and both `--tx-idle-timeout-secs 0` and `--max-open-transactions 0`:

```text
WARNING: --tx-idle-timeout-secs and --max-open-transactions are both 0 on non-loopback --host <host>. An abandoned transaction never expires and the registry is unbounded, so it holds a snapshot pin until restart. Set one of the two to bound it (ADR-0435).
```

The defaults (128 connections, a 60-second idle expiry and 128 open transactions) print neither. A run with only `--mcp stdio` binds no listener and prints no warning. [Authentication and TLS for relate serve](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/serve/auth-and-tls/) covers a TLS-terminating proxy in front of relate.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
A run that stops on a signal or on the end of stdin exits 0. Every other exit is one of these:

| Event                                          | What happens                                       | Exit code |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| The store does not open                        | `Error: Failed to open Relate: <detail>`           | 1         |
| A port does not bind, or `--auth` is malformed | The error line; no surface line prints             | 1         |
| Any usage error                                | The error line, the usage line and a `--help` hint | 2         |

The refusals a run meets before it serves anything:

| Rule                                      | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No surface flag                           | Exit code 2: `Error: serve has nothing to serve: pass --http PORT and/or --mcp PORT\|stdio and/or --bolt PORT`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Port value                                | `0` through `65535`. `0` binds a free port the operating system picks, and the startup line names the bound port. Any other value exits 2: `Error: --http expects a port number (0-65535), got "<value>"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| A port already in use                     | Exit code 1 before any surface line prints: `Error: serve --http <port>: cannot bind <host>:<port>: <reason>`; the reason is the operating system's text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `--mcp` twice, or both `PORT` and `stdio` | Exit code 2: `Error: serve --mcp may be given only once`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| A listener flag without its listener      | Exit code 2. `--origin` needs `--http`; `--ws-allow-origin`, `--ws-max-connections` and `--bolt-identity` need `--bolt`; `--tx-idle-timeout-secs` and `--max-open-transactions` need `--http`; `--header-deadline-secs` and `--body-deadline-secs` need `--http` or `--mcp PORT`. Each message names the flag and the listener, such as `Error: serve --origin configures the --http surface, which this run does not serve: pass --http PORT or drop --origin` |
| `--auth` with only `--mcp stdio`          | Exit code 2: `Error: serve --mcp stdio skips auth (the host spawned the process, ADR-0232); --auth applies to the --http PORT/--mcp PORT/--bolt listeners only`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| A statement after the flags               | Exit code 2: `Error: unexpected argument to serve: <statement>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

[Read-only serving](#read-only-serving) lists the refusals of `--read-only`, and the server pages list each surface's request errors.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
These examples run in a new, empty directory. This first command writes: it creates the directory store `./team` with three people and two projects:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

The stdio transport, read-only, with stdin already closed: relate opens the store, starts the transport, sees the end of input, and exits 0. An MCP host keeps stdin open instead:

```bash verify
relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team --read-only < /dev/null
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
serve: opened the store read-only — no writer lease and never creates the store; every write fails
serve: MCP (stdio) serving on stdin/stdout (auth: none)
serve: stdin closed, shutting down
exit=0
```

The HTTP Query API on port 8869, read-only, with the credential from `RELATE_AUTH`. The script waits for the port, sends one statement without the credential and one with it, stops the server with SIGTERM, and then prints the server's stderr:

```bash
RELATE_AUTH=ada:example-password relate serve --database ./team --read-only --http 8869 2> serve.log &
server=$!
for i in $(seq 50); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8869/ && break; sleep 0.1; done
curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8869/db/neo4j/query/v2 \
  -d '{"statement": "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"}'
echo
curl -s -u ada:example-password -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8869/db/neo4j/query/v2 \
  -d '{"statement": "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name"}'
echo
kill -TERM "$server"
wait "$server"
echo "exit=$?"
cat serve.log
```

A run on port 8869 printed:

```text
{"errors":[{"code":"42NFF","message":"authentication required"}]}
{"data":{"fields":["name"],"values":[["Ada"],["Grace"],["Noor"]]},"bookmarks":[]}
exit=0
serve: opened the store read-only (ADR-0306) — no writer lease and never creates the store; every write fails
auth: basic (from RELATE_AUTH)
serve: HTTP Query API v2 listening on http://127.0.0.1:8869 (auth: basic)
serve: shutting down
```

Without `--read-only`, the server allows writes and takes a final checkpoint when it stops.

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
`--database` (short form `-d`) is required: a directory, a path ending in `.rl`, or `:memory:`. Each flag beats its environment variable, which beats the default. Besides its own flags, `relate serve` takes `--snapshot-format` and the query-run flags named in the table's last row, with the same resolution as in a query session. Any other query-run flag, such as `--timeout`, `--mode` or `--wal-dir`, exits 2 with `Error: unexpected argument to serve: <flag>`. `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS` sets the checkpoint period, since `--checkpoint-interval-secs` is not accepted.

| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--database`, `-d`                                                                                                                                                     | `PATH`                    | `required`                                                                                                           | `relate serve` | —     | The store to serve: a directory, a `.rl` file, or `:memory:`.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `--host`                                                                                                                                                               | `HOST`                    | `127.0.0.1`                                                                                                          | `relate serve` | —     | Bind host for every served surface; a non-loopback value exposes the plaintext surfaces and prints a startup WARNING.                                                                                                              |
| `--http`                                                                                                                                                               | `PORT`                    | unset                                                                                                                | `relate serve` | —     | HTTP Query API v2 on HOST:PORT.                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--mcp`                                                                                                                                                                | `PORT\|stdio`             | unset                                                                                                                | `relate serve` | —     | MCP: `stdio` runs the stdio transport in the foreground (no auth); `PORT` serves streamable HTTP.                                                                                                                                  |
| `--bolt`                                                                                                                                                               | `PORT`                    | unset                                                                                                                | `relate serve` | —     | Bolt and Bolt-over-WebSocket on HOST:PORT.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `--bolt-identity`                                                                                                                                                      | `STRING`                  | `Relate/<version>`                                                                                                   | `relate serve` | —     | HELLO SUCCESS `server` agent string for the Bolt surface. Environment: [`RELATE_IDENTITY`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-identity).                                                                     |
| `--read-only`                                                                                                                                                          | `[=snapshot\|live]`       | unset                                                                                                                | `relate serve` | —     | Open the existing store read-only: no writer lease, never creates it, every write fails; `live` tails the WAL (directories only). The MCP surface does not list `write_cypher`.                                                    |
| `--load`                                                                                                                                                               | `SOURCE`                  | unset                                                                                                                | `relate serve` | —     | Load a store from a source (a local `.rl`, a directory, or an http(s) URL to a `.rl`) into `--database`.                                                                                                                           |
| `--auth`                                                                                                                                                               | `USER:PASSWORD\|none`     | a generated token                                                                                                    | `relate serve` | —     | One basic-auth credential shared by every served listener; `none` disables authentication. HTTP transport only for MCP. Environment: [`RELATE_AUTH`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-auth).               |

Environment: [`RELATE_MAX_OPEN_TRANSACTIONS`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-max-open-transactions).  |

Environment: [`RELATE_MAX_CONNECTIONS`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-max-connections).                                            |

Environment: [`RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-snapshot-format). |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

properties.heading: Read-only serving
properties.text:
`--read-only` opens an existing store read-only for every surface. It never creates a store, holds no writer lease, refuses every write, and skips the final checkpoint at shutdown. The MCP surface then lists `read_cypher` and `get_schema` and no `write_cypher`.

| Spelling                              | Serves                                                                                                                                                                                      | Startup line                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--read-only`, `--read-only=snapshot` | The store as it was at open, beside any process that writes a directory store later                                                                                                         | `serve: opened the store read-only (ADR-0306) — no writer lease and never creates the store; every write fails`          |
| `--read-only=live`                    | A [live read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#live-read-only) open of a directory store: the writer's commits appear as they land. Refused for `.rl` files and `:memory:` | `serve: opened the store read-only and following the WAL (ADR-0306) — the writer's committed frames appear as they land` |
| `--database :memory: --load SOURCE`   | The source's content in memory, the source released after the load; every write fails                                                                                                       | `serve: loaded the store into memory (ADR-0500) — read-only, the source released after the load; every write fails`      |

`--read-only` must follow the word `serve`. Before it, the run exits 2 with `Error: serve takes --read-only after the verb, not before it (relate serve --read-only …)`, so a server never starts writable by accident. `--read-only live`, with a space, exits 2 with `Error: --read-only takes its value attached: --read-only=live`. A missing directory store exits 1 with `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`, and a missing `.rl` file with `Error: Failed to open Relate: storage error: database not found: <path>`. A `.rl` file another process holds for writing also exits 1 (`storage locked: <path>`).

properties.text:

properties.heading: Startup and shutdown
properties.text:
`relate serve` writes its startup lines to stderr, in this order: the non-loopback `--host` warning, the access line of a read-only open, the `auth:` lines, the two non-loopback limit warnings when they apply, then one line per surface. Stdout carries nothing, except the JSON-RPC replies of `--mcp stdio`. This run served a directory store read-only on all three port surfaces:

```text
serve: opened the store read-only (ADR-0306) — no writer lease and never creates the store; every write fails
auth: basic (token reused from ./team.auth-token)
serve: HTTP Query API v2 listening on http://127.0.0.1:8869 (auth: basic)
serve: Bolt listening on bolt://127.0.0.1:8871 (auth: basic)
serve: MCP (streamable HTTP) listening on http://127.0.0.1:8870 (auth: basic)
```

| Event                                     | What happens                                                                                                       | Exit code |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| SIGINT or SIGTERM                         | Prints `serve: shutting down`, closes the listeners, and takes the final checkpoint of a writable persistent store | 0         |
| The MCP host closes stdin (`--mcp stdio`) | Prints `serve: stdin closed, shutting down` and takes the same final checkpoint                                    | 0         |

The server sends one usage metrics event when it exits, unless usage metrics are off ([relate telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/telemetry/)); the statements it serves send none ([Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/)).

properties.heading: Surfaces
properties.text:
| Flag          | Surface                        | Listens on         | Requests                                                                                                         | Authentication |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `--http PORT` | HTTP Query API v2              | `http://HOST:PORT` | `POST /db/<name>/query/v2`, transactions under `/db/<name>/query/v2/tx`, and a public `GET /` discovery document | Basic          |
| `--mcp PORT`  | MCP, streamable HTTP transport | `http://HOST:PORT` | `POST /` with a complete JSON-RPC message                                                                        | Basic          |
| `--mcp stdio` | MCP, stdio transport           | stdin and stdout   | Newline-delimited JSON-RPC, until the host closes stdin                                                          | None           |
| `--bolt PORT` | Bolt and Bolt over WebSocket   | `bolt://HOST:PORT` | A Bolt driver, or a WebSocket upgrade from an allowed origin                                                     | Basic          |

The request and response formats are on the server pages: [HTTP Query API](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/http/), [MCP server](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/), and [Bolt server](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/bolt/).

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate serve --database PATH [--host HOST] [--http PORT] [--origin ORIGIN] [--mcp PORT|stdio] [--bolt PORT [--bolt-identity STRING] [--ws-allow-origin ORIGIN] [--ws-max-connections N]] [--read-only[=FRESHNESS]] [--load SOURCE] [--auth USER:PASSWORD] [--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE] [--max-traversal-depth N] [--expression-memory-limit SIZE] [--safe | --no-safe] [--logical-graph-size-limit SIZE] [--durability-mode MODE] [--snapshot-format F]
```

The usage line is the one `relate serve --help` prints. The HTTP limits (`--tx-idle-timeout-secs`, `--max-open-transactions`, `--header-deadline-secs`, `--body-deadline-secs`) and `--max-connections` are left out of it and listed under [Options](#options).

properties.heading: relate skill
properties.text: `relate skill` manages the copies of relate's agent [skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#skill) in the home directories of coding agents. The [skill bundle](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#skill-bundle) (`SKILL.md` and 15 reference files) is embedded in the binary, so every action works offline. The command has four actions: `install` writes the bundle into each detected agent's skills directory, `list` prints each agent's install state, `check` compares installed copies with the binary's bundle, and `remove` deletes copies relate wrote. It never opens a store.

properties.heading: Agents and paths
properties.text:
An agent is detected when the directory in the "Detected when this exists" column exists. The skill goes to `relate` under the agent's skills directory. The names are the ones the binary prints in its `valid agents:` line, in its order.

| `--agent`     | Agent       | Detected when this exists   | The skill goes to                         |
| ------------- | ----------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `claude-code` | Claude Code | `~/.claude`                 | `~/.claude/skills/relate`                 |
| `cursor`      | Cursor      | `~/.cursor`                 | `~/.cursor/skills/relate`                 |
| `windsurf`    | Windsurf    | `~/.codeium/windsurf`       | `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/relate`       |
| `copilot`     | Copilot     | `~/.copilot`                | `~/.copilot/skills/relate`                |
| `antigravity` | Antigravity | `~/.gemini/antigravity`     | `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills/relate`     |
| `gemini-cli`  | Gemini CLI  | `~/.gemini`                 | `~/.gemini/skills/relate`                 |
| `cline`       | Cline       | `~/.cline`                  | `~/.agents/skills/relate`                 |
| `codex`       | Codex       | `~/.codex`                  | `~/.codex/skills/relate`                  |
| `pi`          | Pi          | `~/.pi/agent`               | `~/.pi/agent/skills/relate`               |
| `opencode`    | OpenCode    | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode` | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/skills/relate` |
| `junie`       | Junie       | `~/.junie`                  | `~/.junie/skills/relate`                  |

`~` is `$HOME`. When `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is unset or empty, OpenCode's paths use `$HOME/.config` in its place. A skills directory inside a project, such as `.claude/skills/`, is outside every action's reach.

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code | When                                                                                                                |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | The action completed; for `check`, every installed copy matches                                                     |
| 1         | `check` found drift; no agent detected and no `--agent`; a refused path; a file system error                        |
| 2         | A usage error: no action, an unknown action or flag, `--force` with `list` or `check`, or an unknown `--agent` name |

| Message on stderr                                                                                                                             | Exit code | Cause                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Error: skill: no supported agents detected`                                                                                                  | 1         | No `--agent`, and none of the directories in the agent table exists; a second line lists the valid names |
| `Error: skill: unknown agent: '<name>'`                                                                                                       | 2         | `--agent` names no agent in the table; a second line lists the valid names                               |
| `Error: skill: refusing to touch <path>: no .relate-installed marker present (directory was not created by relate); pass --force to override` | 1         | `install` met a foreign directory, or `remove` met a foreign or legacy one                               |
| `Error: skill requires an action (install, remove, list or check)`                                                                            | 2         | `relate skill` with no action                                                                            |
| `Error: unexpected argument to skill: <argument>`                                                                                             | 2         | An unknown action or flag, or `--force` with `list` or `check`                                           |

The second line of the two agent errors is the same:

```text
valid agents: claude-code, cursor, windsurf, copilot, antigravity, gemini-cli, cline, codex, pi, opencode, junie
```

The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-skill-refusing-to-touch) has the remedies.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The examples run with a fresh home directory, written `<home>`. With no agent directory in it, every action that has no `--agent` stops:

```bash verify
relate skill list
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: skill: no supported agents detected
valid agents: claude-code, cursor, windsurf, copilot, antigravity, gemini-cli, cline, codex, pi, opencode, junie
exit=1
```

`--agent` installs for one agent, and creates its directory:

```bash verify
relate skill install --agent claude-code
```

```text
installed relate skill into <home>/.claude/skills/relate
```

With a Codex directory present too, `list` reports both detected agents:

```bash verify
mkdir -p "$HOME/.codex"
relate skill list
```

```text
claude-code: installed (<home>/.claude/skills/relate)
codex: not installed (<home>/.codex/skills/relate)
```

After a local edit to `SKILL.md`, `check` reports the drift and exits 1:

```bash verify
printf 'local note\n' >> "$HOME/.claude/skills/relate/SKILL.md"
relate skill check
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
claude-code: drifted (<home>/.claude/skills/relate)
  differs: SKILL.md
codex: not installed (<home>/.codex/skills/relate)
exit=1
```

`remove` deletes the copy that carries the marker:

```bash verify
relate skill remove --agent claude-code
```

```text
removed relate skill from <home>/.claude/skills/relate
```

properties.heading: Install states
properties.text:
`list` and `check` print one of four states for each agent's `<skills dir>/relate`. The state decides what `install` and `remove` may do without `--force`.

| State                             | What is at the path                                                                                                                  | `install`                       | `remove`                    |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `not installed`                   | Nothing                                                                                                                              | Writes the bundle               | Succeeds; nothing to delete |
| `installed`                       | A directory with relate's `.relate-installed` marker file                                                                            | Replaces the bundle             | Deletes the directory       |
| `installed (legacy bundle)`       | A directory without the marker whose `SKILL.md` frontmatter has `name: relate` and a `version:` line: an older or hand-copied bundle | Replaces it and adds the marker | Refused                     |
| `foreign (not managed by relate)` | Anything else, including a symbolic link                                                                                             | Refused                         | Refused                     |

A refusal names the path and exits with [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) 1. `--force` replaces or deletes the directory whatever its state.

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
| Flag      | Argument | Default             | Scope          | Since | Description                                                                                               |
| --------- | -------- | ------------------- | -------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--agent` | `NAME`   | all detected agents | `relate skill` | —     | Scope the action to one agent (case-insensitive).                                                         |
| `--force` | —        | `refuse`            | `relate skill` | —     | Clobber `<skills dir>/relate` even when the command would refuse it; a usage error on `list` and `check`. |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

| Rule                    | Behavior                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--agent` names         | Matched case-insensitively against the names in the agent table; given twice, the last one applies                   |
| `--agent` and detection | A named agent is a target whether or not its directory exists; `install --agent <name>` creates the skills directory |
| `--force`               | Accepted by `install` and `remove` only; with `list` or `check` it is a usage error (exit code 2)                    |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Install the agent skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/install-the-skill/): the CLI installer, the skills CLI, and a checked manual copy
- [`relate upgrade`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/upgrade/): the binary update that refreshes installed copies
- [Agent mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/agent-mode/): how the CLI behaves under a detected [agent harness](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#agent-harness)
- [Exit codes and errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/): the exit codes every command shares

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate skill install|remove|list|check [--agent NAME] [--force]
```

| Action    | Does                                                                | Prints on stdout                                                                                                                            | Exit code on success                              |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `install` | Writes the bundle into `<skills dir>/relate` for each target agent  | `installed relate skill into <path>`, one line per agent                                                                                    | 0                                                 |
| `list`    | Reads each target agent's `<skills dir>/relate` and classifies it   | `<agent>: <state> (<path>)`, one line per agent                                                                                             | 0                                                 |
| `check`   | Compares each installed copy with the binary's bundle, file by file | `<agent>: up to date (<path>)` or `<agent>: drifted (<path>)` with one line per differing file; agents without a copy get their `list` line | 0 when every copy matches, 1 when any has drifted |
| `remove`  | Deletes `<skills dir>/relate` for each target agent                 | `removed relate skill from <path>`, one line per agent                                                                                      | 0                                                 |

Without `--agent`, an action targets every detected agent. `list` and `check` write nothing.

properties.heading: What install writes
properties.text:
| Item                | Content                                                                                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SKILL.md`          | The bundle's cheat sheet, with the binary's version written into its `version:` frontmatter line |
| `references/`       | The 15 reference files, unchanged                                                                |
| `.relate-installed` | The marker that makes the directory relate's own                                                 |

The bundle is written into a staging directory beside the destination and then renamed into place, so a reader never sees a half-written bundle; the previous copy is replaced whole, and a reference file the new bundle no longer has does not linger. With several targets, `install` and `remove` check every target's state before changing any, so a refusal on one agent leaves the others untouched.

`check` compares the bytes `install` would write. Each difference is one indented line: `missing: <file>`, `differs: <file>` or `extra: <file>`, with paths relative to the skill directory.

After [`relate upgrade`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/upgrade/) replaces the binary, it runs `relate skill install` from the new binary for the detected agents. When any of them holds a relate copy, this happens without a prompt; when none does, it asks first on a terminal, installs without asking under `--yes`, and otherwise prints `run: relate skill install` and installs nothing. A foreign directory is never touched.

properties.heading: relate telemetry
properties.text: `relate telemetry on|off|status` manages the anonymous usage metrics the `relate` CLI sends, its [telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#telemetry). `off` and `on` write the setting to `config.json` in the user's config directory and print the file's path; `status` prints whether usage metrics are on and which layer decided it. The setting is the third of four layers: `DO_NOT_TRACK` and `RELATE_TELEMETRY` in the environment outrank it. Usage metrics are on by default. What the events hold, and what they never hold, is on [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/#events).

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code                                                                 | When                                                                 | Message on stderr                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [0](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-0) | The action ran                                                       | None                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [1](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-1) | `on` or `off` found no config directory, or could not write the file | `Error: telemetry: cannot resolve a config directory (set $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, $HOME, $APPDATA, or $USERPROFILE)`, or `Error: telemetry: writing <path to config.json>: <reason>` |
| [2](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/#exit-2) | No action                                                            | `Error: telemetry requires an action (on, off, or status)`                                                                                                                     |
| 2                                                                         | An unknown action, or a second argument                              | `Error: unexpected argument to telemetry: <argument>`                                                                                                                          |

Each exit 2 also prints the usage line and `Run 'relate telemetry --help' for more information.`

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
These examples run with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` set, in a fresh home directory shown as `<home>`, so no command here sends anything. `status` names the environment layer, `off` writes the file, and `env -u DO_NOT_TRACK` runs one command without the variable to show the file's layer underneath:

```bash verify
relate telemetry status
relate telemetry off
env -u DO_NOT_TRACK relate telemetry status
```

```text
disabled (DO_NOT_TRACK)
telemetry disabled (<home>/.config/relate/config.json)
disabled (config file)
```

The file holds one key:

```bash verify
cat "$HOME/.config/relate/config.json"
echo
```

```text
{"telemetry":false}
```

`RELATE_TELEMETRY` outranks the file:

```bash verify
env -u DO_NOT_TRACK RELATE_TELEMETRY=0 relate telemetry status
```

```text
disabled (RELATE_TELEMETRY)
```

With `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set to an absolute path, the file goes under it:

```bash verify
mkdir -p "$PWD/config"
XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$PWD/config" relate telemetry off
```

The working directory is shown as `<dir>`:

```text
telemetry disabled (<dir>/config/relate/config.json)
```

A missing or unknown action is a usage error:

```bash verify
relate telemetry
echo "exit=$?"
relate telemetry maybe
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: telemetry requires an action (on, off, or status)
Usage: relate telemetry on|off|status
Run 'relate telemetry --help' for more information.
exit=2
Error: unexpected argument to telemetry: maybe
Usage: relate telemetry on|off|status
Run 'relate telemetry --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/): the events, what is never collected, and the surfaces that never send anything
- [Run relate in a sandbox](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/run-in-a-sandbox/): relate for an agent with usage metrics off
- [Environment variables](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/environment-variables/): `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `RELATE_TELEMETRY` and the variables for development and testing
- [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/): every flag of every command

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate telemetry on|off|status
```

| Action   | Does                                          | Prints on stdout                                                                                                |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `on`     | Writes `{"telemetry":true}` to `config.json`  | `telemetry enabled (<path to config.json>)`                                                                     |
| `off`    | Writes `{"telemetry":false}` to `config.json` | `telemetry disabled (<path to config.json>)`                                                                    |
| `status` | Reads the layers; writes nothing              | `<enabled\|disabled> (<layer>)`, the layer being `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `RELATE_TELEMETRY`, `config file` or `default` |

Exactly one action is required, in lowercase. The command takes no flags beyond `--help`.

properties.heading: The first-run notice and the events
properties.text: The first statement run with usage metrics on prints `relate collects anonymous usage metrics; disable anytime: relate telemetry off` on stderr, once per install. A run with usage metrics off prints no notice, sends nothing and writes no `state.json`. The setting a run reads is the one in force when it starts, so `relate telemetry off` itself still sends its own command event when usage metrics were on. The four events, their properties, the install ID and the delivery are listed on [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/); the `agent` and `minimal` builds from source contain no usage metrics code and have no `telemetry` command.

properties.heading: Where the setting lives
properties.text:
`on` and `off` write one file, created with mode `0600` on Unix:

| Environment                                           | File                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set to an absolute path             | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/config.json`                                                                                                    |
| Otherwise, with `HOME` set                            | `$HOME/.config/relate/config.json`                                                                                                       |
| Otherwise, with `APPDATA` set to an absolute path     | `$APPDATA/relate/config.json`                                                                                                            |
| Otherwise, with `USERPROFILE` set to an absolute path | `$USERPROFILE/.config/relate/config.json`                                                                                                |
| None of them                                          | No file: exit code 1 with `Error: telemetry: cannot resolve a config directory (set $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, $HOME, $APPDATA, or $USERPROFILE)` |

The same directory holds `state.json`, which holds the random install ID and the first-run notice flag. Any run with usage metrics on, `relate telemetry off` included, creates it when it is missing and sends one `RELATE-CLI_COMMAND` event (`command: telemetry`, `action: off`) before the new setting takes effect. A run with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` set writes neither.

properties.heading: Which layer decides
properties.text:
The first layer that matches decides, and `status` names it:

| Order | Layer                                                     | Turns usage metrics off | Turns them on       | `status` prints                                               |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `DO_NOT_TRACK`                                            | `1` or `true`           | —                   | `disabled (DO_NOT_TRACK)`                                     |
| 2     | `RELATE_TELEMETRY`                                        | `0`, `false` or `off`   | `1`, `true` or `on` | `disabled (RELATE_TELEMETRY)` or `enabled (RELATE_TELEMETRY)` |
| 3     | `config.json`, written by `relate telemetry off` and `on` | `false`                 | `true`              | `disabled (config file)` or `enabled (config file)`           |
| 4     | Default                                                   | —                       | on                  | `enabled (default)`                                           |

Both variables are read trimmed and case-insensitive (`DO_NOT_TRACK=TRUE` and `RELATE_TELEMETRY=OFF` count). `DO_NOT_TRACK=0` is not an opt-out and passes the decision to the next layer, and so does a `RELATE_TELEMETRY` value other than those six, in any case. `relate telemetry on` writes the file even while `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` is set, and the variable still wins. `relate telemetry off` does not change the environment, so a `RELATE_TELEMETRY=1` in it still turns usage metrics on.

properties.heading: relate upgrade
properties.text: `relate upgrade` replaces the running `relate` binary with the latest release, after checking the release's checksum list against the signing key built into the binary. `relate update` is the same command. `--check` reports the installed and latest versions and changes nothing. Self-upgrade runs on macOS and Linux, on amd64 and arm64; it never opens a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store).

properties.heading: Errors and exit codes
properties.text:
| Exit code | When                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0         | Up to date, `--check` completed, or the upgrade completed                                                                                       |
| 1         | Any failure in the steps of [What it checks](#what-it-checks), including no network                                                             |
| 2         | A usage error: `Error: unexpected argument to upgrade: <argument>`, then the usage line and `Run 'relate upgrade --help' for more information.` |

When the release list cannot be read, the message names its URL, the reason, and the reinstall command:

```text
Error: upgrade: could not read the release list: GET <url>: <reason>; reinstall manually instead: curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash
```

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The `--check` runs on this page were recorded with `RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL` pointing at a copy of `releases.json` served from the local machine, so they needed no network. With the latest release equal to the installed version:

```bash
relate upgrade --check
```

```text
current version: 1.0.1
latest release:  1.0.1
relate is up to date
```

With the copy edited to list a higher version, `v1.99.0`, the report names it and nothing is downloaded:

```text
current version: 1.0.1
latest release:  1.99.0
upgrade available: run `relate upgrade` to install 1.99.0
```

A run that cannot reach the release list exits 1. This one had `RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8874/releases.json` with nothing listening; the text after `io:` comes from the operating system, and this recording is from macOS:

```text
Error: upgrade: could not read the release list: GET http://127.0.0.1:8874/releases.json: io: Connection refused (os error 61); reinstall manually instead: curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash
```

A flag the command does not take is a usage error:

```bash verify
relate upgrade --json
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Error: unexpected argument to upgrade: --json
Usage: relate upgrade [--yes] [--check]
Run 'relate upgrade --help' for more information.
exit=2
```

properties.heading: Options
properties.text:
| Flag      | Argument | Default | Scope            | Since | Description                                                                              |
| --------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--yes`   | —        | off     | `relate upgrade` | —     | Install the skill bundle after the upgrade when none is installed yet, without a prompt. |
| `--check` | —        | off     | `relate upgrade` | —     | Read-only report of the current and latest versions.                                     |

A — under Since: the data does not record the release that added the flag.

Any other argument, such as `--json`, is a usage error (exit code 2).

properties.heading: Output
properties.text:
