Every successful outcome, `--check` included, prints its status lines and nothing after them; releases up to 0.1.1 also printed a two-line notice of the project's rename.

| Outcome                  | Status lines on stdout                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--check`, current       | `current version: <version>`, `latest release:  <version>`, `relate is up to date`                                           |
| `--check`, newer release | `current version: <version>`, `latest release:  <version>`, ``upgrade available: run `relate upgrade` to install <version>`` |
| No `--check`, current    | `relate <version> is up to date (latest release: <version>)`                                                                 |
| No `--check`, upgraded   | `upgrading relate <old> -> <new> (<asset>)`, then `upgraded relate <old> -> <new> at <path>`                                 |

Every failure starts with `Error: upgrade: ` on stderr and exits 1; a failed replace (step 8) adds a second line that names the reinstall command.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/): the first install, with the same signature check
- [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/): the signing key and the manual verification steps
- [`relate skill`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/skill/): the skill copies the upgrade refreshes
- [Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/): what a new release does to a store written by an older one
- [Problems relate solves: offline and sandboxed use](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#offline-and-sandboxed-use): the commands that reach the network

properties.heading: Skill refresh
properties.text:
After the binary is replaced, `relate upgrade` runs `relate skill install` from the new binary for every detected agent, so the installed [skill](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#skill) matches the new version:

| Detected agents                               | What happens                                            |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| At least one holds a relate copy              | Installs into every detected agent without a prompt     |
| None holds a copy, stdin is a terminal        | Asks `Install the relate skill? [Y/n] ` first           |
| None holds a copy, `--yes`                    | Installs without asking                                 |
| None holds a copy, not a terminal, no `--yes` | Prints `run: relate skill install` and installs nothing |
| A directory relate does not manage            | Left untouched, with a note naming it                   |
| No agent detected                             | Nothing                                                 |

The [`relate skill` reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/skill/#install-states) defines the states.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate upgrade [--yes] [--check]
relate update  [--yes] [--check]
```

| Run                      | Reads                                            | Changes                                                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate upgrade --check` | The release list                                 | Nothing                                                         |
| `relate upgrade`         | The release list, then the newer release's files | The binary at its current path, then the installed skill copies |

properties.heading: What it checks
properties.text:
`relate upgrade` runs these steps in order and stops at the first that fails. A failure before the last step leaves the running binary as it was.

| Step | Check                                                                                                                                                               | On failure                                                                                                  |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | The platform is macOS or Linux on amd64 or arm64                                                                                                                    | Exits 1; on Windows the message points to a manual download, because a running `.exe` cannot replace itself |
| 2    | `releases.json` is read, and its `latest.tag` has the form `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>`                                                                               | Exits 1 naming the URL and the reinstall command                                                            |
| 3    | The latest version is compared with the binary's own as three numbers                                                                                               | Not newer: prints that relate is up to date and exits 0                                                     |
| 4    | The release lists the platform binary (`relate-<os>-<arch>`), `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig`                                                                     | Exits 1 naming the missing file                                                                             |
| 5    | `SHA256SUMS.sig` verifies over the exact bytes of `SHA256SUMS`, as an SSH signature in the `relate-release` namespace, against the public key built into the binary | Exits 1                                                                                                     |
| 6    | The first line of `SHA256SUMS`, `# relate-release-version: <tag>`, names the release from step 2                                                                    | Exits 1; a list without that line is accepted only for a release at or below v0.14.0, and with a warning    |
| 7    | The platform binary is downloaded, and its SHA-256 equals its line in `SHA256SUMS`                                                                                  | Exits 1: `checksum verification failed for <asset> (expected <hash>, got <hash>); not upgrading`            |
| 8    | The new binary replaces the running one at its path                                                                                                                 | Exits 1 naming the reinstall command                                                                        |
| 9    | The skill copies are refreshed                                                                                                                                      | Never fails the upgrade                                                                                     |

`--check` stops after step 3. The key is the one `install.sh` pins; the [security reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/) gives it and the manual checks that match these steps. Steps 4 to 9 are described from the binary's source, not from a recorded run, because no release newer than the verified version exists to upgrade to.

properties.heading: Where it downloads from
properties.text:
| File                                                                                | Location                                                            | Variable that overrides it                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| The release list                                                                    | `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json`                                 | `RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL`                               |
| `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.sig` and the binary                                       | `https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases/download/<tag>/<file>` | `RELATE_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_URL` (the part before `/<tag>`) |
| The same three files, when the first location answers 404 and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set | The GitHub API's release-asset route, `https://api.github.com`      | `RELATE_GITHUB_API_URL`                                  |

`GITHUB_TOKEN`, when set, is sent as a bearer token on the requests for the three files and never on the request for `releases.json`, and is never printed. The release list request has no retry, no cache, and no fallback location.

| Variable                      | Effect                                                                                        | Default                                                | Used by                                      |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`                | Optional bearer token for release-asset downloads; required while the repository is internal. | —                                                      | `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install` |
| `RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL`    | Override the release-metadata URL (dev and test).                                             | `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json`                    | `relate upgrade`                             |
| `RELATE_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_URL` | Override the base of the direct release-download route (dev and test).                        | `https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases/download` | `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install` |
| `RELATE_GITHUB_API_URL`       | Override the base of the GitHub API asset route (dev and test).                               | `https://api.github.com`                               | `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install` |

properties.heading: Composing clauses
properties.text: Composing clauses combine queries. `UNION` stacks the rows of two queries, a `CALL { … }` subquery runs a query once per input row, `EXISTS`, `COUNT` and `COLLECT` turn a subquery into a value, `USE` picks the [namespace](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#namespace) a statement runs against, `CALL <procedure>` runs a built-in procedure, `NEXT` feeds one query's rows into the next, and `WHEN … THEN … ELSE` picks one query by condition. Every form on this page runs without a preview opt-in.

properties.heading: CALL IN TRANSACTIONS
properties.text:
`IN TRANSACTIONS` commits the subquery's work in batches of input rows, each batch its own [transaction](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#transaction). `ON ERROR …` and `REPORT STATUS AS …` may come in either order. Outside an explicit transaction, each batch commits on its own: a batch that committed stays committed when a later one fails. Inside an explicit transaction, the batches commit or roll back with that transaction.

| Option                                     | Default                | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `OF <n> ROWS`                              | 1,000 rows             | Input rows per batch                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `IN [<n>] CONCURRENT TRANSACTIONS`         | Off                    | Accepted; the batches run one after another                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ON ERROR FAIL`                            | The default            | The statement fails at the first failing batch; earlier batches stay committed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `ON ERROR CONTINUE`                        | —                      | Skips the failing batch and runs the rest                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `ON ERROR BREAK`                           | —                      | Stops at the failing batch; the statement succeeds with what committed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `ON ERROR RETRY [FOR <duration>] [THEN …]` | Without `THEN`: `FAIL` | Accepted, but no batch is retried: the duration is ignored and the `THEN` fallback applies at once. Without `THEN`, the statement fails as under `ON ERROR FAIL`                                                                                                                                                      |
| `REPORT STATUS AS <variable>`              | Off                    | Binds a map per input row: `started`, `committed`, `transactionId` and `errorMessage`. Needs `ON ERROR CONTINUE`, `BREAK`, or `RETRY … THEN CONTINUE` or `THEN BREAK`; otherwise `syntax error: InvalidReportStatusUsage: REPORT STATUS requires ON ERROR CONTINUE, BREAK, or RETRY with THEN CONTINUE or THEN BREAK` |

A write before `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` in the same statement fails with `syntax error: WriteBeforeCallInTransactions: a write cannot precede CALL IN TRANSACTIONS`, and `LOAD CSV` counts as a write ([writing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/writing-clauses/#examples)). Every input row runs the subquery once and counts against the fixed budget of 100,000 nested evaluation passes per statement ([limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/)).

properties.heading: CALL procedure
properties.text:
| Form                                      | Result                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CALL db.labels()` as the whole statement | Every column the procedure yields                                                 |
| `CALL db.labels() YIELD label`            | The named columns                                                                 |
| `YIELD *`                                 | Every column                                                                      |
| `YIELD label AS l`                        | The column renamed                                                                |
| `YIELD … WHERE <predicate>`               | The rows that pass the predicate                                                  |
| Inside a larger query                     | Runs once per input row                                                           |
| A column the procedure does not yield     | ``syntax error: UnknownProcedureOutput: <procedure> does not return `<column>` `` |
| A name that is not a procedure            | `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: <name>`                                         |

`SHOW PROCEDURES` lists the procedures with their signatures; the [procedures](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/procedures/) page describes them.

properties.heading: CALL subqueries
properties.text:
A `CALL { … }` subquery runs once for each incoming row. The scope clause in parentheses names the outer variables the body can read.

| Scope               | Body can read                            | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CALL (a, b) { … }` | `a` and `b`                              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `CALL (*) { … }`    | Every variable in scope                  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `CALL () { … }`     | No outer variable                        | Reading one fails with `syntax error: UndefinedVariable: variable '<name>' not defined`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `CALL { WITH a … }` | The variables the leading `WITH` imports | Deprecated. `EXPLAIN` reports notification `01N00`, ``The `CALL { … }` subquery has no variable scope clause.``, with the remedy ``Add the scope clause the body imports: `CALL (n) { … }`, or `CALL () { … }` when it imports nothing.`` |

| Body                                                        | Rows after the subquery                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ends in `RETURN`                                            | One row per row the body returns, per input row; an input row for which the body returns nothing is dropped                                  |
| Ends in `RETURN`, under `OPTIONAL CALL`                     | One row per row the body returns, per input row; an input row for which the body returns nothing is kept, with the returned variables `null` |
| No `RETURN` (a unit subquery, such as one that only writes) | The input rows, unchanged                                                                                                                    |

| Rule                                               | Behavior                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A returned name that an outer variable already has | ``syntax error: VariableAlreadyBound: Variable `<name>` already declared in outer scope`` |
| Aggregation in the body                            | Per input row: `CALL (p) { MATCH (p)-->(x) RETURN count(x) AS n }` counts for each `p`    |
| Nesting                                            | A body can hold another `CALL` subquery                                                   |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store, starting from the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

`ORDER BY` after a `UNION` sorts the last branch only:

```cypher run name=union-last-branch
MATCH (r:Project) RETURN r.name AS name
UNION
MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name DESC
```

```table
| name             |
|------------------|
| "relate"         |
| "opencypher-tck" |
| "Noor"           |
| "Grace"          |
| "Ada"            |
5 rows
```

Wrapped in `CALL () { … }`, the sort covers every row:

```cypher run name=union-sorted
CALL () {
  MATCH (r:Project) RETURN r.name AS name
  UNION
  MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name
}
RETURN name ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name             |
|------------------|
| "Ada"            |
| "Grace"          |
| "Noor"           |
| "opencypher-tck" |
| "relate"         |
5 rows
```

A scoped subquery counts per person; Noor, with no project, gets `0` because an aggregate always returns a row:

```cypher run name=call-scope
MATCH (p:Person)
CALL (p) {
  MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->(r:Project)
  RETURN count(r) AS projects
}
RETURN p.name AS name, projects ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name    | projects |
|---------|----------|
| "Ada"   | 1        |
| "Grace" | 2        |
| "Noor"  | 0        |
3 rows
```

Without an aggregate, Noor's row is dropped, unless the call is `OPTIONAL`:

```cypher run name=optional-call
MATCH (p:Person)
OPTIONAL CALL (p) {
  MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->(r:Project)
  RETURN r.name AS project
}
RETURN p.name AS name, project ORDER BY name, project
```

```table
| name    | project          |
|---------|------------------|
| "Ada"   | "relate"         |
| "Grace" | "opencypher-tck" |
| "Grace" | "relate"         |
| "Noor"  | null             |
4 rows
```

Batches that report their status. This writes a `Row` node for each value except the one that divides by zero:

```cypher run name=in-transactions
UNWIND [1, 0, 2] AS i
CALL (i) { CREATE (:Row {inverse: 1 / i}) } IN TRANSACTIONS OF 1 ROWS
  ON ERROR CONTINUE
  REPORT STATUS AS s
RETURN i, s.committed AS committed, s.errorMessage AS error
```

```table
| i | committed | error       |
|---|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | true      | null        |
| 0 | false     | "/ by zero" |
| 2 | true      | null        |
3 rows · nodes created: 2, properties set: 2, labels added: 2
```

The three subquery expressions on one row per person:

```cypher run name=subquery-expressions
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.name AS name,
       EXISTS { (p)-[:KNOWS]->() } AS knowsSomeone,
       COUNT { (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->() } AS projects,
       COLLECT { MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->(r) RETURN r.name ORDER BY r.name } AS projectNames
ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name    | knowsSomeone | projects | projectNames                 |
|---------|--------------|----------|------------------------------|
| "Ada"   | true         | 1        | ["relate"]                   |
| "Grace" | false        | 2        | ["opencypher-tck", "relate"] |
| "Noor"  | false        | 0        | []                           |
3 rows
```

```cypher run name=collect-two-columns expect=error
RETURN COLLECT { MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name, p.role } AS pairs
```

```table
error: syntax error: parse error: A COLLECT subquery must end with a single return column
  RETURN COLLECT { MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name, p.role } AS pairs
                                                            ^
```

`USE` names the namespace; `system` refuses a `MATCH`:

```cypher run name=use-neo4j
USE neo4j MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people
```

```table
| people |
|--------|
| 3      |
1 row
```

```cypher run name=use-system expect=error
USE system MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS n
```

```table
error: semantic error: SemanticError: The following unsupported clauses were used: MATCH. 
The system database supports a restricted set of Cypher clauses. The supported clause structure for procedure calls is: CALL, YIELD, RETURN. YIELD and RETURN clauses are optional. The order of the clauses is fixed and each can only occur once.
```

A procedure call, with its column renamed and filtered:

```cypher run name=procedure
CALL db.labels() YIELD label AS l WHERE l STARTS WITH 'Pro'
RETURN l
```

```table
| l         |
|-----------|
| "Project" |
1 row
```

`NEXT` passes the returned columns on, and `WHEN` picks a branch per row:

```cypher run name=next-when
MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.role AS role
NEXT
WHEN role = 'maintainer' THEN RETURN name, 'reviews' AS duty
ELSE RETURN name, 'builds' AS duty
```

```table
| name    | duty      |
|---------|-----------|
| "Noor"  | "reviews" |
| "Ada"   | "builds"  |
| "Grace" | "builds"  |
3 rows
```

properties.heading: NEXT and WHEN
properties.text:
| Form                                             | Result                                                                                                | Rule                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<query> NEXT <query>`                           | The second query runs on the first one's returned rows, with its column names as variables            | `NEXT` at the start fails: `syntax error: parse error: InvalidNextStatement: NEXT must follow a statement, not begin one`                                                                 |
| `WHEN <predicate> THEN <query> … [ELSE <query>]` | The query of the first branch whose predicate is `true`; no `true` branch and no `ELSE` gives no rows | Starts a statement, a subquery body or a query after `NEXT`. Every branch returns the same columns: `syntax error: ColumnNameConflict: conditional branches must return the same columns` |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Reading clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/reading-clauses/): `MATCH`, `WITH`, `RETURN` and the rest of a single query.
- [Writing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/writing-clauses/): what runs inside a writing subquery.
- [Procedures](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/procedures/): the built-in procedures `CALL` runs.
- [Namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/namespaces/): the three namespaces `USE` can name.
- [Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/): how statements and explicit transactions commit.

properties.heading: Subquery expressions
properties.text:
| Form            | Value                                     | Body                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `EXISTS { … }`  | `true` when the body has at least one row | A pattern with an optional `WHERE`, or a query with `MATCH` and `RETURN`                                                                         |
| `COUNT { … }`   | The number of rows the body returns       | The same as `EXISTS`                                                                                                                             |
| `COLLECT { … }` | A list of the body's single column        | A query ending in `RETURN` of exactly one column; otherwise `syntax error: parse error: A COLLECT subquery must end with a single return column` |

| Rule                | Behavior                                                                                 |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Outer variables     | The body reads them without a scope clause                                               |
| Writes in the body  | `syntax error: InvalidClauseComposition: writes are not allowed in subquery expressions` |
| `UNION` in the body | Allowed, with the same column-name rule as a top-level `UNION`                           |

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
<query> UNION [DISTINCT | ALL] <query> [UNION [DISTINCT | ALL] <query> …]

[OPTIONAL] CALL [(<variable>, … | * )] { <query> }
  [IN [<n> CONCURRENT] TRANSACTIONS [OF <n> ROWS]
    [ON ERROR CONTINUE | BREAK | FAIL | RETRY [FOR <duration>] [THEN CONTINUE | BREAK | FAIL]]
    [REPORT STATUS AS <variable>]]

EXISTS { <pattern> [WHERE <predicate>] | <query> }
COUNT { <pattern> [WHERE <predicate>] | <query> }
COLLECT { <query that returns one column> }

USE <namespace> <query>

CALL <procedure>([<argument>, …]) [YIELD * | YIELD <column> [AS <alias>], … [WHERE <predicate>]]

<query> NEXT <query> [NEXT <query> …]

WHEN <predicate> THEN <query> [WHEN <predicate> THEN <query> …] [ELSE <query>]
```

properties.heading: UNION
properties.text:
| Form                      | Result                                       |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `UNION`, `UNION DISTINCT` | The rows of every branch, duplicates removed |
| `UNION ALL`               | The rows of every branch, duplicates kept    |

| Rule                                              | Behavior                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Column names                                      | Every branch returns the same column names; the order of the columns may differ, and rows are matched by name                |
| Mixing `UNION` and `UNION ALL` in one statement   | `syntax error: InvalidClauseComposition: mixing UNION and UNION ALL`                                                         |
| Different column names                            | `syntax error: DifferentColumnsInUnion: all UNION branches must have the same column names`                                  |
| `ORDER BY`, `SKIP`, `LIMIT` after the last branch | Apply to that branch only; an `ORDER BY` after a `CALL () { … }` that wraps the union sorts every row ([example](#examples)) |
| `USE`                                             | Each branch may start with `USE`, naming the same namespace                                                                  |

properties.heading: USE
properties.text:
A store has three fixed namespaces: `neo4j` holds the graph, `system` answers administration commands, and `system_ontologies` is listed but not queryable. A statement without `USE` runs against the session namespace, `neo4j` unless `--namespace` says otherwise ([namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/namespaces/)).

| Form                                                      | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `USE neo4j <query>`                                       | Runs against the graph                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `USE system <query>`                                      | Runs a procedure call or `SHOW DATABASES`; `SHOW INDEXES` and `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` fail with `syntax error: InvalidClauseComposition: NotAllowedOnSystemDatabase: SHOW INDEXES and SHOW CONSTRAINTS are per-database catalogs and are not available on the system database`, and a `MATCH` fails with `semantic error: SemanticError: The following unsupported clauses were used: MATCH.` followed by the clauses `system` supports |
| `USE system_ontologies <query>`                           | `semantic error: SemanticError: This database is not queryable. Use the db.ontology.* procedures on the user database 'neo4j' instead.`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `USE <other name>`                                        | `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `USE` in two `UNION` branches naming different namespaces | `semantic error: SemanticError: Multiple graphs in the same query not allowed here. This feature is only available on composite databases. Attempted to access graph <name>`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `USE graph.byName(…)`                                     | `semantic error: SemanticError: Dynamic graph lookup not allowed here. This feature is only available on composite databases. Attempted to access graph graph.byName(<argument>)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `USE` after another clause                                | `syntax error: InvalidPlacementOfUseClause: USE clause must be either the first clause in a query, or preceded by an importing WITH clause`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `CALL { USE neo4j … }`                                    | Runs; `USE` may open a subquery without a scope clause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `CALL () { USE neo4j … }`                                 | `syntax error: UndefinedVariable: variable 'neo4j' not defined`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

properties.heading: Cypher versions
properties.text: Every [Cypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#cypher) statement runs as [Cypher 25](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#cypher-25), the Neo4j Cypher version aligned with [GQL](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#gql), the ISO graph query language. A `CYPHER 5` prefix runs one statement as Cypher 5. Syntax that is not settled yet ships as a [preview feature](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#preview-feature) and stays off until `RELATE_PREVIEW` names it. No other version exists, and nothing else changes the version a statement runs as.

properties.heading: Conformance
properties.text:
The openCypher Technology Compatibility Kit (TCK) is the language contract. relate's published compliance record states that "no engine document publishes a current TCK pass count any more": coverage is measured by a spec harness that reports on each pull request ready for review and never blocks a merge.

The retired in-repository figures are on the [Cypher overview](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/overview/#conformance), and [the Cypher dialect](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/cypher-dialect/) explains why the pin carried deviations.

properties.heading: Default language
properties.text:
Each [namespace](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#namespace) records a default language, which `SHOW DATABASES` reports in the `defaultLanguage` column.

| Setting                                                    | Value                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Recorded default                                           | `CYPHER 25` for `neo4j`, `system` and `system_ontologies`                                                |
| `ALTER DATABASE <namespace> SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 5` | Stores `CYPHER 5` in the store; `SHOW DATABASES` reports it in this process, and after the store reopens |
| Effect on statements                                       | None: a statement without a prefix still runs as Cypher 25. Only the prefix selects Cypher 5             |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store. The default language of each namespace:

```cypher run name=languages
SHOW DATABASES YIELD name, defaultLanguage RETURN name, defaultLanguage
```

```table
| name                | defaultLanguage |
|---------------------|-----------------|
| "neo4j"             | "CYPHER 25"     |
| "system"            | "CYPHER 25"     |
| "system_ontologies" | "CYPHER 25"     |
3 rows
```

String interpolation is a Cypher 25 form:

```cypher run name=prefix-25
CYPHER 25 RETURN s'{1 + 1} hops' AS label
```

```table
| label    |
|----------|
| "2 hops" |
1 row
```

```cypher run name=prefix-5 expect=error
CYPHER 5 RETURN s'{1 + 1} hops' AS label
```

```table
error: syntax error: SyntaxError: UnsupportedLanguageFeature: string interpolation (s'...') is only available in Cypher 25
```

```cypher run name=prefix-4 expect=error
CYPHER 4 RETURN 1 AS one
```

```table
error: syntax error: parse error: SyntaxError: 22N10 invalid pre-parser option value: "4" is not a valid cypher version
  CYPHER 4 RETURN 1 AS one
         ^
```

Setting the default language to Cypher 5 changes what `SHOW DATABASES` reports:

```cypher run name=set-default
ALTER DATABASE neo4j SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 5;
SHOW DATABASES YIELD name, defaultLanguage WHERE name = 'neo4j'
RETURN name, defaultLanguage
```

```table
| name    | defaultLanguage |
|---------|-----------------|
| "neo4j" | "CYPHER 5"      |
1 row
```

A statement without a prefix still runs as Cypher 25:

```cypher run name=default-unchanged
RETURN s'{1 + 1} hops' AS label
```

```table
| label    |
|----------|
| "2 hops" |
1 row
```

A preview feature without its opt-in:

```cypher run name=preview-off expect=error
RETURN datetime('2026-01-01T00:00Z') IS BEFORE datetime('2026-06-01T00:00Z') AS earlier
```

```table
error: semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'chronological-comparisons' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=chronological-comparisons
```

The same statement on the CLI, with the opt-in in the command's environment:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=chronological-comparisons relate --mode table "RETURN datetime('2026-01-01T00:00Z') IS BEFORE datetime('2026-06-01T00:00Z') AS earlier"
```

```text
+---------+
| earlier |
+---------+
| true    |
+---------+
```

A name that is not a preview feature fails the open:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=chronological relate --mode table "RETURN 1 AS one"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: semantic error: SemanticError: invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature 'chronological' (known features: hybrid-search, local-callables, graph-type-opt-props, graph-type-default-values, graph-type-implied-labels, ontology, obfuscated-literals, mixed-label-syntax, float16-coordinate-types, chronological-comparisons, complex-search-patterns, coll-zip, coll-has, gql-stddev-aliases)
```

properties.heading: Preview features
properties.text:
`RELATE_PREVIEW` is an environment variable of the process that opens the store. The [Cypher overview](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/overview/#preview-features) lists each feature, what it enables and the error it gives while off.

| Rule                     | Behavior                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Default                  | No feature enabled                                                                                                                             |
| When it is read          | Once, when the store opens                                                                                                                     |
| Several features         | Comma-separated; spaces around a name are accepted                                                                                             |
| Names                    | Lowercase, exactly as listed: `Chronological-Comparisons` is unknown                                                                           |
| An unknown name          | The open fails with exit code 1 and lists the known names                                                                                      |
| A feature used while off | Usually `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature '<name>' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=<name>`; the overview lists the exceptions |
| The cells on this site   | Run on the WebAssembly build with no preview feature enabled                                                                                   |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [The Cypher dialect](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/cypher-dialect/): why relate targets Cypher 25 and how the layers fit.
- [Cypher overview](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/overview/): the supported Cypher 25 features and every preview feature.
- [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/): the Neo4j habits that fail in relate.
- [Environment variables](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/environment-variables/): `RELATE_PREVIEW` beside the other variables the CLI reads.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
[CYPHER 5 | CYPHER 25] [EXPLAIN | PROFILE] <statement>
ALTER DATABASE <namespace> SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 5 | CYPHER 25
RELATE_PREVIEW=<feature>[,<feature> …]
```

`EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` may also come before the version prefix.

properties.heading: Version prefix
properties.text:
| Prefix           | Statement runs as | Notes                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| None             | Cypher 25         | The default for every statement                                                                                          |
| `CYPHER 25`      | Cypher 25         |                                                                                                                          |
| `CYPHER 5`       | Cypher 5          | Some Cypher 25 forms fail, as the next table shows                                                                       |
| Any other number | —                 | `syntax error: parse error: SyntaxError: 22N10 invalid pre-parser option value: "<n>" is not a valid cypher version`     |
| Two prefixes     | —                 | `syntax error: parse error: SyntaxError: 22N09 conflicting pre-parser combination: multiple values for 'cypher version'` |

Under `CYPHER 5`, these Cypher 25 forms fail:

| Form                         | Message                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| String interpolation, `s'…'` | `syntax error: SyntaxError: UnsupportedLanguageFeature: string interpolation (s'...') is only available in Cypher 25` |
| `vector(…)`                  | `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function 'vector'`                                                            |

Other Cypher 25 forms, such as `LET` and the `||` operator, run under both prefixes.

properties.heading: Differences from Neo4j
properties.text: relate speaks Neo4j's [Cypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#cypher), including much of Cypher 25, inside your process. It runs embedded, with no procedure libraries such as APOC and no user accounts, and serves a network surface only when `relate serve` starts one, so a statement or a connection string written from Neo4j habits can fail in relate. The table lists those habits with the error relate returns, character for character, and the form that works. Everything not in the table behaves as the [Cypher overview](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/overview/) describes.

properties.heading: Differences
properties.text:
| Feature                                 | Neo4j                                                                                        | relate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Write instead                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| APOC functions                          | The APOC library adds `apoc.*` functions                                                     | No APOC. `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function apoc.text.join()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | A built-in function, such as `string.join(list, ', ')`; `SHOW FUNCTIONS` lists them all                                                                                                   |
| APOC procedures                         | The APOC library adds `apoc.*` procedures                                                    | `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: apoc.meta.schema`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties()`, `CALL db.schema.relTypeProperties()` or `CALL db.schema.visualization()` for the schema; `SHOW PROCEDURES` lists the rest                          |
| Graph Data Science procedures           | The GDS library adds `gds.*` procedures                                                      | `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: gds.pageRank.stream`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Cypher patterns and aggregation, or an algorithm in your own code over a query result                                                                                                     |
| Index procedures                        | Neo4j 5 releases created vector indexes with the procedure `db.index.vector.createNodeIndex` | `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: db.index.vector.createNodeIndex`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | `CREATE VECTOR INDEX <name> FOR (n:<Label>) ON (n.<property>) OPTIONS {indexConfig: {…}}`, or `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX`                                                                     |
| `db.index.vector.queryNodes`            | A procedure for top-k vector queries                                                         | Runs, and is deprecated: `EXPLAIN` reports ``The procedure `db.index.vector.queryNodes` is deprecated.`` with the remedy ``Use the `SEARCH` clause instead.`` The three other search procedures report the same                                                                                                                | `MATCH (n:<Label>) SEARCH n IN (VECTOR INDEX <name> FOR $vector LIMIT <k>) SCORE AS score`                                                                                                |
| The `SEARCH` score                      | The `SEARCH` clause                                                                          | `LIMIT` is required, and the score exists only through `SCORE AS`: `syntax error: UndefinedVariable: variable 'score' not defined`                                                                                                                                                                                             | `SEARCH n IN (… LIMIT <k>) SCORE AS score`; the [search reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#rules-of-the-search-clause) has every rule                           |
| Cosine similarity range                 | `vector.similarity.cosine` returns 0 to 1                                                    | The same range: `1.0` same direction, `0.5` orthogonal, `0.0` opposite. A threshold taken from a raw cosine (−1 to 1) is on another scale                                                                                                                                                                                      | Convert a raw-cosine threshold `t` to `(1 + t) / 2`; `vector_distance(a, b, COSINE)` returns the raw cosine distance                                                                      |
| Drivers and `bolt://`                   | A server; drivers connect to `bolt://` or `neo4j://`                                         | Embedded: no server unless one is started. `Failed to open Relate: storage error: unsupported URI scheme bolt:// (engine URIs are :memory:, a filesystem path, or file://)` (exit code 1); the Python client raises `OperationalError` with the message that follows `Failed to open Relate: `                                 | Open the store in your process with a client, `relate.connect("./graph.rl")`, or serve it to a Neo4j driver with `relate serve --bolt <port> --database ./graph.rl --read-only`           |
| Several databases                       | `CREATE DATABASE`, then `USE <name>`                                                         | Three fixed [namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#namespace): `neo4j`, `system`, `system_ontologies`. `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: movies`; `semantic error: UnsupportedAdministrationCommand: Unsupported administration command: CREATE DATABASE movies`                          | One store per graph: `--database ./movies.rl`; [Namespaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/namespaces/) explains the three names                                                       |
| Users, roles, and privileges            | `CREATE USER`, roles, `GRANT`                                                                | No user management. `CREATE USER bob SET PASSWORD 'secret'` fails with `syntax error: parse error: expected a pattern`                                                                                                                                                                                                         | File permissions on the store, `--read-only`, and `relate serve --auth <user>:<password>` on a served store                                                                               |
| Many writers on one database            | The server takes writes from many clients                                                    | One writing process per store. A second opener fails with `Failed to open Relate: storage locked: <path>` (exit code 5)                                                                                                                                                                                                        | One process owns the store. Beside that writer, a directory store opens with `--read-only`; a `.rl` file opens read-only only after the writer exits. Otherwise go through `relate serve` |
| `DROP INDEX`, `DROP CONSTRAINT`         | The result summary counts what was removed                                                   | The CLI prints nothing on success. A missing name fails: ``semantic error: NoSuchIndex: `<name>` ``, `semantic error: ConstraintNotFound`                                                                                                                                                                                      | `SHOW INDEXES` or `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` before and after; `IF EXISTS` for a drop that may find nothing                                                                                       |
| `LOAD CSV` sources                      | Files from the server's import directory, and `http` and `https` URLs                        | Local files under the `--load-csv-dir` directory only, denied by default. Anything else: `LOAD CSV file unavailable` (exit code 1)                                                                                                                                                                                             | Download the file first, then `--load-csv-dir <dir>`; see [import a CSV](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/import-csv/)                                                              |
| Long explicit path bounds               | No fixed ceiling on `*1..N`                                                                  | More than 500 hops: `syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: This query allows paths up to <n> hops. This is a safety limit protecting against excessive traversal (not a database limit) — lower the path bound, or raise it with --max-traversal-depth (up to 2000).`, where `<n>` is the statement's own bound, not the limit | A lower bound, or `--max-traversal-depth <n>` up to 2000                                                                                                                                  |
| Browser and shell commands              | `:param`, `:use` and other colon commands in Neo4j Browser and `cypher-shell`                | Not Cypher: `syntax error: parse error: unexpected token ":"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `--param <name>=<value>` on the CLI, a parameters map in a client                                                                                                                         |
| `id()`                                  | Deprecated                                                                                   | Runs, and is deprecated: `EXPLAIN` reports ``The function `id()` is deprecated.`` with the remedy ``Use `elementId` instead.``                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `elementId(n)`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `CALL { … } IN CONCURRENT TRANSACTIONS` | Batches run in parallel                                                                      | Accepted; the batches run one after another in the embedded engine                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | No change needed                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Default Cypher version                  | Set by the server's version and configuration                                                | `CYPHER 25` for every namespace, as `SHOW DATABASES` reports in `defaultLanguage`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | A `CYPHER 5` prefix on a statement that needs Cypher 5 behavior                                                                                                                           |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The examples run in page order on one in-memory [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) with the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

An APOC function fails, and the built-in returns the same string:

```cypher run name=apoc-function expect=error
MATCH (p:Person) RETURN apoc.text.join(collect(p.name), ', ') AS names
```

```table
error: syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function apoc.text.join()
```

```cypher run name=string-join
MATCH (p:Person) WITH p ORDER BY p.name RETURN string.join(collect(p.name), ', ') AS names
```

```table
| names              |
|--------------------|
| "Ada, Grace, Noor" |
1 row
```

An APOC schema procedure fails; the `db.schema` procedures describe the same graph:

```cypher run name=apoc-procedure expect=error
CALL apoc.meta.schema() YIELD value RETURN value
```

```table
error: syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: apoc.meta.schema
```

```cypher run name=schema
CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties() YIELD nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes
RETURN nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes
ORDER BY nodeType, propertyName
```

```table
| nodeType   | propertyName | propertyTypes       |
|------------|--------------|---------------------|
| ":Person"  | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
| ":Person"  | "role"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
| ":Project" | "language"   | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
| ":Project" | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] |
4 rows
```

An index procedure fails; `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` is the statement:

```cypher run name=index-procedure expect=error
CALL db.index.vector.createNodeIndex('person_focus', 'Person', 'focus', 3, 'cosine')
```

```table
error: syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: db.index.vector.createNodeIndex
```

A database name other than the three namespaces fails, and so does creating one:

```cypher run name=use-database expect=error
USE movies MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS n
```

```table
error: semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: movies
```

```cypher run name=create-database expect=error
CREATE DATABASE movies
```

```table
error: semantic error: UnsupportedAdministrationCommand: Unsupported administration command: CREATE DATABASE movies
```

```cypher run name=namespaces
SHOW DATABASES YIELD name, defaultLanguage RETURN name, defaultLanguage
```

```table
| name                | defaultLanguage |
|---------------------|-----------------|
| "neo4j"             | "CYPHER 25"     |
| "system"            | "CYPHER 25"     |
| "system_ontologies" | "CYPHER 25"     |
3 rows
```

A path bound beyond the default limit of 500 hops fails before the statement runs:

```cypher run name=path-bound expect=error
MATCH (a:Person)-[:KNOWS*1..1000]->(b:Person) RETURN count(*) AS n
```

```table
error: syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: This query allows paths up to 1,000 hops. This is a safety limit protecting against excessive traversal (not a database limit) — lower the path bound, or raise it with --max-traversal-depth (up to 2000).
```

The cosine scale, and the raw cosine distance next to it:

```cypher run name=cosine
RETURN vector.similarity.cosine([1, 0], [0, 1]) AS orthogonal,
       vector.similarity.cosine([1, 0], [-1, 0]) AS opposite,
       vector_distance(vector([1, 0], 2, FLOAT32), vector([0, 1], 2, FLOAT32), COSINE) AS rawDistance
```

```table
| orthogonal | opposite | rawDistance |
|------------|----------|-------------|
| 0.5        | 0.0      | 1.0         |
1 row
```

A `bolt://` address is not a store, on the CLI:

```bash verify
relate --database bolt://localhost:7687 --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
```

The first line is stderr, the second the error object on stdout:

```text
Failed to open Relate: storage error: unsupported URI scheme bolt:// (engine URIs are :memory:, a filesystem path, or file://)
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"storage","message":"storage error: unsupported URI scheme bolt:// (engine URIs are :memory:, a filesystem path, or file://)","retryable":false}}
```

`LOAD CSV` does not fetch a URL, even with a directory allowed:

```bash verify
mkdir import
relate --load-csv-dir ./import --mode envelope "LOAD CSV FROM 'https://example.com/people.csv' AS row RETURN row"
```

```text
LOAD CSV file unavailable
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"execution","message":"LOAD CSV file unavailable","retryable":false}}
```

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
Each row is one habit. The relate column quotes the message relate returns: the CLI prints it on stderr and, under `--mode json`, `jsonl` or `envelope`, in the error object's `message` on stdout; a client raises it. The [examples](#examples) run each one.

The Neo4j column gives the habit's origin in Neo4j as of 2026-11-07, for current releases under Cypher 25 unless a row names a release. It summarizes Neo4j's behavior and was not checked against a Neo4j server; the relate and Write instead columns were checked against relate.

properties.heading: EXPLAIN and PROFILE
properties.text: `EXPLAIN <statement>` returns the [plan](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#plan) relate would run, without running it. `PROFILE <statement>` runs the statement, returns its rows, and returns the same plan with what each operator did. Both also return the planner's [notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#notification). [Tune a query](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/tune-a-query/) walks through reading a plan and acting on it; this page lists what a plan holds.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run on the shared example graph. An `EXPLAIN` cell's result shows no rows; its JSON view holds the plan and the notifications. The two plans below raise no notification:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

```cypher run name=explain-aggregation
EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
WITH proj, count(p) AS people WHERE people > 1
RETURN proj.name AS project, people ORDER BY people DESC LIMIT 5
```

```table
(no rows)
```

The recorded JSON view holds a `relate.plan/v1` tree: `ProduceResults` (`2 item(s), ordered, limit`) over `EagerAggregation` (`2 item(s), keys: proj, aggregation, WHERE filter`) over `Expand` (`(proj:Project)<-[:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person)`). The plan viewer reads the same document. In a browser it draws the tree; **PROFILE** runs the statement on this page's database and adds each operator's rows, time and database hits as bars (the table's `Rows`, `Time (ms)` and `Db Hits` columns), with a download of the profile in the `--mode speedscope` format; **Plan as text** shows the table `--mode table` prints.

The plan recorded for cell `explain-aggregation`, as `relate --mode table` prints it:

```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) WITH proj, count(p) AS people WHERE people > 1 RETURN proj.name AS project, people ORDER BY people DESC LIMIT 5
Plan:
+----------------------+----+--------------------------------------------------+
| Operator             | Id | Details                                          |
+----------------------+----+--------------------------------------------------+
| + ProduceResults     | 0  | 2 item(s), ordered, limit                        |
+----------------------+----+--------------------------------------------------+
| | + EagerAggregation | 1  | 2 item(s), keys: proj, aggregation, WHERE filter |
+----------------------+----+--------------------------------------------------+
| | | + Expand         | 2  | (proj:Project)<-[:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person)           |
+----------------------+----+--------------------------------------------------+
```

Notifications: none.

Live: the plan is drawn as a tree, and PROFILE runs the statement on the page's database in your browser and adds each operator's rows, time and database hits as bars; the index button creates the index on the page's database, plans the statement with and without it side by side with the changes, and drops it again; a PROFILE downloads as a speedscope file.

```cypher run name=explain-optional
EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person) OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[:KNOWS]->(f) RETURN p.name AS name, f.name AS friend
```

```table
(no rows)
```

The recorded JSON view holds `ProduceResults` over `Optional(Expand)` (`(p)-[:KNOWS]->(f), optional`, an estimate of 1 row) over `NodeByLabelScan` (`(p:Person)`, an estimate of 3 rows).

The same plans on the CLI. This setup step writes the shared example graph to a new [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store), `team.rl`, and adds a range [index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#index) on `Person.name`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
CREATE INDEX person_name FOR (p:Person) ON (p.name)"
```

An aggregation in table mode, read-only:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode table "EXPLAIN MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) WITH proj, count(p) AS people WHERE people > 1 RETURN proj.name AS project, people ORDER BY people DESC LIMIT 5"
```

```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project) WITH proj, count(p) AS people WHERE people > 1 RETURN proj.name AS project, people ORDER BY people DESC LIMIT 5
```

A range seek on the index:


```text
Query: MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name >= 'G' RETURN p.name AS name
```
