properties.heading: Index use in a plan
properties.text:
| Index use                        | How the plan shows it                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A range index serves an equality | `NodeIndexSeek` with `RANGE INDEX <var>:<Label>(<property>) WHERE <property> = <value>`                                  |
| A range index serves a range     | `NodeIndexSeekByRange` with the comparison                                                                               |
| No index serves a filter         | `NodeByLabelScan` or `Expand`, and under `EXPLAIN` notification `03C91` with the `CREATE INDEX` statement that would     |
| A vector or full-text `SEARCH`   | The `MATCH` operator's `Details` end in `SEARCH`; the index's top results feed it, and the estimate is the label's count |
| A `db.index.*` procedure         | `ProcedureCall` with the procedure's name, and notification `01N01`, because the procedures are deprecated               |

properties.heading: Operators
properties.text:
| Operator                                  | Plans                                                                                                                                                                 | `Details`                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AllNodesScan`                            | A node pattern with no label                                                                                                                                          | The pattern, `(n)`                                                                             |
| `NodeByLabelScan`                         | A node pattern with labels                                                                                                                                            | The pattern, `(p:Person)`                                                                      |
| `NodeIndexSeek`                           | An equality on a range-indexed label and property                                                                                                                     | `RANGE INDEX p:Person(name) WHERE name = 'Ada'`, then the rest of the pattern                  |
| `NodeIndexSeekByRange`                    | A `<`, `<=`, `>` or `>=` comparison on a range-indexed label and property                                                                                             | `RANGE INDEX p:Person(name) WHERE name >= 'G'`                                                 |
| `NodeByLabelSeek`                         | A label disjunction whose labels each have a range index on the filtered property, such as `(p:Model OR p:Source) AND p.id = 1`, served as one keyed lookup per label | `RANGE INDEX p:Model(id), p:Source(id)`, one target per label; no `WHERE`, no count of its own |
| `Expand`                                  | A `MATCH` pattern with relationships, or several patterns                                                                                                             | The patterns as written, from the chosen start                                                 |
| `Optional(<operator>)`                    | An `OPTIONAL MATCH`                                                                                                                                                   | The pattern, then `optional`                                                                   |
| `Create`                                  | `CREATE`                                                                                                                                                              | The created patterns                                                                           |
| `Merge`                                   | `MERGE`                                                                                                                                                               | The pattern, then `ON CREATE SET` or `ON MATCH SET` when present                               |
| `Delete`, `DetachDelete`                  | `DELETE`, `DETACH DELETE`                                                                                                                                             | `<n> expression(s)`                                                                            |
| `SetProperty`                             | `SET`                                                                                                                                                                 | `<n> item(s)`                                                                                  |
| `RemoveProperty`                          | `REMOVE`                                                                                                                                                              | `<n> item(s)`                                                                                  |
| `Projection`                              | `WITH`                                                                                                                                                                | `<n> item(s)` and its flags                                                                    |
| `Let`                                     | `LET`                                                                                                                                                                 | `<n> item(s)`                                                                                  |
| `Filter`                                  | `FILTER`                                                                                                                                                              | `<n> item(s)` and its flags                                                                    |
| `EagerAggregation`                        | A `WITH` or `RETURN` with an aggregate or `GROUP BY`                                                                                                                  | `<n> item(s)`, `keys: <grouping keys>`, `aggregation` and the flags                            |
| `Unwind`                                  | `UNWIND`                                                                                                                                                              | `AS <variable>`                                                                                |
| `ProduceResults`                          | `RETURN`, or `FINISH`                                                                                                                                                 | `<n> item(s)` and its flags, or `FINISH`                                                       |
| `ProcedureCall`                           | `CALL <procedure>`                                                                                                                                                    | `<procedure>()`                                                                                |
| `CallSubquery`                            | `CALL { … }`, `CALL (…) { … }`                                                                                                                                        | `optional`, `IN TRANSACTIONS` when present                                                     |
| `Conditional`                             | `WHEN … THEN … ELSE`                                                                                                                                                  | `<n> branch(es)`, `ELSE` when present                                                          |
| `Foreach`                                 | `FOREACH`                                                                                                                                                             | The loop variable                                                                              |
| `LoadCSV`                                 | `LOAD CSV`                                                                                                                                                            | `WITH HEADERS AS <variable>` or `AS <variable>`                                                |
| `CreateIndex`, `DropIndex`, `ShowIndexes` | Range index statements                                                                                                                                                | The index name and schema, for `CreateIndex`                                                   |
| `Catalog`                                 | Other schema and catalog statements                                                                                                                                   | The statement's keyword                                                                        |
| `Use`                                     | `USE`                                                                                                                                                                 | —                                                                                              |
| `Union`, `UnionAll`                       | `UNION`, `UNION ALL`                                                                                                                                                  | `<n> parts`                                                                                    |
| `Next`                                    | `NEXT`                                                                                                                                                                | `stage <n>`, the number of the stage it introduces                                             |

The flags a projection's `Details` can carry are `distinct`, `WHERE filter`, `ordered` (an `ORDER BY`), `skip` and `limit`. A `MATCH` operator adds `optional`, `SEARCH` and `WHERE filter`.

properties.heading: Plan warnings
properties.text:
Four notifications also appear in the plan table's `Warnings` column and in a `Warnings:` line under the table, instead of in the `Notifications:` block:

| Warning                | GQLSTATUS | Fires on                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CartesianProduct`     | `03N90`   | Patterns in one `MATCH` that share no variable                                            |
| `AllNodesScan`         | `03C90`   | A node pattern with no label while the store has a property index                         |
| `EstimationMiss`       | `03C93`   | `PROFILE` only: an estimate 10 times the actual rows or more                              |
| `LabelDisjunctionScan` | `03C94`   | An equality on a property of a label disjunction that no range index on each label serves |

[Notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/notifications/) lists every notification with its text and the statements it fires on.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Tune a query](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/tune-a-query/): reading a plan, acting on a notification, and confirming the fix.
- [Notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/notifications/): every notification code, its text, and its remedy.
- [Search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/): the vector and full-text indexes behind a `SEARCH`.
- [Output modes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/output-modes/): each CLI mode's layout.
- [Text-to-Cypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/#text-to-cypher): `EXPLAIN` as the check before a generated statement runs.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
[CYPHER 5 | CYPHER 25] EXPLAIN <statement>
[CYPHER 5 | CYPHER 25] PROFILE <statement>
```

|                      | `EXPLAIN`                                                   | `PROFILE`                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Runs the statement   | No: writes, procedure calls and `LOAD CSV` are only planned | Yes, writes included                                |
| Returns rows         | None, and no columns                                        | The statement's own columns and rows                |
| Plan                 | Operators, details, and row estimates                       | The same, plus the measured columns                 |
| Notifications        | Yes                                                         | Yes, plus `03C93` for an estimate 10 times too high |
| On a read-only store | Any statement, writes included                              | Reads only; a write fails as any write does         |

On the CLI, the clients and the WASM build, a statement without either prefix builds no plan and derives no notifications. The [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/) `read_cypher` and `write_cypher` tools differ: they plan every statement as `EXPLAIN <statement>` before running it, so each call returns a plan and its plan-time notifications, and a statement that already starts with `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` fails with `syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "EXPLAIN"` (or `"PROFILE"`).

properties.heading: The plan in each output mode
properties.text:
| Surface or mode                   | The plan                                                                                                                                    | Notifications                                                                       |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| CLI `--mode table`                | The plan table, on stderr; `PROFILE` prints its rows on stdout first                                                                        | A `Notifications:` block under the plan, on stderr, without the three plan warnings |
| CLI `--mode json`                 | `{"notifications": […], "plan": {…}}`; `PROFILE` adds `"data": [rows]`                                                                      | In the object, every kind                                                           |
| CLI `--mode jsonl`                | `PROFILE` prints one line per row, then the plan object on its own line                                                                     | In the plan line                                                                    |
| CLI `--mode envelope`             | The [envelope](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#envelope)'s `plan` key, beside `columns`, `columnTypes`, `rows` and `truncated` | The envelope's `notifications`                                                      |
| CLI `--mode toon`                 | A `plan:` entry, then a `notifications:` entry, as compact JSON                                                                             | In the `notifications:` entry                                                       |
| CLI `--mode markdown`             | None                                                                                                                                        | A `Notifications:` block after the rows, every kind                                 |
| CLI `--mode csv`, `--mode cypher` | None                                                                                                                                        | None                                                                                |
| CLI `--mode speedscope`           | `PROFILE` only: a speedscope evented profile, one frame per operator, times in nanoseconds                                                  | None                                                                                |
| Clients, the WASM build           | A `relate.plan/v1` document                                                                                                                 | The result's notification list                                                      |
| MCP `read_cypher`, `write_cypher` | A `relate.plan/v1` document on every call, without measured columns                                                                         | The plan-time notifications of every statement, without `03C93`                     |

The CLI's machine modes carry the plan as a structured-plan tree: each node is `{operatorType, args, identifiers, children}`. `args` holds `Details`, `Id` and `EstimatedRows`. On the root it also holds `string-representation` (the plan table as text), `version` and the `planner*` and `runtime*` fields, which name relate. A `PROFILE` adds `Rows`, `TimeNs`, `DbHits`, `MemoryBytes`, `ExpressionBuiltBytes`, `Hops`, `NeighborWalks`, `NodeReads`, `SeekTimeNs` and `WalkTimeNs`, and `StartElement`, `StartBackward` and `StartReason` on a walk.

The `relate.plan/v1` document that the clients return is `{schema, profiled, statement, root}`. Each node is `{operator, details, identifiers, estimated_rows, actual, children, warnings}`; `actual` is `null` under `EXPLAIN` and holds `rows`, `time_ms`, `total_time_ms`, `db_hits` and the other measures under `PROFILE`. A cell's JSON view on this site shows that document.

`--mode speedscope` on a statement without `PROFILE` fails with exit code 1:

```bash verify
relate --mode speedscope "EXPLAIN RETURN 1 AS one"
```

```text
speedscope mode requires a PROFILE statement: per-operator times are what it exports (the plan tree carries no PROFILE metrics)
```

properties.heading: The plan tree
properties.text:
A plan is a tree of operators, one per clause. The root is the clause that produces the result: `ProduceResults` for a `RETURN`, `EagerAggregation` for a `RETURN` that aggregates, or the last write clause. Each operator's input is the clause before it, nested beneath it, so a plan reads from the bottom up. `Union` and `UnionAll` hold one child per part. Each `NEXT` adds a `Next` operator under the previous stage's root, holding that stage's pipeline as its one child.

| Column           | Holds                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Operator`       | The operator name; `\| +` nests it under the operator that reads its rows                                                                     |
| `Id`             | The operator's number, in pre-order from the root at `0`; notifications name it as `operator_id`                                              |
| `Details`        | What the operator works on: a pattern, an index seek, or the item count and flags of a projection                                             |
| `Estimated Rows` | The rows the planner expects, from label and relationship type counts; `-` where it has no estimate. Shown when some operator has an estimate |
| `Warnings`       | The operator's plan warning, `-` for none. Shown when some operator has one                                                                   |

properties.heading: What PROFILE measures
properties.text:
`PROFILE` adds these columns to the plan table. Times differ on every run.

| Column                     | Holds                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Rows`                     | The rows the operator produced                                                                                                                |
| `Time (ms)`                | The operator's own time                                                                                                                       |
| `Total (ms)`               | The operator's time plus all of its descendants'                                                                                              |
| `Db Hits`                  | Store accesses: relationships followed, adjacency entries read, and node records read                                                         |
| `Nodes`                    | Node records read; shown when some operator read one, and blank for zero                                                                      |
| `Rels`                     | Relationships followed to their other end; shown and blank by the same rule                                                                   |
| `Degree`                   | Adjacency entries read, one per neighbor a walk visited; same rule                                                                            |
| `Memory (Bytes)`           | The size of the rows the operator produced                                                                                                    |
| `Expression Built (Bytes)` | The size of the values the operator built (`range`, `collect`, comprehensions, concatenation); a running total, not a peak                    |
| `Est/Actual`               | Estimated over actual rows, as `25.0x`; `!` after it when the estimate is 10 times too high or more. Shown when some operator has an estimate |
| `Executed`                 | `✓` or `x`; shown when some operator never ran because its input produced no rows, whose metric cells then read `(never executed)`            |

A walking operator's `Details` also names how it started, as `[start #<k>, forward | backward, <reason>]`, where the reason is `bound-pivot`, `cheapest`, `seek-anchored` or `index-0`.

properties.heading: Expressions
properties.text: An expression computes one value from literals, variables, [properties](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property), [parameters](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter), operators, and function calls. relate evaluates expressions in `RETURN`, `WITH`, `WHERE`, `SET`, `ORDER BY` and anywhere else a clause takes a value. The cells on this page run on relate's WebAssembly (WASM) build; the CLI and the clients evaluate expressions with the same engine.

properties.heading: Arithmetic
properties.text:
| Operator      | Operands                      | Result                                                                                                     | Edge cases                                             |
| ------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `+`, `-`, `*` | Two integers                  | `INTEGER`                                                                                                  | Overflow fails with `type error: integer out of range` |
| `+`, `-`, `*` | A float and a number          | `FLOAT`                                                                                                    | IEEE 754 64-bit arithmetic                             |
| `/`           | Two integers                  | `INTEGER`, truncated toward zero: `-7 / 2` is `-3`                                                         | `1 / 0` fails with `type error: / by zero`             |
| `/`           | A float and a number          | `FLOAT`                                                                                                    | `1 / 0.0` is `Infinity`                                |
| `%`           | Two integers                  | `INTEGER`; the sign follows the dividend: `-7 % 3` is `-1`                                                 | `1 % 0` fails with `type error: % by zero`             |
| `%`           | A float and a number          | `FLOAT`: `7.5 % 2` is `1.5`                                                                                | —                                                      |
| `^`           | Two numbers                   | Always `FLOAT`: `2 ^ 3` is `8.0`                                                                           | `2 ^ -1` is `0.5`                                      |
| `-`           | One number                    | The negation                                                                                               | —                                                      |
| `+`, `-`      | Temporal values and durations | See [temporal arithmetic](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/types-and-values/#temporal-arithmetic) | —                                                      |

```cypher run name=arithmetic
RETURN 7 / 2 AS int_div, -7 / 2 AS truncates, -7 % 3 AS remainder,
       7.0 / 2 AS float_div, 2 ^ 3 AS power, 0.1 + 0.2 AS ieee
```

```table
| int_div | truncates | remainder | float_div | power | ieee                |
|---------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-------|---------------------|
| 3       | -3        | -1        | 3.5       | 8.0   | 0.30000000000000004 |
1 row
```

```cypher run name=divide-by-zero expect=error
RETURN 1 / 0 AS boom
```

```table
error: type error: / by zero
```

properties.heading: CASE
properties.text:
| Form                   | Syntax                                                          | Result                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Simple                 | `CASE <expr> WHEN <value> THEN <result> … [ELSE <default>] END` | The first `THEN` whose value equals `<expr>` |
| Simple, several values | `CASE <expr> WHEN <v1>, <v2> THEN <result> … END`               | The first `THEN` with any matching value     |
| Simple, comparison     | `CASE <expr> WHEN > <value> THEN <result> … END`                | The first `THEN` whose comparison holds      |
| Generic                | `CASE WHEN <predicate> THEN <result> … [ELSE <default>] END`    | The first `THEN` whose predicate is `true`   |

Without `ELSE`, a `CASE` that matches nothing gives `null`.

```cypher run name=case
RETURN CASE 2 WHEN 1 THEN 'one' WHEN 2 THEN 'two' ELSE 'many' END AS simple,
       CASE 2 WHEN 1, 2 THEN 'small' ELSE 'big' END AS several,
       CASE 5 WHEN > 3 THEN 'above three' ELSE 'three or less' END AS comparison,
       CASE WHEN 1 > 2 THEN 'never' END AS no_else
```

```table
| simple | several | comparison    | no_else |
|--------|---------|---------------|---------|
| "two"  | "small" | "above three" | null    |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Comparison and equality
properties.text:
| Operator             | Meaning                  | Rules                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `=`                  | Equal                    | An integer equals a float of the same value (`1 = 1.0` is `true`). Values of different types are not equal (`'1' = 1` is `false`). Lists are equal element by element, maps key by key. `NaN = NaN` is `false`                                                                                                        |
| `<>`                 | Not equal                | The negation of `=`, with the same `null` rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` | Order                    | Numbers by value, strings by code point (`'B' < 'a'` is `true`), booleans with `false < true`, lists element by element (`[1, 2] < [1, 2, 0]` is `true`), temporal values of the same type by instant. Values that have no order between them give `null`: `1 < 'a'`, a `DATE` against a `ZONED DATETIME`, two points |
| `=~`                 | Regular expression match | The whole string must match: `'Ada' =~ 'A'` is `false`. `(?i)` at the start ignores case                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

Any comparison with a `null` operand gives `null`, and so does an equality between two lists or maps that are equal except where one holds `null` (`[1, null] = [1, null]` is `null`). `IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL` are the tests that never give `null`.

```cypher run name=comparison
RETURN 1 = 1.0 AS int_float, '1' = 1 AS cross_type, 1 < 'a' AS unordered,
       'B' < 'a' AS code_point, [1, 2] < [1, 2, 0] AS lists,
       NaN = NaN AS nan, [1, null] = [1, null] AS null_inside, 'Ada' =~ '(?i)ada' AS regex
```

```table
| int_float | cross_type | unordered | code_point | lists | nan   | null_inside | regex |
|-----------|------------|-----------|------------|-------|-------|-------------|-------|
| true      | false      | null      | true       | true  | false | null        | true  |
1 row
```

properties.heading: List and pattern comprehensions
properties.text:
A list comprehension builds a list from another list; a pattern comprehension builds one from the matches of a pattern, once per row.

| Form                                            | Result                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `[x IN list WHERE <predicate>]`                 | The elements for which the predicate is `true`                                                         |
| `[x IN list \| <expression>]`                   | The expression for every element                                                                       |
| `[x IN list WHERE <predicate> \| <expression>]` | Both                                                                                                   |
| `[<pattern> WHERE <predicate> \| <expression>]` | The expression for every match of the pattern, which usually starts from a variable of the current row |

The pattern cells on this page run on the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

```cypher run name=comprehensions
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Grace'})
RETURN [x IN range(1, 10) WHERE x % 2 = 0 | x * x] AS even_squares,
       [(p)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj) WHERE w.since >= 2023 | proj.name] AS recent_projects
```

```table
| even_squares         | recent_projects |
|----------------------|-----------------|
| [4, 16, 36, 64, 100] | ["relate"]      |
1 row
```

properties.heading: List operators
properties.text:
| Operator         | Result             | Notes                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `a + b`          | Concatenation      | A non-list on the right is appended: `[1] + 2` is `[1, 2]`                                                                                                                       |
| `a \|\| b`       | Concatenation      | Both sides must be lists                                                                                                                                                         |
| `x IN list`      | `BOOLEAN`          | Element equality, with the `null` rule of the [null table](#null-and-three-valued-logic); a list can be an element: `[1] IN [[1]]` is `true`                                     |
| `list[i]`        | The element at `i` | Zero-based; a negative index counts from the end (`[1, 2, 3][-1]` is `3`); past the end is `null`. A float index fails with `InvalidArgumentType: list index must be an integer` |
| `list[from..to]` | A sublist          | `from` is included and `to` is not; either bound may be left out or negative; bounds outside the list are clamped                                                                |

A subscript on a string fails with `type error: InvalidArgumentType: subscript requires a list or map`; `substring()` and `left()` take characters from a string.

```cypher run name=lists
RETURN [1, 2] + [3] AS plus, [1] + 2 AS append, [1, 2, 3][0] AS first,
       [1, 2, 3][-1] AS last, [1, 2, 3, 4][1..3] AS slice, [1, 2, 3][5] AS past_end,
       [1] IN [[1]] AS nested
```

```table
| plus      | append | first | last | slice  | past_end | nested |
|-----------|--------|-------|------|--------|----------|--------|
| [1, 2, 3] | [1, 2] | 1     | 3    | [2, 3] | null     | true   |
1 row
```

properties.heading: List predicates
properties.text:
| Predicate                   | `true` when                            | On an empty list |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `all(x IN list WHERE p)`    | `p` is `true` for every element        | `true`           |
| `any(x IN list WHERE p)`    | `p` is `true` for at least one element | `false`          |
| `none(x IN list WHERE p)`   | `p` is `true` for no element           | `true`           |
| `single(x IN list WHERE p)` | `p` is `true` for exactly one element  | `false`          |

When no element decides the answer and `p` gives `null` for some element, the predicate gives `null`: `any(x IN [null] WHERE x > 1)` is `null`.

```cypher run name=predicates
RETURN all(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x > 0) AS all_positive, any(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x > 1) AS any_big,
       none(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x > 5) AS none_huge, single(x IN [1, 2] WHERE x > 1) AS one_big,
       all(x IN [] WHERE false) AS empty_all, any(x IN [null] WHERE x > 1) AS unknown
```

```table
| all_positive | any_big | none_huge | one_big | empty_all | unknown |
|--------------|---------|-----------|---------|-----------|---------|
| true         | true    | true      | true    | true      | null    |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Map and property access
properties.text:
| Form                            | Result                         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `m.key`, `n.key`                | The value under `key`          | `null` when the key is absent                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `m['key']`, `n[$key]`, `n[k]`   | The value under a computed key | A dynamic key on a [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node) or relationship never uses an index; on an indexed label `EXPLAIN` reports notification `03N95` ([notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/notifications/)) |
| `a + b` on two maps             | A merged map                   | A key in `b` replaces the same key in `a`: `{a: 1} + {a: 2, b: 3}` is `{a: 2, b: 3}`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `{i IN list \| <key>: <value>}` | A map comprehension            | One entry per element; a key that is not a string fails with `type error: map comprehension key expression must be a STRING`                                                                                                                             |

properties.heading: Map projections
properties.text:
A map projection builds a map from a node, a relationship, or a map variable.

| Item                | Adds                                                     |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.key`              | The property `key`, or `null` when it is not set         |
| `.*`                | Every property                                           |
| `key: <expression>` | A computed entry, which may hold a pattern comprehension |
| `var`               | The value of the variable `var`, under its own name      |

```cypher run name=projection
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p {.name, .role, projects: [(p)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj) | proj.name]} AS person
ORDER BY person.name
```

```table
| person                                                                    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| {name: "Ada", projects: ["relate"], role: "engineer"}                     |
| {name: "Grace", projects: ["opencypher-tck", "relate"], role: "engineer"} |
| {name: "Noor", projects: [], role: "maintainer"}                          |
3 rows
```

properties.heading: Null and three-valued logic
properties.text:
`null` stands for a missing or unknown value. An operator or function that gets `null` returns `null` unless its row says otherwise; `AND`, `OR` and `XOR` follow three-valued logic:

| `a`     | `b`    | `a AND b` | `a OR b` | `a XOR b` | `NOT a` |
| ------- | ------ | --------- | -------- | --------- | ------- |
| `true`  | `null` | `null`    | `true`   | `null`    | `false` |
| `false` | `null` | `false`   | `null`   | `null`    | `true`  |
| `null`  | `null` | `null`    | `null`   | `null`    | `null`  |

| Expression          | Result            | Rule                                                 |
| ------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `null = null`       | `null`            | Equality with `null` is unknown                      |
| `x IS NULL`         | `true` or `false` | The test for a missing value                         |
| `1 + null`          | `null`            | Arithmetic propagates `null`                         |
| `2 IN [1, null]`    | `null`            | Not found, but the `null` element might have matched |
| `1 IN [1, null]`    | `true`            | Found before the `null` matters                      |
| `null IN [1]`       | `null`            | Membership of an unknown value                       |
| `n.missing`         | `null`            | A property that is not set reads as `null`           |
| `[1, 2][5]`         | `null`            | An index past the end                                |
| `coalesce(null, 1)` | `1`               | The first argument that is not `null`                |

A `WHERE` keeps a row only when its predicate is `true`; `false` and `null` both drop it. A property set to `null` is removed, so `keys(n)` does not list it.

```cypher run name=nulls
RETURN null = null AS eq, null IS NULL AS is_null, true AND null AS and_null,
       false AND null AS false_and, true OR null AS or_null,
       2 IN [1, null] AS maybe, 1 IN [1, null] AS found, coalesce(null, 1) AS first
```

```table
| eq   | is_null | and_null | false_and | or_null | maybe | found | first |
|------|---------|----------|-----------|---------|-------|-------|-------|
| null | true    | null     | false     | true    | null  | true  | 1     |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Operator precedence
properties.text:
Operators bind in this order, tightest first. Operators on one row have the same precedence and group from left to right, except the comparison row, which chains.

| Level | Operators                                                                                                  | Grouping                                  | Example                   | Result |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------ |
| 1     | `.key`, `[index]`, `[from..to]`                                                                            | Postfix                                   | `[1, 2, 3][1] * 2`        | `4`    |
| 2     | Unary `-`, unary `+`                                                                                       | Prefix                                    | `-2 ^ 2`                  | `4.0`  |
| 3     | `^`                                                                                                        | Left to right                             | `2 ^ 3 ^ 2`               | `64.0` |
| 4     | `*`, `/`, `%`                                                                                              | Left to right                             | `2 * 3 % 4`               | `2`    |
| 5     | `+`, `-`, `\|\|`                                                                                           | Left to right                             | `10 - 4 - 3`              | `3`    |
| 6     | `IN`, `STARTS WITH`, `ENDS WITH`, `CONTAINS`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `IS [NOT] :: <type>`, `IS [NOT] NORMALIZED` | Left to right                             | `1 + 2 IN [3]`            | `true` |
| 7     | `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `=~`                                                                      | Chained: `a < b < c` is `a < b AND b < c` | `1 < 2 < 3`               | `true` |
| 8     | `NOT`                                                                                                      | Prefix                                    | `NOT true = false`        | `true` |
| 9     | `AND`                                                                                                      | Left to right                             | `true OR false AND false` | `true` |
| 10    | `XOR`                                                                                                      | Left to right                             | `true XOR true AND false` | `true` |
| 11    | `OR`                                                                                                       | Left to right                             | `false AND false OR true` | `true` |

Parentheses override the table. Two rows surprise readers who come from other languages: unary minus binds tighter than `^`, so `-x ^ 2` is `(-x) ^ 2`, and a comparison chains, so `1 < 2 = true` is `1 < 2 AND 2 = true`, which is `false`.

```cypher run name=precedence
WITH 2 AS x
RETURN -x ^ 2 AS neg_first, -(x ^ 2) AS pow_first, 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 AS left_assoc,
       1 = 1 IN [true] AS in_binds_tighter, 1 < 2 = true AS chained,
       (1 < 2) = true AS grouped, true XOR true AND false AS xor_and
```

```table
| neg_first | pow_first | left_assoc | in_binds_tighter | chained | grouped | xor_and |
|-----------|-----------|------------|------------------|---------|---------|---------|
| 4.0       | -4.0      | 64.0       | false            | false   | true    | true    |
1 row
```

properties.heading: reduce and allReduce
properties.text:
| Form                                                                 | Result                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `reduce(acc = <initial>, x IN list \| <expression>)`                 | Evaluates the expression for each element in order, with `acc` holding the previous result; returns the last |
| `allReduce(acc = <initial>, x IN list \| <expression>, <predicate>)` | `true` when the predicate holds for the accumulator after every step; stops at the first step where it fails |

```cypher run name=reduce
RETURN reduce(total = 0, x IN [1, 2, 3, 4] | total + x) AS total,
       allReduce(s = 0, x IN [1, 2, 3] | s + x, s < 5) AS stays_under_five
```

```table
| total | stays_under_five |
|-------|------------------|
| 10    | false            |
1 row
```

properties.heading: String operators
properties.text:
| Operator                                             | Result              | Notes                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `a + b`                                              | Concatenation       | A number on either side is converted: `'a' + 1` is `'a1'`                                                       |
| `a \|\| b`                                           | Concatenation       | Both sides must be strings; otherwise `type error: InvalidArgumentType: \|\| requires two strings or two lists` |
| `a STARTS WITH b`                                    | `BOOLEAN`           | Case-sensitive                                                                                                  |
| `a ENDS WITH b`                                      | `BOOLEAN`           | Case-sensitive                                                                                                  |
| `a CONTAINS b`                                       | `BOOLEAN`           | Case-sensitive                                                                                                  |
| `a =~ <regex>`                                       | `BOOLEAN`           | The whole string must match; a comparison operator, so it chains                                                |
| `a IS [NOT] [NFC \| NFD \| NFKC \| NFKD] NORMALIZED` | `BOOLEAN`           | Unicode normalization test; the form defaults to `NFC`                                                          |
| `s'… {<expression>} …'`                              | Interpolated string | `\{` and `\}` are literal braces; an embedded `null` makes the whole string `null`                              |

```cypher run name=strings
RETURN 'rel' + 'ate' AS plus, 'rel' || 'ate' AS concat, 'a' + 1 AS mixed,
       'relate' STARTS WITH 'rel' AS starts, 'relate' CONTAINS 'lat' AS contains,
       'abc' IS NFC NORMALIZED AS normalized, s'{1 + 1} items' AS interpolated
```

```table
|----------|----------|-------|--------|----------|------------|--------------|
| "relate" | "relate" | "a1"  | true   | true     | true       | "2 items"    |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Subquery expressions
properties.text:
| Form                                | Result                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `EXISTS { <pattern or statement> }` | `true` when the subquery returns at least one row |
| `COUNT { <pattern or statement> }`  | The number of rows                                |
| `COLLECT { <statement> }`           | A list of the single column the statement returns |

Variables of the outer row are visible inside. [Composing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/composing-clauses/) covers `CALL` subqueries, which return more than one column.

```cypher run name=subqueries
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Grace'})
RETURN COUNT { (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->() } AS projects,
       EXISTS { (p)<-[:KNOWS]-() } AS known,
       COLLECT { MATCH (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->(proj) RETURN proj.name ORDER BY proj.name } AS names
```

```table
| projects | known | names                        |
|----------|-------|------------------------------|
| 2        | true  | ["opencypher-tck", "relate"] |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
<literal> | <variable> | $<parameter>
<expression>.<key> | <expression>[<index or key>] | <list>[<from>..<to>]
<unary operator> <expression> | <expression> <binary operator> <expression>
<function>(<argument>, …)
CASE … WHEN … THEN … [ELSE …] END
[<variable> IN <list> [WHERE <predicate>] [| <expression>]]
[<pattern> [WHERE <predicate>] | <expression>]
<variable> {.<key>, .*, <key>: <expression>, …}
reduce(<accumulator> = <initial>, <variable> IN <list> | <expression>)
all | any | none | single (<variable> IN <list> WHERE <predicate>)
<expression> IS [NOT] :: <type>
COUNT { … } | EXISTS { … } | COLLECT { … }
```

[Types and values](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/types-and-values/) lists the literal forms of each type, and [functions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/functions/) lists every function.

properties.heading: Type predicates
properties.text:
`<expression> IS :: <type>` tests a value's type; `IS NOT ::` negates it. `IS TYPED <type>` and `:: <type>` are the same test. The type names are the ones `valueType()` returns ([types and values](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/types-and-values/#value-types)).

| Form                        | Rule                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `x IS :: INTEGER`           | `true` for an integer, and for `null`: every type includes `null` unless it says `NOT NULL` |
| `x IS :: INTEGER NOT NULL`  | `false` for `null`                                                                          |
| `x IS :: INTEGER \| STRING` | `true` for either type                                                                      |
| `x IS :: LIST<INTEGER>`     | `true` for a list whose elements are all integers                                           |
| `x IS :: ANY`               | `true` for every value                                                                      |
| `valueType(x)`              | The type name as a string, with its nullability: `valueType(1)` is `'INTEGER NOT NULL'`     |

```cypher run name=type-predicates
RETURN 5 IS :: INTEGER AS int, null IS :: INTEGER AS null_is_int,
       null IS :: INTEGER NOT NULL AS not_null, 1 IS :: INTEGER | STRING AS union_type,
       [1] IS :: LIST<INTEGER> AS list_type, valueType([1, 'two']) AS mixed
```

```table
| int  | null_is_int | not_null | union_type | list_type | mixed                                               |
|------|-------------|----------|------------|-----------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| true | true        | false    | true       | true      | "LIST<STRING NOT NULL | INTEGER NOT NULL> NOT NULL" |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Functions
properties.text:
relate ships 194 function signatures under 176 names, the rows `SHOW FUNCTIONS` returns, plus six more behind preview opt-ins. This page lists each one by category with its signature as `SHOW FUNCTIONS` prints it, what it returns, and a note on the edge cases. A row that differs from its catalog signature says so. Rows that name several functions (the trigonometric, hyperbolic, clock and `*.truncate` rows), the `format(value :: …, pattern :: STRING)` row, and the `[, pattern :: STRING]` form of the GQL temporal names each condense several catalog signatures into one. The cells run on relate's WebAssembly (WASM) build, which runs the same engine as the CLI and the clients.

| Category                                                | Functions                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Graph element functions](#graph-element-functions)     | `elementId`, `id`, `labels`, `type`, `keys`, `properties`, `startNode`, `endNode`, `nodes`, `relationships`, `length`, `path_length`, `db.nameFromElementId`                                                  |
| [Scalar functions](#scalar-functions)                   | `coalesce`, `nullIf`, `valueType`, `size`, `cardinality`, `char_length`, `character_length`, `head`, `last`, `linenumber`, `file`                                                                             |
| [Conversion functions](#conversion-functions)           | `toString`, `toStringOrNull`, `toInteger`, `toIntegerOrNull`, `toFloat`, `toFloatOrNull`, `toBoolean`, `toBooleanOrNull`, `toStringList`, `toIntegerList`, `toFloatList`, `toBooleanList`                     |
| [String functions](#string-functions)                   | `toUpper`, `upper`, `toLower`, `lower`, `trim`, `ltrim`, `rtrim`, `btrim`, `normalize`, `replace`, `substring`, `left`, `right`, `split`, `reverse`, `string.join`, `string.regexReplace`, `string.indexOf`   |
| [List functions](#list-functions)                       | `tail`, `reverse`, `range`, `reduce`, `coll.flatten`, `coll.sort`, `coll.indexOf`, `coll.insert`, `coll.remove`, `coll.max`, `coll.min`, `coll.distinct`                                                      |
| [Math functions](#math-functions)                       | `abs`, `ceil`, `ceiling`, `floor`, `round`, `sign`, `rand`, `isNaN`, `sqrt`, `exp`, `log`, `ln`, `log10`, `e`, `pi`, and the trigonometric functions                                                          |
| [Temporal functions](#temporal-functions)               | `date`, `time`, `localtime`, `datetime`, `localdatetime`, their GQL names, `duration`, `duration.*`, `*.truncate`, `*.realtime`, `*.statement`, `*.transaction`, `datetime.fromepoch*`, `format`, `timestamp` |
| [Spatial functions](#spatial-functions)                 | `point`, `point.distance`, `point.withinBBox`                                                                                                                                                                 |

properties.heading: Aggregating functions
properties.text:
An aggregating function reduces the rows of a group to one value; the other items of the `RETURN` or `WITH` are the grouping keys. `DISTINCT` before the argument aggregates each distinct value once, and `ALL` is the default.

| Signature                                                                             | Returns                                     | Notes                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `count(input :: ANY) :: INTEGER`                                                      | The number of values that are not `null`    | `count(*)` counts rows, `null` included                |
| `sum(input :: INTEGER \| FLOAT \| DURATION) :: INTEGER \| FLOAT \| DURATION`          | The sum                                     | `0` over no values; mixing numbers and durations fails |
| `avg(input :: INTEGER \| FLOAT \| DURATION) :: INTEGER \| FLOAT \| DURATION`          | The mean                                    | A float for integers; `null` over no values            |
| `min(input :: ANY) :: ANY`                                                            | The smallest value                          | Across types, the type order of `ORDER BY` applies     |
| `max(input :: ANY) :: ANY`                                                            | The largest value                           | Same rule                                              |
| `collect(input :: ANY) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                  | The values as a list                        | `null` values are left out; `[]` over no values        |
| `stDev(input :: FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                                                      | Sample standard deviation, divided by N − 1 | `null` over no values                                  |
| `stDevP(input :: FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                                                     | Population standard deviation, divided by N | —                                                      |
| `percentileCont(input :: FLOAT, percentile :: FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                        | The percentile, interpolated                | `percentile` from 0 to 1                               |
| `percentileDisc(input :: INTEGER \| FLOAT, percentile :: FLOAT) :: INTEGER \| FLOAT`  | The nearest value at the percentile         | Returns a `FLOAT` for integer input: `2.0`             |
| `collect_list(input :: ANY) :: LIST<ANY>`                                             | Same as `collect`                           | GQL name                                               |
| `stdev_samp(input :: FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                                                 | Same as `stDev`                             | GQL name                                               |
| `stdev_pop(input :: FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                                                  | Same as `stDevP`                            | GQL name                                               |
| `percentile_cont(input :: FLOAT, percentile :: FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                       | Same as `percentileCont`                    | GQL name                                               |
| `percentile_disc(input :: INTEGER \| FLOAT, percentile :: FLOAT) :: INTEGER \| FLOAT` | Same as `percentileDisc`                    | GQL name                                               |

Every aggregate but `count(*)` skips `null` values.

```cypher run name=aggregates
MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
RETURN proj.name AS project, count(*) AS people, collect(p.name) AS names,
       min(w.since) AS first, avg(w.since) AS mean, percentileDisc(w.since, 0.5) AS median
ORDER BY project
```

```table
| project          | people | names            | first | mean   | median |
|------------------|--------|------------------|-------|--------|--------|
| "opencypher-tck" | 1      | ["Grace"]        | 2022  | 2022.0 | 2022.0 |
| "relate"         | 2      | ["Grace", "Ada"] | 2023  | 2023.5 | 2023.0 |
2 rows
```

properties.heading: Conversion functions
properties.text:
| Signature                                                              | Returns                                      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toString(input :: ANY) :: STRING`                                     | The value as a string                        | Maps, lists and graph values render in display form (`{a: 1}`). A list literal fails at compile time with `syntax error: InvalidArgumentValue: toString()`; a list in a variable or property converts                                                                         |
| `toStringOrNull(input :: ANY) :: STRING`                               | As `toString`, or `null` instead of an error | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `toInteger(input :: BOOLEAN \| STRING \| INTEGER \| FLOAT) :: INTEGER` | The value as an integer                      | A float truncates toward zero; a string parses decimal, hexadecimal (`'0x1F'`), octal and `_` forms. A `BOOLEAN` argument fails with `type error: InvalidArgumentValue: toInteger()`, although the catalog lists it. A string outside the range fails with `NumberOutOfRange` |
| `toIntegerOrNull(input :: ANY) :: INTEGER`                             | As `toInteger`, or `null`                    | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `toFloat(input :: STRING \| INTEGER \| FLOAT) :: FLOAT`                | The value as a float                         | `'NaN'` and `'Infinity'` parse; other spellings are `null`                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `toFloatOrNull(input :: ANY) :: FLOAT`                                 | As `toFloat`, or `null`                      | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `toBoolean(input :: BOOLEAN \| STRING \| INTEGER) :: BOOLEAN`          | The value as a boolean                       | Strings `'true'` and `'false'` in any case; other strings give `null`. An integer is `false` only for `0`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `toBooleanOrNull(input :: ANY) :: BOOLEAN`                             | As `toBoolean`, or `null`                    | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `toStringList(input :: LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<STRING>`                     | Each element as a string                     | A `null` element becomes `'null'`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `toIntegerList(input :: VECTOR \| LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<INTEGER>`         | Each element as an integer                   | An element that does not convert becomes `null`; never fails for an element                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `toFloatList(input :: VECTOR \| LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<FLOAT>`             | Each element as a float                      | Same rule; also takes a vector                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `toBooleanList(input :: LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<BOOLEAN>`                   | Each element as a boolean                    | Same rule                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

```cypher run name=conversion
RETURN toString({a: 1}) AS display, toInteger(-3.9) AS truncated, toInteger('0x1F') AS hex,
       toIntegerOrNull('x') AS bad_int, toBoolean('TRUE') AS bool, toBoolean('yes') AS not_bool,
       toIntegerList(['1', 'x']) AS ints, toFloatList(vector([1, 2], 2, INT8)) AS from_vector
```

```table
| display  | truncated | hex | bad_int | bool | not_bool | ints      | from_vector |
|----------|-----------|-----|---------|------|----------|-----------|-------------|
| "{a: 1}" | -3        | 31  | null    | true | null     | [1, null] | [1.0, 2.0]  |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Graph element functions
properties.text:
These functions read a [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node), a [relationship](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship) or a [path](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#path): its labels or type, its [properties](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property), its end nodes and its [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id).

| Signature                                                    | Returns                                 | Notes                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `elementId(input :: NODE \| RELATIONSHIP) :: STRING`         | The element id                          | `4:rl-id:n<k>` for a node, `5:rl-id:r<k>` for a relationship in the `neo4j` namespace |
| `id(input :: NODE \| RELATIONSHIP) :: INTEGER`               | The integer id                          | Deprecated; the catalog names `elementId` as the replacement                          |
| `db.nameFromElementId(elementId :: STRING) :: STRING`        | The namespace of an element id          | `neo4j` for the data namespace                                                        |
| `labels(input :: NODE) :: LIST<STRING>`                      | The node's labels                       | —                                                                                     |
| `type(input :: RELATIONSHIP) :: STRING`                      | The relationship type                   | —                                                                                     |
| `keys(input :: NODE \| RELATIONSHIP \| MAP) :: LIST<STRING>` | The property names, or a map's keys     | In sorted order                                                                       |
| `properties(input :: NODE \| RELATIONSHIP \| MAP) :: MAP`    | Every property as a map                 | A map argument returns the map                                                        |
| `startNode(input :: RELATIONSHIP) :: NODE`                   | The start node                          | —                                                                                     |
| `endNode(input :: RELATIONSHIP) :: NODE`                     | The end node                            | —                                                                                     |
| `nodes(input :: PATH) :: LIST<NODE>`                         | The path's nodes, in order              | —                                                                                     |
| `relationships(input :: PATH) :: LIST<RELATIONSHIP>`         | The path's relationships, in order      | —                                                                                     |
| `length(input :: PATH) :: INTEGER`                           | The number of relationships in the path | —                                                                                     |
| `path_length(input :: PATH) :: INTEGER`                      | The number of relationships in the path | GQL name of `length`                                                                  |

The cells from here on run on the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

```cypher run name=graph-elements
MATCH p = (a:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[r:WORKS_ON]->(proj)
RETURN labels(a) AS labels, type(r) AS type, keys(a) AS keys, properties(r) AS props,
       endNode(r).name AS ends_at, length(p) AS hops, size(nodes(p)) AS path_nodes,
       db.nameFromElementId(elementId(a)) AS namespace
```

```table
| labels     | type       | keys             | props         | ends_at  | hops | path_nodes | namespace |
|------------|------------|------------------|---------------|----------|------|------------|-----------|
| ["Person"] | "WORKS_ON" | ["name", "role"] | {since: 2024} | "relate" | 1    | 2          | "neo4j"   |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Graph reference functions
properties.text:
| Signature                                            | Returns                            | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `graph.names() :: LIST<STRING>`                      | The graphs of a composite database | Fails in relate, which has no composite databases: `semantic error: SemanticError: Dynamic graph lookup not allowed here. This feature is only available on composite databases. Attempted to access graph <call>`, where `<call>` is the call as written, such as `graph.names()` |

properties.heading: List functions
properties.text:
| Signature                                                                                                                 | Returns                                             | Notes                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tail(input :: LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                                                   | Every element but the first                         | `[]` for an empty list                                                                               |
| `reverse(input :: STRING \| LIST<ANY>) :: STRING \| LIST<ANY>`                                                            | The elements in reverse order                       | —                                                                                                    |
| `range(start :: INTEGER, end :: INTEGER) :: LIST<INTEGER>`                                                                | `start` to `end`, both included                     | `range(1, 0)` is `[]`                                                                                |
| `range(start :: INTEGER, end :: INTEGER, step :: INTEGER) :: LIST<INTEGER>`                                               | Every `step`-th integer                             | A negative step counts down; a zero step fails with `NumberOutOfRange: range() step cannot be 0`     |
| `reduce(accumulator :: VARIABLE = initial :: ANY, variable :: VARIABLE IN list :: LIST<ANY> \| expression :: ANY) :: ANY` | The list folded into one value                      | Syntax in [expressions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/expressions/#reduce-and-allreduce) |
| `coll.flatten(list :: LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                                            | Nested lists flattened one level                    | `coll.flatten([1, [2, [3]]])` is `[1, 2, [3]]`                                                       |
| `coll.flatten(list :: LIST<ANY>, depth :: INTEGER) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                          | Nested lists flattened `depth` levels               | —                                                                                                    |
| `coll.sort(list :: LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                                               | The elements in ascending order                     | —                                                                                                    |
| `coll.indexOf(list :: LIST<ANY>, value :: ANY) :: INTEGER`                                                                | The zero-based index of the first match             | `-1` when absent                                                                                     |
| `coll.insert(list :: LIST<ANY>, index :: INTEGER, value :: ANY) :: LIST<ANY>`                                             | The list with `value` at `index`                    | —                                                                                                    |
| `coll.remove(list :: LIST<ANY>, index :: INTEGER) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                           | The list without the element at `index`             | —                                                                                                    |
| `coll.max(list :: LIST<ANY>) :: ANY`                                                                                      | The largest element                                 | —                                                                                                    |
| `coll.min(list :: LIST<ANY>) :: ANY`                                                                                      | The smallest element                                | —                                                                                                    |
| `coll.distinct(list :: LIST<ANY>) :: LIST<ANY>`                                                                           | The list without duplicates, first occurrences kept | —                                                                                                    |

`size`, `head` and `last` are under [scalar functions](#scalar-functions).

```cypher run name=lists
RETURN tail([1, 2, 3]) AS tail, range(0, 10, 3) AS stepped, range(5, 1, -2) AS down,
       coll.flatten([1, [2, [3]]], 2) AS flat, coll.sort([3, 1, 2]) AS sorted,
       coll.insert([1, 3], 1, 2) AS inserted, coll.distinct([1, 1, 2]) AS distinct
```

```table
| tail   | stepped      | down      | flat      | sorted    | inserted  | distinct |
|--------|--------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|----------|
| [2, 3] | [0, 3, 6, 9] | [5, 3, 1] | [1, 2, 3] | [1, 2, 3] | [1, 2, 3] | [1, 2]   |
1 row
```
