properties.heading: Cypher overview
properties.text: relate runs [openCypher](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#opencypher), plus a large part of Neo4j's Cypher 25 and its extensions aligned with GQL, the ISO graph query language. Statements run as Cypher 25 unless a `CYPHER 5` prefix says otherwise. Preview features stay off until `RELATE_PREVIEW` names them. Cypher for servers and clusters, such as users, roles and composite databases, is out of scope for an engine that runs inside one process.

properties.heading: Conformance
properties.text:
The openCypher Technology Compatibility Kit (TCK) is the language contract. The relate project measures coverage against it outside the engine's own repository, and its published compliance record says that "no engine document publishes a current TCK pass count any more". This page therefore states no current pass rate.

| Measure                                 | What it covers                                                                                                                  | Published result                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Spec harness                            | Neo4j's Cypher spec suites, the openCypher TCK among them, run against the engine built from each ready-for-review pull request | Coverage reported on every such pull request; reporting only, never a merge gate; no pass count published                                                                                                                        |
| In-repo TCK run, retired 2026-11-05     | A pinned openCypher TCK 2024.3 corpus, checked strictly: error class, error phase, and side effects                             | 3,892 of 3,892 expanded scenarios passed with 0 skipped, in CI, until 2026-11-05. The pinned corpus was not unmodified 2024.3: one scenario was removed and seven were re-pinned to current Neo4j behavior. The claim is retired |
| Cypher Improvement Proposal (CIP) suite | Neo4j Cypher beyond the TCK, derived from Neo4j's CIP documents                                                                 | Landing run in the spec harness: 4,942 passed, 924 failing and 51 skipped of 5,917 scenarios. A tracker, not a floor                                                                                                             |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store, starting from the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

The default language of each namespace:

```cypher run name=languages
SHOW DATABASES YIELD name, defaultLanguage RETURN name, defaultLanguage
```

```table
| name                | defaultLanguage |
|---------------------|-----------------|
| "neo4j"             | "CYPHER 25"     |
| "system"            | "CYPHER 25"     |
| "system_ontologies" | "CYPHER 25"     |
3 rows
```

A [label expression](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label-expression) with a pattern predicate, and a quantified path pattern:

```cypher run name=label-expression
MATCH (p:Person&!Project WHERE p.role = 'engineer') RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name    |
|---------|
| "Ada"   |
| "Grace" |
2 rows
```

```cypher run name=quantified-path
MATCH (:Person {name: 'Ada'}) ((a)-[:KNOWS|WORKS_ON]->(b)){1,2} (reached)
RETURN DISTINCT reached.name AS reached ORDER BY reached
```

```table
| reached          |
|------------------|
| "Grace"          |
| "opencypher-tck" |
| "relate"         |
3 rows
```

`LET`, `FILTER` and a `COUNT` subquery in one pipeline:

```cypher run name=let-filter
MATCH (p:Person)
LET projects = COUNT { (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->() }
FILTER projects > 0
RETURN p.name AS name, projects ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name    | projects |
|---------|----------|
| "Ada"   | 1        |
| "Grace" | 2        |
2 rows
```

String interpolation, and explicit grouping:

```cypher run name=interpolation
MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(proj:Project)
RETURN s'{p.name} works on {proj.name}' AS line ORDER BY line
```

```table
| line                            |
|---------------------------------|
| "Ada works on relate"           |
| "Grace works on opencypher-tck" |
| "Grace works on relate"         |
3 rows
```

```cypher run name=group-by
MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.role AS role, count(*) AS people GROUP BY role ORDER BY role
```

```table
| role         | people |
|--------------|--------|
| "engineer"   | 2      |
| "maintainer" | 1      |
2 rows
```

A preview feature without its opt-in:

```cypher run name=preview-off expect=error
DEFINE FUNCTION twice(x) = x * 2
RETURN twice(21) AS answer
```

```table
error: semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'local-callables' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=local-callables
```

The same statement on the CLI, with the opt-in in the command's environment:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=local-callables relate --mode envelope "DEFINE FUNCTION twice(x) = x * 2 RETURN twice(21) AS answer"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["answer"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"answer":42}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":0.438125,"execute_ms":0.246333,"lex_parse_ms":0.025042,"lower_ms":0.042208,"parse_ms":0.113125,"plan_ms":0.07037500000000001,"result_generation_ms":0.00020800000000000001,"rewrite_ms":0.020583},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Out of scope
properties.text:
| Area                                                | relate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Alternative                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Users, roles, and privileges                        | Not implemented                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | File permissions on the store, `--read-only`, and `relate serve --auth` on a served store                                                                 |
| Several databases                                   | Three fixed namespaces per store: `neo4j` for data, `system`, and `system_ontologies` (listed, not queryable)                                                                                                                                    | One store per graph                                                                                                                                       |
| Database administration                             | Only `SHOW DATABASE[S]`, `SHOW DEFAULT DATABASE`, `SHOW HOME DATABASE` and `ALTER DATABASE … SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE`; anything else fails with `semantic error: UnsupportedAdministrationCommand: Unsupported administration command: <statement>` | —                                                                                                                                                         |
| Composite, remote and sharded databases; clustering | Not implemented                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | —                                                                                                                                                         |
| Queries across graphs                               | A statement runs against one graph                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Query each store and join the results in your code                                                                                                        |
| APOC and Graph Data Science libraries               | Not included                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The built-in functions and procedures; [differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) lists the replacements |
| Long explicit path bounds                           | An explicit bound of more than 500 hops fails with `TraversalDepthExceeded`                                                                                                                                                                      | `--max-traversal-depth <n>`, up to 2000                                                                                                                   |

[Limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/) lists each limit and the reason for it.

properties.heading: Preview features
properties.text:
A [preview feature](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#preview-feature) ships in the engine and stays off until its name is in `RELATE_PREVIEW`, which is read once when the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) opens. Several names are separated by commas. An unknown name fails the open with exit code 1 and lists the known names. The error a feature gives while it is off depends on the feature, as the When off column shows. Most give the preview message, `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature '<name>' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=<name>`, which names the opt-in. A name gate fails as an unknown function, and a few fail as the parser or the `SEARCH` rules would without the feature; those messages do not mention `RELATE_PREVIEW`.

| Name                        | Enables                                                                                  | When off                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `hybrid-search`             | `COMBINE` inside `SEARCH`: weighted reciprocal-rank fusion of two or more index searches | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `local-callables`           | `DEFINE FUNCTION` and `DEFINE PROCEDURE`, scoped to one statement                        | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ontology`                  | The `db.ontology.*` procedures: `get`, `set`, `apply` and `drop`                         | The preview message; any other `db.ontology.*` name is `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: <name>` with the feature on or off                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `graph-type-opt-props`      | Optional properties, `prop :: ANY`, in a graph type                                      | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `graph-type-default-values` | `DEFAULT ON COMMIT <value>` on a graph type's property                                   | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `graph-type-implied-labels` | Implied labels and inheritance between graph types                                       | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `obfuscated-literals`       | The `******` placeholder literal                                                         | `syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "*"`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `mixed-label-syntax`        | Mixing `:A:B`, GQL label symbols and `IS` across one clause's label expressions          | `syntax error: parse error: InvalidLabelExpression: mixing label expression symbols (\|, &, !, and %) with colon (:) between labels is not allowed`, or for `IS`, `syntax error: parse error: MixedIsAndColonConjunction: cannot mix the IS introducer with colon-conjunction within the same clause` |
| `float16-coordinate-types`  | `FLOAT16` and `BFLOAT16` vector coordinates                                              | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `chronological-comparisons` | `IS [NOT] BEFORE`, `AFTER`, `SAME INSTANT` and `SAME REPRESENTATION`                     | The preview message                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `complex-search-patterns`   | `SEARCH` on a `MATCH` with more than one node or hop                                     | The `MATCH` shape errors in the [search rules](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#rules-of-the-search-clause): `SearchClauseTooComplexPattern` or `SearchClauseMultipleBoundVariables`                                                                                                 |
| `coll-zip`                  | The `coll.zip` function (name gate)                                                      | `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function coll.zip()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `coll-has`                  | The `coll.hasAnyOf`, `coll.hasAllOf` and `coll.hasNoneOf` functions (name gate)          | `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function <name>()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `gql-stddev-aliases`        | The `stddev_samp` and `stddev_pop` spellings (name gate)                                 | `syntax error: UnknownFunction: unknown function <name>()`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/): the Neo4j habits that fail in relate, and what to write instead.
- [Search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/): vector and full-text indexes and the `SEARCH` clause.
- [Limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/): the scope choices, with their reasons.
- [The Cypher dialect](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/cypher-dialect/): why the dialect is shaped this way.

properties.heading: Supported Cypher 25 and GQL-aligned features
properties.text:
Each feature runs on the WebAssembly build the cells on this site use and on the CLI, without an opt-in. The exception is a generated identifier: `uuid()` with no argument and `randomUUID()` run on the CLI and the clients, and on the WebAssembly build the engine panics with `time not implemented on this platform` and the instance stops. `uuid('<uuid string>')` runs on both.

| Feature                  | Form                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Label expressions        | `(n:Person\|Project)`, `(n:Person&!Bot)`, `(n:%)`, `(n IS Person)`                                       |
| Pattern predicates       | `(p:Person WHERE p.role = 'engineer')`                                                                   |
| Quantified path patterns | `((a)-[:KNOWS]->(b)){1,3}`, `-[:KNOWS]->{1,3}`                                                           |
| Path selectors and modes | `SHORTEST 1`, `ANY SHORTEST`, `ALL SHORTEST`, `TRAIL`, `ACYCLIC`, `WALK`                                 |
| Dynamic labels and types | `MATCH (n:$($label))`, `CREATE ()-[:$($type)]->()`                                                       |
| Type predicates          | `x IS :: INTEGER`, `valueType(x)`                                                                        |
| New clauses              | `LET`, `FILTER`, `NEXT`, `WHEN … THEN … ELSE`, `FINISH`, `INSERT`                                        |
| Subquery expressions     | `COUNT { … }`, `COLLECT { … }`, `EXISTS { … }`                                                           |
| `CALL` scope clause      | `CALL (p) { … }`, `CALL () { … }`                                                                        |
| Batched writes           | `CALL (row) { … } IN TRANSACTIONS OF <n> ROWS`                                                           |
| String interpolation     | `s'{p.name} works on {proj.name}'`                                                                       |
| Explicit grouping        | `RETURN p.role AS role, count(*) AS n GROUP BY role`                                                     |
| Concatenation            | `'rel' \|\| 'ate'`, `[1] \|\| [2]`                                                                       |
| Map comprehensions       | `{i IN [1, 2] \| toString(i): i * 10}`                                                                   |
| Value types              | `VECTOR` through `vector(…)`, `UUID` through `uuid('<uuid string>')`                                     |
| Graph types              | `CREATE GRAPH TYPE`, `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE`, `SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE`                               |
| Index search             | `SEARCH` over vector and full-text indexes ([search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/)) |
| Unicode identifiers      | `RETURN 1 AS café`, unquoted                                                                             |

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
[CYPHER 5 | CYPHER 25] [EXPLAIN | PROFILE] <statement>
```

| Setting          | Default                                                                                                                                     | Values                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Language version | `CYPHER 25` for every [namespace](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#namespace), as `SHOW DATABASES` reports in `defaultLanguage` | A `CYPHER 5` or `CYPHER 25` prefix on one statement. `ALTER DATABASE <name> SET DEFAULT LANGUAGE CYPHER 5` changes only what `SHOW DATABASES` reports ([Cypher versions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/cypher-versions/#default-language)) |
| Preview features | None enabled                                                                                                                                | `RELATE_PREVIEW=<feature>[,<feature>…]` in the environment of the process that opens the store                                                                                                                                                         |
| Plan prefixes    | None                                                                                                                                        | `EXPLAIN` plans without running; `PROFILE` runs and measures ([tune a query](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/tune-a-query/))                                                                                                                    |

properties.heading: Patterns
properties.text: A pattern is the shape a statement looks for or creates. A [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node) pattern sits in parentheses, a [relationship](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship) pattern in brackets between two nodes, and a chain of them is a [path](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#path) pattern. `MATCH`, `OPTIONAL MATCH`, `MERGE`, `CREATE`, pattern predicates and `EXISTS` and `COUNT` subqueries all take patterns; `CREATE` and `MERGE` accept only fixed-length ones. relate accepts the GQL forms of Cypher 25: label expressions, quantified path patterns, path selectors and path modes, with no preview opt-in.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store, starting from the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

Four label expressions, counted:

```cypher run name=label-expressions
RETURN COUNT { (n:Person|Project) } AS personOrProject,
       COUNT { (n:!Person) } AS notPerson,
       COUNT { (n:%) } AS anyLabel,
       COUNT { (n IS Person) } AS isPerson
```

```table
| personOrProject | notPerson | anyLabel | isPerson |
|-----------------|-----------|----------|----------|
| 5               | 2         | 5        | 3        |
1 row
```

A type expression: every relationship from Grace except `KNOWS`:

```cypher run name=type-expression
MATCH (:Person {name: 'Grace'})-[r:!KNOWS]->(x)
RETURN type(r) AS type, x.name AS target ORDER BY target
```

```table
| type       | target           |
|------------|------------------|
| "WORKS_ON" | "opencypher-tck" |
| "WORKS_ON" | "relate"         |
2 rows
```

Labels from a parameter; `$any` matches either label:

```json data=labels
{"labels": ["Person", "Project"]}
```

```cypher run name=dynamic-labels params=labels
MATCH (n:$any($labels)) RETURN count(n) AS nodes
```

```table
| nodes |
|-------|
| 5     |
1 row
```

Colon conjunction and a symbol in one label expression:

```cypher run name=mixed-labels expect=error
MATCH (n:Person:Project|Bot) RETURN count(n) AS nodes
```

```table
error: syntax error: parse error: InvalidLabelExpression: cannot mix colon-conjunction with label expression symbols
  MATCH (n:Person:Project|Bot) RETURN count(n) AS nodes
                         ^
```

Inline `WHERE` on a node and on a relationship:

```cypher run name=inline-where
MATCH (p:Person WHERE p.role = 'engineer')-[w:WORKS_ON WHERE w.since < 2024]->(r:Project)
RETURN p.name AS person, r.name AS project ORDER BY project
```

```table
| person  | project          |
|---------|------------------|
| "Grace" | "opencypher-tck" |
| "Grace" | "relate"         |
2 rows
```

A variable-length relationship binds a list:

```cypher run name=variable-length
MATCH (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[r:KNOWS|WORKS_ON*1..2]->(x)
RETURN [rel IN r | type(rel)] AS types, x.name AS reached
ORDER BY size(types), reached
```

```table
| types                 | reached          |
|-----------------------|------------------|
| ["KNOWS"]             | "Grace"          |
| ["WORKS_ON"]          | "relate"         |
| ["KNOWS", "WORKS_ON"] | "opencypher-tck" |
| ["KNOWS", "WORKS_ON"] | "relate"         |
4 rows
```

A variable-length pattern follows a hierarchy to any depth. This cell writes a small package tree and returns every dependency path from `app`. The graph view draws the result in layers, `app` at the top and each package one layer below the deepest package that depends on it; its Layout menu switches to the force and circular layouts:

```cypher run name=dependency-tree layout=hierarchical
CREATE (app:Package {name: 'app'}),
       (cli:Package {name: 'cli'}),
       (engine:Package {name: 'engine'}),
       (parser:Package {name: 'parser'}),
       (storage:Package {name: 'storage'}),
       (lexer:Package {name: 'lexer'}),
       (app)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(cli),
       (app)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(engine),
       (cli)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(parser),
       (engine)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(parser),
       (engine)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(storage),
       (parser)-[:DEPENDS_ON]->(lexer);
MATCH p = (:Package {name: 'app'})-[:DEPENDS_ON*]->(:Package)
RETURN p
```

```gram
// 7 rows · nodes created: 6, relationships created: 6, properties set: 6, labels added: 6
(n5:Package {name: "app"})-[r6:DEPENDS_ON]->(n7:Package {name: "engine"})
(n5)-[r6]->(n7)-[r9:DEPENDS_ON]->(n9:Package {name: "storage"})
(n5)-[r6]->(n7)-[r8:DEPENDS_ON]->(n8:Package {name: "parser"})
(n5)-[r6]->(n7)-[r8]->(n8)-[r10:DEPENDS_ON]->(n10:Package {name: "lexer"})
(n5)-[r5:DEPENDS_ON]->(n6:Package {name: "cli"})
(n5)-[r5]->(n6)-[r7:DEPENDS_ON]->(n8)
(n5)-[r5]->(n6)-[r7]->(n8)-[r10]->(n10)
```

![The graph this cell returns, under "Examples"](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/patterns/result-dependency-tree-light.svg)

The seven rows are seven paths. `parser` and `lexer` are reached two ways, through `cli` and through `engine`, so they appear in more than one path but once in the graph.

Group variables of a quantified path pattern are lists, one entry per repetition:

```cypher run name=group-variables
MATCH (:Person {name: 'Ada'}) ((a)-[r]->(b)){2} (end)
RETURN [x IN a | x.name] AS from, [rel IN r | type(rel)] AS via, end.name AS reached
ORDER BY reached
```

```table
| from             | via                   | reached          |
|------------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| ["Ada", "Grace"] | ["KNOWS", "WORKS_ON"] | "opencypher-tck" |
| ["Ada", "Grace"] | ["KNOWS", "WORKS_ON"] | "relate"         |
2 rows
```

The two shortest routes from Noor to Grace, in either direction:

```cypher run name=shortest
MATCH p = SHORTEST 2 (:Person {name: 'Noor'})-[]-+(:Person {name: 'Grace'})
RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.name] AS route, length(p) AS hops
ORDER BY hops
```

```table
| route                              | hops |
|------------------------------------|------|
| ["Noor", "relate", "Grace"]        | 2    |
| ["Noor", "relate", "Ada", "Grace"] | 3    |
2 rows
```

A path variable binds what the pattern matched. This cell returns the path from Ada through Grace to `opencypher-tck` as `p`, and the people graph beside it as `people`. The graph view draws the path's three nodes and two relationships on top and dims the rest, and its legend names the path:

```cypher run name=named-path highlight=path
MATCH p = (:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'})
MATCH g = (:Person)-->()
RETURN p, collect(g) AS people
```

```gram
// 1 row
[ | (n0:Person {name: "Ada", role: "engineer"})-[r4:KNOWS]->(n1:Person {name: "Grace", role: "engineer"})-[r2:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(n4:Project {language: "Gherkin", name: "opencypher-tck"}), [ | (n0)-[r0:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(n3:Project {language: "Rust", name: "relate"}), (n0)-[r4]->(n1), (n1)-[r2]->(n4), (n1)-[r1:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(n3), (n2:Person {name: "Noor", role: "maintainer"})-[r3:MAINTAINS]->(n3)]]
```

![The graph this cell returns, under "Examples"](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/patterns/result-named-path-light.svg)

`shortestPath` binds one shortest path. From Noor to Grace in either direction it runs through `relate`, two hops; the route through Ada takes three:

```cypher run name=shortest-path highlight=path
MATCH p = shortestPath((:Person {name: 'Noor'})-[*]-(:Person {name: 'Grace'}))
MATCH g = (:Person)-->()
RETURN p, length(p) AS hops, collect(g) AS people
```

```gram
// 1 row
[{hops: 2} | (n2:Person {name: "Noor", role: "maintainer"})-[r3:MAINTAINS]->(n3:Project {language: "Rust", name: "relate"})<-[r1:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]-(n1:Person {name: "Grace", role: "engineer"}), [ | (n0:Person {name: "Ada", role: "engineer"})-[r0:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(n3), (n0)-[r4:KNOWS]->(n1), (n1)-[r2:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(n4:Project {language: "Gherkin", name: "opencypher-tck"}), (n1)-[r1]->(n3), (n2)-[r3]->(n3)]]
```

![The graph this cell returns, under "Examples"](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/patterns/result-shortest-path-light.svg)

Only a column of type `PATH` is highlighted: `people` is a list of paths too, and stays dimmed. Without a `PATH` column, every path in the rows is highlighted. Every graph view with a path in its result has the Highlight path button; these two cells start with it on.

`TRAIL` allows a path back to Ada around the Ada, Grace and relate triangle; `ACYCLIC` does not:

```cypher run name=path-modes
RETURN COUNT { MATCH p = TRAIL (a:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[]-+(a) RETURN p } AS trail,
       COUNT { MATCH p = ACYCLIC (a:Person {name: 'Ada'})-[]-+(a) RETURN p } AS acyclic
```

```table
| trail | acyclic |
|-------|---------|
| 2     | 0       |
1 row
```

`REPEATABLE ELEMENTS` lets a path reuse a relationship, so more paths of up to four hops connect Noor and Grace:

```cypher run name=match-modes
RETURN COUNT { MATCH p = (:Person {name: 'Noor'})-[]-{1,4}(:Person {name: 'Grace'}) RETURN p } AS differentRelationships,
       COUNT { MATCH REPEATABLE ELEMENTS p = (:Person {name: 'Noor'})-[]-{1,4}(:Person {name: 'Grace'}) RETURN p } AS repeatableElements
```

```table
| differentRelationships | repeatableElements |
|------------------------|--------------------|
| 2                      | 7                  |
1 row
```

An explicit bound over the default limit of 500 hops fails before the statement runs:

```cypher run name=hop-bound expect=error
MATCH (:Person)-[:KNOWS*1..1000]->(b) RETURN count(b) AS reached
```

```table
error: syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: This query allows paths up to 1,000 hops. This is a safety limit protecting against excessive traversal (not a database limit) — lower the path bound, or raise it with --max-traversal-depth (up to 2000).
```

A line of 40 stops shows the two unbounded cases: `MATCH` walks all 39 hops, and the `shortestPath` expression stops at 32. This cell writes 40 `Stop` nodes and the 39 `NEXT` relationships between them:

```cypher run name=unbounded
UNWIND range(1, 40) AS i CREATE (:Stop {i: i});
MATCH (a:Stop), (b:Stop) WHERE b.i = a.i + 1 CREATE (a)-[:NEXT]->(b);
MATCH (first:Stop {i: 1}), (stop33:Stop {i: 33}), (stop34:Stop {i: 34})
OPTIONAL MATCH p = (first)-[:NEXT*]->(:Stop)
RETURN max(length(p)) AS longestWalk,
       length(shortestPath((first)-[:NEXT*]->(stop33))) AS hopsTo33,
       length(shortestPath((first)-[:NEXT*]->(stop34))) AS hopsTo34
```

```table
| longestWalk | hopsTo33 | hopsTo34 |
|-------------|----------|----------|
| 39          | 32       | null     |
1 row · nodes created: 40, relationships created: 39, properties set: 40, labels added: 40
```

On the CLI, `--max-traversal-depth` raises the limit for one run. The store is in memory and empty, so no path matches:

```bash verify
relate --max-traversal-depth 1000 --mode table "MATCH (:Person)-[:KNOWS*1..1000]->(b) RETURN count(b) AS reached"
```

```text
+---------+
| reached |
+---------+
| 0       |
+---------+
```

properties.heading: Hop bound limit
properties.text:
An explicit upper bound greater than the traversal-depth limit fails before the statement runs. The limit is a safety limit that protects the process stack, not a database limit.

| Setting           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Default limit     | 500 hops                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Applies to        | An explicit upper bound: `*1..<n>`, `*..<n>`, `*<n>`, `{1,<n>}`, `{<n>}`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Exempt            | An unbounded upper bound (`*`, `*1..`, `+`, `{1,}`), including inside `shortestPath(…)` and `allShortestPaths(…)`. An explicit bound inside them, or under a `SHORTEST` selector, is checked like any other                                                                                                  |
| Raised by         | `--max-traversal-depth <n>` or `RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH`, from 1 to 2000 ([flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#max-traversal-depth))                                                                                                                                                     |
| Over the limit    | `syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: This query allows paths up to <n> hops. This is a safety limit protecting against excessive traversal (not a database limit) — lower the path bound, or raise it with --max-traversal-depth (up to 2000).`, where `<n>` is the statement's own bound; CLI exit code 6 |
| Flag out of range | `Error: invalid --max-traversal-depth: must be between 1 and 2000` (exit code 2)                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

properties.heading: Label expressions
properties.text:
A label expression tests a node's [labels](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label); the same operators on a relationship test its type.

| Form                                      | Node matches when                           | On a relationship                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `:A:B`                                    | It has `A` and `B`                          | —                                          |
| `:A&B`                                    | It has `A` and `B`                          | Never matches: a relationship has one type |
| `:A\|B`                                   | It has `A` or `B`                           | The type is `A` or `B`                     |
| `:!A`                                     | It does not have `A`                        | The type is not `A`                        |
| `:%`                                      | It has at least one label                   | Any type                                   |
| `:!%`                                     | It has no label                             | —                                          |
| `:(A\|B)&!C`                              | Parentheses group                           | The same                                   |
| `IS A`, `IS A\|B`                         | The same as `:`                             | The same                                   |
| `:$(<expression>)`, `:$all(<expression>)` | It has every label the string or list names | The type is the one named                  |
| `:$any(<expression>)`                     | It has any label the list names             | The type is one of those named             |
| `n:A\|B`, `n IS LABELED A` in `WHERE`     | The same test as a predicate                | —                                          |

| Mixing rule                                                              | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `:A:B` and a symbol (`\|`, `&`, `!`, `%`) in one label expression        | `syntax error: parse error: InvalidLabelExpression: cannot mix colon-conjunction with label expression symbols`; with `RELATE_PREVIEW=mixed-label-syntax` it still fails, and the message ends `… within one label expression` |
| `:A:B` in one pattern and a symbol in another pattern of the same clause | `syntax error: parse error: InvalidLabelExpression: mixing label expression symbols (\|, &, !, and %) with colon (:) between labels is not allowed`; `RELATE_PREVIEW=mixed-label-syntax` allows it                             |
| `IS` and `:A:B` in one clause                                            | `syntax error: parse error: MixedIsAndColonConjunction: cannot mix the IS introducer with colon-conjunction within the same clause`; `RELATE_PREVIEW=mixed-label-syntax` allows it                                             |

properties.heading: Node and relationship patterns
properties.text:
| Part           | Node                                                      | Relationship                                                      |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Variable       | `(p)` binds the node to `p`                               | `[r]` binds the relationship to `r`; with a length, `r` is a list |
| Labels or type | `(p:Person)`, or a [label expression](#label-expressions) | `[:WORKS_ON]`, or a [type expression](#label-expressions)         |
| Property map   | `(p {name: 'Ada'})`: equality on each key                 | `[w {since: 2024}]`: the same                                     |
| Inline `WHERE` | `(p:Person WHERE p.role = 'engineer')`                    | `[w:WORKS_ON WHERE w.since < 2024]`                               |
| Parameters     | `(p {name: $name})`                                       | `[w {since: $year}]`                                              |

| Direction                        | Matches          |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `-[…]->`, `-->`                  | Left to right    |
| `<-[…]-`, `<--`                  | Right to left    |
| `-[…]-`, `--`, `<-[…]->`, `<-->` | Either direction |

In `CREATE`, a relationship needs a direction and exactly one type ([writing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/writing-clauses/#errors)). In `CREATE` and `MERGE`, a variable-length or quantified relationship fails with `syntax error: CreatingVarLength: variable length relationships cannot be used in CREATE`; the `MERGE` form names `MERGE`.

properties.heading: Path selectors and modes
properties.text:
A selector keeps some of the paths between each pair of end nodes; a mode restricts what one path may repeat.

| Selector              | Keeps, per pair of end nodes                   |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `ANY SHORTEST`        | One shortest path                              |
| `ALL SHORTEST`        | Every path of the shortest length              |
| `SHORTEST <k>`        | The `k` shortest paths                         |
| `SHORTEST <k> GROUPS` | Every path in each of the `k` shortest lengths |
| `ANY`                 | One path                                       |
| `ANY <k>`             | `k` paths                                      |

| Mode      | A path may not repeat                       |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `WALK`    | Anything beyond what the match mode forbids |
| `TRAIL`   | A relationship                              |
| `ACYCLIC` | A node, so it never returns to its start    |

`shortestPath(<pattern>)` and `allShortestPaths(<pattern>)` are the older forms. In `MATCH p = shortestPath(…)` with no upper bound, the search has no hop cap. As an expression, `shortestPath(…)` with no upper bound finds paths of up to 32 hops and returns `null` for a longer one. Outside a `MATCH`, both end nodes must be variables bound earlier: `(a)-[:NEXT*]->(:Stop)` fails with `syntax error: InvalidPatternCharacter: A shortestPath(...) requires bound nodes when not part of a MATCH clause.`, and a property map on the relationship, `[:NEXT* {w: 1}]`, fails with `syntax error: InvalidPatternCharacter: unsupported use of properties: properties are not supported in the shortestPath() function`.

properties.heading: Path variables
properties.text: `p = <pattern>` binds the matched path. `nodes(p)` and `relationships(p)` return its parts as lists and `length(p)` its number of relationships; the [functions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/functions/) page has the rest.

properties.heading: Quantified path patterns
properties.text:
A [quantified path pattern](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#quantified-path-pattern) repeats a parenthesized pattern, `((a)-[r:KNOWS]->(b)){1,3}`, or a single relationship, `-[:KNOWS]->{1,3}`.

| Quantifier  | Repetitions |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| `{<n>}`     | Exactly `n` |
| `{<n>,<m>}` | `n` to `m`  |
| `{<n>,}`    | `n` or more |
| `{,<m>}`    | 0 to `m`    |
| `+`         | 1 or more   |
| `*`         | 0 or more   |

Variables inside the repeated part are group variables: after the match, each is a list with one entry per repetition. An inline `WHERE` inside the repeated part applies to every repetition.

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Reading clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/reading-clauses/): `MATCH`, `OPTIONAL MATCH` and `WHERE`, which take patterns.
- [Writing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/writing-clauses/): the patterns `CREATE` and `MERGE` accept.
- [Flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#max-traversal-depth): `--max-traversal-depth` and its environment variable.
- [Limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/): the traversal-depth limit and the reason for it.
- [The Cypher dialect](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/cypher-dialect/): where the GQL pattern forms come from.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
Node:          (<variable> <label expression> {<key>: <value>, …} WHERE <predicate>)
Relationship:  -[<variable> <type expression> <length> {<key>: <value>, …} WHERE <predicate>]->
               <-[…]-   -[…]-   <-[…]->   -->   <--   --
Length:        *   *<n>   *<n>..<m>   *<n>..   *..<m>
Quantified:    (<path pattern>)<quantifier>     -[…]-><quantifier>
Quantifier:    {<n>}   {<n>,<m>}   {<n>,}   {,<m>}   +   *
Path:          <path variable> = [<selector>] [<path mode>] <path pattern>
Match mode:    MATCH [DIFFERENT RELATIONSHIPS | REPEATABLE ELEMENTS] <path pattern>, …
Selector:      ANY SHORTEST | ALL SHORTEST | SHORTEST <k> | SHORTEST <k> GROUPS | ANY | ANY <k>
Path mode:     WALK | TRAIL | ACYCLIC
Functions:     shortestPath(<pattern>)   allShortestPaths(<pattern>)
```

Every part inside the parentheses and brackets is optional.

properties.heading: Uniqueness
properties.text: Within one `MATCH`, a relationship appears at most once per row: two relationship patterns never bind the same relationship. This is the `DIFFERENT RELATIONSHIPS` match mode, the default. Separate `MATCH` clauses do not share the rule. `REPEATABLE ELEMENTS` lets one relationship appear several times in a row; it needs every quantifier bounded, otherwise `syntax error: parse error: UnsafeRepeatableElements: REPEATABLE ELEMENTS cannot be combined with an unbounded quantified path pattern`.

properties.heading: Variable-length relationships
properties.text:
The classic form puts a length after the type.

| Length      | Hops                                       |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `*`         | 1 or more                                  |
| `*<n>`      | Exactly `n`                                |
| `*<n>..<m>` | `n` to `m`                                 |
| `*<n>..`    | `n` or more                                |
| `*..<m>`    | 1 to `m`                                   |
| `*0..<m>`   | 0 to `m`: the start node itself is a match |

The relationship variable of a variable-length pattern is a list of relationships. A property map applies to every relationship in the list.

properties.heading: Procedures
properties.text: A procedure is a built-in routine that `CALL` runs; it returns rows with named columns that `YIELD` picks. relate has 22 callable procedures that `SHOW PROCEDURES` lists, four ontology procedures behind a preview opt-in, and two callable procedures it does not list. `SHOW PROCEDURES` returns 31 rows by default; the other 9 are catalog entries kept for tools that read Neo4j's catalog, and a `CALL` to one fails with `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: <name>`. The cells run on relate's WebAssembly (WASM) build, and the `bash verify` blocks on the CLI.

properties.heading: Catalog-only entries
properties.text:
`SHOW PROCEDURES` lists these 9 names so that tools built for Neo4j find the rows they expect. None of them runs: each `CALL` fails with `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: <name>`.

| Group               | Names                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Indexes and tokens  | `db.awaitIndex`, `db.index.fulltext.awaitEventuallyConsistentIndexRefresh`, `db.index.fulltext.listAvailableAnalyzers`, `db.prepareForReplanning`, `db.createProperty`, `db.createRelationshipType` |
| Database operations | `db.checkpoint`, `db.clearQueryCaches`, `db.listLocks`                                                                                                                                              |

Releases up to and including 0.1.2 listed 57 more catalog entries, for change data capture, server configuration and connections, clustering and routing, fleet management, usage statistics, index resampling and the vector-property setters. relate 1.0.1 lists only what an embedded engine can answer, and a `CALL` to one of those names fails the same way.

```cypher run name=catalog-only expect=error
CALL db.checkpoint()
```

```table
error: syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: db.checkpoint
```

properties.heading: Index procedures
properties.text:
The query procedures search a [vector index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#vector-index) or a full-text index, created with `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` or `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` ([search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/)). The `SEARCH` clause replaces them, and all four are deprecated.

| Signature                                                                                                                                                               | `YIELD` columns         | Notes                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `db.index.vector.queryNodes(indexName :: STRING, numberOfNearestNeighbours :: INTEGER, query :: LIST<FLOAT>) :: (node :: NODE, score :: FLOAT)`                         | `node`, `score`         | The nearest nodes, highest score first; the score is the index's similarity, from 0 to 1      |
| `db.index.vector.queryRelationships(indexName :: STRING, numberOfNearestNeighbours :: INTEGER, query :: LIST<FLOAT>) :: (relationship :: RELATIONSHIP, score :: FLOAT)` | `relationship`, `score` | The same over a relationship vector index                                                     |
| `db.index.fulltext.queryNodes(indexName :: STRING, query :: STRING) :: (node :: NODE, score :: FLOAT)`                                                                  | `node`, `score`         | Matching nodes, highest score first, with the query syntax and scores of a full-text `SEARCH` |
| `db.index.fulltext.queryRelationships(indexName :: STRING, query :: STRING) :: (relationship :: RELATIONSHIP, score :: FLOAT)`                                          | `relationship`, `score` | The same over a relationship full-text index                                                  |
| `db.awaitIndexes(timeOutSeconds = 300 :: INTEGER)`                                                                                                                      | —                       | Returns at once with no rows; `SHOW INDEXES` reports every index `ONLINE`                     |

```cypher run name=create-indexes
CREATE VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR (p:Person) ON (p.focus)
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 3}};
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX person_role FOR (p:Person) ON EACH [p.role];
MATCH (p:Person)
SET p.focus = CASE p.name
  WHEN 'Ada' THEN vector([0.9, 0.1, 0.2], 3, FLOAT32)
  WHEN 'Grace' THEN vector([0.3, 0.9, 0.1], 3, FLOAT32)
  ELSE vector([0.2, 0.3, 0.9], 3, FLOAT32) END
```

```table
(no rows) · properties set: 3, indexes added: 2
```

```cypher run name=vector-query
CALL db.index.vector.queryNodes('person_focus', 2, [0.1, 0.9, 0.1]) YIELD node, score
RETURN node.name AS name, round(score, 4) AS score
```

properties.heading: Ontology procedures
properties.text:
The ontology procedures are a [preview feature](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#preview-feature); set `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology` in the environment of the process that opens the store to call them. They keep one Ontology Graph Spec 1.1.0 document per store, for the `neo4j` namespace. Without the opt-in, `SHOW PROCEDURES` leaves them out and a call fails with `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'ontology' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology`. The WASM build has no process environment, so the cells on this page cannot call them. [Model an ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/ontology/) is the task guide.

| Signature                                                            | Mode    | `YIELD` columns | Notes                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `db.ontology.set(ontology :: STRING)`                                | `WRITE` | —               | Validates the JSON or YAML document and stores it, replacing any earlier one. Auto-commit only, and the statement may write nothing else |
| `db.ontology.get(format = "yaml" :: STRING) :: (ontology :: STRING)` | `READ`  | `ontology`      | The stored document as YAML, or as the stored text with `'json'`; `null` when none is stored                                             |
| `db.ontology.apply()`                                                | `WRITE` | —               | Sets the current graph type from the stored document, as `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET` does; fails when the data violates it            |
| `db.ontology.drop()`                                                 | `WRITE` | —               | Removes the stored document; succeeds when none is stored. Auto-commit only                                                              |

The calls on the CLI, in order. This setup step writes the shared example graph to a new single-file store, `team.rl`:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

`db.ontology.set` writes a document that requires a `name` on every `Person`:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl "CALL db.ontology.set('{\"schema\": \"https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json\", \"version\": \"1\", \"id\": \"team\", \"nodes\": {\"Person\": {\"label\": \"Person\", \"properties\": {\"name\": {\"type\": \"STRING\", \"must_exist\": true}}}}}')"
```

`db.ontology.get`, read-only:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode jsonl "CALL db.ontology.get() YIELD ontology RETURN ontology"
```

```text
{"ontology":"---\nschema: \"https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json\"\nversion: \"1\"\nid: team\nnodes:\n  Person:\n    label: Person\n    properties:\n      name:\n        type: STRING\n        must_exist: true"}
```

`db.ontology.apply` writes the graph type, which `SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE` then prints:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology relate --database ./team.rl "CALL db.ontology.apply()"
```

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl --read-only --mode jsonl "SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE"
```

```text
{"specification":"{\n  (:`Person` => {`name` :: STRING NOT NULL})\n}"}
```

properties.heading: Schema procedures
properties.text:
These procedures read the store's [labels](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#label), [relationship types](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type) and [property](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property) keys from the data as it is now.

| Signature                                                                                                                                                         | `YIELD` columns                                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `db.labels() :: (label :: STRING)`                                                                                                                                | `label`                                                                | The labels some node carries                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `db.relationshipTypes() :: (relationshipType :: STRING)`                                                                                                          | `relationshipType`                                                     | The types some relationship has                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `db.propertyKeys() :: (propertyKey :: STRING)`                                                                                                                    | `propertyKey`                                                          | The keys some node or relationship has                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `db.schema.nodeTypeProperties() :: (nodeType :: STRING, nodeLabels :: LIST<STRING>, propertyName :: STRING, propertyTypes :: LIST<STRING>, mandatory :: BOOLEAN)` | `nodeType`, `nodeLabels`, `propertyName`, `propertyTypes`, `mandatory` | One row per label set and property. `nodeType` is the sorted label set, `:A:B`; `propertyTypes` are `valueType()` names; `mandatory` is `true` when every node of the label set has the key. A label set with no properties gives one row with `propertyName` `null`             |
| `db.schema.relTypeProperties() :: (relType :: STRING, propertyName :: STRING, propertyTypes :: LIST<STRING>, mandatory :: BOOLEAN)`                               | `relType`, `propertyName`, `propertyTypes`, `mandatory`                | `relType` is written `[:TYPE]`; same rules as `nodeTypeProperties`                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `db.schema.visualization(options = true :: BOOLEAN\|MAP) :: (nodes :: LIST<NODE>, relationships :: LIST<RELATIONSHIP>)`                                           | `nodes`, `relationships`                                               | One row: a virtual node per label, with `name`, `indexes` and `constraints`, and a virtual relationship per start label, type and end label, with `name`. `false` leaves out combinations that no relationship in the data has; `null` gives no row. An empty store gives no row |
| `db.createLabel(newLabel :: STRING)`                                                                                                                              | —                                                                      | Returns no rows; `db.labels()` lists the label only once a node carries it                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```cypher run name=node-type-properties
CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties()
YIELD nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes, mandatory
RETURN nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes, mandatory ORDER BY nodeType, propertyName
```

```table
| nodeType   | propertyName | propertyTypes       | mandatory |
|------------|--------------|---------------------|-----------|
| ":Person"  | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
| ":Person"  | "role"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
| ":Project" | "language"   | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
| ":Project" | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
4 rows
```

```cypher run name=rel-type-properties
CALL db.schema.relTypeProperties()
YIELD relType, propertyName, propertyTypes, mandatory
RETURN relType, propertyName, propertyTypes, mandatory ORDER BY relType
```

```table
| "[:MAINTAINS]" | null         | []                   | false     |
| "[:WORKS_ON]"  | "since"      | ["INTEGER NOT NULL"] | true      |
3 rows
```

```cypher run name=visualization
CALL db.schema.visualization() YIELD nodes, relationships
```

- [Search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/): the `SEARCH` clause that replaces the index query procedures.
- [Model an ontology](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/ontology/): the ontology procedures in a task.
