properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
CALL <name>([<argument>, …]) [YIELD <column> [AS <alias>], … [WHERE <predicate>]] [<more clauses>]
CALL <name>([<argument>, …])                -- standalone: every column, as rows
CALL <name>([<argument>, …]) YIELD *        -- standalone only: every column
SHOW PROCEDURES [YIELD <column>, …] [WHERE <predicate>] [RETURN …]
```

| Rule                         | Detail                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Optional arguments           | A parameter written `name = <default>` in the signature may be left out                                                                                                                                                               |
| `YIELD *`                    | Standalone `CALL` only; in a longer statement it fails with `syntax error: UnexpectedSyntax: YIELD * is not allowed in in-query CALL`, and the columns are named instead                                                              |
| Wrong arity                  | `syntax error: InvalidNumberOfArguments: <name> expected <n>, got <m>`                                                                                                                                                                |
| Unknown or catalog-only name | `syntax error: ProcedureNotFound: <name>`                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Deprecated procedures        | Of the callable procedures, the four index query procedures; under `EXPLAIN` a call raises notification `01N01` with ``Use the `SEARCH` clause instead.`` ([notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/notifications/)) |
| `SHOW PROCEDURES` columns    | `name`, `description`, `mode`, `worksOnSystem`, `signature`, `argumentDescription`, `returnDescription`, `admin`, `option`, `isDeprecated`, `deprecatedBy`                                                                            |
| Extensions                   | An extension adds no procedure: it is a `relate run` command that reaches the store over MCP stdio ([write an extension](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/extensions/write-an-extension/))                                             |

properties.heading: Transaction metadata
properties.text:
| Signature                               | `YIELD` columns | Notes                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tx.setMetaData(metadata :: MAP)`       | —               | Accepts a map and returns no rows                                             |
| `tx.getMetaData() :: (metadata :: MAP)` | `metadata`      | Returns `{source: "cip230"}`; a map set with `tx.setMetaData` is not returned |

properties.heading: Reading clauses
properties.text: Reading clauses find rows and shape them. `MATCH` and `OPTIONAL MATCH` bind variables from patterns, `WHERE` filters, `WITH` and `RETURN` project, `ORDER BY`, `SKIP` and `LIMIT` sort and page, and `UNWIND` turns a list into rows. relate runs them with Cypher 25 semantics by default, and also accepts the [GQL](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#gql) spellings `FOR`, `LET` and `FILTER`. A [statement](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#statement) that only reads is a [query](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#query); the pattern syntax inside `MATCH` is on the [patterns](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/patterns/) page.

properties.heading: Clauses
properties.text:
| Clause           | Takes                             | Produces                                                                            | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `MATCH`          | One or more patterns              | One row per way the patterns match; no match, no rows                               | Comma-separated patterns form a cartesian product, joined on shared variables. Within one `MATCH`, each relationship is matched at most once per row                                                                                                         |
| `OPTIONAL MATCH` | One or more patterns              | The input row with the new variables bound, or bound to `null` when nothing matches | Its `WHERE` filters the optional part only; a row whose optional part fails the filter is kept with `null`s                                                                                                                                                  |
| `WHERE`          | A predicate                       | The rows where it is `true`                                                         | A row where the predicate is `null` is dropped, the same as `false`. Follows `MATCH`, `OPTIONAL MATCH` or `WITH`                                                                                                                                             |
| `WITH`           | Projection items                  | A new row per input row, holding only the projected variables                       | Every expression needs `AS`; a bare variable does not. Variables not projected go out of scope                                                                                                                                                               |
| `RETURN`         | Projection items                  | The result columns                                                                  | A column without `AS` is named after its expression text, such as `p.name`. Two columns with one name fail                                                                                                                                                   |
| `ORDER BY`       | Sort keys                         | The rows sorted                                                                     | `ASC` is the default. After `DISTINCT` or an aggregation, a sort key can use the projected values, the projected expressions, and aggregates over the group; other row variables are out of scope. Also a clause of its own between other clauses, as in GQL |
| `SKIP`, `OFFSET` | A non-negative integer            | All but the first `n` rows                                                          | `OFFSET` is the GQL spelling of `SKIP`. Also a clause of its own between other clauses, as in GQL                                                                                                                                                            |
| `LIMIT`          | A non-negative integer            | At most `n` rows                                                                    | `LIMIT 0` returns no rows. Also a clause of its own between other clauses, as in GQL                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `UNWIND`         | A list and a variable name        | One row per element                                                                 | `[]` and `null` give no rows; a value that is not a list gives one row                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `FOR`            | A variable name and a list        | The same rows as `UNWIND`                                                           | GQL spelling; the variable comes first. `FOR <list> AS <variable>` is a parse error. The CLI accepts it; the WebAssembly build the cells on this page use does not ([example](#examples))                                                                    |
| `LET`            | `<variable> = <expression>` pairs | The input row with new variables                                                    | A pair cannot refer to another pair of the same `LET`; a second `LET` can refer to the first                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `FILTER`         | A predicate                       | The rows where it is `true`                                                         | A clause of its own; `WHERE` after it is optional                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                 | Cause                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax error: NoExpressionAlias: expressions in WITH must be aliased with AS`          | A `WITH` item that is an expression has no `AS`                                                                                                                           |
| `syntax error: ColumnNameConflict: multiple result columns with the same name '<name>'` | Two `RETURN` items share a name                                                                                                                                           |
| `syntax error: UndefinedVariable: variable '<name>' not defined`                        | The variable is out of scope: not projected by the previous `WITH`, or a row variable used in `ORDER BY` after `RETURN DISTINCT` or an aggregation without being returned |
| `syntax error: parse error: expected binding variable in FOR, got "<token>"`            | `FOR` written in the `UNWIND` order                                                                                                                                       |

Under the CLI each of these exits with code 6; the [exit code table](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/exit-codes-and-errors/) lists the rest.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store, starting from the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

`OPTIONAL MATCH` keeps Noor, who works on no project, and its `WHERE` drops only Grace's 2022 match:

```cypher run name=optional-match
MATCH (p:Person)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(r:Project) WHERE w.since >= 2023
RETURN p.name AS person, r.name AS project
ORDER BY person, project
```

```table
| person  | project  |
|---------|----------|
| "Ada"   | "relate" |
| "Grace" | "relate" |
| "Noor"  | null     |
3 rows
```

Within one `MATCH`, the two `WORKS_ON` relationships must differ, so nobody is paired with themselves:

```cypher run name=coworkers
MATCH (a:Person)-[:WORKS_ON]->(:Project)<-[:WORKS_ON]-(b:Person)
RETURN a.name AS person, b.name AS coworker
ORDER BY person
```

```table
| person  | coworker |
|---------|----------|
| "Ada"   | "Grace"  |
| "Grace" | "Ada"    |
2 rows
```

No person has a `team` property, so both comparisons are `null` for every row, and `WHERE` keeps none:

```cypher run name=null-predicate
MATCH (p:Person)
WHERE p.team = 'core' OR p.team <> 'core'
RETURN count(p) AS people
```

```table
| people |
|--------|
| 0      |
1 row
```

A descending sort puts `null` first:

```cypher run name=order-nulls
MATCH (p:Person)
OPTIONAL MATCH (p)-[w:WORKS_ON]->()
RETURN p.name AS person, w.since AS since
ORDER BY since DESC
```

```table
| person  | since |
|---------|-------|
| "Noor"  | null  |
| "Ada"   | 2024  |
| "Grace" | 2023  |
| "Grace" | 2022  |
4 rows
```

Values of different types sort by type first:

```cypher run name=order-types
UNWIND [3, null, 'relate', 2.5, true, [1], {k: 1}] AS value
RETURN value
ORDER BY value
```

```table
| value    |
|----------|
| {k: 1}   |
| [1]      |
| "relate" |
| true     |
| 2.5      |
| 3        |
| null     |
7 rows
```

`WITH` aggregates, and its `WHERE` filters on the aggregate:

```cypher run name=with-where
MATCH (p:Person)
WITH p.role AS role, count(*) AS people
WHERE people > 1
RETURN role, people
```

```table
| role       | people |
|------------|--------|
| "engineer" | 2      |
1 row
```

`SKIP` and `LIMIT` page through a sorted result; a float is refused:

```cypher run name=skip-limit
MATCH (p:Person)
RETURN p.name AS name
ORDER BY name
SKIP 1 LIMIT 1
```

```table
| name    |
|---------|
| "Grace" |
1 row
```

```cypher run name=skip-float expect=error
MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name ORDER BY name SKIP 1.0
```

```table
error: syntax error: InvalidArgumentType: SKIP requires an integer value, got FLOAT
```

`ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` also stand as clauses of their own, between `MATCH` and `RETURN`:

```cypher run name=order-limit-clauses
MATCH (p:Person)
ORDER BY p.name DESC
LIMIT 2
RETURN p.name AS name
```

```table
| name    |
|---------|
| "Noor"  |
| "Grace" |
2 rows
```

`UNWIND` gives one row per element: the empty list and `null` give none, and a string gives one:

```cypher run name=unwind
UNWIND [[1, 2], [], null, 'solo'] AS item
UNWIND item AS value
RETURN value
```

```table
| value  |
|--------|
| 1      |
| 2      |
| "solo" |
3 rows
```

`LET` and `FILTER` in one pipeline:

```cypher run name=let-filter
UNWIND ['Ada', 'Noor'] AS name
MATCH (p:Person {name: name})
LET projects = COUNT { (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->() }
FILTER projects > 0
RETURN p.name AS name, projects
```

```table
| name  | projects |
|-------|----------|
| "Ada" | 1        |
1 row
```

`FOR` on the CLI. The WebAssembly build the cells on this page run on rejects it with `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'gql-for' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=gql-for`; the CLI accepts it without an opt-in, and its `RELATE_PREVIEW` has no `gql-for` name.

```bash verify
relate --mode table "FOR name IN ['Ada', 'Grace', null] RETURN name"
```

```text
+---------+
| name    |
+---------+
| "Ada"   |
| "Grace" |
| <null>  |
+---------+
```

properties.heading: Ordering and nulls
properties.text:
| Rule                        | Behavior                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `null` in an ascending sort | Last                                                                                                                                    |
| `null` in a descending sort | First                                                                                                                                   |
| Mixed types, ascending      | Maps, then nodes, relationships, lists, paths, vectors, points, temporal values, durations, strings, booleans, numbers, and `null` last |
| Integers and floats         | Compared as numbers: `1 < 2.5 < 3`                                                                                                      |
| Equal keys                  | No defined order between them; a second key makes the order stable                                                                      |
| `ORDER BY` in a `UNION`     | Sorts the last branch only ([composing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/composing-clauses/#union))                    |

properties.heading: Projection
properties.text:
| Form                               | Result                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `RETURN *`, `WITH *`               | Every variable in scope, as one column each                                                    |
| `RETURN DISTINCT`, `WITH DISTINCT` | Duplicate rows removed                                                                         |
| `RETURN ALL`                       | Every row kept; the default, written out                                                       |
| Aggregate beside plain items       | Plain items are the grouping keys: `RETURN p.role AS role, count(*) AS people` counts per role |
| `GROUP BY <key>, …`                | The listed aliases are the grouping keys, in place of the inferred ones                        |
| `GROUP BY ()`                      | One group: aggregates over every row                                                           |
| `GROUP BY ALL`                     | Every plain item is a key, as without `GROUP BY`                                               |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Patterns](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/patterns/): node, relationship and path patterns, label expressions, and quantifiers.
- [Composing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/composing-clauses/): `UNION`, `CALL` subqueries and subquery expressions.
- [Writing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/writing-clauses/): `CREATE`, `MERGE`, `SET` and `DELETE`.
- [Expressions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/expressions/): operators, `CASE`, comprehensions, and precedence.
- [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/): the Neo4j habits that fail in relate.

properties.heading: SKIP and LIMIT values
properties.text:
The value is an integer expression that does not depend on the row: a literal, a parameter, or arithmetic on them.

| Value                             | Result                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A non-negative integer            | Skips or keeps that many rows                                                                                   |
| `0`                               | `SKIP 0` keeps every row; `LIMIT 0` returns none                                                                |
| A float literal                   | `syntax error: InvalidArgumentType: SKIP requires an integer value, got FLOAT` (the `LIMIT` form names `LIMIT`) |
| A negative integer                | `syntax error: NegativeIntegerArgument: LIMIT must not be negative` (the `SKIP` form names `SKIP`)              |
| `null`, or a float at run time    | `type error: InvalidArgumentType: SKIP/LIMIT must be an integer`                                                |
| An expression over a row variable | `syntax error: NonConstantExpression: LIMIT must be a non-negative integer constant`                            |
| A parameter not supplied          | `semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): <names>`                                              |

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
[OPTIONAL] MATCH <pattern> [, <pattern> …] [WHERE <predicate>]

WITH [DISTINCT] <expression> AS <alias> [, …] | *
  [GROUP BY <key>, … | GROUP BY () | GROUP BY ALL]
  [ORDER BY <expression> [ASC | ASCENDING | DESC | DESCENDING] [, …]]
  [SKIP <n> | OFFSET <n>] [LIMIT <n>]
  [WHERE <predicate>]

UNWIND <list> AS <variable>
FOR <variable> IN <list>
LET <variable> = <expression> [, …]
FILTER [WHERE] <predicate>

RETURN [DISTINCT | ALL] <expression> [AS <alias>] [, …] | *
  [GROUP BY <key>, … | GROUP BY () | GROUP BY ALL]
  [ORDER BY <expression> [ASC | ASCENDING | DESC | DESCENDING] [, …]]
  [SKIP <n> | OFFSET <n>] [LIMIT <n>]

ORDER BY <expression> [ASC | ASCENDING | DESC | DESCENDING] [, …]
SKIP <n> | OFFSET <n>
LIMIT <n>
```

properties.heading: WHERE predicates
properties.text:
| Predicate          | Form                                                   | `true` when                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Comparison         | `=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`                        | The comparison holds; a comparison with `null` is `null`                                                                                   |
| Boolean            | `AND`, `OR`, `XOR`, `NOT`                              | Three-valued: `null AND false` is `false`, `null OR true` is `true`, otherwise `null` propagates                                           |
| String             | `STARTS WITH`, `ENDS WITH`, `CONTAINS`                 | Case-sensitive match on strings                                                                                                            |
| Regular expression | `<string> =~ '<regex>'`                                | The whole string matches                                                                                                                   |
| Null test          | `IS NULL`, `IS NOT NULL`                               | The value is (or is not) `null`                                                                                                            |
| List membership    | `<value> IN <list>`                                    | The list holds the value                                                                                                                   |
| Label test         | `n:Person`, `n:Person\|Project`, `n IS LABELED Person` | The node carries the labels; the [label expression](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/patterns/#label-expressions) operators apply |
| Pattern            | `(p)-[:KNOWS]->()`, `NOT (p)-[:WORKS_ON]->()`          | The pattern has (or has no) match from the bound variables                                                                                 |
| Subquery           | `EXISTS { … }`                                         | The subquery returns a row ([composing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/composing-clauses/#subquery-expressions))        |

Operators beyond these, and their precedence, are on the [expressions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/expressions/) page.

properties.heading: Schema clauses
properties.text: Schema statements manage the indexes, [constraints](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#constraint) and [graph type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#graph-type) of a [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store). An index speeds up lookups and searches; a constraint is a rule every write must satisfy; a graph type declares the node and relationship types of the whole graph and turns each declaration into constraints. Each statement takes effect when it commits. On success, `CREATE` and `DROP` return no rows, and the CLI prints nothing; `SHOW INDEXES` and `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` are how to see what changed.

properties.heading: Constraint violations
properties.text:
A write that breaks a constraint fails, and the statement changes nothing. The message names the constraint and the rule:

| Rule broken                          | Message                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Uniqueness, or a key's uniqueness    | ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `<name>` uniqueness``                |
| Existence, or a key property missing | ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `<name>` requires properties``       |
| Property type                        | ``semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `<name>` property type``             |
| A graph type's implied label         | `ConstraintValidationFailed: node with label <label> must also have label <label>` |

Under the CLI the first three exit with code 6, the implied-label violation with code 1.

properties.heading: Constraints
properties.text:
| Constraint    | `REQUIRE` form                                                         | Entity                                       | `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` `type`                                      | Owns an index |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Uniqueness    | `IS UNIQUE`, `IS NODE UNIQUE`, `IS RELATIONSHIP UNIQUE`                | Node or relationship; one property or a list | `NODE_PROPERTY_UNIQUENESS`, `RELATIONSHIP_PROPERTY_UNIQUENESS` | Yes           |
| Existence     | `IS NOT NULL`                                                          | Node or relationship; one property or a list | `NODE_PROPERTY_EXISTENCE`, `RELATIONSHIP_PROPERTY_EXISTENCE`   | No            |
| Key           | `IS KEY`, `IS NODE KEY`, `IS RELATIONSHIP KEY`                         | Node or relationship; one property or a list | `NODE_KEY`, `RELATIONSHIP_KEY`                                 | Yes           |
| Property type | `IS :: <type>`, `IS TYPED <type>`; a union such as `STRING \| INTEGER` | Node or relationship; one property           | `NODE_PROPERTY_TYPE`, `RELATIONSHIP_PROPERTY_TYPE`             | No            |

| Rule                                                                                  | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No name                                                                               | relate generates one, such as `constraint_unique_Person_name`                                                                                                                                                   |
| `IF NOT EXISTS`                                                                       | No error and no change when a constraint of that name exists                                                                                                                                                    |
| A name another constraint uses                                                        | `semantic error: ConstraintAlreadyExists`                                                                                                                                                                       |
| A name an index uses                                                                  | `semantic error: DuplicatedIndexName`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The same rule under another name                                                      | `semantic error: EquivalentSchemaRuleAlreadyExists`                                                                                                                                                             |
| A uniqueness or key constraint on the label and properties of an existing range index | `semantic error: AlreadyExists: there already exists an index (:<Label> {<property>, …}). A constraint cannot be created until the index has been dropped.` A text index on the same property does not block it |
| More than one property in `IS ::` or `IS TYPED`                                       | `syntax error: InvalidConstraintSyntax: only single property IS TYPED constraints are supported`                                                                                                                |
| Existing data breaks the rule                                                         | The `CREATE CONSTRAINT` fails with the violation message and creates nothing                                                                                                                                    |
| A uniqueness constraint and a missing property                                        | Allowed: uniqueness applies to entities that have the property                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DROP CONSTRAINT`                                                                     | Removes the constraint and the index it owns                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `DROP CONSTRAINT` on a missing name                                                   | `semantic error: ConstraintNotFound`; with `IF EXISTS`, nothing happens and no error is raised                                                                                                                  |
| `DROP CONSTRAINT` on a constraint a graph type created                                | `DependentConstraintManagedIndividually: dependent constraints cannot be dropped` (CLI exit code 1)                                                                                                             |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store, starting from the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

One index of three kinds, then the list:

```cypher run name=create-indexes
CREATE INDEX works_on_since IF NOT EXISTS FOR ()-[w:WORKS_ON]-() ON (w.since);
CREATE TEXT INDEX person_role IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) ON (p.role);
CREATE LOOKUP INDEX node_labels IF NOT EXISTS FOR (n) ON EACH labels(n)
```

```table
(no rows) · indexes added: 3
```

```cypher run name=show-indexes
SHOW INDEXES YIELD name, type, entityType, labelsOrTypes, properties
RETURN name, type, entityType, labelsOrTypes, properties
ORDER BY name
```

```table
| name             | type     | entityType     | labelsOrTypes | properties |
|------------------|----------|----------------|---------------|------------|
| "index_1b9dcc97" | "LOOKUP" | "RELATIONSHIP" | null          | null       |
| "index_460996c0" | "LOOKUP" | "NODE"         | null          | null       |
| "node_labels"    | "LOOKUP" | "NODE"         | null          | null       |
| "person_role"    | "TEXT"   | "NODE"         | ["Person"]    | ["role"]   |
| "works_on_since" | "RANGE"  | "RELATIONSHIP" | ["WORKS_ON"]  | ["since"]  |
5 rows
```

A uniqueness constraint owns an index, so the index cannot be dropped on its own:

```cypher run name=unique-constraint
CREATE CONSTRAINT person_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) REQUIRE p.name IS UNIQUE
```

```table
(no rows) · constraints added: 1
```

```cypher run name=drop-owned-index expect=error
DROP INDEX person_name
```

```table
error: Unable to drop 'person_name': the index belongs to a constraint.
```

A second Ada breaks the constraint, and the write fails:

```cypher run name=violation expect=error
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'designer'})
```

```table
error: semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `person_name` uniqueness
```

A constraint that existing data breaks is not created: two people share the role `engineer`:

```cypher run name=create-violated expect=error
CREATE CONSTRAINT person_role_unique FOR (p:Person) REQUIRE p.role IS UNIQUE
```

```table
error: semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `person_role_unique` uniqueness
```

Constraints listed by filter:

```cypher run name=show-constraints
SHOW UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS YIELD name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, ownedIndex
RETURN name, type, labelsOrTypes, properties, ownedIndex
```

```table
| name          | type                       | labelsOrTypes | properties | ownedIndex    |
|---------------|----------------------------|---------------|------------|---------------|
| "person_name" | "NODE_PROPERTY_UNIQUENESS" | ["Person"]    | ["name"]   | "person_name" |
1 row
```

`DROP CONSTRAINT` removes the constraint and its index; a missing name with `IF EXISTS` is no error:

```cypher run name=drop-constraint
DROP CONSTRAINT person_name;
DROP CONSTRAINT person_name IF EXISTS;
SHOW INDEXES YIELD name RETURN collect(name) AS indexes
```

```table
| indexes                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ["index_1b9dcc97", "index_460996c0", "node_labels", "person_role", "works_on_since"] |
1 row · constraints removed: 1
```

A graph type for the example graph, registered and then made current:

```cypher run name=graph-type
CREATE GRAPH TYPE team {
  (p:Person => {name :: STRING NOT NULL, role :: STRING}),
  (r:Project => {name :: STRING NOT NULL, language :: STRING}),
  (p)-[:WORKS_ON => {since :: INTEGER}]->(r)
};
ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET GRAPH TYPE team;
SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE YIELD specification RETURN specification
```

```table
| specification                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| "{\n  (:`Person` => {`name` :: STRING NOT NULL, `role` :: STRING}),\n  (:`Project` => {`language` :: STRING, `name` :: STRING NOT NULL}),\n  (:`Person` =>)-[:`WORKS_ON` => {`since` :: INTEGER}]->(:`Project` =>)\n}" |
1 row · constraints added: 9
```

A person without a name now fails:

```cypher run name=graph-type-violation expect=error
CREATE (:Person {role: 'engineer'})
```

```table
error: semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: `constraint_238af3a3` requires properties
```

The inferred node schema:

```cypher run name=node-type-properties
CALL db.schema.nodeTypeProperties() YIELD nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes, mandatory
RETURN nodeType, propertyName, propertyTypes, mandatory
ORDER BY nodeType, propertyName
```

```table
| nodeType   | propertyName | propertyTypes       | mandatory |
|------------|--------------|---------------------|-----------|
| ":Person"  | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
| ":Person"  | "role"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
| ":Project" | "language"   | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
| ":Project" | "name"       | ["STRING NOT NULL"] | true      |
4 rows
```

properties.heading: Graph types
properties.text:
A graph type lists node element types, `(:<Label> => {<property> :: <type> [NOT NULL], …})`, and relationship element types, `(:<Label> =>)-[:<TYPE> => {…}]->(:<Label> =>)`. The `=>` (or `IMPLIES`) after a label is required before a property block. A property declaration can end in `IS KEY` or `IS UNIQUE`, and a `CONSTRAINT … REQUIRE …` entry can sit in the list. A graph type is open: nodes with labels it does not declare are accepted.

| Statement                                         | Effect                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE GRAPH TYPE <name> { … }`                  | Registers a named type. It does not apply it. A second `CREATE` with the same name replaces it without an error |
| `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET GRAPH TYPE <name>`  | Makes the named type current; an unknown name fails with `semantic error: GraphTypeNotFound`                    |
| `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE SET { … }`              | Replaces the current type                                                                                       |
| `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE ADD { … }`              | Adds element types                                                                                              |
| `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE ALTER { … }`            | Redefines element types that exist                                                                              |
| `ALTER CURRENT GRAPH TYPE DROP { (:<Label> =>) }` | Removes element types and their constraints                                                                     |
| `SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE`                         | One row, `specification`: the current type as text, `{}` when none is set                                       |
| `SHOW CURRENT GRAPH TYPE AS GRAPH`                | One row with `nodes` and `relationships` lists                                                                  |

Setting a type creates the constraints it implies, which `SHOW CONSTRAINTS` lists under generated names, including `RELATIONSHIP_SOURCE_LABEL` and `RELATIONSHIP_TARGET_LABEL` for a relationship's endpoints. Data that breaks the new type makes the `ALTER` fail with the violation message. Constraints created with `CREATE CONSTRAINT` while a type is current appear in its specification. Optional properties, default values and inheritance between element types are preview features ([Cypher overview](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/overview/#preview-features)).

properties.heading: Indexes
properties.text:
| Kind      | Statement                                                                                              | Entity                                                                                            | Properties                                                | `SHOW INDEXES` `type` |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| Range     | `CREATE INDEX` or `CREATE RANGE INDEX`                                                                 | Node label or [relationship type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type) | One or more                                               | `RANGE`               |
| Text      | `CREATE TEXT INDEX`                                                                                    | Node label or relationship type                                                                   | Exactly one                                               | `TEXT`                |
| Point     | `CREATE POINT INDEX`                                                                                   | Node label or relationship type                                                                   | Exactly one, holding points                               | `POINT`               |
| Lookup    | `CREATE LOOKUP INDEX … ON EACH labels(n)` or `… ON EACH type(r)`                                       | Every node, or every relationship                                                                 | None                                                      | `LOOKUP`              |
| Vector    | `CREATE VECTOR INDEX` ([search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#index-statements))   | Node label or relationship type                                                                   | One, holding vectors, plus `WITH [...]` filter properties | `VECTOR`              |
| Full-text | `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX` ([search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#index-statements)) | Node label or relationship type                                                                   | One or more strings, in `ON EACH [...]`                   | `FULLTEXT`            |

A new store has no indexes. A [point index](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#point-index) narrows distance and bounding-box predicates on `point` values ([geospatial](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/geospatial/)).

| Rule                                                                                               | Behavior                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No name                                                                                            | relate generates one; `SHOW INDEXES` reports it                                                                                                                     |
| `IF NOT EXISTS`                                                                                    | No error and no change when an index of that name exists, even with another definition                                                                              |
| A name another index uses                                                                          | `semantic error: IndexAlreadyExists`                                                                                                                                |
| A name a constraint uses                                                                           | `semantic error: There already exists a constraint called '<name>'.`                                                                                                |
| The same kind, entity and properties under another name, or a constraint already owning that index | `semantic error: EquivalentSchemaRuleAlreadyExists`                                                                                                                 |
| More than one property on a text or point index                                                    | `syntax error: InvalidArguments: this index type requires one property`                                                                                             |
| `OPTIONS {…}`                                                                                      | One key is accepted, `indexConfig`, whose settings depend on the index kind; any other key, `indexProvider` included, fails with `syntax error: InvalidIndexOption` |
| `CREATE BTREE INDEX`                                                                               | `syntax error: parse error: UnsupportedIndexType: BTREE indexes were removed; use RANGE, POINT, TEXT, FULLTEXT, LOOKUP, or VECTOR`                                  |
| `DROP INDEX` on a missing name                                                                     | ``semantic error: NoSuchIndex: `<name>` ``; with `IF EXISTS`, nothing happens and no error is raised                                                                |
| `DROP INDEX` on an index a constraint owns                                                         | `Unable to drop '<name>': the index belongs to a constraint.` (CLI exit code 1)                                                                                     |
| State after `CREATE`                                                                               | `SHOW INDEXES` reports `state` `ONLINE` and `populationPercent` `100.0`                                                                                             |

properties.heading: Schema procedures
properties.text:
| Procedure                                     | Yields                                                                 | Notes                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `db.schema.nodeTypeProperties()`              | `nodeType`, `nodeLabels`, `propertyName`, `propertyTypes`, `mandatory` | Inferred from the stored nodes: one row per label set and property                                                                                                       |
| `db.schema.relTypeProperties()`               | `relType`, `propertyName`, `propertyTypes`, `mandatory`                | The same for relationships                                                                                                                                               |
| `db.schema.visualization([<boolean or map>])` | `nodes`, `relationships`                                               | The argument defaults to `true`. One virtual node per label and one virtual relationship per label-type-label combination; `false` limits it to combinations in the data |
| `db.labels()`                                 | `label`                                                                | The labels in use                                                                                                                                                        |
| `db.relationshipTypes()`                      | `relationshipType`                                                     | The relationship types in use                                                                                                                                            |
| `db.propertyKeys()`                           | `propertyKey`                                                          | The property keys in use                                                                                                                                                 |
| `db.awaitIndexes([<seconds>])`                | Nothing                                                                | Returns when every index is online; the timeout defaults to 300 seconds                                                                                                  |

The [procedures](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/procedures/) page lists the rest.
