properties.heading: Strings
properties.text: A string literal is in single or double quotes. The escapes are `\'`, `\"`, `\\`, `\n`, `\t` and `\uXXXX`. An interpolated literal, `s'…'`, evaluates each `{<expression>}` inside it; `\{` and `\}` are literal braces, and an embedded `null` makes the whole string `null`. `size()` and `char_length()` count Unicode characters, so `size('café')` is `4`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
42  -7  0x1F  0o17  1_000          INTEGER
3.5  .5  6.02e23  Infinity  NaN    FLOAT
'text'  "text"  s'{expr} text'     STRING
true  false                        BOOLEAN
null                               NULL
[1, 2, 3]                          LIST<…>
{name: 'Ada', since: 2024}         MAP
date('2026-11-08')  duration('P1D')  point({x: 1, y: 2})
vector([0.1, 0.2], 2, FLOAT32)  uuid('f066ecfc-5151-4121-8a36-b35e00d72918')
```

properties.heading: Temporal arithmetic
properties.text:
| Expression                                           | Result                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<instant> + <duration>`, `<instant> - <duration>`   | An instant of the same type; a month step clamps to the end of a shorter month (`date('2026-01-31') + duration('P1M')` is `2026-02-28`) |
| `<duration> + <duration>`, `<duration> - <duration>` | A duration                                                                                                                              |
| `<duration> * <number>`, `<duration> / <number>`     | A duration                                                                                                                              |
| `<instant> - <instant>`                              | `type error: - type mismatch`; `duration.between(a, b)` gives the difference                                                            |
| `<instant> < <instant>`                              | Order of two values of the same type; a `DATE` against a `ZONED DATETIME` gives `null`                                                  |

```cypher run name=temporal
RETURN date('2026-01-31') + duration('P1M') AS month_end,
       datetime('2026-11-08T10:00Z') + duration('PT90M') AS later,
       duration.between(date('2026-01-01'), date('2026-11-08')) AS between,
       duration({days: 1, hours: 25}) AS kept_apart, date('2026-11-08').dayOfWeek AS weekday
```

```table
| month_end    | later                  | between  | kept_apart | weekday |
|--------------|------------------------|----------|------------|---------|
| "2026-02-28" | "2026-11-08T11:30:00Z" | "P10M7D" | "P1DT25H"  | 7       |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Temporal types
properties.text:
| Type             | Constructor from a string                                                                | From a map                                                                                          | Components                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DATE`           | `date('2026-11-08')`, `date('2026-W45-7')`, `date('20261108')`                           | `date({year: 2026, month: 11, day: 8})`                                                             | `year`, `quarter`, `month`, `week`, `weekYear`, `day`, `ordinalDay`, `dayOfQuarter`, `dayOfWeek` (also `weekDay`)                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `LOCAL TIME`     | `localtime('10:15:30')`                                                                  | `localtime({hour: 10, minute: 15})`                                                                 | `hour`, `minute`, `second`, `millisecond`, `microsecond`, `nanosecond`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `ZONED TIME`     | `time('10:15:30+01:00')`                                                                 | `time({hour: 10, timezone: '+01:00'})`                                                              | The local time components, `offset`, `offsetMinutes`, `offsetSeconds`, `timezone`                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `LOCAL DATETIME` | `localdatetime('2026-11-08T10:15:30')`                                                   | `localdatetime({year: 2026, month: 11, day: 8, hour: 10})`                                          | The date and time components                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `ZONED DATETIME` | `datetime('2026-11-08T10:15:30+01:00')`, `datetime('2026-11-08T10:15:30[Europe/Paris]')` | `datetime({year: 2026, month: 11, day: 8, timezone: 'Europe/Paris'})`, `datetime({epochMillis: 0})` | The date and time components, `offset`, `offsetMinutes`, `offsetSeconds`, `timezone`, `epochSeconds`, `epochMillis`                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `DURATION`       | `duration('P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.5S')`                                                           | `duration({days: 1, hours: 2})`                                                                     | `years`, `quarters`, `months`, `weeks`, `days`, `hours`, `minutes`, `seconds`, `milliseconds`, `microseconds`, `nanoseconds`; `quartersOfYear`, `monthsOfQuarter`, `monthsOfYear`, `daysOfWeek`, `minutesOfHour`, `secondsOfMinute`, `millisecondsOfSecond`, `microsecondsOfSecond`, `nanosecondsOfSecond` |

A component is read with a dot: `date('2026-11-08').dayOfWeek` is `7`, and `.dayOfQuarter` is `39`. A component the type lacks fails with `type error: no such component '<name>' on a <type> value`, as `date('2026-11-08').hour` does. A duration keeps months, days and seconds apart and never converts between them: `duration({days: 1, hours: 25})` is `P1DT25H`. A plural duration component counts its whole part in that unit, and an `…Of…` component the remainder below the next unit: for `duration('P1Y2M3DT4H5M6.5S')`, `months` is `14` and `monthsOfYear` is `2`, `minutes` is `245` and `minutesOfHour` is `5`. Called with no argument, each temporal constructor returns the current instant; [functions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/functions/#temporal-functions) lists the clock variants.

properties.heading: UUIDs
properties.text:
`uuid('<36-character string>')` parses a UUID and `uuid(<high>, <low>)` builds one from two 64-bit integers. `uuid()` with no argument returns a random UUID, and `randomUUID()` returns one as a `STRING`. On the WASM build, the random forms stop the engine with `time not implemented on this platform`; they run on the CLI and the clients. `toString()` and the output modes print the 36-character form; `uuid.mostSignificantBits()` and `uuid.leastSignificantBits()` return the halves.

```cypher run name=uuids
RETURN uuid('f066ecfc-5151-4121-8a36-b35e00d72918') AS parsed, uuid(0, 1) AS from_halves,
       valueType(uuid(0, 1)) AS type
```

```table
| parsed                                 | from_halves                            | type            |
|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------|
| "f066ecfc-5151-4121-8a36-b35e00d72918" | "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001" | "UUID NOT NULL" |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Value types
properties.text:
The type name is the one `valueType()` returns and the `IS ::` predicate takes ([expressions](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/expressions/#type-predicates)); `valueType()` adds ` NOT NULL` to every value that is not `null`.

| Type             | Literal or constructor                         | Range or form                                                  | Stored as a property                                             |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `INTEGER`        | `42`, `-7`, `0x1F`, `0o17`, `1_000`            | 64-bit signed: `-9223372036854775808` to `9223372036854775807` | Yes                                                              |
| `FLOAT`          | `3.5`, `.5`, `1e3`, `Infinity`, `NaN`          | IEEE 754 64-bit                                                | Yes                                                              |
| `STRING`         | `'…'`, `"…"`, `s'…{expr}…'`                    | Unicode; `size()` counts characters                            | Yes                                                              |
| `BOOLEAN`        | `true`, `false`                                | —                                                              | Yes                                                              |
| `NULL`           | `null`                                         | The absence of a value                                         | No: setting a property to `null` removes it                      |
| `LIST<T>`        | `[1, 2, 3]`                                    | Any values, mixed types allowed                                | Only a list whose elements are one storable type and none `null` |
| `MAP`            | `{key: value}`                                 | String keys                                                    | No                                                               |
| `NODE`           | A pattern variable                             | Labels, properties, and an element id                          | No                                                               |
| `RELATIONSHIP`   | A pattern variable                             | One type, properties, and a start and end node                 | No                                                               |
| `PATH`           | `p = (a)-[r]->(b)`                             | Alternating nodes and relationships                            | No                                                               |
| `DATE`           | `date('2026-11-08')`                           | A calendar date                                                | Yes                                                              |
| `LOCAL TIME`     | `localtime('10:15:30')`                        | A time of day without a zone                                   | Yes                                                              |
| `ZONED TIME`     | `time('10:15:30+01:00')`                       | A time of day with an offset                                   | Yes                                                              |
| `LOCAL DATETIME` | `localdatetime('2026-11-08T10:15:30')`         | A date and time without a zone                                 | Yes                                                              |
| `ZONED DATETIME` | `datetime('2026-11-08T10:15:30Z')`             | A date and time with an offset or a named zone                 | Yes                                                              |
| `DURATION`       | `duration('P1Y2M3DT4H')`                       | Months, days, seconds and nanoseconds, kept apart              | Yes                                                              |
| `POINT`          | `point({x: 1, y: 2})`                          | Two or three coordinates in one coordinate reference system    | Yes                                                              |
| `VECTOR<T>(n)`   | `vector([1, 2, 3], 3, INT8)`                   | `n` coordinates of one numeric type                            | Yes                                                              |
| `UUID`           | `uuid('f066ecfc-5151-4121-8a36-b35e00d72918')` | 128 bits                                                       | Yes                                                              |

```cypher run name=value-types
RETURN valueType(42) AS int, valueType(3.5) AS float, valueType('Ada') AS string,
       valueType(null) AS nothing, valueType([1, 2]) AS list, valueType({k: 1}) AS map,
       valueType(duration('P1D')) AS duration, valueType(vector([1, 2], 2, INT8)) AS vector
```

```table
| int                | float            | string            | nothing | list                              | map            | duration            | vector                                  |
|--------------------|------------------|-------------------|---------|-----------------------------------|----------------|---------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| "INTEGER NOT NULL" | "FLOAT NOT NULL" | "STRING NOT NULL" | "NULL"  | "LIST<INTEGER NOT NULL> NOT NULL" | "MAP NOT NULL" | "DURATION NOT NULL" | "VECTOR<INTEGER8 NOT NULL>(2) NOT NULL" |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Vectors
properties.text:
`vector(<list or string>, <dimensions>, <coordinate type>)` builds a vector. All three arguments are required, the list length must equal the dimensions, and the coordinate type is a bare keyword, not a string.

| Keyword                                | `valueType()` element | Coordinates                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `INT8`, `INTEGER8`                     | `INTEGER8`            | Signed 8-bit; a value outside the range fails with `type error: Overflow`                                                                                                                              |
| `INT16`, `INTEGER16`                   | `INTEGER16`           | Signed 16-bit                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `INT32`, `INTEGER32`                   | `INTEGER32`           | Signed 32-bit                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `INT`, `INT64`, `INTEGER`, `INTEGER64` | `INTEGER`             | Signed 64-bit                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `FLOAT32`                              | `FLOAT32`             | 32-bit float                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `FLOAT`, `FLOAT64`                     | `FLOAT`               | 64-bit float                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `FLOAT16`, `BFLOAT16`                  | —                     | Preview feature `float16-coordinate-types`; off, it fails with `semantic error: SemanticError: preview feature 'float16-coordinate-types' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=float16-coordinate-types` |

| Rule                                   | Detail                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Type name                              | `VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(3) NOT NULL` for `vector([0.1, 0.2, 0.3], 3, FLOAT32)`                                                                                                                  |
| Dimensions                             | The value takes any length the list has, `0` included; a vector index takes `vector.dimensions` from 1 to 4096 ([search](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/search/#vector-index-options)) |
| Length mismatch                        | `type error: vector() dimension does not match list`                                                                                                                                              |
| A float into an integer type           | Truncated: `vector([1.5], 1, INT8)` holds `1`                                                                                                                                                     |
| A `null` coordinate                    | `type error: vector() coordinates must be numbers`                                                                                                                                                |
| A string coordinate type               | `syntax error: parse error: vector() third argument must be a coordinate type keyword`                                                                                                            |
| `size(v)`, `vector_dimension_count(v)` | The dimensions                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `toFloatList(v)`, `toIntegerList(v)`   | The coordinates as a list                                                                                                                                                                         |

```cypher run name=vectors
RETURN vector([1, 2, 3], 3, INT8) AS small, vector('[1.5, 2.5]', 2, FLOAT32) AS from_string,
       valueType(vector([0.1, 0.2], 2, FLOAT32)) AS type, size(vector([1, 2, 3], 3, INT8)) AS dims
```

```table
| small                          | from_string                    | type                                   | dims |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------|------|
| vector([1, 2, 3], 3, INTEGER8) | vector([1.5, 2.5], 2, FLOAT32) | "VECTOR<FLOAT32 NOT NULL>(2) NOT NULL" | 3    |
1 row
```

properties.heading: Writing clauses
properties.text: Writing clauses change the graph: `CREATE` and `INSERT` add nodes and relationships, `MERGE` matches a pattern or creates it, `SET` and `REMOVE` change labels and properties, `DELETE` removes entities, `FOREACH` runs updates once per list element, and `LOAD CSV` reads rows from a local file. Each change lands in the [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) the statement runs against. A statement that writes commits whole, or fails and changes nothing; `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` is the exception, and commits each batch on its own. A write with no `RETURN` returns no rows.

properties.heading: Clauses
properties.text:
| Clause                          | Does                                                                                        | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CREATE`                        | Creates every node and relationship in the pattern that is not a bound variable             | Each relationship needs a direction and exactly one [relationship type](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship-type). A variable bound earlier in the statement cannot be redeclared with labels or properties. A variable created in one `CREATE` cannot be read in the same clause; a second `CREATE` can read it |
| `INSERT`                        | The same as `CREATE`                                                                        | GQL spelling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `MERGE`                         | Matches the whole pattern; when it has no match, creates the whole pattern                  | One pattern per `MERGE`. Properties in the pattern must not be `null`. Relationships need exactly one type; an undirected relationship matches either direction and is created left to right                                                                                                                                           |
| `ON CREATE SET`                 | Runs its items only on a row where `MERGE` created the pattern                              | Same items as `SET`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ON MATCH SET`                  | Runs its items only on a row where `MERGE` matched                                          | Same items as `SET`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `SET n.key = v`                 | Sets one [property](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#property)                  | `null` removes the property                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SET n[expr] = v`               | Sets the property the string expression names                                               | A dynamic key                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `SET n = map`                   | Replaces every property with the map's entries                                              | Another node or relationship in place of the map copies its properties; labels are unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `SET n += map`                  | Adds or overwrites the map's keys and keeps the rest                                        | A `null` value in the map removes that key                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `SET n:Label`, `SET n IS Label` | Adds labels                                                                                 | `$(<expression>)` takes a string or a list of strings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `REMOVE`                        | Removes properties or labels                                                                | Removing what is absent is not an error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `DELETE`                        | Deletes relationships, nodes with no relationships, or a path's relationships and nodes     | A node that still has relationships fails the statement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `DETACH DELETE`                 | Deletes nodes and their relationships                                                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `NODETACH DELETE`               | The same as `DELETE`                                                                        | GQL spelling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `FOREACH`                       | Runs its update clauses once per element of the list                                        | Only update clauses inside (`CREATE`, `MERGE`, `SET`, `REMOVE`, `DELETE`, `FOREACH`); a `null` list runs nothing. Variables bound inside stay inside                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `LOAD CSV`                      | One row per CSV record: a list of strings, or with `WITH HEADERS` a map keyed by the header | Local files only, under the directory `--load-csv-dir` allows; denied by default. Every value is a string. The [CSV guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/import-csv/) has the file policy, quoting, and size limit                                                                                                            |
| `FINISH`                        | Ends the statement with no result columns                                                   | For a statement run only for its writes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                  | CLI exit code | Cause                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax error: RequiresDirectedRelationship: CREATE relationships must have a direction`                 | 6             | A `CREATE` relationship written `-[:TYPE]-`                                                                                                   |
| `syntax error: NoSingleRelationshipType: CREATE relationships must have exactly one type`                | 6             | No type, or `:A\|B`; the `MERGE` form names `MERGE`                                                                                           |
| `syntax error: CreatingVarLength: variable length relationships cannot be used in CREATE`                | 6             | A variable-length or quantified relationship in `CREATE`; the `MERGE` form names `MERGE`                                                      |
| `syntax error: SyntaxError: Entity, '<name>', cannot be created and referenced in the same clause`       | 6             | `CREATE (a {…}), (b {name: a.name})`, or a `MERGE` whose properties read the entity it merges: `MERGE (p:Person {name: 'Ida', nick: p.name})` |
| `syntax error: VariableAlreadyBound: variable '<name>' already declared`                                 | 6             | `MATCH (a) CREATE (a:Person)`                                                                                                                 |
| `type error: InvalidPropertyType`                                                                        | 6             | A map, a mixed list or a list holding `null` as a property value                                                                              |
| `syntax error: InvalidClauseComposition: invalid FOREACH: invalid use of MATCH inside 'FOREACH'`         | 6             | A reading clause inside `FOREACH`                                                                                                             |
| `syntax error: WriteBeforeCallInTransactions: a write cannot precede CALL IN TRANSACTIONS`               | 6             | A write, or `LOAD CSV`, before `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` in the same statement                                                             |
| `syntax error: parse error: MERGE requires exactly one pattern path at line 0, col 0`                    | 6             | Two comma-separated patterns in one `MERGE`                                                                                                   |
| `MergeReadOwnWrites: cannot MERGE with null properties`                                                  | 1             | A `MERGE` pattern property that is `null`                                                                                                     |
| `ConstraintVerificationFailed: DeleteConnectedNode: Cannot delete node with relationships unless DETACH` | 1             | `DELETE` or `NODETACH DELETE` on a node with relationships                                                                                    |
| `DeletedEntityAccess: cannot access properties of a deleted node`                                        | 1             | A property read after `DELETE` in the same statement                                                                                          |
| `LOAD CSV file unavailable`                                                                              | 1             | The file is outside the allowed directory, missing, a URL, or no directory is allowed                                                         |
| `semantic error: ConstraintValidationFailed: <constraint> <rule>`                                        | 6             | The write breaks a constraint ([schema clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/schema-clauses/#constraint-violations))             |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: …`                                                       | 6             | The store is open read-only ([errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-write-on-read-only))                                  |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
The cells run in page order on one in-memory store. Each one writes, and says what before it runs. First, the shared example graph:

```cypher run name=seed
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

`CREATE` adds a person, a project and the relationship between them, and returns them:

```cypher run name=create
CREATE (lin:Person {name: 'Lin', role: 'engineer'})-[w:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(docs:Project {name: 'relate-docs', language: 'Markdown'})
RETURN lin.name AS person, type(w) AS type, docs.name AS project
```

```table
| person | type       | project       |
|--------|------------|---------------|
| "Lin"  | "WORKS_ON" | "relate-docs" |
1 row · nodes created: 2, relationships created: 1, properties set: 5, labels added: 2
```

A relationship in `CREATE` needs a direction:

```cypher run name=create-undirected expect=error
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Kim'})-[:KNOWS]-(:Person {name: 'Sam'})
```

```table
error: syntax error: RequiresDirectedRelationship: CREATE relationships must have a direction
```

`MERGE` finds Ada, so only `ON MATCH SET` runs and sets `seen`:

```cypher run name=merge-node
MERGE (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})
  ON CREATE SET p.created = true
  ON MATCH SET p.seen = true
RETURN p.name AS name, p.created AS created, p.seen AS seen
```

```table
| name  | created | seen |
|-------|---------|------|
| "Ada" | null    | true |
1 row · properties set: 1
```

Merging a relationship between existing nodes starts by matching both ends. This creates Ada's `WORKS_ON` to the TCK project:

```cypher run name=merge-relationship
MATCH (a:Person {name: 'Ada'}), (r:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck'})
MERGE (a)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(r)
  ON CREATE SET w.since = 2026
RETURN w.since AS since
```

```table
| since |
|-------|
| 2026  |
1 row · relationships created: 1, properties set: 1
```

`MERGE` on a whole pattern creates the whole pattern when any part is missing. Zed does not exist, so this creates Zed, the relationship, and a second Grace:

```cypher run name=merge-whole-pattern
MERGE (:Person {name: 'Zed'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person {name: 'Grace'});
MATCH (g:Person {name: 'Grace'}) RETURN count(g) AS graces
```

```table
| graces |
|--------|
| 2      |
1 row · nodes created: 2, relationships created: 1, properties set: 2, labels added: 2
```

A `null` property in a `MERGE` pattern fails:

```cypher run name=merge-null expect=error
MERGE (p:Person {name: null}) RETURN p
```

```table
error: MergeReadOwnWrites: cannot MERGE with null properties
```

`DETACH DELETE` removes Zed, the second Grace and the relationship between them:

```cypher run name=detach-delete
MATCH (z:Person {name: 'Zed'})-[:KNOWS]->(g:Person)
DETACH DELETE z, g
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes deleted: 2, relationships deleted: 1
```

`SET` with `+=` adds a key, `:Lead` adds a label, and `null` removes Ada's `role` and the `seen` flag:

```cypher run name=set-forms
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})
SET p += {level: 3, seen: null}, p:Lead, p.role = null
RETURN labels(p) AS labels, properties(p) AS props
```

```table
| labels             | props                   |
|--------------------|-------------------------|
| ["Person", "Lead"] | {level: 3, name: "Ada"} |
1 row · properties set: 3, labels added: 1
```

`SET` with `=` replaces every property and keeps the labels:

```cypher run name=set-replace
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})
SET p = {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}
RETURN labels(p) AS labels, properties(p) AS props
```

```table
| labels             | props                           |
|--------------------|---------------------------------|
| ["Person", "Lead"] | {name: "Ada", role: "engineer"} |
1 row · properties set: 3
```

A list property holds values of one type:

```cypher run name=property-type expect=error
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'}) SET p.tags = ['rust', 1]
```

```table
error: type error: InvalidPropertyType
```

`REMOVE` takes the label back off:

```cypher run name=remove
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Ada'})
REMOVE p:Lead
RETURN labels(p) AS labels
```

```table
| labels     |
|------------|
| ["Person"] |
1 row · labels removed: 1
```

`DELETE` refuses a node that still has relationships:

```cypher run name=delete-connected expect=error
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Noor'}) DELETE p
```

```table
error: ConstraintVerificationFailed: DeleteConnectedNode: Cannot delete node with relationships unless DETACH
```

`FOREACH` creates two people who work on relate, one per list element:

```cypher run name=foreach
MATCH (r:Project {name: 'relate'})
FOREACH (name IN ['Kim', 'Sam'] |
  CREATE (:Person {name: name, role: 'engineer'})-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2026}]->(r))
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 2, relationships created: 2, properties set: 6, labels added: 2
```

`FINISH` ends a statement that only writes. This removes the two again:

```cypher run name=finish
MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name IN ['Kim', 'Sam']
DETACH DELETE p
FINISH
```

```table
(no rows)
```

`LOAD CSV` reads files from disk, which the in-browser cells cannot reach, so its examples run on the CLI. This setup step writes a file into a directory named `import`:

```bash verify
mkdir import
printf 'name;role\nKim;engineer\nSam;maintainer\n' > import/people.csv
```

`WITH HEADERS` makes each record a map, and `FIELDTERMINATOR` names the separator. No `--database` means an in-memory store, so nothing is kept:

```bash verify
relate --load-csv-dir ./import --mode table "LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS FROM 'people.csv' AS row FIELDTERMINATOR ';' RETURN row.name AS name, row.role AS role"
```

```text
+-------+--------------+
| name  | role         |
+-------+--------------+
| "Kim" | "engineer"   |
| "Sam" | "maintainer" |
+-------+--------------+
```

`LOAD CSV` counts as a write before `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS`, so the batched form fails before it runs:

```bash verify
relate --load-csv-dir ./import --mode table "LOAD CSV WITH HEADERS FROM 'people.csv' AS row FIELDTERMINATOR ';' CALL (row) { CREATE (:Person {name: row.name}) } IN TRANSACTIONS OF 1 ROWS"
```

```text
syntax error: WriteBeforeCallInTransactions: a write cannot precede CALL IN TRANSACTIONS
```

properties.heading: Property values
properties.text:
A property holds a scalar, a temporal or spatial value, a vector, or a list of one of those types. The [types and values](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/types-and-values/) page lists them.

| Value set                                        | Result                            |
| ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `null`                                           | Removes the property              |
| A list of one type, such as `['rust', 'cypher']` | Stored                            |
| A list that mixes types, such as `['rust', 1]`   | `type error: InvalidPropertyType` |
| A list holding `null`                            | `type error: InvalidPropertyType` |
| A map                                            | `type error: InvalidPropertyType` |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Import a CSV](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/cypher/import-csv/): the `LOAD CSV` file policy, type conversion, and size limit.
- [Schema clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/schema-clauses/): the constraints a write must satisfy.
- [Composing clauses](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/composing-clauses/#call-subqueries): `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` for batched writes.
- [Types and values](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/types-and-values/): the values a property holds.
- [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/): every message with its exit code and remedy.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
CREATE <pattern> [, <pattern> …]
INSERT <pattern> [, <pattern> …]

MERGE <pattern>
  [ON CREATE SET <set item> [, …]]
  [ON MATCH SET <set item> [, …]]

SET <set item> [, …]
  <set item> = <variable>.<key> = <expression>
             | <variable>[<key expression>] = <expression>
             | <variable> = <map or entity>
             | <variable> += <map or entity>
             | <variable>:<Label>[:<Label> …]
             | <variable> IS <Label>
             | <variable>:$(<expression>)

REMOVE <variable>.<key> | <variable>[<key expression>] | <variable>:<Label>[:<Label> …] | <variable>:$(<expression>) [, …]

[DETACH | NODETACH] DELETE <expression> [, …]

FOREACH (<variable> IN <list> | <update clause> [<update clause> …])

LOAD CSV [WITH HEADERS] FROM <file> AS <variable> [FIELDTERMINATOR <character>]

FINISH
```

properties.heading: What a write returns
properties.text:
| Situation                | Result                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No `RETURN`              | No rows. The CLI prints nothing for it                                                                                                                                             |
| `RETURN` after the write | The rows, with the written values; a created node already has its [element id](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#element-id)                                            |
| Nothing changed          | No rows; the CLI prints `note: write statement changed nothing; the graph is unchanged` on stderr                                                                                  |
| Counters                 | The cells on this page show the counters the WebAssembly envelope carries (`nodes created`, `properties set` and the rest), except after `FINISH`; the CLI's envelope carries none |
| A failure                | The statement changes nothing                                                                                                                                                      |

Reading a deleted entity's properties later in the same statement fails; a value projected with `WITH` before the `DELETE` stays readable.

properties.heading: The docs graph
properties.text: The relate documentation is also published as a graph. Every page, heading, code example, glossary term, CLI command and flag, cookbook recipe, capability and problem is a [node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node), and the links between pages, the prerequisites, the terms a page uses and the flags it documents are [relationships](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#relationship). The build writes the graph from the same files as the pages, so it says what the pages say, at the version in the page header. It ships as a Cypher seed script, as JSON and, from launch, as a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store); the cookbook recipe [Turn a question into the relate docs you need](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/query-the-relate-docs/) searches it. The view on this page draws its pages, grouped by section, below the tables of its labels and relationship types.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
Over the store, or the seed script replayed into an empty one, these statements read the graph. Their results change as the pages do.

The pages that link to the MCP server reference:

```cypher
MATCH (p:Page)-[:LINKS_TO]->(:Page {id: 'reference/server/mcp'})
RETURN DISTINCT p.id AS page, p.section AS section ORDER BY page
```

The glossary terms the most pages use:

```cypher
MATCH (:Page)-[:USES_TERM]->(t:Term)
RETURN t.term AS term, count(*) AS pages ORDER BY pages DESC, term LIMIT 5
```

The chains of prerequisites that lead to a page:

```cypher
MATCH path = (:Page)-[:PREREQUISITE_OF*1..]->(:Page {id: 'guides/agents/connect-over-mcp'})
RETURN [n IN nodes(path) | n.id] AS chain ORDER BY length(path) DESC
```

properties.heading: Files
properties.text:
**Seed script.** `/docs/graph.cypher` is Cypher for an empty store: a comment header with the verified version, the node and relationship counts and the schema; a uniqueness constraint per label; `UNWIND` statements of up to 500 rows that create the nodes, then the relationships; the statements that set the section vectors; then the three indexes. Its header names the command that builds a new store from it, `relate query --database ./relate-docs.rl < graph.cypher`.

**JSON.** `/docs/graph.json` holds `format` (1), `kind` (`documentation`), `verified`, `seed` (the seed script's URL), `embeddings` (the label, property, index, dimension, similarity and model of the vectors, which it does not carry), then `nodes`, each with `id` (`Label:id`), `labels` and `properties`, and `relationships`, each with `type`, `start`, `end` and `properties`. It carries every section's text and every example's code, so it runs to several megabytes.

**relate store.** `/docs/relate-docs.rl` is the seed script built into a [single-file store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#single-file-store) by the relate CLI, with its SHA-256 beside it. Neither URL is served yet: the store is built and served once the deploy workflows install relate. `--load` reads it into an [in-memory store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#in-memory-store), which is read-only.

**Per page.** Every published page has `/docs/<page>.graph.md`, a markdown list of its neighborhood under the headings Prerequisites, Prerequisite of, Related, Links to, Linked from, Terms, Sections, Examples, and CLI commands and flags.

**The view's data.** `/docs/graph-view.json` is what the view on this page draws: the pages, terms, capabilities, problems, recipes, commands, flags and surfaces, each with its title, description, link and position, and the relationships between them. It leaves out sections and examples, and it is shaped for this page; the seed script and `graph.json` are the complete forms.

properties.heading: Node labels
properties.text:
A property whose value would be null is left out, as Cypher stores it. Section `text` and Example code are quoted from the pages: reference text, not instructions.

| Label            | One per                                                                                       | Properties                                                                                                |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Page`           | Docs page, planned pages included (`status` is `planned` and there is no `url`)               | `id`, `url`, `md_url`, `title`, `description`, `type`, `section`, `status`, `since`, `verified`, `tokens` |
| `Section`        | H2 and H3 of a published page, plus one at level 1 for the text before the first of them      | `id`, `page`, `anchor`, `heading`, `level`, `position`, `url`, `text`, `length`, `embedding`              |
| `Example`        | Code block the page's markdown twin carries; a recorded result and a diagram are not examples | `id`, `page`, `section`, `position`, `lang`, `first_line`, `title`, `runnable`, `cell`                    |
| `Term`           | Glossary term                                                                                 | `id`, `term`, `short`, `context`, `see`, `url`                                                            |
| `Surface`        | Front door, such as `cli`, `python` or `mcp`                                                  | `id`                                                                                                      |
| `CookbookRecipe` | Cookbook recipe                                                                               | `id`, `title`, `summary`, `url`, `md_url`                                                                 |
| `Command`        | CLI command                                                                                   | `id`, `word`, `synopsis`, `disputed`                                                                      |
| `Flag`           | CLI flag, global or of one command                                                            | `id`, `flag`, `names`, `command`, `value`, `disputed`                                                     |
| `Index`          | `llms.txt`, and the docs landing page                                                         | `id`, `url`, `title`                                                                                      |
| `Capability`     | Entry of the [capability catalog](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/)  | `id`, `title`, `problem`, `capability`, `url`, `schema_url`, `verify`                                     |
| `Problem`        | A capability's problem, and each other way of asking it                                       | `id`, `text`, `kind`                                                                                      |

`embedding` is a `VECTOR<FLOAT32>(384)` from the bge-small-en-v1.5 model. It is set in the seed script and the store, not in the JSON.

properties.heading: Relationship types
properties.text:
| Type                   | From, to                                   | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LINKS_TO {anchor}`    | `Page` to `Page` or `CookbookRecipe`       | A link in the page's body                                                                       |
| `PREREQUISITE_OF`      | `Page` to `Page`                           | The frontmatter `prerequisites`, pointing from the page to read first at the page that needs it |
| `RELATED_TO {anchor}`  | `Page` to `Page` or `CookbookRecipe`       | The frontmatter `related`                                                                       |
| `HAS_SECTION`          | `Page` to `Section`                        | Each section of the page                                                                        |
| `HAS_EXAMPLE`          | `Page` to `Example`                        | Each code example on the page                                                                   |
| `USES_TERM`            | `Page` to `Term`                           | Each glossary term the page marks                                                               |
| `APPLIES_TO`           | `Page` or `Capability` to `Surface`        | The page's frontmatter `surfaces`, or the capability's surfaces                                 |
| `DOCUMENTS`            | `Page` to `Command` or `Flag`              | A command or flag the page names in a shell or config block, or in inline code                  |
| `HAS_FLAG`             | `Command` to `Flag`                        | The command's own flags                                                                         |
| `LISTS`                | `Index` to `Page`                          | The pages `llms.txt` and the landing page list                                                  |
| `SOLVES`               | `Capability` to `Problem`                  | The capability's problem and its other phrasings                                                |
| `CITES {role, anchor}` | `Capability` to `Page`                     | The pages the catalog entry cites                                                               |
| `DEMONSTRATES`         | `CookbookRecipe` to `Capability`           | A recipe that shows the capability                                                              |
| `VERIFIED_BY {cell}`   | `Capability` to `CookbookRecipe` or `Page` | The recorded cell that proves the capability                                                    |
| `HAS_CAPABILITY`       | `Page` to `Capability`                     | The catalog page to each of its entries                                                         |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Turn a question into the relate docs you need](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/query-the-relate-docs/): vector search and graph traversals over a part of this graph, in the browser.
- [MCP server](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/): relate's own server, which the local form runs.
- [The capability catalog](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/problems-relate-solves/): the source of the `Capability` and `Problem` nodes.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
| Item         | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Seed script  | `https://relatedb.ai/docs/graph.cypher`: Cypher statements that build the graph in an empty store                                                                                                                                                                          |
| JSON         | `https://relatedb.ai/docs/graph.json`: the same nodes and relationships as two arrays, without the section vectors                                                                                                                                                         |
| relate store | `https://relatedb.ai/docs/relate-docs.rl`, with its SHA-256 in `relate-docs.rl.sha256`; not served yet                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Per page     | `https://relatedb.ai/docs/<page>.graph.md`: one page's prerequisites, links both ways, terms, sections, examples and CLI references, as markdown                                                                                                                           |
| Indexes      | Full-text index `docs` on `(:Section)` `heading` and `text`; vector index `docs_vector` on `(:Section)` `embedding`, 384 dimensions, cosine, declaring `page` so a vector search can filter on it (`WHERE s.page IN …`); full-text index `problems` on `(:Problem)` `text` |
| Constraints  | One per label: `id` is unique within the label                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Source       | The docs pages, the glossary, the cookbook's recipes, the CLI facts behind the CLI reference, and the capability catalog                                                                                                                                                   |
| Determinism  | The same source files give the same bytes: nothing reads the clock or git, and every list is sorted by `id`                                                                                                                                                                |

properties.heading: The graph, drawn
properties.text:
The view draws each published page as a node, one cluster and one color per section, with the links and prerequisites between pages. Glossary terms, capabilities and cookbook recipes sit on the ring nearest the pages; CLI commands, flags and surfaces on the middle ring; the problems capabilities solve on the outermost ring. Each ring is off until its toggle is on. Sections and examples are not drawn: there are more than 3,000 of them, past the roughly 1,000 nodes a canvas draws comfortably, and each belongs to a page that is drawn. The build places every page from the list of pages alone, not from the links between them, so the live view draws each page where the picture puts it, and nothing moves when it loads. The links, and the counts of every kind, change with nearly every edit to any page; the view reads them from the data the site is built with.

The live view draws the 142 published pages, one cluster per section: Get started 12, Guides 66, Reference 55, Concepts 9. The picture places them where the live view first draws them. The links and prerequisites between them, and the number of nodes and relationships of each kind, change with nearly every edit, so the live view draws and counts them from the data the site is built with; the seed script's header lists the same counts.

| Label            | In the live view                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Page`           | drawn at first: each published page, colored by section (planned pages are not drawn) |
| `Section`        | left out: one per heading, part of its page                                           |
| `Example`        | left out: one per code block, part of its page                                        |
| `Term`           | a toggle, on the nearest ring around the pages                                        |
| `Surface`        | a toggle, on the middle ring around the pages                                         |
| `CookbookRecipe` | a toggle, on the nearest ring around the pages                                        |
| `Command`        | a toggle, on the middle ring around the pages                                         |
| `Flag`           | a toggle, on the middle ring around the pages                                         |
| `Index`          | left out: llms.txt and the landing list nearly every page                             |
| `Capability`     | a toggle, on the nearest ring around the pages                                        |
| `Problem`        | a toggle, on the outermost ring around the pages                                      |

| Relationship      | In the live view                                     |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `LINKS_TO`        | a toggle, on at first                                |
| `PREREQUISITE_OF` | a toggle, on at first                                |
| `RELATED_TO`      | a toggle, off at first                               |
| `HAS_SECTION`     | not drawn: its far end is a kind the view leaves out |
| `HAS_EXAMPLE`     | not drawn: its far end is a kind the view leaves out |
| `USES_TERM`       | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `APPLIES_TO`      | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `DOCUMENTS`       | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `HAS_FLAG`        | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `LISTS`           | not drawn: its far end is a kind the view leaves out |
| `SOLVES`          | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `CITES`           | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `DEMONSTRATES`    | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `VERIFIED_BY`     | drawn when both ends are                             |
| `HAS_CAPABILITY`  | drawn when both ends are                             |

Live: the view draws the pages with the links and prerequisites between them from `/docs/graph-view.json` and counts every kind; a search box enlarges the nodes whose title matches and dims the rest, toggles add glossary terms, capabilities and the other kinds, hovering a node shows its description and the nodes it is joined to, and a click opens its page.

![The published docs pages, one cluster per section, where the live view first draws them](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/docs-graph/element-docs-graph-1-light.svg)

properties.heading: What runs on it
properties.text:
| Reader                                                                                                          | How it loads the graph                                                                                                                               | What it offers                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| relate's own [MCP server](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/), on the reader's machine              | `--load` of `relate-docs.rl` into an in-memory store                                                                                                 | `read_cypher` and `get_schema` over the whole graph; `write_cypher` is not listed on a read-only store                                                        |
| The recipe [Turn a question into the relate docs you need](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/query-the-relate-docs/) | The graph's pages, terms, capabilities and recipes with the sections of five pages and their vectors, in the recipe's data block, run in the browser | Vector search over the sections, then traversals that expand the hits into context, scope the search and reach the capability behind the answer, step by step |

The local form serves the docs graph to an MCP host over stdio, once the store is served:

```bash
relate serve --mcp stdio --database :memory: --load https://relatedb.ai/docs/relate-docs.rl --read-only
```

A store opened read-only lists `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, not `write_cypher` ([read-only policy](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/mcp/#read-only-policy)), and `--load` into `:memory:` opens it read-only. `--safe` refuses a remote `--load` source, so the checked path is to download the store, compare its SHA-256 with the published value, and load the local copy. In this block, `<sha256>` is the value in `relate-docs.rl.sha256`, and the search runs only when it matches; on macOS, `shasum -a 256 --strict -c -` stands in for `sha256sum --strict -c -`:

```bash
curl -sSfLO https://relatedb.ai/docs/relate-docs.rl
echo "<sha256>  relate-docs.rl" | sha256sum --strict -c - && relate --load ./relate-docs.rl --mode envelope "MATCH (s:Section) SEARCH s IN (FULLTEXT INDEX docs FOR 'exit code' LIMIT 5) SCORE AS score RETURN s.page AS page, s.heading AS heading, s.url AS url, score"
```

The downloaded store served to an MCP host. A relative path resolves against the directory the host starts the server in:

```bash
claude mcp add relate-docs-local -- relate serve --mcp stdio --database :memory: --load <absolute-path>/relate-docs.rl --read-only
```

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text: Each error relate reports has a stable id, and each id is an anchor on this page: `https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#<id>`. A row gives the message pattern as relate prints it, where it is recorded, the cause, the remedy, whether retrying the same statement can succeed, and the CLI exit code. The tables are generated from one data file, so this page and its markdown twin list the same entries.

properties.heading: Bolt errors
properties.text:
Errors from `relate serve --bolt` that the Bolt surface adds to the engine errors.

| Error                                                                                | Message                                                     | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Remedy                          | Retryable | Exit code |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------- | --------- |
| `bolt-unauthorized`; Neo4j `Neo.ClientError.Security.Unauthorized`                   | `The client is unauthorized due to authentication failure.` | A failed or missing auth token; the connection closes. A Bolt 4.4 HELLO with a wrong or missing credential answers the message `authentication failed`; the message in this row is the Bolt 5.4 LOGON failure. | Use the `serve` credential.     | —         | —         |
| `bolt-request-invalid`; Neo4j `Neo.ClientError.Request.Invalid`                      | —                                                           | A malformed message: a RUN without a string statement, a bad PULL/DISCARD `n` or `qid`, an unconvertible parameter, a HELLO without `user_agent`, or a protocol breach.                                        | Use a supported Neo4j driver.   | —         | —         |
| `bolt-result-too-large`; Neo4j `Neo.ClientError.General.TransactionOutOfMemoryError` | `query result exceeds max-result-bytes limit of <N> bytes`  | A result over the Bolt server's fixed cap of 256 MiB of retained data per connection; `relate serve` has no flag that changes it.                                                                              | Add `LIMIT` or page the result. | —         | —         |
