| `engine-constraint-index-already-exists`; code `validation_error`, kind `semantic`                                                                                                                          | `semantic error: AlreadyExists: there already exists an index (<schema>). A constraint cannot be created until the index has been dropped.`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | A uniqueness constraint over a label and property that a range index already covers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Drop the index, then create the constraint; the constraint brings its own index.                                                                                    | no        | 6         |
| `engine-invalid-index-option`; code `validation_error`, kind `syntax`                                                                                                                                       | `syntax error: Invalid input '<key>' for 'OPTIONS'. Expected 'indexConfig'.`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `CREATE INDEX … OPTIONS {…}` with a key other than `indexConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Put settings under `indexConfig`.                                                                                                                                   | no        | 6         |
| `engine-delete-connected-node`; code `fatal_error`, kind `execution`; Python `IntegrityError`                                                                                                               | `DeleteConnectedNode: Cannot delete node with relationships unless DETACH`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | `DELETE` on a node that still has relationships.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Use `DETACH DELETE`, or delete the relationships first.                                                                                                             | no        | 1         |
| `engine-merge-null-property`; code `fatal_error`, kind `execution`                                                                                                                                          | `MergeReadOwnWrites: cannot MERGE with null properties`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | A `MERGE` pattern with a property whose value is null.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Filter out the null first, or `MERGE` on the properties that have values.                                                                                           | no        | 1         |
| `engine-invalid-property-type`; code `validation_error`, kind `type`                                                                                                                                        | `type error: InvalidPropertyType`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | A property value that cannot be stored: a map, a list of mixed types, or a list holding null.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Store a scalar or a homogeneous list without nulls; model a map as properties or nodes.                                                                             | no        | 6         |
| `engine-write-before-call-in-transactions`; code `validation_error`, kind `syntax`                                                                                                                          | `syntax error: WriteBeforeCallInTransactions: a write cannot precede CALL IN TRANSACTIONS`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | A write, `LOAD CSV` included, before `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` in the same statement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Move the write inside the subquery, or run it as its own statement.                                                                                                 | no        | 6         |
| `engine-system-restricted-clauses`; code `validation_error`, kind `semantic`                                                                                                                                | `semantic error: SemanticError: The following unsupported clauses were used: <clauses>.  The system database supports a restricted set of Cypher clauses. The supported clause structure for procedure calls is: CALL, YIELD, RETURN. YIELD and RETURN clauses are optional. The order of the clauses is fixed and each can only occur once.`                                             | A `MATCH`, `RETURN` or other clause outside a procedure call, routed to the `system` namespace. Two spaces follow the first period, as printed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Run the statement on `neo4j`, or use `SHOW …` or `CALL … YIELD … RETURN` on `system`.                                                                               | no        | 6         |
| `engine-point-latitude-range`; code `validation_error`, kind `argument`                                                                                                                                     | `InvalidArgumentValue: point() latitude must be in the range [-90, 90]`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | A geographic `point()` with a latitude outside -90 to 90; longitude and latitude may be swapped. The CLI prints it after `semantic error:`; the WebAssembly build after `type error:`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Pass the latitude as `latitude` (or `y`) and keep it within range.                                                                                                  | no        | 6         |
| `engine-no-transaction`; GQL status `42000`; Neo4j `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError`                                                                                                                | `semantic error: no transaction`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | A commit or rollback with no explicit transaction open: `.commit` or `.rollback` in the shell, or `commit()`/`rollback()` in a client. The Java, Go, Swift and Node.js clients report it with GQL status `42000` and stage runtime; in a CLI script it stops the run with exit code 1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Begin a transaction first, or drop the commit.                                                                                                                      | no        | 1         |
| `engine-ontology-unsupported-version`; code `validation_error`, kind `semantic`                                                                                                                             | `semantic error: Unsupported ontology spec version: '<uri>'. This version of Relate supports up to Ontology Graph Spec 1.1.0 ('https://neo4j.com/docs/ontology-graph-spec/1.1.0/schema.json').`                                                                                                                                                                                           | `db.ontology.set` got a document whose `schema` names a spec version this build does not support (preview: `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Write the document against Ontology Graph Spec 1.1.0 or earlier.                                                                                                    | no        | 6         |
| `engine-ontology-argument-type`; code `validation_error`, kind `type`                                                                                                                                       | ``type error: InvalidArgumentType: db.ontology.set argument `ontology` expects STRING``                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `db.ontology.set` got a map or another non-string value; the document is passed as one string (preview: `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Pass the document as a string.                                                                                                                                      | no        | 6         |
| `engine-ontology-user-database-only`; code `validation_error`, kind `semantic`                                                                                                                              | `semantic error: SemanticError: Ontologies can only be stored for the user database 'neo4j'.`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | An ontology procedure called with the session on the `system` namespace (preview: `RELATE_PREVIEW=ontology`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Call it on `neo4j`.                                                                                                                                                 | no        | 6         |

properties.heading: HTTP Query API errors
properties.text:
Errors from `relate serve --http`, in the Query API v2 error envelope.

| Error                                                          | Message                                                                                                                | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Remedy                                                                                               | Retryable | Exit code |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------- |
| `http-unauthorized`; GQL status `42NFF`; HTTP 401              | —                                                                                                                      | Missing or wrong credential.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Send `Authorization: Basic` with the `serve` credential (the generated token is printed at startup). | —         | —         |
| `http-not-found`; GQL status `42N00`; HTTP 404                 | —                                                                                                                      | Unknown `{databaseName}`, or any unknown route. An unknown path answers the message `not found`; an unknown namespace `semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Use `neo4j` or `system`.                                                                             | —         | —         |
| `http-transaction-expired`; GQL status `42N90`; HTTP 404       | `transaction <id> expired after <n>s idle`                                                                             | A managed transaction sat idle past `--tx-idle-timeout-secs`. Message pattern from the recorded example `transaction tx-7 expired after 60s idle`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Begin a new transaction; raise the idle timeout if needed.                                           | —         | —         |
| `http-transaction-registry-full`; GQL status `42N91`; HTTP 429 | `transaction registry full: 128 open transactions (close one or raise --max-open-transactions)`                        | A begin over the `--max-open-transactions` cap. The count in the message is the configured cap.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Close an open transaction or raise the cap.                                                          | —         | —         |
| `http-malformed-or-syntax`; GQL status `42N06`; HTTP 400       | —                                                                                                                      | Malformed request body, or a Cypher syntax error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Fix the body or the statement.                                                                       | —         | —         |
| `http-general`; GQL status `42000`; HTTP 400                   | —                                                                                                                      | Any other caller-facing engine error, undecodable `parameters`, or (with 405) a wrong method; with 500, an IO, storage or locked failure, genericized. Observed messages: a body over the 16 MiB cap is `malformed request: body too large`; a request line that is not HTTP/1.1 is `unsupported HTTP version HTTP/1.0: this surface answers HTTP/1.1`; a wrong method (405) is `method not allowed`. | Read the message.                                                                                    | —         | —         |
| `http-internal`; GQL status `50N42`; HTTP 500                  | —                                                                                                                      | Engine-internal error; the message is genericized.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Report it with the server version.                                                                   | —         | —         |
| `http-unsupported-media-type`; GQL status `42000`; HTTP 415    | `the request content type is browser-"simple" — a cross-origin form cannot send a non-simple type without a preflight` | A `POST` with no `Content-Type`, or a browser-simple one (`text/plain` or a form type; `curl -d` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Send `Content-Type: application/json`.                                                               | —         | —         |
| `http-origin-forbidden`; GQL status `42000`; HTTP 403          | `origin is not allowed`                                                                                                | A browser request whose `Origin` is not the server's own and not one `--origin` allows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Add the page's origin with `--origin`.                                                               | —         | —         |
| `http-read-transaction-write`; GQL status `42000`; HTTP 400    | `writing is not allowed in a READ transaction`                                                                         | A write in a managed transaction begun with `"accessMode": "READ"`. It does not poison the transaction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Begin the transaction without `accessMode`, or with `WRITE`.                                         | —         | —         |
| `http-transaction-not-found`; GQL status `42000`; HTTP 404     | `transaction <id> not found`                                                                                           | The transaction id was never issued, or the transaction was committed, rolled back or closed after a failed commit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Begin a new transaction.                                                                             | —         | —         |

properties.heading: MCP errors
properties.text:
Errors from `relate serve --mcp`. A tool refusal comes back as a tool result with `isError: true`; a protocol error is a JSON-RPC error with the code in its row.

| Error                                       | Message                                                                                                                              | Cause                                                                                                                                                                                             | Remedy                                                                                                              | Retryable | Exit code |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------- |
| `mcp-read-query-only`                       | `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query`                                                                                      | `read_cypher` received a write (`w`/`rw`) or schema DDL (`s`) statement. Any pure read passes, `OPTIONAL MATCH` included.                                                                         | Use `write_cypher` for writes, where the server lists it.                                                           | —         | —         |
| `mcp-write-query-only`                      | `Only write queries are allowed for write-query`                                                                                     | `write_cypher` received a read-only statement. `write_cypher` is absent when the store is opened `--read-only`.                                                                                   | Use `read_cypher`.                                                                                                  | —         | —         |
| `mcp-unknown-tool`                          | `unknown tool '<name>'`                                                                                                              | `tools/call` named a tool the server does not list; `write_cypher` is not listed when the store is opened `--read-only`. Returned as a tool result with `isError: true`, not as a JSON-RPC error. | Call a tool from `tools/list`; to write, serve the store without `--read-only`.                                     | —         | —         |
| `mcp-internal-error`                        | `Error: internal error`                                                                                                              | An internal-class engine failure (engine-internal, IO, storage, locked); detail is genericized so it never reaches tool-call logs.                                                                | Check the server's own stderr.                                                                                      | —         | —         |
| `mcp-method-not-found`; JSON-RPC -32601     | `Method not found: <method>`                                                                                                         | Unknown JSON-RPC method.                                                                                                                                                                          | Use `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` or `tools/call`.                                                             | —         | —         |
| `mcp-invalid-params`; JSON-RPC -32602       | `Invalid params: <detail>`                                                                                                           | Malformed `tools/call` params.                                                                                                                                                                    | Match the tool's input schema.                                                                                      | —         | —         |
| `mcp-parse-error`; JSON-RPC -32700          | `malformed JSON-RPC message: <detail>`                                                                                               | A body that is not JSON, omits `jsonrpc` or `method`, or carries an unknown member.                                                                                                               | Send a strict JSON-RPC 2.0 message.                                                                                 | —         | —         |
| `mcp-unsupported-version`; JSON-RPC -32600  | `unsupported JSON-RPC version '<version>'`                                                                                           | A `jsonrpc` version other than `2.0`.                                                                                                                                                             | Send `"jsonrpc": "2.0"`.                                                                                            | —         | —         |
| `mcp-missing-statement`                     | `invalid params: missing string "statement"`                                                                                         | A Cypher tool call without a `statement` string. A tool result with `isError: true`.                                                                                                              | Pass the statement as `statement`.                                                                                  | —         | —         |
| `mcp-parameters-not-object`                 | `invalid params: "parameters" must be an object`                                                                                     | `parameters` is a string, list, number or boolean; `null` is accepted as no parameters. properties.heading: Python exception classes
properties.text:
The classes the Python client (`relate-db`) raises, at their own anchors.

| Class                        | Parent             | Raised for                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Error`; alias `RelateError` | `Exception`        | Base of every relate database error.                                                                 |
| `InterfaceError`             | `Error`            | Native module communication.                                                                         |
| `DatabaseError`              | `Error`            | Fallback for an unmapped engine error.                                                               |
| `DataError`                  | `DatabaseError`    | Bad type or value; every capacity refusal (kind MemoryLimitExceeded); an out-of-range int parameter. |
| `OperationalError`           | `DatabaseError`    | Open, I/O, transaction; namespace errors; writes on a read-only database.                            |
| `IntegrityError`             | `DatabaseError`    | Constraint violations and deleting a still-connected node without DETACH.                            |
| `InternalError`              | `DatabaseError`    | An engine invariant the caller cannot fix.                                                           |
| `ProgrammingError`           | `DatabaseError`    | Syntax errors, missing parameters, parameter-shape mistakes, closed connections, wrong-thread use.   |
| `NotSupportedError`          | `DatabaseError`    | Unsupported administration commands.                                                                 |
| `ResultNotSingleError`       | `ProgrammingError` | `cursor.single()` got zero rows or more than one.                                                    |

Every exception carries the attributes `kind`, `tck_class`, `neo4j_code`, `gql_status`, `stage`, `retryable`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
On the CLI, a failed statement prints its message on stderr and exits with the [exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) of its class. In `--mode envelope`, `--json` and `--jsonl`, it also prints an [error object](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#error-object) on stdout. The object's `code` is the class, `kind` is the engine's error variant, `retryable` is `true` for a write-write conflict and for a `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit` refusal while other statements hold the workspace pool, and `message` repeats the stderr text.

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope 'RETURN $x AS x'
```

The first line of the output is stderr, the second is stdout:

```text
semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): x
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","exit_code":6,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): x","retryable":false}}
```

A syntax error adds `column` and `source`, so a caller can point at the failing token without parsing the message:

```text
syntax error: parse error: expected RightParen, got "RETURN" (RETURN)
  MATCH (n RETURN n
           ^
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","column":10,"exit_code":6,"kind":"syntax","message":"syntax error: parse error: expected RightParen, got \"RETURN\" (RETURN)   MATCH (n RETURN n            ^","retryable":false,"source":"MATCH (n RETURN n"}}
```

`relate agent-context` prints the exit codes of the installed version:

```text
Exit codes:
  0  success: success, including an empty result
  1  fatal_error: runtime failure: store open or I/O error, capacity limit, query execution failure, internal error
  2  usage_error: unknown flag, bad or missing value, extra positional
  5  conflict: write-write conflict, or the store is locked by another opener
  6  validation_error: the statement is rejected: syntax, semantic or type error
  7  timeout: a statement exceeded --timeout
```

In the tables, a message's `<name>` marks a variable part and `…` is an elision in the source. A dash (—) means the sources do not state the value, or it does not apply to that [surface](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#surface).

properties.heading: Limitations
properties.text: relate is an embedded graph database for one process on one machine: the whole graph of an open [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) is held in memory, one process writes a store at a time, a statement runs against one graph, and there is no cluster. This page lists every limit that follows from that shape, and every guard rail the engine adds, as of the version in the page header. Each row names the limit, what a caller meets (the exact error, or the behavior), and the page that explains it.

properties.text:
| Limit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | What a caller meets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Explained in                                                                                |

Any other `USE` target is refused before the statement runs.                                                                                 | [`semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-database-not-found), exit code 6                                                                                                                            | [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) |

This feature is only available on composite databases. Attempted to access graph <name>`, exit code 6 ([42N72](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-composite-only-function))           | [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) |

Use the db.ontology.* procedures on the user database 'neo4j' instead.`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-system-ontologies-not-queryable), exit code 6                                                                  | [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) |

Fixed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | `syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`, exit code 6                                                                                                                                                                        | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)          |
| A statement's expressions and clauses nest at most 500 levels deep. Fixed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `syntax error: parse error: maximum nesting depth of 500 exceeded`, exit code 6                                                                                                                                                                                             | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)          |

Fixed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `ValueDepthExceeded: value nesting exceeds 500 levels; container nesting compounds per level (security limit).`, exit code 1                                                                                                                                                | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)          |
| One statement gets 100,000 nested evaluation passes. Fixed. A `CALL` subquery runs once per input row and each run counts, so `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` over more than 100,000 rows fails; a larger load is split into several statements.                                                                               | [`NestedEvaluationBudgetExceeded: nested evaluation exceeds 100000 passes per statement; nested subqueries compound per level (security budget).`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-nested-evaluation-budget), exit code 1                                 | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)          |
| An explicit variable-length bound (`*1..N`, `{1,N}`) is at most `--max-traversal-depth`: 500 hops by default, 2000 at most. An unbounded `*` and `shortestPath` are not checked against it.                                                                                                                                 | [`syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: This query allows paths up to <n> hops. …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-traversal-depth-exceeded), exit code 6                                                                                                | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)          |
| One value a statement builds (a list, string or map) is at most 256 MiB by default. `--expression-memory-limit` changes it; `none` turns it off.                                                                                                                                                                            | [`This statement tried to build a single value of <size>. …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-expression-memory-cap), exit code 1                                                                                                                         | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)          |

An unknown name fails the open.                                                                                                                                                                                        | `preview feature '<name>' is not enabled: set RELATE_PREVIEW=<name>`; an unknown name prints `invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature '<name>' (known features: …)`, exit code 1                                                                              | [Cypher overview](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/overview/)                      |

It cannot see the store's size, so it refuses an unbounded read of a small store too, and it checks a `CALL { … }` body on its own. `collect()` does not count as reducing.       | [`syntax error: SafeModeViolation: …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-safe-mode-violation), exit code 6                                                                                                                                                  | [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/)                  |

Coverage is measured outside the engine by a spec harness that reports on each ready pull request and does not gate merges. The last published figure, 3,892 of 3,892 scenarios of a pinned TCK 2024.3 corpus, was retired on 2026-11-05. | No error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | [Differences from Neo4j](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/differences-from-neo4j/) |

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
Each statement in these examples is refused before it runs. A `USE` target outside the three namespaces:

```cypher run name=use-other-graph expect=error
USE archive
RETURN 1 AS x
```

```table
error: semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: archive
```

An explicit path bound over the default traversal limit of 500 hops:

```cypher run name=deep-path expect=error
MATCH (a)-[*1..600]->(b)
RETURN count(*) AS paths
```

```table
error: syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: This query allows paths up to 600 hops. This is a safety limit protecting against excessive traversal (not a database limit) — lower the path bound, or raise it with --max-traversal-depth (up to 2000).
```

properties.heading: Process model
properties.text:
| Limit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | What a caller meets                                                                                                                                  | Explained in                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One process at a time opens a persistent store for writing. A second writer is refused at open, whether it is another CLI run, a client in another process, or `relate serve`.                                                                                 | [`storage locked: <path>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked), exit code 5; not retryable until the first process exits | [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/) |
| A `.rl` file opens only while no writer holds it, `--read-only` included. A directory store can be opened [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) beside its writer.                                                               | The same `storage locked: <path>`, exit code 5                                                                                                       | [Share one store between two processes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/two-processes-one-store/) |
| `--read-only=live`, which follows the writer's commits, works on directory stores only.                                                                                                                                                                        | `semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases`, exit code 1, for a `.rl` file or `:memory:`          | [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#read-only)                                      |
| Threads in one process can read at once. Two transactions that write the same element conflict, and the later commit fails. relate does not retry it.                                                                                                          | [`write-write conflict`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-conflict), exit code 5; retryable                                   | [Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/)           |
| Conflict detection compares the elements each transaction wrote, plus the values of `unique` and `key` constraints at commit. It does not detect write skew: two transactions that each read what the other writes, and write different elements, both commit. | Both commits succeed                                                                                                                                 | [Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/)           |
| Transactions are single-level. There are no nested transactions and no savepoints. `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` commits its own batches; it is not a savepoint.                                                                                                | `.begin` inside an open transaction prints `semantic error: already in a transaction`                                                                | [Transactions and concurrency](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/transactions-and-concurrency/)           |
| `:memory:` lives as long as the process. Nothing is written to disk, and nothing survives the exit.                                                                                                                                                            | The graph is gone when the process ends                                                                                                              | [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/)                                    |
| There is no client/server engine. `relate serve` puts HTTP, MCP, and Bolt in front of one open store in one process; it does not let several processes share a store.                                                                                          | A second process that opens the served store meets `storage locked: <path>`                                                                          | [Architecture](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/architecture/)                                           |

properties.heading: Server
properties.text:
These rows apply to `relate serve`, which hosts the HTTP Query API, MCP, and Bolt on one open store.

| Limit                                                                                                                                                                                                       | What a caller meets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Explained in                                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No served surface has TLS. Every surface binds to `127.0.0.1` by default. Any other `--host` exposes them in plaintext.                                                                                     | At startup: `serve: WARNING: --host <host> exposes the PLAINTEXT HTTP/MCP/Bolt surfaces to the network — serve has no TLS; anyone who can reach the ports can present credentials. …`                                                                                                                               | [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/#served-surfaces)                 |
| One Basic-auth credential is shared by every surface. There are no users, no roles and no role-based access control. `--auth none` turns authentication off.                                                | A missing or wrong credential is refused (HTTP 401)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/#served-surfaces)                 |
| No clustering, replication, sharding, failover, or composite or remote databases. One `relate serve` process serves one store.                                                                              | No error; these features do not exist                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | [Where relate fits](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/where-relate-fits/)                |
| An HTTP managed transaction idle for 60 seconds expires (`--tx-idle-timeout-secs`; `0` turns expiry off). At most 128 managed transactions are open at once (`--max-open-transactions`; `0` is unlimited).  | [`transaction <id> expired after <n>s idle`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#http-transaction-expired), HTTP 404; [`transaction registry full: 128 open transactions (close one or raise --max-open-transactions)`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#http-transaction-registry-full), HTTP 429 | [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#serve-tx-idle-timeout-secs)    |
| At most 128 sessions at once across every surface (`--max-connections`).                                                                                                                                    | A connection over the cap is accepted, then closed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#serve-max-connections)         |
| A Bolt connection that sends nothing for 300 seconds is closed, and its open transaction rolled back. `relate serve` has no flag that changes it.                                                           | The connection closes; uncommitted work is lost                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/)                               |
| A Bolt result holds at most 256 MiB of retained bytes. `relate serve` has no flag that changes it.                                                                                                          | [`query result exceeds max-result-bytes limit of <N> bytes`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#bolt-result-too-large)                                                                                                                                                                                      | [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#bolt-result-too-large)               |
| On a store served `--read-only`, a write inside an HTTP managed transaction or a Bolt explicit transaction runs and is visible inside that transaction; only the commit is refused, and nothing is written. | At commit: HTTP 400 with GQL status `42N18`; on Bolt, `Neo.ClientError.Statement.SemanticError`                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [HTTP Query API reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/server/http/#transactions) |
| `RELATE_PREVIEW` is read once by the server process, not per caller. With `ontology` enabled, every connected client can call the ontology procedures, including the ones that write.                       | No error                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [Keep an agent safe](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/)               |

properties.heading: Storage
properties.text:
| Limit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | What a caller meets                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Explained in                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The whole graph and its indexes are held in memory. relate has no buffer pool, no paging and no spill to disk, so the graph has to fit in the process's memory.                                                                                                                                                                        | Without a cap, the process grows until the machine runs out of memory. With `--logical-graph-size-limit`, a write that grows the graph past the cap fails with [`capacity exceeded: used=… limit=…`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-graph-size-cap), exit code 1 | [Size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/) |
| One commit's record in the [WAL](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal) is at most 64 MiB. A larger single transaction is refused whole.                                                                                                                                                                                    | [`This statement tried to commit a single WAL record of at least <size>. …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-wal-payload-cap), exit code 1; nothing is written                                                                                                    | [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/)        |
| A directory store holds one snapshot codec, chosen when the directory is empty. `--snapshot-format` naming a codec other than the store's own is refused.                                                                                                                                                                              | `storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is parquet, requested json`, exit code 1                                                                                                                                                                                         | [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/)                    |
| The store format migrates forward on open and has no downgrade. Once a newer relate has opened a store, an older binary rejects it.                                                                                                                                                                                                    | The older binary fails at open, naming the unsupported version, before it changes anything                                                                                                                                                                                          | [Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/)               |
| The `everysecond` and `snapshot` durability modes acknowledge a commit before it is synced. A crash can lose about the last second of acknowledged writes under `everysecond`, or every write since the last [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint) under `snapshot`. The default, `full`, syncs first. | No error; acknowledged writes are missing after a crash                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | [Durability modes](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/durability-modes/)             |

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
Limits come in two kinds:

| Kind       | What it is                                                                                                                               | How it shows up                                                                                                          |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Scope      | The shape of the tool: one writing process per store, the graph in memory, three fixed graphs per store, no cluster. No flag changes it. | An error such as `storage locked: <path>`, or a behavior such as data held only in memory                                |
| Guard rail | A default that keeps one statement from exhausting the process's memory or stack                                                         | An error that names the mechanism, says it is a safety limit and not a database limit, and names the flag that raises it |

The guard rails, with their defaults and the flags that change them, are tabled on [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/). Each error's cause and remedy are on [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/), at the anchor the rows link to. In the tables, `<name>` in a message marks a variable part and `…` an elision.

properties.heading: Privacy and telemetry
properties.text: The `relate` CLI binary sends anonymous usage metrics to Mixpanel. They are on by default, and `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `RELATE_TELEMETRY=0`, or `relate telemetry off` turns them off. The events carry command shapes and a random install ID; query text, [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) paths, and [parameter](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#parameter) values are never collected, because the code that builds an event has no field to hold them. The client libraries, the WebAssembly build, the C library, and the served [surfaces](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#surface) never send usage metrics. The docs and cookbook pages and the home page load Google Tag Manager from `googletagmanager.com` for page-view measurement, and only after you accept the banner: until then, and if you reject, nothing is requested from Google. Your choice is kept in your browser's local storage, and the "Cookie settings" link in the footer reopens it. The playground does not load it, and neither does a preview build. Beyond that these pages load nothing from a third party with the page. One recipe downloads an embedding model from Hugging Face, and only when the reader presses the button that states its size.

properties.heading: Events
properties.text:
The CLI sends four events. This table is the disclosure:

| Event                | Event-specific properties                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `RELATE-CLI_STARTUP` | `kind`: `oneshot`, `stdin`, `repl`, `version` or `help`                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `RELATE-CLI_QUERY`   | `success` (true or false); `source`: `oneshot`, `stdin` or `repl`; `storage`: `memory` or `persistent`; `output_mode`: `table`, `csv`, `json`, `jsonl`, `toon`, `markdown` or `cypher`, the mode actually used (`--mode envelope` and `--mode speedscope` report `json`) |
| `RELATE-CLI_COMMAND` | `command`: the command word, such as `skill`, `upgrade`, `telemetry`, `pull`, `serve` or `run`; `action`: the sub-action, such as `install` (`run` reports `extension`, never the extension's name; left out for a command with no action); `success` (true or false)    |
| `RELATE-CLI_HELP`    | None beyond the base properties                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

Every event also carries these properties:

| Property      | Meaning                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `token`       | The Mixpanel project token compiled into the binary                                                                      |
| `time`        | The event time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch                                                                     |
| `distinct_id` | The random install ID                                                                                                    |
| `$insert_id`  | A random UUID per event, to drop duplicates                                                                              |
| `$os`         | The operating system                                                                                                     |
| `arch`        | The CPU architecture                                                                                                     |
| `version`     | The CLI version                                                                                                          |
| `uptime`      | Seconds since the CLI started                                                                                            |
| `invoker`     | `agent` when a known agent-harness environment variable is set, else `ci` when `CI` is set to a true value, else `human` |

| Topic           | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Never collected | Query text, store paths, and parameter values. The event types have no fields for them, so adding one would be a compile error, not a policy change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Install ID      | A random UUID, generated once and kept in `state.json` in the config directory. No hardware or operating-system identifier is read.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Files           | `state.json` (the install ID and the notice flag), `config.json` (the setting `relate telemetry` writes) and the spool, one `telemetry-spool-<uuid>.jsonl` file per run that recorded events, all mode `0600` on Unix, in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/` when that is set to an absolute path, else `~/.config/relate/`; on Windows, `%APPDATA%\relate`, else `%USERPROFILE%\.config\relate`                                              |
| Delivery        | A run sends nothing while it works. At exit it appends its events to its own spool file, a local write with no network wait. The next run with usage metrics on sends the spooled files in the background, as `POST https://api.mixpanel.com/track` with a 2-second HTTP timeout, and deletes each file once delivered; a file that fails stays for a later run. The spool is bounded: past its limits, events and files are dropped. |
| Failure         | Every [telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#telemetry) error is ignored: nothing is printed, and exit codes do not change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Recipient       | A Mixpanel project shared with another command-line tool; its operator is not named here yet. The `RELATE-CLI_` prefix keeps relate's events apart. The CLI does not set Mixpanel's `ip` parameter, so Mixpanel's own handling of the request's IP address applies.                                                                                                                                                                   |

properties.heading: Hosting and logs
properties.text:
| Item                                   | Status                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Host                                   | Cloudflare Pages serves `relatedb.ai`, with a Pages Function on the docs paths                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Docs page analytics                    | Decided, not deployed: Cloudflare Web Analytics on the docs pages, with no cookies and no script beyond Cloudflare's own                                                                                                                                     |
| Agent-path hits                        | Deployed with the Pages Function: one log line per request for a `.md` twin, a data file a twin links, `llms.txt`, a page asked for with `Accept: text/markdown` or `?section=`, or the skill, with the path, the status and the user agent; no query string |
| What Cloudflare logs, and for how long | Not published yet                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
