properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
| Surface                                                                              | Sends usage metrics                                                                     | Network access it starts on its own                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `relate` CLI (release binary)                                                        | Yes, unless turned off                                                                  | Only the usage metrics. `relate upgrade`, `relate extension install`, `--load <url>`, `--fetch-params`, `pull`, and `push` reach the addresses they are given or document, and only when run |
| `relate serve` (HTTP, [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp), Bolt) | One `RELATE-CLI_COMMAND` event when the server exits; statements it serves send nothing | Only that one usage metrics event, unless turned off                                                                                                                                         |
| Python, Node.js, Java, Go, Swift, and Rust clients, and the C library                | Never                                                                                   | None                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| WebAssembly (WASM) build                                                             | Never                                                                                   | None                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `agent` and `minimal` CLI builds, from source                                        | Never; the usage metrics code is not compiled in                                        | `agent`: only `pull`, `push`, `--fetch-params`, `--load <url>`, and `extension install`, when run. `minimal`: none                                                                           |

properties.heading: The first-run notice
properties.text:
The first statement run with usage metrics on, whether a one-shot statement, piped stdin, or the REPL, prints one line to stderr, whether or not stdin is a terminal:

```text
relate collects anonymous usage metrics; disable anytime: relate telemetry off
```

It prints once per install: a `notice_shown` flag in `state.json` stops it repeating. `--version`, `--help`, and the commands (`serve`, `skill`, `upgrade`, `telemetry`, `extension`, `run`, and the rest) never print it, and they send their events whether or not it has been shown. So a first command on a new install, such as `relate --version`, sends an event before any notice has appeared. A run with usage metrics turned off never prints it and sends nothing.

properties.heading: Turning usage metrics off
properties.text:
Usage metrics are on unless a layer turns them off. The first layer that matches decides:

| Order | Layer                                                                      | Off                    | On                   |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1     | `DO_NOT_TRACK`                                                             | `1` or `true`          | —                    |
| 2     | `RELATE_TELEMETRY`                                                         | `0`, `false`, or `off` | `1`, `true`, or `on` |
| 3     | `"telemetry"` in `config.json`, written by `relate telemetry off` and `on` | `false`                | `true`               |
| 4     | Default                                                                    | —                      | On                   |

`relate telemetry status` prints the effective state and the layer that decided it: `default`, `config file`, `RELATE_TELEMETRY`, or `DO_NOT_TRACK`. `relate telemetry off` and `on` write the setting and print the file they wrote; `off` also deletes the spool, so events recorded before it are never sent. The commands exit 0 on success, 1 when no config directory resolves or the write fails, and 2 for a missing action, an unknown action, or an extra argument.

The commands on this page run with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` set, so `status` names that layer. `off` writes the config file, and `DO_NOT_TRACK` still decides:

```bash verify
relate telemetry status
relate telemetry off
relate telemetry status
```

The home directory is shown as `<home>`:

```text
disabled (DO_NOT_TRACK)
telemetry disabled (<home>/.config/relate/config.json)
disabled (DO_NOT_TRACK)
```

The environment variables that control usage metrics, including the ones for development and testing:

| Variable                   | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Default                          | Used by                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `DO_NOT_TRACK`             | `1`/`true` disables anonymous usage metrics; beats every other layer.                                                                                                                                  | —                                | usage metrics                                     |
| `RELATE_TELEMETRY`         | `0`/`false`/`off` disables, `1`/`true`/`on` enables anonymous usage metrics.                                                                                                                           | —                                | usage metrics                                     |
| `RELATE_MIXPANEL_ENDPOINT` | Overrides the Mixpanel /track URL (development and testing); https\:// for any host, http\:// only for a loopback host; a rejected value turns usage metrics off for the run, with one stderr warning. | `https://api.mixpanel.com/track` | usage metrics                                     |
| `RELATE_MIXPANEL_TOKEN`    | Overrides the compiled-in Mixpanel project token (development and testing).                                                                                                                            | —                                | usage metrics                                     |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`          | When set, non-empty and absolute, the config directory is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/`.                                                                                                                  | —                                | usage metrics, `relate extension`, `relate skill` |
| `HOME`                     | The fallback config directory `~/.config/relate/`, and the base of the agent directories `relate skill install` writes to.                                                                             | —                                | usage metrics, `relate extension`, `relate skill` |
| `CI`                       | A value other than empty, `0` or `false` reports the usage-metrics invoker as `ci`.                                                                                                                    | —                                | usage metrics                                     |

`RELATE_MIXPANEL_ENDPOINT` accepts an `https://` URL, or an `http://` URL on a loopback host; any other value turns usage metrics off for that run, with one warning on stderr. Unset, the endpoint is `https://api.mixpanel.com/track`.

properties.heading: What never phones home
properties.text:
| Surface                                                                                | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The embedded engine, as used by the Python, Node.js, Java, Go, Swift, and Rust clients | Usage metrics live in the CLI binary only                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| The C library (`relate-ffi`)                                                           | Same                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| The WASM build (`@relate/relate-wasm`, and the engine on these pages)                  | Same                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Statements served by `relate serve` over HTTP, MCP, or Bolt                            | The server process sends one `RELATE-CLI_COMMAND` event when it exits, unless usage metrics are off; no event is sent per connection or statement                                                                                                             |
| `agent` and `minimal` CLI builds                                                       | Built without the usage metrics code: no events, no notice, no telemetry config or state files. The `agent` build still reaches the network when `pull`, `push`, `--fetch-params`, `--load <url>`, or `extension install` is run; `minimal` has none of these |

properties.heading: What the relatedb.ai site loads
properties.text:
| Page                                                                                                                                                                                    | What the browser fetches                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Docs, cookbook, and playground pages                                                                                                                                                    | Files from `relatedb.ai` only: the pages, self-hosted fonts, the search index, the engine from `/wasm/` (on the first Run of a cell, never with the page), and the graph view (when a graph result comes into view)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| The home page                                                                                                                                                                           | The same, plus the console's graph view: the first time the console draws a graph, it loads the Neo4j Visualization Library (NVL) 2.0.0 from `esm.sh`, a third-party CDN, with NVL's telemetry turned off                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The recipe [Turn a question into the relate docs you need](https://relatedb.ai/cookbook/query-the-relate-docs/#ask-your-own-question), after its "Download the model" button is pressed | The cookbook page's files, plus the embedding model bge-small-en-v1.5 at a pinned revision from `huggingface.co`: its half-precision weights (66.7 MB) and its tokenizer (0.7 MB). Hugging Face redirects the weights to its content delivery network, a host under `hf.co`. The requests carry no cookies and no referrer, so Hugging Face sees the reader's IP address and the browser's user agent, as with any download. Each file is checked against its pinned SHA-256 before it is used. The ONNX runtime that runs the model (14.2 MB) comes from `relatedb.ai`. The question typed into the recipe is embedded in the tab and never sent anywhere. Nothing is fetched before the press |

NVL, the graph view, includes a telemetry module. The cookbook and docs pages replace it with an empty module at build time (`astro.config.mjs` aliases `@segment/analytics-next`), so none of its code ships. The playground and the home page run NVL with `disableTelemetry: true`. Today the site's own code sets no cookies and runs no analytics script, and it downloads a model only on that recipe's button press. It writes the model to no browser storage; the browser's own HTTP cache may keep the files, as it keeps any download. It stores two values in the browser's `localStorage`: the light or dark theme (`theme`) and the docs tab choice (`docs-tab`), so a tab picked on one page stays picked on the next.

properties.heading: Project
properties.text: relate is open source under the Apache License 2.0. It is pre-1.0: under semantic versioning, any 0.x release can change behavior, a patch release included, and every change that can break working code is marked in the changelog. Releases are cut by hand and signed; the CLI ships for macOS, Linux, and Windows, and the clients cover Python, Node.js, the browser, Rust, Java, Go, Swift, and C. This page records those facts and where each comes from.

properties.heading: Governance
properties.text:
The repository states how it takes contributions:

| Contribution                                           | Accepted                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bug reports, feature requests and questions, as issues | Yes                                                                                          |
| Pull requests from outside the maintainer team         | No; pull requests are turned off for accounts without write access                           |
| Issues written with an AI tool                         | Yes, when the tool is disclosed in the issue and a person who hit the problem has checked it |
| Issues filed by an agent with no person involved       | May be closed without warning                                                                |

Only the maintainer team merges changes. Design decisions are recorded as architecture decision records in the repository's `docs/adr/` directory. The repository publishes no governance document, steering body, or foundation membership.

properties.heading: License
properties.text: The repository's `LICENSE` file is the Apache License, Version 2.0, and the binary's `--version` names it. The Rust crates (the Cargo workspace's `license` field) and the Node.js package (`package.json`) declare `Apache-2.0`.

properties.heading: Platforms
properties.text:
| Artifact                                                                                              | macOS arm64 | macOS amd64 | Linux arm64 | Linux amd64 | Windows amd64 | Requires                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| CLI binary, `relate-<os>-<arch>` from the first relate-named release                                  | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes (`.exe`)  | Linux: glibc                                                                                     |
| `install.sh`                                                                                          | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | No            | `curl`, `ssh-keygen`                                                                             |
| `relate upgrade`                                                                                      | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | No            | —                                                                                                |
| Python client, `relate-db`                                                                            | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes           | Python 3.9 or later                                                                              |
| Node.js client, `@relate/relate`                                                                      | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes           | Node.js 18 or later                                                                              |
| Java client, `com.relate:relate`                                                                      | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes           | Java 17 or later; the native library is in the jar                                               |
| Go client                                                                                             | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes           | cgo, and the C library for the target; on Windows, a MinGW import library generated from the DLL |
| C library, `relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` (`cypherlite-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` up to and including 0.16.1) | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes         | Yes           | —                                                                                                |
| Swift package, `Relate`                                                                               | Yes         | Yes         | —           | —           | —             | macOS 13 or later; iOS 16 or later                                                               |

Releases up to and including 0.16.1 were published under the project's earlier name, cypherlite, with `cypherlite-<os>-<arch>` binaries; the first release named relate restarted the version numbers at 0.1.0. The Swift package also builds for iOS devices (arm64) and the iOS simulator. The browser package, `@relate/relate-wasm`, is a WebAssembly build that runs in the browser on any of these systems; a durable browser [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) needs a dedicated worker and the origin private file system. The Rust crate, `relate`, builds from source with Rust 1.88 or later. No artifact is built for another operating system or architecture.

Each release publishes the packages below at its version, from the same commit as the release downloads. As of 1.0.1:

| Registry          | Name                                                                                                                                                                                  | Install                                                              |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PyPI              | `relate-db` (`import relate`): wheels for the five platforms above and a source distribution                                                                                          | `pip install relate-db`                                              |
| npm               | `@relate/relate`, with its engine in a platform package, `@relate/relate-<platform>-<arch>`, which npm picks; `@relate/relate-wasm` for the browser                                   | `npm install @relate/relate`                                         |
| crates.io         | `relate`, with the crates it depends on at the same version                                                                                                                           | `cargo add relate`                                                   |
| Go modules        | `github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go`, resolved from the repository; the module has no version tag of its own, so a release is pinned by its commit and Go records a pseudo-version | `go get github.com/relatedb/relate/clients/go@ef436ce` (1.0.1)       |
| SwiftPM           | `Relate`, from `github.com/relatedb/relate` at the release tag                                                                                                                        | `.package(url: "https://github.com/relatedb/relate", from: "1.0.1")` |
| Release downloads | `github.com/relatedb/relate/releases`: the CLI binaries, the C libraries, the Java jars and the Swift XCFramework                                                                     | [Install relate](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/install/)      |

`com.relate:relate` is not on Maven Central: the Java jars are release downloads only, and a Maven or Gradle build installs the jar into its local repository ([Java guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/embed/java/)).

properties.heading: Questions and bug reports
properties.text:
Questions and bug reports go to the issues of [github.com/relatedb/relate](https://github.com/relatedb/relate/issues). A useful bug report holds:

| Part                 | Detail                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Version and platform | The output of `relate --version`, the operating system, and the architecture                                                         |
| Reproduction         | The smallest statement or command that shows the problem, and what was expected instead                                              |
| Store                | How it was opened: a directory, a `.rl` file or `:memory:`, and the snapshot format and durability mode if they are not the defaults |
| Client               | For a client issue, the package version and how it was installed                                                                     |

A wrong or missing docs page is reported as `/docs/feedback.md` describes; the person the agent works for decides whether a report is sent. A docs report goes to the issues of [github.com/relatedb/relate-web](https://github.com/relatedb/relate-web/issues); [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/#reporting-a-vulnerability) has no reporting address yet.

properties.heading: Releases
properties.text:
| Step           | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cut            | A maintainer starts the release workflow by hand and picks a patch, minor, or major bump. The version comes from the existing tags plus that bump.                                                        |
| Build and sign | The CLI binaries, the C libraries and the client packages build from one commit. The macOS binaries are signed and notarized. The tag is pushed only after every build passes.                            |
| Publish        | The release carries every artifact, a `SHA256SUMS` manifest and its signature, `SHA256SUMS.sig`. `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json`, which `relate upgrade` reads, is rewritten to list the new release. |
| Recover        | A release that fails after its tag is pushed is not redone under the same version; the next release takes the next version.                                                                               |

The project publishes no release cadence and no support period for older releases. [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/) describes the signing; the [changelog](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/changelog/) lists each release.

properties.text:

`relate --version` prints the version and the license:

```bash verify
relate --version
```

```text
Relate v1.0.1
License: Apache 2.0 (binary)
```

properties.heading: Versioning and stability
properties.text:
relate follows semantic versioning, as its changelog states, and 1.0.0 is its first stable release:

| Promise                               | What it means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Breaking changes take a major version | Under semantic versioning, a change that breaks working code or statements comes in a new major version; a 1.x minor release adds features, and a patch release fixes bugs. Before 1.0, any release could break, a patch release included: 0.16.1 removed the `apoc.coll.sort` spelling and replaced the C application binary interface (ABI) with an incompatible typed one, 0.1.2 and 0.1.3 changed the strings `elementId()` returns, and 1.0.0 removed the change-data-capture methods from the Rust crate. The first patch release after 1.0 did not hold to it either: 1.0.1 changed the default `--jsonl` output, what Python's `Record.data()` returns, and which Cypher statements validate, each marked **Breaking** in its [changelog entry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/changelog/). |
| Breaking changes are marked           | A change that can make working code or statements fail is marked **Breaking** in the [changelog](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/changelog/) entry of the release that ships it, with its replacement when there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Deprecations are listed               | A feature that still works but is to be removed is listed under Deprecated in the release that deprecates it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| One version number                    | The binary and every client package carry the same version number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Preview features are opt-in           | A preview feature runs only when its name is in `RELATE_PREVIEW`, read once when a store opens. An unknown name fails the open. A preview feature's syntax can change between releases. When it graduates, its gate is removed and it works without the opt-in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Stores migrate forward                | A store written by an older release is upgraded in place the first time a newer release opens it. There is no downgrade: an older binary rejects a store a newer one has opened.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

A [preview feature](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#preview-feature) named in `RELATE_PREVIEW` that the engine does not know fails the open with exit code 1:

```bash verify
RELATE_PREVIEW=time-travel relate "RETURN 1 AS ok"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: semantic error: SemanticError: invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature 'time-travel' (known features: hybrid-search, local-callables, graph-type-opt-props, graph-type-default-values, graph-type-implied-labels, ontology, obfuscated-literals, mixed-label-syntax, float16-coordinate-types, chronological-comparisons, complex-search-patterns, coll-zip, coll-has, gql-stddev-aliases)
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"semantic","message":"semantic error: SemanticError: invalid RELATE_PREVIEW value: unknown preview feature 'time-travel' (known features: hybrid-search, local-callables, graph-type-opt-props, graph-type-default-values, graph-type-implied-labels, ontology, obfuscated-literals, mixed-label-syntax, float16-coordinate-types, chronological-comparisons, complex-search-patterns, coll-zip, coll-has, gql-stddev-aliases)","retryable":false}}
```

The first line is stderr. The second is the error object on stdout, which a run with piped output prints after the message.

properties.heading: Security
properties.text: Every relate CLI release ships a `SHA256SUMS` manifest signed with one Ed25519 key. `install.sh` and `relate upgrade` check that signature against a copy of the key pinned inside themselves, check that the manifest names the release being installed, check the binary's SHA-256, and install nothing if any check fails. The macOS binaries are also signed and notarized by Apple. Since 1.0.1 the engine repository publishes a security policy, `SECURITY.md`: vulnerabilities are reported by email to `security@neo4j.com`, and only the latest release line receives security fixes. No release carries a software bill of materials (SBOM) or SLSA provenance.

properties.heading: Agent-facing files on the site
properties.text:
| File                                   | Integrity                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/skills/relate/` (the skill bundle)   | Copied from the engine repository at a recorded commit, with the SHA-256 of every file recorded                                                                   |
| `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` | One `sha256:` digest per entry, over the bytes served                                                                                                             |
| `/docs/docs-artifacts.json`            | Lists the skill and discovery files and the docs graph seed with their SHA-256; a signature with the release key, `docs-artifacts.json.sig`, is not published yet |

properties.heading: Code signing and notarization
properties.text:
| Artifact                                                                                                | Signature beyond `SHA256SUMS`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| macOS CLI binaries                                                                                      | Signed with an Apple Developer ID Application identity, with the hardened runtime and a secure timestamp, then notarized by Apple. A bare binary cannot carry a stapled ticket, so Gatekeeper checks the notarization online the first time the binary runs. |
| Linux CLI binaries                                                                                      | None                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Windows CLI binary                                                                                      | None; the release workflow has no Authenticode step                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| C libraries (`relate-ffi-<target>.tar.gz`; `cypherlite-ffi-<target>.tar.gz` up to and including 0.16.1) | None                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Python wheels and source distribution                                                                   | None on the release assets. On PyPI, each `relate-db` file carries a PEP 740 attestation from trusted publishing: the `publish-registries.yml` workflow of `relatedb/relate`, in its `release` environment                                                   |
| Java jars                                                                                               | None; `com.relate:relate` is published as release assets only, not to Maven Central                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Swift package                                                                                           | SwiftPM checks the release's `RelateFFI.xcframework.zip` (`CypherLiteFFI.xcframework.zip` up to and including 0.16.1) against the checksum in the tagged `Package.swift`                                                                                     |
| npm packages                                                                                            | npm provenance (SLSA provenance v1) through trusted publishing, from the `publish-registries.yml` workflow of `relatedb/relate`; `npm audit signatures` checks it                                                                                            |
| Rust crates                                                                                             | None; published to crates.io through trusted publishing from the GitHub Actions of `relatedb/relate`                                                                                                                                                         |

`SHA256SUMS` lists the five CLI binaries only. The other artifacts are not in it.

properties.heading: Engine defaults that limit reach
properties.text:
| Behavior                               | Default                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `LOAD CSV` from local files            | Denied unless `--load-csv-dir <dir>` (or `RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR`) names a directory; paths that escape it, symlink escapes and special files are refused                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `--load <url>`, `--fetch-params <url>` | Reach only the URL given; `--load` keeps no copy after loading                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `relate upgrade`                       | Reads `https://relatedb.ai/releases.json` and downloads release assets, checked as `install.sh` checks them                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `relate extension install`             | From the default first-party channel: checks the channel's signed index against the same release key, and the package's SHA-256. With `--github REPO@TAG` or `@SHA`: checks the pinned asset's SHA-256 and the tag's commit, with no signature. With `--url` (https only) or `--from DIR`: no signature; naming the source is the trust decision |
| Usage metrics                          | On by default in the CLI only; [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/) lists what is sent and how to turn it off                                                                                                                                                                                      |

properties.heading: Manual verification
properties.text:
The same three checks run by hand with `curl`, `ssh-keygen`, and `sha256sum`. For a release on Linux amd64, from 0.1.0 on, with `VERSION` holding the release's version number (without the `v`), the commands and their expected output are:

```bash
ASSET=relate-linux-amd64
BASE="https://github.com/relatedb/relate/releases/download/v$VERSION"
curl -sSfLO "$BASE/$ASSET"
curl -sSfLO "$BASE/SHA256SUMS"
curl -sSfLO "$BASE/SHA256SUMS.sig"
echo 'relate-release ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHgv/GHY5mtv/HopH/J/T7KrTT7eOVFEG2ueT4iRKwbK relate-release' > allowed_signers
ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I relate-release -n relate-release -s SHA256SUMS.sig < SHA256SUMS
head -n 1 SHA256SUMS
grep "  $ASSET\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c -
```

```text
Good "relate-release" signature for relate-release with ED25519 key SHA256:BfnIA0YD0h+ldihdq8V1k/xFY91lm8mRCuVS21+3kzA
# relate-release-version: v<version>
relate-linux-amd64: OK
```

In the output, `<version>` is that version number. The other assets are `relate-linux-arm64`, `relate-darwin-arm64`, `relate-darwin-amd64`, and `relate-windows-amd64.exe`. On macOS, `shasum -a 256 -c -` takes the place of `sha256sum -c -`. The [pinned install steps](https://relatedb.ai/docs/get-started/agent-quickstart/#install-a-pinned-relate) in Connect your agent to relate give the same steps with the install that follows them. The checks for a release up to and including 0.16.1 use that release's names instead: the `cypherlite-<os>-<arch>` asset, `cypherlite-release` as the identity, the namespace and the `allowed_signers` principal, and `# cypherlite-release-version: ` as the header.

properties.heading: Provenance and software bill of materials
properties.text: No release publishes a software bill of materials (SBOM), and no release publishes a build provenance attestation in the SLSA format. The release workflow has no step that produces either.

properties.heading: Release signing key
properties.text:
```text
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHgv/GHY5mtv/HopH/J/T7KrTT7eOVFEG2ueT4iRKwbK relate-release
```

| Where the key is                                                                                           | Form                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `https://relatedb.ai/install.sh`                                                                           | The `SIGNING_KEY` line                          |
| The `relate` binary                                                                                        | Compiled in; `relate upgrade` checks against it |
| `distribution/release-signing-key.pub` in [github.com/relatedb/relate](https://github.com/relatedb/relate) | The public key file                             |
| A standalone key file at a `relatedb.ai` URL                                                               | Not published yet                               |

All three copies are the same bytes. Its fingerprint, computed from the key:

```bash verify
echo 'ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIHgv/GHY5mtv/HopH/J/T7KrTT7eOVFEG2ueT4iRKwbK relate-release' > release-signing-key.pub
ssh-keygen -lf release-signing-key.pub
```

```text
256 SHA256:BfnIA0YD0h+ldihdq8V1k/xFY91lm8mRCuVS21+3kzA relate-release (ED25519)
```

The signer identity and the signature namespace are both `relate-release`, from 0.1.0, the first relate-named release, on. Releases up to and including 0.16.1 were published under the earlier name, as `cypherlite-<os>-<arch>`, signed with the same key under the identity and namespace `cypherlite-release`, with the manifest header `# cypherlite-release-version: `. A new key ships inside a release. A binary installed before a key change still trusts the old key, so its `relate upgrade` refuses releases signed with the new one; `install.sh`, which carries the new key, installs them.

properties.heading: Reporting a vulnerability
properties.text: Report a vulnerability in relate by email to `security@neo4j.com`, not in a public issue. `SECURITY.md` in the engine repository is the policy: reporting and disclosure follow the [Neo4j responsible-disclosure policy](https://neo4j.com/responsible-disclosure/), which publishes the PGP key for encrypted reports; there is no bug bounty. The policy covers the engine, the `relate` CLI with its extension host, the Bolt, HTTP Query API and MCP servers, the C ABI, and every language client, the browser WASM client included. It names this website and the cookbook out of scope, and lists the accepted design allowances, such as no engine-level access control and plaintext served surfaces, that are not vulnerabilities. The site publishes no `/.well-known/security.txt`.

- [Privacy and telemetry](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/privacy-and-telemetry/): what the CLI reports, and what never phones home
