properties.heading: Value encoding
properties.text:
| Cypher type                                               | Plain (`application/json`)                                                                                                 | Typed (`application/vnd.neo4j.query`)                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Integer, float                                            | A JSON number                                                                                                              | `{"$type": "Integer", "_value": "2"}`, `{"$type": "Float", "_value": "1.5"}`: the number as a string           |
| String, boolean, null                                     | The JSON value                                                                                                             | `String`, `Boolean`, `Null` with the JSON value                                                                |
| List, map                                                 | A JSON array or object                                                                                                     | `List` or `Map`, with each member typed                                                                        |
| [Node](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#node) | `{"elementId", "labels", "properties"}`                                                                                    | `Node` with `_element_id`, `_labels` and typed `_properties`                                                   |
| Relationship                                              | `{"elementId", "startNodeElementId", "endNodeElementId", "type", "properties"}`                                            | `Relationship` with the same fields in the typed form                                                          |
| Path                                                      | A JSON array alternating nodes and relationships                                                                           | `Path`                                                                                                         |
| Date, time, datetime, duration                            | The ISO 8601 string: `"2024-01-02"`, `"2024-01-02T03:04:05Z"`, `"2024-01-02T03:04:05+01:00[Europe/Stockholm]"`, `"P1DT2H"` | `Date`, `Time`, `LocalTime`, `LocalDateTime`, `OffsetDateTime`, `ZonedDateTime` or `Duration`, with the string |
| Point                                                     | `{"type": "Point", "coordinates": [13.0, 55.6], "crs": {…}}`, `crs` naming the SRID, such as `4326` (`wgs-84`)             | `Point` with `coordinates` and `crs`                                                                           |
| Byte array                                                | A list of integers from 0 to 255                                                                                           | A `List` of `Integer`                                                                                          |

The `elementId` in this API is the node's or relationship's number as a string (`"0"`); Bolt 5.4 carries the `elementId()` form, such as `4:rl-id:n0`. A byte array reaches the engine only as a Bolt or Rust parameter, never through this API's JSON.

properties.heading: MCP server
properties.text: `relate serve --mcp` serves one relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) to agent hosts over [MCP](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#mcp) (the Model Context Protocol), with three tools: `get_schema`, `read_cypher` and `write_cypher`. It runs on the host's stdin and stdout (`--mcp stdio`) or as a streamable HTTP listener (`--mcp <port>`), and a store opened [read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#read-only) lists only the first two. This server reads and writes a store of yours.

properties.heading: Authentication
properties.text:
The HTTP transport asks for HTTP Basic authentication (RFC 7617) on every request. The stdio transport asks for none, because the host that spawned the process is the only peer.

| Source                 | Credential                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--auth USER:PASSWORD` | That user and password. A value with no colon exits 1 with `Error: --auth: expected user:password or 'none'`, and one with an empty side with `Error: --auth: expected user:password with both sides non-empty`                                                           |
| `RELATE_AUTH`          | The same forms, read when `--auth` is absent                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `--auth none`          | No credential is checked                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Neither                | A generated token for the user `relate`, printed on stderr at startup. For a directory or `.rl` store it is saved beside the store as `<store>.auth-token` (mode `0600`, holding `relate:<token>`) and reused on restart; `:memory:` generates a new token on every start |

The credential is the one `relate serve` shares with its `--http` and `--bolt` listeners, so one token opens all three. A failed check waits 1 second before the 401 goes out. A credential given as `--auth` on the command line is visible in the process list; `RELATE_AUTH` and the generated token keep it out of the arguments. Every surface is plaintext, so a credential sent to a non-loopback `--host` crosses the network unencrypted; [Security](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/security/#served-surfaces) lists the defaults.

properties.heading: Differences from mcp-neo4j-cypher
properties.text:
The tools follow the contract of Neo4j's `mcp-neo4j-cypher` server under relate's own names, as relate's MCP specification records it; the specification names no version of that server, and it was not run for this page:

| relate         | `mcp-neo4j-cypher`   | Difference                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_schema`   | `get_neo4j_schema`   | None in the input or output shape                                                                                             |
| `read_cypher`  | `read_neo4j_cypher`  | The rows arrive inside the result envelope, under `rows`, with column types, notifications, the plan, and timings beside them |
| `write_cypher` | `write_neo4j_cypher` | The counters arrive inside the result envelope, under `stats`                                                                 |

The refusal texts `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query` and `Only write queries are allowed for write-query` are the same in both.

properties.heading: Errors and refusals
properties.text:
A tool that fails returns a result with `isError: true` and the message as its text; it is not a JSON-RPC error. These runs show the refusals of a read-only server:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"MATCH (p:Person {name: $name}) DETACH DELETE p","parameters":{"name":"Ada"}}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"CREATE INDEX person_name FOR (p:Person) ON (p.name)"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"write_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"CREATE (:Person {name: \"Eve\"})"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"query":"MATCH (p:Person) RETURN count(p) AS people"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"RETURN $limit AS n","parameters":"10"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"RETURN $limit AS n"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{"sample_size":-2}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"text":"Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"text":"Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{"content":[{"text":"unknown tool 'write_cypher'","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"result":{"content":[{"text":"invalid params: missing string \"statement\"","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"result":{"content":[{"text":"invalid params: \"parameters\" must be an object","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":6,"result":{"content":[{"text":"Error: semantic error: ParameterMissing: Expected parameter(s): limit","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"result":{"content":[{"text":"invalid params: sample_size must be -1 or non-negative, got -2","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
```

| Tool error text                                                   | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query`                   | `read_cypher` got a write or a schema statement ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#mcp-read-query-only))                                                                                                               |
| `Only write queries are allowed for write-query`                  | `write_cypher` got a read ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#mcp-write-query-only))                                                                                                                                    |
| `unknown tool '<name>'`                                           | The tool is not listed, including `write_cypher` on a read-only server ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#mcp-unknown-tool))                                                                                           |
| `invalid params: missing string "statement"`                      | A Cypher tool's `arguments` has no string `statement` (an argument named `query` is not read)                                                                                                                                                      |
| `invalid params: "parameters" must be an object`                  | `parameters` is a string, a list, a number or a boolean; `null` counts as no parameters                                                                                                                                                            |
| `invalid params: sample_size must be -1 or non-negative, got <n>` | `get_schema` got a negative `sample_size` other than `-1`                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `Error: <engine message>`                                         | The engine refused the statement: a syntax error, a missing parameter, a type error, `SafeModeViolation`; the text after `Error: ` is the engine's message, as on the [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-errors) |
| `Error: internal error`                                           | An engine-internal, storage, IO or lock failure; the detail stays out of the tool result ([errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#mcp-internal-error))                                                                       |

A request that is not a valid call gets a JSON-RPC error. A body that cannot be decoded gets `"id": null`:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"resources/list"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"ping","extra":true}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"1.0","id":4,"method":"ping"}' \
  'not json' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found: resources/list"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"Invalid params: tools/call needs a string \"name\""}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"malformed JSON-RPC message: unknown field `extra`, expected one of `jsonrpc`, `id`, `method`, `params` at line 1 column 47"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"unsupported JSON-RPC version '1.0'"}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"malformed JSON-RPC message: expected ident at line 1 column 2"}}
```

| JSON-RPC code | Message                                    | When                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-32700`      | `malformed JSON-RPC message: <detail>`     | The body is not JSON, lacks `jsonrpc` or `method`, carries a member other than `jsonrpc`, `id`, `method` and `params`, or is a JSON array (batches are not accepted) |
| `-32600`      | `unsupported JSON-RPC version '<version>'` | `jsonrpc` is not `"2.0"`                                                                                                                                             |
| `-32601`      | `Method not found: <method>`               | Any method outside [Methods](#methods)                                                                                                                               |
| `-32602`      | `Invalid params: <detail>`                 | `tools/call` without a string `name`                                                                                                                                 |

On the HTTP transport, the server answers these before any JSON-RPC handling, with a JSON body of one key, `error`:

| HTTP status | Body `error`                                                                                                           | When                                                                                                |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 401         | `authentication required`                                                                                              | No credential or a wrong one, after a 1-second delay; with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="relate"` |
| 403         | `origin is not allowed`                                                                                                | A present `Origin` that is not loopback                                                             |
| 405         | `streamable HTTP MCP is POST-only`                                                                                     | Any method but `POST`, with `Allow: POST`                                                           |
| 415         | `the request content type is browser-"simple" — a cross-origin form cannot send a non-simple type without a preflight` | A `POST` with no `Content-Type`, `text/plain`, or a form type                                       |
| 400         | `unsupported HTTP version HTTP/1.0: this surface answers HTTP/1.1`                                                     | A request line that is not HTTP/1.1                                                                 |
| 400         | `malformed request: body too large`                                                                                    | A body over the 16 MiB cap                                                                          |
| 202         | Empty body                                                                                                             | A JSON-RPC notification                                                                             |

The 403 and 415 checks run before the credential check, and the credential check runs before the body is read.

properties.heading: get_schema
properties.text:
| Input         | Type    | Default | Meaning                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | ------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `sample_size` | integer | `1000`  | How many nodes and relationships per label are examined to infer property types and relationship types; `-1` examines all. Any other negative value is refused |

The result is a JSON object keyed by node label. Each entry holds `type` (`"node"`), `count` (the exact number of nodes with the label), `properties` (each key with its inferred `type`, such as `String` or `Integer`) and, when the sample found any, `relationships`: each outgoing relationship type with its `direction`, the `labels` at the other end, and its own `properties`. Property types come from the sample, and a key seen with mixed types keeps the first type seen. Counts never depend on the sample; the relationship types do:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_schema","arguments":{"sample_size":1}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"Person\":{\"count\":3,\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"role\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"relationships\":{\"KNOWS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Person\"]},\"MAINTAINS\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"]},\"WORKS_ON\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"],\"properties\":{\"since\":{\"type\":\"Integer\"}}}},\"type\":\"node\"},\"Project\":{\"count\":2,\"properties\":{\"language\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"type\":\"node\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"Person\":{\"count\":3,\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"role\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"relationships\":{\"WORKS_ON\":{\"direction\":\"out\",\"labels\":[\"Project\"],\"properties\":{\"since\":{\"type\":\"Integer\"}}}},\"type\":\"node\"},\"Project\":{\"count\":2,\"properties\":{\"language\":{\"type\":\"String\"},\"name\":{\"type\":\"String\"}},\"type\":\"node\"}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

With `sample_size` 1, `Person` still counts 3 nodes, and only one of its three relationship types was seen.

properties.heading: Limits
properties.text:
Every row is a limit.

| Limit                     | Value                                                                                             | Over the limit                                  |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Statements per call       | 1                                                                                                 | A second statement after `;` is a syntax error  |
| Messages per HTTP request | 1                                                                                                 | A JSON array is a `-32700` error                |
| HTTP request body         | 16 MiB                                                                                            | HTTP 400, `malformed request: body too large`   |
| HTTP header deadline      | 10 seconds for the whole header block (`--header-deadline-secs`, `0` turns it off, at most 86400) | The connection is dropped with no reply         |
| HTTP body deadline        | 60 seconds for the whole body (`--body-deadline-secs`, `0` turns it off, at most 86400)           | The connection is dropped with no reply         |
| Concurrent connections    | 128, shared with the `--http` and `--bolt` listeners (`--max-connections`)                        | The connection is accepted, then closed         |
| Failed credential checks  | One answer per second per connection                                                              | The 401 waits 1 second                          |
| `get_schema` sample       | 1000 nodes and relationships per label by default                                                 | Types a smaller sample did not see are left out |
| Traversal depth           | An explicit hop bound up to 500 (`--max-traversal-depth`, 1 to 2000)                              | A tool error carrying `TraversalDepthExceeded`  |
| Expression memory         | One value up to 256 MiB (`--expression-memory-limit`)                                             | A tool error                                    |

The server has no per-call timeout and no row cap: `relate serve` takes neither `--timeout` nor `--max-rows`, and a `read_cypher` result holds every row. A bounded read uses `LIMIT`, and `--safe` refuses an unbounded `MATCH` read.

properties.heading: Logging
properties.text: The server writes its startup and shutdown lines to stderr: on stdio, `serve: MCP (stdio) serving on stdin/stdout (auth: none)` and, when stdin closes, `serve: stdin closed, shutting down`; on HTTP, `serve: MCP (streamable HTTP) listening on http://<host>:<port> (auth: basic)`, plus an `auth:` line naming where the credential came from, and the generated token when there is one. On stdio, stdout carries only JSON-RPC. The runs recorded for this page wrote no line per request on either transport. An internal engine failure reaches the caller only as `Error: internal error`.

properties.heading: Methods
properties.text:
| Method                                             | Result                                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `initialize`                                       | `protocolVersion`, `capabilities` (`{"tools": {}}`) and `serverInfo`                       |
| `notifications/initialized`, any `notifications/*` | No response on stdio; HTTP 202 with an empty body on HTTP                                  |
| `ping`                                             | `{}`                                                                                       |
| `tools/list`                                       | `tools`: each tool's `name`, `description`, `inputSchema` and `annotations`                |
| `tools/call`                                       | `content` (one item, `type` `text`, the result serialized as JSON in `text`) and `isError` |
| Any other method                                   | JSON-RPC error `-32601`, message `Method not found: <method>`                              |

The messages a host sends to open a session, against a writable in-memory store so that every tool is listed:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"shell","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"ping"}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database :memory: 2>/dev/null
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"capabilities":{"tools":{}},"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","serverInfo":{"name":"relate-mcp","version":"1.0.1"}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"annotations":{"destructiveHint":true,"idempotentHint":false,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":false,"title":"Write Cypher"},"description":"Execute one writing Cypher statement (CREATE, MERGE, SET, DELETE, …). `parameters` is passed as the statement's parameters; an object with a `rows` array feeds the statement's `$rows` parameter. Returns the mutation counters.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"parameters":{"default":{},"description":"The statement's parameters; a `rows` array feeds `$rows`.","type":"object"},"statement":{"description":"The Cypher statement.","type":"string"}},"required":["statement"],"type":"object"},"name":"write_cypher"},{"annotations":{"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true,"title":"Read Cypher"},"description":"Execute one read-only Cypher statement. Returns the result's rows. Write and schema (DDL) statements are rejected.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"parameters":{"default":{},"description":"The statement's parameters; a `rows` array feeds `$rows`.","type":"object"},"statement":{"description":"The Cypher statement.","type":"string"}},"required":["statement"],"type":"object"},"name":"read_cypher"},{"annotations":{"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true,"title":"Get Schema"},"description":"Get the schema of the graph store: node labels with their property keys and inferred types, and the relationship types between them. `sample_size` bounds how many nodes and relationships are examined per label (larger is slower but more accurate; -1 examines all).","inputSchema":{"properties":{"sample_size":{"description":"The sample size used to infer the graph schema. Larger samples are slower, but more accurate. Smaller samples are faster, but might miss information. -1 samples the whole graph.","type":"integer"}},"type":"object"},"name":"get_schema"}]}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"result":{}}
```

The notification got no response line, and `tools/list` names `write_cypher`, `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, in that order.

properties.heading: Read-only policy
properties.text:
Before it runs a statement, each Cypher tool plans it with `EXPLAIN` and reads the statement's query type from the plan. That plan is the `plan` in the result, and its notifications are the result's `notifications`; a `PROFILE` never runs. A statement that already starts with `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE` fails with `syntax error: parse error: unexpected token "EXPLAIN"` (or `"PROFILE"`), because the tool plans it as `EXPLAIN <statement>`; [notifications](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cypher/notifications/) lists what the result can carry.

| Store opened                           | Tools listed                                | `read_cypher`                                                                                                                             | `write_cypher`                                           |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Writable (the default)                 | `write_cypher`, `read_cypher`, `get_schema` | Runs a read (query type `r`); refuses a write (`w`, `rw`) and a schema statement (`s`: `CREATE`/`DROP INDEX`, `CREATE`/`DROP CONSTRAINT`) | Runs a write or a schema statement; refuses a read       |
| `--read-only`                          | `read_cypher`, `get_schema`                 | The same                                                                                                                                  | Not listed; a call answers `unknown tool 'write_cypher'` |
| `--read-only=live` (a directory store) | `read_cypher`, `get_schema`                 | The same, against the writer's latest commits                                                                                             | Not listed                                               |
| Any, with `--safe`                     | As without it                               | Also refuses a `MATCH` read with no `LIMIT` and no reducing aggregate, as `SafeModeViolation`                                             | Also refuses a new named node without a label            |

`--read-only` takes no writer lease and never creates the store; a missing store fails the open. `--read-only=live` follows a directory store that another process writes ([live read-only](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#live-read-only)), and is refused for a `.rl` file and for `:memory:`. The tools of a read-only server carry `readOnlyHint: true`, and hosts that approve read-only tools without asking can use that. The [agent safety guide](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/agents/agent-safety/) has the permission matrix across the CLI and MCP.

properties.heading: read_cypher
properties.text:
| Input        | Type   | Default  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------ | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `statement`  | string | required | One Cypher statement. A pure read passes, `OPTIONAL MATCH` included; a write or a schema statement is refused ([Read-only policy](#read-only-policy))          |
| `parameters` | object | `{}`     | The statement's parameters, as plain JSON values; a key named `rows` binds `$rows` like any other key. A value that is neither an object nor `null` is refused |

The result is the envelope described in [Results](#results). The timings change on every run, so this example replaces them with `<ms>`:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"read_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since","parameters":{"project":"relate"}}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./team.rl --read-only 2>/dev/null \
  | sed -E 's/(_ms\\":)[0-9.e-]+/\1<ms>/g'
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"columnTypes\":[\"STRING\",\"INTEGER\"],\"columns\":[\"name\",\"since\"],\"elapsed_ms\":<ms>,\"error\":null,\"execute_ms\":<ms>,\"lex_parse_ms\":<ms>,\"lower_ms\":<ms>,\"notifications\":[{\"category\":\"PERFORMANCE\",\"code\":\"Relate.Notification.Statement.MissingIndex\",\"description\":\"the equality predicate on name filters :Project without a range index on (:Project {name})\",\"gql_status\":\"03C91\",\"operator_id\":1,\"remedy\":\"CREATE INDEX relate_Project__name FOR (n:Project) ON (n.name)\",\"severity\":\"INFORMATION\",\"title\":\"Missing index\"}],\"parse_ms\":<ms>,\"plan\":{\"profiled\":false,\"root\":{\"actual\":null,\"children\":[{\"actual\":null,\"children\":[],\"details\":\"(:Project)<-[w:WORKS_ON]-(p:Person)\",\"estimated_rows\":null,\"identifiers\":[],\"operator\":\"Expand\",\"warnings\":[{\"category\":\"PERFORMANCE\",\"code\":\"Relate.Notification.Statement.MissingIndex\",\"description\":\"the equality predicate on name filters :Project without a range index on (:Project {name})\",\"gql_status\":\"03C91\",\"remedy\":\"CREATE INDEX relate_Project__name FOR (n:Project) ON (n.name)\",\"severity\":\"INFORMATION\",\"title\":\"Missing index\"}]}],\"details\":\"2 item(s), ordered\",\"estimated_rows\":null,\"identifiers\":[],\"operator\":\"ProduceResults\",\"warnings\":[]},\"schema\":\"relate.plan/v1\",\"statement\":\"MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since\"},\"plan_cache\":\"miss\",\"plan_ms\":<ms>,\"result_generation_ms\":<ms>,\"rewrite_ms\":<ms>,\"rows\":[{\"name\":\"Grace\",\"since\":2023},{\"name\":\"Ada\",\"since\":2024}],\"stats\":{\"constraints_added\":0,\"constraints_removed\":0,\"indexes_added\":0,\"indexes_removed\":0,\"labels_added\":0,\"labels_removed\":0,\"nodes_created\":0,\"nodes_deleted\":0,\"properties_set\":0,\"relationships_created\":0,\"relationships_deleted\":0}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

The rows are Grace since 2023 and Ada since 2024. The [notification](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#notification) in the result comes from the plan, before the statement ran.

properties.heading: Results
properties.text:
The text of a successful `read_cypher` or `write_cypher` call is one JSON object, the same result metadata the CLI's `--mode envelope` and the clients carry:

| Key                                      | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `columns`                                | The column names, in order                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `columnTypes`                            | One type name per column, from the first row: `STRING`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `BOOLEAN`, `NODE`, `RELATIONSHIP`, `PATH`, `LIST`, `MAP`, `POINT`, `DATETIME`, `DATE`, `TIME`, `DURATION`, `VECTOR`, `UUID`, `BINARY` or `ANY`                                       |
| `rows`                                   | One object per row, keyed by column. A node is `{"id", "kind": "node", "labels", "properties"}`, a relationship `{"id", "kind": "relationship", "type", "start_node", "end_node", "properties"}`, a date its ISO 8601 string                                     |
| `stats`                                  | The 11 mutation counters, zeros included: `nodes_created`, `nodes_deleted`, `relationships_created`, `relationships_deleted`, `properties_set`, `labels_added`, `labels_removed`, `indexes_added`, `indexes_removed`, `constraints_added`, `constraints_removed` |
| `notifications`                          | The plan's notifications, each with `code`, `gql_status`, `severity`, `category`, `title`, `description`, `remedy` and, on an operator's notification, `operator_id`. Always present; `[]` when there are none                                                   |
| `plan`                                   | The plan of the statement as a `relate.plan/v1` document: `schema`, `statement`, `profiled` (`false`) and `root`, an operator tree of `operator`, `details`, `estimated_rows`, `identifiers`, `warnings`, `actual` and `children`                                |
| `elapsed_ms`                             | The statement's time in the engine, in milliseconds                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `parse_ms`, `plan_ms`, `execute_ms`      | The parse, plan and execute parts of `elapsed_ms`; their sum is never more than `elapsed_ms`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `lex_parse_ms`, `rewrite_ms`, `lower_ms` | Parts of `parse_ms`: lexing and parsing, the rewrite pass, and validation with lowering                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `result_generation_ms`                   | The part of `execute_ms` spent building the result                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `plan_cache`                             | The plan cache's outcome, such as `miss`, or `hit-raw-fastpath` for a statement the server planned before                                                                                                                                                        |
| `error`                                  | `null` on a result; a failed call is a tool error instead ([Errors and refusals](#errors-and-refusals))                                                                                                                                                          |

A byte array, which reaches the engine only as a Bolt or Rust parameter and never through this server's parameters, is a list of integers from 0 to 255 in a result, with the column type `BINARY`.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate serve --database PATH --mcp stdio [--read-only[=FRESHNESS]] [--safe]
relate serve --database PATH --mcp PORT [--host HOST] [--auth USER:PASSWORD] [--read-only[=FRESHNESS]] [--safe]
```

| Item              | Value                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Protocol          | JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line on stdio, one message per `POST` body on HTTP                                                                                                            |
| `serverInfo`      | `name` `relate-mcp`, `version` the relate version (`1.0.1`)                                                                                                                                 |
| `protocolVersion` | The client's `protocolVersion` from `initialize`, echoed; `2024-11-05` when the client sends none                                                                                           |
| Capabilities      | `tools` only: no resources, prompts, or sampling                                                                                                                                            |
| Tools             | `get_schema`, `read_cypher`, `write_cypher`; `write_cypher` is not listed when the store is opened `--read-only`                                                                            |
| Sessions          | None. Each request stands alone; no `Mcp-Session-Id` is issued                                                                                                                              |
| Authentication    | None on stdio; HTTP Basic on the HTTP transport, from one credential shared with the other `relate serve` surfaces                                                                          |
| Writes            | Allowed unless the store is opened `--read-only`; `read_cypher` refuses writes and schema changes either way                                                                                |
| Flags             | `--mcp` and the other `relate serve` flags are on [relate serve](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/serve/) and in [CLI flags](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#serve-mcp) |

properties.heading: Tools
properties.text:
| Tool           | Listed                          | Annotations                                                                                     | Input                                                                         | Result in `content[0].text`                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_schema`   | Always                          | `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`  | `sample_size` (integer, optional)                                             | A schema map keyed by label                                 |
| `read_cypher`  | Always                          | `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`  | `statement` (string, required); `parameters` (object, optional, default `{}`) | The result envelope, with rows                              |
| `write_cypher` | Only when the store is writable | `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: true`, `idempotentHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false` | `statement` (string, required); `parameters` (object, optional, default `{}`) | The result envelope: empty rows, plus the mutation counters |

Each call runs one statement. The examples in this section run against `team.rl`, the shared example graph of three people and two projects. This step writes it, with the CLI:

```bash verify
relate --database ./team.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)"
```

The same graph is in this page's in-browser database, and the tryout answers the three tools on it with the calls this section records. Each reply is built from the engine's result the way the server builds it; apart from the timings, it is the reply the recorded runs below print:

```cypher run name=team
CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace)
```

```table
(no rows) · nodes created: 5, relationships created: 5, properties set: 13, labels added: 5
```

```json data=calls
{"calls": [
  {"tool": "get_schema", "arguments": {}},
  {"tool": "read_cypher", "arguments": {"statement": "MATCH (p:Person)-[w:WORKS_ON]->(:Project {name: $project}) RETURN p.name AS name, w.since AS since ORDER BY since", "parameters": {"project": "relate"}}},
  {"tool": "write_cypher", "arguments": {"statement": "CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})", "parameters": {"name": "Ada", "role": "engineer"}}}
]}
```

These calls ran when the page was recorded, on a database that holds what this page's cells write, through the same mapping the live tryout uses. Timings show as `<ms>`; live, each reply carries the timings of its own run. The server lists `write_cypher`, `read_cypher`, `get_schema`.

| Project | 2     | language (String), name (String) | -                                                          |

**`write_cypher` on a server started `--read-only`**: it lists only `read_cypher` and `get_schema`, and answers a `write_cypher` call with a tool error before the engine sees the statement. This run is recorded from relate 1.0.1 (errors.json `mcp-unknown-tool`, replayed against the binary by `docs:cli-check`); the page quotes it as the binary printed it:

```bash
printf '%s\n' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"check","version":"0"}}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"write_cypher","arguments":{"query":"CREATE (:B)"}}}' | relate serve --mcp stdio --database ./graph.rl --read-only
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"text":"unknown tool 'write_cypher'","type":"text"}],"isError":true}}
```

Live: each call is a button that sends its `tools/call` request to the page's database in your browser and shows the request and the reply, built from the engine's result the way `relate serve --mcp` builds it, with the statement and parameters editable; "Serve read-only" drops `write_cypher` from the tool list, as `--read-only` does, and shows the engine's own refusal of the write on a read-only database beside the server's recorded answer.

properties.heading: Transports
properties.text:
`--mcp` takes the keyword `stdio` or a port number, once per run. A second `--mcp` exits 2 with `Error: serve --mcp may be given only once`.

|                                    | `--mcp stdio`                                                                                                                                                                                                        | `--mcp PORT`                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Framing                            | Newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin and stdout                                                                                                                                                                       | One complete JSON-RPC message per HTTP/1.1 `POST`; the request path is not read                                         |
| Started by                         | The MCP host, as a child process                                                                                                                                                                                     | An operator, as a long-running process                                                                                  |
| Runs until                         | The host closes stdin; exit code 0                                                                                                                                                                                   | SIGINT or SIGTERM                                                                                                       |
| Authentication                     | None. `--auth` with `--mcp stdio` and no `--http` or `--bolt` listener beside it exits 2 with an error that begins `Error: serve --mcp stdio skips auth`; with one beside it, `--auth` applies to that listener only | HTTP Basic, from `--auth`, `RELATE_AUTH` or a generated token ([Authentication](#authentication))                       |
| Binds                              | Nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                              | `127.0.0.1:PORT`; `--host` changes the address, with no TLS on any address                                              |
| stdout                             | JSON-RPC responses only                                                                                                                                                                                              | Not used                                                                                                                |
| stderr                             | Startup and shutdown lines                                                                                                                                                                                           | Startup and shutdown lines                                                                                              |
| Browser requests                   | Not applicable                                                                                                                                                                                                       | A present `Origin` must be loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, any port, `http` or `https`); no CORS headers |
| Other surfaces in the same process | `--http` and `--bolt` listeners can run beside it and stop when stdin closes                                                                                                                                         | `--http` and `--bolt` can run beside it                                                                                 |

properties.heading: write_cypher
properties.text:
`write_cypher` takes the same two inputs as `read_cypher` and runs a statement that writes. A statement that only reads is refused with `Only write queries are allowed for write-query`. The result is the same envelope, with empty `columns`, `columnTypes`, and `rows`, and the mutation counters under `stats`. This example writes to a throwaway in-memory store, so the server runs without `--read-only`:

```bash verify
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"write_cypher","arguments":{"statement":"CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})","parameters":{"name":"Ada","role":"engineer"}}}}' \
  | relate serve --mcp stdio --database :memory: 2>/dev/null \
  | sed -E 's/(_ms\\":)[0-9.e-]+/\1<ms>/g'
```

```text
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"content":[{"text":"{\"columnTypes\":[],\"columns\":[],\"elapsed_ms\":<ms>,\"error\":null,\"execute_ms\":<ms>,\"lex_parse_ms\":<ms>,\"lower_ms\":<ms>,\"notifications\":[],\"parse_ms\":<ms>,\"plan\":{\"profiled\":false,\"root\":{\"actual\":null,\"children\":[],\"details\":\"(:Person)\",\"estimated_rows\":null,\"identifiers\":[],\"operator\":\"Create\",\"warnings\":[]},\"schema\":\"relate.plan/v1\",\"statement\":\"CREATE (:Person {name: $name, role: $role})\"},\"plan_cache\":\"miss\",\"plan_ms\":<ms>,\"result_generation_ms\":<ms>,\"rewrite_ms\":<ms>,\"rows\":[],\"stats\":{\"constraints_added\":0,\"constraints_removed\":0,\"indexes_added\":0,\"indexes_removed\":0,\"labels_added\":1,\"labels_removed\":0,\"nodes_created\":1,\"nodes_deleted\":0,\"properties_set\":2,\"relationships_created\":0,\"relationships_deleted\":0}}","type":"text"}],"isError":false}}
```

properties.heading: Storage formats
properties.text: A relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) has one of three layouts, picked by the path given to `--database`: in memory, a directory, or a single `.rl` file. A durable store also has one [codec](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#codec), the encoding its checkpoints write the [snapshot](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#snapshot) in: `parquet` (the default), `json` or `markdown`. Every layout and codec runs the same engine: the graph is held in memory while the store is open, and every commit goes to the store's [write-ahead log](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal) (WAL) before it applies. The layout and codec decide only what a [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint) writes to disk.

properties.heading: Codecs
properties.text:
The codec is chosen when a store is created, with `--snapshot-format` or the `RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` environment variable, and recorded in the store. An existing store keeps its recorded codec, so later opens need no flag. One store holds one codec.

| Codec               | Snapshot files                                                                                                                                                               | A checkpoint writes                                   | Readable as text     | `relate info` reports                                                                           |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parquet` (default) | `manifest.json`, `nodes/<lo>-<hi>-<hash>.parquet`, `relationships/<lo>-<hi>-<hash>.parquet`, with a typed column per shared property key ([data files](#parquet-data-files)) | The node and relationship id ranges that changed      | No (columnar binary) | Format version, node and relationship counts at the checkpoint, and index and constraint counts |
| `json`              | `manifest.json`, `graph.json`                                                                                                                                                | The whole `graph.json`                                | Yes                  | Layout, codec, checkpoint, size; the rest as `unavailable`                                      |
| `markdown`          | One note per node at `<Label>/<name>.md`, an `index.md` per label, a root `index.md` and `log.md`; engine state under `.cypherlite/`                                         | The notes that changed; the index and log notes again | Yes                  | Layout, codec, checkpoint, size; the rest as `unavailable`                                      |

`graph.json` holds every node and relationship with its labels or type and properties, then the index and constraint catalog. A store holding one `KNOWS` relationship between two people starts like this:

```text
{"value_encoding":2,"nodes":[{"id":0,"labels":["Person"],"properties":{"name":"Ada"}},{"id":1,"labels":["Person"],"properties":{"name":"Grace"}}],"relationships":[{"id":0,"type":"KNOWS","start_node":0,"end_node":1,"properties":{"since":2024}}],"indexes":[],"constraints":[], …
```

A `markdown` note keeps a node's properties and outgoing relationships in YAML frontmatter, with relationships as `[[Label/name]]` links. `--markdown-body-properties` names the properties written as the note's body (default: `body`). A note edited by hand while no process has the store open is read at the next open.

```text
---
type: Person
name: Ada
role: engineer
KNOWS:
  - "[[Person/Grace]]"
WORKS_ON:
  - since: 2024
    target: "[[Project/relate]]"
---
```

`relate clone --to-snapshot-format <codec>` copies a store into a new store in another codec; the source is not written. In relate 1.0.1 a `markdown` store clones into a `.rl` file only with `--to-snapshot-format parquet` or `json` ([`relate clone`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/clone/#markdown-into-a-rl-file)).

properties.heading: Directory store files
properties.text:
| Path                                                                                       | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `manifest.json`                                                                            | The codec and the checkpoint's log sequence number (LSN) and commit timestamp; for `parquet`, also the format version, the next node and relationship ids, the list of data files, and the index and constraint catalog                 |
| `nodes/`, `relationships/`                                                                 | `parquet` data files, one per id range                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `graph.json`                                                                               | The `json` snapshot                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `wal/NNNNNNNN.log`                                                                         | WAL segments: commits since the last checkpoint, as physical changes to nodes, relationships, labels and properties, not Cypher text ([segment format](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/wal-and-checkpoints/#segment-format)) |
| `.cypherlite/schema/`                                                                      | A text copy of the schema (indexes, constraints, graph type), rewritten at each checkpoint                                                                                                                                              |
| `.cypherlite.lock`, `.cypherlite.writer`, `wal/.cypherlite.lock`, `wal/.cypherlite.writer` | The writer lock                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

A `markdown` store keeps `manifest.json` and the WAL in its `.cypherlite/` folder (`.cypherlite/manifest.json`, `.cypherlite/wal/NNNNNNNN.log`, `.cypherlite/wal/.cypherlite.lock`, `.cypherlite/wal/.cypherlite.writer`) and the root lock files `.cypherlite.lock` and `.cypherlite.writer` beside its notes; the `parquet` and `json` codecs keep them at the root and in `wal/`.

The snapshot files hold the state at the last checkpoint; the WAL holds every commit since. Opening a store loads the snapshot, then replays the WAL. A copy of the snapshot files without the WAL folder holds the state at the last checkpoint only, and a `--read-only` open of it fails.

On-disk names that start with `.cypherlite` and the magic numbers in the version markers table keep the product's former name, so stores written by earlier releases open unchanged.

The schema copy is plain text. After two schema statements on a directory store, `schema.cypher` holds one statement per index and constraint:

```bash verify
relate --database ./people --mode envelope "CREATE CONSTRAINT person_name IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) REQUIRE p.name IS UNIQUE"
relate --database ./people --mode envelope "CREATE INDEX person_role IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) ON (p.role)"
```

```bash verify
cat people/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
```

```text
CREATE RANGE INDEX `person_role` FOR (n:`Person`) ON (n.`role`);
CREATE CONSTRAINT `person_name` FOR (n:`Person`) REQUIRE (n.`name`) IS UNIQUE;
```

The copy is checked on every open, so an edited file stops the store from opening, read-only included:

```bash verify
echo "// edited" >> people/.cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher
relate --database ./people --read-only --mode envelope "RETURN 1 AS ok"
echo "exit=$?"
```

```text
Failed to open Relate: storage error: schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher differs from the schema this store's checkpoint persisted; it was edited by hand or copied from another store; delete the .cypherlite/schema/ directory and reopen: the next checkpoint regenerates it from the store's schema
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"storage","message":"storage error: schema mirror .cypherlite/schema/schema.cypher differs from the schema this store's checkpoint persisted; it was edited by hand or copied from another store; delete the .cypherlite/schema/ directory and reopen: the next checkpoint regenerates it from the store's schema","retryable":false}}
exit=1
```

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
| Message                                                                                                                     | Exit code | When                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `storage error: snapshot codec mismatch: directory is <codec>, requested <codec>`                                           | 1         | `--snapshot-format` names a codec other than the store's                                                                                                   |
| `Error: invalid --snapshot-format: storage error: unknown snapshot format '<value>' (expected parquet or json or markdown)` | 2         | `--snapshot-format` is not a codec name                                                                                                                    |
| `storage locked: <path>`                                                                                                    | 5         | A second writable open, or a `--read-only` open of a `.rl` file a writer holds ([details](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-conflict-locked)) |
| `storage error: database not found: <path>`                                                                                 | 1         | A `--read-only` open of a missing `.rl` path                                                                                                               |
| `storage error: read-only open requires an existing database at <path>`                                                     | 1         | A `--read-only` open of a missing or empty directory                                                                                                       |
| `storage error: read-only open requires an existing WAL at <path>`                                                          | 1         | A `--read-only` open of a directory store whose WAL folder is missing; `<path>` is the WAL folder                                                          |
| `semantic error: live freshness (WAL follow) is only supported for native directory databases`                              | 1         | `--read-only=live` on a `.rl` file or `:memory:`                                                                                                           |
| `Error: info cannot use :memory: or an empty --database path (info reads an on-disk store)`                                 | 2         | `relate info` on `:memory:`                                                                                                                                |
| `storage error: wal_dir is not supported for .rl single-file databases (ADR-0074)`                                          | 1         | `--wal-dir` with a `.rl` path                                                                                                                              |

On stderr, an error at open is prefixed `Failed to open Relate: `. The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-storage) lists the storage errors with their remedies.

properties.heading: Layouts
properties.text:
|                                         | In memory                       | Directory store                                                                              | `.rl` file                                   |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| On disk                                 | Nothing                         | A folder: snapshot files, the WAL (`wal/`, or `.cypherlite/wal/` for `markdown`), lock files | One file holding the same tree, WAL included |
| Durable                                 | No: gone when the process exits | Yes                                                                                          | Yes                                          |
| Codecs                                  | None                            | `parquet`, `json`, `markdown`                                                                | `parquet`, `json`, `markdown`                |
| Writers                                 | One process                     | One process at a time                                                                        | One process at a time                        |
| `--read-only` beside a writer           | Not applicable                  | Allowed; several readers can share the store                                                 | Refused while a writer holds the file        |
| `--read-only=live`                      | Refused                         | Allowed: follows the writer's commits                                                        | Refused                                      |
| `--wal-dir`                             | Not applicable                  | Allowed (default `<database>/wal`; `<database>/.cypherlite/wal` for `markdown`)              | Refused                                      |
| `relate info`                           | Refused (exit code 2)           | Allowed, without opening the store                                                           | Allowed, without opening the store           |
| `relate clone` as source or destination | Refused                         | Allowed                                                                                      | Allowed                                      |

A writable open of a durable store that another process holds open for writing fails with `storage locked: <path>` (exit code 5). The writer lock is held while the store is open.

properties.heading: Parquet data files
properties.text:
A `parquet` data file gives each property key that its rows share with one type (boolean, integer, float or string) a typed column of its own, named `p_<key>`; the remaining properties stay in a tagged-JSON `properties` column. `relate info` reports the format version as `5` (`6` while the store holds an ontology). These commands create a directory store and read its format version:

```bash verify
relate --database ./wide "CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'}), (:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'})"
```

```bash verify
relate info --database ./wide | head -n 3
```

```text
layout: native directory
codec: parquet
format version: 5
```

Releases up to and including 0.1.2 wrote every property in the tagged-JSON column (format version `3`, or `4` with an ontology) unless the store was opened with `--snapshot-format parquet-wide`. relate 1.0.0 reads those files, and the first checkpoint after a writable open, at the latest the one the open writes when it closes, rewrites every data file with typed columns; a `--read-only` open leaves them as they are. relate 0.1.2 reads format version `5` too, so it still opens the store afterwards. `parquet-wide` is no longer a `--snapshot-format` value: it fails with `invalid --snapshot-format: storage error: unknown snapshot format 'parquet-wide' (expected parquet or json or markdown)`.

properties.heading: Size on disk
properties.text:
These commands write the same 100,000 nodes into a `parquet` directory store, a `json` directory store and a `.rl` file, then clone the `.rl` file, and print each store's size as `relate info` reports it:

```bash verify
relate --database ./items --mode envelope "UNWIND range(1, 100000) AS i CREATE (:Item {id: i, name: 'item-' + toString(i), score: i * 0.5})"
relate --database ./items-json --snapshot-format json --mode envelope "UNWIND range(1, 100000) AS i CREATE (:Item {id: i, name: 'item-' + toString(i), score: i * 0.5})"
relate --database ./items.rl --mode envelope "UNWIND range(1, 100000) AS i CREATE (:Item {id: i, name: 'item-' + toString(i), score: i * 0.5})"
relate clone ./items.rl ./items-clone.rl
```

