```text
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":369.608875,"execute_ms":369.399625,"lex_parse_ms":0.006833,"lower_ms":0.0077919999999999994,"parse_ms":0.1995,"plan_ms":0.004292,"result_generation_ms":0.00029099999999999997,"rewrite_ms":0.000375},"truncated":false}
{"columnTypes":[],"columns":[],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":387.91008300000004,"execute_ms":387.68233299999997,"lex_parse_ms":0.007416,"lower_ms":0.008875000000000001,"parse_ms":0.21529099999999998,"plan_ms":0.006167000000000001,"result_generation_ms":0.000166,"rewrite_ms":0.000542},"truncated":false}
```

```bash verify
for store in items items-json items.rl items-clone.rl; do printf '%s: ' "$store"; relate info --database "./$store" | grep 'total bytes'; done
```

```text
items: total bytes: 2270050
items-json: total bytes: 9245067
items.rl: total bytes: 18640896
items-clone.rl: total bytes: 2293760
```

| Layout                          | Size characteristic                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parquet` directory store       | The smallest of the durable forms: columnar, compressed data files                                                                                                   |
| `json` directory store          | Larger than `parquet` for the same graph (about 4 times in the measurement, rounded)                                                                                 |
| `.rl` file                      | Grows to the most space its snapshot and WAL have needed at once, then reuses that space; it does not shrink. A large commit leaves the file larger than its content |
| `.rl` file after `relate clone` | About the size of the `parquet` directory store: the clone holds only the current state                                                                              |

[Size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/) covers the memory a store needs while it is open.

properties.heading: Surfaces
properties.text:
| Surface                                        | Opens                                                                        | Read-only open                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| CLI (`relate`, `relate query`, `relate serve`) | `--database :memory:`, a directory, a `.rl` path                             | `--read-only`, `--read-only=live`         |
| Python client (`relate-db`)                    | `relate.Database(path)`, `relate.connect(path)`; `":memory:"` is the default | `read_only=True`                          |
| Node.js client (`@relate/relate`)              | `Database.open(path)`                                                        | `Database.open(path, { readOnly: true })` |

`RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT` selects the codec of a new store, a directory or a `.rl` file, on all three.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate --database <path> [--read-only[=live]] [--snapshot-format parquet|json|markdown] [--wal-dir <dir>] [<statement>]
relate clone [--wal-dir <dir>] [--to-snapshot-format parquet|json|markdown] <source> <dest>
relate info --database <path> [--json]
```

| `--database` value       | Layout            |
| ------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `:memory:` (the default) | In memory         |
| A path ending in `.rl`   | Single-file store |
| Any other path           | Directory store   |

A missing path is created on the first writable open. A `--read-only` open of a missing path is an error and creates nothing. `.cl` files written by releases up to 0.16 open as single-file stores. These pages call the single-file layout a `.rl` file; `relate info` prints it as `layout: .rl bundle`, and the directory layout as `layout: native directory`.

properties.heading: Version markers
properties.text:
Each durable part of a store carries a version marker. A store is checked against every marker before anything is written.

| Part                | Marker                                          | This release writes                                                           | This release reads                                                          |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parquet` snapshot  | `format_version` in `manifest.json`             | `5`; `6` while the store holds an ontology                                    | `1` to `6`; `3` and `4` are rewritten as `5` and `6` at the next checkpoint |
| `json` snapshot     | `value_encoding` in `graph.json`                | `2`; `3` while the store holds an ontology                                    | absent, `2`, `3`                                                            |
| `markdown` snapshot | `value_encoding` in `.cypherlite/manifest.json` | `2`; `3` while the store holds an ontology                                    | `1` to `3`; an absent marker counts as current                              |
| WAL segment         | The first 8 bytes                               | `MDBWAL01`; `MDBWAL02` for segments written while the store holds an ontology | `MDBWAL01`, `MDBWAL02`                                                      |
| `.rl` container     | Superblock magic and version                    | `MDBCLB01`, version `1`                                                       | `MDBCLB01`, version `1`                                                     |

A store at an older readable version is upgraded in place when it is opened writable, and older releases can't open it afterward. A store written by a newer release fails to open, with the unsupported version in the error. [Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/) covers both. A `--read-only` open never migrates.

properties.heading: Limits and sizing
properties.text: relate holds the whole graph of an open [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) in memory, so the first limit is the machine's memory. On top of that, relate enforces the limits on this page. Most protect the process from one statement exhausting memory or the stack, and each refusal names what it protected and how to clear it. The graph's size has no limit unless one is set.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
A graph size limit of `1mb` is 1,000,000 bytes, and `1mib` is 1,048,576; the limit appears in the message:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope --logical-graph-size-limit 1mb "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS i CREATE (:Item {i: i})"
relate --mode envelope --logical-graph-size-limit 1mib "UNWIND range(1, 20000) AS i CREATE (:Item {i: i})"
```

The output alternates stderr and stdout:

```text
capacity exceeded: used=258 limit=1000000
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"capacity","message":"capacity exceeded: used=258 limit=1000000","retryable":false}}
capacity exceeded: used=258 limit=1048576
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"capacity","message":"capacity exceeded: used=258 limit=1048576","retryable":false}}
```

`kb` is not a unit:

```bash verify
relate --logical-graph-size-limit 64kb "RETURN 1 AS ok"
```

```text
Error: invalid --logical-graph-size-limit: semantic error: invalid memory limit unit 'kb'; use bytes, mb, mib, gb, or gib
```

A single string property of 67,108,864 characters makes a commit record over 64 MiB, so the commit is refused:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "WITH reduce(s = 'a', i IN range(1, 26) | s + s) AS s CREATE (:Blob {s: s})"
```

```text
This statement tried to commit a single WAL record of at least 64 MB. This is a safety limit protecting against memory exhaustion — the per-record WAL payload cap is 64 MB; commit the data in smaller transactions.
{"error":{"code":"fatal_error","exit_code":1,"kind":"capacity","message":"This statement tried to commit a single WAL record of at least 64 MB. This is a safety limit protecting against memory exhaustion — the per-record WAL payload cap is 64 MB; commit the data in smaller transactions.","retryable":false}}
```

The message writes the 64 MiB limit as `64 MB`. A string of half that length commits:

```bash verify
relate --mode envelope "WITH reduce(s = 'a', i IN range(1, 25) | s + s) AS s CREATE (:Blob {s: s}) RETURN size(s) AS characters"
```

```text
{"columnTypes":["INTEGER"],"columns":["characters"],"notifications":[],"planCache":"miss","rows":[{"characters":33554432}],"timings":{"elapsed_ms":46.503208,"execute_ms":46.268917,"lex_parse_ms":0.007208,"lower_ms":0.009000000000000001,"parse_ms":0.2215,"plan_ms":0.007042,"result_generation_ms":0.000583,"rewrite_ms":0.0005},"truncated":false}
```

properties.heading: Fixed limits
properties.text:
These limits have no flag or environment variable.

| Limit                                                                                                | Value                                                                                    | Met as                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One commit's record in the [write-ahead log](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal) (WAL) | 64 MiB (67,108,864 bytes)                                                                | [`This statement tried to commit a single WAL record of at least <size>. …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-wal-payload-cap), exit code 1; nothing is written |
| Statement text                                                                                       | 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes)                                                                  | `syntax error: query text of <n> bytes exceeds the maximum query size of 4194304 bytes`, exit code 6                                                                             |
| Nesting of a statement's expressions and clauses                                                     | 500 levels                                                                               | `syntax error: parse error: maximum nesting depth of 500 exceeded`, exit code 6                                                                                                  |
| Nesting of a list or map a statement builds at run time                                              | 500 levels                                                                               | `ValueDepthExceeded: value nesting exceeds 500 levels; container nesting compounds per level (security limit).`, exit code 1                                                     |
| Evaluation passes of nested subqueries, `EXISTS` and `FOREACH` in one statement                      | 100,000                                                                                  | [`NestedEvaluationBudgetExceeded: …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-nested-evaluation-budget)                                                                |
| One file read by `LOAD CSV`                                                                          | 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes)                                                                  | [`LOAD CSV file exceeds byte limit`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-load-csv-byte-limit), exit code 1                                                            |
| A store downloaded by `--load <url>`                                                                 | 1 GiB, and 300 seconds                                                                   | A message containing `the remote database exceeded the 1 GiB cap`                                                                                                                |
| One source fetched by `--fetch-params`                                                               | 64 MiB, and 60 seconds                                                                   | A message containing `source exceeded the 64 MiB cap`                                                                                                                            |
| Graphs in a store                                                                                    | 3 fixed namespaces: `neo4j`, `system`, `system_ontologies`; a statement runs against one | [`semantic error: DatabaseNotFound: Graph not found: <name>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-database-not-found), exit code 6                                 |

Every property value is subject to two limits on this page: the expression limit while a statement builds it, and the 64 MiB WAL record limit when it is committed, together with everything else in the same commit. A commit over 64 MiB is refused whole; splitting the write into smaller transactions clears it.

properties.heading: Limits you can set
properties.text:
| Limit                                                                                                                        | Default   | Set with                                                                            | Range                                     | Met as                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Live graph and index size, in logical bytes (not process memory)                                                             | Unlimited | `--logical-graph-size-limit`, `RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT`                     | A size; `0` is unlimited                  | [`capacity exceeded: used=… limit=…`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-graph-size-cap), exit code 1                                |
| One value an expression builds: a list, string or map from `range`, concatenation, `collect`, a comprehension or an `UNWIND` | 256 MiB   | `--expression-memory-limit`, `RELATE_EXPRESSION_MEMORY_LIMIT`                       | A size; `none` or `0` turns the limit off | [`This statement tried to build a single value of <size>. …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-expression-memory-cap), exit code 1 |
| Workspace shared by the statements running at once                                                                           | Off       | `--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit`, `RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT` | A positive size; `0` is a usage error     | `resource limit exceeded: concurrent-logical-workspace-limit limit=<bytes>`, exit code 1                                                            |
| Explicit upper bound of a variable-length path (`*1..N`, `{1,N}`)                                                            | 500 hops  | `--max-traversal-depth`, `RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH`                               | 1 to 2000                                 | [`syntax error: TraversalDepthExceeded: …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-traversal-depth-exceeded), exit code 6                |

The graph size limit refuses only writes that grow the graph, when they reach the WAL. `DELETE` and a `SET` that shrinks a value still run, and opening a store and replaying its WAL always succeed, even over the limit.

The expression limit applies to each value on its own, not to a statement's total, so a long statement that builds many small values never accumulates against it.

The traversal depth limit applies to an explicit upper bound. A path pattern with no upper bound (`*`, `*1..`) is not checked against it, and neither is `shortestPath`.

properties.heading: Parameters in the Node.js client
See also
properties.text:
- [Errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/): every message on this page with its cause, remedy, and exit code.
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/): the files each layout writes, with measured sizes.
- [Size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/): how much memory a graph needs.
- [Limitations](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/limitations/): what relate does not do, next to what to use instead.

properties.heading: Sizing
properties.text:
| What                         | Size                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Memory while a store is open | The whole graph and its indexes, held in memory; relate has no buffer pool and does not page to disk. [Size a store and its memory](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/sizing-and-memory/) has a worked sizing                                                                                                                          |
| Snapshot on disk             | Depends on the codec; the [storage formats reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#size-on-disk) has measured sizes                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| WAL on disk                  | The commits since the last [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint). The current WAL segment closes, and a checkpoint runs, at 64 MiB, at 10,000 commits, or when the checkpoint timer fires ([when a checkpoint runs](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/wal-and-checkpoints/#when-a-checkpoint-runs)) |
| Checkpoint timer             | 300 seconds by default; `--checkpoint-interval-secs`, `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS`; `0` turns off the timer only; `relate serve` takes only `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS`                                                                                                                                                           |

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate [--logical-graph-size-limit <size>] [--expression-memory-limit <size>|none]
       [--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit <size>] [--max-traversal-depth <n>]
       [--checkpoint-interval-secs <n>] [--database <path> [--read-only]] [<statement>]
```

Each flag has an environment variable that sets its default; the flag wins over the variable. A `<size>` is a whole number, optionally followed by a unit:

| Unit                  | Bytes         |
| --------------------- | ------------- |
| No unit, `b`, `bytes` | 1             |
| `mb`                  | 1,000,000     |
| `mib`                 | 1,048,576     |
| `gb`                  | 1,000,000,000 |
| `gib`                 | 1,073,741,824 |

Units are case-insensitive and may follow the number with or without a space. Any other unit, `kb` included, is a usage error ([exit code](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#exit-code) 2).

properties.heading: WAL and checkpoints
properties.text: Every commit to a relate [store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#store) is appended as one record to the store's [write-ahead log](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#wal) (WAL) before it applies to the graph in memory. A [checkpoint](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#checkpoint) writes the committed graph to the store's [snapshot](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#snapshot) files and deletes the WAL segments the snapshot now covers. Opening a store loads the snapshot, then replays the WAL records written after it. The WAL's format is the same under every layout and codec. [Storage and durability](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/storage-and-durability/) explains why the write path has this shape.

properties.heading: Errors
properties.text:
The first seven errors stop the open with exit code 1. On stderr each is prefixed `Failed to open Relate: `, and in `--mode envelope` it is an error object with `kind` `storage`. `<segment>` is the segment's name, such as `00000002.log`.

| Message                                                                                                                                                      | Exit code | When                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `storage error: WAL checksum mismatch`                                                                                                                       | 1         | A complete record fails its checksum with bytes after it, or as the last record of a closed segment ([storage errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-storage)) |
| `storage error: undecodable WAL record at offset <n> in <segment>: may have been written by a newer Relate (<detail>)`                                       | 1         | A record's checksum matches but its payload does not decode; a newer release wrote it ([Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/))                        |
| `storage error: invalid WAL magic: <segment>`                                                                                                                | 1         | A segment's first 8 bytes are neither `MDBWAL01` nor `MDBWAL02`                                                                                                                            |
| `storage error: truncated WAL magic: <segment>`                                                                                                              | 1         | A segment is shorter than its 8-byte magic, and is not a newest segment a writable open can rewrite                                                                                        |
| `storage error: invalid WAL payload length <n> in <segment> (limit 64 MiB)`                                                                                  | 1         | A record's length field is 0 or larger than 67,108,864                                                                                                                                     |
| `storage error: non-increasing or unsupported WAL commit timestamp <ts> after <previous> in <segment>`                                                       | 1         | A record's `commit_ts` is `0`, or not larger than the previous record's                                                                                                                    |
| `storage error: ontology op in non-MDBWAL02 WAL segment <segment> at offset <n>`                                                                             | 1         | A record that changes the ontology sits in an `MDBWAL01` segment                                                                                                                           |
| `Error: final checkpoint failed: <reason>`                                                                                                                   | 1         | The checkpoint at a clean exit failed ([details](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-final-checkpoint-failed))                                                                  |
| `semantic error: WriteOnReadOnlyAccessDatabase: No write operations are allowed on this database. The database is in read-only mode on this Neo4j instance.` | 1         | `.checkpoint` on a `--read-only` open ([details](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-write-on-read-only))                                                                    |

The errors at open that concern the WAL folder itself, such as a `--read-only` open without one or `--wal-dir` on a `.rl` path, are in the [storage formats errors](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#errors). The [errors reference](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-fatal-error-storage) lists the storage errors with their remedies.

properties.heading: Examples
properties.text:
These commands write three commits to a new directory store in one script run, then print the store's metadata, the WAL folder and its one segment:

```bash verify
cat > team.cypher <<'EOF'
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer'});
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer'});
CREATE (:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer'});
EOF
relate query --database ./team < team.cypher
relate info --database ./team
ls -A team/wal
cat team/wal/00000002.log; echo
```

```text
layout: native directory
codec: parquet
format version: 5
checkpoint LSN: 3
commit timestamp: 3
total bytes: 2300
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 3): 3
relationships (at checkpoint LSN 3): 0
indexes: 0
constraints: 0
.cypherlite.lock
.cypherlite.writer
00000002.log
MDBWAL01
```

The run closed the store cleanly, so its checkpoint covers all three commits: `checkpoint LSN: 3`. The checkpoint recycled `00000001.log`, and the open segment `00000002.log` holds its magic and no records. `wal segments past checkpoint` counts the segment files that may hold commits newer than the snapshot, so an empty open segment counts as 1.

This script commits one relationship, prints the WAL and checkpoint fields, forces a checkpoint with `.checkpoint`, and prints them again:

```bash verify
cat > checkpoint.cypher <<'EOF'
MATCH (a:Person {name: 'Ada'}), (g:Person {name: 'Grace'}) CREATE (a)-[:KNOWS]->(g);
.info
.checkpoint
.info
EOF
relate query --database ./team < checkpoint.cypher | grep -E '^(checkpoint LSN|total bytes|wal segments)'
```

```text
checkpoint LSN:               3
total bytes:                  2418
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
checkpoint LSN:               4
total bytes:                  3628
wal segments past checkpoint: 1
```

Before `.checkpoint`, the commit is in the WAL only: the checkpoint LSN is still 3, and the store is larger by the new record. After it, the checkpoint LSN is 4, the snapshot holds a `relationships/` data file, and the WAL is back to one empty segment.

A single statement makes 10,001 commits with `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS OF 1 ROWS`. Commit number 10,000 fills the open segment's commit count and starts a checkpoint:

```bash verify
relate query --database ./batch <<'EOF' | grep -E '^(checkpoint LSN|nodes)'
UNWIND range(1, 10001) AS i CALL (i) { CREATE (:Item {i: i}) } IN TRANSACTIONS OF 1 ROWS;
.info
EOF
relate info --database ./batch | grep -E '^(checkpoint LSN|nodes)'
```

```text
checkpoint LSN:               10000
nodes:                        10001
checkpoint LSN: 10001
nodes (at checkpoint LSN 10001): 10001
```

Inside the session the checkpoint LSN is 10,000 while the live graph holds 10,001 nodes; the last commit is in the WAL. The checkpoint at exit covers it.

properties.heading: Files on disk
properties.text:
| Layout                                     | WAL location                                             | Segment files                      | Lock files                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Directory store, `parquet` or `json` codec | `<database>/wal/`, or the `--wal-dir` folder             | `NNNNNNNN.log`                     | `.cypherlite.lock` and `.cypherlite.writer` in the WAL folder |
| Directory store, `markdown` codec          | `<database>/.cypherlite/wal/`, or the `--wal-dir` folder | `NNNNNNNN.log`                     | `.cypherlite.lock` and `.cypherlite.writer` in the WAL folder |
| `.rl` file                                 | Inside the file, as `wal/` in the same tree              | `wal/NNNNNNNN.log` inside the file | None beside the file; a writer holds the `.rl` file itself    |
| In memory                                  | Process memory; nothing on disk                          | Not applicable                     | Not applicable                                                |

The store's root also holds its own `.cypherlite.lock` and `.cypherlite.writer`. The `manifest.json` of the last checkpoint records the checkpoint's log sequence number (LSN) as `checkpoint_lsn`, with its `commit_ts`; [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#directory-store-files) lists the snapshot files beside them.

properties.heading: Record format
properties.text:
| Field    | Size                   | Content                                                                                                                                |
| -------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Checksum | 4 bytes, little-endian | CRC-32 of the payload                                                                                                                  |
| Length   | 4 bytes, little-endian | The payload's length in bytes: at least 1, at most 67,108,864 (64 MiB). A limit: a larger commit is refused before anything is written |
| Payload  | The length in bytes    | One JSON object with the keys `lsn`, `commit_ts` and `ops`                                                                             |

| Payload key | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lsn`       | The record's log sequence number. It increases with every record, and replay applies only records with an LSN higher than the snapshot's `checkpoint_lsn`                                                                                                                                 |
| `commit_ts` | The commit timestamp. It increases strictly from one record to the next across every segment, and is never `0`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ops`       | The commit's physical changes: a node or relationship created or deleted, a property set or removed, or a label added or removed. Never Cypher text, so replay never re-runs a statement. The encoding of each entry belongs to the engine; a change to it comes with a new segment magic |

properties.heading: See also
properties.text:
- [Storage and durability](https://relatedb.ai/docs/concepts/storage-and-durability/): why every commit goes through the WAL, and what checkpoints trade.
- [Storage formats](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/): the snapshot files, codecs, and version markers.
- [Limits and sizing](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/limits-and-sizing/): the 64 MiB record limit and the other limits.
- [Choose a durability mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/durability-modes/): when a commit's record reaches the disk.
- [Recover from a crash](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/crash-and-recovery/): replay and the torn tail, step by step.
- [Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/): the checkpoint that migrates an older store.

properties.heading: Segment format
properties.text:
The WAL is a series of segment files. Exactly one, the segment with the highest id, is open for appends.

| Part    | Size                 | Content                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name    | Not applicable       | The segment id as 8 decimal digits, then `.log`. A new WAL starts at `00000001.log`; each new segment takes the next id. Other file names in the folder are ignored |
| Magic   | 8 bytes              | `MDBWAL01`; `MDBWAL02` for a segment created while the store holds an ontology. Both are readable by this release                                                   |
| Records | The rest of the file | Zero or more records, back to back, up to the end of the file                                                                                                       |

A segment that holds no records is 8 bytes long: its magic alone.

properties.heading: Synopsis
properties.text:
```text
relate --database <path> [--wal-dir <dir>] [--checkpoint-interval-secs <n>]
       [--durability-mode full|everysecond|snapshot] [--read-only[=live]] [<statement>]
relate query --database <path> < <script>
relate info --database <path> [--json]
```

| Setting                                                                                                                | Default                                                                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`--checkpoint-interval-secs <n>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#checkpoint-interval-secs)             | `300`                                                                   | Seconds between timed checkpoints, on `relate` and `relate query`. `0` turns off the timer only; the other triggers still run                                                           |
| [`RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#env-relate-checkpoint-interval-secs) | `300`                                                                   | The same period for an open that sets no interval, `relate serve` included; the flag wins over the variable. A value that is not a whole number is not an error: the period stays `300` |
| [`--wal-dir <dir>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#wal-dir)                                             | `<database>/wal`; `<database>/.cypherlite/wal` for the `markdown` codec | Where a directory store keeps its WAL. Refused for a `.rl` file; `relate serve` has no such flag                                                                                        |
| [`--durability-mode`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/cli/flags/#durability-mode), `RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE`         | `full`                                                                  | When a commit's record is synced to disk relative to its acknowledgment                                                                                                                 |

Two dot commands of the interactive shell, also accepted as lines of a script piped to `relate query`, act on the WAL and checkpoints:

| Dot command   | Effect                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.checkpoint` | Runs a checkpoint now and prints nothing on success. Refused on a `--read-only` open                                                  |
| `.info`       | Prints the fields of `relate info` from inside the session; its node and relationship counts are the live graph's, not the snapshot's |

properties.heading: The torn-tail rule
properties.text:
A torn tail is the damage a crash leaves at the very end of a segment: a record whose writing stopped part of the way through. Its commit was never acknowledged under `full` durability. The rule decides which damage replay drops and which stops the open:

| Damage                                                                                                        | Where                     | Result                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| An incomplete record at the end of the file: 1 to 7 header bytes, or a header whose payload runs past the end | Any segment               | Torn tail: dropped                                                                 |
| A complete last record whose checksum fails                                                                   | The open segment          | Torn tail: dropped                                                                 |
| A complete last record whose checksum fails                                                                   | A closed segment          | The open fails: `WAL checksum mismatch`                                            |
| A record whose checksum fails, with more bytes after it                                                       | Any segment               | The open fails: `WAL checksum mismatch`                                            |
| A record whose checksum matches but whose payload does not decode                                             | Any segment, any position | The open fails: `undecodable WAL record … may have been written by a newer Relate` |

Dropping a torn tail prints nothing. A writable open writes the segment's intact records to a new file and renames it over the old one, so a failure part of the way through leaves the original in place. [Recover from a crash](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/crash-and-recovery/) rehearses a crash and its recovery.

properties.heading: What a checkpoint does
properties.text:
| Step               | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rotate             | The open segment closes, if it holds records; new commits go to a segment with the next id                                                                                                                     |
| Pin                | The checkpoint takes the LSN of the newest closed segment's last record                                                                                                                                        |
| Write the snapshot | The committed state up to that LSN is written through the store's codec ([codecs](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/storage/formats/#codecs)), together with the schema text copy under `.cypherlite/schema/` |
| Publish            | Files are written under a temporary name and renamed into place, `manifest.json` last; the manifest's `checkpoint_lsn` is the pinned LSN. A crash before this step leaves the previous snapshot in force       |
| Recycle            | Closed segments whose last record's LSN is no higher than the checkpoint LSN are deleted                                                                                                                       |

An in-memory store has no snapshot files: its automatic checkpoints only recycle the WAL, and `.checkpoint` writes a snapshot that lives in the process.

properties.heading: What a commit appends
properties.text:
| Statement or transaction                                                           | WAL effect                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A statement outside a transaction that changes the graph                           | One record                                                                                                                                                                        |
| An explicit transaction (`.begin` … `.commit` in the CLI)                          | One record at commit, holding every statement's changes                                                                                                                           |
| An explicit transaction with no changes, or one rolled back                        | Nothing                                                                                                                                                                           |
| A statement that changes nothing: a read, or a write whose pattern matches nothing | Nothing                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS`                                                       | One record per batch                                                                                                                                                              |
| A commit whose record would exceed 64 MiB                                          | Nothing; the statement fails with [`This statement tried to commit a single WAL record of at least <size>. …`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#engine-wal-payload-cap) |
| A commit that sets an ontology while the open segment is `MDBWAL01`                | A new `MDBWAL02` segment first, then one record in it                                                                                                                             |
| Any write on a `--read-only` open                                                  | Nothing; the write is refused                                                                                                                                                     |

The record is appended to the open segment. When that segment then holds 64 MiB or 10,000 commits, it closes and a checkpoint starts. Under the default `full` [durability mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/glossary/#durability-mode) the record is synced to disk before the commit is acknowledged, and commits waiting together share one sync; `everysecond` syncs about once a second and `snapshot` never syncs on commit. [Choose a durability mode](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/durability-modes/) states each mode's loss window.

properties.heading: What replay does on open
properties.text:
| Step                                                | Writable open                                                                                                                                    | `--read-only` open                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Check the version markers                           | Before anything is written; a store from a newer release fails to open                                                                           | The same                                                   |
| Load the snapshot                                   | The state at its `checkpoint_lsn`                                                                                                                | The same                                                   |
| WAL folder missing                                  | A new, empty WAL is created; the store opens at the snapshot's state, without the commits the missing segments held                              | Fails: `read-only open requires an existing WAL at <path>` |
| Scan the segments                                   | Every segment in id order. Every record is checked, including those up to the checkpoint LSN; records with a higher LSN are applied in LSN order | The same                                                   |
| A torn tail                                         | Dropped, then removed from its file once every segment has scanned; later appends go to a new segment                                            | Dropped; the file is left as it is                         |
| A newest segment shorter than its 8-byte magic      | Rewritten as an empty `MDBWAL01` segment, when lower-numbered segments exist and are intact and its bytes start that magic                       | Fails: `truncated WAL magic: <segment>`                    |
| Any other damaged record                            | The open fails; no partial graph is served and no segment is recycled                                                                            | The same                                                   |
| The graph size limit (`--logical-graph-size-limit`) | Not applied to replay; an open always succeeds over it                                                                                           | The same                                                   |
| An older readable version                           | Migrated: a checkpoint at the current format, then a new segment                                                                                 | Not migrated                                               |
| At exit                                             | A checkpoint on clean close                                                                                                                      | No checkpoint                                              |

properties.heading: When a checkpoint runs
properties.text:
| Trigger                                                           | Default                                   | Changed with                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The open segment reaches a size                                   | 64 MiB (67,108,864 bytes)                 | Fixed; a limit with no flag or variable                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The open segment reaches a commit count                           | 10,000 commits                            | Fixed; a limit with no flag or variable                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The timer fires while the WAL holds commits the snapshot does not | Every 300 seconds                         | `--checkpoint-interval-secs`, `RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS`; `0` turns off the timer only. An in-memory store has no timer                                                                                    |
| A writable store closes cleanly                                   | Always                                    | Not configurable. Every clean exit of a writable CLI run checkpoints; a failure exits 1 with [`Error: final checkpoint failed: <reason>`](https://relatedb.ai/docs/reference/errors/#cli-final-checkpoint-failed) |
| `.checkpoint`                                                     | On request                                | Not applicable                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| A writable open of a store at an older readable version           | Once, at the current format, after replay | Not configurable ([Upgrade a store](https://relatedb.ai/docs/guides/operate/upgrade-a-store/))                                                                                                                    |
| `relate clone`                                                    | Once, into the destination                | Not applicable; the destination starts at the source's loaded LSN with an empty WAL                                                                                                                               |

A `--read-only` open never checkpoints, in either freshness. A `--read-only=live` reader that finds a segment it still needed recycled by the writer's checkpoint reloads the current snapshot and the WAL that remains.

properties.short: The program that runs a model and executes the commands it chooses, such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor; relate detects one from its environment variables.
CLI defaults for a detected agent harness on a non-terminal stdout, or forced on: at most 100 rows printed per statement, the cut reported, TOON in a pipe.
Neo4j's binary client protocol; `relate serve --bolt <port>` speaks it, so Neo4j's drivers and Neo4j Browser can run statements against a relate store.
The marker a commit returns, `relate:<n>`, naming its place in the store's commit sequence; returned by the clients and over Bolt.
The step that writes a fresh snapshot of committed state and recycles old WAL segments: every 300 seconds by default, on clean exit, and on `.checkpoint`.
A language package that runs the relate engine inside a program's process: the Python, Node.js, Rust, Java, Go and Swift clients.
`relate clone`: the command that copies a store into a new one, optionally in another codec, reading the source without writing it.
The on-disk encoding of a store's snapshot: Parquet (the default), JSON or markdown, fixed when the store is created.
The retryable error a commit gets when another transaction committed a change to the same node or relationship after it began; exit code 5 on the CLI.
A rule the store enforces on every write, such as a unique property, a required property, a property type or a node key; a violating write fails.
The declarative graph query language relate runs, written as ASCII-art patterns such as `(a)-[:KNOWS]->(b)`; relate follows Neo4j's Cypher 25 by default.
The Neo4j Cypher version aligned with GQL; the default language of every relate namespace, with `CYPHER 5` as the per-statement alternative.
A store kept as a folder of snapshot files, a WAL folder and lock files; the layout for any `--database` path that is not `:memory:` and does not end in `.rl`.
When a commit counts as safe on disk: `full` (the default) syncs the WAL first, `everysecond` about once a second, and `snapshot` only at checkpoints.
The string `elementId()` returns for a node or relationship, such as `4:rl-id:n0`; it stays the same when the store is closed and opened again.
One compact JSON object per result set, printed by `--mode envelope`, that keeps the column list even when there are no rows.
The JSON object a failed query run prints on stdout in the `json`, `jsonl`, `envelope` and `speedscope` modes: the class, the kind, the message, the exit code.
The number a `relate` run returns to the shell; each nonzero value names a class of failure, such as 2 for usage, 5 for conflict, 6 for a rejected statement.
A package that adds an action to the CLI, run as `relate run <name>` and installed with `relate extension install`.
An index over one or more string properties that finds entities containing given words, ranked by a BM25 relevance score.
The ISO standard graph query language; Neo4j's Cypher 25 aligns Cypher with it, and relate follows that alignment.
A schema for a whole graph, declared in Cypher, that lists node and relationship types with their properties; writes that break it fail.
The JSON-over-HTTP statement endpoint `relate serve --http <port>` hosts, in the shape of Neo4j's Query API v2: `POST /db/<name>/query/v2`.
A store that lives only in the process that opened it, named `:memory:`; the default `--database`, gone when the process exits.
A structure the planner uses to find nodes or relationships by a property without scanning a label: range, text, point, vector or full-text.
A name that classifies a node, such as `Person`; a node has zero or more, and patterns, indexes and constraints refer to them.
A test on a node's labels or a relationship's type built with `&`, `|`, `!` and `%`, such as `(n:Person|Project)` or `(n IS Person)`.
A read-only open of a directory store, `--read-only=live`, that tails the WAL and follows the writer's commits as they land.
relate's own byte count of the live nodes, relationships, properties and index entries; what `--logical-graph-size-limit` caps.
The Model Context Protocol, which agent hosts use to call tools; `relate serve --mcp` exposes a store as `read_cypher`, `get_schema` and `write_cypher`.
One of the three fixed graphs in every store: `neo4j` for user data, `system` for administration, and `system_ontologies`, listed but not queryable.
An entity in the graph: it carries zero or more labels and a map of properties, and relationships connect it to other nodes.
Advice the planner attaches to a plan, such as a missing index, with a GQLSTATUS code, a severity and a remedy; derived only under `EXPLAIN` or `PROFILE`.
An Ontology Graph Spec document stored with a store, managed by the `db.ontology.*` procedures behind the `ontology` preview, and appliable as the graph type.
The open specification of Cypher and its Technology Compatibility Kit (TCK) of scenarios; relate treats it as the floor of its dialect.
A named value a statement refers to as `$name` and the caller binds separately, such as with `--param name=value` on the CLI.
An alternating sequence of nodes and relationships that a pattern matched, bound with `p = …` and read with `nodes(p)`, `relationships(p)` and `length(p)`.
The tree of operators the planner chooses to run a statement; `EXPLAIN` shows it without running, `PROFILE` runs and adds rows and time per operator.
An index over a property holding `point` values that narrows bounding-box and radius predicates to nearby nodes through an R-tree.
A Cypher feature from a not-yet-settled proposal that relate ships switched off; it runs only when `RELATE_PREVIEW` names it when the store opens.
A named value stored on a node or relationship, such as `name: 'Ada'`; values are scalars, temporal and spatial values, vectors, or lists of them.
`relate pull`: the command that copies a subgraph from Neo4j or Aura into a store, over the HTTP Query API, from Cypher that returns graph elements.
`relate push`: the command that copies a scoped subgraph of a store into Neo4j or Aura over the HTTP Query API; the mirror of `relate pull`.
A pattern repeated a bounded or unbounded number of times, written `((a)-[:R]->(b)){1,3}` or `-[:R]->{1,3}`; GQL's form of a variable-length path.
A statement that reads, where the contrast with writing matters; also `relate query`, the command that runs a statement session.
An open mode (`--read-only`) that never writes, checkpoints or migrates the store; writes fail, and a directory store can be read beside its writer.
A directed, typed connection between two nodes, with properties of its own; every relationship has exactly one type and a start and an end node.
The single name every relationship carries, such as `KNOWS` or `WORKS_ON`; patterns match on it, and a relationship cannot change it.
The file extension of a single-file store; a `--database` path that ends in `.rl` selects that layout.
The limit on rows printed per statement, 100 by default under a detected agent harness; `--max-rows` sets it, and a cut is reported in-band.
An opt-in policy (`--safe`) that refuses a new named node without a label, an unbounded `MATCH` read and a remote `--load`, before anything runs.
The text copy of a store's schema under `.cypherlite/schema/`: indexes and constraints, the graph type and the ontology, rewritten at each checkpoint.
The Cypher 25 `SEARCH` clause, which restricts a `MATCH` to the top results of a vector or full-text index and binds their score.
A store kept in one `.rl` file that holds the snapshot and the WAL together; the layout for a `--database` path ending in `.rl`.
The `SKILL.md` cheat sheet and reference files a coding agent reads before it uses relate; `relate skill install` writes them.
The set of files that make up the relate skill: `SKILL.md` and 15 reference files, embedded in the binary and served by the site.
The committed graph state a checkpoint writes to disk, loaded on open before the WAL replays; not the `snapshot` durability mode or `--read-only` freshness.
One unit of Cypher that relate parses, plans and runs, such as a `MATCH … RETURN` read or a `CREATE` write; a script holds several, separated by `;`.
A relate database: a directory, a single `.rl` file, or `:memory:`, opened with `--database`.
Any front door to the relate engine: the CLI, a language client, the C ABI, the WebAssembly build, or a server that `relate serve` hosts.
The anonymous usage metrics the `relate` CLI sends: on by default, off with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, `RELATE_TELEMETRY=0` or `relate telemetry off`.
Token-Oriented Object Notation: an output mode that prints the columns once, then one comma-separated line per row; the piped default in agent mode.
A unit of work that commits as a whole or not at all; each statement is its own transaction unless an explicit `begin` … `commit` groups several.
An index over a property holding embeddings that answers nearest-neighbor searches exactly, by cosine or Euclidean similarity.
Append-only log each commit goes to before it applies; under the default `full` durability mode it is synced first, so a crash loses no acknowledged write.

properties.title: Pick up where the last session left off
properties.summary: Turn chat messages into facts and decisions in a graph, and let a later session recall them from a blank prompt. When a decision changes, the new one replaces the old one but keeps its history, so the agent knows both what's true now and what it used to be.

properties.title: Let an agent look back at its own steps
properties.summary: Record each tool call as a step on a session timeline, and read back the latest steps, earlier pages, or everything since a given time. The agent can check what it already tried before acting again, and a supervisor can track token use and the newest steps across every session.

properties.title: Know what an agent believed, and when
properties.summary: Keep a bi-temporal decision log that records both when a decision was true and when the agent learned it, through late corrections, rejections, and planned changes. You can explain a past decision by what the agent knew at the time, not by what turned out to be true later.

properties.title: Answer codebase questions text search can't
properties.summary: Build a graph of a codebase's packages and design decisions, use text search to find a starting point, and follow short links to the answer. Questions like "was this decision replaced?" or "what builds on the parser?" are answered by the links between documents, not by the paragraph that matches the words.

properties.title: Trace how vulnerabilities reach your app
properties.summary: Load the full dependency graphs of three real packages, and find which known vulnerabilities each one can reach, through which chain, and what disappears if you drop a dependency. A lockfile lists what you install but not why; the graph shows why, and turns the answer into a CI check.

properties.title: Merge duplicate customers across systems
properties.summary: Match a CRM export and a billing export that spell the same companies differently, typos included, and resolve 396 records into 211 companies, with a short list of doubtful pairs for a person to review. It's entity resolution entirely inside the database, with no fuzzy-matching library, and it finds 216 of 218 duplicate pairs with no false merges.

properties.title: Find a note, then what was decided since
properties.summary: Combine vector and keyword search (hybrid search) in one Cypher query, then follow each matching note to the latest decision on its topic. The best-matching note can be out of date: here it says Auth0, and the follow-up step shows the team later chose Okta.

properties.title: Catch a migration that quietly loses data
properties.summary: Fingerprint a graph before a migration, declare what the migration may change, and compare afterward. Node counts and intended-change checks can all pass while data is destroyed; here the fingerprint catches 352 lost city links and restores them.

properties.title: Answer "what's nearby?" from memory
properties.summary: Store the places a travel assistant's users mention and its agents visit, and turn them into five small location tools: within 2 km, nearest, inside a map area, and recently visited nearby. The agent answers location questions from its own memory, with distances in meters.

properties.title: Turn a question into the Relate docs you need
properties.summary: Search the Relate docs, loaded as a graph, then follow links from each matching section to the pages to read first, the terms to know, and a worked example. The graph also narrows the search to the right pages, so a word with two meanings doesn't send the agent to the wrong one.

properties.title: Audit where an agent's memories came from
properties.summary: Write every memory tool call into the same graph as the memory, linked to everything it wrote or read. When a memory looks wrong, you can find the call that wrote it, who has read it since, what failed calls left behind, and what each tool costs.

properties.synopsis: relate clone [--wal-dir DIR] [--to-snapshot-format F] [--markdown-body-properties LIST] SOURCE DEST
relate pull [--from FILE] --query Q [--param N=V] [--allow-plaintext] --database PATH

relate push --to CREDS --database PATH [--query Q | --labels L1,L2 | --types T1,T2] [--batch-size N] [--nodes-update POLICY] [--rels-update POLICY] [--updated-at NAME[,NAME]] [--rel-mode MODE] [--merge-key LABEL:PROP[,PROP]] [--rel-key TYPE:PROP[,PROP]] [--unkeyed-labels ACTION] [--dry-run] [--json] [--allow-plaintext]

relate serve --database PATH [--host HOST] [--http PORT] [--origin ORIGIN] [--mcp PORT|stdio] [--bolt PORT [--bolt-identity STRING] [--ws-allow-origin ORIGIN] [--ws-max-connections N]] [--read-only[=FRESHNESS]] [--load SOURCE] [--auth USER:PASSWORD] [--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE] [--max-traversal-depth N] [--expression-memory-limit SIZE] [--safe | --no-safe] [--logical-graph-size-limit SIZE] [--durability-mode MODE] [--snapshot-format F]

properties.title: Agent memory
properties.problem: Give an agent memory that survives restarts, which a later session can recall by meaning and by connection.
properties.capability: A durable store the agent's process opens itself, with uniqueness constraints and `MERGE` for one node per entity, `SUPERSEDES` chains for corrections, and vector `SEARCH` for recall.

properties.title: Agent trajectory timeline
properties.problem: Log every step an agent takes and read the last few, the page before them, and everything since a cutoff, in the right order every time.
properties.capability: Steps on a timestamped relationship whose integer sort key relationship property type and existence constraints enforce, read newest first with `ORDER BY`, `LIMIT` and `SKIP`.

properties.title: Bi-temporal facts
properties.problem: Answer both what was true on a date and what the agent believed on that date, after late corrections and rejected decisions.
properties.capability: Two time ranges on every fact, valid time and record time, written with `datetime()` and `MERGE` so nothing is deleted, and queried with chained comparisons.

properties.title: Codebase context graph
properties.problem: Give a coding agent answers to multi-hop questions about a codebase, such as what replaced a design decision or what builds on a module.
properties.capability: Crates, design records and their sections as one graph, IDF-weighted full-text `SEARCH` to find where to start, and bounded quantified path patterns to follow the links.

properties.title: Dependency analysis
properties.problem: Find which known advisories a package can reach and through which chain, and what goes away when a dependency is dropped.
properties.capability: Resolved dependency graphs as nodes and relationships, quantified path patterns and `SHORTEST` for reachability and chains, and `COUNT` and `EXISTS` subqueries for blast radius.

properties.title: Diffable memory
properties.problem: Keep an agent's memory in the repository, so each session's changes show up in a pull request as a diff a person can review.
properties.capability: A directory store whose checkpoint writes the graph as text, one `graph.json` with the `json` codec or one note per node with `markdown`, and `MERGE` writes that replay to no change.

properties.title: Embedded graph in an app
properties.problem: Add a graph database to an application without running, securing or paying for a database server.
properties.capability: The engine as a library in the application's process, through the Python, Node.js, Rust, Java, Go and Swift clients, the C ABI or the WebAssembly build.

properties.title: Entity resolution
properties.problem: Merge two messy exports that list the same customers spelled differently into one record per company, with doubtful pairs left for a person.
properties.capability: Normalized keys, bigram similarity and IDF-weighted scores computed in Cypher over records, entities and tokens, with `SAME_AS` and `POSSIBLE_MATCH` relationships for the decisions.

properties.title: Fresh graph per test run
properties.problem: Give every test or CI run its own graph, built from a fixture and thrown away afterwards, with results a script can check.
properties.capability: The in-memory store, the default, gone when the process exits; `--load` to read a fixture store into memory; envelope output and typed exit codes for the script that checks it.

properties.title: Geospatial memory
properties.problem: Let an agent answer what is near here, what is nearest, what is inside this map box, and where it went recently near a place.
properties.capability: WGS-84 points stored as properties, distances in metres with `point.distance`, map boxes with `point.withinBBox`, and a `POINT` index, in the same graph as the rest of the memory.

properties.title: Graph queries over MCP
properties.problem: Give a coding agent or an agent framework a graph it can query through MCP, without letting it change the data.
properties.capability: `relate serve --mcp stdio` on a store opened `--read-only`, which lists the `read_cypher` and `get_schema` tools and leaves out `write_cypher`.

properties.title: Hybrid retrieval for RAG
properties.problem: Retrieve the passages that answer a question by meaning and by keyword at once, then follow links to the context around them.
properties.capability: Vector and full-text indexes queried with the `SEARCH` clause, fused by reciprocal rank in one Cypher statement, with a graph hop from each hit to its related nodes.

properties.title: Migration rehearsal
properties.problem: Check that a data migration changed only what it was meant to, before it runs on the real graph.
properties.capability: A fingerprint of the graph taken in Cypher before the migration, probes that compare it afterwards, and `relate clone` or `--load` to run the migration on a copy.

properties.title: Neo4j subgraph mirror
properties.problem: Work on a slice of a Neo4j or Aura graph locally, offline or in a test, and copy changes back when they are ready.
properties.capability: `relate pull`, which copies the graph elements a query returns from Neo4j or Aura into a local store, and `relate push`, which copies a scoped subgraph back with a `--dry-run` plan.

properties.title: Offline and sandboxed use
properties.problem: Run a graph database where an agent works isolated, with no network after setup and nothing sent anywhere.
properties.capability: A single binary that needs no network once installed with usage metrics off (`DO_NOT_TRACK=1`), stores that are files in the workspace, and network access visible on the command line.

properties.title: Schema as files
properties.problem: Let an agent or a reviewer read a store's indexes and constraints from a file instead of opening the database, and see a schema change as a text diff.
properties.capability: A text copy of the schema under `.cypherlite/schema/`, with `schema.cypher` holding one `CREATE` statement per index and constraint, rewritten at every checkpoint and checked at every open.

properties.title: Shared store across processes
properties.problem: Let an agent and an application, or several readers, use the same graph without corrupting it or blocking each other.
properties.capability: One writer per store, enforced by a lock; `--read-only` opens beside the writer on a directory store; `--read-only=live` to follow its commits; or one `relate serve` process.

properties.title: Single-file graph
properties.problem: Keep a whole graph in one file that can be copied, attached, checked in or handed to another program.
properties.capability: The `.rl` store: one file holding the snapshot and the write-ahead log, created on the first open, compacted by `relate clone`, and read into memory with `--load`.

properties.title: Text-to-Cypher
properties.problem: Let a model turn a question into a Cypher statement over a graph whose schema it can read, and check the statement before it runs.
properties.capability: The schema as data from the `db.schema` procedures and the MCP `get_schema` tool, `EXPLAIN` to plan a statement without running it, and read-only opens that refuse writes.

properties.title: Tool-call provenance
properties.problem: Find out which tool call wrote a fact in an agent's memory, which calls read it since, and what failed calls left behind.
properties.capability: Each tool call recorded as a node in the same graph, by the same statement as the call, linked to every node it wrote or returned and guarded by `NODE KEY` and relationship property constraints.
